intro.heading: Two questions to answer before you pay anybody
paragraphs: Which board, and which tier. Those are the two questions, and a surprising number of Jumeirah Village Triangle parents cannot answer either when they first call. It is not carelessness — schools rarely spell it out in a letter. But the answers determine which specification document matters, which past papers are useful and what grade is even reachable, so an IGCSE home tutor in Jumeirah Village Triangle who does not ask them in the first five minutes is guessing.

Take board first. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel both offer International GCSEs, and Dubai schools use both, sometimes mixing boards across subjects in the same cohort. Cambridge Mathematics is 0580; Pearson's International GCSE Mathematics A is 4MA1. Cambridge Physics is 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610. The content overlaps heavily, but paper structures, formula sheet provision and the way questions are worded differ enough that a term of practice on the wrong board's papers is a term partly wasted. Pearson also runs some subjects on a modular basis, which Cambridge does not.

Then tier. Cambridge offers many subjects at Core and Extended. Core covers less content and caps the grade at 5 on the 9-1 scale, or C on the legacy letter scale. Extended covers the full syllabus and reaches grade 9. A student entered for Core cannot be awarded a grade above the cap however well they perform, so a child aiming at a sixth form that wants grade 6 mathematics has to be on Extended, and the entry decision usually sits with the school months before the exam. If your child is on Core and the target needs more, that conversation has a deadline.

The practical point for a family in the Triangle is that both of those facts are checkable in an afternoon. Ask the school's examinations officer for the board and syllabus code per subject and the tier of entry. Write them down. Then any tutor you speak to can be asked directly whether they have taught that code, and the answer stops being a matter of trust rather than a matter of record. It also changes what you buy: at that point you are paying for familiarity with a specific specification and its mark scheme, which is a thing a tutor either has or does not, instead of paying for general subject confidence that cannot be tested until the first marked paper comes back.

This page then does the work that follows: a syllabus-code reference for the subjects Dubai schools enter most, the paper structure and tier rules behind each one, the specific topics where IGCSE students in UAE schools lose marks, what the Dubai market charges in AED, an honest comparison of a home visit in JVT against an online session, the Cambridge and Pearson examination calendar with the India-only series warning, and the Ministry of Education equivalency rule that decides how many subjects your child actually needs. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video; there are no home visits anywhere in the UAE.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-villa.programmesIntro: IGCSE sits inside a wider British-curriculum route, and which stage your child is at changes what tutoring should do. The three stages below cover almost every enquiry from the Jumeirah Village Triangle and Dubailand communities.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: No external examinations, which makes this the stage where gaps form quietly. The skills that decide an IGCSE grade two years later are built here: algebraic manipulation, written structure in English, and the habit of showing method. Tutoring at KS3 is cheap in both money and hours compared with repair work in Year 11, and it is almost always the better investment when a report flags weak foundations.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools set their Year 9 option choices in the spring term, and those choices decide the IGCSE subject list. Jumeirah Village Triangle families frequently ask for help across that decision rather than for a subject: whether to take triple science, whether a second language is worth the slot, and whether the mathematics set the child is in implies Core or Extended entry later.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight to ten subjects, examined externally by Cambridge or Pearson. Most subjects are fully examined with no coursework; some sciences carry an alternative-to-practical paper rather than a practical examination. The grade comes from a weighted total across papers, so diagnosing which paper is weak is more useful than general revision. Tier of entry is set by the school and caps the attainable grade.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, UK curricula account for 37% of private-school enrolment across 227 schools and 387,441 students, so IGCSE cohorts here are large and tutoring supply for mainstream subjects is deep. That depth does not extend to every specification: a school entering a minority subject on Pearson may have very few locally resident tutors who have taught that exact code.

programmes.name: A Level or IB Diploma after Year 11
programmes.description: The IGCSE grade is a gate. A Level courses typically ask for grade 6 or 7 in the subject, and IB Higher Level courses expect comparable attainment. This is where a Core entry becomes visible as a constraint, because a capped grade may not clear the threshold even when the student is capable of the work. Planning backwards from the sixth-form requirement is the only sensible order.
programmes.countryNote: Triangle students split both ways at sixteen. Some stay on the British route for A Levels; others move to the IB Diploma at schools such as JESS Arabian Ranches, Nord Anglia International School Dubai or Fairgreen International School. The IGCSE-to-Diploma step is sharpest in mathematics and the sciences, where the Diploma's internally assessed component is unlike anything in IGCSE.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-villa.subjectsIntro: The IGCSE subjects Jumeirah Village Triangle families ask about most, with the Cambridge syllabus code where one applies and what the papers actually demand. Where Pearson differs materially, that is noted.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: Extended Paper 2 and Paper 4 both permit a calculator, and both reward visible method. The heaviest mark loss sits in algebraic fractions, transformations of graphs and compound interest problems where students round too early. Pearson's 4MA1 covers similar ground with a different paper split and its own formula provision.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by stronger sets in some Dubai schools, and the single best preparation for A Level or IB Higher Level mathematics. Calculus and trigonometric identities arrive early. Students who find 0580 Extended comfortable but then struggle here are usually short on algebraic fluency rather than concepts.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism produce the most lost marks, followed by anything requiring a graph to be drawn and read accurately. The alternative-to-practical paper assesses experimental technique on paper, including precision of measurement and sensible control variables, and is routinely under-practised.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Moles calculations and ionic equations carry the mark loss. Examiners want state symbols, balanced equations and units carried through. Qualitative analysis — the tests for cations, anions and gases — is pure recall and is often the quickest grade gain available in the last month.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: The problem is command terms against content volume. 'Describe' and 'explain' attract different answers, and a student who writes a paragraph for a two-mark 'state' question loses time they need later. Transport in plants, genetics and the human digestive system are the recurring trouble spots.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: Reading comprehension marks depend on lifting the right phrase, not on paraphrasing elegantly. The summary task has a strict word count and rewards content points over style. Speaking is separately assessed in some entries, and preparation for it is usually left too late.

subjects.name: English First Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and descriptive or narrative composition, plus reading responses that must quote precisely. Students lose marks writing about what a text says rather than how it achieves its effect. Timed practice matters more than content teaching in this subject.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram marks are awarded independently of the prose: axes labelled, curves shifted, new equilibrium marked. Four-part structured questions escalate from definition to evaluation, and students often spend the time budget on the first part and leave the eight-mark evaluation thin.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Application to the case material is the difference between a 5 and an 8. Generic answers about motivation or marketing score low; answers naming the firm in the stimulus and using its numbers score high. Break-even and ratio arithmetic is a reliable mark source if drilled.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Paper 1 covers data representation, networks and hardware; Paper 2 is algorithms and programming, answered in pseudocode. Students who only write Python lose marks on Cambridge pseudocode conventions. Trace tables and binary or hexadecimal conversion are high-frequency, low-effort marks.

sections.heading: Finding out which board and tier your child is actually entered for
paragraphs: Ask the examinations officer, not the class teacher. The examinations officer holds the entry data and can tell you the board, the syllabus code and the tier for every subject, which is the complete answer. A class teacher will usually know their own subject and may not know the rest. Put the request in writing and ask for it per subject; schools in Dubai answer this routinely.

Why it matters is practical. A Year 11 student revising Cambridge 0580 past papers for a Pearson 4MA1 entry is doing useful mathematics in the wrong format, and format is a meaningful share of the grade in a timed examination. Formula provision differs. Paper lengths differ. Pearson's modular option in some subjects means assessment can be spread rather than taken in one series, which changes revision planning entirely.

Tier is the other half. Cambridge Core and Extended are different syllabuses with different content and different grade ceilings, and the entry sits with the school. If your child is targeting a sixth form that asks for grade 6 in mathematics and they are entered for Core, the ceiling makes that impossible regardless of effort. That is a conversation to have with the school as early in Year 10 as possible, with evidence, because entries close months before the examination.

Once you have board, code and tier written down, interviewing a tutor becomes straightforward. 'Have you taught 0620 Extended?' is a question with a yes or no answer. 'Are you good at chemistry?' is not.

sections.heading: Core versus Extended, and what the ceiling means in practice
paragraphs: Cambridge Core and Extended are not easy and hard versions of the same paper. Extended covers additional syllabus content as well as harder questions on shared content, so a student moved late from Core to Extended has material to learn, not just difficulty to absorb. That is why the decision has a deadline and why it is worth getting right in Year 10 rather than arguing about it in Year 11.

The ceiling is the part parents most often miss. A Core entry caps the awarded grade — commonly at 5 on the 9-1 scale or C on the legacy letter scale — and no amount of performance lifts it above the cap. For a student heading to a sixth form or an A Level course that asks for grade 6 or 7 in the subject, Core closes the door before the examination is sat. For a student who needs a solid pass and is at risk of under-performing on Extended, Core is the sensible and protective choice.

Schools make the entry decision on evidence: internal assessment results, set placement and teacher judgement. A parent who wants it reconsidered needs evidence of the same kind, which is one legitimate use of tutoring in Year 10 — not to argue, but to produce a track record on Extended-level questions that the school can see. Where that evidence does not materialise, Core is usually the right answer and accepting it early beats a capped surprise in August.

The equivalent question on the Pearson route is different, because most Pearson International GCSE subjects are untiered. There the question is not tier but whether a modular entry pattern is being used, and if so which units are being sat when.

sections.heading: The topics where IGCSE marks go missing in Dubai schools
paragraphs: Mark loss repeats. Across cohorts the same topics produce the same errors, and because IGCSE papers are heavily structured the errors are easy to name once a marked script is in front of you. A tutor who starts by teaching the syllabus from the beginning is spending your money on content the student already has.

In Mathematics 0580 Extended the recurring losses are early rounding in multi-step problems, algebraic fractions, transformations of graphs described imprecisely, and bearings. In Physics 0625 it is electricity circuits, electromagnetic induction and graph work where axes are mislabelled or gradients computed from the wrong points. In Chemistry 0620 it is moles arithmetic, ionic equations without state symbols, and the qualitative analysis tests, which are pure recall and therefore the cheapest marks on the paper to recover.

Across every subject the biggest single category is command-term mismatch. 'State' wants a short answer with no working. 'Describe' wants what happens. 'Explain' wants why. 'Evaluate' or 'discuss' wants judgement with both sides. A student who writes a good explanation for a 'state' question loses time; a student who describes when asked to explain loses marks. Annotating the command term before writing is mechanical, teachable in one session, and transfers across the whole entry.

The second category is the alternative-to-practical paper in the sciences. It assesses experimental method on paper — choosing apparatus, identifying control variables, judging precision, spotting anomalous results — and school revision programmes often leave it until last because the theory papers carry more marks. For a student a grade away from their target, it is frequently the best-value four sessions available.

sections.heading: What the cheapest IGCSE tutoring in Dubai costs, and what it leaves out
paragraphs: Work up from the bottom of the market rather than down from the top, because the bottom is where most families start. Tutopiya publishes online tuition from AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65. At those rates the tutor is usually a university student or a non-specialist graduate, and for Key Stage 3 consolidation or basic homework support that can be entirely adequate. What it does not buy is somebody who knows that 0620 wants state symbols or that Core caps at grade 5.

The next band up is where specification knowledge starts. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts qualified subject tutors online in the AED 150-300 range, IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 or above, and in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180-350, with independent home tutors going to AED 500 once travel is included. TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist work and BartyED sits at AED 650 at the premium end.

Converted to a monthly commitment for one weekly hour, Bestimate's estimates are roughly AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for exam-year specialist support. Published packages in the Dubai market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. All of these are provider-published figures read in October 2026.

For context worth having: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for Dubai private schools for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total. School fees are flat; tutoring is the variable line in a Dubai education budget. IB Gram does not publish a fixed hourly rate here because it depends on subject, tier and urgency — take the free diagnostic lesson and get a quote against the actual paper.

sections.heading: A home visit in JVT against an online session
paragraphs: Jumeirah Village Triangle is easy to reach by Al Khail Road and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, and hard to reach quickly between four and half past six. A tutor travelling in from Mirdif, Deira or Dubai Marina in term time is spending forty minutes to an hour each way, and that journey is paid for in the hourly rate, in a two-hour booking minimum, or in a tutor whose last session of the day is their fourth.

A home visit has real advantages and it is worth naming them rather than arguing them away. A Year 7 or 8 student who cannot yet self-manage a screen does better with an adult in the room. A student whose handwriting and working need physical correction as they write benefits from presence. Parents who want to overhear the session find it simpler. That is why the in-home market in Dubai is substantial and charges a premium over online.

What online changes for an IGCSE family specifically is specification match. The question stops being 'who will drive to JVT at five' and becomes 'who has taught 0580 Extended and marked it'. Sessions can be 45 minutes rather than two hours. A 20:00 slot is possible after a late fixture without anybody driving home at night. The recording means a November session can be rewatched in May at no extra cost, which matters for recall-heavy content like the Chemistry test tables.
IB Gram offers only the online format in the UAE. The table sets both out so the decision is made on the facts.

sections.heading: The IGCSE examination calendar, and the series your child will never sit
paragraphs: One warning first, because it is the single most common factual error on UAE tutoring pages. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only. A UAE candidate does not sit it, and a revision plan built around a March examination window is built around a date that does not exist for your child. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. Cambridge also runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, which is a different thing entirely and is sometimes what a parent has half-remembered.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and in November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Results give a sense of the lag between sitting and knowing: Pearson's June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the right habit is to open the live official timetable rather than trust a restated date.

Cambridge has one administrative rule that genuinely catches families out. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong version. If you are printing a timetable at home, get the zone right from the exams officer first.

Counted backwards, the sequence is: results day, examination window, zone timetable confirmation, mock examinations, school coursework and internal deadlines, final entry deadline including tier. The entry deadline is the one that closes options, and it falls months before the papers are sat.

sections.heading: How many IGCSE subjects your child actually needs for the UAE
paragraphs: Ministry of Education equivalency is the recognition of a foreign secondary certificate for UAE university admission and some employment routes, and the British-track rule is specific enough to plan around. A student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must additionally show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

Two details inside that rule are worth repeating. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, so a student taking them in addition to five others is fine but should not count them towards the five. And the figure is five. A competitor page ranking for UAE searches states that candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is wrong, and a parent who plans around it buys a year of tuition in a subject their child did not need.

The same Ministry framework covers other curricula. On the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB Diploma, this page publishes no points threshold, because the sourced article states none and no figure has been read on moe.gov.ae. Writing a number there would be exactly the mistake described in the paragraph above.

Finally, the boundaries. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency; it is a Ministry process and you deal with the Ministry or the emirate's attestation authority directly. And tutoring is not required for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression. Where you see that implied, it is urgency being manufactured.

sections.heading: Booking, permits and the honest version of availability
paragraphs: The sequence is short. Send the board, syllabus code and tier per subject, plus a marked mock or the latest report. A specialist runs a free diagnostic lesson and, within a working day, sends a written note naming the error patterns and estimating the number of sessions. You decide after reading it. Nothing is charged before that point.

Availability, honestly stated. Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, English 0500 and 0510, Economics 0455 and Business Studies 0450 have deep cover for UAE evening slots, and a match normally takes one to three working days. Minority specifications are different: an uncommon language, a Pearson code a Dubai school has only just adopted, or a subject with a small cohort may have no free UAE-resident specialist, in which case the tutor comes from our India-based faculty working on Gulf Standard Time. We say so before you book.

On permits, because it is a reasonable thing for a parent to check. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no amount is quoted here. MoHRE's own service is 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', with no listed fee and a two-working-day completion time.

One further caution worth stating plainly: a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is issued to training institutes. IB Gram holds no such permit, has no UAE office or centre, and makes no claim of approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson. We explain what those bodies do; none of them endorses us.

process.title: Get board, code and tier in writing
process.description: Ask the school's examinations officer for the board, syllabus code and tier of entry for each subject. It takes one email and it makes every later decision concrete. Without it, a tutor is choosing past papers on probability rather than on fact, and a term of the wrong board's papers is partly wasted work.

process.title: Send a marked script
process.description: A marked mock, a returned topic test or a report with subject comments tells a specialist more in five minutes than a long conversation does. If the student has nothing marked and recent, say so and the diagnostic lesson includes a short timed paper from the correct tier instead.

process.title: Free diagnostic lesson
process.description: A full session at no charge, spent on the student's own errors rather than on a topic. Most students show two or three repeating patterns — rounding too early, command-term mismatch, missing state symbols — and the plan is built on those rather than on a syllabus checklist.

process.title: Written diagnosis and session count
process.description: Within a working day you get a short note naming the error patterns, the syllabus areas behind them and an honest estimate of sessions needed. If the time left is not enough to reach the target, the note says that too and suggests what is realistically reachable instead.

process.title: Weekly slot, reviewed on real marks
process.description: Same tutor, same time, 45 or 60 minutes, scheduled around the JVT school run and shifted to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan. Progress is judged on the school's next marked assessment, not on our exercises, and the focus or the tutor changes if that evidence does not move.

whyPoints.title: Specification-level matching
whyPoints.description: Tutors are matched to a syllabus code, not to a subject name. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 split topics differently and provide different formulae, and practising the wrong board's papers costs marks that have nothing to do with ability.

whyPoints.title: The tier conversation, early
whyPoints.description: Core caps the attainable grade. If your child's sixth-form target needs grade 6 and the entry is Core, that is a Year 10 conversation with evidence, not a Year 11 complaint. We produce the evidence in the form of marked Extended-level work the school can look at.

whyPoints.title: Rates with the source attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is a named provider's own published figure read in October 2026, not an invented average. We do not publish a fixed hourly rate for ourselves here because subject, tier and urgency move it, and a wrong number would be worse than none.

whyPoints.title: Alternative-to-practical taken seriously
whyPoints.description: The science alternative-to-practical papers assess experimental method on paper and are routinely the last thing revised. Four focused sessions on apparatus choice, control variables, precision and anomalous results is often the best-value block available in the final month.

whyPoints.title: Material referenced, never redistributed
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson specifications, past papers and mark schemes are copyright. We cite and link them at their official sources and teach from them in session; we do not hand over scanned folders of marking material, which is a copyright problem and, for unreleased papers, worse.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated before you pay
whyPoints.description: Mainstream codes match in one to three working days. Where a specification has no free UAE-resident specialist, we name that and say where the tutor is based instead, before a booking rather than after. No competitor in this market publishes a coverage limit.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE home tutors actually visit homes in Jumeirah Village Triangle?
faqs.answer: Independent tutors and agencies in Dubai do, and the published bands put it at AED 180-350 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 rate table, rising towards AED 500 for independent home tutors once travel is included. IB Gram does not. Our UAE service is one-to-one tuition over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are something we run only in India. What that buys a Triangle family is a tutor matched to the syllabus code rather than to a driving radius, plus 45-minute sessions, since nobody has a journey to recover.

faqs.question: Who at a Dubai school can tell me the exact syllabus code my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: The examinations officer, and nobody else reliably. Email them and ask for the board, syllabus code and tier of entry for every subject. That person holds the entry data; a class teacher will usually know only their own subject. The answer matters because Cambridge Mathematics is 0580 while Pearson's is 4MA1, formula provision differs, and paper structures differ enough that practising the wrong board's papers costs marks on format alone. Dubai schools answer this request routinely, and once you have it in writing you can ask any tutor whether they have taught that exact code.

faqs.question: My child is entered for Core maths but needs grade 6 for sixth form. What now?
faqs.answer: Raise it with the school immediately, because a Cambridge Core entry is commonly capped at grade 5 or C and no performance lifts a result above the cap. Entries close months before the series, so the window is finite. The school decides on internal evidence, which means the useful response is evidence: a term of marked Extended-level work showing the student can handle the additional content, not just harder versions of Core questions. If that evidence does not appear, Core is the protective choice and accepting it early beats a capped result in August.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do students at JVT schools most often need help with?
faqs.answer: Mathematics 0580 Extended first, by a wide margin, usually for algebraic fluency and early rounding rather than for concepts. Then Physics 0625, where electricity and electromagnetism produce most of the loss, and Chemistry 0620, where moles arithmetic and ionic equations do. English as a Second Language 0510 appears steadily in a multilingual community, generally because reading-comprehension marks depend on lifting the right phrase rather than paraphrasing. Across all of them the single largest category is command-term mismatch, which is teachable in about one session and transfers to the whole entry.

faqs.question: Does my child sit the Cambridge February or March IGCSE series in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. The February/March series is offered to India only, so no UAE candidate sits it, and any revision plan built around a March examination window is built on a date that does not apply. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. What does run in March, May and October are Cambridge Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests, which are a different assessment entirely and are sometimes what has been half-remembered. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Confirm your child's series with the examinations officer.

faqs.question: What is the Cambridge zone timetable and why does it matter to us?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and each zone gets its own version of the timetable. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. The practical risk is a parent downloading a timetable PDF from a search result, printing it, and planning a family trip around a date that belongs to another zone. Ask the exams officer which zone your centre is in before you print anything.

faqs.question: When will we know the results after a November IGCSE sitting?
faqs.answer: Later than most families expect. For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so the gap between the last paper and the result is roughly two months. By comparison, Pearson's June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so check the live official timetable rather than a restated date on any third-party page, including this one.

faqs.question: Is the alternative-to-practical paper worth paying a tutor for?
faqs.answer: Often it is the best-value block in the final month. The paper assesses experimental method on paper rather than in a laboratory: choosing apparatus, identifying control variables, judging the precision of a measuring instrument, spotting anomalous results and drawing or reading graphs accurately. School revision programmes tend to prioritise the theory papers because they carry more marks, which leaves this one under-practised across whole cohorts. Four focused sessions working through real alternative-to-practical questions and their mark schemes will usually move the score on it noticeably, with no new content to learn.

faqs.question: How much should a Dubai family budget per month for one IGCSE subject?
faqs.answer: On Bestimate's 2026 Dubai estimates for a single weekly hour: roughly AED 240-600 at the entry level, AED 600-1,200 for a qualified subject tutor, and AED 1,000-2,000 or above for specialist exam-year support. Published package pricing in this market includes about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are other providers' figures, read in October 2026, not ours. For context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, so tutoring is the variable line in the budget.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover triple science for a Year 11 student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth testing rather than assuming. Many specialists cover two of Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 to a high standard; very few cover all three at Extended level with equal command of the mark schemes. Where one tutor can genuinely cover two, scheduling and continuity improve and the student explains less context each week. Where they cannot, splitting is the better outcome even though it means two slots. Ask directly which codes a tutor has taught and which they have marked, and treat a vague answer as a no.

faqs.question: Should a JVT student add Additional Mathematics to the Year 9 option list?
faqs.answer: For a student heading to A Level Mathematics or IB Higher Level, usually yes. It introduces calculus and trigonometric identities a year early, which flattens the step into sixth form considerably. For a student who finds 0580 Extended demanding, it is an extra examination load for limited benefit and the slot is better spent securing the five subjects that equivalency and sixth-form offers actually depend on. The decision belongs in the Year 9 options conversation. Students who handle 0580 easily but struggle with 0606 are almost always short on algebraic fluency rather than on understanding.

faqs.question: Do Dubai schools teach Arabic alongside IGCSE, and does it count for equivalency?
faqs.answer: They must teach it, and it does not count towards the five. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, and schools must run separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, however, Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required GCSE or IGCSE subjects.

faqs.question: How fast can you match an IGCSE tutor for a student at Sunmarke or Arcadia?
faqs.answer: One to three working days for a mainstream specification in a UAE evening slot — Mathematics 0580, the three separate sciences, English 0500 and 0510, Economics 0455 and Business Studies 0450 all have deep cover. Minority codes take longer and occasionally cannot be filled from UAE-resident tutors at all: an uncommon language, a Pearson specification a school has only just adopted, or a small-cohort subject. Where that happens the tutor comes from our India-based faculty teaching on Gulf Standard Time, and we tell you before the booking rather than after it.

faqs.question: Can we see the mark schemes and past papers you teach from?
faqs.answer: We teach from them in session and link them at source, but we do not hand over copies. Cambridge and Pearson specifications, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are copyright, and a tutor distributing a folder of scanned marking material is creating a copyright problem — and for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. What a tutor will do is work through a real question with you on screen, show exactly what the published scheme credits, and point you to the official site so you can download the same documents yourself through the proper route.

faqs.question: Can sessions shift during Ramadan or a school's mock week?
faqs.answer: Yes, and both come up every year with Triangle families. In Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar timing, usually 20:30 to 22:00 on Gulf Standard Time, often shortened to 45 minutes. During a school's internal examination or mock week most families pause so the student owns their own evenings, then restart with a session spent reading the marked scripts, which is the most useful hour of the term. Because every session is recorded, a pause loses nothing — November's work can be rewatched in May without paying twice. Give us the dates at the start of term and the slot is held.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-villa.closingHeading: Get the code and the tier, then get the right tutor
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-villa.closingBody: The first email to send is not to a tutor. It is to your child's examinations officer, asking for the board, syllabus code and tier of entry for each subject. With those three facts written down, the rest becomes mechanical: check whether the tier ceiling clears the sixth-form requirement, find the marked paper that is losing marks, and ask any tutor the one question that matters — have you taught this code and marked it. For families in Jumeirah Village Triangle that tutor works one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time rather than driving in at five. Send the marked script and the codes, and book the free diagnostic lesson.

intro.heading: Two years, one shape, and most families join it late
paragraphs: The IGCSE years are more structured than they look from the outside. Option choices are made in Year 9 and quietly decide how many qualifications a child will leave with. Tier entries are made by the school months before any paper is sat, and the tier sets a hard ceiling on the grade available. Mocks happen, usually on real past papers, and produce the single most useful diagnostic document of the whole two years. A run-in follows, then the series, then results day, then a review window with its own deadline, then - for anyone who wants it - a November resit. Every one of those is a date, and almost all of them are knowable in advance.

What happens in practice in Karama is that a family arrives in February or March of Year 11, after a disappointing mock, and asks for a tutor. That is a legitimate and common moment to ask, and it is also the moment with the fewest options left. The tier is locked. The entries are made. The option choices are two years old. What remains is converting knowledge the student already has into marks the mark scheme will award, which is real and worth buying, but it is a narrower product than the one the family thinks they are buying.

The year before is where the leverage sits, and almost nobody uses it. Year 10 is the only period in which the tier decision is genuinely open, in which a subject can still be dropped or added, and in which a weak foundation can be rebuilt slowly rather than patched. A student whose algebra is secure by the end of Year 10 can be entered on the higher tier with confidence rather than hope. That is a different conversation from the one that happens in February of Year 11, and it is cheaper.

The other end of the calendar is also under-used. Results day is not the end of the process. There is a review-of-results route, requested through the school within a deadline set by the board, and there is a November series that functions as a same-calendar-year second attempt - for Pearson International GCSE, November results have reached students in January, with November 2025 results landing on 22 January 2026. Families who have never been told about either of those treat an August grade as final when it may not be.

On delivery, since the URL says home tutor: that is the phrase Karama parents type and we are going to answer the home-tutoring question rather than ignore it. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we provide only in India. Every lesson for a Karama family is one-to-one over live video, and we say so before anyone pays. The argument for it sits in a table further down, and the short version is that a deadline-driven run-in cannot afford a session lost to a blocked creek crossing.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-karama.programmesIntro: Where a Karama family actually sits in the two-year map. The year matters more than the subject here, because it determines what is still open.

programmes.name: Year 9 and the option choices
programmes.description: The year in which subjects are chosen and, in science, in which the triple, double or single award decision is usually made. This decides how many IGCSE grades a student will finish with and which sixth-form routes stay available. It is made with half an eye on the timetable and almost never revisited, which is why it is worth a single deliberate conversation at the time.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count. That arithmetic is worth knowing before a subject is dropped in Year 9.

programmes.name: Year 10
programmes.description: The year of maximum leverage and minimum urgency, which is why it goes unused. The tier decision is still open, a weak foundation can be rebuilt rather than patched, and past papers can be introduced gradually instead of arriving as a shock. A standing hour in Year 10 in the one subject that is genuinely behind does more than three hours in Year 11 at the same total cost.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools often make a provisional tier judgement at the end of Year 10 using internal assessment evidence. That makes the spring of Year 10 the window in which tutoring can change the entry rather than work inside it, and it is the single best-value period in the whole two years.

programmes.name: Year 11
programmes.description: Entries are finalised, mocks are sat, the run-in happens and the series arrives. What tutoring can do here is diagnostic and technical: read a mock script, rank where marks are being lost, repair the two or three highest-cost areas, and drill the mechanical losses. It cannot lift a tier ceiling and it cannot cover nine subjects in eight weeks.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit June and November. The February and March series that appears in online searches is offered to India only. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct timetable for your zone, so take it from the school rather than from a search result.

programmes.name: Results day and afterwards
programmes.description: A review-of-results route exists, requested through the centre within a deadline the board sets, and a November series functions as a same-calendar-year second attempt. For Pearson International GCSE, June results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November results have reached students in January. Both routes need deciding quickly rather than contemplated.
programmes.countryNote: A resit decision made in October is usually too late, because the November entry deadline sits well before the series. The useful window is the fortnight after August results, and the useful work is diagnostic rather than a repeat of the same revision.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-karama.subjectsIntro: Nine or ten subjects is normal, and tutoring cannot cover them all. These are the subjects where a well-timed block most reliably changes a grade, and what the block should contain.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The subject where the tier decision is sharpest and where algebra taxes everything else. Cambridge now sets a non-calculator paper worth half the grade; Pearson permits a calculator in both of its two-hour papers. The two need different diets, so the syllabus code has to come before any past paper.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Most physics marks lost in this district go to algebra and unit conversion rather than to physics: a formula rearranged wrongly, a milli or kilo prefix not converted, an answer without a unit. Treating it as a mathematics problem is faster and improves every topic at once.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Splits into a recall half - tests, colours, reactivity, bonding - and a calculation half built on relative formula mass and moles. Diagnose which half is failing before teaching either, because the recall half responds to one organised table and the calculation half needs a four-to-six session block.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The largest content volume of the three sciences and marked on precision of language. The right idea in the wrong words scores nothing, and six-mark questions want six distinct creditable points rather than one fluent paragraph. Mark-scheme wording drills move this faster than content revision.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing, descriptive and narrative writing, and reading response tasks. Marks concentrate on reading precision and on controlled structure rather than on vocabulary. Students who write a great deal and plan nothing lose structure marks that twenty minutes of planning practice would recover.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Rewards close analysis of how a writer's choices create effect, with textual reference embedded rather than appended. Plot retelling caps a response in the lower bands however well it is written. Essay structure and quotation integration are the two most teachable gains here.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken alongside the main mathematics by students heading for A Level or Diploma Higher Level mathematics, and introducing calculus. It is also the subject most often dropped under timetable pressure. Worth a deliberate decision in Year 10 rather than an abandonment in Year 11.

subjects.name: Economics and Business
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, correct use of technical vocabulary, and answers applied to the stimulus rather than recited generically. Evaluation questions need a judgement at the end rather than a balanced list, and that is a structural fix worth two sessions.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Both run source or data-based components alongside extended writing. History Paper work rewards evaluating sources for origin, purpose, value and limitation rather than describing them. Geography rewards case-study specificity: named places, named figures, named consequences.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Theory papers that reward precise technical definition, plus practical or pseudocode components. Students who can code lose theory marks for imprecise terminology, and students who know the theory lose practical marks on trace tables. Diagnose which half is failing first.

subjects.name: Arabic and additional languages
subjects.levels: Cambridge and Pearson first and foreign language options
subjects.description: Separate from the mandatory Arabic provision a Dubai school runs, and examined on reading, writing, listening and speaking components. The speaking component is the one students prepare least, and it responds well to short, frequent rehearsal rather than to long sessions.

subjects.name: Exam technique across subjects
subjects.description: Command words, mark allocation, question triage, showing working, and attempting rather than abandoning a question for partial credit. These are mechanical losses that recur in every subject, and one block on them in the autumn of Year 11 is worth more than subject revision in three.

sections.heading: The IGCSE two years as a calendar, from option choices to the review window
paragraphs: Laid out as dates rather than as years, the IGCSE route is a sequence of decisions with different amounts of slack behind each. Some of them, like the option choices, have consequences that last four years and get five minutes of thought. Others, like the review-of-results deadline, are short windows that most families in this district have never been told exist.

The chain runs like this. Options are chosen in Year 9. Teaching runs through Year 10, during which schools gather the internal evidence they will use to judge tier. A provisional tier judgement is often made at the end of Year 10. Entries are finalised by the school's exams office months before the series. Mocks are sat, usually on real past papers. A run-in follows. The series happens, by zone for Cambridge candidates. Results are issued. A review-of-results route opens with a deadline. And a November series sits as a second attempt in the same calendar year.

Knowing where you are in that chain is the single most useful thing before buying tutoring, because it tells you what is still available to change. In Year 10, the tier is open and the foundations can be rebuilt. In the autumn of Year 11, the entry may still be adjustable and exam technique can be drilled with time to embed. In February of Year 11, the tier is locked and the work is conversion of existing knowledge into marks. In September after results, the question is review or resit, and both have deadlines.

A practical note on the Cambridge zone point, because it catches families out for no reason. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. A timetable found through a search engine is not necessarily the one your child's centre is using. Take it from the exams office.

sections.heading: Year 10 is the year nobody uses, and the only one with real leverage
paragraphs: Year 10 feels like a year with time in it, which is exactly why it passes without intervention. Nothing has gone wrong yet. There is no mock to react to. The examinations are eighteen months away and a family naturally defers spending. The consequence is that almost all IGCSE tutoring in this district is bought in the final six months, at the point of least leverage and highest price per unit of effect.

What Year 10 can do that Year 11 cannot is change the entry. A school's tier judgement rests on internal evidence gathered across the year, and that evidence is still being created. A student whose algebra becomes secure by the spring of Year 10 presents differently in that judgement from one whose algebra is still shaky, and the difference is a grade ceiling. That is not a marginal effect. Moving from a lower tier to a higher one changes the maximum grade available, and no amount of Year 11 revision does that.

The second thing Year 10 allows is rebuilding rather than patching. A student who has never been secure on fractions in algebra, or who has never learned to plan a piece of extended writing, or who cannot state what a gradient physically represents, has a foundation problem. Foundation problems respond to slow, repeated work across months and respond poorly to intensive blocks. In Year 11 there is no time for the slow version, so the patch is applied and it holds unevenly under pressure.

The third is past papers as a habit rather than as an event. Introduced from the second term of Year 10 at a rate of one every few weeks, past papers become ordinary and the student learns the mark scheme's language gradually. Introduced in March of Year 11, they arrive as a verdict and frequently damage confidence at the worst moment. The same material, differently timed, produces a different student. Our recommendation to Karama families with a Year 10 student is simple: one subject, one standing hour, the subject that is genuinely behind - not three subjects, and not later.

sections.heading: The entry, the tier and the ceiling nobody mentions
paragraphs: Entries are made by your child's school months before the papers are sat, and the entry fixes four things: the board, the syllabus code, the series and the tier. The first three determine which past papers are the right ones. The fourth determines the maximum grade available, and it is the one families most often do not know has been decided.

Both major boards tier several subjects. Cambridge splits into Core and Extended; Pearson splits into Foundation, covering grades 5 to 1, and Higher, covering 9 to 4 with an allowed grade 3. A student entered on the lower tier cannot be awarded above that tier's ceiling however well they perform. If the family's target grade sits above the ceiling, the target is unreachable and anybody selling hours against it is selling something that cannot be delivered.

Schools make these decisions for defensible reasons. A student placed on a tier beyond their current reach risks coming away with nothing at all, and a secure grade on the lower tier is sometimes the better outcome. The issue is communication rather than judgement: parents frequently discover the tier after the fact. Ask explicitly, in writing, which tier each tiered subject is entered for, what the ceiling is, what evidence the decision rested on, and whether and when it could be reviewed. All four are reasonable questions and a department can answer them.

There is one more entry detail worth knowing for science specifically, because it changes how the practical component is prepared. Cambridge schools choose between entering a laboratory practical test and an alternative-to-practical written paper. Those are prepared for differently - the written paper tests experimental reasoning on paper, the practical test requires performance in a laboratory. Ask which one is entered, because tutoring aimed at the wrong one is aimed at nothing.

sections.heading: Mock season, and why the script matters more than the grade
paragraphs: Mocks are the pivot of Year 11 and most families extract about a tenth of the available value from them. A mock grade comes home, it is better or worse than hoped, and the family reacts to the number. The number is the least informative part. Mocks are usually sat on real past papers, which means the marked script is a precise record of where this student loses marks on this board's questions under timed conditions - and those are the same losses that will recur in the series.

So the request to make, immediately and politely, is for the script. Not the grade, not a percentage, the paper itself with the marker's annotations. With it, a first tutoring session can produce a ranked list of mark losses in forty minutes. Without it, that session is spent reconstructing information the department already had in December, which is an expensive way to begin.

What the scripts reliably show across this district is that mark losses cluster into a small number of mechanical faults rather than spreading evenly across topics. Answering the wrong command word - describing when asked to explain. Making four creditable points on a six-mark question. Omitting units. Not showing working, so no method marks are available. Abandoning a question entirely rather than attempting it for partial credit. Running out of time through poor triage. Those six account for a large share of the gap between what a student knows and what they score, and all six are fixable in weeks rather than months.

One honest caveat about mock marks. Ask which topics had not yet been taught at the time of the mock, because a low mark on untaught content is not a diagnosis. Ask also whether the mock was marked to the real scheme or generously, since a generously marked mock conceals the very losses the exercise exists to reveal. Both are reasonable questions and both change how the script should be read.

sections.heading: Eight weeks, nine subjects: how triage actually works
paragraphs: The arithmetic of a Year 11 run-in is unforgiving and it is better faced than finessed. A student sitting nine or ten subjects has perhaps eight to twelve usable weeks of concentrated revision and cannot buy tutoring in all of them. Anyone who offers to cover nine subjects in that window is selling hours rather than a plan. Triage is the only honest approach, and the criterion is marks recoverable per hour spent.

That criterion produces a counter-intuitive order. The first thing to work on is not the weakest subject; it is the mechanical faults that recur across every subject, because one block on command words, mark allocation, showing working and question triage improves nine papers rather than one. Two or three sessions there typically returns more than the same hours spent on a single subject's content, and it is the cheapest intervention in the entire two years.

Second comes the subject with the largest gap between what the student knows and what they scored, which is not the same as the subject with the lowest mark. A student who scored badly in a subject they have barely been taught has a content gap that eight weeks will not fill. A student who scored badly in a subject they understand has a conversion problem, and conversion problems move fast. The mock scripts tell you which is which.

Third, and only if time genuinely remains, comes content repair in one subject - the two highest-cost topics, taught through past-paper questions rather than through notes so the student meets the material in the examiner's form. The final fortnight gets nothing new at all. Introducing unfamiliar content to a student two weeks out reliably destabilises what they already knew, and we will decline to do it even when asked.

sections.heading: Results day, the review window and the November decision
paragraphs: Results day is treated as a verdict and is actually a decision point with two routes out of it, both time-limited. Families in Karama are rarely told about either, and both have deadlines short enough that the finding-out has to happen on results day rather than a fortnight later.

The first is a review of results. Both boards operate a route by which a centre can request that a candidate's marking be reviewed, within a deadline the board sets, and the request goes through the school rather than through the family directly. It is not a free second chance and it is not appropriate for every disappointing grade - it is appropriate where a grade sits oddly against everything else the student produced. The action on results day is simply to ask the exams office what the deadline is and what the school's process for requesting one is. That question costs nothing and the window closes quickly.

The second is the November series, which functions as a same-calendar-year second attempt. For Pearson International GCSE, the November final timetable has run from late October to 19 November, with results reaching students in January - November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. For Cambridge, November is the resit route for UAE centres. June results reached Pearson centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, which gives a sense of how little time sits between results and the November entry deadline.

Whether to take November is a genuine decision. In favour: a fresh grade before sixth-form or university applications harden, a short highly focused period of work, and a student who now knows what the paper feels like. Against: January results can sit awkwardly against application timelines, the student is simultaneously starting a new course, and - the big one - a resit with unchanged revision tends to reproduce the original grade. If November is used, the work has to start from evidence: the script where the school can obtain it, or a fresh timed paper diagnosed properly in the first fortnight.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the shortened day and a run-in that survives it
paragraphs: A revision plan that ignores the UAE academic calendar looks fine on paper and fails in practice. Two features matter for Karama families. The first is the ordinary school week, which in a Dubai private school carries mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies alongside the licensed international curriculum. Instructional time for those is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises a minimum of 25 minutes for any mandatory subject lesson. Those hours sit in a week that already has nine or ten IGCSE subjects in it.

The second is Ramadan, which in some years falls inside the Year 11 run-in. School days shorten, household routines change, and a fixed 5pm session that worked in January often will not hold. The failure mode is predictable: a family tries to keep the slot, misses two weeks, reschedules twice, and loses a third of a short programme. The answer is to agree in advance that the slot moves for that period - frequently to a later post-Iftar time - rather than renegotiating weekly.

Then there is the Karama afternoon itself. Students here commonly attend schools in Bur Dubai or Oud Metha, sometimes across the creek, and the return journey at five o'clock varies. Choosing the session time against the worst realistic commute rather than the best one is the most useful local decision a family makes during a run-in, because in an eight-week programme a session lost is more than a tenth of the plan.

The last practical point is the room. Karama flats generally have one quiet surface and often several children who need it. Staggering session times across siblings does more good than finding a better tutor at a worse hour, and an online session that can run in a bedroom with headphones leaves the shared table free for somebody else. These are small things that compound across a revision term, and they are worth deciding deliberately in week one rather than improvising in week five.

sections.heading: What IGCSE support costs across the two years, counted honestly
paragraphs: Karama households are price-sensitive and well informed, so here are the published market figures with their sources rather than a range we made up. All were read in October 2026 from each provider's own pages, and none of them are IB Gram prices.

At the budget end, Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, which buys homework supervision rather than examination coaching. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 an hour. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table places IGCSE, IB and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above; TutorChase publishes AED 270; BartyED sits at AED 650 for premium named tutors. In-home one-to-one visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent home tutors. Monthly, Bestimate estimates a weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work, with packages advertised around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Now count the two years rather than the hour, because that is the decision a family is actually making. A standing weekly hour in one subject through Year 10 at the mid band is a predictable monthly commitment and it is the version with the most leverage. A Year 11 run-in in two subjects, at the specialist band, over ten weeks, is a shorter and larger number. Both together, in one subject, is usually cheaper than three subjects crammed into the final term and reliably more effective. The expensive pattern is the common one: nothing in Year 10, then three subjects from February.

For household context rather than tutoring context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package, valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. We publish no rate card on this page, hold no office or centre in the UAE, and claim no approval or accreditation from KHDA, Cambridge International, Pearson or anyone else. Two questions for any provider including us: is the rate per hour or per lesson, and what happens if you stop after one session.

sections.heading: A tutor in a Karama flat against one-to-one online, with a date fixed
paragraphs: We are not going to dismiss the in-home case, because in a Karama apartment it has real arguments behind it. A tutor in the room removes a journey, makes the hour visible, and means a younger child does not have to be left. Plenty of families here use that arrangement and it works for them.

Our position is stated before anyone pays rather than after: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we provide only in India. Every lesson for a Karama family is one-to-one over live video. We put that on the page because two providers ranking for these searches route UAE parents to overseas phone numbers without disclosing where the tutor actually sits, and a family should not discover that at the end of a billing month.

With a fixed examination date, the argument for online is mostly about reliability and supply. Reliability first: an eight-week run-in has no spare weeks. A session lost because the tutor is stuck on the creek crossing is more than a tenth of the programme, and that risk exists only in the travel-based model. The fixed hour holds, and a student who gets home late joins late instead of missing the lesson. During exam season, a slot that reliably happens is worth more than a nominally better tutor whose arrival time varies.

Supply second. A specialist in a particular syllabus code and tier - Cambridge 0607, Pearson 4MB1, a coordinated science route, a Cambridge alternative-to-practical paper - is defined by the examination rather than by geography. Insisting on physical proximity narrows the pool to whoever can reach a Karama address and is free at the right hour, which for a specific code often means accepting a generalist. And the market data shows what the in-home premium buys: rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, against AED 150 to 450 online. The difference is paying for a drive.

sections.heading: Equivalency, the regulator and the permit a parent can verify
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. In 2024-25 the sector was 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of students and Indian at 26 per cent. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools - four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate - creating 16,846 new places.

On equivalency, which is why the number of subjects entered matters: the Ministry of Education's British track requires a student to pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and to show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject requirement; the sourced figure is five. Verify your own case through the Ministry's own channel - we describe the process, do not perform it, and tutoring is not a requirement of it.

Across the other emirates the regulator differs, which matters for families who may move. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority. Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so the regulator's role is broader than inspection in those emirates.

On permits, the facts are checkable by any parent. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and states a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published officially, no amount should be quoted to you. We also do not reproduce or distribute Cambridge or Pearson past papers, mark schemes or syllabus documents as downloads; we cite them and link out.
