process.title: Locate yourself on the two-year map
process.description: Year 10, autumn of Year 11, spring of Year 11, or after results. That answer decides whether the tier is open, whether a mock script exists, and whether a review or resit window is in play. Everything else follows, and getting it wrong wastes the first paid hour.

process.title: Get the entry details in writing
process.description: Board, syllabus code, tier and series for each tiered subject, and - for Cambridge sciences - which practical route is entered. Five short answers from the exams office that determine which past papers are right and whether a target grade is even available.

process.title: Ask for the mock script, not the grade
process.description: Mocks usually use real past papers, so the annotated script is the best diagnostic of the two years. Ask also which topics were untaught at the time and whether marking was to the real scheme, because both change how the script should be read.

process.title: A free trial that produces a ranked list
process.description: One session at no cost with the tutor you would continue with, worked on a question from the correct code and marked against the official scheme. You get a written note of where marks actually went, ranked by size, whether or not you book anything further.

process.title: Fix the hour against the Karama afternoon
process.description: Choose a slot that survives a bad commute rather than a good one, stagger it against siblings needing the same table, and agree in advance that it shifts during Ramadan. Al Mankhool and Oud Metha can often hold 4pm; Karama around five; Deira-side after six. Times are Gulf Standard Time.

process.title: Check the deadlines on results day
process.description: On the morning results arrive, ask the exams office two things: the review-of-results deadline and the November entry deadline. Both windows are short, both go through the school, and a family that waits a fortnight to ask has usually lost one of them.

whyPoints.title: We tell you where the leverage is, even when it has passed
whyPoints.description: Year 10 is the only period in which the tier is open and foundations can be rebuilt. If you arrive in February of Year 11 we will say plainly that the work is conversion of knowledge into marks, not a change of ceiling, because selling the other thing would be dishonest.

whyPoints.title: Triage, not coverage
whyPoints.description: Nine subjects cannot be revised in eight weeks and anybody offering to is selling hours. We rank by marks recoverable per hour, which usually puts mechanical faults first because one block there improves every paper at once rather than one.

whyPoints.title: The script before the topic list
whyPoints.description: A mock script marked against the real scheme shows where marks go in forty minutes. Starting from a conversation about which topics feel hard usually locates the problem in the wrong place, and in a short run-in that is an expensive detour.

whyPoints.title: Honest about grade ceilings
whyPoints.description: If the entry is Core or Foundation and the target sits above the ceiling, the target is unreachable and we will say so. Where the tier is still open, we aim the work at the specific gap the department is worried about, because changing an entry is worth more than any revision.

whyPoints.title: Clear about where the tutor sits
whyPoints.description: The URL says home tutor because that is what parents search, and the honest answer is that IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Every lesson here is one-to-one over live video, stated before payment rather than discovered afterwards.

whyPoints.title: Figures attributed, claims absent
whyPoints.description: Each AED range names the provider that published it and the month it was read. We publish no satisfaction percentage, star rating or tutor count, hold no UAE premises, and claim no approval from KHDA, Cambridge International or Pearson.

faqs.question: When in the two IGCSE years is tutoring most worth buying?
faqs.answer: Year 10, and almost nobody does it then because nothing has gone wrong yet. Year 10 is the only period in which the school's tier judgement is still open, so work there can change the grade ceiling rather than operate inside it. It is also the only time a foundation problem can be rebuilt slowly rather than patched under pressure, and the only time past papers can be introduced gradually instead of arriving as a verdict. One subject, one standing hour, the subject genuinely behind.

faqs.question: What is a review of results and how do we request one?
faqs.answer: Both boards operate a route by which a centre can ask for a candidate's marking to be reviewed, within a deadline the board sets, and the request goes through the school rather than the family. It is not a free second chance and it is not right for every disappointing grade - it suits a grade that sits oddly against everything else a student produced. The action to take is on results day itself: ask the exams office what the deadline is and what the school's process is, because the window is short.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE series will a student in Karama sit?
faqs.answer: June and November. Cambridge runs June as the main series with November as the resit route for UAE centres, and Pearson International GCSE is available in May/June and November. The February and March series that appears in searches is offered to India only and does not apply here. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, stating it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, so take the timetable from the exams office rather than from a search result.

faqs.question: Can my child change tier after the entry has been made?
faqs.answer: Usually not, which is why the question has to be asked earlier than families ask it. The entry fixes the tier and the tier sets a hard ceiling on the grade available - Cambridge Core against Extended, Pearson Foundation covering grades 5 to 1 against Higher covering 9 to 4 with an allowed 3. Ask the department in writing which tier each tiered subject is entered for, what the ceiling is, what evidence the decision rested on, and whether it can be reviewed. Those are all fair questions.

faqs.question: What should we ask for after the Year 11 mocks?
faqs.answer: Three things. The annotated script for each subject, because mocks are usually sat on real past papers and the losses on them are the losses that will recur. Which topics had not yet been taught when the mock was sat, so a low mark on untaught content is not misread as a weakness. And whether the paper was marked to the real scheme or generously, since generous marking conceals exactly the mechanical losses the exercise exists to expose. All three change how the script should be read.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we buy tutoring in for the final term?
faqs.answer: One, usually, plus a short block on mechanical faults that applies to all of them. Nine or ten subjects cannot be revised in eight weeks and anybody offering to cover them is selling hours. The ranking we use is marks recoverable per hour, which puts command words, mark allocation, showing working and question triage first, because two or three sessions there improves every paper rather than one. Then the subject with the biggest gap between what the student knows and what they scored.

faqs.question: Is a November IGCSE resit a good idea?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the decision has to be made within days of August results because the November entry deadline sits well before the series. In favour: a fresh grade before sixth-form applications harden and a short focused period with a clear target. Against: results reach students in January, which can sit awkwardly against application timelines, and a resit with unchanged revision tends to reproduce the original grade. If you take it, start from the script or a fresh diagnosed paper rather than from more of the same.

faqs.question: Why does my child know the material but score poorly?
faqs.answer: Because knowing and scoring are different skills, and the gap is usually mechanical. The recurring losses across this district are answering the wrong command word - describing when asked to explain - making four creditable points on a six-mark question, omitting units, not showing working so no method marks are available, abandoning questions rather than attempting them for partial credit, and running out of time through poor triage. None are content problems, all are fixable in weeks, and one block addresses them across every subject.

faqs.question: Do you send an IGCSE tutor to our flat in Karama?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every lesson for a Karama family is one-to-one over live video, stated before you pay. With an examination date fixed the online format is genuinely safer: an eight-week run-in has no spare weeks, and a session lost because a tutor is stuck on the creek crossing is more than a tenth of the plan. That risk only exists in the travel-based model.

faqs.question: How much does IGCSE tutoring cost across the two years in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Count the commitment rather than the hour. Market rates read in October 2026: Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 an hour, Bestimate's Dubai table places specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase publishes AED 270, and the budget end runs AED 33 to 65 with Tutopiya and EdFlik. Bestimate estimates a weekly hour at AED 600 to 1,200 a month mid-market. A Year 10 standing hour in one subject plus a Year 11 run-in in that subject is usually cheaper and more effective than three subjects from February.

faqs.question: How should an IGCSE revision plan handle Ramadan?
faqs.answer: By agreeing in advance that the session time moves for that period rather than renegotiating weekly. School days shorten and household routines change, so a fixed 5pm slot that worked in January often will not hold, and families who try to keep it typically lose two or three weeks of a short programme to repeated rescheduling. A later post-Iftar slot, agreed before the period begins, protects the hours. Dubai timetables also carry mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies throughout.

faqs.question: Does the Year 9 option choice really matter that much?
faqs.answer: More than it gets credit for. It decides how many IGCSE grades a student will finish with and which sixth-form routes stay open, and in science it is where the triple, double or single award decision is made. It also interacts with Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, which requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE passes at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count. One deliberate conversation at the time prevents a shortfall discovered after results day.

faqs.question: Our flat has one table and three children. How do we make a run-in work?
faqs.answer: Stagger the sessions rather than hunting for a better tutor at a worse hour. An online lesson needs a device and headphones and can run in a bedroom, which leaves the shared surface free for whoever is not in a session. Decide the week's shape deliberately in the first week of the run-in rather than improvising in the fifth, and choose each slot against the worst realistic commute rather than the best one. These sound minor and they compound across an exam term.

faqs.question: Can my child sit IGCSEs as a private candidate from Karama?
faqs.answer: Yes, through an approved examination centre rather than through us. Private-candidate entry is a separate route from a school entry with its own arrangements, deadlines and centre requirements, and it is what a student uses when they are no longer enrolled at the school that would have entered them. We teach and we do not administer entries or act as a centre. Start with the current school's exams office, or contact an approved Cambridge or Pearson centre in Dubai directly to confirm what it accepts and by when.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE tutor working with a Karama family need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and states a two-working-day completion time. Ask any prospective tutor directly. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties, and no official fine schedule is published anywhere.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting IGCSE tutoring three weeks before the papers?
faqs.answer: With a narrow brief, sometimes. Three weeks will not repair a subject and should not try. What it can do is drill the mechanical mark-losers - command words, mark allocation, showing working, units, question triage - and run two or three full timed papers to build stamina. For a student who knows the content and is leaking marks, that is a real effect. If the content genuinely is not there, we will say so rather than take the booking, and introducing new material at that point does more harm than good.

intro.heading: Every IGCSE decision has a closing date, and most families meet them in the wrong order
paragraphs: The IGCSE years look open-ended and are not. A series of decisions close one after another, each quietly limiting what the next can achieve, and a family who learns about them in order does far better than one who meets them as surprises. Tier is decided in Year 10. The entry, with its syllabus codes, is lodged months before the papers. The timetable belongs to one of six Cambridge administrative zones. Results arrive at a fixed point and the resit entry closes before the previous result has been fully digested.

Almost nobody searching for a tutor from Dubai Knowledge Park is thinking about that sequence. They are thinking about a mock paper that came home last week. That is entirely reasonable, and it is also why the first useful thing a tutor can do is establish where in the sequence the family actually is, because it determines what the money can buy. Sixteen weeks before the papers, content repair is sensible. Eight weeks out, content has to be rationed to two topics. Four weeks out, adding new material is harmful rather than merely inefficient.

There is also a quieter sequence running alongside the official one, which is the household's own. Mock weeks for two children in two different schools rarely align. Public holidays and school activity weeks eat into any block booked by the calendar month. Ramadan moves school hours for several weeks and often lands close to a mock series. None of that appears on a board timetable, and all of it determines how many sessions a family can genuinely sustain, which is why we subtract it before agreeing a number rather than discovering it in week five.

Dubai Knowledge Park sits in Al Sufouh, a free zone built around universities and training institutes, bordered by Dubai Internet City and Dubai Media City, with the tram along its edge. Families searching from here live in Al Sufouh, The Greens, The Views, Barsha Heights, the Marina and JBR, and the Year 10 and 11 students among them attend British-curriculum schools in Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and along the coast. The afternoon return coincides with the free zones emptying, which matters to any arrangement that depends on somebody travelling.

On that point we are direct, because the search phrase deserves a direct answer. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. We teach one-to-one, online, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. In a revision block built around fixed dates, the format matters mainly through reliability: sixteen sessions booked is only worth something if sixteen sessions happen, and an online slot has to survive the household rather than the road.

The rest of this page is the calendar in detail, the entry and results milestones for both boards, what the market charges, and what a family should settle before buying anything. It also says plainly what we do not do: we do not enter candidates, we hold no board or regulator approval, and we do not perform Ministry equivalency.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-knowledge-park.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects most requested from this corridor, with the code that decides which past papers matter and a note on where the grade is actually won.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.description: The most requested subject here. Non-calculator fluency matters on Cambridge; rounding and interpretation matter more on Pearson, where a calculator is allowed throughout.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Formula rearrangement, standard form and gradients read from a drawn line. A physics problem is usually an algebra problem in costume.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Method selection in calculations, plus balanced equations and state symbols, which are marked as right or wrong rather than as presentation.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: Terminology precision and long answers containing as many distinct points as the mark allocation demands. Point-counting is the fastest recoverable gain.

subjects.name: English Language (0500 / 0990)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the reading responses. Students lose marks by writing well in the wrong register rather than by writing badly.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: A different qualification from First Language with different papers. Confirm which one is on the entry, because the preparation diverges sharply.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and precise definitions. The data-response paper rewards brevity, and strong writers often run out of time by over-explaining.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Break-even, ratio and cash-flow questions are examined arithmetic, and a numerate student can lift this grade quickly by treating them as free marks.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode, trace tables and the theory paper. Students who code confidently still lose marks on the written conventions the mark scheme expects.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Early calculus and trigonometric identities, taken alongside the main grade. Worth it once the main grade is secure, and a liability before that.

sections.heading: The IGCSE calendar as a sequence of doors that close
paragraphs: The useful way to see the two IGCSE years is not as a syllabus to be covered but as a series of decisions, each with a point after which it cannot be revisited. Families who understand the sequence make different and better choices, mostly by acting earlier and more cheaply. Families who meet the decisions as surprises end up buying intensive support to compensate for a decision that was made by default months before.

The first door is tier. Cambridge separate sciences and mathematics are entered at Core or Extended, and Pearson mathematics at Foundation or Higher. The department usually decides from set performance during Year 10, and Extended or Higher is what the top grades require. Once the entry is lodged the question changes from which tier to how to get the best from this tier, which is a smaller conversation with a lower ceiling.

The second door is the subject combination, including whether sciences are sat as separates or as a double award. That decision shapes post-16 options, and it is made early. The third is the entry itself, with its syllabus codes, lodged months before the papers. The fourth is the zone-correct timetable, which is administrative and consequential: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one.

The table below sets out these decisions with who makes each one and what a parent should do before it closes. Nothing in it requires knowing any subject content. All of it requires asking the school a specific question at a specific time, which is why the right-hand column is written as an action rather than as information.

sections.heading: Entries, results and the resit window, for both boards
paragraphs: Entry deadlines sit months ahead of papers and results arrive months afterwards, which is why the practical calendar is longer than the examination window. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. For a UAE candidate those are the windows that exist. The Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only, and any date attached to it should be disregarded by a Dubai family.

Pearson's published pattern gives a sense of the real shape of a year. Its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series, which is precisely why any table on a page like this should be treated as a shape rather than as a schedule: the live official timetable is the document to work from.

The resit arithmetic is the part most families have not considered. If a summer result is disappointing, the November entry has to be lodged within weeks, while the script has not yet been seen and the decision is being made under emotional pressure. The better approach is to have the conversation in the spring: ask the examinations officer when the November entry closes, ask what the process is for obtaining a copy of a script, and decide in advance what evidence would justify a resit. That turns an August scramble into a decision.

One further caution. Where a post-16 place, a school transfer or a Ministry equivalency application depends on a particular grade, the binding deadline is usually the receiving institution's rather than the board's. Ask them in writing what they will accept and by when. A resit that arrives after the deadline it was meant to satisfy has cost a term for nothing, and this happens more often than it should.

sections.heading: Why a dated plan and a travelling tutor pull against each other
paragraphs: A revision block is a promise about a number of sessions. Eight weeks at two sessions a week is sixteen appointments, and the plan assumes all sixteen happen, because each one was allocated to something specific. In an open-ended arrangement a missed session is an inconvenience. In a dated plan it is a hole, and the hole cannot be filled later because later is already allocated.

That is where the home-tutor format struggles in this part of Dubai, and it is a logistics argument rather than a quality one. A tutor driving to Al Sufouh, Barsha Heights or the Marina in the late afternoon is travelling at the hour the free zones empty. Some evenings that is fifteen minutes and some evenings it is forty. A tutor who arrives late has consumed part of a session that was paid for whole, and a tutor who cannot come at all has removed a week from a plan with no spare weeks in it.

The cost difference points the same way and is easier to quantify. Published Dubai rates put in-home one-to-one visits at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the fee, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. Monthly packages run about AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits and around AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those figures come from published provider pages and the Bestimate Dubai rate table. They are the market rather than our price list.

We should be clear about where this argument does not apply. For a younger child who needs an adult beside them, presence has value that a screen does not fully replace, and we do not sell that format in the UAE at all. For a Year 11 student working to a fixed date with a specific subject gap, the things that decide the outcome are the tutor's experience of that syllabus and the number of sessions that actually happen. Both of those favour working on screen, and the table sets out why.

sections.heading: What eight weeks can do, and what it cannot
paragraphs: The honest answer to the question every Year 11 parent asks is that eight weeks changes technique reliably and content partially. The marks lost to instruction-reading, rounding, unfinished method and pacing are recoverable in that window, and on most marked mock papers they are the largest single category. The marks lost to three years of missing algebra are not, and a tutor who implies otherwise is selling rather than teaching.

What that means in practice is rationing. Two topics get taught properly and the rest of the time goes to whole papers under time and the elimination of repeated errors. Choosing which two topics is the week-one job, and it is done by categorising every lost mark on a marked paper rather than by asking the student which topics feel hard. Students systematically name the topics they dislike rather than the ones costing marks, and the two lists overlap less than anyone expects.

The mid-block review is the other thing that makes eight weeks work. A second paper is sat and marked at week four, the error tally is compared with week one, and the plan either continues or changes. If the pattern has not moved, something is wrong with the approach or the match and both are fixable at week four in a way they are not at week seven. If the realistic conclusion is that the target needs the November series instead, week four is when that can still be acted on.

Four weeks is a different proposition again. At that point introducing new content displaces revision of material the student half-knows, which is where the recoverable marks actually are. The work is error elimination, pacing, and settling the order in which each paper will be attempted. Students resist that and it is the rule that most reliably protects a grade, so it is worth agreeing in advance rather than arguing about in the final fortnight.

sections.heading: Ramadan, holidays and the shape of the Dubai school year
paragraphs: A revision calendar in Dubai has to accommodate features a generic plan does not. Ramadan shifts school hours for several weeks each year, and for a Year 11 student those weeks frequently sit close to a mock series or inside a revision block. The workable adjustment is fewer and shorter sessions moved to the late morning or the post-Iftar window, with lighter work set between them, agreed before the month begins rather than improvised through it.

The long summer break and the winter holiday both sit immediately before high-stakes terms, which makes them the most undervalued weeks in the year. Short daily sessions across two or three weeks of a holiday hold better than one long weekly session during term, because nothing is competing for the student's attention. For families travelling out of Dubai, an online arrangement simply follows them, which is the one clear scheduling advantage of the format that nobody disputes.

There is also a household-level calendar worth mapping. Where two children are in different schools, as is common in this corridor, the mock weeks rarely align, and a household cannot realistically sustain two intensive schedules in the same fortnight. Planning around the busier child's calendar rather than pretending both are flexible avoids the usual outcome, which is that the quieter child's sessions are the ones that get cancelled.

Finally, the national and school holiday calendar should be read before a block is booked rather than after. An eight-week block that contains a week of public holidays and a week of school trips is a six-week block being sold as eight. We check this at the planning stage and adjust the session count rather than discovering it in week five, which is a small piece of administration that changes how honest the plan is.

sections.heading: Equivalency: what the five subjects have to be
paragraphs: Families in Dubai planning for UAE university entry eventually meet the Ministry of Education equivalency requirements, and the IGCSE grades feed directly into them. For the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among the five required subjects.

That last point is worth repeating because one ranking competitor publishes a six-subject figure, which does not match the published rule, and a parent planning a subject combination on the wrong number may take a decision they cannot reverse. The practical consequence for a Year 10 family is to check the combination against the requirement while it is still changeable, which is the same window in which the tier decision sits.

For the American track the published requirements are different in kind: English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test. No International Baccalaureate points threshold appears in the source we rely on, so no IB equivalency figure should be published without a reading from the Ministry's own site, and we leave that gap rather than filling it with a number.

Equivalency is a regulatory process that IB Gram does not perform, influence or guarantee. We describe it, point you at the official channel, and would rather be the page that tells you where to check than the page that asks you to take its word. Nothing here should be read as implying that tutoring is required for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression; it is not, and a provider suggesting otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process.

sections.heading: Permits, limits and what we do not claim
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is lawful and regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with the application made through its smart app, website and e-services system. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published, any specific amount you see should be treated as unverified.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from Cambridge, Pearson, the International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education, and no page on this site will imply one. We operate no office, centre or branch in the UAE. We do not enter candidates for examinations, we do not perform Ministry equivalency, and we do not offer home visits anywhere in the Emirates. A tutoring operation with premises in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute; we hold none because we have no premises.

On materials, we reference and link official syllabus, specimen and timetable documents rather than reproducing them, and we do not supply board-owned papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Your child's school has legitimate access through its own subscriptions. On figures, every number on this page carries a source, and we publish no success rates, satisfaction scores or star ratings, because we could not produce the data behind any of them.

Private schools in Dubai are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are regulated by ADEK, Sharjah by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah by the federal Ministry of Education. Inspection reports live on the regulator's own site, and that is where to read them rather than in anybody's summary.

process.title: Establish where in the sequence you are
process.description: Year group, the series your child is entered for, and roughly how many weeks remain. That tells us whether content repair is still sensible, whether the plan has to ration topics, or whether the only useful work left is error elimination and pacing. It also tells us what not to sell you, which is the part most enquiries never reach.

process.title: Get the codes, the tier and the timetable
process.description: One email to the examinations officer asking for the syllabus codes on the entry, the tier, and the zone-correct Cambridge timetable where it applies. Those three facts determine which past papers are useful and remove the largest source of wasted revision time in this qualification.

process.title: Send a marked mock paper
process.description: The marked script rather than the grade. Twenty minutes with it shows whether marks are going to instruction-reading, unfinished method, a genuine content gap or simply to questions never reached, and those four lead to four different plans. We categorise every lost mark rather than counting them.

process.title: Agree a written plan with the holidays counted
process.description: Two priority topics named in writing, whole papers scheduled from the midpoint, nothing new in the final fortnight, and the public and school holidays subtracted from the session count before anyone agrees a number. An eight-week block containing two holiday weeks is a six-week block, and saying so up front is the difference between a plan and a sales document.

process.title: Review at week four on marked evidence
process.description: A second paper, marked, with the error tally compared against week one. If the pattern has not moved we change the approach or the tutor rather than defending either. If the honest conclusion is that the target needs the November series, that is said at week four while the entry decision is still open.

whyPoints.title: The calendar is treated as fact, not as background
whyPoints.description: UAE candidates sit June and November; the Cambridge February and March series is India-only and has no bearing on a Dubai entry. We also insist on the zone-correct timetable from the school, because Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who used the wrong version.

whyPoints.title: Holidays are subtracted before the block is priced
whyPoints.description: An eight-week plan that contains a holiday week and a school trip week is six weeks of teaching. We count that at the planning stage and adjust the session number, which is a small administrative habit that makes the rest of the plan honest.

whyPoints.title: Sessions that do not depend on a car
whyPoints.description: In a dated revision block a lost week cannot be recovered, because later is already allocated. Nothing here is lost to the Al Sufouh evening or the Marina return, which over sixteen appointments matters more than any plausible difference between two competent tutors.

whyPoints.description: This page names Dubai in-home and online bands in dirhams and says who published each figure. Three of six competitor pages in this market publish no price at all. A parent who cannot tell whether a quote is ordinary is negotiating with no information.

whyPoints.title: Topics chosen from a script, not from a conversation
whyPoints.description: Students name the topics they dislike rather than the ones costing marks, and the two lists overlap less than anyone expects. We categorise every lost mark on a marked paper and let the tally choose, which is why the two priority topics are written down and not quietly changed.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what we are not
whyPoints.description: A tutor-matching platform with no board or regulator approval, no UAE premises, and no home-visit service in the Emirates. We do not enter candidates or perform equivalency. Where this page names a regulator it explains what that body does and links its own site.

faqs.question: When does the tier decision for IGCSE actually close?
faqs.answer: In practice during Year 10, when the department allocates sets and decides which students will be entered at Core or Extended, or at Foundation or Higher on Pearson mathematics. Many families only discover the tier when a Year 11 mock timetable arrives, by which point the entry is lodged. If your child is aiming at A Level or Diploma study afterwards, raise it early in Year 10 and ask the specific question: what would need to improve for a higher tier entry to be considered? That answer is a work plan, and it is far cheaper than rescuing a capped grade later.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send IGCSE tutors to homes in Dubai Knowledge Park?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family address is something we do only in India. IGCSE support for this corridor is delivered one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time. In a dated revision block the format matters mainly through reliability: sixteen booked sessions are only worth something if sixteen happen, and an online slot has to survive the household rather than the Al Sufouh evening traffic. You also select from everyone who has taught that syllabus code rather than from those who can drive to you.

faqs.question: How far ahead of the papers does the IGCSE entry close?
faqs.answer: Months, which surprises most families. The entry carries the syllabus codes and the tier, and it is lodged by the centre well before the series opens. That is why the single most useful email a parent can send is to the examinations officer, asking for the codes and the tier in writing. Everything downstream depends on it: which past papers are worth sitting, how much content exists, and whether practical skills are examined by a test or a written alternative. A student revising on the wrong board's papers is working hard in the wrong dialect.

faqs.question: What is a Cambridge timetable zone and why should a parent care?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the examination timetable. Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. The practical point is that a timetable found through an internet search is not a timetable. Ask the school for the version that applies to your centre, keep it, and check any date you are relying on against it rather than against a revision website.

faqs.question: For a Knowledge Park family, when is the right moment to weigh up a November resit?
faqs.answer: In the spring, not in August. Summer results arrive late in the month and the November entry closes within weeks, which means the decision gets made under time pressure and before anyone has seen the script. The better sequence is to ask the examinations officer in the spring when the November entry closes and how a copy of a script can be obtained, then agree in advance what evidence would justify a resit. Where a post-16 place or an equivalency application depends on a grade, ask the receiving institution in writing what they will accept and by when.

faqs.question: What can an eight-week IGCSE block realistically recover, and what is out of reach?
faqs.answer: It reliably recovers marks lost to technique: instruction-reading, rounding, unfinished method and pacing, which on most marked mock papers is the largest single category. It does not rebuild three years of missing algebra, and a tutor who implies otherwise is selling. The honest process is a full paper sat and marked in week one, every lost mark categorised, two priority topics named, and a second marked paper at week four to check whether the pattern has moved. No tutor can promise a grade, and the week-four evidence is what an honest recommendation rests on.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE support cost for a family near the Al Sufouh free zones?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates put a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and an IGCSE specialist at about AED 200 to 450 or more. In-home visits are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour because the journey sits inside the fee, with monthly packages around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits and about AED 799 for eight online sessions. Monthly estimates from the Bestimate Dubai table run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 in the mid band. Those are market figures with sources, not our price list.

faqs.question: How do public holidays and school trips affect a revision block?
faqs.answer: They shorten it, and almost nobody counts them before agreeing a number of sessions. An eight-week block containing a week of public holidays and a week of school activities is six weeks of teaching being sold as eight, and the shortfall usually appears in week five as a sense that the plan has slipped. We read the school and national calendars at the planning stage and adjust the session count accordingly. It is a small piece of administration and it is the difference between a plan and a hopeful schedule.

faqs.question: Can sessions be rearranged during Ramadan for a Year 11 student?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the sensible version is fewer and shorter sessions rather than the same load pushed later. Dubai schools adjust their hours during Ramadan, and for a Year 11 student those weeks often sit close to a mock series or inside a revision block. Late-morning slots suit students whose day has been compressed; the post-Iftar window suits households that prefer the evening. We agree the revised pattern before the month begins and reduce the work set between sessions, because improvising through it tends to cost the weakest subject first.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subject should we prioritise if time is short?
faqs.answer: The one where a marked paper shows the largest recoverable loss, which is not always the lowest grade. A subject eighteen marks behind with most of those marks lost to technique is a better target than one twelve marks behind where the gap is genuine content, because technique recovers faster. Mathematics is often the highest-leverage choice, since the same weaknesses that cost marks there also damage physics and chemistry calculations. Send one marked paper per subject and we will name the order rather than guessing from grades.

faqs.question: My child says they do not know which topics are weak. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: With a marked paper rather than with the conversation. Students systematically name the topics they dislike rather than the ones costing marks, and the two lists overlap less than anyone expects. Categorising every lost mark on a recent script into content gap, instruction-reading, unfinished method, arithmetic, graph accuracy and timing produces a tally, and the tally chooses the two priority topics. It takes twenty minutes and it prevents a term spent revising the topics that felt uncomfortable rather than the ones that were expensive.

faqs.question: Do holiday blocks work better than weekly term-time sessions?
faqs.answer: For content repair, usually yes. Short daily sessions across two or three weeks of a holiday hold better than one longer session a week during term, because nothing else is competing for the student's attention and the spacing is tighter. The long Dubai summer and the winter break both sit immediately before high-stakes terms, which makes them the most undervalued weeks in the year. Because sessions run online, a family travelling out of Dubai keeps the arrangement, which is the one scheduling advantage of the format that nobody argues with.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the Ministry require for equivalency?
faqs.answer: The published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education not counted among those five, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. One ranking competitor states six subjects, which does not match the published rule. Equivalency is a Ministry process that we do not perform or influence, so verify your own case on the Ministry's own channel, and check the combination in Year 10 while it is still changeable.

faqs.question: What should we ask an IGCSE tutor before booking a revision block?
faqs.answer: Five things. Which syllabus codes and tiers have you taught to examination? How will you mark my child's papers, and against what? What are the two priority topics, and when will they be named? How many sessions are actually in this block once holidays are subtracted? And what will you tell me at week four if it is not working? Clear answers to all five matter more than any single claim about quality, and a provider who cannot answer the fourth has not read the school calendar.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-knowledge-park.closingHeading: Tell us the date, and we will tell you what is still possible
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-knowledge-park.closingBody: IGCSE support is priced by timing more than by anything else. Sixteen weeks out, a weekly session alongside school is enough. Eight weeks out, the plan has to ration content and spend the rest on whole papers. Four weeks out, adding anything new costs more than it returns. Send us the year group, the series, the syllabus codes and a marked mock paper, and we will tell you honestly which of those three you are in, how many sessions a realistic block actually contains once the holidays come out, and what we would not sell you. The trial lesson is free. Everything runs one-to-one, online, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: The cost question, answered before anything else
paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor in LA Mer is quoted at a different price from the same tutor working online, and the gap is not small. Published market rates in Dubai put a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, while a one-to-one in-home visit including travel sits at roughly AED 180 to AED 500. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai rate table gives 180 to 350 for a standard home visit and notes independent home tutors charging 200 to 500. Unitors publishes its IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and its IB tuition from AED 200. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour at the budget end, and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. None of those numbers are ours. They are the market you are shopping in, and the first useful thing a page like this can do is write them down, because three of the six competitor pages researched in October 2026 publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars.

The second useful thing is to say what the premium buys. On a LA Mer address the honest answer is travel. The beachfront strip runs along Jumeirah 1 between the Jumeirah Road and the sea, and a tutor driving in from Al Barsha, Mirdif or Silicon Oasis is absorbing forty minutes each way at six in the evening. That time is priced into the hourly rate whether the invoice itemises it or not. A family paying AED 350 for a 90-minute home session in Jumeirah 1 is paying somewhere around AED 100 of that for a car on the Jumeirah Road, and no part of that AED 100 teaches a child the difference between a Core and an Extended paper.

The third thing is where the money is wasted, which is rarely the hourly rate and almost always the match. A generalist tutor who covers maths, physics and chemistry for Years 7 to 11 will cost less per hour than a Cambridge IGCSE physics specialist, and will cost more per grade, because the Extended paper 4 on 0625 asks for things a generalist has never had to mark. Families in this part of Dubai frequently pay a mid-band rate for eighteen months and discover in February of Year 11 that nobody has ever shown the student a full mark scheme. That is the expensive mistake. The hourly rate is a rounding error next to it.

IB Gram works the other way round. Lessons for UAE families are delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, and the tutor is chosen for the syllabus and the paper rather than for proximity to the Jumeirah coast. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Removing the drive from the equation removes the travel premium from the price and, more importantly, removes the twenty-minute radius from the shortlist. A LA Mer family gets the person who has marked Extended chemistry papers rather than the person who can be parked outside by 5:50pm.

What follows is the detail: the AED bands set out by tier and format, the monthly arithmetic rather than the hourly, a comparison of online against in-home for this specific address, the Cambridge and Pearson calendar counted backwards from results day, what the MoHRE private tutor permit means for whoever you hire, and the honesty line that separates teaching from the essay mills that sell completed coursework in this same search result.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two examined years leading to the certificate most Dubai British schools award at sixteen. Papers are sat in the June and November series. Core and Extended tiering in several Cambridge subjects caps the attainable grade, which makes the tier decision a money decision as much as an academic one.
programmes.countryNote: For MoE equivalency on the British track, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five. One ranking UAE competitor states six subjects are required; the sourced figure is five. Getting this right changes which subjects a LA Mer family pays to support.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE, where Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October. This is the cheapest place to buy a grade, because an hour spent on algebraic fluency in Year 8 does work that no amount of Year 11 revision replicates. Tutoring here is usually one session a week on a single subject rather than an exam-season block.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai families on the Jumeirah coast often arrive mid-stage from another system, and Year 7 to 9 is where a transfer gap shows up without an exam to expose it. Support at this stage is priced at the lower end of the market band because the content is less specialised, which makes it the best value window a family will get before Year 10.

programmes.name: AS and A Level
programmes.description: The post-16 route taken by most students leaving Jumeirah College or Dubai College. Specialist A Level tuition sits in the AED 200 to AED 450 band in published market data, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and premium named tutors reaching AED 650 at BartyED. Modular entry with Pearson and linear entry with Cambridge change the revision plan substantially.
programmes.countryNote: MoE equivalency on the British track also requires one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. That single sourced requirement is worth knowing before a family drops a fourth AS to save a tuition line.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The alternative post-16 route, offered at Jumeira Baccalaureate School and Emirates International School Jumeirah among others. Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level plus the core of Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. IB tuition prices higher than IGCSE across the market, with Unitors from AED 200 against its IGCSE from AED 150.
programmes.countryNote: No IB points threshold for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency has been confirmed on an official source, so this page publishes none. A LA Mer family planning the Diploma should confirm the current requirement with the school's IB coordinator and the Ministry directly rather than take a figure from any tutoring site.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-la-mer.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects LA Mer families request most, with what each one assesses and the place the marks actually go missing. Rates do not vary much by subject in the Dubai market, but the number of hours needed does.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Two written papers, no coursework. Extended reaches grade 9; Core caps at grade 5 on the Cambridge 0580 structure, which makes tier choice the single most consequential decision in the subject. Marks are lost on method presentation in multi-step questions and on the transformation, vectors and histogram topics that sit late in the scheme of work.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Assessed on multiple choice, a theory paper and a practical paper. The practical component rewards students who can describe a method precisely enough for someone else to repeat it. Electricity, and specifically series and parallel reasoning with real component values, is where Extended candidates in Dubai schools shed the most marks.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Three papers including an alternative-to-practical or practical component. Moles arithmetic carries forward through half the syllabus, so a student shaky on relative formula mass in Year 10 is still losing marks in Year 11 organic questions. Qualitative analysis tables are pure recall and are the cheapest marks on the paper to recover.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: Content-heavy and deceptively forgiving until the command terms bite. Students who write everything they know about transport in plants score less than students who answer the verb in the question. Transport, homeostasis and inheritance generate the most dropped marks, usually on explain and suggest rather than on describe.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Reading response and directed writing dominate the mark allocation. Second Language candidates in Dubai often sit the wrong specification for their actual fluency, which costs a grade before any teaching happens. Tutoring focuses on timing, on the summary task, and on writing to a specified audience rather than on vocabulary lists.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Closed-text or set-text depending on specification, with an unseen poetry element in several routes. The failure mode is narration instead of argument. A paragraph that retells the plot of a set text scores in the bottom band however elegant the prose, and that is a habit a tutor can break in four sessions.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by students heading for A Level Mathematics or Further Mathematics, often at Dubai College and Jumeirah College. Calculus notation and proof structure arrive here first and are the two things students carry into AS badly. Worth one session a week from the start rather than a rescue block in spring.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Data response and extended written answers with a heavy evaluation weighting. UAE students have plenty of real context to draw on and rarely use it. Marks sit in the final sentence of an evaluative answer, where a judgement with a reason is required and a summary of both sides is not.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Theory paper plus a problem-solving and programming paper. Pseudocode conventions are examined precisely, so a student who codes fluently in Python can still lose marks on paper. Trace tables and binary arithmetic are high-yield, teachable and routinely under-practised in school time.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Second Language
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must teach Arabic alongside the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Many LA Mer families treat this as a compliance subject until a report grade forces attention. It responds quickly to short, frequent sessions.

sections.heading: Where the money gets wasted on this coast
paragraphs: The three expensive mistakes in LA Mer are the same three everywhere in Dubai, but the beachfront location sharpens the first one. Mistake one is paying the travel premium and not noticing. A home visit rate includes the drive, and on Jumeirah 1 at 6pm the drive is long. If the tutor lives in Al Barsha, somewhere between a fifth and a third of the hourly rate is petrol and Sheikh Zayed Road. Parents who ask a visiting tutor for their online rate are frequently quoted AED 80 to AED 150 less for the identical hour.

Mistake two is paying for hours against the wrong tier. A Cambridge 0580 Core candidate cannot score above grade 5 on that route, so a family spending AED 1,500 a month chasing a grade 7 on the Core tier is buying something the specification does not sell. Equally, a student sitting Extended with gaps in Core content needs the gaps closed before any Extended technique is worth teaching. A tutor who does not look at the tier in the first session is a tutor who will bill you for the discovery later.

Mistake three is buying generalist hours for a specialist problem. A good all-round tutor at AED 180 an hour for forty weeks costs AED 7,200 and may well leave a student exactly where they started on the 0625 practical paper, because that paper rewards a particular kind of method writing that is rarely taught by anyone who has not marked it. Eight sessions with someone who has, at AED 280, costs AED 2,240 and moves the grade. The cheaper invoice is the more expensive purchase. That inversion is the single most useful thing to understand before you book anything.

sections.heading: Online against a home visit, for a LA Mer address specifically
paragraphs: This comparison is usually written as a list of generic advantages. For LA Mer it is worth writing as geography. The development sits on reclaimed beachfront off Jumeirah 1, with access from the Jumeirah Road and parking that fills in the evening. A tutor arriving for a 6pm session leaves their own area at around 5:10pm and leaves yours at about 7:40pm. That is two hours and thirty minutes of their working evening for one teaching hour, which is why in-home rates carry the premium they do and why a visiting tutor can realistically serve two families a night.

The consequence for the parent is not mainly cost. It is choice. A tutor who must physically reach Jumeirah 1 by 6pm has to live within a sensible radius, which reduces your shortlist to whoever is nearby and free. Online, the radius disappears and the shortlist is defined by the syllabus instead. For a mainstream subject such as 0580 maths this matters less. For Cambridge 0620 chemistry at Extended tier, or for an Additional Mathematics student heading into A Level, it is the whole difference between a specialist and whoever was available.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE, and this page will not pretend otherwise: home visiting is a service we run in India only. Everything for a LA Mer family happens over live video, one-to-one, in Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard and a recording of the session if the family wants one. Write on the board, both parties see it. That last point is the one parents are usually sceptical about and the one the free trial lesson settles in forty minutes.

sections.heading: Cambridge and Pearson sessions, counted backwards from results day
paragraphs: Nobody in this search result publishes a calendar, which is strange, because the calendar is what determines whether tutoring money is spent usefully. The first fact to fix is which series your child sits. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series. The February/March series is offered to India only and does not apply to UAE candidates; a page that tells a Dubai parent to prepare for a March window is giving them a date they cannot use. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November.

Second, work backwards rather than forwards. Entry deadlines sit months before the paper, mock windows sit months before the entry closes, and the useful tutoring hours sit before the mocks, not after them. The Pearson November series gives the shape clearly: the final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results reach students in January, with the November 2025 results landing on 22 January 2026. June results move faster, with the June 2026 results reaching centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026.

Third, check the zone. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Your child's school knows its zone. Ask the exams officer rather than reading a timetable off a tutoring site, including this one. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, which is why the table below links behaviour rather than restating dates that move.

sections.heading: Is the tutor you are about to pay legally permitted to teach?
paragraphs: This is a cost question too, because an unpermitted tutor is a tutor who can stop appearing without notice. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Anyone quoting you a permit fee is quoting something that does not exist. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so this page quotes no amount; a figure circulating online as a specific dirham penalty could not be verified against any ministry source and should be ignored wherever you see it. The official application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time.

There is a separate constraint worth knowing on this coast. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat the ADEK detail as press-reported and check the current policy document before relying on the exact wording. The practical rule for a parent anywhere in the UAE is simple: do not arrange for your child's own class teacher to tutor them privately for money. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different animal again, requiring a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE or MoHRE approval, accreditation or partnership, operates no UAE office or centre, and would be misrepresenting itself to suggest otherwise.

sections.heading: Coursework, and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: One of the pages competing for this search sells completed Internal Assessments. That is not a cheaper tutoring option; it is academic malpractice, and the consequence lands on the student, not the seller. IGCSE carries less assessed coursework than the IB Diploma, but several subjects still include a component the student must produce themselves, and anyone sitting IGCSE in a Dubai school is two years away from an IB Diploma or A Level where the stakes are considerably higher.

What a tutor may do is substantial and worth paying for. A tutor may teach the skills the task assesses, explain the criteria, read a draft the student has written and say where it falls short of the criterion, model the technique on a different example, and coach the planning and time management around a deadline. That is teaching, and it is the part that transfers. What a tutor may not do is write, complete, rewrite to a standard, or produce any part of work that must be the student's own. IB Gram tutors teach, review and give feedback; they do not write coursework.

There is a related rule on materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. We reference them and link to the official source rather than reproducing or supplying them, and so should any tutor you hire. A tutor offering a private library of leaked or unreleased material is offering you a malpractice risk with your child's name on it. The honest version is less exciting and is the only version worth buying.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in the context of a Dubai school bill
paragraphs: Tutoring spend only makes sense next to the fee it supplements. Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with the UK curriculum the largest segment by enrolment, followed by Indian, US and International Baccalaureate. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family on the Jumeirah coast that fee freeze is the first year in a while where the tutoring line has not had to compete with a fee rise.

Supply is moving too. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. More places in the British and IB segments is relevant to a LA Mer parent in one specific way: it loosens the assumption that your child's current school is the only viable route to a good IGCSE outcome, and it changes the calculus on whether a persistent subject problem is a tutoring problem or a fit problem.

The practical framing is a simple ratio. A term-long weekly session in a mid-band is AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month against a school fee that, for the schools named on this page, is a multiple of that. Tutoring at one session a week is a small percentage of the education budget and buys a specific thing. Tutoring at four sessions a week across three subjects stops being a supplement and starts being a parallel school, and at that point the question to ask is not which tutor but why the school hours are not working.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects nobody budgets for
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. These sit alongside IGCSE, not instead of it, and they appear on the report card. Families in LA Mer regularly budget carefully for maths and science support and then meet an Arabic grade they had not planned for.

The structure matters if you are buying support. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

Two further details shape what tutoring can usefully do. Schools must ensure all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a credential a parent can actually ask about. And for the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the MoE is strictly prohibited, so support here means working the prescribed material properly rather than importing a parallel course. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes.

sections.heading: Starting, including what happens when we cannot help
paragraphs: The useful first step is not a phone call, it is a marked paper. Find the most recent piece of assessed work your child has had returned with a mark on it and have it to hand. From that, a tutor can tell in one session whether the problem is content, method, timing or reading the question, and those four problems need four different plans at four different costs. Without it, the first two sessions are diagnosis you are paying full rate for.

Then the free trial lesson, which is one lesson per family and happens before any payment. Watch for three things rather than for rapport. Does the tutor ask what tier and which syllabus code before teaching anything? Does your child do most of the talking and writing? Does the session end with something specific that was not true at the start? A session that was pleasant and covered a lot is usually a session where the tutor did the work.

And the honest part. Some subject and level combinations have no UAE-based tutor free at the hour a LA Mer family wants. When that happens we say so rather than putting a general tutor in the slot, and we will tell you the realistic match time or offer a tutor in another time zone whose hours still fit a Gulf Standard Time evening. No competitor page in the researched set discloses a coverage limit, which is exactly why it is worth saying: a platform that never admits to being short of someone is a platform that quietly substitutes.
