process.title: Tell us the school, not just the subject
process.description: Name the school your child travels to, the year group, the board and syllabus code if you have it, and roughly what time they are home and settled. Those four facts decide the slot, the session length and which subject should occupy it, which is most of what makes a plan survive its first month.

process.title: Send the activity calendar too
process.description: The school's fixture and club schedule, plus anything recurring in the family week. The point is to find the one weekday afternoon with nothing on it and protect that slot absolutely. A session placed on a day with a fortnightly fixture gets rescheduled until it quietly dies.

process.title: A free diagnostic trial lesson
process.description: One live session with no payment and no card, spent working a past-paper section at the correct tier and marking it together rather than teaching a topic. You get a written note naming the dominant pattern in the lost marks, how many sessions it suggests, and which slot shape suits the subject.

process.title: Match the subject to the slot
process.description: Calculation subjects go early in the afternoon and early in the week; recall subjects survive a later slot. Subjects needing an uninterrupted stretch — timed writing, a full paper section, a coursework draft — go to a weekend block. Fitting the slot to the subject rather than the reverse is what makes a late school run workable.

process.title: Plan the Year 11 step up in advance
process.description: A single weekly slot is enough in the autumn and is not enough by February. Decide now that the mock aftermath and the final six to eight weeks will run at two or three sessions a week, and identify where those slots will come from before school revision classes take the obvious ones.

process.title: Rebuild on the mock scripts
process.description: When mocks return, the plan is rewritten rather than continued. Lost marks are sorted into content, command term, slip and timing; the dominant category becomes the work for a fixed fortnight; and a list of topics being abandoned is written down. That fortnight is the most informative of the year and it does not keep.

whyPoints.title: Planned from the school run outwards
whyPoints.description: Meydan has almost no schools inside it, so the session window is set by where your child travels rather than where you live. We ask for the school and the arrival time before proposing a slot, because a plan built on an average afternoon fits nobody.

whyPoints.title: Slots that survive the activity calendar
whyPoints.description: The right day is the one with nothing recurring on it, identified from the school's fixture and revision-session schedule. A slot that collides with a fortnightly fixture gets moved until it dies, and that is the most common reason a tutoring arrangement ends.

whyPoints.title: The subject matched to the slot
whyPoints.description: Calculation subjects early, recall subjects later, uninterrupted tasks at the weekend. A student home at 16:45 should be doing 45 minutes of biology rather than an hour of physics, and saying so is more useful than insisting on a standard session.

whyPoints.title: Ramadan and travel planned, not improvised
whyPoints.description: Sessions move earlier or post-Iftar during Ramadan and shorten to 45 minutes. Long Eid and summer absences are normal here, and because delivery is over live video the session follows the student rather than pausing until the family returns.

whyPoints.title: The exam-term cadence is possible at all
whyPoints.description: The mock aftermath and the final weeks need two or three sessions a week, which in this district is where visiting arrangements break. Three video slots are three slots; three journeys through pick-up traffic are a different proposition and cost the travel premium each time.

whyPoints.title: Terms and credentials stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Session length, VAT, materials, cancellation and who bears a session lost to a late bus, all in writing before payment. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none.

faqs.question: Can we book an IGCSE home tutor in Meydan who comes to the villa?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We deliver one-to-one tuition to UAE families over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and do not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE — home visits are a service we run only in India. The market does supply in-home tutoring here at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. In Meydan specifically the premium also buys a later start, because a visiting tutor travels against every school run in the corridor.

faqs.question: What time can a tutoring session realistically start in Meydan?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which school your child travels to, because Meydan has almost no schools inside it. Families attending Hartland International or North London Collegiate School Dubai in Sobha Hartland can be ready before 15:30. Those travelling to Kings' School Nad Al Sheba, Repton Dubai or GEMS Modern Academy land around 16:00. Al Quoz, Al Barsha and Silicon Oasis runs put a child home after 16:45, which is when a weekend block usually beats a weekday session.

faqs.question: Which school clusters does this district send children to?
faqs.answer: Most travel to one of two nearby clusters. Sobha Hartland holds Hartland International School and North London Collegiate School Dubai, minutes away inside the same wider development. Nad Al Sheba holds Kings' School Nad Al Sheba, Repton School Dubai and GEMS Modern Academy. Beyond those, families who chose on provision rather than proximity travel to Safa Community School in Al Quoz, Swiss International Scientific School Dubai at Al Jaddaf, or the Al Barsha and Silicon Oasis schools. Those schools are neighbourhood context only; we have no affiliation with any of them.

faqs.question: How long should a session be if my child gets home late?
faqs.answer: Shorter, and with a different subject in it. A student home at 16:00 can sustain a full hour of maths. A student home at 16:45 should be doing 45 minutes, and that slot should hold a subject that survives tiredness — biology or geography recall rather than physics calculation, because an abandoned rearrangement loses the back half of a question. Matching the subject to the slot rather than forcing the slot to fit the subject is what makes a long school run workable.

faqs.question: Which day of the week is best for a weekly slot?
faqs.answer: The one with nothing recurring on it, which you find from the school's fixture and club calendar rather than by guessing. In most Year 11 weeks in this corridor that turns out to be midweek, with one or two afternoons already taken by sport and, in the spring term, school revision sessions appearing at short notice. Having found the clear day, protect that slot absolutely — including from the family's own calendar — because a repeatedly moved session is a session that eventually stops.

faqs.question: Are weekend sessions as good as weekday ones?
faqs.answer: For some students and some subjects they are better. Weekends win for the long school run, for subjects that cannot be split — a timed English writing task, a full past-paper section, a coursework draft read properly — and during mock season when a weekend double plus one weekday slot is the only realistic way to reach three sessions. Weekdays win where the subject wants repetition rather than length, like chemistry precision habits or non-calculator maths fluency, and where the school run is short.

faqs.question: Does the Ramadan school day change when sessions run?
faqs.answer: They move rather than pause. School hours shorten and the day reorganises around Iftar and later sleep, so sessions generally shift either earlier into the gap the shorter school day creates, or later to post-Iftar timing. Productive length drops in both cases, so 45 minutes is the working maximum. For a Year 11 student sitting the summer series the cadence usually holds and only the clock changes, because a four-week spring gap is expensive in June. Younger students can defensibly pause.

faqs.question: What happens if the school bus is late and we miss the start?
faqs.answer: With a video session it shifts by fifteen minutes rather than being lost, which in a district where every child commutes is a practical difference rather than a theoretical one. Whatever format you choose, agree in advance who bears a session missed for that reason and with how much notice. In Meydan it will come up, and a provider with a clear answer to the question has thought about commuter families; one without an answer has not.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does Year 11 actually need?
faqs.answer: One a week through the autumn, rising to two or three around the mock aftermath and again in the final six to eight weeks before the series. That step up is the thing most arrangements fail to plan for: a single standing slot is more than necessary in September and not enough by February. Decide in advance where the extra slots will come from, because by the spring term school revision sessions will already have taken the obvious afternoons.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE tutoring cost in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Hourly figures read in October 2026: AED 45 to 150 for budget online tutoring, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52; AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150; AED 200 to 450 or more for a specialist, TutorChase publishing AED 270; AED 180 to 500 in-home including travel. Monthly, Bestimate gives AED 240 to 600 budget, 600 to 1,200 mid and 1,000 to 2,000 plus for specialist exam-year support.

faqs.question: Is Year 10 or Year 11 the better moment to begin?
faqs.answer: Year 10, if there is genuinely missing content, because it is the only year in which content can be rebuilt unhurriedly and the slot is easiest to protect. Year 11 is better suited to technique: timing, command terms, question selection and mock-driven targeting, all of which are recoverable quickly. The expensive version is starting in the spring of Year 11 with a content problem, when the honest answer becomes a partial fix and a written list of what to abandon.

faqs.question: Does the mandatory Arabic lesson affect the tutoring plan?
faqs.answer: It affects the week rather than the plan directly. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and schools advised that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Those minutes sit inside the school day, so an IGCSE revision plan competes with them. Where Arabic itself needs support, it works within the school's own approved material.

faqs.question: What should we do in the two weeks after mock results?
faqs.answer: Get the script back rather than just the grade, and sort every lost mark into four categories: content not known, command term misread, arithmetic or notation slip, and ran out of time. Tally across subjects. One category almost always dominates — in this corridor usually timing in maths and the sciences, command terms in the humanities. Work only that category for a fixed fortnight and write down the topics being abandoned, because with four months left even coverage is the same as random coverage.

faqs.question: Is one long session better than two short ones?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject. Chemistry precision habits, non-calculator maths fluency and trace tables respond to repetition, so two 45-minute sessions beat one 90-minute block. Timed English writing, a full past-paper section and a coursework draft read properly need an uninterrupted stretch, so one longer session is the right shape. For families on the long school run, the practical version is one weekend block for the second kind and one short weekday slot for the first.

faqs.question: Do tutors in Dubai need a licence to teach privately?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

faqs.question: When are the IGCSE exams and can we plan travel around them?
faqs.answer: Both Cambridge and Pearson run series available to UAE candidates in June and November, with November the standard resit route; the Feb/March Cambridge route is India only. For exact dates use your school's own timetable rather than a search result, because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones each with its own timetable version and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong one. Book travel only after the exams officer has confirmed the dates.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-meydan.closingHeading: Tell us which school, and what time they are home
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-meydan.closingBody: An IGCSE home tutor in Meydan is a scheduling question first, because the district has almost no schools inside it and every child commutes. Send the school your child travels to, the year group, the syllabus code if you have it, and roughly what time they are home and settled — plus the fixture calendar if you can. From those we can name the slot that will actually survive the term, the session length that fits the arrival time, and which subject belongs in it. The first lesson is a free diagnostic with no payment and no card.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-mirdif.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach IGCSE subjects to Mirdif students over video, by board and by tier. A Cambridge Extended candidate and a Pearson modular candidate are preparing for different papers, and the plan differs from the first lesson.

intro.heading: Work backwards from the session, not forwards from today
paragraphs: Every useful IGCSE revision plan is built in reverse. You start at the exam, count back to the last useful teaching week, and fill the space with the smallest number of things that will actually move marks. Families who plan forwards from the day they decide to act end up revising in syllabus order and running out of time somewhere in the middle, which is why so much tutoring money in Dubai buys thorough coverage of the first third of a course.

That matters particularly in early November, because the November series is live. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May or June and in November each year, and the final November 2026 timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series. A Mirdif family searching for help this week is therefore either inside the session, in which case the job is damage limitation and paper technique, or preparing for June, in which case there is a genuine eight-month runway and it should not be wasted on panic.

The deadline that catches Mirdif families is not the exam, it is the entry. A centre has to register a candidate months before the first paper, so the practical question in February is not whether there is time to revise for a June paper, it is whether the entry has already been filed and for which tier. Private candidates feel this hardest, because there is no school office quietly doing it for them. Ask the centre for the statement of entry, confirm the board, the syllabus code and the tier on it, and only then build the revision weeks around the published window.

Mirdif sits in the eastern suburbs between Al Mizhar, Al Warqa, Al Khawaneej and Nad Al Hamar, and the schools families here use run both Cambridge and Pearson syllabuses, sometimes in the same building for different subjects. The first question any tutor should ask is which board, which syllabus code and which tier, because Cambridge 0580 Mathematics and Pearson 4MA1 are not the same paper structure and preparing for the wrong one wastes the whole block.

Lessons for Mirdif are delivered one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. In exam term that delivery model earns its keep in a specific way: a lesson can be moved from Tuesday to Monday because a paper got rescheduled, without anybody renegotiating a drive across Nad Al Hamar at 16:00.

What follows is the session laid out backwards, an eight-week plan with weekly outputs, the zone problem that costs candidates an exam every year, what the market charges, the Core and Extended tier decision and its grade ceiling, and the five-subject rule that governs Ministry of Education equivalency for IGCSE students in the UAE.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-mirdif.programmesIntro: IGCSE is a two-year course with decisions taken early that set the ceiling late. These are the stages Mirdif families ask about, and the handover points where tutoring tends to be booked.

programmes.name: International General Certificate of Secondary Education
programmes.description: Typically eight to ten subjects examined at the end of Year 11, offered by Cambridge International and by Pearson Edexcel. Cambridge tiers many subjects as Core and Extended with different grade ceilings; Pearson offers single-tier papers in most subjects and modular entry in some. Syllabus codes matter: 0580 and 0607 are different Cambridge mathematics courses entirely.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, IGCSE is the dominant pre-16 route, with UK-curriculum schools accounting for thirty-seven per cent of private-school enrolment in 2024-25. Mirdif families often have one child on Cambridge and another on Pearson, which is why board identification is the first question rather than a detail.

programmes.name: Year 9 and option choices
programmes.description: The year the subject set is chosen and, in Cambridge subjects, the year a Core or Extended recommendation is first made. Choices made here set what is possible at 16 and what is possible at 18, and they are frequently made on timetable convenience rather than on where the student is actually strong.
programmes.countryNote: Tutoring requests from Mirdif in Year 9 are usually about securing an Extended recommendation in mathematics or a science, because a Core entry caps the achievable grade and closes some A Level and Diploma routes two years later.

programmes.name: A Level, IB Diploma or BTEC after IGCSE
programmes.description: IGCSE results determine entry to A Level, the IB Diploma or vocational routes, and each has different subject prerequisites. Mathematics and the sciences are where the grade thresholds bite, and a grade 5 against a required grade 6 in one subject can redirect a whole sixth-form plan.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools in the eastern-suburbs arc run the IB Diploma, so IGCSE students here have a genuine choice between A Level and DP. The transition work differs: A Level wants depth in three subjects, DP wants breadth in six plus the core.

programmes.name: Resit and private candidate entry
programmes.description: The November series functions as the resit route for June candidates, and November candidates can resit in June. Private candidates must be entered through an approved examination centre, and the centre, not the tutor, controls entry deadlines and the timetable zone the candidate sits under.
programmes.countryNote: Mirdif families whose child missed a grade in June often ask about November entry too late. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers, which is the single most expensive thing not to know, so ask the school or centre for the deadline the week the results arrive.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-mirdif.subjectsIntro: Requests from Mirdif concentrate on the subjects where a tier or a paper structure decides the grade, and where eight focused weeks can still change the outcome.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two papers in most routes, calculator and non-calculator depending on the board and tier. Extended and Higher candidates lose most marks on algebraic manipulation and on multi-step problems where the method is never written down.

subjects.name: Additional and International Mathematics
subjects.description: 0607 International Mathematics assumes a graphic display calculator and assesses investigation; 0606 Additional Mathematics is a harder algebraic course. Confusing the two when buying tutoring is common and wastes the first two lessons.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and waves absorb the most lesson time. Required practical skills are examined on a written paper, so students who did the experiments but never learned to describe a method precisely lose those marks on paper.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles calculations, ionic equations and the qualitative analysis tables are the three recoverable areas. The qualitative tables in particular are pure recall and are routinely left unlearned until the final fortnight.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term driven. Describe, explain and suggest are marked differently, and a student writing the same style of answer to all three plateaus in the middle grades regardless of how much content they know.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and the composition task carry structure marks that are independent of ideas. Reading questions reward precise selection of evidence, and most lost marks come from quoting too much and analysing too little.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A different qualification from English Language with different expectations, and the choice between them affects post-16 entry. Worth confirming which one your child is entered for before buying any tutoring.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Data response and extended answers reward applied analysis over definitions. Students who learn definitions thoroughly and apply none of them sit around the middle of the grade range for the whole course.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions, trace tables and the theory paper. The theory paper is where marks are won cheaply, because it is largely learnable recall that students neglect in favour of programming.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.levels: First language and additional language streams
subjects.description: Mandatory in Dubai private schools alongside the licensed curriculum, and streamed separately for Arabs and non-Arabs under KHDA rules. Support should work from the school's own material because the permitted content is prescribed.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-mirdif.regionsIntro: The eastern-suburbs communities around Mirdif share schools, roads and arrival times, so the weekly scheduling described on this page applies across them.

regions.note: North-east of Mirdif across Al Khawaneej Road, on most of the same school routes. Exam-term scheduling is interchangeable with Mirdif's, including evening slots during the November papers.

regions.name: Al Warqa
regions.note: South of Mirdif and closer to the Dubai-Al Ain Road. A high proportion of households here run two boards across siblings, which makes board identification the first question.

regions.name: Al Khawaneej
regions.note: Outer eastern edge with the longest bus runs in the cluster. Families here book 18:00 and 19:00 slots, and in exam term often shift to a morning slot on a study-leave day.

regions.name: Nad Al Hamar
regions.note: Between Mirdif and the creek, closest to the Festival City schools. Earlier arrivals make a 16:30 slot workable here when it is not workable in outer Mirdif.

regions.name: Dubai Festival City
regions.note: Holds two of the schools the eastern suburbs use, so children living here are home earliest and can take the first slot of the afternoon.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis
regions.note: Apartment-heavy and close to Academic City. A frequent origin for Pearson candidates, and for private candidates entered through centres nearby.

regions.note: Dense and well connected to the eastern school arc. Study-leave weeks here often mean a student is at home all day, which opens morning revision slots.

regions.note: On the metro between Mirdif and the airport. Short commutes and the one part of the cluster where mid-afternoon sessions are routinely possible in term time.

schoolClusters.note: The nearest group, running Cambridge and Pearson syllabuses between them and in some cases both within one school. Secondary finishes cluster near 15:00 and the internal bus runs are short, so afternoon slots are workable in term time.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE home tutor in Mirdif can change in eight weeks
paragraphs: Eight weeks is enough for three things and not enough for a fourth. It is enough to rebuild two or three topics that were never understood, enough to fix paper technique across a whole subject, and enough to turn a student who leaves marks on the table into one who collects them. It is not enough to learn a two-year syllabus. Any tutor who tells a Mirdif parent in November that a June-standard Extended course can be covered before the papers is selling, and the parent should treat the answer as disqualifying.

The useful diagnosis takes one marked mock. Sort every lost mark into content not known, technique not applied, or time not managed. In most IGCSE scripts from this cohort the split is roughly a third content and two thirds the other two, which is good news, because technique and timing move much faster than content does. A student who knows the chemistry and loses eleven marks to unwritten working can recover those in four lessons.

The honest limit on the other side is attendance. An eight-week block only works if eight lessons happen. In exam term, lessons collapse because of rescheduled papers, school revision sessions and illness, and in Mirdif they also collapse because somebody has to drive. Delivery over live video removes the last of those: a lesson can shift from Tuesday 17:30 to Monday 19:00 with a message, because nobody has committed to a journey.

So the answer to the search is specific rather than reassuring. An IGCSE home tutor in Mirdif, in the sense of somebody arriving at your villa, is a service other providers offer at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel. IB Gram offers the same teaching over video, one-to-one, with no home visits anywhere in the UAE, and the first lesson costs nothing so the plan can be tested before it is bought.

paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes the calendar, which is odd, because it is the first thing a parent needs. Dates shown are the ones published by Pearson for the International GCSE and are quoted with their source framing; the live official timetable is the only version to plan on, because provisional timetables are revised.

The pattern worth internalising is that entry deadlines sit months before the papers. That is why a family reading a disappointing June result in late August has a window to act for November that closes long before the November papers appear on the horizon. The centre, not the tutor and not the parent, controls entry, so the question goes to the school's examinations officer the week results land.

Results timing is equally worth knowing in advance. Pearson's June 2026 International GCSE results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. November results come considerably later: the November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A student sitting November papers is therefore waiting into the new year, which matters for sixth-form applications and is better known in October than discovered in December.

Build the plan around those fixed points and the eight weeks allocate themselves. Work the last two weeks as timed papers only, the middle four as topic repair with one timed paper a week, and the first two as diagnosis and the two highest-weighted topics. That sequence survives contact with reality better than a syllabus-order plan does.

sections.heading: Which series and which board your child is actually in
paragraphs: A surprising number of parents cannot say with certainty which board their child sits, and in Dubai it is frequently not one board. Schools routinely enter mathematics with one provider and sciences with another, because the specifications suit different teaching teams. For tutoring, that distinction is not academic: Cambridge 0580 Extended and Pearson 4MA1 Higher reward different styles of working, and the past papers are not interchangeable.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series. UAE candidates sit those two. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May or June and in November each year, with the final November 2026 timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026 and provisional timetables published ahead of each series, including one already published for the next International GCSE November series.

Pearson also offers modular entry in some subjects, where units are sat across sessions rather than all at the end. If your child is on a modular route, the planning question changes completely: the next unit may be weeks away rather than months, and a block of tutoring has a much shorter and sharper target. Ask the school explicitly whether any subject is modular, because it is rarely volunteered.

Two minutes of checking saves a wasted block. Ask the school, for each subject: which board, which syllabus or specification code, which tier, and whether entry is linear or modular. Write the four answers down. Any tutor worth hiring will ask for exactly that list before the first lesson, and a tutor who does not ask is about to teach the wrong paper.

sections.heading: The zone problem that costs candidates an exam
paragraphs: This is the most consequential administrative fact in the IGCSE calendar and almost nobody writes it down. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and the timetable differs between them. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable.

What that means in practice for a Mirdif family: a timetable found through a search engine, or shared in a parents' group by somebody whose child attends a different school, may be the wrong zone. A paper that falls on a Tuesday morning in one zone can fall on a different day in another. The only safe source is the timetable your child's own centre issues, and the only safe cross-check is the official site rather than a reproduction of it.

There is a milder version of the same trap with provisional timetables. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is useful for planning and dangerous for precision, because they are revised before becoming final. A revision plan built on a provisional date is fine. A study-leave travel booking built on one is not.

The rule we apply on every page here, and the rule worth applying at home, is that no tutoring website should be your date source. Plan from the live official timetable and from the paper your child's examinations officer hands over. This page quotes Pearson's published November 2026 window because it is sourced, and still tells you to check it.

The structural reason is simple: specialist tutors fill their evening slots first, and by late October the AED 150 to 300 band for a qualified subject tutor online has fewer people with free hours in it than it had in September. Booking in August for November costs less and gets a better match than booking in November for November.

The published market splits as follows. Budget online tutoring, typically university students, runs AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one, travel included, is quoted at AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500. IB and IGCSE specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named tutors reach AED 500 to 650 or more, with BartyED at AED 650.

For an eight-week block the figure that matters is the total. Eight weekly sessions at the qualified online band comes to roughly AED 1,200 to 2,400 for one subject. The same block in-home comes to roughly AED 1,440 to 4,000. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, and monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

The practical advice is to buy one subject properly rather than three thinly. sections.heading: Core or Extended, and the ceiling it sets
paragraphs: In Cambridge subjects that are tiered, the Core and Extended decision caps what is achievable before any revision happens. Core papers are assessed over a narrower grade range than Extended papers, so a student capable of a high grade who sits Core cannot reach it, and a student entered for Extended who cannot cope with the harder paper risks a worse outcome than Core would have produced. The decision is the school's recommendation with the parent in the conversation, and it is usually taken in Year 10 or early Year 11.

The argument for Extended is not ambition, it is what comes next. A Core mathematics grade closes some A Level and Diploma mathematics routes two years later, and the family typically discovers that in Year 12 rather than Year 10. If your child is borderline, the useful question to the school is not whether they can pass Extended but what the Extended entry does to their predicted grade and to their sixth-form options.

Where tutoring genuinely helps is in making the borderline case viable. The gap between Core-comfortable and Extended-viable in mathematics is usually algebraic fluency and multi-step problem structure rather than new topics, and that is a teachable, finite piece of work. Eight to twelve weeks of weekly lessons on exactly that gap changes the conversation with the school, and the conversation should happen before the entry is submitted rather than after.

Pearson's equivalent is Foundation and Higher in some subjects, with the same logic. Ask the school for the tier per subject in writing, because a mixed picture across eight subjects is normal and nobody remembers it accurately from a parents' evening.

sections.heading: Why online delivery earns its keep in the weeks that matter
paragraphs: In September the delivery format is a preference. In exam term it is a logistics decision. Papers get rescheduled, schools add revision sessions at short notice, study leave starts and the student is suddenly at home all day, and one person in the family is already doing four school runs a day between Mirdif and Festival City.

Over video, a lesson can move from Tuesday 17:30 to Monday 19:00 with a message, and during study leave it can move to 10:00 because the student is home. None of that requires renegotiating a journey across Nad Al Hamar or Al Khawaneej Road at 16:00. An in-home arrangement cannot flex that way, not because the tutor is unwilling but because their whole afternoon is built around the drive.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all; home visits are an India-only service, and in exam term that is a feature rather than an apology. The second benefit is subject choice. In late October the local pool of people who will drive to the eastern suburbs for a single evening slot and who know Cambridge 0620 qualitative analysis is extremely small. The online pool is not.

The honest counterweight: a fourteen-year-old revising alone in a bedroom needs more supervision than a sixteen-year-old does, and video lessons do not supply a parent. Put the laptop somewhere visible, keep the camera on, and treat the written note after each lesson as the thing you actually read. That recovers most of what the in-person format offered and keeps the schedule flexible.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency: the five-subject rule
paragraphs: IGCSE families in the UAE eventually meet equivalency, and the detail is published and frequently misreported. For the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade.

Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. That is worth stating plainly because one ranking competitor in this market tells UAE candidates they must take six IGCSE subjects, which is wrong, and a parent planning a subject set on that basis may add a subject nobody needs.

For the American track the requirements are different: English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB, no points threshold should be quoted without reading it on the Ministry's own pages, and this page does not publish one.

Two caveats matter. Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs, not something a tutoring provider performs, guarantees or accelerates, and nothing on this page should be read as implying that tutoring is required for it. Verify your own case against the Ministry's current published requirements, because the detail is revised, and ask the school's university counsellor who has handled the paperwork many times.

faqs.question: Can an IGCSE tutor visit our villa in Mirdif?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and UAE tuition is delivered one-to-one over live video. In exam term the online format also flexes when papers move, which an arrangement built around a drive cannot do.

faqs.question: Which exam series will my child sit in the UAE?
faqs.answer: June and November. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May or June and in November each year. The November 2026 Pearson final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. If anyone quotes you a February or March exam window for a UAE candidate, that is the series offered to India and it does not apply to your child.

faqs.question: When do November IGCSE results come out?
faqs.answer: Considerably later than June results, which catches families out. Pearson's November 2025 International GCSE results reached students on 22 January 2026, so a November candidate is waiting into the new year. By comparison, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. If sixth-form applications depend on the grade, plan for that gap now and ask the school how it handles predicted grades in the interim.

faqs.question: Is eight weeks enough to turn a grade around?
faqs.answer: Enough for some things and not others. Eight weeks can rebuild two or three topics, fix paper technique across a subject, and stop a student leaving marks on the table through unwritten working or poor time management. It cannot cover a two-year syllabus that was never learned. Send the last marked mock and the split is usually clear: in most scripts from this cohort roughly a third of lost marks are content and two thirds are technique and timing, and the second group moves fastest.

faqs.question: What is the exam zone and why does it matter for a Dubai centre?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and the timetable differs between them. Cambridge states that using the correct version of the timetable for your zone is essential and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. The practical consequence is that a timetable found online, or shared by a parent whose child attends a different school, may be wrong for your centre. Use the timetable your examinations officer issues.

faqs.question: How do I find out which board each of my child's subjects uses?
faqs.answer: Ask the school by email and get four facts per subject in writing: board, syllabus or specification code, tier, and whether entry is linear or modular. Mixed entry across subjects is completely normal in Dubai, with mathematics on one board and sciences on another. Those four facts decide which past papers are useful and which are a waste of a lesson, and any tutor who does not ask for them before starting is about to prepare your child for the wrong paper.

faqs.question: Core or Extended: what does the tier on the entry form do to the grade ceiling?
faqs.answer: That is the school's recommendation and it sets a ceiling, so it deserves a proper conversation rather than a nod. Core papers are assessed over a narrower grade range, so a capable student entered for Core cannot reach the top grades, while a student entered for Extended who cannot handle the paper may do worse than Core would have given them. The question to ask the school is what the Extended entry does to the predicted grade and to post-16 options, not simply whether your child would pass.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does UAE equivalency actually require?
faqs.answer: Five. For the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E, or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One ranking competitor states that UAE candidates need six IGCSE subjects, which is incorrect. Verify your own case against the Ministry's current published requirements before planning a subject set.

faqs.question: Does tutoring help with the equivalency process itself?
faqs.answer: No, and no provider should suggest otherwise. Equivalency is run by the Ministry of Education and the emirate attestation authorities, and it is a documentation process rather than an academic one. Tutoring affects the grades your child achieves, which in turn affect whether the published thresholds are met, and that is the entire connection. We describe the requirements, cite the published source, and point you to the official channel and to your school's university counsellor, who has handled the paperwork many times.

faqs.question: My child is a private candidate. Does that change the plan?
faqs.answer: It changes the administration more than the teaching. Private candidates must be entered through an approved examination centre, and the centre controls the entry deadline, the fees and the timetable zone the candidate sits under. Find the centre first and the deadline second, because the deadline sits months before the papers and missing it removes the session entirely. Once entry is confirmed, the revision block is built the same way: backwards from the paper, with weekly outputs.

faqs.question: What does an eight-week IGCSE block cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Depends on the band. Eight weekly hours at the qualified online rate of AED 150 to 300 comes to roughly AED 1,200 to 2,400 for one subject. The same block at the in-home rate of AED 180 to 500 comes to roughly AED 1,440 to 4,000. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are other providers' published figures; ours is quoted after the free trial.

faqs.question: Is it better to tutor one subject properly or three a little?
faqs.answer: One, almost always. Three subjects at a lesson a fortnight produces no measurable change in any of them and is the commonest way an exam-term budget is wasted in this city. A single subject at one lesson a week for eight weeks, with a weekly marked output, moves marks you can see on a script. If two subjects genuinely need work, the honest answer is two specialists on two evenings rather than one tutor spread across both.

faqs.question: Can lessons move during study leave or Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is where video delivery pays for itself. During study leave students are at home all day, so morning slots become available and sessions can be re-sequenced to sit the day before each paper. During Ramadan evening schedules shift and post-iftar slots are frequently more productive than late-afternoon ones. None of that requires renegotiating a drive across the eastern suburbs, so a same-week change takes a message rather than a conversation.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in the UAE need a licence, and is my tutor covered?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Ask any independent tutor directly, and note that the permit's code of conduct bars serving students from the tutor's own school.

faqs.question: What should the last fortnight before the papers look like?
faqs.answer: Whole papers under time, marked strictly against the official mark scheme, and nothing else. Topic teaching in the final fortnight rarely survives into the exam hall, while timing strategy and question-order decisions do. Two or three complete papers a week per subject, with the lesson spent on the five questions that lost marks for a nameable reason, is the highest-return use of those weeks. Your child's school holds licensed access to the papers and mark schemes; we do not reproduce or supply board material.

intro.heading: Nobody knows nine IGCSE specifications. The ones who say they do are the problem
paragraphs: The question behind a search for a local IGCSE tutor is usually practical rather than academic: who can come to the house and help with the subjects that are going badly. In a large-plot district where a visit costs a tutor forty minutes of driving at each end, the temptation is to find one person who can cover several subjects in a single visit. That is understandable and it is the wrong structure, because the thing you actually need is specification knowledge, and specification knowledge does not generalise.

Consider what a tutor has to hold in mind to be useful in one subject. For maths, whether the specification includes a paper taken without a calculator, because the answer differs between the two main boards and determines the whole drill. For a science, whether practical skills are assessed through an alternative-to-practical paper or inside the written papers. For English, whether the student is entered for First Language or Second Language, which are different qualifications. For Literature, which set texts the school chose this year. Multiply that by nine subjects across three possible awarding bodies and the claim to cover them all collapses.

What a generalist delivers instead is homework supervision, which is a real service and worth a real price, just not a specialist one. A student who needs a topic re-explained after a fortnight of illness is well served by it. A student losing method marks in maths, misreading command terms in Biology and answering generically in Business Studies has three different problems, each diagnosable by someone who has marked that paper, and none of them visible to a competent generalist sitting at the kitchen table.

The supply picture explains why this is not simply a counsel of perfection. The people who know a specification best are usually teaching it full time at a school, with a few evening hours a week at most, and those hours go first to whoever asks earliest. Spread across Dubai's many curricula and several awarding bodies, that leaves a thin layer of genuinely specification-literate tutors in any one neighbourhood, and the ones who will drive into a gated villa district at four in the afternoon are thinner still.

IB Gram covers an IGCSE timetable differently: a specialist per subject, delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the specification code confirmed before anyone teaches. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The sections below set out what a tutor must know in each subject, the questions that catch a generalist, what cannot honestly be taught remotely, and the series calendar counted backwards.

Nothing on this page promises a grade. What it offers is a way to tell, in the first two minutes of a conversation, whether the person offering to teach your child has taught the examination your child will sit. In a market where several providers overstate their coverage and nobody publishes a limit, that is the more useful thing to hand a parent.

programmes.name: Years 10 and 11, the examination course
programmes.description: Eight to ten subjects sat as external examinations, with tiering decided by the school where it applies. In most subjects the written papers carry the whole grade, so nothing cushions a weak paper. This is the stage where the specification determines paper structure, tier names, calculator rules and how practical or spoken skills are assessed, and where a generalist stops being sufficient.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools use more than one awarding body and sometimes different ones for different subjects within the same school. Ask the examinations officer for each code in writing. From this district that single email saves more wasted tutoring hours than any amount of comparison shopping.

programmes.name: What the IGCSE grades have to carry
programmes.description: Grades gate post-16 entry, and schools set their own thresholds for A Level and IB Diploma courses. A bare pass at a threshold is not the same as readiness: a student heading for Higher Level sciences or A Level Mathematics needs fluency that a borderline grade does not evidence, which is a different target from general revision.
programmes.countryNote: Schools serving this district offer both A Levels and the IB Diploma after IGCSE, so results decide the shape of the next two years. Households that look up the actual entry thresholds during Year 10 usually buy far less tutoring in Year 12 than those who wait for results day.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-mohammed-bin-r.subjectsIntro: The argument of this page is that each subject is its own specialism. These are the subjects we cover for households in this district, and for each one the specific thing a tutor must know before they are useful.
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-mohammed-bin-r.igcseSubjectsIntro: The same subjects viewed by awarding body, because the code rather than the subject name determines what your child sits. Ask the examinations officer for it before booking anything.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The tutor must know whether a non-calculator paper exists on this specification, because it determines the entire drill. Marks go on algebraic slowness, on multi-step problems with no working written, and on missing final statements in geometry.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The tutor must know how practical skills are assessed on this board. Beyond that, the losses are equation rearrangement and standard form rather than conceptual misunderstanding, which is why a maths block often lifts the Physics grade.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The tutor must be able to say where students lose marks in mole calculations without being prompted. Organic chemistry rewards mechanism detail, and balancing practice underpins every calculation question on the paper.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The tutor must teach command terms as instructions rather than as synonyms. Terminology precision and data interpretation carry the marks, and fluent but imprecise writing is the standard reason a grade plateaus.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: The tutor must establish which of the two qualifications the student is entered for before teaching anything, because the components and the criteria differ. Some routes include a spoken element that needs rehearsing in format.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: The tutor must teach the school's actual set texts, which vary by school and by year. A tutor who offers to teach the skill in the abstract has not understood that the questions are about specific texts.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and percentage work carry the quantitative marks and the evaluation marks are verbal. A tutor who cannot describe what a top-band evaluation looks like will leave a student at the middle of the range.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Application to the given case study is where the analysis marks sit. The commonest loss is a generically correct answer that never refers to the business in the question, which a competent marker spots immediately.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions differ between specifications, so this is a subject where the code must be confirmed rather than assumed. Number bases and logic are learnable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: ICT
subjects.description: Practical software skills are formally assessed, and the software versions and task formats matter. A tutor needs to know what the school's practical programme has actually covered this term.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
igcseSubjects.description: Under the syllabus in use from 2025, each tier pairs a non-calculator paper with a calculator paper at 50% each. A tutor who never mentions the non-calculator paper has not taught this specification recently.

igcseSubjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1
igcseSubjects.description: Two papers of two hours at 50% each, calculator permitted throughout. The useful drill here is multi-step problem structuring rather than mental arithmetic, which is the reverse of the Cambridge emphasis.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE sciences 0620, 0625, 0610
igcseSubjects.description: Tiered papers with an alternative-to-practical route available for experimental skills. Which practical option the centre uses changes what revision of experimental method should look like.

igcseSubjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences 4CH1, 4PH1, 4BI1
igcseSubjects.description: Practical understanding is assessed inside the written papers rather than through a separate practical examination, so experimental method is revised in writing throughout.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English 0500 and 0510
igcseSubjects.description: Two distinct qualifications with different components, and in some routes a speaking element. A student entered for the wrong one works to the wrong criteria for two years.

igcseSubjects.name: Oxford AQA International GCSE
igcseSubjects.description: In use at some Dubai centres and the body most often assumed away by tutors who know the other two. Paper structures differ, so the specification has to be confirmed rather than inferred.

sections.heading: What a tutor must actually know, subject by subject
paragraphs: This is the table that makes the argument concrete. For each subject there is one specific piece of knowledge that separates a tutor who has taught the paper from one who knows the subject, and in every case it is checkable by a parent in a first conversation without any subject expertise. None of these is obscure. All of them are invisible to someone who has only ever studied the subject rather than marked it.

Read the middle column as a set of questions rather than as information. If a prospective maths tutor cannot say whether your child's specification includes a non-calculator paper, they do not know which board you are talking about. If a science tutor has no view on how practical skills are assessed, they will revise the wrong thing. If an English tutor does not ask whether the entry is First Language or Second Language, they are about to teach to the wrong criteria.

The right-hand column is the other half of the test. A tutor who has marked the paper knows where the marks leak, and they describe it in specific terms rather than general ones. Students losing method marks, misreading command terms, answering a case study generically: these are named, diagnosable patterns. A tutor who answers a question about losses by saying the student needs to practise more is describing a hope rather than a diagnosis.

One caution on using the table. Specifications are revised, schools change boards, and set texts rotate, so treat every row as a reason to check with the examinations officer rather than as a fact about your child's course. The point of the table is not to make you an expert. It is to let you tell within two minutes whether the person you are speaking to has taught the examination your child will sit.

sections.heading: The questions that catch a generalist
paragraphs: A household in this district will often be offered one tutor for several subjects, usually with warmth and genuine confidence. The questions below separate breadth of knowledge from depth of it, and they are not hostile: a good tutor enjoys being asked because the questions are the ones they would ask on your behalf. A tutor who bristles at them has told you something useful at no cost.

Start with the board. Ask them to name the awarding body and specification code for each subject before you tell them, and accept that a careful tutor may say they need to check. Checking is fine; not knowing that it matters is not. Then ask the subject-specific question from the table above, which takes ten seconds and is decisive. Then ask what practice they will set, from which board's material, and how it will be marked.

Then ask the question that exposes overreach: which of these subjects would you decline? A tutor willing to take all nine has either not understood the request or is prepared to improvise at your expense. A tutor who says they will teach maths and physics properly and would rather someone else took Literature and Business Studies is telling you they know what they know, which is the single most reliable indicator of competence in this market.

Finally, ask where they are based and what time zone they work to. There is nothing wrong with a specialist outside the UAE teaching a UAE student on Gulf Standard Time; several of the strongest subject tutors available to this district are exactly that. The problem is concealment, and several providers ranking for Dubai queries present a local appearance while routing families elsewhere behind a non-UAE number or a price in US dollars. A straight answer costs nothing to give.

sections.heading: The First Language and Second Language English trap
paragraphs: This deserves its own section because it is the most consequential silent error in IGCSE entries and almost nobody warns parents about it. English First Language and English Second Language are different qualifications with different components and different criteria. A student entered for one while being taught, tutored and assessed as though they were sitting the other spends two years working towards the wrong standard.

The entry is made by the school, often sensibly, on the basis of the student's language background and the timetable available. Sometimes it is made on the timetable alone. A student with strong spoken English and weaker written accuracy may be placed in one route when the other would reward them better, and a student whose first language is not English may be entered for First Language because that is what the cohort does. Neither situation is scandalous and both are worth checking.

For a tutor, knowing which route applies is non-negotiable, because the mark schemes reward different things. Writing that scores well in one can sit mid-band in the other. Some routes also include a spoken component, which has to be rehearsed in the format the specification sets rather than practised as general conversation, and a tutor who does not know whether a speaking element exists cannot prepare for it.

What to do is simple. Ask the examinations officer which English qualification your child is entered for, in writing, along with the code. If the answer surprises you, raise it early rather than in Year 11, because entry decisions and their deadlines belong to the school and a change becomes progressively harder as the course goes on. Then make sure whoever tutors them knows the answer before the first session rather than discovering it in week three.

sections.heading: Practical science, spoken work and what cannot honestly be taught remotely
paragraphs: A page arguing for online delivery has an obligation to say what online delivery cannot do, and the honest list is short but real. Nobody runs a school laboratory over video. A tutor cannot supervise a titration, cannot watch a student handle apparatus, and cannot substitute for the school's own practical programme. Any provider implying otherwise is overselling, and that is worth noticing because it tells you how they will describe everything else.

What can be taught remotely is the part that is actually examined in writing, which on both main boards is considerable: experimental method, independent and dependent variables, controls, reliability, uncertainty, graph work, and the written conventions a mark scheme rewards. Whether that is assessed through an alternative-to-practical paper or inside the written papers depends on the specification, which is one more reason the code matters.

Spoken components are a different case and remote delivery handles them well, provided the tutor knows the format. A speaking element has a structure, a timing and a set of criteria, and rehearsing it over video is closer to the examination experience than an informal conversation at a kitchen table. What matters is that the rehearsal matches the specification's format rather than being general practice in speaking English.

The table below sets out what sits where, so a household can see which parts of a science or language course a tutor can genuinely help with and which belong to the school. Used as a checklist, it also catches a tutor who claims more than is possible, which in a market where several competitors overstate their coverage is a useful filter in itself.

sections.heading: The June and November series, counted backwards
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. The February and March series that appears in some online revision material is offered to India only, so it has no place in a Dubai plan, and material quoting it should make you doubt the rest of the document. November functions as the resit route inside the same academic year for both main awarding bodies, which is worth knowing before results day rather than after it.

The published record shows the rhythm. For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with results following in January: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. For the summer series, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Those are past dates, cited so you can see the pattern rather than so you can act on them.

For anything ahead, open the awarding body's live timetable rather than a restatement, including this page's, because Pearson publishes provisional timetables and revises them. There is also an administrative detail almost nobody passes on: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable.

That last point matters practically for a household revising from documents found online. Ask the school which zone your centre sits in and use the timetable they issue. It is a thirty-second question that removes an entire category of risk, and it is the kind of thing a tutor who has worked with UAE centres will raise unprompted.

sections.heading: Online against a home visit, for a multi-subject problem
paragraphs: For a household weighing a visit against online delivery, the multi-subject case is where the comparison tips hardest, and it is worth being precise about why. The variables that matter are whether each subject can be matched to someone who has taught it, what a journey costs in a large-plot district, what happens when a session must move, and whether a person in the room is genuinely required.

Matching favours online decisively. Four subjects taught by four specialists is achievable online and essentially impossible in-home at a sane cost, because it would mean four separate journeys into a gated district. The in-home structure therefore pushes families towards one tutor covering several subjects, which is the structure this page argues against. That is not a criticism of in-home tutors; it is a consequence of how travel time works here.

Cost favours online by the travel premium. Market in-home rates in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the figure, against about AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online and AED 200 to 450 and above for a specialist. Those are other providers' published figures, read in October 2026. Rescheduling favours online too: a cancelled visit wastes a journey and is often charged, while an online session moves inside the same week at no cost to anyone.

Presence is the variable where a local arrangement has a real claim, particularly for a student who will not work unless someone is physically there. We will not argue that away, and for that household a local tutor is the right answer with this page's bands to judge the price by. To be unambiguous: IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, so the choice here is between our online delivery and an arrangement you would make yourself.

sections.heading: KHDA, equivalency and the mandatory subjects alongside IGCSE
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, with annual inspection on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. The departmental commentary inside a report is more informative than the headline band, because a strong department can sit inside an averagely rated school and the reverse is equally true.

The scale of the market explains the variability in tutoring. Dubai's private sector served 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools creating 16,846 new places; six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. KHDA also confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year. A market that large, using several awarding bodies, is one where nothing visibly distinguishes a specification-literate tutor from a confident generalist unless a parent asks.

The grades have a later use worth planning for. For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five, alongside one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong. Equivalency is a process the ministry performs, so verify your own case through its attestation channel rather than through any tutoring service, and do not treat tutoring as a requirement for it.

Finally, the mandatory UAE subjects run alongside IGCSE rather than instead of it. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, and separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in several of them. On our own position, plainly: IB Gram is not KHDA approved, ADEK approved or accredited by Cambridge, Pearson or Oxford AQA, and does not claim to be.

sections.heading: Getting started from Mohammed Bin Rashid City, and what we decline
paragraphs: Begin with one email to the school's examinations officer asking for the awarding body, the specification code and the tier for each subject you are considering, plus which English qualification your child is entered for. Send that to us with the latest grades labelled as mock or classwork, the teacher comments quoted rather than summarised, and a photograph of one marked script per subject if you have them.

We then propose a specialist per subject rather than one tutor for the timetable, and run a free trial lesson. Use the questions from earlier in this page. Ask the subject-specific question cold, ask what practice will be set and from which board's material, and ask which subjects they would decline. Afterwards, ask for a written account of where the marks are going. If the answer is general, do not book, with us or anyone.

What we decline is worth stating. We will not accept a booking to cover a specification nobody on the team has taught, because the differences matter most in the final eight weeks when there is no time to absorb them. We will not put one tutor across four subjects to simplify a schedule. We will not claim to supervise practical work remotely. And we will not reproduce or distribute syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; we reference them and link to the awarding body's own page.

We also disclose, before you book, that a proposed tutor may be based in the UAE or outside it and which, that we send no tutors to UAE homes at all, and that coverage in English Literature with unusual set texts, Computer Science and Oxford AQA specifications is thinner than in maths and the main sciences. If any of that rules us out for your household, better to establish it now than in week three, and the trial lesson costs nothing either way.

process.title: One email to the examinations officer
process.description: Ask for the awarding body, specification code and tier in each subject, plus which English qualification your child is entered for. It takes two minutes and it prevents the two most expensive errors in this market, which are the wrong board and the wrong English route.

process.title: Send one marked script per subject
process.description: A script shows what no description can: whether marks are going on method, on command terms, on generic answers or on content the student cannot access. It also tells us which subjects genuinely carry the problem and which are collateral.

process.description: We will not offer one tutor for a timetable. Each subject gets someone who has taught that specification, in its own slot, which costs the same as a stretched generalist and delivers people who have marked the papers.

process.description: Ask the subject-specific question without prompting, ask which subjects they would decline, and ask where they are based. Then ask for a written account of where the marks are going. Vague answers are a reason not to book at any rate.

process.title: Start with one subject even when four look weak
process.description: Weak grades across maths and the sciences usually share one cause, and across humanities usually share another. Fixing the shared cause once shows up in more than one grade, which is cheaper and faster than four parallel arrangements.

process.title: Review against the next marked work
process.description: Progress is judged on the next piece of marked school work rather than on how the sessions felt. If the named loss has not moved across two pieces, the plan changes rather than the block being extended.

whyPoints.description: Nobody knows nine IGCSE specifications, so we do not offer one tutor for a timetable. Four subjects means four people who have taught those papers, which is achievable online and effectively impossible as four journeys into a gated district.

whyPoints.title: The proof published subject by subject
whyPoints.description: For each subject we name the one thing a tutor must know and the loss they should be able to describe. It lets a parent tell within two minutes whether they are speaking to someone who has marked the paper.

whyPoints.title: The English entry route flagged
whyPoints.description: First Language and Second Language are different qualifications with different criteria, and a student entered for one and taught as the other works to the wrong standard for two years. Almost nobody in this market warns parents to check it.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what cannot be done remotely
whyPoints.description: Nobody supervises apparatus over video. We teach the examined written element of practical science and say plainly that technique belongs to the school's own programme, which is also a test of any provider claiming more.
