whyPoints.description: We say whether a tutor is in the UAE or outside it, and which subjects are thin. Several providers in this market conceal non-UAE delivery behind a local appearance, and the concealment rather than the location is the problem.

whyPoints.title: No borrowed credentials and no leaked papers
whyPoints.description: We explain what KHDA and MoHRE do and link to their own material, and we do not host syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes. We reference them, so what a student works from is the current version.

faqs.question: Can one home tutor cover all of my child's IGCSE subjects?
faqs.answer: Not well. Each subject carries specification-specific knowledge that does not generalise: whether maths includes a non-calculator paper, how a science assesses practical skills, whether English is First Language or Second Language, which set texts a Literature cohort studies. A tutor willing to take nine subjects has either not understood the request or is prepared to improvise. What a generalist genuinely delivers is homework supervision, which is useful for a missed topic and is not specialist work, and should not be charged as though it were.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether a tutor has actually taught my child's subject?
faqs.answer: Ask the subject-specific question cold. A maths tutor should know whether the specification includes a non-calculator paper. A science tutor should have a view on how practical skills are assessed on that board. A Business Studies tutor should mention application to the case study unprompted. Then ask what loss they would expect to find in your child's work, and judge the specificity. A tutor who answers that the student needs to practise more is describing a hope rather than a diagnosis.

faqs.question: Do your tutors visit homes in Mohammed Bin Rashid City?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition over live video throughout the UAE, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. We state it plainly because home tutor is the phrase parents search. The practical consequence for a household in a large-plot district is that four subjects can be matched to four specialists without four journeys, and a session starts when the student is ready rather than when a tutor has cleared gated access at four in the afternoon.

faqs.question: Which English IGCSE is my child sitting, and why does it matter?
faqs.answer: Ask the examinations officer in writing, because First Language and Second Language are different qualifications with different components and criteria, and some routes include a spoken element. A student entered for one while being taught and tutored as though sitting the other works to the wrong standard for two years. Entry is made by the school, usually sensibly and occasionally on timetable grounds alone. If the answer surprises you, raise it in Year 10 rather than Year 11, while a change is still administratively possible.

faqs.question: How are science practicals handled if the tutoring is online?
faqs.answer: The examined written element is taught and the laboratory work is not. Online sessions cover experimental method, independent and dependent variables, controls, reliability, uncertainty, graph work and the written conventions the mark scheme rewards. Handling apparatus belongs entirely to the school's practical programme, and any provider implying they can supervise it remotely is overselling. Whether your child's board uses an alternative-to-practical paper or assesses practical understanding inside the written papers depends on the specification, which is one more reason to get the code.

faqs.question: My child has four weak subjects. Do we need four tutors?
faqs.answer: Start with one. Weak grades across maths and the sciences usually share a single cause, which is arithmetic and algebra, and weak humanities grades usually share writing structure. Fixing the shared cause once shows up in more than one grade, which is both cheaper and faster than four parallel arrangements competing for the same evenings. If after a half-term two subjects have moved and two have not, that is the point to add a second specialist, with evidence rather than guesswork.

faqs.question: Is it a problem if the subject specialist is not based in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Not in itself, provided you are told. A specialist elsewhere who has taught your child's exact specification and works to Gulf Standard Time is a better match than a nearby generalist. The problem is concealment, and several providers ranking for Dubai queries present a local appearance while routing families overseas, sometimes behind a non-UAE phone number or a price in US dollars. Ask directly where the tutor sits and what hours they keep. We answer that before the first lesson and flag it where a subject is only covered that way.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE home tutor cost in a district like this one?
faqs.answer: In-home one-to-one in Dubai runs roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the figure, and quotes to large-plot districts cluster in the upper half of that range because of access time. Online equivalents sit at about AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor and AED 200 to 450 and above for a specialist, with packages advertised around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Those are other providers' published figures read in October 2026 rather than IB Gram's prices.

faqs.question: Should I ask a tutor which subjects they would refuse?
faqs.answer: It is the most informative question available. A tutor who says they will teach maths and physics properly and would rather someone else took Literature and Business Studies is telling you they know the limits of their own knowledge, which is the most reliable competence signal in this market. A tutor who accepts all nine has either misunderstood the request or intends to improvise at your expense. Asking is not rude, and a good tutor will answer it without hesitation.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are hardest to cover well?
faqs.answer: English Literature where the set texts are unusual, Computer Science, Additional Mathematics, second languages beyond the commonly taught ones, and any subject entered through Oxford AQA, because fewer tutors have taught that specification. Mathematics, Biology and Business Studies are well covered, and Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English Language are reasonable. We tell you which category each subject falls into before you book, with the fallback stated, rather than accepting the booking and improvising.

faqs.question: Can my child resit IGCSE subjects in November?
faqs.answer: Yes, November functions as a resit route inside the same academic year for both main awarding bodies, which is worth knowing before results day. The published pattern is instructive: Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Entry goes through the school's examinations officer shortly after summer results, and the preparation window is roughly eight to ten weeks, which is enough if the marked script is used to target it.

faqs.question: What timetable should we revise from?
faqs.answer: Only the one the school issues. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and its guidance states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. A timetable found online may belong to a different zone entirely. Ask the examinations officer which zone your centre is in, and for future series open the awarding body's live timetable rather than a restatement.

faqs.question: Is there a licence a Dubai tutor should hold, and may I ask to see it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and asking about it is reasonable. MoHRE issues a private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Applications run through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: How many of these nine subjects actually count towards UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five, on the British track. Students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five, alongside one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. One ranking competitor states six subjects, which is incorrect. Equivalency is a process the ministry performs, so verify your own case through its attestation channel rather than through any tutoring site.

faqs.question: With four subjects running, how do sessions survive Ramadan and mock season?
faqs.answer: Yes, and with four subjects running it is one of the clearer advantages of online delivery. During Ramadan sessions commonly shift to post-Iftar slots, with no journey to renegotiate at either end. In mock weeks a session can pause or redirect towards whatever the mock has just exposed. When the family travels the lessons follow the student. Agree which time zone sessions are pinned to if you are leaving the Gulf, and give notice so the slots are held rather than released.

faqs.question: What should I send to get a useful set of recommendations?
faqs.answer: Four things. The awarding body, specification code and tier for each subject, from the examinations officer, plus which English qualification applies. The latest grades, labelled as mock or classwork. The teacher comments quoted rather than paraphrased. And one marked script per subject if you have them, which is worth more than the rest combined because it shows which subjects genuinely carry the problem. With those we can usually propose specialists the same day.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-mohammed-bin-r.closingHeading: Four subjects means four specialists, not one visit
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-mohammed-bin-r.closingBody: The convenience of a single home visit is real, and it pushes households towards one tutor covering subjects nobody can cover equally well. The alternative is not more expensive: a specialist per subject, each confirmed against the specification code, costs about what a stretched generalist does and delivers people who have marked the papers. Send the codes, the tiers, the latest grades and one marked script per subject, and we will propose specialists and run the first session free. Then ask which subjects they would decline.

intro.heading: Everything that matters in an IGCSE closes before the exam does
paragraphs: Motor City is built around the Dubai Autodrome, with GEMS Metropole School inside the community running a British curriculum through IGCSE and on to sixth form. That means most families here are on the IGCSE route and most of them will go looking for help at some point in Year 11. The thing worth knowing before that happens is that the decisions which actually bound a result have already been made by then.

Three dates close the options. The tier of entry on Cambridge subjects, decided by the school on internal evidence and capping the grade that can be awarded. The final entry deadline, which the examination centre works to on the board's schedule and which falls months before the first paper. And the Year 9 option choices, which decide whether separate sciences and a second language are on the list at all. None of those can be revisited in the spring of Year 11, which is when the search for a tutor usually starts.

What can still be changed in Year 11 is substantial, and worth being precise about: examination technique, timing on the long papers, procedural habits like showing method and rounding once at the end, recall content, and the alternative-to-practical skill set in the sciences. Those are real gains and a short block buys them. What cannot be changed is the ceiling, the subject list or the board. Knowing which list you are on when you pick up the phone is the difference between a plan and a hope, and it is the reason this page leads with dates instead of subjects.

This page sets the two IGCSE years out as a calendar with the published dates attached. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and the February/March series offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is the practical reason to open the live official timetable rather than trust a date restated on any third-party page, this one included.

It also covers the part of a Dubai academic year that no competitor page addresses: how Ramadan sits against the spring revision window, and what kind of work fits a shortened school day and a post-Iftar evening. Teaching is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with no home visits anywhere in the UAE, and sessions move to post-Iftar timing on request at no extra cost.

subjects.description: Content volume makes this the subject where falling behind in Year 10 compounds most. Definitions are credited against specific wording, so recall testing should run continuously from the spring rather than in a final push.

subjects.description: Diagram marks are separately allocated, so diagram drill is cheap and effective at any point. The eight-mark evaluation at the end of a structured question is where the time budget runs out, which is a Year 11 timing fix.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Application to the stimulus separates grades. Break-even and ratio arithmetic can be drilled in Year 10 and then maintained, and generic theory answers are the habit that most needs correcting before the mock.

subjects.description: Added at Year 9 options and best supported from the start of Year 10, because calculus and trigonometric identities arrive early. A student struggling here despite coping with 0580 is short on algebraic fluency rather than on understanding.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)

sections.heading: The two IGCSE years, counted backwards from results day
paragraphs: A calendar counted forwards produces a revision timetable. A calendar counted backwards shows which decisions close and when, and that is the information that changes outcomes. For an IGCSE student the sequence of closures is Year 9 options, then the tier of entry, then the final entry deadline, then the zone timetable, then the papers. Each one narrows what is possible, and only the last two are visible to most families.

Year 9 closes the subject list. Separate sciences or a combined award, a second language or not, Additional Mathematics or not. That list determines what a sixth form can offer at sixteen, and it cannot be reopened in Year 11. Year 10 closes the tier, because schools decide entries on internal evidence gathered across that year, and a Core entry caps the awarded grade commonly at 5 on the 9-1 scale or C on the letter scale.

The final entry deadline falls months before the first paper and is handled by the examination centre to the board's schedule. By that point board, syllabus code and tier are fixed in writing for every subject. Mock examinations follow in the winter of Year 11 and are the single most useful piece of evidence a family will get, because a marked mock shows exactly which habits are costing marks.

Then the zone timetable, which is the administrative detail that catches families out. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, and notes that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Ask the examinations officer which zone your centre is in before printing anything or booking travel.

sections.heading: Year 11 month by month, and what each stage should produce
paragraphs: Year 11 has a shape, and a plan that ignores it ends up doing the right work at the wrong time. Content completion belongs in the autumn. Mocks fall in the winter and should be treated as data rather than as a verdict. The spring is where technique, recall and the alternative-to-practical work belong. The final weeks are for full timed papers and the error log, not for new content.

The autumn job is coverage. Every subject should have been through its syllabus once by the winter, because a mock sat on partially taught content produces a misleading score and wastes the most useful diagnostic of the year. Where a school is behind in one subject, that is worth knowing in November rather than in March, and it is a reasonable thing to ask a head of department directly.

The winter job is reading the mocks properly. A marked mock is the best evidence a family will ever get, and most of it is discarded. What should come out of it is a list of habits rather than a list of weak topics: answering without working, rounding partway through, command-term mismatch, running out of time on the long paper. Each of those has a known cost to change, measured in two to six sessions, and naming them is what turns a mock score into a plan.

The spring job is execution, and it is where the Dubai calendar intervenes. Mocks, internal deadlines and the Ramadan weeks can land close together, so full-length timed paper practice has to start earlier than a plan written in September assumed. Recall programmes — the chemistry test tables, biology definitions, formulae not provided in the examination — fit well into short post-Iftar sessions, and content teaching does not. The final weeks then run on timed papers and residual errors only.

sections.heading: Results, remarks and the resit cycle with real dates
paragraphs: What happens after results day is the part of the calendar families are least prepared for, and it has published dates that can be planned around. On the Pearson Edexcel route, June 2026 International GCSE results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official timetable is the only version to plan around.

The first decision after a short grade is whether to query the mark. Enquiries about results, including remarks, are submitted by the school rather than by the family, and the windows are set by the awarding body and are short. If a grade sits one mark below a boundary and a sixth-form place depends on it, that conversation with the examinations officer needs to happen within days of results day, not weeks.

The second decision is whether to resit. UAE candidates resit in November on both the Cambridge and Pearson routes; the February/March series is offered to India only and is not available. The crucial practical point is that a November result reaches students in January, mid-academic-year. Before entering, get written confirmation from the receiving sixth form that a January grade satisfies their offer, because some will hold a place on that basis and some will not.

The third is the mechanics. A candidate who has left the school may need to enter as a private candidate through an approved examination centre, and the centre sets both the fee and the deadline, which falls well before the series. A resit revision programme should therefore be built backwards from that entry date rather than from the examination date. IB Gram is not an examination centre and cannot enter a candidate; the family arranges entry through a school or an approved centre.

sections.heading: Ramadan against the IGCSE spring term
paragraphs: The spring term of Year 11 is where a Dubai IGCSE plan most often comes apart, and the reason is that three things compete for the same weeks: mock follow-up, the final content push, and the Ramadan period. Almost no tutoring page in this market mentions the third, which is strange given that it reshapes both the school day and the family evening in the run-up to a summer series.

What changes in practice is the shape of the day rather than the amount of work possible. School hours shorten. Afternoon concentration is lower. The productive window for focused study moves to after Iftar. For a Year 11 student that collides with precisely the period when full-length timed paper practice should be at its most intense, because a three-hour paper at four in the afternoon is not a realistic proposition and a three-hour paper at ten at night is not much better.

The planning response has two halves. Front-load the long papers: if Ramadan falls before the series, full timed papers should start earlier in the spring than a September plan would have assumed, so that several have been sat before the period begins. And change the work rather than pausing it: short post-Iftar sessions between 20:30 and 22:00 are well suited to recall testing, reviewing a paper the student sat earlier, and marking work against a scheme. New content and long papers belong either side.

Recall work in particular fits this window unusually well. Chemistry qualitative analysis tables, biology definitions credited against specific wording, physics formulae not provided in the examination — all of it is short, repetitive and does not require sustained concentration. A student who uses the Ramadan weeks to take those three things from recognition to blank recall arrives at the series with a block of marks secured, which is a better use of the period than a frustrated attempt to carry on as normal.

sections.heading: What support costs across the two years, by stage
paragraphs: Pricing an IGCSE by the hour hides the decision that matters, which is when to spend. The need is uneven: groundwork in Year 10 is cheap and high-leverage, the post-mock window in Year 11 is the single most productive block available, and a resit programme is the most expensive because the student has no school timetable holding the structure.

The published Dubai bands, read in October 2026: Tutopiya from AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65 at the entry level; Unitors IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; Bestimate's 2026 rate table at AED 150-300 for qualified online subject tutors, AED 180-350 for in-home one-to-one and AED 200-450 or above for IGCSE and IB specialists, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500 once travel is included; TutorChase at AED 270; BartyED at AED 650 at the premium end.

A family with a fixed budget almost always does better spreading it across Year 10 groundwork and the post-mock block than concentrating all of it in May, because May can only buy technique and timing while Year 10 can still buy fluency and a tier.

Monthly, Bestimate's estimates for one weekly hour run roughly AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or above for exam-year specialist support, and published packages in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. IB Gram publishes no fixed rate here because subject, tier and urgency move it. sections.heading: Scheduling a Motor City week, and the format that allows it
paragraphs: Motor City has an advantage most of this corridor does not: GEMS Metropole School is inside the community, so IGCSE students here have a short school run and are home early. A 16:30 session start is realistic, which matters for a fluency programme because short early sessions work better than long late ones. Families driving back from Dubai Hills, Arabian Ranches or the wider Dubailand schools generally want 17:30 or later.

That earlier availability makes short frequent sessions practical, which is the right shape for most of the work this page describes. Three 45-minute mathematics sessions a fortnight beats one long weekly hour for manipulation speed. Daily recall testing with weekly marking beats a single revision session. Four alternative-to-practical sessions in a fortnight beats four spread over two months.

A visiting tutor cannot deliver that shape. Forty to sixty minutes of travel each way in term traffic means a two-hour minimum booking to justify the journey, and a latest workable start of roughly 18:30. The published premium for the visit is AED 30-150 an hour over the equivalent online band, and what it buys is presence rather than teaching time.

Presence is nonetheless the right purchase for some students, and it is worth saying so plainly: a younger child who cannot self-manage a screen, or a student whose written method needs correcting as it is produced. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE — that is an India-only service — so the comparison below is here to inform a decision rather than to argue a family out of one.

sections.heading: Equivalency timing, and the claims nobody should make
paragraphs: There is a documentary calendar alongside the academic one, and for a family planning on a UAE university it is worth reading in Year 10 rather than discovering in Year 12. Ministry of Education equivalency is the recognition of a foreign secondary certificate, required for admission to UAE institutions and for some employment routes, and the British-track rules are published and specific.

A student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. They must additionally show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One competitor page ranking for UAE searches states that six IGCSE subjects are required; the published figure is five, and planning around six over-subscribes a child by a subject's worth of attention.

For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requires at least 450 in SAT Math before applying. Two boundaries apply throughout: IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency — it is a Ministry process handled with the Ministry or the emirate's attestation authority — and tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, admission or progression.

And the claims we do not make. Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, with ADEK covering Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA covering Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge covering Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education covering Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership from any of them, nor from Cambridge or Pearson, holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, is not an examination centre and has no UAE office. Private tutoring is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students, and individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws — no fine schedule is published, so no amount appears here.

process.title: Get the dates from the examinations officer
process.description: Board, syllabus code and tier per subject, the centre's internal entry deadline, the mock window and the Cambridge zone. One email returns all of it and it converts a vague year into a list of dates that can be planned against.

process.title: Say which stage you are at
process.description: Year 9 options, Year 10 groundwork, post-mock Year 11, final spring or a November resit. The right purchase is different at each, and naming the stage is what prevents a family buying the final-spring product in Year 10 or the reverse.

process.title: Free diagnostic lesson
process.description: A full session at no charge spent on the student's own marked work. The output is a list of habits with a session count against each — answering without working, rounding partway, command-term mismatch, running out of time — rather than a list of weak topics.

process.title: Place the work where the calendar allows it
process.description: Fluency in Year 10. Technique straight after the mocks. The alternative-to-practical block before Ramadan. Recall testing through the Ramadan weeks in short post-Iftar sessions. Full timed papers front-loaded if the period falls before the series.

process.title: Review against the next real paper
process.description: Progress is judged on the school's next marked assessment rather than on our exercises. If the habits named in the diagnosis are still appearing, either the work between sessions is not happening or the diagnosis was wrong, and both are better established early than in May.

whyPoints.title: The calendar quoted, not paraphrased
whyPoints.description: Cambridge runs June and November with the February/March series offered to India only. Pearson November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026 and June 2026 results on 20 August 2026. Those are the awarding bodies' own published positions, and we link the live timetable rather than restating dates that can change.

whyPoints.title: Closures named before they happen
whyPoints.description: Year 9 closes the subject list, Year 10 closes the tier, and the entry deadline closes the board and code. We say which of those are still open at the point you contact us, which is the difference between a plan and a hope.

whyPoints.title: Ramadan built into the plan
whyPoints.description: Shortened school days and post-Iftar evenings change what work fits, and the period often falls just before a summer series. Front-load the long papers, use short late sessions for recall and review, and arrange post-Iftar timing at the start of term rather than mid-period.

whyPoints.title: The mock treated as the key data point
whyPoints.description: A marked mock is the best evidence a family will get and most of it is discarded. We read the scripts and produce a list of habits with session counts attached, because that is what converts a score into something actionable.

whyPoints.title: Spending shown by stage
whyPoints.description: Year 10 groundwork can still buy fluency and a tier; May can only buy technique and timing. Pricing by stage makes that visible, and a fixed budget spread across both usually beats the same money spent entirely at the end.

whyPoints.title: The resit route stated accurately
whyPoints.description: November is the UAE resit series, a result reaches students in January, and entry goes through your school or an approved centre rather than through us. We tell you to get the receiving school's acceptance of a January grade in writing before entering.

faqs.question: Will an IGCSE tutor come to our villa in Motor City?
faqs.answer: Independent tutors and agencies in Dubai do offer it, at AED 180-350 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 rate table and up to about AED 500 for independent home tutors with travel included. IB Gram does not, anywhere in the UAE. For a Motor City family the online format also allows a session shape that a visiting tutor cannot: 16:30 starts for a GEMS Metropole student with a short school run, 45-minute lengths, three short sessions a fortnight for fluency work, and post-Iftar slots during Ramadan.

faqs.question: When does the IGCSE entry deadline actually fall?
faqs.answer: Months before the first paper, and it is handled by the examination centre to the awarding body's schedule rather than by the family. By that date the board, the syllabus code and the tier of entry are fixed in writing for every subject, which is why the tier conversation belongs in Year 10 and not in the spring of Year 11. Ask the examinations officer for the centre's own internal deadline, which is usually earlier than the board's, because that is the date your family actually has to meet.

faqs.question: What should a Year 11 student be doing in each part of the year?
faqs.answer: Autumn is coverage: every subject through its syllabus once before the mock, because a mock sat on partly taught content produces a misleading score. Winter is reading the marked mocks and turning them into a list of habits. Early spring is technique drill, the alternative-to-practical block and starting a recall programme. The Ramadan weeks suit short post-Iftar review and recall. Late spring is full timed papers and the error log. The final fortnight is residual errors only, never new topics.

faqs.question: How should a Dubai family plan revision around Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Front-load and change the work rather than trying to continue unchanged. School hours shorten, afternoon concentration drops and the productive window moves to after Iftar, which collides with the period when full-length timed paper practice should be heaviest. So sit several long papers before the period begins, and use short post-Iftar sessions between 20:30 and 22:00 for recall testing, review and marking work against a scheme. Recall content in particular — chemistry test tables, biology definitions, unprovided physics formulae — fits those weeks very well.

faqs.question: If a grade comes back one mark short, what happens next?
faqs.answer: Move quickly, because the windows are short and the school has to act, not you. Enquiries about results, including remarks, are submitted by the centre to the awarding body within a board-set window measured in weeks rather than months. If a sixth-form place depends on a boundary mark, that conversation with the examinations officer belongs in the days immediately after results day. Pearson's June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026, which gives a sense of how little time sits between results and the start of a new year.

faqs.question: Is a November resit worth it if the result arrives in January?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what the grade is needed for. For a Ministry of Education equivalency file a January result is usually fine. For a sixth-form place it may not be, because the academic year is already underway: Pearson's November 2025 International GCSE results reached students on 22 January 2026. So the step before entering is written confirmation from the receiving school that a January grade satisfies their offer and that the place will be held. Some will, some will not, and the answer changes the decision entirely.

faqs.question: Can my child sit the February or March IGCSE series from Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only, so no UAE candidate sits it, and a revision plan built around a March examination window is built on a date that does not apply to them. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. What does run in March, May and October are Cambridge Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests, which are a different assessment entirely and are sometimes what has been half-remembered from a search result.

faqs.question: What is the Cambridge zone timetable and how do we check ours?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Your examinations officer knows which zone your centre is in, and it is worth asking before you print a timetable or book any travel, because a date from another zone's version can be out by a day or more.

faqs.question: How early should we start tutoring for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Year 10 if the aim is to change a grade, and Year 9 if the aim is to change the subject list. Fluency, method discipline and recall habits are built by frequency over months, which makes Year 10 the cheapest and most effective window, and it is also the year in which marked Extended-standard evidence can still influence a tier decision. Starting in the spring of Year 11 is a legitimate purchase but it buys a narrower set of things: technique, timing, recall and residual content, with the ceiling and the subject list already fixed.

faqs.question: What does a term of IGCSE support cost in Motor City?
faqs.answer: At published Dubai bands, twelve weekly sessions over a term comes to roughly AED 1,800-3,600 at the AED 150-300 qualified band or AED 2,400-5,400 at the AED 200-450 specialist band. A post-mock block of eight sessions is AED 1,200-3,600, and a four-session alternative-to-practical block AED 600-1,800. Those are other providers' published figures read in October 2026. The more useful question is which stage to spend at, because Year 10 can still buy fluency and a tier while May can only buy technique.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle two subjects for a Year 11 student?
faqs.answer: Often, and it is worth testing rather than assuming. Many specialists cover two related subjects to a high standard — two sciences, or mathematics and physics — and where they genuinely do, continuity improves and the student spends less time re-explaining context. Few cover three at Extended level with equal command of the mark schemes. Ask directly which syllabus codes a tutor has taught and which they have marked, and treat a general claim about being good at science or maths as a no rather than a yes.

faqs.question: Does GEMS Metropole School being in Motor City change the scheduling?
faqs.answer: Yes, favourably. A short school run means students are home early and a 16:30 session start is realistic, which suits fluency and recall work because short early sessions are more productive than long late ones. That also makes three 45-minute sessions a fortnight practical, which is the right shape for manipulation speed in mathematics. Families driving back from Dubai Hills, Arabian Ranches or the wider Dubailand schools generally need 17:30 or later, and the later slots across this corridor fill first.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does a UAE university route actually need?
faqs.answer: Five on the Ministry of Education British track, not six. The published rule is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A-Level at no less than E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. A competitor page ranking for UAE searches states six, which over-subscribes a child by a subject. Sixth-form entry adds its own thresholds, usually grade 6 or 7 in each subject to be continued, and those are often the binding constraint.

faqs.question: Can you enter my child for a resit if the school will not?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is a tutoring service, not an examination centre, and we hold no approval, accreditation or partnership from Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or MoHRE. Entries are made by a school or by an approved private-candidate centre, which sets its own fees and deadlines, and those deadlines fall well before the series. We will help build the revision programme backwards from whatever entry date the centre gives you, but the entry itself has to be arranged by the family.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-motor-city.closingHeading: Find out what is still open before you buy anything
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-motor-city.closingBody: An IGCSE is decided by a sequence of closures. Year 9 fixes the subject list. Year 10 fixes the tier and the grade ceiling. The entry deadline fixes the board and the code months before a paper is sat. After that, what remains movable is technique, timing, habits and recall — real gains, but a narrower set than a family in the spring of Year 11 usually imagines. Ask the examinations officer for the codes, the tiers, the centre's entry deadline and your Cambridge zone, send a marked mock, and take the free diagnostic lesson while the answer still has options in it.

Each profile names the board and the papers that person works with, so a request for 0625 Physics Paper 4 goes to someone who has marked Paper 4 rather than to a general science tutor.

intro.heading: What this term has to achieve for a Mudon Year 11
paragraphs: An IGCSE year has a shape, and most tutoring arrives too late in it. The autumn term decides which tier a student sits and whether the Extended paper is realistic. The spring term is where past papers either become routine or never start. The weeks immediately before the series are for error patterns, not new content. A family in Mudon reading this in the middle of that cycle needs to know which of those three phases they are in, because the right eight weeks of work looks completely different in each.

Mudon sits off Al Qudra Road in Dubailand, a villa and townhouse community with no secondary school inside its own boundaries. Students travel to Jebel Ali School in DAMAC Hills, GEMS Metropole in Motor City, South View School on the Remraam side, Ranches Primary and then onward, or further along Al Khail Road to Al Barsha South. The practical consequence for a Year 11 is a long day: home after four, homework from a school that sets plenty of it, and an evening that has to hold revision somewhere.

The exam calendar itself is simpler than parents fear, provided the right document is read. Cambridge runs its International GCSE exams in a June series and a November series. The February and March series is offered in India only, so an Indian timetable circulating in a parents' group is the wrong paper for a Dubai centre. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that the correct zone timetable must be used, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version.

Entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers, and this is where families lose options rather than marks. By the time a student realises in March that a subject is going badly, the entry is lodged and the tier is fixed. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. That January lag is the one to plan around if a resit is in view, because it lands in the middle of the next academic year.

IB Gram works this as online one-to-one tuition, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, so a session can sit at 4.30pm or after 8pm depending on the evening. Home visits are a service IB Gram offers in India only, and nothing here promises a tutor at a Mudon address. What the online format buys a family on this side of Dubailand is a tutor chosen for the board and the paper rather than for the drive, and a slot that can move when a bus is late.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-mudon.programmesIntro: IGCSE is not one qualification but a pair of board routes with a tiering decision inside each. Getting that structure right matters more in Year 10 than any amount of revision in Year 11.

programmes.name: Cambridge International GCSE
programmes.description: Two-year linear courses assessed at the end, with Core and Extended tiers in several subjects. Core caps at grade C or 5; Extended reaches A* or 9. Subjects carry syllabus codes a parent can look up: 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 First Language English.
programmes.countryNote: Most British-curriculum schools serving Mudon run Cambridge, and the tier decision is usually made in Year 10 on the basis of Year 9 attainment. If a student is placed on Core and later wants a science A Level, that conversation needs to happen with the school early, not in the spring of Year 11.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes run 4MA1 Mathematics, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology, 4EA1 English Language A. Mathematics is tiered Foundation and Higher. Several subjects are available in both linear and modular patterns depending on the centre, which changes when a student can bank a result.
programmes.countryNote: Some Dubailand schools run Pearson for maths and Cambridge for sciences, or offer a choice by subject. A Mudon family should confirm board and code per subject rather than assuming one board across the timetable, because the past papers a tutor sets depend entirely on that answer.

programmes.name: Year 11 into Diploma or A Level
programmes.description: IGCSE results decide sixth-form options, and the thresholds are school-specific. A Higher Level science in the IB Diploma or an A Level in the same subject usually expects a strong grade at Extended or Higher tier, and the gap between an IGCSE 7 and the first term of Higher Level is wider than most students expect.
programmes.countryNote: Mudon students who stay in the British system and those who move to an IB Diploma school in Dubai Hills or The Sustainable City face different bridging work. Both benefit from the summer between Year 11 and Year 12 being used, which is the cheapest tutoring window in the year.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-mudon.subjectsIntro: These are the International GCSE subjects Dubailand families ask about most. Each note names what the papers test and where marks go missing, because the papers are the plan.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Extended and Higher reach the harder algebra, trigonometry and probability. Marks go missing for unshown working on multi-step questions and for rounding too early. Past-paper routine beats topic revision from about February onwards.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism are where grades split. Students lose marks stating what happens without the because, and on practical-style questions that ask for a method a reader could repeat.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles calculations, electrolysis and organic chemistry. The recurring loss is in equations: unbalanced, or balanced without state symbols where the mark scheme required them. Qualitative analysis tests are easy marks routinely dropped.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: Long-answer questions reward sequence and terminology. Describing osmosis without water potential, or respiration without naming the products, costs marks that content knowledge alone should have earned.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Sciences
subjects.description: The compressed route many Dubai schools use. Content is narrower than three separate sciences but the paper structure is less forgiving, because one weak topic has nowhere to hide across fewer questions.

subjects.name: English Language (0500 / 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the reading responses. Students who summarise instead of analysing, or who write in a register the task did not ask for, lose more than those with weaker vocabulary.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Extract-based and essay questions on set texts. Quotation accuracy and sustained argument matter more than plot recall, and timing is the most common cause of an incomplete final answer.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Case-study papers where the marks sit in application to the named business. Definitions earn one mark; applying a concept to the stimulus material earns the rest, and that is a trainable habit.

subjects.name: Arabic as a second language
subjects.description: Reading, writing and oral components. Separate from the Arabic that KHDA requires every Dubai private school to teach, which runs alongside the IGCSE timetable rather than replacing it.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Pseudocode, trace tables and data representation. Students who can code in Python still lose marks writing pseudocode in the board's expected form, and trace tables reward slow, mechanical working.

sections.heading: The IGCSE year, counted backwards from the series
paragraphs: Pick the series your child is entered for and count back. Twelve months out, subject choices and tiers are being settled in Year 10 on the strength of Year 9 work. Nine months out, the school lodges entries and the tier stops being a conversation. Six months out, mocks are sat and they are the single best diagnostic a family will get. Three months out, the work should be timed papers rather than notes. Six weeks out, it should be nothing but error patterns from marked scripts.

Most tutoring requests from Dubailand arrive at the three-month mark, which is late but workable, and a meaningful number arrive at six weeks, which limits what is possible to technique and triage. The difference is not effort; it is which levers are still available. At six months a tier can sometimes still be changed with the school. At six weeks it cannot, and the honest plan becomes maximising marks inside the paper the student is entered for.

The dated anchors are worth writing down because they make the lag concrete. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A November resit therefore returns a grade in the middle of the following academic year, which matters if a sixth-form place depends on it.

Always read the live official timetable rather than a restated date. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and they can be revised, and Cambridge's zone system means two centres in different zones sit the same subject on different days.

sections.heading: What eight focused weeks can and cannot change
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the most commonly requested block and the most commonly oversold one. What it reliably changes is technique: working shown, command terms obeyed, timing managed, equations balanced with state symbols, graphs drawn with the axes the question asked for. Those are habits, and habits move inside eight weeks because they are drilled rather than learned.

What eight weeks does not do is rebuild two years of missing content. A Year 11 who has never understood moles will not reach a confident Extended Chemistry grade in eight weeks, and saying so is more useful than promising otherwise. What is achievable in that case is a sharp focus on the topics with the highest mark density in the papers the student will actually sit, accepting that some marks are being written off deliberately.

The way to tell which case you are in is a marked mock paper. Scattered small losses across every question point to technique and respond quickly. Entire questions left blank or abandoned point to content, and content needs a longer runway. A tutor who asks for the mock script before quoting a plan is doing the right thing; one who proposes a fixed programme before seeing any work is selling a package.

No tutor can promise a grade, and this page makes no such promise. What can be committed to is that the hour is spent on the marks that are still available, chosen from evidence rather than from a syllabus checklist.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher: the decision that sets the ceiling
paragraphs: Tiering is the most consequential IGCSE decision and the least discussed. In Cambridge subjects with two tiers, Core caps the available grade; Extended reaches the top. In Pearson Mathematics, Foundation and Higher work the same way. A student placed on the lower tier cannot earn a grade they were never entered for, however well they perform on the day.

Schools place students on evidence, and they place conservatively because a student who sits Extended and collapses ends up worse off than one who sits Core and does well. That caution is reasonable, but it is based on attainment at the time of the decision, usually late in Year 10. If a student's trajectory changes after that, the case for moving up has to be made with work, and it has to be made early enough that the entry can still be amended.

The practical consequence for a Mudon family is that the autumn term of Year 10 is worth more tutoring money than the spring term of Year 11, and almost nobody spends it that way. A student working at the top of Core who wants a science A Level or a Higher Level Diploma subject needs Extended, and the work that gets them there is harder topics early, not revision later.

Ask the school three questions: which tier is my child currently expected to sit, what evidence would change that, and when is the last date the entry can be amended. The answers turn a vague worry into a dated plan.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition costs in Dubai, and what the drive adds
paragraphs: Take the cheapest end first, because that is where most families start looking. Budget online tutors and university students advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya AED 33 to 52. That tier can work for routine maths practice with a motivated student. It is less suited to an Extended science paper eight weeks out, where the value is in a tutor recognising a mark-scheme pattern.

The qualified online band sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Subject specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 650 at BartyED. In-home visits are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the price, Bestimate's range being AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500.

Across a month, Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts a weekly hour at AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Packages in the market include AED 799 monthly for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 monthly for four two-hour in-home sessions. For context, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27.

These are market figures with their sources named, not IB Gram prices. The relevant comparison from Mudon is that the in-home band carries the Al Qudra Road drive inside it, and the online band does not.

sections.heading: Mocks: the diagnostic most families throw away
paragraphs: Mock results arrive, a number is read, a conversation happens, and the scripts go in a drawer. That is the single most common waste in an IGCSE year, because the scripts contain the only specific information anyone has about where the marks went. A grade tells you the size of the problem. The script tells you its shape.

Read properly, a mock paper separates four different failures that feel identical to a student. There is content absence, where a question was never attempted. There is technique loss, where the method was right and the presentation lost the marks. There is timing collapse, visible as a strong first half and an abandoned last page. And there is misreading, where the student answered a different question from the one asked, usually because a command term was skipped.

Each of those has a different fix and a different timescale. Timing collapse responds inside two weeks to papers sat with a clock. Misreading responds to command-term drilling. Technique loss responds to marking the student's own work against the scheme until the pattern is obvious to them. Content absence is the slow one, and it is the only one that genuinely needs months.
A first session built on a mock script is worth three built on a conversation. It is also the reason we ask for one marked piece of work before anything is scheduled.

One caution about mock grades themselves: schools set mocks at different levels of severity, and a mock marked harshly to motivate a cohort is not a prediction. Treat the number as a rough position and the annotations as the real information. Where a school publishes its own grade boundaries for the mock, compare them against the board's most recent published boundaries for the same paper rather than assuming they match.
bullets: A grade gives the size of the problem; the script gives its shape
Content absence, technique loss, timing collapse and misreading look identical to a student

sections.heading: The five subjects that matter for UAE equivalency
paragraphs: Beyond the grades themselves, an IGCSE timetable has a second job: satisfying Ministry of Education equivalency for a student who may later apply to a UAE university. On the British track, a student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The detail that catches families out is which subjects count. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, even though Dubai private schools must teach them. A student who assumes those two carry part of the load can arrive at the count short. One page currently ranking for these searches states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the published rule is five, and getting that right matters more than any ranking.

For the American track the requirements are different again, with English proficiency shown by an IELTS academic score of 5, a TOEFL iBT score of 61, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics by at least 450 in the SAT Math test. For the IB, no points threshold should be taken from a tutoring page without being read on the Ministry's own site.

IB Gram does not perform equivalency or attestation and does not guarantee any result from it. The process belongs to the Ministry and the relevant emirate authority, and families should use their official channels. Nor is tutoring required for equivalency; the subjects and grades are what the rule asks for.
bullets: Five accredited IGCSE subjects at grade E or 3 or above, plus A Level or AS Level at E
Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five
American track: SAT Math 450, and IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT 450 reading and writing
No IB points figure should be published without a Ministry source

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the IGCSE timetable
paragraphs: Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies regardless of the international curriculum it is licensed for, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. For a Year 11 in Mudon, that means these subjects sit on the timetable next to the IGCSE courses and compete for the same evening hours.

The rules around them are specific. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and moral, social and cultural studies.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. For these subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited, which is a real constraint on how any tutoring in them can be described: support means working with the school's own material, not substituting something else.

Practically, families in this belt treat the mandatory subjects as a scheduling problem rather than an attainment one, and the fix is usually sequencing the week so that IGCSE past-paper work does not land on the same evening as an Arabic assessment.
bullets: Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies are required in all Dubai private schools
Separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs are required; combined classes are prohibited
Instructional time is counted in 40-minute units, with a 25-minute minimum advised per lesson

sections.heading: Coursework, permits and what a tutor is allowed to do
paragraphs: International GCSE carries less internally assessed work than the IB Diploma, but where it exists the boundary is the same. A tutor may teach the subject, explain what the assessment criteria reward, critique an approach and mark a student's own draft against published descriptors. A tutor may not write, complete or produce the work. That holds for English coursework where a centre offers it, for science practical write-ups and for any project component.

Board material has its own boundary. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson. Sessions reference the official pages and link to them; nothing is redistributed, and no unreleased material exists to be shared regardless of what anyone claims.

On the tutor's side, the UAE requires a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit came in under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service listing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted.

One arrangement to avoid: Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar bar. If a teacher offers to tutor your child privately, ask whether their school and the permit allow it.
bullets: Tutors teach, critique and mark; they do not produce assessed work
Official syllabus and past-paper material is linked, never redistributed
MoHRE private tuition permit: free, two years, two working days to issue

process.title: Name the board and the code
process.description: The first useful detail is not the subject but the syllabus code: 0580 or 4MA1, 0625 or 4PH1, and whether the entry is Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher. That single line determines which past papers the tutor sets, and schools in this belt do not all use the same board across the timetable.

process.title: Send a marked mock or past paper
process.description: One marked script shows whether the losses are content, technique, timing or misreading, and those four problems have different fixes and different timescales. Sending it before the trial lesson means the first hour is spent working rather than diagnosing.

process.title: Agree the block, not just the hour
process.description: Term-time weekly, an eight-week paper block or a holiday intensive are different products. Which one fits depends on how far the series is away and what the script showed. We say which we think it is, including when the honest answer is that less is needed than you expected.

process.title: Free trial, then a fixed slot
process.description: A trial lesson over live video at no cost, before any payment, so the student meets the tutor. After that the slot is fixed on Gulf Standard Time around the school run, and it can move during Ramadan or an exam fortnight without a travel charge attached.

process.title: Check against the school's calendar monthly
process.description: Session notes go to the parent, and the plan is reviewed against the school's own deadlines and the entry dates every few weeks. Mocks, coursework deadlines and the series itself each change what the hour should be doing, and the plan should change with them rather than run on autopilot.

whyPoints.title: The plan starts from a date
whyPoints.description: Every plan is counted backwards from the series the student is entered for, with the tier, the mocks and the entry deadline marked on it. A plan without those dates is a subscription, and families in this belt have usually bought one of those before.

whyPoints.title: Board and code are confirmed, not assumed
whyPoints.description: Dubailand schools mix Cambridge and Pearson across subjects, and the papers a tutor sets are worthless if they belong to the other board. Confirming the code per subject takes one message and prevents a term of misaimed practice.

whyPoints.title: Marked scripts drive the sessions
whyPoints.description: Work is chosen from what the student's own marked papers show rather than from a syllabus checklist. Content absence, technique loss, timing collapse and misreading each get a different response, and only the script tells you which you have.

whyPoints.title: Rates on this page are sourced market figures
whyPoints.description: Every AED band here is attributed to the provider or table that published it, so you can check it before spending anything. None of them is an IB Gram price list, and no competitor figure is quoted without naming who published it.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling absorbs a Dubailand evening
whyPoints.description: A late bus from DAMAC Hills, a fixture at school, a slot moving after Iftar during Ramadan: none of those cost anything, because nobody is driving to Al Salam or Arabella. The session starts when the student sits down.

whyPoints.title: No regulator or board claims
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no KHDA permit, no ADEK registration, no board affiliation and no UAE office. Where a page in this market attaches a regulator's name to its tutors, that is a claim worth checking rather than a credential.

faqs.question: Will an IGCSE tutor travel to our house in Mudon?
faqs.answer: Not one arranged through IB Gram. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only. Independent tutors and agencies in Dubai do offer visits, quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with the travel inside the price according to Bestimate's Dubai cost table and the rates home tutors advertise. From a Mudon address, which sits off the main tutor corridors through Motor City and Dubai Sports City, that loading is noticeable. The online route buys you a tutor chosen for the board and the paper instead of for the drive.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the series should we start tutoring?
faqs.answer: It depends which problem you have. For technique losses, eight weeks of two sessions a week is a sensible block and can move timing, working shown and command-term discipline measurably. For missing content, three to six months is realistic, because foundational gaps do not close under pressure. For a tier decision, the autumn term of Year 10 is the moment, long before anyone feels urgency. A marked mock script tells you which case applies, which is why we ask for one before proposing a block rather than selling a fixed package to everybody.

faqs.question: Which series does a Dubai centre actually enter students for?
faqs.answer: For Cambridge, UAE candidates sit the June and November series. The February and March series is offered in India only, so an Indian timetable shared in a parents' group is the wrong document for a Dubai school. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that the correct zone timetable must be used, warning it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. Ask your school which zone it sits in rather than assuming.

faqs.question: Can my son move from Core to Extended partway through Year 11?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and only with the school. Tier entries are lodged months before the papers, and once they are in, the available grade range is fixed whatever happens on the day. If your son's work has improved since the decision was made, the case has to be put with evidence and early enough for the entry to be amended. Ask the school three questions: which tier is he currently entered for, what evidence would change that, and what is the last date an amendment is possible. Those answers convert a worry into something actionable.

faqs.question: What does an eight-week block realistically change in IGCSE Maths?
faqs.answer: It changes how marks are earned on questions he can already partly do. Working shown on multi-step problems, rounding held to the end, graphs drawn with the axes the question specified, time allocated so the last page is attempted: those are habits and they respond to drilling inside eight weeks. What it will not do is build algebraic fluency that was never there. If a marked paper shows whole questions abandoned rather than scattered small losses, the honest plan is longer, and we would say so before taking a booking.

faqs.question: Do you cover both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel for the sciences?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the distinction matters more than parents expect. Cambridge 0625 Physics and Pearson 4PH1 cover similar ground with different paper structures, different question styles and different mark-scheme conventions, so practice from the wrong board teaches the wrong habits. Tell us the code for each subject, and the tutor sets papers from that board only. Where a Dubailand school runs one board for maths and another for sciences, which happens, the plan simply follows the codes rather than assuming a single board across the whole timetable.

faqs.question: How much should we budget monthly for one IGCSE subject from Mudon?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle band, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Market packages include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are published market figures rather than IB Gram prices. For a single subject on a term-time weekly hour, the middle band is the realistic planning number.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper university-student tutor good enough for Extended science?
faqs.answer: For routine practice with a self-motivated student, often yes. Budget online tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya AED 33 to 52, and that can be sensible value for working through exercises. Close to a series on an Extended paper it is usually false economy, because the value then lies in someone recognising a mark-scheme pattern in a marked script and knowing which three topics carry the most available marks. Ask any tutor at any price which papers they have marked.

faqs.question: How do mocks help if the exams are still months away?
faqs.answer: The mock script is the best diagnostic a family gets all year, and most of them are read as a single grade and then filed. Read properly, a script separates content absence, technique loss, timing collapse and misreading, which feel identical to the student and need completely different fixes. Timing collapse shows as a strong start and an abandoned last page; misreading shows as a good answer to the wrong question. Bring the marked papers to a trial lesson and the first hour becomes work rather than diagnosis.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do UAE universities count for equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track, Ministry of Education equivalency asks for five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five, which is the detail that catches families short. One page ranking for these searches states six subjects are required; the published figure is five. IB Gram does not perform equivalency, and the Ministry's own channels are the place to verify it.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor help with a Year 11 into Year 12 transition?
faqs.answer: Usually, and the summer between the two years is the cheapest useful tutoring window in the whole cycle. The gap between an IGCSE grade and the first term of an A Level or a Higher Level Diploma subject is wider than most students expect, particularly in Maths, Physics and Chemistry, where notation and expected independence both change. Six to eight sessions across the break on the specific bridging content stops September being a shock. Tell us which route the student is taking, because bridging into Higher Level Diploma differs from bridging into A Level.

faqs.question: Do the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons affect the IGCSE timetable?
faqs.answer: They sit alongside it. Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies whatever international curriculum it is licensed for, with KHDA's requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are prohibited. Instructional time is counted in 40-minute units. For most families the effect on tutoring is a scheduling one: avoid stacking past-paper work on the same evening as an Arabic assessment.

faqs.question: What happens if we need to pause lessons for travel or exams?
faqs.answer: Say so and the slot pauses. Because no travel is being arranged, a gap costs nothing to accommodate and the same slot can usually be held. Families in this belt commonly pause during the exam fortnight itself, when another hour of input helps less than sleep does, and during summer travel. During Ramadan, sessions more often move than pause, with slots after Iftar being the most requested. The plan is reviewed every few weeks anyway, so a pause becomes part of it rather than an interruption to it.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Dubai need a licence, and can we check it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and you can ask directly. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service listing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. A tutoring business with premises in Dubai needs a separate KHDA Educational Services Permit, which IB Gram does not hold.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-mudon.closingHeading: Put a date on it and work backwards
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-mudon.closingBody: The useful first step from Mudon is not choosing a tutor; it is writing down the series your child is entered for, the tier, the mock dates and the coursework deadlines, and then deciding what the next eight weeks have to achieve. Send that list with the syllabus codes and one marked paper, and a free trial lesson over live video is arranged before any payment is taken. If the honest answer is that less tutoring is needed than you expected, you will hear that too. Lessons are online; no tutor is sent to a UAE address.
