dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-muhaisnah.tutorsIntro: The tutors matched to Muhaisnah IGCSE enquiries teach to a named syllabus code rather than to a general subject, and they plan a week around the student's school calendar rather than their own.

intro.heading: Working backwards from when your child actually gets home
paragraphs: Start with the clock, because in this neighbourhood the clock decides everything. A Year 10 or Year 11 student living in Muhaisnah is very unlikely to attend school in Muhaisnah. The British-curriculum schools that run IGCSE sit in Al Qusais, Mirdif, Al Warqa, Al Garhoud and Dubai Festival City, which means a bus or a car journey at both ends of the day. Add the Al Ittihad Road and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road afternoon peak and a school day ending at 2.45pm routinely becomes a front door opening at 4.15pm or later.

That single fact invalidates most tutoring plans before they begin. A 4.30pm booking looks sensible on paper and fails in practice, every week, because the student arrives hungry, hot and ten minutes late. Families then conclude the tutor is not working. In our experience the slot was wrong, not the tutor, and the correction is cheap: move the session to 6pm or 7.30pm, accept that homework happens after it rather than before, and the same tutor suddenly looks competent.

The second thing the school run does is compress the week unevenly. Most British-curriculum schools in eastern Dubai run co-curricular and intervention sessions on particular afternoons, so Monday and Wednesday may end an hour later than Tuesday. Year 11 students frequently have school-run revision clinics attached to one weekday. A fixed weekly tutoring slot has to dodge all of that, and the only way to choose it correctly is to look at the actual school calendar rather than guess.

Then there is the home-tutoring question itself, which deserves a straight answer rather than a sales line. In-home IGCSE tutoring in Dubai is a real market and it is priced accordingly: published bands put in-home one-to-one visits at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, travel included. What the premium buys from a Muhaisnah address is mainly convenience, and what it costs is a shortlist limited to tutors already driving this side of the city. IB Gram does not sell that service here. Home visiting is an India-only service for us; in the UAE every lesson is live, one-to-one and over video.

The rest of this page is the practical material. A table of the schools this catchment feeds with their typical end times and the first workable session slot. A table of the evening slots themselves, with what each is good and bad for. A table of Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel syllabus codes so you can check which board your child is actually entered for. Then the exam series counted backwards, what happens to science practicals when lessons are online, and the five-subject Ministry of Education equivalency rule that decides whether an IGCSE set is accepted for a UAE university application.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-muhaisnah.programmesIntro: Muhaisnah IGCSE enquiries come from three stages of a British-curriculum school, and the scheduling problem is different at each. Here is how the week looks in practice.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE courses begin, where the foundations that decide Core or Extended entry are built. No external exam, which is precisely why gaps survive here unnoticed. Number fluency, algebraic manipulation and written structure are the three that matter, and a student who reaches Year 10 shaky on negative indices or topic sentences will pay for it twice.
programmes.countryNote: Key Stage 3 students in this catchment finish earlier in the day than Year 11 and often have the least congested evenings. It is the cheapest stage at which to fix something, and the easiest to schedule: a 5.30pm slot twice a week is realistic for a Year 8 in a way it stops being by Year 11.

programmes.name: IGCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Two years of linear courses examined externally, usually seven to ten subjects, with tiering decisions in maths and the sciences and coursework or practical components in some subjects. Grades come out on either the 9-1 or A*-G scale depending on board and subject. Entry decisions are made by the school months before the exam and are hard to reverse late.
programmes.countryNote: Year 10 is when tutoring is cheapest and most effective in this area, and Year 11 is when most families actually start. By the spring of Year 11 the school's own revision programme has already taken the best weekday slots, so a Muhaisnah family usually ends up on a weekend morning or a 7.30pm weekday session.

programmes.name: AS and A Level
programmes.description: Three or four subjects taken in depth, often modular with Pearson and linear with Cambridge. The step up from IGCSE is largest in mathematics and the sciences, where the volume of independent practice required roughly doubles. Universities, including those in the UAE, generally quote their offers in A Level grades with IGCSE results used as a supporting signal.
programmes.countryNote: Sixth-form students in eastern Dubai often have free periods and a later start, which opens up morning and early-afternoon tutoring slots nobody else wants. For a Muhaisnah A Level student that is the easiest scheduling win available, and it avoids the 6pm to 8pm congestion entirely.

programmes.name: Mandatory UAE subjects alongside IGCSE
programmes.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run in every Dubai private school regardless of the licensed curriculum. They occupy real timetable minutes, calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and carry their own homework. They are not optional and they are not assessed by Cambridge or Pearson, which is why families routinely forget them when budgeting a student's week.
programmes.countryNote: For a Muhaisnah student this is the hidden load. A Year 11 carrying nine IGCSE subjects plus three mandatory UAE subjects has very little slack, and adding two tutored subjects at once is how a term gets lost. One subject, properly targeted, is almost always the right starting point here.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-muhaisnah.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Muhaisnah families most often name, with the syllabus most common in this catchment and what the tutoring hour actually has to fix.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1 depending on the school. Extended candidates lose marks on method rather than arithmetic: unlabelled working, a transformation described without naming it, a bearing measured from the wrong north line. The tier decision matters more than any single topic.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1. Electricity and waves do the most damage. Students who can rearrange an equation still lose marks describing what a graph gradient means, and practical-skills questions reward anyone who has actually planned an experiment.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4CH1. Moles, electrolysis and organic families carry the paper. The characteristic failure is a student who has memorised equations and cannot explain a periodic trend, which is exactly what the longer questions ask for.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cambridge 0610 or Pearson 4BI1. Volume of content makes this feel manageable and it is not; the marks sit in command-term precision. Describe, explain and suggest want three different answers, and data questions on unfamiliar experiments reward method literacy.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Science
subjects.description: Cambridge 0654 Coordinated Sciences is a double award covering all three sciences; 0653 Combined Science is a single award. Pearson's double award is 4SD0. Which one your child sits changes the content depth substantially, and schools do not always make the distinction clear to parents.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Cambridge 0500 First Language or 0510 and 0511 as a second language; Pearson 4EA1 for Language A. Directed writing and analysis of unseen texts carry most marks, and the fastest gain is usually learning to plan for four minutes before writing.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Set texts examined on close reading and comparison, with quotation integrated into argument rather than dropped between sentences. Students who know the plot and not the language lose the top band consistently, and that is a teachable rather than an innate gap.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Cambridge 0455 and 0450. Diagram accuracy with labelled axes, then evaluation that weighs two sides and reaches a judgement. Case-study questions punish generic framework recitation, which is what a student revising from notes alone tends to produce.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Cambridge 0478 Computer Science and 0417 ICT are different qualifications with different papers; ICT carries practical assessment. Pseudocode and trace tables are where Computer Science marks go missing, and they are drillable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Cambridge 0460 and 0470. Both reward case studies held with figures and dates attached, and source-based questions in History reward provenance reasoning rather than content recall. Fieldwork and coursework components vary by school, so check before planning.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Cambridge 0606, taken by stronger Extended candidates as a bridge into A Level. It is a genuinely harder paper and students entered for it late struggle, so the useful tutoring question is whether the entry is right rather than how to revise for it.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Offered as an IGCSE subject and separately mandated by KHDA as a school subject. The two are not the same requirement, and Ministry of Education equivalency excludes Arabic and Islamic Education from the five required subjects, which surprises most families.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-muhaisnah.regionsTitle: Schools, bus routes and arrival times around Muhaisnah
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-muhaisnah.regionsIntro: These are the communities whose school runs intersect with Muhaisnah, described by what they do to an afternoon rather than by what they look like.

regions.name: Muhaisnah
regions.note: Four numbered sub-communities off Al Awir Road. Almost no IGCSE provision inside the neighbourhood itself, so every school day involves a journey out and back, usually northwest to Al Qusais or east to Mirdif.

regions.name: Al Qusais
regions.note: The densest school district within reach, and the commonest destination for Muhaisnah students. Afternoon departures from here feed straight into the Al Nahda bottleneck, which is why a 3pm finish often means a 4.15pm arrival home.

regions.name: Mirdif
regions.note: Villa communities east of Muhaisnah with several British-curriculum schools. The run is shorter in distance than Al Qusais but slower between 2.30pm and 4pm because of the school gate queues around Mirdif City Centre.

regions.name: Al Warqa
regions.note: Large residential area south of Mirdif with substantial school provision. Bus routes serving Al Warqa schools often loop through several communities, so the last child dropped can be forty minutes behind the first.

regions.name: Al Garhoud
regions.note: Older district near the airport with long-established schools and quick access along Al Rebat Street. Students schooling here tend to arrive home earlier than those in Mirdif, which makes a 5.30pm slot genuinely possible.

regions.name: Dubai Festival City
regions.note: Reachable from Muhaisnah in reasonable time outside peak, and home to schools running both IGCSE and IB. Pick-up times here are staggered by year group, so an older sibling may arrive an hour after a younger one.

regions.name: Al Nahda
regions.note: On the Sharjah boundary and the single biggest variable in this catchment's afternoon. Families living here but schooling in Dubai lose the most time, and should plan a 7.30pm session rather than anything earlier.

regions.name: Nad Al Hamar
regions.note: Between Rashidiya and Mirdif, with good road access to Festival City schools. Shorter runs than most of this cluster, so an early-evening slot usually holds without drama.

regions.name: Al Mizhar
regions.note: Quiet villa district beyond Mirdif, served by school buses with long routes. Distance is modest but the bus timetable, not the map, is what determines when a session can start.

regions.name: International City
regions.note: Dense apartment community to the south-east. School runs from here are long in both directions and families often prefer weekend morning sessions to any weekday slot.

modes.description: The format that survives a Dubai term. One subject, one tutor, the same evening each week, chosen after looking at the school's co-curricular timetable rather than before. Work is set between sessions and marked before the next one, which means the student arrives with something to discuss instead of starting cold.

sections.heading: Which schools this catchment feeds, and when a session can actually start
paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor in Muhaisnah is, in practice, a tutor who has to fit into a gap that the school run has already decided the size of. So before anything else, here are the school clusters this neighbourhood uses, the end times typical of each, and the earliest evening slot that holds across a term rather than looking good in September.

Two things about the table. The end times are typical rather than official: schools stagger finishes by year group, and Year 11 in particular often stays later for intervention sessions. Check your own school's calendar. And the first workable slot assumes the student eats and changes before the session, because a lesson that starts with a sandwich in one hand delivers about forty useful minutes out of sixty.

The pattern across the table is consistent. Short runs, Garhoud and Festival City, allow a 5.30pm start. Longer or more congested runs, Al Qusais through Al Nahda and the Mirdif gate queues, push the first realistic slot to 6.30pm or 7pm. Year 11 students anywhere in this catchment are safest at 7.30pm from January onwards, because that is when school revision programmes start eating the earlier hours.

This is also the reason an in-home arrangement is harder to sustain here than families expect. A tutor driving to Muhaisnah is caught in the same traffic the school bus is, arriving at the end of it, and the later the slot the less a tutor wants to take it. An online slot at 7.30pm costs the tutor nothing extra, which is why the late-evening availability is so much better.

sections.heading: What each evening slot is good for, and what it ruins
paragraphs: Having established when a session can start, the next question is which of the available slots to take, and the answer is not simply the earliest. Different hours of a Dubai evening suit different work. A student doing timed past-paper practice needs to be alert and will not be at 8.30pm. A student doing consolidation and question-answering can manage later. A student who has not eaten cannot do either.

The table sets this out slot by slot, with what each is suited to and what tends to go wrong. It is built from what actually sticks across a term in this catchment rather than from an ideal schedule. The honest headline is that 6pm and 7.30pm carry almost all our Muhaisnah bookings, and that the 4.30pm slot families instinctively ask for is the one most likely to be abandoned by week five.

There is one more variable specific to this part of Dubai: Maghrib prayer and, during Ramadan, Iftar. Both move with the calendar. A 6pm slot that works in November sits awkwardly in Ramadan, and families who plan for that in advance keep continuity while families who do not lose a month. We ask about it at the consultation rather than discovering it later, and sessions shift to post-Iftar timing where that suits the household.

Homework order matters too. Parents often want tutoring before homework so the tutor can help with it, which is understandable and usually wrong. A tutoring hour spent on tonight's homework teaches tonight's homework. A tutoring hour spent on the thing the student cannot do, with homework afterwards as independent practice, teaches the subject. If the homework genuinely cannot wait, that is a signal the slot is too late, not that the plan is wrong.

sections.heading: Check the board before you book: Cambridge and Pearson are not interchangeable
paragraphs: This is the mistake that costs Muhaisnah families the most money, and it happens before a single lesson. A parent books an IGCSE maths tutor, the tutor teaches to Cambridge 0580, and the child is entered for Pearson Edexcel 4MA1. The content overlaps heavily, so nobody notices for weeks. The paper structure, the formula sheet provision and the style of question do not overlap, and those are precisely what the final weeks of preparation are about.

Dubai schools use both boards and sometimes split by subject: Cambridge sciences with Pearson maths is a common combination. Some schools also enter students for OxfordAQA. The only reliable source is your child's own entry information, which the school issues, or the subject teacher. Asking the student is not reliable; most cannot tell you, and the ones who are confident are sometimes wrong.

The table below gives the codes most common in this catchment so you can match them against what the school has told you. Take the syllabus code to any tutor you are considering and ask them to describe the papers for it. A specialist will do so immediately. Someone who says the boards are basically the same is telling you they teach the subject rather than the qualification, which is fine for Year 9 and not fine for the spring of Year 11.

One board difference worth understanding on its own terms: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series. Cambridge International runs a June series and a November series, with every centre allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable.

sections.heading: The exam series counted backwards from results day
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes a calendar, which is odd, because it is the single most useful planning document a Year 11 parent can have. The principle is simple: the dates that constrain you are not the exam dates. They are the entry deadline, which sits months earlier, and the internal school deadlines for any coursework, which sit earlier still. By the time the exam timetable is on the fridge, every decision that mattered has already been taken.

UAE candidates sit the June and November series. The February/March series exists but it is offered to India only, so ignore any timetable or deadline you find quoted for it; a date a parent acts on being wrong for their country is worse than no date at all. For Cambridge, the June series is the main sitting and November is the resit route. For Pearson Edexcel, International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year.

On dates that can be checked: the Pearson International GCSE November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Pearson's June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are backward-looking and verifiable. For anything in the future, use the official live timetable rather than a figure copied onto a tutoring page, because provisional timetables are revised.

Work the plan backwards from there. If the target is the June series, the useful tutoring window opens in the autumn and the intensive block runs February to April, finishing before study leave. If a resit in November is in play, the decision point is immediately after results in August, and the eight weeks from early September are worth more than anything done in October. Either way, the table below is the sequence to hold in your head.

sections.heading: Science practicals when the lessons are online
paragraphs: This is the most reasonable objection a parent raises to online science tutoring, and it deserves a real answer rather than reassurance. The answer turns on how IGCSE sciences are actually assessed. Practical skills are examined on paper. Cambridge offers an alternative-to-practical written paper alongside a practical test, and most international centres enter candidates for the written route. The marks are awarded for planning an investigation, identifying variables, reading instruments, tabulating results, plotting and interpreting graphs, and evaluating sources of error.

Every one of those is a paper skill, and several are taught better on a shared screen than at a bench. Plotting is a good example: a student who loses marks on scale choice and line of best fit learns faster when a tutor can annotate their actual graph in real time than when the graph goes home in an exercise book. Identifying a dependent variable in an unfamiliar method is pure reading comprehension applied to science.

What online tutoring cannot replace is hands-on time with apparatus, and we do not pretend otherwise. That is the school's job and the school has the equipment. Where a student's school runs a practical test rather than the written alternative, the tutoring focus shifts to the recording and processing conventions the test rewards, and to rehearsing the sequence of a method so the student is not reading it for the first time under pressure.

The practical requirement for a Muhaisnah family is modest: a way for the tutor to see the student's written work live. A tablet with a stylus is ideal; a phone propped to show a page works; a shared document for tables and graphs works well for data handling. Families who sort this out in the first week get noticeably more from science sessions than families who spend six weeks describing their working out loud.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency: the five-subject rule
paragraphs: If your child may apply to a UAE university, or will need their certificate recognised locally, equivalency matters and it is widely misreported. For the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. They must also submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade.

The detail families most often get wrong: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. So a student with five passes of which two are Arabic and Islamic Education does not meet the rule, and needs to look again at their subject spread. One ranking tutoring site in this market publishes a six-subject requirement, which is simply incorrect, and a family planning around it may drop a subject they needed or keep one they did not.

What this means for a Year 10 subject-selection conversation in Muhaisnah is concrete. Count the subjects that will count. Make sure at least five of them are accredited subjects outside Arabic and Islamic Education, and that the student is on track for grade 3 or E in all five rather than hoping. That is a cheaper intervention than any amount of Year 11 tutoring, and it is free.

Two cautions. Equivalency is a Ministry of Education process and the authority's own page is the only source to act on; nothing on a tutoring site, including this one, should be treated as the final word, and the requirements can be updated. And no tutoring provider performs, expedites or guarantees equivalency. We can tell you what the published rule says and point you at the official channel. Nobody should be implying that tutoring is required for a regulatory process to succeed.

sections.heading: The honest position on home visits, and what we sell instead
paragraphs: Because the phrase in your search was home tutor, here is the position without hedging. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visiting is a service we run only in India. For a Muhaisnah family, what we offer is live one-to-one tuition over video, scheduled into the slots the earlier tables identify, with the same tutor each week and work marked between sessions.

The reason is not cost-cutting, it is supply. Limiting a shortlist to tutors who can drive to Muhaisnah 3 by seven in the evening removes most people who teach a particular IGCSE syllabus for a living, and keeps the ones whose subject spread is widest. For a Year 11 student eight weeks from a series, breadth is not the quality you want. You want somebody who can describe the papers for 0620 from memory and knows which electrolysis questions trip students up.

In-home tutoring remains a legitimate choice and some families should make it, particularly for younger children who need an adult physically present to stay on task. If that is your situation, the market rate is roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, and the thing to check hardest is whether the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and applies regardless of whether lessons happen in a home or on a screen.

What we would ask you to compare is not atmosphere but delivered teaching minutes. An online session starts when the clock says so and can be moved by message when the school changes something. An in-home session absorbs the arrival slippage and tends to be cancelled rather than moved. Across a thirty-week year the difference in lessons actually taught is larger than most families expect, and continuity is the part of tutoring that does the work.

sections.heading: Getting started from a Muhaisnah address
paragraphs: Send four things and the match is usually right first time. The subject and the syllabus code if you have it, or the school and year group so we can establish it. The school's current weekly timetable, including which afternoons run late, because that is what decides the slot. The most recent marked paper or report. And the two evening slots you genuinely believe will survive until June, not the ones you hope will.

We then identify a tutor who teaches that syllabus at that tier and offer a free trial lesson in one of your slots. Nothing is charged before the trial. If the slot turns out to be wrong in practice, we move it; that is the single most common adjustment in the first month and it is nobody's fault. If the tutor is wrong, say so and we match again.

The review point is session six, against something specific agreed in advance. For IGCSE that is usually a paper skill rather than a topic: tabulating and plotting without losing presentation marks, or structuring an eight-mark evaluation that reaches a judgement. You assess it from the student's own marked work, not from a conversation. If it has not moved, the diagnosis was wrong and we change the plan rather than adding hours.

One last Muhaisnah-specific suggestion. If you are reading this in Year 10 rather than Year 11, book the autumn rather than the spring. The slots are better, the tutors are freer, the student is less exhausted, and the thing you fix in October is a thing they do not have to carry into the series. Almost every family who starts in March tells us the same thing, which is that they wish they had started earlier.

process.title: Send the syllabus code and the timetable
process.description: The subject with its board and code if you know it, the school and year group if you do not, plus the school's weekly timetable showing which afternoons finish late. Those two documents decide both the tutor and the slot, and sending them saves a week of back and forth.

process.title: Name the slots that will actually survive
process.description: Two evening times you believe will hold until the series, chosen against the school run rather than against the ideal. If nothing weekday works, say so and we look at Saturday mornings, which in this catchment are often the most reliable hour of the week.

process.title: Free trial in your chosen slot
process.description: A full one-to-one lesson at the time you want it, over live video, with no payment taken and no obligation. Ask the tutor to describe the papers for your child's syllabus code; a specialist answers in numbers, and that tells you more than any credential list.

process.title: Fix the cadence, set work between sessions
process.description: One subject, one weekly slot, a written task set and marked before the next session. The student should arrive with something to discuss rather than starting cold, which is what turns a sixty-minute booking into sixty minutes of teaching.

process.title: Review at session six against a paper skill
process.description: Judge it on the student's own marked work against the specific capability agreed at the start. If it has not moved, we change the tutor or the diagnosis rather than adding a second hour, because more of the wrong thing is still the wrong thing.

process.title: Plan the series backwards
process.description: Once the slot is stable, set the intensive block so it ends before study leave rather than running into it, and agree in advance how a resit decision would be made in August. Both are easier to settle in October than in May.

whyPoints.title: The slot is chosen, not assumed
whyPoints.description: We ask for the school's timetable before proposing a time, because in this catchment a 4.30pm booking fails for reasons that have nothing to do with teaching. Getting the hour right is the cheapest improvement available to a Muhaisnah family and most providers never ask.

whyPoints.title: Syllabus code first, subject second
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different papers with different formula provision. We match to the code the school has entered your child for, and a tutor who cannot describe those papers does not get the booking.

whyPoints.title: Series dates handled correctly for the UAE
whyPoints.description: UAE candidates sit the June and November series. The February/March series is offered to India only, and any page quoting its entry deadline to a Dubai parent is giving them a date that is wrong for their country. We link the live official timetable instead.

whyPoints.title: Continuity over intensity
whyPoints.description: A slot that holds for twenty-eight weeks beats a slot that looks better and gets cancelled nine times. Online sessions can be moved with a message when a school trip or a Ramadan timing change lands, which is why continuity survives in this format.

whyPoints.title: Equivalency explained, not sold
whyPoints.description: We publish the five-subject rule with its source because one ranking site in this market publishes a six-subject figure. We do not perform equivalency, expedite it, or suggest tutoring is required for it, and the Ministry's own page is the only thing to act on.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what we do not do
whyPoints.description: No home visits in the UAE, no production of coursework, no claim of KHDA or board approval, and no promise about a grade. Saying this plainly costs us some enquiries and saves every family who reads it a wasted conversation.

faqs.question: What time should an IGCSE session start if my child goes to school in Al Qusais?
faqs.answer: Plan for 6.30pm rather than anything earlier. A 2.45pm to 3.15pm finish in Al Qusais typically puts a Muhaisnah student through the door between four and half past, and the Al Nahda and Al Ittihad Road peak is unforgiving. By the time they have eaten and changed, a 5pm booking has already failed. Year 11 students from January are usually safest at 7.30pm, because school revision clinics take the earlier hours. Saturday mornings at 9.30am are the most reliable slot available in this catchment, and the one we suggest most often to families whose weekdays are genuinely full.

faqs.question: Can an IGCSE tutor come to our apartment in Muhaisnah?
faqs.answer: Other providers will arrange that and the market rate is roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included. IB Gram does not; we do not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE, and home visiting is a service we run only in India. For Muhaisnah families every lesson is live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time. The practical argument is arrival slippage: a tutor driving into this neighbourhood at 6pm is in the same traffic the school bus was, and the minutes lost are not recovered. An online session starts when the clock says so.

faqs.question: My child's school never told us the syllabus code. Where do I get it?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's exams officer or the subject teacher, and ask for the syllabus code rather than the board name. Dubai schools frequently mix boards by subject, so Cambridge sciences alongside Pearson Edexcel maths is common. Do not rely on the student; most cannot say, and a confident answer is sometimes wrong. The code matters because Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 have different paper structures and formula provision, and the final weeks of preparation are almost entirely about paper structure. Take the code to any tutor you are considering and ask them to describe the papers for it.

faqs.question: When do UAE students actually sit their IGCSE exams?
faqs.answer: UAE candidates sit the June and November series. Cambridge International runs a June series and a November series, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, stating that it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The February/March series is offered to India only, so disregard any entry deadline quoted for it on a UAE page. Always check the board's live official timetable rather than a restated date.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting tutoring in Year 10 rather than waiting for Year 11?
faqs.answer: In this catchment, yes, decisively. Year 10 students arrive home earlier, have fewer school revision commitments competing for the evening, and are less tired, so the slots available are better and the sessions are more productive. More importantly, tiering decisions in maths and science are often taken during Year 10, and a student's position at that point sets a grade ceiling that Year 11 work cannot lift. Families who start in March of Year 11 almost always tell us afterwards that they wish they had begun in the autumn, and the cost per grade is considerably higher.

faqs.question: How are science practicals handled if lessons are on a screen?
faqs.answer: IGCSE practical skills are assessed on paper. Cambridge offers an alternative-to-practical written paper alongside a practical test, and most international centres use the written route. The marks go to planning an investigation, naming variables, reading instruments, tabulating, plotting, interpreting graphs and evaluating error. Those are paper skills, and several are taught better on a shared screen where a tutor can annotate the student's actual graph than in an exercise book that goes home. Hands-on apparatus time is the school's job and the school has the equipment; we work on the recording and processing conventions the paper rewards.

faqs.question: My child is entered for Core rather than Extended. Can tutoring change that?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but the decision belongs to the school and it is usually taken earlier than parents realise. The honest sequence is to ask the subject teacher what evidence would change the entry and by when, then work on exactly that rather than on general improvement. Be clear-eyed about the ceiling: Core and Extended award different grade ranges, so a confident Core grade and a struggling Extended grade are not simply two versions of the same result. A tutor who promises to move your child up a tier without having seen their marked work is guessing.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects should we get tutoring for at once?
faqs.answer: One to start, two at most. A Year 11 in a Dubai private school is carrying seven to ten IGCSE subjects plus mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies, which occupy real timetable minutes calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Adding three tutored hours a week to that tends to cost more in sleep than it returns in marks. Pick the subject where the gap is largest and most fixable, run it for six sessions, review against the student's own marked work, and only then consider a second.

faqs.question: Do tutoring sessions need to move during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Usually, and it is better planned than discovered. School days shorten, Iftar timing shifts the evening, and a 6pm slot that worked in November sits awkwardly. Families who agree the Ramadan arrangement in advance keep continuity through the month; families who do not tend to lose it entirely and then restart in a worse position. Post-Iftar sessions work well for many households, and some prefer a late-morning slot on non-school days instead. We ask about this at the consultation rather than waiting for the first missed lesson to raise it.

faqs.question: What does the UAE Ministry of Education require from an IGCSE set?
faqs.answer: For the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among the five. One ranking tutoring site in this market publishes a six-subject requirement, which is incorrect and could cause a family to plan the wrong subject spread. Verify the current rule on the Ministry of Education's own site; no tutoring provider performs or guarantees equivalency.

faqs.question: Does my child's tutor need a permit even if the lesson is online?
faqs.answer: The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 for individuals providing private tutoring in the UAE. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's smart app, website or e-services, with a stated two-working-day completion. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat specific dirham figures online as unverified.

faqs.question: Can my child do homework during the tutoring session?
faqs.answer: It is tempting and it is usually the wrong use of the hour. A session spent on tonight's homework teaches tonight's homework; a session spent on the thing the student cannot do, with homework afterwards as independent practice, teaches the subject. There is one exception: when a piece of homework is diagnostic, a tutor watching a student attempt it cold learns more in ten minutes than any conversation provides. If homework genuinely cannot wait until afterwards, that is a signal the slot is too late in the evening rather than a problem with the plan.

faqs.question: What happens if our slot stops working after a few weeks?
faqs.answer: We move it, and this is the single most common adjustment in the first month for families in this catchment. School timetables shift after the first few weeks of term, co-curricular commitments land, and a slot that looked fine in September turns out to collide with something. Moving an online session is a message rather than a re-planned cross-city drive, which is the main practical reason continuity survives in this format. What we would not do is keep a failing slot out of politeness; a session the student arrives late and flustered to is not worth paying for.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do eastern Dubai students most often need help with?
faqs.answer: Extended mathematics and the separate sciences dominate our enquiries from this catchment, with Physics the most requested single subject and Chemistry close behind. English Language appears often among students who speak another language at home, usually not because of vocabulary but because of directed-writing structure. Economics and Business Studies come up in the spring of Year 11, when evaluation marks start deciding grades. The pattern is consistent: the subjects where a correct answer can still lose marks on presentation or structure are the ones where tutoring moves a grade fastest.

faqs.question: Can we pause sessions during the school's own revision programme?
faqs.answer: Yes, and sometimes you should. If a school runs intensive revision clinics in a subject, two sources of preparation competing for the same evening is counterproductive, and the school's version is free and aligned to its own entries. The sensible pattern in that case is to pause the tutored subject, keep the slot reserved, and resume if the clinics finish before study leave. We would rather tell you to use the school's provision than bill for an hour that duplicates it, and the conversation is easier in March than in May.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-muhaisnah.closingHeading: Pick the hour first, then the tutor
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-muhaisnah.closingBody: Everything on this page points at one piece of advice for families in Muhaisnah: decide when the session will happen before you decide who teaches it. Look at the school run, pick a slot that will still work in March, then find somebody who teaches your child's exact syllabus code at that tier. Send us the subject and code, the school timetable, the last marked paper and the two slots you trust, and we will come back with a named specialist and a free trial lesson at the time you asked for. Nothing is charged before that lesson, and if the hour turns out to be wrong in practice, we move it rather than defending it.

intro.heading: Two school years, and the weeks that are actually decisive
paragraphs: The IGCSE years look longer than they are. Year 10 begins in August with no external pressure and ends in June with a set of internal examinations that decide tier entries and set teacher expectations. Year 11 begins in August, meets a mock window after the winter break, and then runs into the examination series. Along the way there are entry deadlines that close months before any paper is sat, a timetable that differs by administrative zone, and a resit route through the following series that most families only discover on results day.

Counted properly, the decisive weeks are few. The autumn of Year 10 is when tier entry is still genuinely open, because the topics that separate the higher tier from the capped one, functions, graph transformations, circle theorems, the harder trigonometry and the sciences' quantitative content, take months to build rather than weeks. The spring of Year 11 is almost entirely examination technique, because by then the content has been covered once and the gap between what a student knows and what the paper awards is a technique gap.

The mock window is the most misread fixture in the two years. Mocks are set by the school, marked by the school, and are useful for one thing above all: they show which of four failure modes a student is in. Not knowing the method, knowing it and misapplying it, being accurate but slow, or misreading the question. Those four need four different responses, and a family that treats a disappointing mock as a general signal to buy more hours usually buys the wrong hours.

Nad Al Hamar adds a logistics layer rather than an academic one. This is a residential district on the eastern side of Dubai, bounded by the Ras Al Khor sanctuary and the Dubai-Al Ain Road, with no secondary school inside it. Children travel out to Dubai Festival City, Mirdif, Al Warqa, Al Qusais or Academic City, and come home between 3.50pm and 4.35pm on an ordinary day. A Year 11 student with nine or ten subjects does not have many usable evening hours, and a plan that ignores the arrival time is a plan that collapses in November.

What is on offer here is one-to-one teaching over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, at a fixed weekly hour. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE, because home tutoring is a service we provide only in India. The in-home market in Dubai is real and priced in this page so you can judge the alternative properly, with rates attributed to whoever published them, and the practical case for the online version is made in a table rather than in adjectives.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-nad-al-hamar.subjectsIntro: A Year 11 candidate cannot be tutored in nine subjects and should not try. These are the subjects Nad Al Hamar families most often need help with, and what the help consists of in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The gatekeeper. Weak algebra shows up in physics, chemistry and economics marks before it shows up in a maths grade. Higher-tier work means functions, graph transformations, circle theorems and vector proofs, all of which are routinely left blank rather than attempted.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Formula rearrangement, units, and the treatment of experimental uncertainty. Students who can recite the physics and cannot rearrange an equation lose marks that look like physics marks and are not. Electricity and waves are the reliable trouble spots.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, concentration, yields and electrolysis. Almost all of the lost marks are arithmetic under pressure plus significant figures, which is correctable with a routine rather than more content teaching. Organic nomenclature is a memory task that rewards short frequent drilling.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of content and command-term precision. Describe, explain, suggest and compare ask for different things, and a student who writes everything they know for every question runs out of time and still loses marks on the ones they answered.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.description: Directed writing and the extended response, with marks driven by structure and the handling of the specific task. The commonest fix is planning time: three minutes spent on a plan produces an answer worth several marks more than ten extra minutes of writing.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Definition accuracy, diagram precision and evaluation structure. Students lose marks for describing a situation rather than applying a concept to it. These are among the fastest subjects to improve, because the gains are structural rather than content-based.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions, trace tables and the theory paper's precise vocabulary. Practical confidence does not transfer to the written paper, and students who code well often score poorly on the exam without targeted practice on the paper's own conventions.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken alongside the main mathematics entry at some schools. Useful preparation for A Level or IB Higher Level mathematics, and worth tutoring only once the main entry is secure, because it is an extension rather than a substitute.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Required in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Progress here is about sustained exposure rather than examination technique.

sections.heading: What home tuition costs in Dubai, and what we deliver instead
paragraphs: A parent weighing an in-home tutor against an online one deserves both numbers. In-home one-to-one visits in Dubai are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is absorbed, with Bestimate's rate table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200 to 500. Monthly in-home packages seen in this market run at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. A qualified subject tutor teaching online is quoted at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150, and an online package at about AED 799 a month for eight sessions.

The premium on the in-home figure buys travel and scarcity. A tutor driving to Nad Al Hamar at 5.30pm is paid, directly or indirectly, for the unpaid hour they spend doing it, and the pool they are drawn from is whoever lives within a reasonable radius of an eastern residential district. For a common subject at a standard tier that pool may be adequate. For a higher-tier physics problem eight weeks before a series, it usually is not.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah or anywhere else in the UAE. Home tutoring is a service we run in India only, and stating that on the page is more useful than discovering it in an email. Every lesson for a Nad Al Hamar family is one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, at a slot fixed around the school run. If an adult in the room is genuinely the requirement, hire an independent local tutor and ask to see their MoHRE private tuition work permit.

The honest case for the online version is not that video is magical. It is that the hour starts when it is supposed to, the tutor is chosen because they have taught the syllabus code your child is entered for, the work is on a shared screen that survives the session, and the rate does not carry a travel premium. Over a two-term Year 11 block those four things compound.

sections.heading: The Year 11 calendar, month by month
paragraphs: August and September are for establishing facts, not for buying hours. Which board and which syllabus code for each subject, which tier, what the school's mock dates are, and which two subjects actually threaten the overall result. A family that knows those four things in September makes better decisions in February than one that is still guessing. The autumn term also carries the last genuinely useful content teaching, because by the spring there is no room for it.

October to December is content completion plus the first serious revision. Entries are being prepared in this window, and this is the last point at which a tier conversation with the school has any chance. The mock window lands in the weeks after the winter break at most schools in the eastern suburbs, though the Festival City and Al Warqa clusters sit a fortnight apart, which matters to a household with two candidates.

January and February are the diagnostic months. Mock results arrive, and they are worth reading for the pattern rather than the grade. A student who scored poorly across the board with time left on the paper has a content problem. One who ran out of time has a pacing problem. One whose marked script shows correct methods with wrong final answers has an accuracy problem. These need different work, and this is the moment to buy the right hours rather than more hours.

March onward is technique and nothing else. Timed papers in the correct syllabus code, mark-scheme logic, command-term handling, and the small bounded topics that are pure recoverable marks. The final timetable is published by the board in this window, and Cambridge candidates must use the version for their centre's administrative zone. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct zone timetable and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one; your school's exams officer knows the zone.

sections.heading: Entry deadlines, zone timetables and the traps in the admin
paragraphs: The administrative layer of IGCSE catches more families than the academic one, partly because nobody writes it down. Entries are submitted by the school to the board months before the papers, and they carry the tier. Once that entry is in, the grade ceiling is set, and a parent who wanted to argue for the higher tier has run out of road. This is the strongest argument for having the tier conversation in the autumn rather than the spring.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only, which means a Dubai parent reading a page that quotes a February examination window is reading advice written for a different country. That mistake is common enough in this market to be worth naming.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and the examination timetable differs between them. Cambridge's own guidance to exams officers states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong version. A parent working from a timetable found through a search engine may be looking at another zone entirely. Ask the exams officer which zone your child's centre sits in.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. For the completed cycles: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those dates are given because they are backward-looking and checkable. For any future series, name the month and read the live official timetable, because Pearson publishes provisional timetables that are later revised.

sections.heading: Nine subjects, two tutors: how to triage
paragraphs: A Dubai Year 11 candidate typically carries nine or ten subjects, and no family should be paying for help in all of them. The arithmetic of triage is simple once it is written down. Rank the subjects by three things: how far the current grade sits below what the sixth-form plan needs, how many marks are recoverable in the time left, and whether the subject gates anything else. Mathematics gates physics, chemistry and economics, which is why it is almost always first on the list even when its own grade is not the worst.

Recoverability is the factor families most often misjudge. A subject where a student is close to a boundary and losing marks to accuracy or pacing is highly recoverable with a few weeks of timed practice. A subject where a student has understood very little of the year is not recoverable in the spring, however much is spent, and the honest recommendation there may be to protect the other eight subjects instead. A provider who will not say that is selling hours rather than advice.

There are also cheap wins that sit inside subjects rather than across them. Circle theorems in higher-tier mathematics are a bounded, learnable set that candidates routinely leave blank. Command-term discipline in biology turns knowledge a student already has into marks. Diagram accuracy in economics does the same. Planning time in English directed writing is worth more than extra content. A tutor who opens with these is reading the paper correctly.

The practical sequence for a Nad Al Hamar family in January is therefore: read the mock scripts rather than the mock grades, pick two subjects, buy a bounded block in each, and leave the rest to school and self-study. That is less than most agencies will propose and it is usually what works.

sections.heading: The Nad Al Hamar weeknight, and when a session actually fits
paragraphs: Door times in this district run from roughly 3.50pm for a Festival City run to after 4.30pm for Academic City, with activity days pushing arrival past 5pm. That is the starting constraint. The second is the evening homework load of a Year 11 candidate with nine or ten subjects, which in the autumn term is substantial and in the spring is replaced by revision that also needs hours. The third is that a tired student at 8.30pm absorbs very little, whatever the hour is nominally spent on.

The slot that survives a full term is therefore between 6pm and 7.30pm, with some homework cleared first. Sixty minutes is right for term-time subject work. Ninety minutes suits a timed paper plus review, which is why a weekend morning becomes valuable once the revision block starts: a full paper and a proper discussion of it does not fit into a weekday evening alongside everything else.

Frequency matters more than length in the final stretch. Two forty-five minute sessions a week beat one ninety-minute session for a student losing marks to accuracy, because accuracy is a habit and habits need repetition rather than depth. For content gaps the opposite holds, and a single longer session with proper working time is better. A tutor should tell you which pattern your child's problem calls for.

Ramadan changes the shape of the month. School hours shorten, door times come forward, and families split between an early-afternoon slot and a post-Iftar one. Both work over video in a way they would not with a tutor crossing the eastern suburbs at Iftar. For a Year 11 candidate the planning point is to move revision forward into the weeks before rather than assume the month will run at full pace.

sections.heading: Results day, and the resit route most families have not read about
paragraphs: Results arrive and the decision window is short, which is why it is worth understanding before the day. Pearson Edexcel June results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge results follow a comparable rhythm for its June and November series. Within days of a disappointing grade a family has to decide between a retake, a review of marking, or accepting the grade and adjusting the sixth-form plan.

A review of marking is a formal process requested through the school and it has a deadline measured in weeks, not months. It is worth considering when a grade sits just below a boundary and the student's mock and coursework evidence is clearly stronger, and it is not worth considering as a general expression of disappointment, because marks can move in either direction. The school's exams officer runs it; a tutoring platform has no role in it and should not claim one.

A retake in the following series is the more common route. The entry goes through the school or, if the school will not enter a retake candidate, through a private examination centre, and in Dubai that is a practical question to ask early because the answer varies. Results from a November entry reach students in January, which for a student already in sixth form means a corrected grade partway through Year 12.

The work for a retake is not the Year 11 syllabus again. It starts from the paper that was sat and the pattern of marks lost on it, targets the specific topics exposed, and rehearses finishing a paper under time pressure with two marked mocks inside the block. Bought as a bounded block with a fixed end date, it is one of the better-value things in this market. Bought as an open-ended weekly arrangement, it drifts.

sections.heading: Permits, and how to check a tutor you hire yourself
paragraphs: Since this page recommends that families wanting an adult in the room should hire independently, it should also explain how to do that properly. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students.

The official application route is MoHRE's own service, titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, with a two working-day completion time listed and no fee. Individuals offering private tutoring without the permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so any page quoting a specific amount is quoting something it cannot source; this one does not.

A separate matter is a tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai, which requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit and does not claim one, because it operates no premises in the UAE. Any provider describing its tutors as carrying a regulator's approval should be asked to produce the permit number.

One rule to know before approaching a teacher at your child's own school. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct addressing the same thing. Treat the ADEK position as press-reported and check the current policy document, but do not build a plan around hiring your child's class teacher.

sections.heading: What we will not do, and what to ask us instead
paragraphs: Two things are off the table regardless of the deadline. We do not produce assessed work, in any subject, at any price. Where an IGCSE subject carries coursework or a controlled assessment, a tutor teaches the content, explains the criteria, demonstrates an example on a different task and questions the student's own draft. A tutor does not write, rewrite, supply content for or edit a student's submission. One site ranking for these searches sells completed assessments outright; the consequence of buying one falls on the candidate.

The second is that we do not supply syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Those belong to Cambridge International and Pearson, the boards publish specifications on their own sites, and your child's school has legitimate access. A tutor works from them in a session. A page offering them for download is handing you someone else's property and, for unreleased material, something worse.

We also do not claim approval from any regulator or board. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge International or Pearson, and no page here will say otherwise. We name regulators in order to explain what they do. The phrase to be suspicious of, in this market, is a tutor described as approved by a regulator, because the permit that exists is an individual's work permit and nothing broader.

What is worth asking us: which syllabus codes has this tutor taught and in how many cohorts, what will they do in the number of weeks we actually have, what is the rate in AED per hour, what happens if the match is wrong after two sessions, and whether anyone will come to our address in Nad Al Hamar. The answer to the last one is no, and it is better to have it now.

process.title: Tell us the board, the code and the date
process.description: Which board for each subject, the tier, and the deadline you are working to. Those three facts shape every useful recommendation, and the first two come off the statement of entry or from the exams officer in one email.

process.title: Send the marked mock script, not the grade
process.description: A marked paper tells a tutor in two minutes what a description takes ten to convey, and it distinguishes content gaps from accuracy, pacing and misreading. Those four need different sessions, and the script is the only reliable way to tell them apart.

process.title: We help you triage to two subjects
process.description: Ranked by how far the grade sits below what is needed, how many marks are recoverable in the weeks available, and whether the subject gates another. If we think a subject is not recoverable in the time left, we will say so rather than sell the hours.

process.title: Trial lesson, forty-five minutes, live online
process.description: Real work on the actual problem, with no card details collected. You get a written note afterwards naming the three things the tutor would do first and, as importantly, what they would leave alone.

process.title: A bounded block with an end date
process.description: For deadline-driven work the plan ends on the deadline and the number of sessions is stated at the start, so the total cost is known. Open-ended arrangements drift, and in a Year 11 spring there is no time for drift.

whyPoints.title: The calendar is treated as the constraint
whyPoints.description: Entry deadlines, zone timetables, mock windows and results dates decide what is possible. We set them out rather than quoting a generic improvement plan, and we will tell you when a window has already closed.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated before you book
whyPoints.description: One-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is an India-only service. The in-home market is priced here so you can judge the alternative fairly.

whyPoints.title: Triage advice, not a subject list
whyPoints.description: Nine or ten subjects cannot all be tutored. We will help you pick two on recoverable marks and gating effects, which usually means proposing less than you expected to buy.

whyPoints.title: Rates attributed and dated
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page was published by the provider named and read in October 2026. Three of six ranking pages in this market publish no price at all; two of the three that do quote US dollars.

whyPoints.title: No claimed approvals
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no accreditation from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge International or Pearson and claims none. We explain what the regulators do and point you to their own pages.

whyPoints.title: A boundary on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Teaching, criteria explanation, worked examples on other tasks and questions on your child's own draft. Never producing, rewriting or editing a submission. The candidate is the person a malpractice finding lands on.

faqs.question: Will an IGCSE tutor travel to our villa in Nad Al Hamar?
faqs.answer: Not through us. IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service we run in India only, never at a UAE address. The Dubai in-home market is real, with visits quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is absorbed and monthly packages at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. If an adult in the room is your requirement, hire independently and ask to see the tutor's MoHRE private tuition work permit before the first session.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE entries close, and can the tier still be changed after that?
faqs.answer: Entries are submitted by the school to the board months before the papers, and they carry the tier. Once the entry is in, the grade ceiling of the lower tier is fixed and no amount of tutoring lifts a result above it. That is why a tier conversation belongs in the autumn term of Year 11 at the latest, and really in Year 10, when the topics that separate the tiers can still be built. Ask the school directly what evidence they would need and by when.

faqs.question: Is there a February IGCSE series my child in Dubai could sit?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series, and the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Pages quoting a February examination window or its entry deadline to a UAE parent have copied guidance written for another country. Check the live official timetable through your school, and note that Cambridge timetables differ by administrative zone, of which there are six.

faqs.question: Our centre is in an administrative zone - which timetable should we print?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and the timetable differs between them. Cambridge's guidance to exams officers states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. A parent who downloads a timetable found through a search engine may be reading another zone's dates. Ask your school's exams officer which zone the centre sits in and work only from that version.

faqs.question: My child has nine subjects. How many should we actually tutor?
faqs.answer: Two, in almost every case. Rank the subjects by how far the current grade sits below what the sixth-form plan requires, how many marks are genuinely recoverable in the weeks left, and whether the subject gates others. Mathematics usually ranks first because it gates physics, chemistry and economics. A subject the student has barely understood all year is not recoverable in a Year 11 spring, and the honest move there is to protect the other eight rather than spend on the one.

faqs.question: How do we read a disappointing mock result usefully?
faqs.answer: Read the marked script, not the grade. Four patterns explain most of the loss: methods not known, methods known but misapplied, accuracy errors on correct methods, and questions misread. A student who left the last page blank has a pacing problem rather than a knowledge problem. One whose working is right and answers wrong needs a checking routine. Each pattern needs a different session shape, and buying generic extra hours without identifying the pattern is the commonest way families waste money in January.

faqs.question: What does a November resit block involve for a Dubai candidate?
faqs.answer: First, confirm the entry route, because some schools will enter a retake candidate and some will not, in which case a private examination centre is needed. Then build the work from the paper actually sat rather than from the syllabus: the topics it exposed, the pacing, and two timed mocks inside the block, marked and explained. Buy it as a bounded block with a fixed end date so the cost is known. Results from a November entry reach students in January.

faqs.question: Which board do the schools near Nad Al Hamar use for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Both, and sometimes both within one school for different subjects. Schools in the Dubai Festival City cluster and the Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Mizhar belt use Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel entries, and the choice is the school's. Check your child's statement of entry for the syllabus code per subject rather than assuming a school-wide answer. Dubai had 227 private schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25. Schools are named here as local context only, with no affiliation implied.

faqs.question: How far can help on an IGCSE controlled assessment legitimately go?
faqs.answer: Within a boundary, and we state it to the student in the first session. A tutor teaches the content, explains how the criteria distribute marks, demonstrates a worked example on a completely different task, and reads the student's own draft to ask questions about method and evidence. A tutor does not write, rewrite, supply content for or edit the submission. One page ranking in this market sells completed assessments, and the consequences of using one fall on the candidate rather than the seller.

faqs.question: Can we download board past papers and mark schemes from you?
faqs.answer: No. Past papers, mark schemes, specifications and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge International and Pearson. The boards publish specifications on their own sites and your child's school has legitimate access to the assessment material. A tutor works from that material inside a session, which is entirely proper; hosting it for download is not, and for unreleased material it is worse. Any site offering a download library of boards' material is handing you someone else's property.

faqs.question: Is my child's online tutor required to hold a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Anyone providing private tuition in the UAE needs the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued by MoHRE. It is free and valid for two years, and eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and students aged fifteen to eighteen. Operating without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. Ask for the permit and check the name matches the person actually teaching.

faqs.question: How much of our evening does an IGCSE session need in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Sixty minutes for term-time subject work, ninety when a full timed paper and a proper review are the point, and forty-five twice a week when the problem is accuracy, because accuracy is a habit and habits need frequency. Door times in Nad Al Hamar run from about 3.50pm to past 4.30pm depending on the school direction, and a Year 11 student needs some homework cleared first, so the slot that survives a whole term is usually between 6pm and 7.30pm.

faqs.question: Should we book sessions through Ramadan or pause them?
faqs.answer: Keep them and move them. School hours shorten during Ramadan, so the Nad Al Hamar door time comes forward and the whole evening changes shape. Households generally choose either an early-afternoon slot or a post-Iftar one, and both work on video in a way they would not with a tutor crossing the eastern suburbs at Iftar. For a Year 11 candidate the sensible planning move is to pull revision forward into the weeks before the month rather than assume full intensity during it.

faqs.question: What should we send in the first message to get a useful reply?
faqs.answer: Four things: the subjects with their boards and syllabus codes, the tier for each where tiers exist, the most recent marked mock script, and the date you are working to. With those a tutor suggestion and a realistic plan take a day. Without them the exchange runs for a week and ends in a generic proposal. If you do not know the codes, the school's exams officer will confirm them in one email, and that email is worth sending before anything else.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-nad-al-hamar.closingBody: Start with the administrative facts: board and syllabus code per subject, tier, the school's mock dates, and the entry deadline. Then read the marked mock scripts rather than the grades, and pick the two subjects where marks are genuinely recoverable in the weeks you have. Then book a bounded block in an evening slot that survives the Nad Al Hamar school run, with an end date and a stated number of sessions. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; home tutoring is an India-only service for us. Last reviewed 22 October 2026.

Each Nad Al Sheba session is one to one over live video, with scripts annotated live against the mark scheme.

intro.heading: What the next eight weeks have to achieve, and what they cannot
paragraphs: Parents in Nad Al Sheba usually start looking for an IGCSE tutor at one of four moments: a weak autumn report, a disappointing set of mock results, a panic in the final term, or a results day in August that did not go as hoped. Those are four different problems with four different answers, and treating them identically is why so much tutoring money achieves so little. The date on the calendar determines what the hour should be spent on, more than the subject does.

In the autumn, support is content. The school is still teaching syllabus, there is time to close genuine gaps, and a weekly hour at ordinary rates does useful work cheaply. By the winter mock block, support becomes diagnosis: the single most valuable tutoring hour of the entire two-year course is the one in the week a marked mock paper comes back, because the student has just demonstrated precisely where the marks go. By the final term, support is technique and timing, and attempting to teach new content is a waste of everybody's time.

Then there is the moment nobody plans for. A result arrives in August, a family decides within days whether to resit, and the window to a November sitting is roughly eight to ten weeks. That is enough for a focused paper-technique block in one subject with a clear end date. It is not enough to rebuild two years of content, and a provider who implies otherwise is selling hours into a family's anxiety.

Delivery, plainly: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. Nad Al Sheba lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For calendar-driven work this matters practically: a revision phase needs the slot to flex, with two sessions in a mock week and none during the series itself, and that is a scheduling change rather than a renegotiation when nobody is driving anywhere.

What follows is the year laid out. Where you are now and what support should be doing. The eight weeks before a series, week by week, with the work named. The mock fortnight. Results day, remarks and the resit decision, counted from published dates. The November route and the timetable-zone trap that Cambridge warns about in its own words. How the shortened-hours stretch of the Dubai year fits a revision calendar. And an honest list of what eight weeks cannot fix, because knowing that before you pay is worth more than any amount of encouragement. Every date cited here is backward-looking and taken from the board's own published pages, and none of it replaces the live official timetable or your school's examinations officer. Boards revise timetables, publish provisional versions ahead of each series and allocate centres to different zones, so a date restated on a tutoring page is a starting point for a question rather than something to plan a morning around.
