regions.name: The Crescent
regions.note: The outer breakwater, furthest from the mainland by road and the slowest address to reach in evening traffic. Travel is the single largest hidden cost in any in-home quote taken here.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: The first district off the trunk and the nearest concentration of tuition centres and campuses. Worth pricing as the realistic alternative to online if a family wants a room outside the house.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JBR
regions.note: A dense centre and freelance-tutor market immediately south of the trunk, which is why Palm families see a wide spread of advertised rates for apparently identical hours. Compare what is included, not the headline figure.

regions.note: Established coastal neighbourhoods with long-standing private tuition activity and a mature word-of-mouth market. Rates quoted here by independent tutors vary widely, and almost none of them include marking time.

regions.note: Reached along the coast road and home to large campuses serving island families. A useful comparison point for any family weighing centre-based group classes against one-to-one at home or online.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition actually costs around Palm Jumeirah
paragraphs: An IGCSE hour in Dubai sells for anything between about AED 33 and AED 650, and the spread is not mostly about quality. It is about who the tutor is, whether anybody is travelling, and how the provider has packaged the hour. The table below sets the bands out by what you are buying rather than by brand, with the published source for each figure and the month it was read.

Read the in-home line carefully. The Bestimate Dubai rate guide puts home visits at AED 180 to 350, and individual home tutors advertise up to AED 500, but those numbers include a journey, and on Palm Jumeirah the journey is long by Dubai standards: one road onto the trunk and then a single frond with no through route. A tutor pricing a Crescent villa at 6pm is pricing roughly ninety minutes of driving around a sixty-minute lesson. Nobody absorbs that for free.

The monthly figures are the ones families misread most often. A package at around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions is roughly AED 100 a session. A package at AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour home visits is roughly AED 200 to 225 an hour with travel inside it. Those are not competing offers for the same thing; they are eight hours against eight hours at very different prices, with different amounts of the fee going to teaching. The Bestimate guide's own monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support.

sections.heading: Where the money goes inside a single hour
paragraphs: Two invoices for sixty minutes can contain completely different things, and the difference is where a family's budget leaks. The table below opens up the hour. It is the most useful comparison on this page, because once you can see what each format pays for, the headline rate stops being the number that matters.

The honest summary is that an in-home hour on Palm Jumeirah spends a substantial part of its value on logistics, and an unmarked online hour spends a substantial part of its value on nothing much at all. Marking is the part parents forget to ask about. A tutor who marks a student's written work against the published mark scheme between sessions has done the work that makes the next session useful, and that work costs them time whether or not it is itemised on your invoice. If it is not happening, you are paying for conversation.

IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in the UAE, so the first column is here as market context rather than as an offer. What we do sell is the online column: a specialist's hour with marking done outside it, no travel priced into it, and a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot that survives a busy term on the island. The reason for publishing this breakdown is that it is the argument against our own highest-margin option, and that tends to be the kind of comparison worth reading. Nothing in the breakdown is confidential, and any provider on the island could publish the same table. The ones that do not are usually the ones whose arithmetic does not survive it.

sections.heading: The five ways island families waste tutoring money
paragraphs: These are not hypothetical. They are the patterns that recur in conversations with families who have already spent a term's budget before they call. Each one is avoidable with a question asked earlier.

The first is buying a term before diagnosing a problem. Six weekly hours disappear into revisiting material the student already had, because nobody established what was actually missing. The second is buying group classes for an individual gap: a group is good value for coverage and poor value for a specific weakness, since the pace cannot bend to one student. The third is buying time instead of marking. A student who completes five past papers that nobody marks against the published scheme has practised their existing mistakes five times.

The fourth is paying for travel without meaning to. An in-home rate that looks like a premium for expertise is often a premium for the drive onto the frond, and the two-hour minimum attached to it buys a second hour the child's concentration cannot use. The fifth is the quiet one: paying for a tutor who does not know which board the school entered the child for. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different papers with different question styles, and a term of excellent teaching on the wrong one is a term of nearly useful work. Ask for the syllabus code at the first conversation, and if the tutor does not ask you for it, that is information too.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel, and why the board changes the bill
paragraphs: Parents are often surprised that "IGCSE Maths" is not one thing. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel run separate qualifications with separate codes, papers and tiering, and a school chooses per subject, which means one child can sit both boards in the same year. The cost consequence is direct: tutoring hours are only efficient when the practice material matches the papers the student will actually sit.

Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge is explicit that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Pearson's International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

There is a worked example of why entry deadlines sit months before the exams, and the honest one for a UAE family is Pearson's. The November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and for the equivalent November 2025 series results did not reach students until 22 January 2026 — so the entry that fixed which tier a candidate sat was lodged long before any of that, while the autumn term was still finding its feet. Cambridge's June series behaves the same way: entries close in the spring, roughly four months before the first paper, and the exact date for your child's centre appears on its statement of entry rather than in any national announcement. A family budgeting for support needs to plan against the entry deadline, not the exam date, because the tier a student is entered for is fixed at that point and no amount of later spending changes the grade ceiling. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so always work from the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: Dubai fees and what a term of support is next to them
paragraphs: Dubai's private school sector enrolled 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum the largest by enrolment at 37 per cent and the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent. On 22 May 2026 KHDA confirmed there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total. For 2026-27 the emirate is adding seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment grew by 6 per cent.

That context matters for a budgeting conversation. School fees are the fixed cost and they are not rising this year; tutoring is the discretionary cost and it is the one families can size deliberately. A single weekly hour with a qualified online subject tutor at the market's AED 150 to 300 band is roughly AED 600 to 1,200 across a four-week month, which lines up with the Bestimate guide's own mid-band monthly estimate. An exam-year specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above lands nearer AED 1,000 to 2,000 and more.

Set against that, the cheapest intervention available to a Palm Jumeirah family costs nothing: a conversation with the school about which tier a child is entered for, and which board. A student moved from Core to Extended entry in Year 10 has had their grade ceiling raised without a dirham changing hands. A student left on Core while a parent spends AED 1,200 a month on tuition has paid for security, not for a higher grade. We would rather you spent the free thing first. On exam entry fees as a private candidate, ask the exam centre directly; those are set by the centre and we do not publish a figure we have not verified.

sections.heading: What to ask before any money moves
paragraphs: A short list of questions separates a priced service from a vague one, and all of them can be asked in a first conversation or a trial lesson. None of them require you to know the subject.

Ask which syllabus code the tutor will teach from, and whether they have taught that code before. Ask whether the price is per hour or per lesson, and what a lesson's length actually is. Ask whether marking of written work between sessions is included, and what you will see of it. Ask what happens if you stop after one session, and what happens if the match is wrong. Ask whether the figure quoted includes value added tax, and treat any general statement about the tax treatment of tuition fees in the UAE with care unless it cites the Federal Tax Authority. Ask where the tutor is based and which time zone sessions run in.

Two more that are specific to this market. Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit: it is granted free of charge for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, so a tutor charging you for it is charging for something that costs nothing. And ask any provider claiming a regulator's approval to show the permit number. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or Cambridge, holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, and operates no premises in the UAE. A service that implies otherwise is making a claim, and a claim should be evidenced before you pay it.

sections.heading: Spending early is cheaper than spending late
paragraphs: The most expensive tutoring in Dubai is the kind bought in the last six weeks before a series. Not because rates rise, though specialist availability tightens and choice narrows, but because late support can only do technique work. Content gaps need weeks the calendar no longer has, so the same money buys a smaller result.

Counting backwards from a June series, the useful shape is a diagnostic in the autumn term, weekly work through the winter on whatever the diagnostic found, and a short block of timed paper practice in the final weeks. For a November entry the same shape compresses into a shorter window, which is why November candidates should start earlier in relative terms, not later. Pearson's November 2026 timetable makes the point in plain numbers: the papers ran from late October to 19 November 2026, so a family that waited for the autumn term to settle before asking for help had already spent the months in which content gaps are still fixable, and the entry that set the tier had been lodged well before that. The decisions that bound a grade are taken long before the first paper is opened.

Ramadan sits inside the Dubai academic year and changes when revision realistically happens. Sessions move later in the evening, often after Iftar, and many families prefer shorter slots for the month. Planning for that in advance is free; discovering it in week two of the month costs you sessions. The same is true of the island's own rhythm: Palm Jumeirah households travel more than the Dubai average over long holidays, and a tutor who knows the plan can set independent work around it rather than billing for a slot nobody attends.

sections.heading: Starting small, and buying only what the diagnosis asks for
paragraphs: The first step costs nothing: tell us the subject, the syllabus code, the tier, the school and what the last marked piece of work said. That is enough to propose a named tutor who has taught that code, and to say honestly whether the problem looks like a content gap, a technique gap or a workload gap. Those three need different amounts of money spent on them.

The second step is the free trial lesson. Use it to ask the questions in the list above and to watch whether the tutor works from your child's marked paper or from a generic worksheet. If the fit is wrong, say so and the tutor changes; there is nothing to argue about, because the point of a free trial is that the decision is made before money moves. If the fit is right, start with the smallest sensible commitment rather than a term, and review it at six sessions against the written gap list.

The honest limits, stated here rather than discovered later. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; Palm Jumeirah lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Some subjects and codes, particularly 0606 and 0607 and the less commonly taken IGCSE options, have a thinner specialist pool and may take a week or more to match, and in the weeks before a series they may not be available at your preferred hour at all. We will tell you that before you pay rather than after, because a family that has bought the wrong thing has lost both the money and the weeks.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE tutor cost per hour around Palm Jumeirah?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates read in October 2026 run from AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik for budget online platforms, from AED 150 an hour for IGCSE at Unitors, AED 270 at TutorChase, AED 200 to 450 and above for specialists in the Bestimate Dubai guide, and AED 650 at BartyED at the premium end. In-home visits sit at AED 180 to 350 in that guide, with listings up to AED 500, because the hour includes a journey. These are market figures, not IB Gram prices; ours follow a free trial lesson and a short diagnostic.

faqs.question: Why would one tutor charge five times what another charges for the same hour?
faqs.answer: Three things explain almost all of the spread. Who is teaching: a university student on a platform and a specialist who has taught the syllabus for a decade are not the same product. Whether anybody is travelling: an in-home rate recovers the drive, and on Palm Jumeirah that drive is long. And what is included beyond the hour: marking written work against the published mark scheme takes the tutor time outside your session, and a rate that does not fund it will not include it. Ask which of the three you are paying for.

faqs.question: Is an online hour genuinely cheaper than a home visit on the island?
faqs.answer: Usually, and the reason is logistics rather than quality. The Bestimate Dubai guide puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 and qualified online tutors at AED 150 to 300, and the in-home figure carries a round trip plus a frequent two-hour minimum. For a villa on a frond or the Crescent, a tutor is pricing something like ninety minutes of driving around a sixty-minute lesson. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all, so for Palm Jumeirah the comparison is settled: lessons run one-to-one over live video.

faqs.question: What is the single most common way families here waste tutoring money?
faqs.answer: Buying a term before anybody has diagnosed the problem. The first six weekly hours then go on revisiting material the student already had, because nobody established what was missing. Two diagnostic sessions working through marked school assessments and a timed past-paper section tell you whether the gap is content, technique or workload, and those three need very different amounts of money. Families who buy the diagnostic first reliably buy fewer hours overall, which is the only honest reason for a tutoring service to recommend it.

faqs.question: Does the board my child sits change what tutoring should cost?
faqs.answer: It changes what the hours are worth rather than the headline rate. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different papers with different question styles and tiering, so practice material must match the code the school entered your child for. A term of excellent teaching against the wrong board's papers is a term of nearly useful work. Ask the school's exams officer for the code before you book anything, and if a tutor does not ask you for it in the first conversation, treat that as information about the tutor.

faqs.question: Should I pay for a group class or one-to-one sessions?
faqs.answer: Group classes are good value for coverage and poor value for a specific weakness, because the pace cannot bend to one student. If your child is broadly fine and needs structured revision alongside others, a centre-based group in Al Sufouh or Dubai Marina may be the cheaper sensible option. If a diagnostic has identified a particular gap, such as moles in 0620 or algebraic manipulation in 0580, a group will teach around it rather than through it. Pay for individual attention where the problem is individual.

faqs.question: Is marking of my child's written work included in the hourly rate?
faqs.answer: Ask, because the answer varies and it is the part families forget. A tutor who marks past-paper answers against the published mark scheme between sessions is doing the work that makes the next session useful, and that takes their time whether or not it appears on an invoice. If nobody is marking, your child is practising their existing mistakes repeatedly and getting faster at them. At IB Gram marking between sessions is part of the work rather than an itemised extra, and you should see the marked scripts.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates in Dubai rise closer to the exam series?
faqs.answer: The published rates do not move much, but availability does, and that costs you in a different currency. In the weeks before a June or November series the specialists who have taught a given syllabus code for years are booked at exactly the hours Palm Jumeirah families want, which are weekday evenings. Choice narrows, and late support can only do technique work because content gaps need weeks the calendar no longer has. The same money buys a smaller result, which is the real late-booking premium.

faqs.question: Does the price include VAT, and how should I ask about it?
faqs.answer: Ask whether the figure quoted is the figure you will pay, and get the answer in writing. We will not state the UAE tax treatment of tuition fees as a general fact, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation rather than a tutoring company's opinion, and several competitor pages assert it anyway. The useful question for a parent is narrow: is this quote inclusive, and is there any other charge. Treat a provider that cannot answer that clearly as a provider whose invoices will also be unclear.

faqs.question: Should I pay for a tutor who comes to the villa instead?
faqs.answer: If having somebody physically in the room is what your child needs, that is a legitimate reason to pay the in-home premium, and the Dubai market serves it at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included. Be clear about what you are buying: a long drive onto a frond or the Crescent, often a two-hour minimum, and less flexibility when a school deadline moves. IB Gram does not provide in-person tutoring in Dubai, so we are not the service for that preference, and we would rather say so than take the booking.

faqs.question: How many hours should I budget for one weak IGCSE subject?
faqs.answer: Most families settle at one hour a week on one subject for a term, which is roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month in the Bestimate guide's mid band, and then taper. A diagnosed technique problem can need as little as four to six well-marked sessions. A genuine content gap across two years of a course needs longer and should start earlier. Anybody quoting a package before seeing marked work is quoting a guess, and more hours never substitute for independent practice between them.

faqs.question: Is a cheap platform tutor ever the right purchase?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the right job. At AED 33 to 65 an hour, platform tutoring is a reasonable way to buy homework supervision, confidence and practice routine for a Year 9 or lower Year 10 student. It is the wrong purchase for an Extended-tier Year 11 candidate eight weeks from a paper, where you are paying for assessment-level knowledge of a specific syllabus code. Match the spend to the job: the error is not buying cheap, it is buying cheap for a problem that needs a specialist.

faqs.question: Are school fees in Dubai going up, and how does that affect this decision?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total. For 2026-27 the emirate adds seven private schools and 16,846 places. For a family, that means the fixed cost is stable this year and the discretionary tutoring cost is the one to size deliberately, rather than treating both as rising together.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest thing I can do that might actually change the grade?
faqs.answer: Talk to the school about the tier and the board. A student entered for Core cannot reach the top grades however much tutoring is bought, so a tier conversation in Year 10 can raise a ceiling for nothing. Second cheapest: get one past paper marked properly against the published scheme, which usually reveals whether the problem is knowledge or technique. Both cost almost nothing and both change what you should spend afterwards. We would rather a family did these first and bought fewer hours as a result.

faqs.question: What happens to our money if we stop after one session?
faqs.answer: The trial lesson is free and carries no obligation, so stopping after it costs nothing. Beyond that, start with the smallest sensible commitment rather than a term, and use the six-session review to decide whether hours go up, down or stop entirely. Stopping is a legitimate outcome and most providers never mention it. We would rather resize honestly at session six than keep a weekly slot running because it is already in the calendar and nobody has looked at it.

intro.heading: The question behind the search, and an honest answer to it
paragraphs: A parent typing IGCSE home tutor in Pearl Jumeira into a search box is not usually asking a geography question. They are asking whether there is anybody available who really understands the course their child is sitting, and proximity has become the proxy for that because proximity is the only thing a search engine can filter on. The two requirements then get bundled together, and the bundling is where families lose money and time.

Here is why they come apart. IGCSE is not one qualification. In Dubai schools the same subject name covers different specifications with different papers, different tier structures and different practical arrangements. Mathematics is either Cambridge 0580, tiered Core and Extended, with a two-hour paper where no calculator is permitted, or Pearson Edexcel 4MA1, tiered Foundation and Higher, with a calculator permitted in both papers. Physics is either Cambridge 0625, which carries a practical component worth 20 per cent taken as Paper 5 or Paper 6, or Pearson 4PH1, which has no separate practical paper and assesses those skills inside the written papers. A tutor who knows one of those thoroughly and the other vaguely is a different proposition depending on which your child sits.

Second, the pool reachable from this island is small in a way that is easy to underestimate. Pearl Jumeira is reclaimed land off the Jumeirah 1 shoreline with one causeway serving it. A tutor has to be free at a fixed hour on a fixed weekday, willing to make the approach in late-afternoon traffic, and in possession of the specific syllabus experience you need. Each of those conditions cuts the set. Applied together they frequently leave nobody, and what happens next is the predictable thing: a capable general tutor is engaged, at a specialist rate, and the first paid sessions go on calibration.

Third, the honest test is not a credential. It is a conversation, and it takes about twenty minutes. There are four or five questions whose answers distinguish somebody who has marked these papers from somebody who has taught the subject in general, and none of them is aggressive or unusual. They are set out below, with what a good answer sounds like, so that the conversation is yours to run rather than ours.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Pearl Jumeira families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The reason that answers the original question rather than dodging it is simple: removing the distance condition is what allows the syllabus condition to be met. The filter stops being who can reach the island on Tuesday and becomes who has taught this code at this tier.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two separate awarding bodies offering what parents think of as one qualification. Cambridge tiers into Core, graded C to G, and Extended, graded A* to E. Paper counts, durations, calculator rules and practical arrangements differ by board and by subject, which is why the code matters more than the subject name.

programmes.description: The alternative route to 16 in continuum schools nearby, assessed against four criteria per subject rather than by terminal papers. dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-pearl-jumeira.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Pearl Jumeira families most often ask about, each with the specification detail that a genuinely experienced tutor will know without being prompted.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The test question is calculator policy. Cambridge Extended sits a two-hour paper without a calculator; Pearson permits one in both papers. A tutor who cannot tell you that straight away has not taught both.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The test question is the practical component. Cambridge carries one worth 20 per cent, taken as a practical test or the alternative to practical in written form. Pearson assesses practical skills inside the written papers instead.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry is where grades separate on both boards, and the practical arrangement differs as it does in physics. Ask which salt-preparation methods the practical paper has examined recently; a specialist will have an answer.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy with marks concentrated in precise explanation. The useful test is whether a tutor talks about the order ideas must appear in for a mechanism question, which is where students who know the biology still lose marks.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences and Combined Science
subjects.description: A different course from three separate sciences, with a longer combined theory paper and two grades from one set of papers for 0654. A tutor who does not distinguish 0654 from 0620 and 0625 has not taught it.

subjects.name: English Language and English Literature
subjects.description: Component structures vary considerably between boards, including whether coursework or an examined alternative applies. The test question is which components the school has entered for, and whether the tutor has marked them.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Command terms carry the grade: students write knowledge where the question demands evaluation. A tutor should be able to name the command terms and the mark allocations they imply without looking anything up.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Practical and theory components vary sharply by board and have been revised in recent years. This is the subject where an out-of-date tutor is hardest for a parent to detect, which makes the specification question essential.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by stronger cohorts in several Jumeirah schools alongside the main maths qualification. A narrow specialism, and a good example of a subject where a reachable local pool often contains nobody at all.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first or additional language
subjects.levels: Cambridge and Pearson specifications, alongside KHDA requirements
subjects.description: Sits alongside the KHDA mandatory subject requirement, where separate classes are required for Arabs and non-Arabs and teachers need appropriate KHDA approval. Tutoring here must be described carefully, because additional content needs prior Ministry permission.

sections.heading: Five questions that separate a specialist from a generalist in twenty minutes
paragraphs: You do not need to be able to teach the subject to run this test. Each question below has a factual answer that somebody who has taught the specification will give immediately and somebody who has not will approach vaguely. The table pairs each question with what a strong answer sounds like and what a weak one sounds like.

Ask them in order and listen for specificity rather than confidence. A tutor who says they are comfortable with all boards and all tiers has told you nothing, because every tutor says that. A tutor who says the Cambridge Extended non-calculator paper is the one that catches students moving from Pearson, and then explains why, has told you something that cannot be bluffed.

The second thing to listen for is whether they ask you questions back. Somebody who has taught Year 11 cohorts will want to know which code the school enters for, which tier the student is on, whether the school has made the tier decision yet, and what the last marked paper looked like. A tutor who takes the booking without asking any of that is going to spend your first sessions finding out.

A third signal is how they handle not knowing something. A tutor who says they have taught Cambridge and not Pearson, and would want a week with the specification before starting, has given you a more useful answer than one who claims both without hesitation. Candour about a gap is the best available evidence that the rest of the answers are real. Run this conversation before paying for anything. It costs twenty minutes and it is the single highest-value thing a parent can do in this market, because it addresses the thing a search engine cannot filter for.

sections.heading: Why the same subject name hides two different courses
paragraphs: The specification differences are not trivia. They determine which past papers are useful, how long the papers run, what a tier decision means, and whether a practical component exists at all. The table sets out the structures a Pearl Jumeira family is most likely to meet, which is also the reference a tutor should not need.

Mathematics is the clearest case. Cambridge 0580 Extended candidates sit Paper 2 without a calculator and Paper 4 with one, each two hours and 100 marks, half the grade apiece. Core candidates sit Paper 1 and Paper 3 at one hour thirty minutes each. Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 has two papers of two hours at Foundation or Higher tier, with a calculator permitted in both. A student drilled for a non-calculator paper they will not sit has spent months on something adjacent to the point.

The sciences differ in a way that is even more consequential. Cambridge separate sciences, Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625, include a practical component worth 20 per cent of the grade, entered either as Paper 5, a practical test with apparatus, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical in written form. Pearson Edexcel Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1 and Physics 4PH1 have no separate practical paper and assess those skills within the written papers. One fifth of the grade exists in one system and does not in the other.

Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 complicates it further. It is a double award: one set of papers covering all three disciplines, producing two grades, with a longer combined theory paper. A student on 0654 does not need three subject specialists, which is useful to know before engaging three. Combined Science 0653 is the single-award equivalent.

sections.heading: The arithmetic of a reachable tutor pool on an island
paragraphs: It is worth being concrete about why a locally reachable pool is smaller than it feels. Every condition you place on a visiting tutor multiplies against the others rather than adding to them, and four or five reasonable conditions can empty a set that looked large.

Start with the whole set of competent IGCSE tutors in Dubai, which is genuinely deep, because UK curriculum schools account for 37 per cent of enrolment across 227 private schools and 387,441 students. Now require that the person can be on this island by 5pm on a specific weekday, which excludes anybody teaching elsewhere at that hour and anybody for whom the causeway approach in late-afternoon traffic is not worth one booking. Now require the correct awarding body. Now require the correct tier, because teaching Core well and teaching Extended well are not the same skill. Now require experience of the particular practical route the school has entered for.

The result is not usually zero, but it is often one or two people, and they may not be free. At that point the family faces a choice nobody states openly: relax the syllabus condition, or relax the distance condition. The market relaxes the syllabus condition, because the distance condition is the one the parent can see. A capable general tutor arrives, the rate reflects the drive rather than the specialism, and the mismatch surfaces in February.

Relaxing the distance condition instead keeps everything that affects the grade and discards the thing that does not. That is the entire argument for online delivery on a page like this, and it is an argument about the pool rather than about technology.

sections.heading: Coverage, match time and what happens when nobody is available
paragraphs: No tutoring platform covers every subject at every level at every hour, and the ones that imply otherwise are the ones to be careful with. Stating coverage honestly is unusual in this market: no competitor reviewed in this cluster discloses a coverage limit, and several route UAE families to numbers outside the country without saying so.

The position here is straightforward. Core IGCSE subjects on both major awarding bodies are well covered, and a match is normally made quickly. Narrower subjects are not uniformly covered, and in those cases the honest answer is a stated match time rather than a yes. Where no suitable tutor is available, that is said before a booking rather than discovered after one, and nothing is taken on account against a match that has not been confirmed.

There is a second kind of limit worth naming. A tutor who has taught a subject at IGCSE is not automatically suitable for the Diploma, and vice versa. Families on this island frequently need both across a few years, and the sensible approach is to ask about both at the outset rather than assume continuity. Where a change of tutor is the right answer at the transition, saying so is part of the job.

The table sets out how this works in practice by subject group. The purpose is not to present limits as a feature, but to let a family plan around real ones instead of discovering them in the week a mock is sat.

sections.heading: The tier decision, and why it is the most consequential thing you will be asked
paragraphs: Somewhere in Year 10 the school will decide, or ask you to help decide, which tier your child sits. It is the single most consequential academic decision of the two-year course, because it sets a ceiling before any teaching happens. Cambridge Core is graded C to G; Extended is graded A* to E. A student entered for Core cannot achieve an A, however well they perform.

The decision is often made on classroom impressions, which are a poor instrument. A student who is quiet in class and accurate on paper looks weaker than they are. A student who is confident in discussion and careless under time pressure looks stronger. The honest instrument is a marked Extended past paper taken under timed conditions, read not for the total but for the pattern: are the lost marks content the student has never been taught, or technique the student has not practised?

That distinction decides the right answer. Technique failures are recoverable within a term, which usually argues for Extended. Content gaps across several unrelated topics, with the series approaching, usually argue for protecting a strong Core grade rather than chasing a weak Extended one, because a secure grade is worth more than an ambitious failure. Either way the decision should follow the evidence rather than optimism, and a tutor who recommends Extended without seeing a paper is not advising, they are flattering.

For MoE equivalency on the British track the relevant rule is that a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among those five. One provider ranking for these searches publishes a different subject count. Verify the requirement through the Ministry of Education's own channel rather than through any tutoring website, including this one.

sections.heading: Checking the permit, and what the rules actually say
paragraphs: The verification conversation has a legal half as well as an academic one, and it is shorter. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, and it is granted free of charge for two years.

Because there is no fee, lacking one is a choice rather than a barrier, and eligibility is broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with no fees stated and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so a specific amount quoted to you is not something anyone can substantiate.

A second point concerns who may teach whom. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. A family should therefore ask not only whether a permit is held but whether their child attends the school where the tutor teaches.

A third point concerns organisations rather than individuals. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, obtained with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a specific permit for a specific kind of business, and nobody without it should be describing themselves in terms that imply it.

sections.heading: Online delivery as the answer to the original question
paragraphs: This page began with a parent asking whether anybody nearby really knows the syllabus. Having set out why the two conditions conflict, it is worth closing the loop concretely rather than with a slogan.

The market rates first, because they are part of the answer. In-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table putting the common range at AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to AED 500. Online qualified subject tutors are published at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and TutorChase AED 270 for specialist work. Budget online options start lower, at AED 33 to AED 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to AED 65 at EdFlik. Those are market figures from the named providers, read in October 2026, and none of them is an IB Gram price list.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Pearl Jumeira families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with screen-shared papers, annotated working kept after the session, and recordings available. What that buys in relation to the original question is the whole pool rather than the causeway-reachable fraction of it, which means the match can be made on code, tier and practical route.

What it does not buy is a person in the room, and some families want that more than they want the specialist, which is a legitimate preference rather than a mistake. The point of this page is that the choice should be visible. Running the five verification questions will tell you quickly whether the reachable option knows your child's specification. If the answers are strong, the local choice is a good one. If they are vague, the premium is paying for a drive.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether a tutor really knows my child's IGCSE syllabus?
faqs.answer: Ask five factual questions and listen for specificity. Which code does the school enter for, and why does it matter? What is the calculator policy on each maths paper? How is practical work assessed in this science? Where did students lose marks on the last paper you marked? How would you decide between Core and Extended? Somebody who has taught the specification answers immediately and concretely. Somebody who has taught the subject in general answers warmly and vaguely, and will usually say that all boards are much the same.

faqs.question: Is a tutor living near Pearl Jumeira better than one who knows the exact specification?
faqs.answer: Only if the nearby tutor also knows the specification, which is less common than it sounds. The island is reached by a single causeway, so a visiting tutor must be free at a fixed hour, willing to make the late-afternoon approach, and in possession of the right awarding body, tier and practical-route experience. Those conditions multiply rather than add. When the reachable set empties, the market relaxes the syllabus condition because it is the one a parent cannot see, which is how a generalist arrives at a specialist price.

faqs.question: What is the practical difference between Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 physics?
faqs.answer: A fifth of the grade. Cambridge 0625 includes a practical component worth 20 per cent, entered either as Paper 5, a practical test using apparatus, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical answered in writing. Pearson Edexcel 4PH1 has no separate practical paper and assesses those skills inside its two written papers instead. A tutor who has only taught Cambridge has spent years preparing students for a component your child may not sit, and the reverse applies equally.

faqs.question: Does the maths calculator rule really change how a tutor should teach?
faqs.answer: Substantially. Cambridge 0580 Extended candidates sit Paper 2 with no calculator permitted, over two hours, which makes standard form, surds, fraction work and mental estimation assessed skills in their own right. Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 permits a calculator in both papers, so the same hours are better spent on long multi-step questions and calculator efficiency. A student drilled for a non-calculator paper they will never sit has lost months, and no amount of general competence recovers that.

faqs.question: My child does Co-ordinated Sciences 0654. Do we need three science tutors?
faqs.answer: No, and engaging three is a common and expensive mistake. 0654 is a double award: one set of papers covers biology, chemistry and physics and produces two grades, with a longer combined theory paper and the same practical component at 20 per cent. The depth in each discipline is shallower than in the separate sciences. What the student needs is one tutor comfortable moving across all three at the level the combined paper actually demands, which is a different profile from a subject specialist.

faqs.question: Why does the Core or Extended tier decision matter so much?
faqs.answer: Because it sets a ceiling before any teaching happens. Cambridge Core is graded C to G and Extended A* to E, so a student entered for Core cannot achieve an A however well they perform. The decision is often made on classroom impressions, which flatter the confident and undersell the quiet. The honest instrument is a marked Extended past paper sat under timed conditions, read for whether the lost marks are untaught content or unpractised technique. Those two patterns point in opposite directions.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to a Pearl Jumeira home?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Pearl Jumeira families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with screen-shared papers, annotated working kept after the session and recordings available. The reason that answers the question on this page rather than avoiding it: removing the distance condition is what makes the specification condition satisfiable, and the specification is what affects the grade.

faqs.question: What should I do if a tutor says all exam boards are basically the same?
faqs.answer: Treat it as the answer to your question. Paper counts, durations, tier names, calculator policy and the existence of a practical component all differ between Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel, and in the sciences the practical difference is worth 20 per cent of the grade in one system and nothing in the other. A tutor who has taught both cohorts knows this without thinking. The statement that boards are much the same is not reassurance; it is a description of how much detail the person has been close to.

faqs.question: How quickly can a specification-matched tutor be found for an island family?
faqs.answer: For core subjects on either major awarding body, normally quickly, because the pool is not limited by who can reach the causeway on a given weekday. For narrower subjects such as Additional Mathematics, Further Pure Mathematics or a less common language, coverage is genuinely thinner and the honest answer is a stated match time rather than a yes. Nothing is taken on account against a match that has not been confirmed, and where no suitable tutor exists we say so.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE tutor cost in Dubai, and does the island change the price?
faqs.answer: It changes in-home pricing and not online pricing. In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table putting the common range at AED 180 to AED 350. Online qualified subject tutors are published at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and TutorChase AED 270. Budget online options start at AED 33 to AED 52 at Tutopiya. Those figures belong to the named providers and were read in October 2026.

faqs.question: Should I ask a potential tutor about both IGCSE and the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Yes, at the outset, because experience in one does not imply experience in the other. IGCSE is marked by terminal papers with tiered entry; the Diploma reintroduces internal assessments with fixed percentages and a different mark-scheme culture. Families on this island often need both across three or four years. Where a change of tutor is the right answer at the transition point, that should be said rather than smoothed over, and asking the question early makes it easier to plan for.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE passes does a British-curriculum student need for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: The published British-track rule is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic Education are not counted among the five. One provider ranking for these searches states six subjects are required, which does not match the published rule. Verify the current requirement through the Ministry of Education's own channel.

faqs.question: Is my tutor allowed to teach my child if they work at the same school?
faqs.answer: This is worth asking directly. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. The practical question for a parent is therefore not only whether a permit is held but whether their child attends the school where the person teaches. Both answers should come without hesitation.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are hardest to find a specialist for in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure Mathematics, taken by stronger cohorts in several Jumeirah schools, and less commonly offered languages. Computer Science and ICT are a different problem: the pool is larger but specifications have been revised, so an out-of-date tutor is hard for a parent to detect. In all three cases the specification question is the one that matters, and a stated match time is a better answer than a confident yes from somebody who last taught the subject several revisions ago.

intro.heading: Why a Remraam family is probably on IGCSE, and what follows from it
paragraphs: Dubai offers an unusual number of school systems in one city. In 2024-25 the emirate's private sector held 387,441 students across 227 schools offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum accounting for 37 per cent of enrolment, the Indian curriculum 26 per cent, the American 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate 7 per cent. A family arriving in Remraam chooses from most of those within a reasonable drive, and the choice usually gets made on availability and fees rather than on a comparison.

That matters for tutoring because a qualification is a means rather than an end. IGCSE at sixteen leads somewhere specific: to A Levels, to an IB Diploma, or to a sixth form abroad, and it feeds a Ministry of Education equivalency rule with a particular shape. Knowing where the route goes changes what a tutoring hour should buy, because a student aiming at a UAE university has a different subject calculus from one aiming at a British one.

Remraam itself is one of the easier communities in this belt for school access. It is a low-rise apartment development in Dubailand, built as the Al Thamam and Al Ramth clusters with its own park and retail, reached from Al Qudra Road and Emirates Road. South View School sits close by and takes students through Year 11, which means IGCSE years here need less travel than they do from Mudon, Arabian Ranches 3 or Town Square.

What Remraam does not have is a dense local tutor pool. The people advertising along this corridor are based around Dubai Investment Park, Dubai Sports City and Motor City, and most of them cover several subjects at IGCSE level. For a student who needs a specific Extended-tier science paper eight weeks out, that pool is shallower than it looks, and distance is a poor way to choose from it.

There is also a transfer dimension that other pages in this market ignore entirely. Dubai's population moves, between countries and between schools inside the city, and a meaningful share of IGCSE students in this corridor did not start the course here. A child arriving from an Indian board, an American school or an IB continuum brings a different combination of content strength and technique gap, and the first thing they need is a map of what the new syllabus assumes rather than a course taught from the start. Two sections of this page are about exactly that.

IB Gram answers the search honestly rather than literally: lessons are one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor matched to the board and code the student is actually entered for. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only, and nothing on this page should be read as an offer to arrive at an Al Ramth or Al Thamam address.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel
programmes.description: Subject-by-subject qualifications examined at the end of Year 11, tiered in several subjects. Cambridge codes include 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry and 0610 Biology; Pearson codes include 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1. Grades decide sixth-form access and feed Ministry equivalency.
programmes.countryNote: UAE Cambridge candidates sit the June and November series, and the February and March series is offered in India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November, and Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones whose timetable must be used.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four published criteria each, marked out of eight and converted to a 1 to 7 grade, with the Personal Project in the final year. External examination is optional, so most MYP students finish without a public qualification at sixteen.
programmes.countryNote: MYP provision in Dubailand is thinner than IGCSE provision, so a Remraam family choosing it usually accepts a longer school run towards Dubai Hills, Al Barsha South or The Sustainable City.

programmes.name: American curriculum and the diploma route
programmes.description: A high school diploma accumulated over four years with grade point averages and standardised testing rather than terminal subject examinations. Advanced Placement courses sit on top for students who want subject depth.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-remraam.subjectsIntro: These are the International GCSE subjects most requested from Remraam, with the detail that decides which board a tutor needs to know.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: 0580 Core and Extended; 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The two boards expect different amounts of written method, so cross-board practice can cost earned marks. Early rounding and abandoned final pages are the other two reliable losses.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism carry most of the losses. Explanations that state without a causal link, and practical answers that name apparatus instead of describing a repeatable method, cost marks the student had earned.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis, rates and organic. Unbalanced equations and missing state symbols are mechanical losses; qualitative analysis questions are routinely available marks left unclaimed.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Long answers reward sequence and precise terminology, and data questions reward reading axes and units before applying content. Command-term misreading costs more here than content gaps do.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and reading responses, where register and task form matter as much as vocabulary. Strong writers lose marks for answering in the form they prefer rather than the one the task set.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Extract and essay questions on set texts. Quotation accuracy and a sustained argument score better than plot recall, and timing is the most common cause of an unfinished final answer.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Case-study papers where definitions earn one mark and application to the named business earns the rest. A trainable habit rather than a knowledge problem for most students.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and precise terminology, with much of the loss mechanical: an unlabelled axis or a curve moved without an explanation. That makes it one of the most improvable subjects by drilling.

subjects.name: Arabic as a second language
subjects.description: Reading, writing and oral components, separate from the Arabic that KHDA requires every Dubai private school to teach alongside the licensed curriculum.

sections.heading: What Dubai's curriculum mix means for one family's choice
paragraphs: The scale of Dubai's private sector is what makes the comparison worth making. In 2024-25 it held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26 per cent, American at 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent. For the following intake, seven new private schools were announced, four UK curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 new places, and KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year.

Those proportions explain something a family often reads as coincidence. A Remraam household will meet far more IGCSE students than MYP students, because the UK route is more than five times as large by enrolment in this city. Advice circulating in community groups is therefore overwhelmingly British-curriculum advice, which is useful if you are on that route and misleading if you are not.

It also explains the tutoring market. Tutors follow enrolment, so IGCSE coverage along this corridor is broader and cheaper than MYP or American coverage, and finding help for Cambridge 0580 is straightforward while finding someone who has marked against MYP criteria takes longer. That asymmetry is worth knowing before choosing a curriculum, not after.

What the proportions do not tell you is which route suits a particular child, or where each one leads. The next sections take those in turn, because a tutoring plan built without them tends to optimise the wrong thing.

sections.heading: IGCSE compared with the Middle Years Programme
paragraphs: This is the comparison Dubai parents ask about most, and it is usually framed as which is harder. That is the wrong question. The two systems differ in what they measure and in what they leave a student holding at sixteen, and either can suit a child depending on how they work.

IGCSE is terminal and subject-by-subject. A student sits papers at the end of Year 11 and receives grades that a sixth form anywhere can read without explanation. It rewards content mastery, examination technique and the ability to perform on a given morning. It also produces a portable qualification, which matters for a family that may move country, and it feeds the Ministry of Education equivalency rule directly.

The MYP is criterion-based and continuous. A student is assessed on skills demonstrated in tasks against published descriptors, across eight subject groups, with external examination optional. It rewards research, reflection and sustained independent work, and it prepares a student unusually well for the IB Diploma because the assessment language carries over. What it generally does not produce is a public qualification at sixteen.

The practical consequence for a Remraam family is about fit and about destination. A student who performs well under examination pressure and may move schools or countries is well served by IGCSE. A student who works steadily, writes well and is heading for an IB Diploma is well served by the MYP. The mistake is choosing on prestige, because neither is more prestigious; they answer different questions.
bullets: IGCSE is terminal, subject-based and produces a portable qualification at sixteen
The MYP is criterion-based, continuous, and usually ends without external examination
The MYP prepares better for the IB Diploma; IGCSE prepares better for A Levels
Choose on fit and destination rather than on perceived prestige

sections.heading: IGCSE against the American and Indian routes
paragraphs: The American route changes the shape of the whole secondary experience. There is no terminal examination at sixteen; a student accumulates credits and a grade point average across four years, with standardised tests and Advanced Placement courses carrying the subject depth. A student who performs inconsistently on a single morning is better protected here, and a student who coasts for a year cannot recover it with a strong examination run.

The Indian boards sit at the other end. Content load is heavier and more prescriptive than IGCSE in mathematics and the sciences, with terminal examinations at Class 10 and Class 12. Students transferring from an Indian board into IGCSE are often ahead on content and behind on the style of answer IGCSE rewards, particularly on application and extended written response. Students moving the other way meet a volume increase they rarely expect.

Transfers in either direction are a meaningful part of the tutoring demand along this corridor, and they need mapping rather than general teaching. The useful first piece of work is a list of exactly what the new syllabus assumes and the previous course did not cover, built by comparing the two documents rather than by teaching from the start.

For the equivalency question, the tracks differ. The British track asks for five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. The American track asks for English through an IELTS academic score of 5, a TOEFL iBT score of 61 or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics through at least 450 in the SAT Math test.

sections.heading: Remraam's school access against its neighbours
paragraphs: Within this corridor, Remraam is comparatively well placed, and that changes the tutoring calculation in a way worth stating. South View School sits close to the community and takes students through Year 11, which means the IGCSE years can be managed with a short run. Families in Mudon, Arabian Ranches 3 and Town Square face longer journeys in every direction, and that difference shows up in how late an evening session has to start.

The advantage is narrower than it looks, though. A school nearby is not a tutor nearby. The people advertising along this stretch of Dubailand are based around Dubai Investment Park, Dubai Sports City and Motor City, and the tuition centres are concentrated in Motor City. A Remraam family can reach a school in ten minutes and still face a thirty-minute round trip for a group class at six.

For the Diploma the position reverses. There is no IB provision inside or immediately beside Remraam, so a student continuing to a Diploma generally moves towards Dubai Hills, Al Barsha South or The Sustainable City. That makes Year 11 a decision year here more than it is in communities where the same school continues to eighteen.

The table sets out what each community in this corridor can actually reach, because the answer to the tutoring question depends less on distance than families assume and more on which board and level they need.

One operational note. Because the run from Remraam to South View School is short, evening sessions here can start earlier than almost anywhere else in this belt, which is worth using. A session at a quarter past four with a student who is not yet tired is a better hour than the same session at eight, and families who have only ever known a long commute often do not realise that option is open to them.

sections.heading: Moving curriculum mid-phase: what actually breaks
paragraphs: Transfers happen constantly in Dubai and they are handled better when the specific risks are named. Three things break, and none of them is general ability. The first is content order: two curricula can cover the same topics in a different sequence across two years, so a student arriving in the middle has met some later material and missed some earlier material, which looks like random weakness.

The second is the style of answer. An Indian-board student may know more content and write it in a form IGCSE does not reward, particularly on application and extended response. An MYP student moving into IGCSE brings strong research habits and has not sat timed papers. An American-curriculum student arrives without terminal examination experience at all. Each of those is a technique gap with a different fix.

The third, and the most consequential, is the tier decision. Where a subject is tiered, schools place students on the evidence they have, and a student who arrives mid-Year-10 has produced little evidence at the new school. Conservative placement is a reasonable response and can cap a grade the student would otherwise have reached. Raising this with the school early, with work from the previous school attached, is the single most useful administrative act available to a transferring family.

The right first piece of tutoring in all three cases is mapping rather than teaching. Comparing the two syllabus documents produces a list of specific gaps, and a list is both cheaper and more reassuring than being taught a course the student has largely already done.
bullets: Content order differs between curricula, which looks like random weakness
Answer style differs: application, extended response and timed performance
Tier placement is made on limited evidence for a mid-phase arrival
Map the gaps against the syllabus before paying for general teaching

sections.heading: Online, in-home and centre help compared from Remraam
paragraphs: A fair comparison counts the whole arrangement rather than the hourly figure. In-home visits carry travel inside the quote, which is why they are advertised at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour in this market, with Bestimate's range at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors publishing AED 200 to 500. They also carry a fixed arrival window, and a visiting tutor cannot absorb a late bus when the next household is elsewhere.

Centre classes shift the travel to the family. A ninety-minute class in Motor City from an Al Thamam apartment is a round trip at peak time, which for a Year 11 means leaving before homework starts and returning after it should have finished. The fee looks lower and the evening pays the difference. Where the group matches the student's board and tier and the timing genuinely suits, that trade can still be worth making.

Online one-to-one sits in the qualified band at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150, and it removes travel from both sides. What it asks in return is a quiet room, a stable connection and a parent who reads the session notes. For practical science work it cannot replace the school laboratory and does not claim to; it teaches what the paper asks about practical work, which is where those marks sit.

Monthly, Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour arrangement run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, with market packages including AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are published market figures, not IB Gram prices.

sections.heading: What the Ministry counts, and what no tutor can promise
paragraphs: Equivalency is the part of this comparison that families discover late, usually when a university application is in view. On the British track, a student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The detail that catches people is which subjects count. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, even though Dubai private schools must teach them. A student who assumed those two carried part of the load can arrive at the count short. One page currently ranking for these searches states that UAE candidates need six IGCSE subjects; the published rule is five, and getting that right matters more than any ranking does.

For the American track the requirements are different, with English proficiency shown by an IELTS academic score of 5, a TOEFL iBT score of 61, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics by at least 450 in the SAT Math test. For the IB, no points threshold should be taken from any tutoring page, including this one, without being read on the Ministry's own site.

Two things follow. IB Gram does not perform equivalency or attestation and cannot guarantee any outcome from it; the process belongs to the Ministry and the relevant emirate authority, and their official channels are the place to verify every detail. And tutoring is not required for equivalency. The rule asks for subjects and grades, and implying otherwise would be a false-urgency claim about a regulatory process.
bullets: British track: five accredited IGCSE subjects at E or 3 or above, plus A Level at E or two AS Levels
Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the five

sections.heading: Permits, premises and coursework boundaries
paragraphs: Three administrative facts bound any tutoring arrangement in Dubai, and all three are checkable. An individual giving private lessons needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students.

MoHRE's own service listing is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, shows no fees and a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so a figure quoted to you as the penalty is unverified.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram has no UAE premises, holds no such permit, and does not use a regulator's name to describe its tutors.

On coursework, where a centre runs assessed work it must be the student's own. A tutor may teach the subject, explain what criteria reward, say that an approach will not produce what the task needs, and mark the student's own draft against descriptors. A tutor may not write, draft, complete or edit the work to completion, or supply text. Board material belongs to its publishers and is linked rather than circulated.
