process.title: Say where the student came from
process.description: For a transferring family this is the most useful single fact. An Indian-board arrival, an MYP arrival and an American-curriculum arrival each bring a different combination of content strength and technique gap, and the first block of work differs completely between them.

process.title: Get board, code and tier in writing
process.description: Ask the school for subject, board, code and tier for each IGCSE entry. Dubailand schools do not all use one board across a timetable, and past papers from the wrong code teach the wrong habits for an entire term.

process.title: Map the gaps before buying teaching
process.description: Comparing the previous syllabus with the IGCSE one produces a list of specific gaps. A list is cheaper than a course and more reassuring than being retaught material the student already knows. It also gives the school something concrete for a tier conversation.

process.title: Free trial lesson, then a fixed slot
process.description: A trial over live video at no cost and before any payment. Afterwards the slot sits on Gulf Standard Time around the short run from South View School or wherever the student attends, and it can move within the evening or after Iftar during Ramadan at no cost.

process.title: Review against the series and the destination
process.description: Every few weeks the plan is checked against the entered series, the mock window and where the student is heading after Year 11. A sixth form in the UAE, a British sixth form and an IB Diploma each imply slightly different subject priorities.

whyPoints.title: The comparison comes before the coaching
whyPoints.description: Knowing what IGCSE is for, against the MYP, American and Indian routes, changes what a tutoring hour should aim at. A student heading for a UAE university has a different subject calculus from one heading for a British sixth form.

whyPoints.title: Transfers are mapped, not retaught
whyPoints.description: A student arriving mid-phase needs a list of specific gaps built by comparing two syllabus documents, not a course taught from the beginning. That is cheaper, faster, and gives the school evidence for a tier conversation.

whyPoints.title: Board and code are confirmed first
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson expect different amounts of written method and phrase questions differently. Confirming the code per subject takes one message to the school and prevents a term of practice aimed at the wrong paper.

whyPoints.title: Equivalency is described, never promised
whyPoints.description: The five-subject British-track rule and the American-track test thresholds are quoted with their source. IB Gram does not perform or guarantee equivalency, and does not suggest tutoring is required for it, because that would be a false claim about a regulatory process.

whyPoints.title: No travel on either side
whyPoints.description: An in-home visit prices the drive inside the hourly rate and a centre class charges the family's evening instead. An online session begins when the student sits down, which is also why a late bus from school does not cost the lesson.

whyPoints.title: No regulator names as credentials
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no KHDA permit, no ADEK registration, no board affiliation and no UAE office. Where a competing page attaches a regulator's name to its tutors, that is a claim to check rather than a qualification.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE tutor visit homes in Remraam?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Lessons are taught one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only. Visiting tutors exist in Dubai and are advertised at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel folded into the price, per Bestimate's Dubai cost table and the rates independent home tutors publish. From an Al Thamam or Al Ramth apartment the online route buys a tutor matched to the board and code the student is entered for, rather than whoever is willing to drive along this corridor at five.

faqs.question: Why is the British curriculum so common in Dubai schools?
faqs.answer: Mostly scale and portability. In 2024-25 the UK curriculum accounted for 37 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment, against 26 per cent Indian, 14 per cent American and 7 per cent International Baccalaureate across 227 schools and 17 curricula. IGCSE produces subject grades at sixteen that a sixth form in almost any country can read without explanation, which suits a population that moves. The practical consequence for tutoring is that IGCSE coverage along this corridor is broader and more price-competitive than coverage for the other routes.

faqs.question: Should a Dubailand child study IGCSE or the Middle Years Programme?
faqs.answer: It depends on how the child works and where they are heading, not on prestige. IGCSE is terminal and subject-based, rewards examination technique, and leaves a portable qualification at sixteen that feeds Ministry equivalency directly. The MYP is criterion-based and continuous, rewards research and reflection, usually ends without external examination, and prepares unusually well for the IB Diploma because the assessment language carries over. A student who performs well under examination pressure and may change country is well served by IGCSE.

faqs.question: What breaks when a child moves from an Indian board into IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Usually not ability. Three things break: content order, because two curricula cover the same material in a different sequence, so gaps look like random weakness; answer style, because Indian-board students often know more content and write it in a form IGCSE rewards less, especially on application and extended response; and tier placement, since a mid-phase arrival has produced little evidence at the new school. The first useful piece of work is a mapped list of specific gaps rather than being retaught a course largely already covered.

faqs.question: Which subjects does the Ministry count when a Remraam student applies locally?
faqs.answer: Five. Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track asks for five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five, which is the detail that leaves families short. One page ranking for these searches states six; the published rule is five. IB Gram does not perform equivalency, and the Ministry's channels are where to verify it.

faqs.question: Is Remraam better placed for school access than Mudon?
faqs.answer: At IGCSE level, yes. South View School sits close to the community and takes students through Year 11, so the school run here is short by the standards of this belt, while Mudon, Arabian Ranches 3 and Town Square have no secondary provision inside their boundaries at all. For the Diploma the advantage disappears, because there is no IB provision beside Remraam and a continuing student generally moves towards Dubai Hills, Al Barsha South or The Sustainable City. A nearby school is also not a nearby tutor.

faqs.question: Does an American-curriculum student need IGCSE-style tutoring?
faqs.answer: A different kind. The American route has no terminal examination at sixteen; a student accumulates credits and a grade point average across four years, with standardised testing and Advanced Placement carrying subject depth. The tutoring need is therefore steady coursework support and test preparation rather than examination technique in a single season. For equivalency, the American track asks for English through IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT 450 reading and writing, and mathematics through at least 450 in the SAT Math test.

faqs.question: Which board does South View School use for IGCSE subjects?
faqs.answer: Ask the school directly and ask per subject, because schools in this belt do not all use one board across a timetable and a single answer for the whole student is often wrong. Request subject, board, code and tier in writing. Then check the code on the front of any past paper the student has been given against that list. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel phrase questions differently and expect different amounts of written method, so practice from the other board can cost marks the student had earned.

faqs.question: Is a group revision class in Motor City worth the trip from Remraam?
faqs.answer: Only when the room matches the student's board and tier and the timing genuinely suits. A group works well where everyone sits the same paper with roughly the same gap, which happens most often in spring-term mathematics. Dubailand groups usually mix Cambridge and Pearson students at two tiers, which forces content teaching rather than paper technique. Then count the evening: a ninety-minute class at peak time means leaving before homework starts and returning after it should have finished, which is a real cost even when the fee is lower.

faqs.question: What should a transferring family ask the new school first?
faqs.answer: Four things, in writing. Which board and code is my child entered for in each subject. Which tier, where the subject is tiered. What is the last date that entry can be amended. And what evidence would you want to see to review the tier. A mid-phase arrival is placed on limited evidence, and conservative placement is a reasonable response that can nonetheless cap a grade. Work from the previous school, attached early, is the most useful thing a transferring family can supply.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle a transfer mapping and then the teaching?
faqs.answer: Usually, and it is the efficient arrangement. The mapping block establishes exactly which content the IGCSE syllabus assumes and the previous course did not cover, which takes two or three sessions with both syllabus documents open. The teaching that follows is then narrow and targeted rather than a general course. The same tutor carrying both means nothing is re-explained, and the gap list doubles as a progress record for the school and for any tier conversation that follows.

faqs.question: How much should a Remraam family budget for one IGCSE subject?
faqs.answer: A qualified subject tutor working online in this market sits at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Across a month, Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Market packages include AED 799 monthly for eight online sessions. These are published figures rather than IB Gram prices, and a free trial comes first.

faqs.question: Do private tutors along this corridor need a licence?
faqs.answer: The individual does. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service listing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. A centre with premises needs a separate KHDA permit instead.

faqs.question: Does the choice of curriculum affect UAE university admission?
faqs.answer: It affects the equivalency route rather than the welcome. Each curriculum has its own set of requirements to satisfy: the British track through five IGCSE subjects at grade E or 3 or above excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus A Level or AS Level grades; the American track through SAT and English test thresholds. Those are Ministry requirements and they are verified through Ministry and emirate channels. No tutor performs equivalency, guarantees it, or is required for it, and any page implying otherwise is making a claim about a regulatory process it does not control.

intro.heading: In Serena, the bus timetable decides what tutoring can achieve
paragraphs: Serena sits at the outer edge of the Dubailand belt, off Al Qudra Road, built around townhouse clusters including Bella Casa and Casa Viva, with Mudon on one side and Remraam and Villanova nearby. Its children do not all attend one school. Some travel ten minutes to the Dubailand and Sustainable City schools, others thirty-five to fifty minutes to the larger British-curriculum schools in Al Barsha and Jumeirah Park. That spread is the first fact any tutoring plan has to deal with.

The practical effect is a difference of nearly an hour in when the school day actually ends. A Year 11 arriving at 15:50 can eat, settle and start a serious session at 16:30. A Year 11 arriving at 16:40 after fifty minutes on Al Khail Road cannot do the same work at 17:15, whatever the diary says. Both students are often sold the same weekly arrangement, and only one of them gets value from it.

An in-home tutor adds a second journey on top of the first. Serena is not on the way to anywhere for most of Dubai's tutoring workforce: a round trip is eighty to a hundred and twenty minutes on an ordinary weekday. That is why market in-home rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for the same qualified tutor teaching online, and why the tutors willing to make the drive are selected by willingness rather than by specification knowledge.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we offer only in India, and Serena students are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The gain is not just the saved journey: the slot becomes a scheduling decision rather than a logistics constraint, so the harder subject can take the earlier, better hour.

This page is built around that. Which schools this community feeds and when each one really releases. What IGCSE work fits an early slot and what survives a late one. How to confirm the board and tier before a single session is booked. What the market charges and what the drive adds. How mock season, Ramadan and the Dubai calendar move the plan. And who is legally permitted to teach your child at all.

Every figure here names its source so you can check it rather than take it on trust. Where a decision depends on your child's specific entry, the answer is in the school's entry statement rather than on any page, including this one. For scale, Dubai's private sector runs 227 schools teaching 17 curricula to 387,441 students, with UK curricula accounting for 37 per cent of enrolment, per Dubai Media Office figures for 2024-25. That is why two Serena neighbours can both say their child sits IGCSEs and mean different boards, different tiers and different practical routes.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-serena.programmesIntro: The right session content changes with the year group as much as with the subject, because what the evening can support changes too.

programmes.name: Year 9, before the course begins
programmes.description: The year with the most usable evening time and the least pressure, which makes it the most efficient year to spend in. Algebraic fluency, scientific notation and writing that answers the question set are the three things that decide IGCSE grades two years later. A short block here routinely removes the need for a year of Year 11 sessions.
programmes.countryNote: Year 9 in Dubai is also when option choices are made, including triple versus combined science. For Serena families the choice interacts with the commute: a subject requiring frequent after-school practical catch-up is harder to sustain from a school fifty minutes away than from one ten minutes away.

programmes.name: Year 10, content delivery
programmes.description: The year to work topic by topic with past-paper questions as each topic is taught, so gaps surface early rather than in Year 11 revision. For students on the long commute, the sustainable pattern is one 60-minute session at a realistic hour rather than 90 minutes that starts too late and finishes badly.
programmes.countryNote: Some Dubai schools enter students for one or two subjects in the June series at the end of Year 10. If your child's school does, the entry deadline sits months earlier and the Year 10 evening is already an exam-year evening. Get the entry list from the exam office in writing.

programmes.name: Year 11, mocks and the series
programmes.description: The year when slot quality matters most, because the work is timed papers and strict marking. A paper attempted at 20:00 after a long day tells you about fatigue rather than about preparation. Where the commute forces a late slot, the fix is to move timed attempts to weekend mornings and use weekday evenings for marking and review.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. The second series functions as a resit route, which means a poor January mock is a decision point rather than a catastrophe, and the decision is easier to make calmly if the plan already allows for it.

programmes.name: After IGCSE
programmes.description: A Level or IB Diploma, and in this belt frequently a change of school and therefore of commute. The step up is steeper than grades suggest: both routes reward sustained argument and independent work rather than coverage. Bridging support over the summer is consistently better value than remediation in the first term.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3 are required, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. Verify current requirements on moe.gov.ae before relying on them.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-serena.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Serena households ask about, with the syllabus codes to quote and a note on when in the evening each kind of work is realistically possible.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: New technique needs an early slot; past-paper marking survives a late one. Confirm the tier first, since it sets the grade ceiling. Method marks lost to unshown working are the cheapest marks in the subject to recover.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity is the reliable weak point in UAE cohorts and needs concentration, so it belongs in the earliest available hour. Alternative-to-practical method writing and graph work are far more tolerant of a late start.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles calculations under time pressure are a fluency problem and need a fresh student. Qualitative analysis wording and organic reaction types are learnable late in the evening because they are recall and pattern rather than reasoning.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: The most late-slot-friendly science: command-term marking, diagram labelling and data interpretation all work at 19:30. The commonest loss is answering 'explain' with description, which is a marking habit rather than a content gap.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Sciences
subjects.description: All three disciplines feed one or two shared grades, so the weakest discipline sets the ceiling. For a student on the long commute, targeting that single discipline is both cheaper and kinder than three sessions a week.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 / 0990)
subjects.description: Composition and directed writing need an alert student and benefit from an early slot. Reading-question technique and annotation practice are perfectly workable later, which makes English a useful subject to schedule around a difficult commute.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: A different course from First Language and often confused with it. Listening and speaking components are examined, and speaking practice works well in any slot because it is conversation rather than sustained writing.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Evaluation question structures take two or three sessions to install and can be taught at almost any hour. Case-study reading is homework rather than tutored time, which makes these subjects efficient for families with short evenings.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478 / 4CP0)
subjects.description: Pseudocode and hand-tracing need focus and belong earlier; theory topics such as binary and data representation are formulaic and survive a late slot. Students fluent in Python still lose marks on board-standard notation.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.description: Mandatory in Dubai private schools under KHDA requirements whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs. Excluded from the five subjects counted for Ministry of Education British-track equivalency, but real timetabled work that competes for the same evening.

sections.heading: What Serena parents are really asking for
paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor, in this community, means one-to-one teaching that happens at home at a time that survives the school run. It almost never means a specific preference for a stranger in the living room. When families describe what they want, they describe outcomes: no second car journey, no 20:30 start, the same tutor every week, and somebody who knows the specification rather than the subject in general.

Those requirements pull against each other once geography is involved. Restrict the search to tutors willing to drive to Al Qudra Road on a weekday afternoon and the pool shrinks to a handful, then you choose within it by availability. For a mainstream need that may be fine. For Pearson 4CH1 Chemistry at Higher tier with a January mock to recover from, the pool may contain nobody who has taught that specification.

IB Gram resolves it by separating the two things parents are conflating. The teaching is one-to-one and live, with a tutor matched to your child's board and tier, and it reaches a desk in Serena over video. No tutor arrives at a UAE address, in Serena or anywhere else, because home visits are an India-only service. What you gain is the specification match and the slot; what you give up is a car in the driveway.

The rest of this page is written for the family that wants that comparison made properly rather than asserted: the arrival times, the work that fits each slot, the board check, the market rates with sources, and the calendar that moves everything twice a year.

sections.heading: The Serena school run, hour by hour
paragraphs: This is the table that decides whether tutoring works in this community, and it is the one no tutoring page bothers to build. Below are the school clusters Serena children travel to, the realistic arrival at home, the earliest session start we would actually recommend, and the IGCSE work that fits the hour that follows.

Two patterns are worth drawing out. The nearest schools are not always the earliest arrivals, because pick-up congestion around Motor City and Sports City between 15:00 and 16:00 can add twenty minutes to a short drive. And the larger British-curriculum schools in Al Barsha release early but sit on the wrong side of the afternoon traffic, so an on-paper 15:15 finish reaches Serena at 16:30 or later.

Treat the final columns as the useful part. The principle is that work requiring sustained reasoning — new mathematical technique, physics problem setup, composition writing — needs the earliest hour available. Work that responds to something already on the page — marking a paper, correcting a past attempt, learning qualitative analysis wording, practising command-term phrasing — survives a late start perfectly well.

That principle has a counter-intuitive consequence for families on the long commute. Rather than fighting for an impossible 17:00 session that happens two weeks in three, move the demanding work to a weekend morning and keep a shorter weekday slot for marking and corrections. A later session that happens forty times beats an earlier one cancelled twelve times, and the second pattern is what most families accidentally buy.

sections.heading: What fits a late evening and what does not
paragraphs: Families on the long commute are often told that a late session is as good as an early one, which is not true, and then told that tutoring will not work for them, which is also not true. The accurate position is that the content has to change.

Work that needs a fresh student: first exposure to any abstract technique, timed papers, extended writing, multi-step problem setup in maths and physics, and anything where the student must hold several steps in mind at once. Attempt these at 20:00 and the result measures tiredness. Worse, a timed paper done badly at that hour produces a misleading diagnosis, and the next four sessions get aimed at a problem the student does not actually have.

Work that survives a late start: marking a paper the student has already attempted, going through corrections, learning recall-heavy material such as qualitative analysis observations or biology definitions, practising command-term phrasing, rehearsing speaking components, planning an essay structure, and talking through the next week's plan. None of these require sustained novel reasoning, and several are improved by the student being calm rather than sharp.

The practical arrangement that follows is a split week: demanding work on a weekend morning, review work in a short weekday slot. It is more effort to schedule and it is the difference between tutoring that holds for a year and tutoring that quietly collapses in February. We will propose it where the arrival time warrants it, rather than selling the standard weekly hour to everybody.

sections.heading: Confirm the board and the tier before booking any slot
paragraphs: Scheduling is half the problem; the other half is making sure the hour is spent on the right specification. Ask the school's exam office for the entry statement, which names the board, the syllabus code and the tier for every subject. Departments inside one Dubai school sometimes differ — Cambridge sciences with Pearson maths is a common combination — so check subject by subject.

The differences are not cosmetic. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 is tiered Core and Extended and includes a non-calculator written paper alongside a calculator paper; Pearson 4MA1 is tiered Foundation and Higher and permits a calculator in both papers. In the sciences, the practical assessment route differs, as does the style of questions about required practicals. Formula provision differs too.

That changes what a session should contain, which is why it changes scheduling as well. A Cambridge student needs regular non-calculator fluency work, which belongs in an early slot because it is mental arithmetic under pressure. A Pearson student needs calculator discipline — showing the input, sketching the display, not trusting a window that hides a root — which is a procedural habit that can be taught at almost any hour.

Confirm all of it against the board's current specification for your child's entry year, because paper structures and grading are revised between versions. Those documents are free on the board's own site and are what any competent tutor works from. Nobody should be charging you for them or supplying them as a resource pack.

sections.heading: What the market charges, and what the drive to Serena adds
paragraphs: Serena is among the furthest-out communities in this belt, so the travel component in any in-home quote is substantial. Market in-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai runs roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table showing AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500. Expect the upper half for this address.

Online, the same qualified subject tutor sits at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150, and an IGCSE or A Level specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Budget online tuition starts at AED 33 to 65, per Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, and buys supervision rather than diagnosis.

The premium between the two formats for the same person is roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour, and across a school year of weekly sessions that is around AED 1,500 to 4,500 spent on driving. It buys presence, which is the right purchase for a child who genuinely cannot work on a screen and the wrong one for a Year 11 marking past papers. Monthly packages visible in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

These are market figures from the parties named rather than IB Gram's price list. We quote per student after the free trial lesson, because the right band depends on what the marked work shows: a Core-tier student securing the top of their tier and an Extended-tier student chasing the upper grades are not the same product.

sections.heading: Mock season, Ramadan and the Dubai calendar
paragraphs: Three things reliably move a Serena family's tutoring plan during the year, and a plan that does not anticipate them is a plan that gets abandoned rather than adjusted.

Mock season is the first. Schools compress mocks into one or two weeks, during which a student's evenings are already full and a weekly session is better used for targeted review than for new content. The useful move is to pause new teaching, mark the mock scripts properly as they come back, and then rebuild the plan from what the scripts show. That is also the cheapest diagnostic a family will ever get, and it is free.

Ramadan is the second. Dubai schools shorten the day, which changes both arrival times and the hours in which concentration is available. Sessions commonly move later, often to post-Iftar, and hold at the new time for the month before moving back. Because nothing depends on a tutor's commute, the change is a diary adjustment rather than a renegotiation. It is also a sensible period to shift from new content to consolidation.

The third is school events and travel, which in this community are frequent. A clashed online session can usually be moved within the same week; a missed in-home visit is a wasted journey and is normally charged in full. Across a two-year IGCSE course that difference compounds into several hours of teaching either kept or lost, which is worth more than a small difference in the hourly rate.

sections.heading: Who is legally permitted to teach your child
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work rather than unregulated work, and verifying it costs nothing. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

The application route is MoHRE's own 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service, through the smart app, website or e-services system, with a two-working-day completion time and no listed fee. Because the permit is free, no tutor should be passing on a licensing cost. And because u.ae states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, a tutor who describes the permit as optional has told you something useful. No fine schedule has been published, so treat any amount quoted at you as unverified.

The institutional layer is separate. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, a specific licence with initial approval, completion steps and annual renewal. IB Gram holds none, claims none, and has no UAE office or centre. KHDA is responsible for overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, which is a fact about KHDA rather than an endorsement of anybody, and no phrase on this site should be read as regulator approval.

One rule from the next emirate is worth knowing, because families cross the border for schools. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document, so verify the current wording — but do not arrange for your child's own class teacher to tutor them privately.

sections.heading: Entries, series and results for a UAE candidate
paragraphs: The calendar point most generic articles get wrong for this country is the exam series, and it is the one a family actually acts on. Cambridge International runs IGCSE exams in a June series and a November series. The February/March series is offered to India only and does not apply to a candidate sitting in the UAE, so advice built around a February window belongs to another country.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and its exams officers' guide states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, adding that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam where the wrong zone timetable was used. Ask your school's exam officer which zone the centre sits in before anything is printed or diarised.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. As checkable reference points: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables for later series that may be revised, so work from the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

Working backwards, the order that matters is the school's internal coursework and mock deadlines first, then the board entry deadline, then the exam window. The first is earliest and is the one a family can actually miss. The November series also functions as the resit route after a June result, which is why a bad January mock is a decision point rather than a disaster.

process.description: A genuine lesson with the person who would continue, no card required. It diagnoses against the specification — what your child can do, which paper the marks are leaking from — and it tests whether the pair of them work well together. A wrong fit means another match, not a paid block nobody enjoys.

whyPoints.description: Because nobody drives to Al Qudra Road, the session time is a scheduling choice rather than a logistics constraint. For a community whose children arrive home anywhere between 15:45 and 16:40, that is the single largest practical gain available.

whyPoints.title: Content matched to the hour
whyPoints.description: New technique, timed papers and extended writing go in the earliest slot available. Marking, corrections, recall material and command-term work go later. Selling the same weekly hour to every family regardless of arrival time is why tutoring collapses in February.

whyPoints.title: Specification before scheduling
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 differ on tiering and calculator rules, and the sciences differ on practical routes. We confirm the board, code and tier from the entry statement before the first session rather than discovering a mismatch after a term.

whyPoints.title: Rescheduling that survives a Dubai year
whyPoints.description: Mock weeks, Ramadan, school events and travel all move sessions in this community. An online slot usually moves inside the same week; a missed home visit is a wasted journey and is normally charged. Across two years that is hours of teaching kept rather than lost.

whyPoints.title: Claims you can verify
whyPoints.description: Every AED band names its publisher, every regulatory statement names u.ae, KHDA or MoHRE, and there is no UAE office, no regulator approval, no named school as a client, and no home visits anywhere in the country — that is an India-only service.

faqs.question: What time can an IGCSE session realistically start in Serena?
faqs.answer: It depends on the school cluster. Children at the Dubailand and Sustainable City schools are usually home by 16:00 and can start comfortably at 16:30. The Arabian Ranches run supports 17:00. Students travelling back from the larger Al Barsha and Jumeirah Park schools arrive between 16:20 and 16:50, which makes 18:00 the earliest start we would actually recommend. Remraam and outer Dubailand routes push that later again. The arrival time matters more than the subject when planning the week.

faqs.question: Will an IGCSE tutor come to our house in Serena?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We teach UAE students one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service we offer only in India, so no tutor will arrive at a Dubailand address. Independent in-home tutors do work in this belt at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, and Serena sits at the upper end of that because the round trip is eighty to a hundred and twenty minutes. If presence in the room is what your child needs, that market is the right place to look.

faqs.question: Can tutoring work if my child only gets home at 16:45?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the content has to change rather than the time being forced earlier. Work needing a fresh student — new technique, timed papers, extended writing, multi-step problem setup — belongs in the earliest hour you can get, which for a long commute often means a weekend morning. A shorter weekday evening slot is then used for marking the week's attempts, going through corrections, recall material and command-term phrasing. That split week holds for a year; a forced 17:00 session usually does not.

faqs.question: Which schools do Serena children usually attend?
faqs.answer: A wide spread rather than one catchment. The nearest cluster includes GEMS Metropole in Motor City, Victory Heights Primary, Jebel Ali School in DAMAC Hills, and the Arabian Ranches schools including Jumeirah English Speaking School and Ranches Primary. Many families travel further to the larger British-curriculum schools in Al Barsha and Jumeirah Park, such as Dubai British School Jumeirah Park, Safa Community School and Kings' School Al Barsha. Schools are named as local context only; no affiliation with any of them is implied or held.

faqs.question: Does a late session actually produce worse results?
faqs.answer: For some work, measurably. A timed paper attempted at 20:00 after a long commute tells you about fatigue rather than preparation, and a misleading diagnosis then misdirects the next several sessions. New abstract technique has the same problem: the student can follow it in the room and cannot reproduce it the next day. What genuinely works late is responding to something already on the page — marking, corrections, recall, planning — which is why the session content, not the session length, is what should change.

faqs.question: How do I confirm which board and tier my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Ask the exam office for the entry statement. It names the board, the syllabus code and the tier for every subject, and it occasionally contradicts what a family has assumed for two years. Departments inside one Dubai school sometimes differ, with Cambridge sciences alongside Pearson maths being a common combination, so check subject by subject. The reason it matters for scheduling as well as content is that Cambridge maths includes a non-calculator paper while Pearson permits a calculator throughout, and those need different kinds of practice at different times of day.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE tutor cost for a Serena family?
faqs.answer: A qualified subject tutor teaching online runs roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150; specialists are AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270. Budget online tuition is AED 33 to 65, per Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel, at the upper end for Serena. Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those are market figures, not our price list.

faqs.question: How should the plan change during mock week?
faqs.answer: Pause new content. Mock weeks fill a student's evenings, and a session during them is better spent on targeted review than on teaching. The valuable work comes afterwards: mark the returned scripts properly, label every lost mark as knowledge, method or reading the question, and rebuild the plan from what the totals show. Mocks are the cheapest and most accurate diagnostic a family will ever get, they are free, and most households read only the overall grade before filing them.

faqs.question: Do sessions move during Ramadan for Dubailand families?
faqs.answer: Usually, and it is straightforward. Dubai schools shorten the day, which changes arrival times and the hours in which concentration is available, so slots commonly move later and often to post-Iftar, holding at the new time for the month before moving back. Because no commute is involved, it is a diary adjustment rather than a renegotiation. It is also a sensible period to shift from new content to consolidation, since review and marking survive a disrupted routine far better than first exposure to a difficult topic.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE exams for a student sitting in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates. The February/March series is offered to India only, so any article quoting a February or March window is not describing your child's exams. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. For reference, the November 2026 Pearson final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026. Because provisional timetables can be revised, open the board's live official timetable rather than relying on a restated date.

faqs.question: What happens when a school event clashes with the session?
faqs.answer: It gets moved, usually within the same week, because there is no journey to re-plan on either side. This matters more than families expect over a two-year course: school events in this community move at short notice, and a missed in-home visit is a wasted journey that is normally charged in full. Across Year 10 and Year 11, with mock weeks, travel and illness, the difference between rescheduling and forfeiting adds up to several hours of teaching either kept or lost.

faqs.question: Can two children in the same Serena household share a tutor?
faqs.answer: They can share a tutor, but rarely a slot. Siblings are usually on different boards or tiers, and often on different bus routes with arrival times forty minutes apart, so consecutive slots work better than a shared one. Where two students genuinely match — same board, same tier, same subject, similar starting point — a pair session lowers the cost per student and halves the scheduling problem. That often works better between neighbouring households in Serena, Villanova and Mudon than between siblings.

faqs.question: Do private tutors teaching Serena children need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, applying through MoHRE's Private Tutor Licensing service with a two-working-day completion time. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule is published, distrust any amount quoted at you.

faqs.question: Does my child still take Arabic and Islamic Education alongside IGCSEs?
faqs.answer: In a Dubai private school, yes. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in all private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and at least 25 minutes advised for any mandatory-subject lesson. Separate classes must be organised for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes are prohibited. Note that for Ministry of Education British-track equivalency, Arabic and Islamic Education are excluded from the five subjects that count, which is worth knowing before option choices are finalised.

With those we can tell you honestly which slots exist, what each one should contain, and whether a weekend session for timed work makes more sense than a weekday hour. The first lesson is free and taught by the tutor who would continue. All teaching is live, one-to-one and online on Gulf Standard Time, and nobody drives to Al Qudra Road.

intro.heading: At IGCSE, "knows the syllabus" means knows the specification code
paragraphs: Parents searching for a local IGCSE tutor are usually worried about the wrong variable. The worry is distance. The actual risk is that the tutor knows the subject and not the specification, and at IGCSE that gap is wider than most families realise. Three awarding bodies are in common use across Dubai schools, and they do not set the same papers, assess practical work the same way, or even always offer the same tiers.

The gap is not academic snobbery. It is the difference between a student who has rehearsed the paper in front of them and one who has rehearsed a similar paper set by a different organisation, and in the last eight weeks before a series that difference is the whole game.

Take maths. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics runs Core and Extended tiers and, under the syllabus in use from 2025, pairs a non-calculator paper with a calculator paper. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A runs Foundation and Higher tiers and permits a calculator in both papers. A tutor who drills mental arithmetic with a Pearson candidate is spending your money on a skill the paper never tests. A tutor who never drills it with a Cambridge candidate has left half a paper unrehearsed. Same subject, same year group, opposite preparation.

The sciences diverge too. Cambridge IGCSE sciences offer an alternative-to-practical paper route, so a candidate's experimental skills may be assessed through a written paper about practical work. Pearson's International GCSE sciences assess practical understanding within the written papers rather than through a separate practical examination. Either way, a Dubai student studying partly online needs to know which model applies to them, and so does whoever is teaching them. The school knows and will tell you if you ask for the specification code in writing.

So that is the honest answer to the question behind the search. Sobha Hartland is well served for schools and thinly served, like every Dubai community, for subject specialists who happen to live nearby and happen to know the exact specification your child sits. The chance of those three conditions coinciding in nine subjects is low. The chance of a parent discovering the mismatch before the final eight weeks is lower still, because a competent tutor teaching the wrong specification looks exactly like a competent tutor.

IB Gram handles it by removing geography from the match. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and we ask for the specification code before proposing anyone. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The sections below give the board comparison, the home-visit market rates, the arithmetic of supporting a student across nine subjects, and the series calendar counted backwards. Nothing here promises a grade. It gives you the questions that make a tutor's competence testable in one lesson, which is more useful than a promise.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-sobha-hartland.programmesIntro: Sobha Hartland students reach IGCSE through more than one route and leave it for more than one destination. These three stages are where a specification question changes what tutoring should actually do, and each has a different cost profile across a year.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9, before IGCSE begins
programmes.description: The years nobody tutors and the years where tutoring is cheapest to make count. Algebraic fluency, reading stamina and scientific vocabulary are built here, and a student who arrives in Year 10 without them spends two years catching up at a time when new content is arriving weekly. A short block in Year 8 or 9 on one weak foundation costs a fraction of a Year 11 recovery programme.
programmes.countryNote: In the central corridor many students transfer between schools and sometimes between curricula during these years, arriving from American, Indian or national systems. Those transitions leave specific, identifiable gaps rather than general weakness, which is why a diagnostic first lesson matters more for a transfer student than for anyone else.

programmes.name: Years 10 and 11, the examination course
programmes.description: Typically eight to ten subjects sat as external examinations, with tiering decided by the school in most subjects that offer it. There is no safety net: in most IGCSE subjects the written papers carry the whole grade, so a weak paper is not offset by coursework. The specification code determines the paper structure, the tiers available and how practical or spoken skills are assessed.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's UK-curriculum schools account for the largest share of private enrolment in the emirate, so IGCSE is the commonest qualification a Hartland tutor is asked about. That breadth is why the specification question matters: a large market using several awarding bodies produces tutors who have taught one and assume the others are the same.

programmes.name: What the IGCSE grade is actually for
programmes.description: IGCSE grades open or close post-16 routes. Schools set entry requirements for A Level and IB Diploma courses, often a grade 6 or 7 in the subject, and those thresholds are where a Year 11 grade stops being a report-card number. Students heading for Higher Level sciences or A Level Mathematics need fluency rather than a bare pass, which is a different target from the one most revision aims at.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools near Sobha Hartland offer both the IB Diploma and A Levels after IGCSE, so the Year 11 results decide the shape of the next two years. Families who work out the post-16 entry requirements during Year 10 tend to buy far less tutoring in Year 12 than those who treat results day as the moment to start planning.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-sobha-hartland.igcseSubjectsIntro: The same subjects viewed by awarding body, because the code is what determines the paper your child actually sits. Ask the school for it in writing before booking any tutoring.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Tier and calculator rules both depend on the board. Marks go missing in algebraic manipulation, in multi-step problems where no working is written down, and in the missing final statement on geometry and trigonometry questions.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Equation rearrangement and standard form cost more marks than conceptual misunderstanding. How practical skills are assessed differs by board, which changes whether a student needs alternative-to-practical preparation at all.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, concentration and percentage yield are the arithmetic choke points, and organic chemistry rewards detail rather than recall. Students who skip balancing practice lose marks across every calculation question.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Terminology precision and data interpretation carry the marks. A student who writes fluently but imprecisely tends to plateau, and command-term work fixes that faster than more content revision.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: First Language and Second Language are different qualifications with different demands, and students are sometimes entered for the one that suits the school's timetable rather than their ability. Worth confirming which.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Set texts vary by school and by year, so a tutor must teach the actual texts rather than the skill in the abstract. Marks are lost in describing plot instead of analysing how a writer creates effect.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and percentage work are the two mark-losing areas, and the evaluation marks are verbal. A numerate student can do well here once the arithmetic is secure.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Break-even, ratio and cash-flow work are the quantitative core, and application to the given case study is where students lose the analysis marks by answering generically.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Number bases, logic and algorithm tracing are learnable in a handful of sessions. Programming questions reward precision in pseudocode conventions that differ between specifications.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by stronger Extended candidates in some corridor schools as a bridge to A Level or Higher Level maths. Students who struggle usually have an Extended gap rather than an Additional Mathematics one.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
igcseSubjects.description: Under the syllabus in use from 2025 each tier pairs a non-calculator paper with a calculator paper, both at 50%. Core cannot reach the top grades. Non-calculator drill is essential preparation here and not elsewhere.

igcseSubjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1
igcseSubjects.description: Two papers of two hours at 50% each, calculator permitted throughout. Higher tier reaches the top grades. The drill that matters is multi-step problem structuring rather than mental arithmetic.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE sciences 0620, 0625, 0610
igcseSubjects.description: Separate papers by tier, with an alternative-to-practical route available for experimental skills. A student studying partly online needs to know which practical option their centre uses.

igcseSubjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences 4CH1, 4PH1, 4BI1
igcseSubjects.description: Practical understanding is assessed within the written papers rather than through a separate practical examination, which changes what revision of experimental method looks like.

igcseSubjects.name: Oxford AQA International GCSE
igcseSubjects.description: In use at some Dubai centres and often overlooked by tutors who assume Cambridge or Pearson. Paper structures and assessment models differ, so the code must be confirmed rather than inferred from the subject name.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English 0500 and 0510
igcseSubjects.description: Two distinct qualifications with different components, including a speaking element in some routes. Students entered for the wrong one are working to the wrong criteria all year.

sections.heading: The three awarding bodies in Dubai and what actually changes between them
paragraphs: This is the section that justifies the page. A tutor who says they teach IGCSE Physics has told you almost nothing, because at least three awarding bodies set IGCSE Physics for Dubai candidates and they differ in paper structure, tiering and practical assessment. The subject name is shared; the examination is not. Ask your school for the specification code in writing, in every subject you are considering tutoring for, and give it to the tutor before the first lesson.

The differences are not cosmetic. Tier vocabulary changes: Cambridge uses Core and Extended, Pearson uses Foundation and Higher. Calculator rules change, and in maths that changes the entire shape of a revision programme. Practical assessment changes: Cambridge sciences offer an alternative-to-practical route, while Pearson assesses practical understanding inside the written papers. Series availability differs slightly, which matters when a resit is being planned. Oxford AQA, in use at some Dubai centres, is the one most often assumed away entirely.

There is one further difference worth understanding, because parents ask about it and almost nobody explains it. Some Pearson International GCSE qualifications allow assessment to be taken across more than one series rather than all at the end, which is where the word modular comes from in Dubai parents' groups. Cambridge IGCSE is normally sat as a complete set in a single series. Which model applies to your child depends on the subject and on what the school has chosen, so it is a question for the examinations officer rather than for a tutoring site. The answer changes when revision has to peak.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE home tutor costs here, and the nine-subject arithmetic
paragraphs: The home-visit market deserves straight figures rather than a redirection. In-home one-to-one in Dubai runs roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, travel included in the figure, with monthly packages advertised around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Online equivalents sit lower: around AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor, AED 200 to 450 and above for a specialist, and around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Those are other providers' published figures, read in October 2026, and they are market context rather than IB Gram's prices.

Now apply that to an IGCSE student, because this is where the arithmetic bites in a way it does not at Diploma level. An IGCSE candidate takes eight to ten subjects. A parent who decides tutoring is needed rarely means one subject; they mean maths, two sciences and possibly English. At in-home rates, four weekly subjects is sixteen to twenty contact hours a month and a figure that exceeds many school fee instalments. At that point the question stops being which tutor and becomes how many subjects genuinely need paying for.

The honest answer is usually one or two. In most cases the subjects that look weak share a cause: arithmetic and algebra showing up in Physics and Chemistry, or writing structure showing up in English and Economics. Fix the cause once and two or three grades move. The table below sets out what each rung costs when scaled to multiple subjects, so you can see where the spend stops being proportionate. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all, so the in-home rows are market context for comparison rather than something we sell.

sections.heading: Online against a home visit, from a Hartland address
paragraphs: With the figures on the table, the comparison can be made on something other than price. For an IGCSE student the variables that matter are slightly different from a Diploma student's, because the problem is usually breadth rather than depth: nine subjects, several mediocre, a parent who cannot tell which one to attack first.

On matching, online wins because the pool is the whole market and the specification code can be honoured. In-home narrows the field to those who will drive to Hartland at four in the afternoon, and in a nine-subject situation the chance that this person knows all the relevant specifications is small. On continuity, online wins because a student who moves house, changes school or travels keeps the same tutor. In a transient community like this one that is not a small advantage.

On accountability, online tends to win because marked practice and written feedback are easier to produce and to keep than verbal comments at a kitchen table, and a parent can check that it is happening without understanding the subject. On cost, online wins by the travel premium, which is between roughly AED 30 and 150 an hour in this market. The one variable where in-home has a real claim is supervision: a fourteen-year-old who will not work unless someone is physically present is a genuine category, and for them a local arrangement may be the right answer. We do not offer home visits in the UAE, so we will say so rather than pretend otherwise.

sections.heading: Nine subjects, one weak report: how to decide what to pay for
paragraphs: The commonest IGCSE enquiry is not about one subject. It is a report card with four or five grades below expectation and a parent who wants all of it fixed. Spending across five subjects at once is the single most expensive decision available in this market, and it is almost never necessary. There is a cheaper method and it takes one session plus a conversation.

Start by separating the subjects where the grade reflects understanding from those where it reflects a transferable weakness. Arithmetic and algebra sit underneath maths, physics, chemistry and the quantitative parts of economics and business. Writing structure sits underneath English, history and the extended answers in every humanities subject. Reading speed and comprehension sit underneath everything. A student whose report shows weakness across science and maths usually has one problem, not four.

Then separate content gaps from technique losses. A content gap shows up as blank answers and wrong methods. A technique loss shows up as right methods scoring badly: no working shown, command terms misread, final statements missing, time running out. Content gaps need teaching. Technique losses need marked practice and are much faster to fix. A parent who can tell these apart buys perhaps a third of the tutoring they first thought they needed, and the trial lesson is designed to produce exactly that distinction in writing.

One more sorting rule, which saves money in the subjects left over. Some weak grades are not weakness at all but entry at the wrong tier or in the wrong qualification, such as a student sitting English First Language who should be sitting Second Language, or a maths candidate capped by a Core entry made in Year 9. Those are conversations with the school rather than purchases from a tutoring service, and a tutor who notices one and tells you has saved you more than a term of sessions would have earned them.

sections.heading: The June and November series, counted backwards
paragraphs: UAE IGCSE candidates sit the June series and the November series. The February and March series that appears in some online revision guides is offered to India only, and a plan built around it for a Dubai student is simply wrong. If you see those months in material sold to you, treat it as a reason to question everything else in the document.

The dates that constrain a student are set well before the examination itself, and the published record shows the pattern. For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results follow in January: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. For the summer series, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Those are past dates, given so you can see the rhythm rather than so you can diary them.

For anything in the future, open the awarding body's live timetable instead of trusting a restatement, including this one. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. That single piece of administrative detail is worth more to a Dubai family than most revision advice, and almost nobody passes it on.

sections.heading: KHDA, the Hartland schools and what the IGCSE grade is used for later
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Annual inspection runs on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak and the outcome is published school by school. For a Hartland parent, the departmental commentary inside a report is more useful than the band, because a strong maths department can sit inside an averagely rated school.

Context on scale and cost: Dubai's private sector served 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, with the UK curriculum the largest single share of enrolment. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools creating 16,846 new places.

The grade itself has two later uses worth planning for. The first is post-16 entry, where schools set their own thresholds for A Level and IB Diploma courses. The second is UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, which requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among those five, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. One competitor ranking for these queries publishes a requirement of six subjects, which is wrong. Equivalency is a process the ministry performs; verify your own case through its attestation channel rather than through any tutoring service, including this one.

On credentials, plainly: IB Gram is not KHDA approved, ADEK approved or accredited by Cambridge, Pearson or Oxford AQA, and does not claim to be. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence for training institutes with premises in Dubai. Any service advertising KHDA-approved tutors is describing something else or saying something untrue, and for a parent comparing quotes that is a quick and useful filter.

sections.heading: Coursework, practicals and what a tutor must refuse to do
paragraphs: Most IGCSE subjects are assessed entirely by written paper, which removes a great deal of temptation. Some are not. Where a coursework, portfolio or spoken component exists, the rules are the same as anywhere else: the work must be the student's own, and a tutor who offers to produce it is offering malpractice with the consequence landing on the student rather than on themselves.

What a tutor does with a coursework component is explain the criteria, question a chosen focus until it is workable, teach the skills it requires, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. What a tutor does not do is choose the focus, supply the content, write or rewrite the text, or hand over an example so close to the task that copying is the obvious next step. We say this to the student directly in the first session rather than burying it in terms and conditions, because a fifteen-year-old under pressure is entitled to know where the line is in advance.

Practical science needs its own note for online students, because it is the question families ask most often. A tutor cannot run a laboratory over video and should not pretend otherwise. What a tutor can do is teach experimental method, variables and controls, uncertainty, graph work and the specific conventions the examination rewards, all of which are examinable in writing. Which model applies, an alternative-to-practical paper or practical understanding assessed within the written papers, depends on the specification, which is one more reason to get the code from the school. We also do not reproduce or distribute syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; we reference them and link to the awarding body's own page.

sections.heading: Getting started from Sobha Hartland, and what we say when a board is unfamiliar
paragraphs: Start with the specification codes rather than with the subject list. Email the school's examinations officer and ask which awarding body and which code each subject is entered for, and which tier where tiering applies. Send that with the latest grades, the teacher comments quoted rather than summarised, and the time the school day ends. From Hartland that last detail is better than in most of Dubai, since two schools sit inside the community, and it makes earlier session times possible.

We then propose a tutor and run a free trial lesson, which is a diagnosis rather than a sales call. Ask afterwards for the content-versus-technique distinction described earlier on this page, in writing. If the answer is general, do not book the block, whatever the rate. A tutor who cannot separate a content gap from a technique loss will teach content for a year to a student who needed marked practice.

And the honest part. Where a specification is unfamiliar to a tutor we tell you rather than letting them learn on your time. Cambridge and Pearson are both well covered. Oxford AQA and the less commonly entered subjects are thinner, and in those cases the options are a different tutor, a short wait, or a tutor based outside the UAE who has taught that specification and works to Gulf Standard Time. What we will not do is accept a booking for a board nobody on the team has taught and hope the differences do not matter. They matter most in the final eight weeks, which is exactly when there is no time to recover.

process.title: Get the specification codes in writing
process.description: Email the school's examinations officer for the awarding body, the code and the tier in every subject you are considering. It takes one message and it prevents the most expensive mismatch in this market, which is a competent tutor preparing a student for the wrong paper.

process.description: Quote the teacher comment rather than summarising it, and say whether each grade came from a mock or from classwork. A mock grade and a classwork grade mean different things, and the difference changes which subject we would start with.

process.description: The first session costs nothing. Afterwards ask, in writing, which of your child's problems are content gaps and which are technique losses. That single distinction usually reduces the number of subjects worth paying for from five to one or two.

process.description: We will recommend the smallest number of subjects that addresses the underlying weakness, and review after a half-term. A service whose answer to a weak report card is four weekly sessions is describing its revenue model rather than your child's problem.

process.description: Each session ends with named past-paper questions matched to the correct specification, and the next begins with them marked against the published criteria. Checking that this happens requires no subject knowledge from you, which makes it the most useful accountability available.

process.description: The plan is checked against the June or November series: mock results, entry confirmation, the final block. Intensity rises for a defined period and then the block ends, rather than continuing because stopping feels like a risk.
