faqs.question: Which IGCSE exam board does my child's school use, and how do I find out?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's examinations officer for the awarding body and the specification code in every subject, in writing. Dubai schools use Cambridge International, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE and Oxford AQA International GCSE, sometimes different bodies for different subjects within one school. The code matters because paper structures, tier names, calculator rules and practical assessment all differ. A tutor who teaches the subject but not the specification can look entirely competent while preparing your child for a paper they will never see, and the mismatch usually surfaces too late to fix.

faqs.question: Are Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSEs really that different?
faqs.answer: Different enough to change a revision programme. Tier names differ: Core and Extended against Foundation and Higher. In maths, Cambridge's current structure pairs a non-calculator paper with a calculator paper while Pearson's Specification A permits a calculator in both, so mental arithmetic drill is essential for one and close to irrelevant for the other. In the sciences, Cambridge offers an alternative-to-practical route while Pearson assesses practical understanding inside the written papers. Both are respected qualifications; neither is a substitute for knowing which one your child sits.

faqs.question: Do your tutors come to homes in Sobha Hartland?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition over live video throughout the UAE, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. We state it plainly because home tutor is the phrase parents search and the ambiguity would be easy to leave in place. If physical supervision is what your child actually needs, a local in-home arrangement is the right choice, and the market rates on this page let you judge it. For specification-matched teaching across several subjects, online delivery produces the better match.

faqs.question: What does "modular" mean with Pearson Edexcel compared with Cambridge?
faqs.answer: It refers to when assessment is taken rather than to the content. Some Pearson International GCSE qualifications allow assessment to be taken across more than one series instead of all at the end, while Cambridge IGCSE is normally sat as a complete set in a single series. Which model applies depends on the subject and on what your school has chosen, so ask the examinations officer rather than assuming. The answer changes when revision has to peak, which is the practical reason it matters to a tutoring plan rather than being a technicality.

faqs.question: How are science practicals handled if my child studies partly online?
faqs.answer: No tutor runs a laboratory over video, and one who implies otherwise is overselling. What is taught online is the examinable part: experimental method, independent and dependent variables, controls, uncertainty, graph work and the written conventions the mark scheme rewards. Whether that is assessed through an alternative-to-practical paper or inside the written papers depends on the specification, which is one more reason to get the code from the school. The hands-on work belongs to the school's own practical programme, and a tutor should be asking what that programme has covered.

faqs.question: My child's report shows five weak subjects. Do we need five tutors?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly not, and buying five is the most expensive mistake available here. Weak grades across maths and the sciences usually share one cause, which is arithmetic and algebra, and weak grades across humanities usually share writing structure. Fix the cause once and several grades move. Separate content gaps, which show as blank answers and wrong methods, from technique losses, which show as right methods scoring badly. The trial lesson exists to produce that distinction in writing so you can buy one or two subjects instead of five.

faqs.question: What does a home tutor cost in this part of Dubai for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: In-home one-to-one runs roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour in this market, travel included, with monthly packages advertised around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Online equivalents sit at about AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor and AED 200 to 450 and above for a specialist, with packages around AED 799 a month for eight sessions. Those are other providers' published figures read in October 2026 and attributed in the tables here. Scaled across four subjects, the in-home figure rarely stays proportionate.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting tutoring in Year 9 rather than waiting?
faqs.answer: For a specific weakness, yes, and it is the cheapest intervention on this page. Algebraic fluency, reading stamina and scientific vocabulary are built before Year 10, and a student who arrives without them spends two years catching up while new content keeps arriving. A short block in Year 8 or 9 on one named foundation costs a fraction of a Year 11 recovery programme. What is not worth buying in Year 9 is open-ended weekly support for a student who is coping, which is how families spend most and gain least.

faqs.question: Which tier should my child be entered for, and who decides?
faqs.answer: The school decides, usually in Year 10, from class performance, and it is right most of the time. The predictable exceptions are a student capped by a weak Year 9 who has since improved, and a student pushed up on effort rather than on algebra who cannot access the harder half of the paper. Both are visible in one marked paper. A tier review is the best possible use of a first session, because it either confirms the school's judgement or gives you evidence for a conversation with the department while a change is still possible.

faqs.question: How quickly can you match a tutor for an unusual IGCSE subject?
faqs.answer: Cambridge and Pearson maths, sciences, English, economics and business are usually days. Oxford AQA specifications and the less commonly entered subjects take longer, sometimes a week or more, and occasionally we cannot cover them at all. When that happens we say so rather than accepting the booking and letting a tutor learn the specification on your time. The alternatives are a different slot, a short wait, or a tutor based outside the UAE who has taught that specification and works to Gulf Standard Time.

faqs.question: If one of my child's IGCSE subjects has a coursework component, how much can a tutor touch it?
faqs.answer: Within limits we state to the student in the first session. A tutor may explain the criteria, question a chosen focus until it is workable, teach the skills the component requires, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not choose the focus, supply content, write or rewrite text, or hand over an example close enough to copy. The work must be the student's own; submitting anything else is malpractice and the consequence falls on the student, not on whoever helped.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit, and is it expensive for them?
faqs.answer: They need one and it costs nothing. MoHRE issues a private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and applications run through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so disregard any specific amount you see quoted.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE exams held for students in the UAE, and is there a resit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge IGCSE runs a June series and a November series; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. The February and March series seen in some online guides is offered to India only and should not appear in a Dubai plan. November functions as the resit route within the same academic year for both bodies. For actual dates, open the awarding body's live timetable: Pearson publishes provisional timetables and revises them, and Cambridge allocates centres to administrative zones and requires the correct zone version of the timetable to be used.

faqs.question: Can sessions move for Ramadan, travel or mock weeks?
faqs.answer: Yes, and online delivery is what makes it straightforward. During Ramadan sessions commonly shift to a post-Iftar slot, with no journey to renegotiate at either end. When a family travels the lesson follows the student rather than the address, and during mock weeks sessions can be paused or redirected towards whatever the mocks have just exposed. Agree the time zone the session is pinned to if you are leaving the Gulf, and give us notice so the slot is held rather than released to someone else.

faqs.question: How many sessions before we see the grade move?
faqs.answer: For a technique loss, often within a half-term, because habits such as writing working and reading command terms properly change quickly with marked practice. For a content gap, a term is realistic and two is common, since the material has to be taught and then practised. Nobody can promise a grade and anyone who does is selling something other than teaching. What is reasonable to expect is a specific written account of what is costing marks after the first lesson, and visible change in the marked practice within six weeks.

faqs.question: What should I send to get a useful recommendation for my child?
faqs.answer: Five things. The awarding body and specification code per subject, from the school. The tier, where tiering applies. The latest grades, labelled as mock or classwork. The teacher's last written comment, quoted rather than paraphrased. And the time the school day ends, which in Sobha Hartland is often earlier in practice than elsewhere because two schools sit inside the community. A photograph of one marked paper is worth more than all five, and with it we can usually propose a tutor the same day.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-sobha-hartland.closingHeading: Send the specification code first, the subject list second
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-sobha-hartland.closingBody: The search that brought you here is about distance. The thing that decides whether the hours you pay for count is whether the tutor knows the exact specification your child is entered for, across the subjects that actually carry the problem. Email the examinations officer, get the codes and tiers in writing, and send them with the latest grades and the teacher's own words. We will propose a tutor, run the first session free, and tell you in writing which weaknesses are content and which are technique before you commit to anything.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-tecom.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE subjects to students living in the TECOM and Barsha Heights towers. Slots are agreed around the actual bus return and homework load rather than offered as whatever is left in a diary, because a lesson at the wrong hour of a Dubai evening achieves very little.

intro.heading: No school inside TECOM, and what that does to an evening
paragraphs: Barsha Heights, which most people here still call TECOM, is a tower district built around media and technology offices. It has no school within its own boundary. Every IGCSE student living in these buildings therefore starts the day on a bus or in a car heading somewhere else: Al Barsha for the larger British and American schools, Al Sufouh and Knowledge Village for several long-established ones, the Marina side and Emirates Hills for others. The journeys are short in distance and unpredictable in time.

That single fact shapes everything about scheduling tutoring here. A Year 11 student does not finish school at 15:00 and sit down at 15:30. They finish, wait for a bus, cross a congested stretch of Al Barsha or Sheikh Zayed Road, arrive in a tower lobby somewhere between 15:40 and 16:30 depending on route, go up, eat something, and are then expected to produce a timed algebra paper. Families who book a 16:00 slot discover within a fortnight that it does not exist.

The second fact is homework volume. An IGCSE student in Dubai carries eight or nine subjects plus the mandatory UAE subjects, which are compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum and whose instructional time KHDA calculates on a 40-minute lesson unit. The evening already has work in it. A tutoring hour added without reference to what else is in that evening does not add an hour of learning; it displaces an hour of homework and produces a tired child and an annoyed teacher.

So this page is a timetable document before it is a tutoring pitch. It maps where the TECOM week actually has room, counts the Dubai academic year in teaching weeks rather than months, sets out which session length suits which subject, and names the weeks that quietly disappear from every plan. Then it fits the IGCSE two-year course into what is genuinely left.

There is a third fact that families discover rather than plan for: the household's own week. TECOM and Barsha Heights sit immediately south of Dubai Internet City and Dubai Media City, so a large share of parents here are not home before 18:30. That concentrates demand on the 18:30 and 19:00 slots, which are the first to go and the worst hour of the day for a tired Year 11 to attempt a non-calculator paper. Add co-curricular commitments running to 16:30 on two or three afternoons, a sibling arriving on a different route, and the mandatory Arabic homework that nobody counts, and the genuinely usable windows in a TECOM week come down to perhaps three.

One thing to be clear about first. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no affiliation to any school or examination board, and tutoring for UAE families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For a tower district where the binding constraint is the clock, that matters practically: an online slot can start eight minutes after a bus arrives, and a visiting tutor cannot.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-tecom.programmesIntro: The TECOM towers send children to schools running several different qualifications at sixteen. These are the three that matter for scheduling, because each one puts pressure on a different part of the week.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses with four-digit syllabus codes such as 0580 Mathematics, 0620 Chemistry and 0500 English First Language, most offering a Core and an Extended tier with the tier set at entry. Assessment is terminal, so the whole two years points at one window of papers rather than at continuous coursework.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE centres, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Use the version your child's school issues.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Specifications such as 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics and 4EA1 English Language A, graded 9-1, with Foundation and Higher tiers in mathematics. Several schools TECOM children attend run Pearson for some departments and Cambridge for others, which produces two different calendars inside one child's week.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs May/June and November series. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so open the live official PDF.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme, the parallel route
programmes.description: Some TECOM children attend IB continuum schools and are assessed against four criteria per subject, each out of 8, rather than sitting IGCSE papers. There is no terminal exam window, so the pressure in their week falls on task deadlines instead.
programmes.countryNote: A household with one child on IGCSE and one on the MYP has two different evening rhythms to manage. The IGCSE student needs protected blocks before mocks and papers; the MYP student needs consistent weekly slots across the term. Scheduling both as one pattern is how one of them gets short-changed.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-tecom.subjectsIntro: Different subjects want different slots in a week. These are the IGCSE subjects most requested from the TECOM towers, with a note on where each one sits best in an evening.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 · 4MA1)
subjects.description: Best early in the evening while concentration is intact, because 0580 Extended includes a non-calculator Paper 2 of two hours and that work degrades badly with fatigue. A 17:00 slot outperforms a 20:00 slot for the same tutor and the same student.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 · 4PH1)
subjects.description: Calculation-heavy and therefore similar to mathematics in its timing needs. The alternative-to-practical paper is the exception: apparatus, variables and error questions are recall work and survive a later slot perfectly well.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 · 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mixed. Moles and electrolysis calculations want an early slot; qualitative analysis tables and organic reaction sequences are memorisation and work fine later. A tutor who sequences the hour accordingly gets more from a tired Year 11.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 · 4BI1)
subjects.description: The most forgiving science for a late slot, because most of the gain is command-term discipline and diagram labelling rather than sustained calculation. Often the subject to move when an evening has to be rearranged.

subjects.name: English First Language (0500 · 0990)
subjects.description: Needs a longer session than most subjects, because feedback on a student's own writing cannot be rushed. Ninety minutes once a fortnight usually works better here than sixty minutes weekly.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 · 0511 · 0993)
subjects.description: A separate qualification from First Language English, with speaking assessed separately. Shorter frequent sessions suit it better, since the gains are in accuracy and precise retrieval rather than in extended drafting.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: One grade covering all three sciences, which means one weak discipline drags the award. Worth a diagnostic before booking, because a family often buys three sciences when the problem sits in one of them.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450) and Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Case-study subjects where the marks are in command terms and use of the data provided. They tolerate a later slot well and benefit from a longer fortnightly session built around a full case study.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Theory plus a pre-release practical task. The theory paper rewards pseudocode conventions and trace tables, which is precise work best placed early in an evening rather than at the end of one.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.description: Mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of curriculum, and occupying real timetable and homework space. Support here must follow the school's approved content, since using different or additional material without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-tecom.regionsIntro: TECOM students travel out of the district every morning. These are the places they travel to and from, with what each journey does to the available evening.

regions.name: Barsha Heights (TECOM)
regions.note: The towers themselves. Lifts at 16:00 are busy, which adds five to ten minutes between the lobby and the apartment. Families consistently underestimate this when booking a slot that starts on the half hour.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-tecom.modesIntro: Three ways to fit IGCSE support into a TECOM week. The right one is decided by the week rather than by the subject, which is the reverse of how most families choose.

modes.title: Fixed weekday slot, protected
modes.description: The same time every week, set after the bus return rather than at a round hour, and treated as unmovable by the household. Consistency is what makes a two-year IGCSE course work, and the main threat to it is not the tutor's diary but the family's own week. A slot that moves twice a month stops being a habit.
bullets: Start time set from the actual bus arrival, often 16:45 or 17:30
Same day each week for the whole term
Rescheduling limited and agreed in advance, not improvised
Delivered one-to-one over live video

modes.title: Longer fortnightly session
modes.description: Ninety minutes every two weeks rather than sixty every week. This suits English, Business Studies and Economics, where the work is a full piece of writing or a complete case study and a sixty-minute slot ends halfway through the thinking. It also costs less per month and takes fewer evenings.
bullets: Built around one complete task or paper per session
Work produced between sessions, marked in them
Fewer disrupted evenings in a crowded week
Suits subjects where drafting matters more than drill

modes.title: Protected block before mocks and papers
modes.description: Extra sessions concentrated into the weeks that matter, agreed in advance and ending on a stated date. A January mock and the final weeks before the June papers justify intensity that the rest of the year does not, and planning it as a block stops it becoming a permanent second weekly slot.
bullets: Dates agreed at the start of the term, not improvised in panic
Full timed papers sat alone between sessions
Marking against the official scheme done by the student
Ends on the stated date unless both sides agree otherwise

sections.heading: Where the TECOM week actually has room
paragraphs: Most Dubai private schools run Monday to Friday, with Friday usually a shorter day. That gives five school evenings and a Saturday-Sunday weekend, and the five evenings are not equivalent. Monday carries the week's new homework. Thursday carries whatever has been deferred. Friday is short at school and therefore long at home, which makes it the most underused slot in the TECOM week.

Layer on the commute and the picture tightens. A bus leaving an Al Barsha school at 15:10 reaches a Barsha Heights lobby between roughly 15:40 and 16:20, and lift traffic at that hour adds another five to ten minutes. Add food and a change of clothes, and the first honest start time for most students in these towers is 16:45. For children bussed from Emirates Hills or the Springs it is closer to 17:30.

The other constraint is parental. Dubai Internet City and Dubai Media City sit immediately north of TECOM, and many parents in these towers are not home before 18:30. That pushes demand hard onto the 18:30 and 19:00 slots, which are the first to fill and the last ones a tired Year 11 should be doing non-calculator algebra in. Families who can supervise an earlier session, or whose child can be trusted to start one alone, get materially better slots.

The table below maps the week as it actually runs. It is worth filling in for your own household rather than accepting ours, because the variable that matters most is your child's specific bus route, and no page can know that. What the table does provide is the reasoning: match the subject to the hour, use Friday, and protect whichever slot you choose.

sections.heading: The Dubai academic year counted in teaching weeks
paragraphs: Parents plan in months and schools operate in terms, but tutoring only happens in teaching weeks, and a Dubai academic year has fewer of them than either figure suggests. Remove the long summer break, the winter and spring breaks, Eid holidays, National Day, school exam weeks when students are sitting internal papers, and the weeks immediately before and after a family's own travel, and a two-year IGCSE course is not twenty-four months of support. It is substantially less.

This is why a plan expressed as a number of months is close to useless and a plan expressed as a number of sessions is honest. A family committing to weekly support for Year 10 and Year 11 should count the sessions they will genuinely attend, not the weeks on a calendar. The gap between the two is routinely a term's worth of teaching, and it explains why plans that looked adequate in September run out of time in April.

The practical response is to front-load. Content teaching belongs in Year 10 and the first half of Year 11, when sessions actually happen and nothing is urgent. Technique and timed-paper work belongs in the second half of Year 11, when sessions are fewer but each one is worth more. Families who do it the other way round, coasting through Year 10 and buying intensity in spring, pay more for less.

The table counts a notional year so that the arithmetic is visible. Your school's dates will differ, and the right move is to take the school calendar, mark the weeks that will not produce a session, and count what is left. It takes twenty minutes and it changes most people's plan.

sections.heading: Session length, by subject rather than by habit
paragraphs: Almost every provider in this market sells an hour, and the hour is a billing convention rather than a pedagogical choice. Some IGCSE work does not fit into sixty minutes and some does not need it, and choosing the length per subject is a free improvement a TECOM family can make.

Sixty minutes suits calculation subjects. A mathematics or physics session can cover a topic, work through examples and set practice inside an hour, and a student's capacity for sustained calculation after a school day is around that long anyway. Pushing to ninety minutes in mathematics usually produces thirty minutes of diminishing returns and a child who resents the subject.

Ninety minutes suits writing subjects. An English First Language session built around a reading response or a directed-writing task needs time to read, plan, write and receive feedback, and an hour ends in the middle of that. The same applies to Business Studies and Economics case studies. A ninety-minute session every fortnight is usually better than sixty minutes weekly for these, costs less per month, and occupies fewer evenings in a crowded week.

Forty-five minutes has a real use that is frequently ignored. For a Year 10 student who needs consistency rather than depth, or for an exhausted child in the week before mocks, a short focused session is better than a long unfocused one. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises at least 25 minutes for any such lesson, which is a reasonable reminder that teaching value is not linear with duration. The condition is that a 45-minute session must be priced as 45 minutes.
bullets: Sixty minutes for mathematics, physics and chemistry calculation work
Ninety minutes fortnightly for English, Business Studies and Economics
Forty-five minutes for consistency with a younger or exhausted student
Check whether a quoted hourly rate is actually being charged for a shorter session

sections.heading: Two children, two buses, one evening
paragraphs: A large share of enquiries from these towers involve two children at different schools on different routes, arriving home twenty-five minutes apart, needing different subjects at different levels. Families usually open the conversation hoping the two can be combined. Almost always they cannot, and the reason is worth stating because it saves a wasted term.

Two students share a session usefully only when they are at the same level in the same subject with similar gaps. Siblings in different year groups have neither. A Year 9 and a Year 11 student in a shared maths hour produces one child being taught and one being supervised, at full price for both. A Year 11 pair at the same level but with different weak topics produces the same outcome more subtly, because the session drifts towards whichever of them speaks first.

What does work in a TECOM evening is sequencing. Two separate online slots back to back, each matched to the right level, costs nothing extra in logistics because there is no travel between them and no second tutor arriving at a building. One child works at 17:00 while the other does homework, then they swap. The apartment is quiet in the right half-hours and both children get taught rather than supervised.

The scheduling constraint to raise early is co-curricular commitments. Sport, music and clubs in Dubai schools frequently run until 16:30 or later on two or three days a week, and those days are effectively unavailable for anything demanding. Map them before choosing a slot, including for the sibling, because a slot chosen around one child's week often collides with the other's.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and the weeks a plan quietly loses
paragraphs: Ramadan reshapes the Dubai school day and the household evening together. School hours shorten, students are fasting or living alongside a fasting household, sleep patterns move, and the useful part of the evening relocates to after Iftar. A tutoring plan that pretends these weeks are normal simply loses them.

The workable approach is to shorten and move rather than to pause entirely. Shorter sessions, often forty-five minutes, placed after Iftar, keep a habit alive without demanding concentration from a fasting teenager at four in the afternoon. For students in the final term before June papers, those weeks are too valuable to abandon, and the compromise of a short post-Iftar session usually holds where a full-length afternoon one does not.

Eid holidays, the winter and spring breaks, National Day and school internal assessment weeks remove further sessions, and they are the weeks families forget when they plan in months. School study leave is the subtlest: it removes school structure at exactly the point a student most needs it, and a student with no school day and no plan converts a fortnight of revision into a fortnight of nothing.

The practical step is small. Take the school calendar at the start of the year, mark every week that will not produce a session, count what remains, and plan the content against that number. Families in TECOM who do this arrive at the June papers having covered the syllabus. Families who plan in months arrive in April discovering they have four topics left and five sessions.
bullets: Shorten sessions to forty-five minutes and move them after Iftar during Ramadan
Treat school internal assessment weeks as unavailable rather than as teaching weeks
Plan study leave in advance; unstructured leave is the biggest single loss
Count the year in sessions you will actually attend, not in months

sections.heading: Mocks, and what a January paper is actually worth
paragraphs: Most schools near TECOM run internal mock examinations in the winter term of Year 11, and the result lands in a household with more weight than it deserves in one direction and less than it deserves in another. The grade itself is a weak predictor. The script is an excellent diagnosis.

The grade is weak because the paper was often sat before the syllabus was finished, under conditions that do not match the real series, marked by a department with its own standards. A grade 5 in January tells you very little about June. What the script tells you is specific and actionable: which topics were not attempted, which questions ran out of time, where method marks were lost, and whether the problem was knowledge, reading or timing.

That makes the fortnight after mocks the most valuable tutoring window in the IGCSE year. The student has a full marked script, the memory of sitting it is fresh, and there is still a term and a half to act. One session spent going through the script question by question, with the student marking against the official scheme and naming the mark type lost each time, produces a plan for the remaining months. Most families instead spend that fortnight discussing the grade.

A warning about the mock weeks themselves. Tutoring during the mock fortnight is largely wasted: the student is sitting papers, has no capacity for new content, and benefits more from sleep. Plan the mock weeks as a pause and the fortnight afterwards as a concentrated block. That is the opposite of what most schedules do, and it is a free gain.

sections.heading: Which board, which series, and the resit route
paragraphs: Two awarding bodies dominate in the schools TECOM children attend, and their calendars differ. Getting the board right is not a detail; it determines when the papers are, when results arrive, and what the retake option looks like.

Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE centres, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only and is not available to a Dubai centre, so any plan built around a spring exam window is wrong for a UAE candidate. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables well in advance, including for later series, so the only safe reference is the live official timetable PDF rather than any restated date.

The resit arithmetic is where this becomes practical. A student who underperforms in June gets results in August and can enter the November series, with results reaching them in January. That January date is tight for a family making plans for the following year, and it is the single most useful date in this section. Build the retake decision around it rather than around the exam window.

sections.heading: Who may tutor here, and what a visit would actually involve
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the MoHRE private tuition work permit, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Tutoring without that permit leaves an individual subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts has been published, so no figure can honestly be quoted. The point for a TECOM parent is that the permit is free, which means there is no cost-based reason for a working tutor to be without one. Ask the question directly; it is a fair one and a reasonable tutor expects it.

There is a second rule about who should be tutoring your child. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported and check the current policy, but the principle is sound anywhere: nobody should be selling you your own child's class teacher.

Dubai's private schools themselves are regulated by KHDA, which oversees the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. A tutoring operation with premises and staff would need a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, has no UAE office, centre or branch, and claims no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; that service runs only in India.

sections.heading: Starting from a TECOM tower, with the limits named
paragraphs: A useful first message from these towers contains the school, the bus return time, the subject with its syllabus code, and the two or three evenings that are genuinely free. With those four things we can offer a slot that survives a term. Without the bus time we offer a slot that gets cancelled in week three, which wastes everybody's month.

The first lesson is free and diagnostic, and it is scheduled at the time you intend to keep rather than at whatever is convenient once. That matters: a trial at 15:00 on a Saturday tells you nothing about whether a 17:00 Tuesday will work. The tutor reviews recent script evidence, tests a sample of the specification, and separates a content gap from a timing or reading gap. You get a written summary whether you continue or not.

The delivery position, once more and plainly: lessons to TECOM, Barsha Heights, The Greens, Dubai Internet City and the surrounding districts are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE and no tutor will arrive at a Dubai address. For a district whose binding constraint is the clock, that is an operational advantage rather than a concession: a session can start minutes after a bus arrives, and it does not lose twenty minutes to the Al Barsha interchange.

On availability, common requests such as 0580 Extended mathematics, 0620 chemistry and 0500 English are usually matched within a few days. Narrower ones, including some Computer Science combinations and minority-language specifications, take longer and occasionally cannot be covered. We say so at enquiry rather than filling the slot with a generalist. The enquiry form collects the student's year group, school, subject, specification and a parent contact; it is used only to make the match and can be deleted on request.

whyPoints.description: Start times are set from the actual bus arrival in a TECOM tower, usually 16:45 or 17:30, rather than offered on the hour. A schedule that ignores the Al Barsha return leg is a schedule that collapses within a month.

faqs.question: What is the earliest a lesson can realistically start for a child living in the TECOM towers?
faqs.answer: For most children bussed to Al Barsha or Al Sufouh, about 16:45. A bus leaving school at 15:10 reaches a Barsha Heights lobby between roughly 15:40 and 16:20 depending on the route and the day, and lift traffic at that hour adds five to ten minutes. Add food and a change of clothes and 16:45 is the first honest start. Children on longer routes from Emirates Hills or the Springs are rarely available before 17:30. Booking 16:00 looks tidy and gets cancelled by week three.

faqs.question: Which school day evening is the best one to use for IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: Tuesday, in most households, because the week's homework has settled and the student is not yet tired. Monday carries the new homework load, Wednesday collects co-curricular clashes, and Thursday carries deferred work. The genuinely underused slot is Friday: Dubai schools generally run a shorter Friday, so the evening is long and almost nobody books it. A ninety-minute English or case-study session on a Friday is one of the easiest improvements a TECOM family can make to a schedule.

faqs.question: How many teaching weeks does a Dubai IGCSE year actually contain?
faqs.answer: Fewer than the calendar suggests. Remove the summer, winter and spring breaks, Eid holidays, National Day, school internal assessment weeks, study leave and whatever family travel the household plans, and a two-year course loses roughly a term's worth of sessions against a month-based plan. The fix takes twenty minutes: take the school calendar, strike out every week that will not produce a session, count what is left, and plan the syllabus against that number rather than against twenty-four months.

faqs.question: Should a maths session be an hour or ninety minutes?
faqs.answer: An hour, in almost all cases. A student's capacity for sustained calculation after a Dubai school day is around sixty minutes, and pushing to ninety in mathematics or physics produces thirty minutes of diminishing returns and a child who resents the subject. Ninety minutes is the right length for English First Language, Business Studies and Economics, where the work is a complete piece of writing or a full case study that cannot be started and finished inside an hour. Choose the length by subject.

faqs.question: Can my two children in the same apartment share one IGCSE session?
faqs.answer: Only if they are the same year, the same subject, the same tier and have similar gaps, which is uncommon. A Year 9 and a Year 11 sharing a maths hour means one is taught and one is supervised, at full price for both. What works in a TECOM evening is two separate online slots back to back with two matched tutors. One child works while the other does homework, then they swap. Because there is no travel between sessions, sequencing costs nothing in logistics.

faqs.question: How should sessions change during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Shorten them and move them after Iftar rather than pausing entirely. School hours shorten, sleep patterns shift, and a fasting teenager at four in the afternoon has little to give a timed algebra paper. A forty-five minute post-Iftar session keeps the habit alive and is realistic. For a Year 11 student in the final term before the June papers, those weeks are too valuable to abandon, and the shortened post-Iftar arrangement is usually what holds when a full-length afternoon slot does not.

faqs.question: Is it worth tutoring during the mock examination fortnight?
faqs.answer: Generally no. During mocks the student is sitting papers, has no capacity for new content, and benefits more from sleep than from an extra hour of teaching. The valuable window is the fortnight immediately afterwards, when a full marked script exists and the memory of sitting it is fresh. One session going through that script question by question, with the student marking against the official scheme and naming the mark type lost each time, sets the plan for the rest of the year.

faqs.question: How much should I read into a January mock grade?
faqs.answer: Less than it feels and more than you think, but in different directions. The grade is a weak predictor: the paper was often sat before the syllabus was finished, under conditions unlike the real series, and marked to a department's own standard. The script is an excellent diagnosis. It shows which topics were skipped, which questions ran out of time, and where method marks were lost. Ask for the script, not just the grade, and bring it to the first tutoring conversation.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE exam series will my child in Dubai actually sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June series, with November available as a resit route, plus Checkpoint tests in March, May and October for younger year groups. The February and March Cambridge series is offered to India only and is not available to a Dubai centre, so ignore any plan built around a spring window. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Cambridge also assigns every centre to one of six administrative zones, so use the timetable version your child's school issues.

faqs.question: If June goes badly, when would retake results arrive?
faqs.answer: For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which is the pattern to plan around rather than a promise about any future series. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. That January date is the one families actually need, because it is when a retake decision converts into something a school or university can act on.

faqs.question: Do after-school clubs make certain evenings unusable?
faqs.answer: Frequently, yes, and it is the most common reason a chosen slot fails. Sport, music and club commitments in Dubai schools often run to 16:30 or later on two or three days a week, which pushes the return into a Barsha Heights lobby past 17:15 and leaves no realistic window before dinner. Map the co-curricular week for every child in the household before choosing a day, including the sibling, because a slot built around one child's timetable regularly collides with the other's.

faqs.question: Does the school send homework that a tutoring hour will displace?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly. An IGCSE student in Dubai carries eight or nine subjects plus the mandatory UAE subjects, which are compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum and whose instructional time KHDA calculates on a 40-minute lesson unit. An hour of tutoring added without reference to that load does not add an hour of learning; it displaces an hour of homework. The better plan is one protected session that improves how the homework is done rather than three that crowd it out.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our tower in Barsha Heights after school?
faqs.answer: Not from us. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Lessons for families in TECOM, Barsha Heights, The Greens and Dubai Internet City are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. In a tower district that is a scheduling advantage rather than a compromise: an online session can start eight minutes after a bus arrives, where a visiting tutor would still be crossing the Al Barsha interchange.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need a permit, and is there a fee for it?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and there is no fee. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the MoHRE private tuition work permit, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no amounts published.

faqs.question: What should I put in a first message to get a slot that lasts?
faqs.answer: Four things: the school, roughly when your child reaches the lobby, the subject with its syllabus code, and the two or three evenings that are genuinely free once clubs and a sibling's return are accounted for. With those we can offer a slot that survives a term. Without the arrival time we offer one that gets cancelled in week three. The first lesson is free and we schedule it at the hour you intend to keep, so it tests the logistics as well as the teaching.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-tecom.closingHeading: Fix the slot, then fix the subject
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-tecom.closingBody: In a district with no school inside it, the tutoring decision that matters most is the hour rather than the tutor. Work out when your child actually reaches the lobby, which evenings survive the clubs and the sibling, and how many teaching weeks the year really contains once breaks and study leave are removed. Then choose a subject, a session length that suits it, and a slot the household will defend. Send us the school, the arrival time, the syllabus code and the free evenings, and the first lesson is free, scheduled at the hour you intend to keep, delivered online over live video.

intro.heading: The honest answer to a reasonable question
paragraphs: A parent typing 'IGCSE home tutor in The Greens' is asking for two things at once, and they are not equally available. The first is proximity: somebody who can be in the room, with a pen, next to a child who works better with company. That is straightforward to buy in Dubai and there is an active market for it. The second is subject precision: somebody who knows that Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is syllabus 0580 and Pearson Edexcel's is 4MA1, that those are different papers with different formats, and which of them your child's school entered them for. That one is scarce, and in a community the size of The Greens it is scarce locally almost by definition.

This page answers both parts without pretending. It sets out what in-home tuition in Dubai actually costs, with the published figures and who published them, and what the travel inside that rate is buying. It explains how to find out which syllabus your child is sitting, in one email. It gives you a question to ask any prospective tutor, subject by subject, that separates somebody who knows the specification from somebody improvising from memory. And it states the position plainly rather than burying it: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, because home visits are a service we provide only in India. Every lesson for a UAE family is taught one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time.

That is not a limitation dressed up as a feature, and it is worth making the case properly rather than asserting it. The Greens is a mid-rise apartment community beside Emirates Golf Club, with Regent International School inside it, The Views next door and Barsha Heights minutes away. The pool of adults within a short drive who have taught Extended-tier Cambridge Physics, or marked Edexcel English Language Paper 1 against the actual mark scheme, is small. Restricting your search to that pool is the main reason families end up with a well-meaning generalist and no grade movement. Removing distance from the search widens the pool enormously and costs you nothing except the person being on a screen.

There are practical gains too, and apartment living makes them sharper. There is no parking, no building access and no lift to negotiate, which in The Greens is not a trivial consideration. A session can start at 7:15pm because that is when your child is free, rather than when a tutor has finished crossing Sheikh Zayed Road. It can move by half an hour on the day. Two children can take back-to-back slots without a gap for a journey. And the hour you pay for is an hour of teaching rather than an hour that includes somebody's drive.

What follows is the detail: the delivery comparison with real figures, the syllabus codes, the Core and Extended decision, how to verify a tutor before you let them teach, what the travel premium costs, and an eight-week plan for a Year 11 who has left it late.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-greens.programmesIntro: Four qualifications cover almost every Greens enquiry at this age, and the difference between them is not difficulty. It is which board set the papers and what that board expects a candidate to be able to do.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Subject-by-subject qualifications with numbered syllabuses: Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, English as a First Language 0500, Economics 0455 and many more. Several are tiered into Core and Extended, which changes both the papers sat and the grades available. Sciences carry a separate practical component worth twenty per cent, taken as a practical test or as a written alternative.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs June and November series, with March available for some syllabuses, and allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one, so take the timetable from your school rather than from a search result.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other board in wide use across Dubai, with its own codes: Mathematics Specification A 4MA1, Physics 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1, Biology 4BI1, English Language 4EA1. The single sciences are untiered and graded 9 to 1, and practical skills are assessed inside the written papers rather than in a separate practical examination, which changes how a candidate should revise.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE examinations in May and June and again in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Provisional timetables are published ahead of each series, so work from the live official document.

programmes.name: Cambridge O Level
programmes.description: Still offered at some schools in the region, often alongside IGCSE in particular subjects. The content overlaps substantially with the equivalent IGCSE but the assessment arrangements differ, including the treatment of practical and coursework components. A tutor needs to know which of the two a candidate is entered for, because past-paper practice is not interchangeable.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs O Level in the same June and November series as IGCSE. A Greens family whose child has moved schools mid-course should check which qualification each subject is entered for, since a transfer can leave a student entered for O Level in one subject and IGCSE in another without anybody mentioning it.

programmes.name: A Level and IB Diploma at sixteen
programmes.description: What IGCSE grades are for. Sixth forms set subject-specific expectations, and the IB Diploma requires six subjects across groups with three at Higher Level, which makes breadth matter as well as depth. A grade profile with a gap in mathematics or a science closes more doors at sixteen than families expect, which is why Year 10 is the economical time to fix one.
programmes.countryNote: Both routes exist within reach of The Greens. Dubai British School Emirates Hills, Dubai College and GEMS Wellington International School run A Levels; Emirates International School Meadows and Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills run the Diploma. Students from this community switch systems at sixteen often enough that the IGCSE profile carries real weight.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-greens.subjectsIntro: The grid below lists both boards' codes side by side, because that is the single piece of information that makes a tutoring arrangement efficient. Ask your school's exams officer for your child's codes; it is one email and it prevents a term of preparing for the wrong paper.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: The most requested subject from this community and the one where the two boards feel most different in paper style. Cambridge 0580 is tiered Core and Extended; Edexcel 4MA1 Specification A has Foundation and Higher tiers. Most marks are lost to method shown badly rather than to arithmetic.

subjects.name: IGCSE Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by students heading for A Level Mathematics or IB Higher Level, usually alongside 0580. It introduces calculus and more demanding algebra, and it is the clearest single predictor of whether a student will cope with mathematics at sixteen. Worth starting early rather than treating as an extra.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and formula rearrangement decide most grades. On Cambridge, twenty per cent sits in a separate practical component; on Edexcel, practical reasoning is examined inside the written papers. Those are genuinely different revision jobs and a tutor needs to know which applies.

subjects.name: IGCSE Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles and reacting masses are where marks disappear quietly, because the arithmetic feels easy and goes unpractised. At Extended tier and on Edexcel, organic chemistry asks students to predict rather than recall, which catches out anyone who learned reactions as a list.

subjects.name: IGCSE Biology
subjects.description: The subject where precise terminology earns or loses the most marks. Students who understand the biology perfectly and describe it loosely score below students who know less and write exactly. Extended-response questions about experimental design are the other reliable weak point.

subjects.name: IGCSE English Language
subjects.description: Reading questions reward evidence selection and writing questions reward structure, and those are separate skills. A strong reader with weak structure and a strong writer with weak reading both score in the middle, and the remedy for each is the opposite of the other.

subjects.name: IGCSE English Literature
subjects.description: Set texts differ by school, so the first thing a tutor needs is the text list. Marks go to close textual reference rather than to plot knowledge, and timed essay practice against the school's actual question format is the highest-value work available here.

subjects.name: IGCSE Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Popular choices in Dubai and both heavily dependent on command terms. Students lose marks by explaining when asked to analyse, or by giving an answer without an evaluation where the question carries evaluation marks. Both are fixable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: IGCSE Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Two different subjects that families often confuse. Computer Science is algorithms, data representation and programming logic; ICT is applied use of software with practical assessment. Confirm which one your child takes before booking, because the tutoring is not interchangeable.

subjects.name: IGCSE Arabic
subjects.description: Relevant to most Dubai families because Arabic is a mandatory school subject regardless of curriculum, and separate streams exist for Arab and non-Arab students. Which syllabus a child is entered for depends on that stream, so check it with the school before arranging support.

sections.heading: What a home tutor in The Greens actually involves, and what it costs
paragraphs: Take the question at face value first. In-home one-to-one tuition is a real and widely available service in Dubai, and the published rates for it sit between AED 180 and 500 an hour: Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate work puts it at AED 180 to 350, while independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to 500. Monthly packages observed in the market run around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visiting sessions. Those are other providers' published figures as of the October 2026 research, not our prices.

The thing to understand about that band is what sits inside it. A visiting tutor's hour includes their journey, and in this part of Dubai the journey is unpredictable rather than long. Crossing Sheikh Zayed Road at six in the evening, finding visitor parking in a Greens building, getting through access control and up a lift: none of that is dramatic, but all of it is time somebody is paying for, and it is why a short session is rarely offered and why an arrival time can only ever be approximate. Compare the two advertised monthly packages in the market and the shape of the trade becomes visible: roughly double the monthly outlay for half the number of contacts, because two-hour visits are how a travelling tutor makes the economics work.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we provide only in India. Every lesson for a family here is taught one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. That is stated plainly because the alternative, implying a service we do not sell, would waste your time and ours. sections.heading: Does anybody within reach of The Greens actually know 0580?
paragraphs: This is the part of the question that distance cannot solve, and it is worth being blunt about. The Greens is an apartment community of a few thousand homes. The number of adults living within a fifteen-minute drive who have taught Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 at Extended tier, or marked Pearson Edexcel 4PH1 against the published mark scheme, is small. It is not zero, and some of them are excellent. But a search filtered by distance returns the whole local supply of competent adults, not the small subset who know your child's specification, and it has no way of telling you which is which.

What you get instead, in practice, is a mixed field. Engineering and finance professionals who are genuinely good at mathematics. University students who sat these examinations recently and remember them. Retired teachers from other systems. Science graduates who can rebuild a topic from scratch. Every one of those can help a child who has missed two weeks of work. None of them reliably knows that a Cambridge Extended candidate sits different papers from a Core candidate, or that Edexcel assesses practical skills inside the written papers while Cambridge uses a separate component worth twenty per cent.

The table below is a filter you can apply in the first five minutes of any conversation, whoever you are talking to. Each row gives a subject, a question to ask, what an answer from somebody who knows the specification sounds like, and what a polite guess sounds like. The questions are deliberately narrow, because broad questions about teaching philosophy cannot be failed. Use them on us as well as on anybody else.

sections.heading: Find the syllabus code before you book anything
paragraphs: One email to your school's exams officer gives you the board, the syllabus code and the tier for every subject your child takes. That is the single most valuable ten minutes available to a Greens parent considering tuition, and almost nobody does it first. Without it, the opening session of any arrangement is spent establishing which examination the child is sitting, which is an hour you paid for to learn something an email would have told you.

The reason it matters is that the same subject name covers different examinations. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580 and Pearson Edexcel's Specification A is 4MA1. Cambridge Physics is 0625 and Edexcel's is 4PH1. The papers differ in format, in tiering and in how practical skills are assessed, and past-paper practice is not transferable between them. A tutor preparing a child for a separate practical paper that their board does not set has wasted the sessions, and the family usually discovers this in the spring.

Schools also mix boards across subjects more often than parents realise, particularly after a mid-course transfer. A student can be entered for Cambridge in mathematics and Edexcel in a science without anybody flagging it, because within the school each department is simply doing what it always does. Ask for the full list in one request: subject, board, syllabus code, tier where applicable, and the series your child is entered for. Keep the reply. It is the brief for every tutoring conversation you have for the next two years.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, and the decision nobody tells you is being made
paragraphs: On several Cambridge IGCSE subjects a candidate is entered either for Core or for Extended, and the two sit different papers and are eligible for different grade ranges, with Extended being the route to the top grades. The decision is taken by the school, usually in Year 11 and sometimes later than parents expect, and it is finalised at the entry deadline, which falls months before the examinations. In the UAE the live series is June, and Cambridge entries for it close in the spring, roughly four months ahead of the first paper; the exact date for a given centre is confirmed on the statement of entry the school issues rather than announced publicly. The practical effect is that a Core placement can be hardening into a final answer while the student still has most of a year of teaching left to prove otherwise.

Families in The Greens often learn about tiering only when a report mentions it. That is unfortunate, because a tier decision is reversible before entry and extremely difficult afterwards. If your child is capable of Extended and has been placed on Core because of a weak run in the autumn term, the window to change that is the term before the deadline rather than the term after it. This is one of the few situations where targeted tuition has a hard deadline attached and a clear, measurable objective.

Pearson Edexcel single sciences are untiered, so families on that board face no equivalent decision, though Edexcel Mathematics Specification A does have Foundation and Higher tiers. The practical instruction is the same either way: ask the school which tier your child is entered for, when the decision is finalised, and what evidence would support a change. Then work backwards from the entry deadline, not from the examination date.

sections.heading: Verifying a tutor before you let them teach your child
paragraphs: If you do engage somebody to teach your child, in your home or on a screen, there are things worth checking first, and most of them take a single question. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with applications through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Anyone offering private tutoring without that permit is, in the ministry's words, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, which means any page quoting a specific amount is guessing, and you should discount it. Asking a prospective tutor whether they hold the permit is an entirely normal question, and a reluctance to answer it is information in itself.

There is a further point about who may teach your child. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. That is press-reported rather than read from the policy document, so verify it before relying on the exact wording, but the principle is sound across the UAE: your child's own class teacher, privately, is not an arrangement anybody should be marketing to you. sections.heading: What the travel premium buys, and what it costs you
paragraphs: The clearest way to think about in-home tuition is to isolate the premium and ask what it purchases. Online one-to-one in the Dubai market sits in a band of roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor and AED 200 to 450 and above for an IGCSE or IB specialist, per Unitors, TutorChase and Bestimate's 2026 rate work. In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500. The overlap is real, so the premium is not uniform, but at the top of each band it is substantial.

What the premium buys is physical presence, and for some students that is worth paying for. A child who cannot stay off a phone without an adult in the room, a younger student who needs the social cue of somebody sitting beside them, a household where a screen session simply will not be respected: those are honest reasons and they are not solved by a better platform. What the premium does not buy is subject depth, because the price is set by travel and availability rather than by expertise. The pool of people willing to drive to a Greens apartment on a Tuesday evening is not the pool of people who have taught your child's specification.

What it costs you is session frequency and flexibility. Advertised Dubai packages run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visiting sessions, which is roughly twice the money for half the contacts. For IGCSE, where grades move through repeated practice against mark schemes rather than through long explanations, frequency is the variable that matters most. A shorter session twice a week usually outperforms a two-hour block once a week, and the shorter session only exists when nobody is travelling. All of these figures are other providers' published rates as of October 2026 and not an IB Gram price list.

sections.heading: Eight weeks out: what to do if your Year 11 has left it late
paragraphs: A fair number of enquiries from this community arrive eight to ten weeks before a series, and the honest answer is that eight weeks is enough to move a grade and not enough to rebuild two years. What decides the outcome is whether the time is spent on the right thing, and the right thing at eight weeks is almost never fresh content. It is identifying which marks are recoverable and drilling those.

Start by sitting one full past paper to time, unaided, in each subject of concern, and marking it against the official mark scheme rather than against a sense of how it went. That exercise typically reveals that a third of the lost marks come from questions the student could do but ran out of time for, another third from command terms misread, and the rest from genuine content gaps. Those three categories have different remedies and only the last one needs teaching. Families who skip the diagnostic spend the eight weeks revising content that was never the problem.

Then work the categories in order of return. Timing drills first, because they are the cheapest marks available. Command-term structure second, with answers rewritten against the mark scheme until the shape is automatic. Content last, and only the topics the paper actually exposed. For Cambridge science candidates, add dedicated practical-component work, because twenty per cent of the grade sits there and it is the component most often left untouched until the final fortnight.
