sections.heading: Getting started from The Greens, and what happens if nobody covers your subject
paragraphs: The enquiry that gets a useful answer fastest contains the board, the syllabus code, the tier where there is one, the last paper mark and the two evening windows that are genuinely free. With those, a tutor can tell you in a single reply whether the issue is content, timing or command terms, and quote a plan against your actual week. Without the code, the first session is an investigation rather than a lesson.

Then a free trial lesson, one per student and bookable without card details, with the tutor who would continue. For IGCSE a good trial includes a real past-paper question from your child's board, because twenty minutes of that reveals more than any conversation. Expect the tutor to name the paper and the command term rather than to talk about confidence. If the match is wrong, say so and ask for another; that costs nothing and it beats three paid sessions of politeness.

The honest caveat is about coverage. Mathematics, the sciences and English are well covered. Some subjects are thinner: Computer Science, Additional Mathematics, Arabic as a first language and the smaller humanities have fewer specialists, and the eight weeks before a series are when every good slot is already taken. If no suitable tutor is free in the window you need, you will be told, with a date, rather than matched to a generalist. Where a UAE-based tutor is not available for a niche subject, the alternative offered is a UAE-timed session with a specialist based elsewhere, delivered in the same format at the same Gulf Standard Time hour. Nobody will be sent to a Greens address, because that is not a service offered here.

process.title: Email the exams officer first
process.description: Ask the school for the board, syllabus code, tier and series for every subject your child takes, and keep the reply. It is the brief for every tutoring conversation for the next two years, and it prevents the single most common waste in this market: preparing a candidate for a paper their board does not set.

process.title: Send the codes and two free evenings
process.description: Tell us the codes, the most recent paper marks and the two weekday windows that genuinely survive activities and the commute. Availability is the real constraint on matching a specialist, so naming two actual windows places your child considerably faster than saying 'after school'.

process.title: Sit one full paper before the first lesson
process.description: A complete past paper, to time and unaided, marked against the official mark scheme. It sorts lost marks into timing, command terms and content gaps, which are three different problems with three different remedies. Most families find the content gap is the smallest of the three.

process.title: A trial with a real paper question in it
process.description: One free trial per student, no card details needed, with the tutor who would continue, using a question from your child's own board. Expect them to name the paper and the command term. A trial that stays general has told you something useful about how specific the teaching will be.

process.title: Work backwards from the entry deadline
process.description: Entries close months before the examinations and the tier decision is fixed at that point, so the plan is built from the deadline rather than from the exam date. For a Cambridge candidate that also means confirming the correct zone timetable through the school's exams officer rather than from a generic copy.

whyPoints.title: The delivery format stated plainly
whyPoints.description: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. Everything here is taught one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. Saying so on the page rather than after an enquiry saves everybody a conversation, and two competitors in this search route UAE parents to overseas numbers without mentioning it.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus code
whyPoints.description: A tutor is matched to Cambridge 0580 or Edexcel 4MA1 specifically, not to 'IGCSE Maths'. Those are different papers with different formats and the past-paper practice is not interchangeable, which is the single most common reason a well-meaning local arrangement produces no grade movement.

whyPoints.title: In-home rates published, not hidden
whyPoints.description: The visiting rates quoted on this page, AED 180 to 500 an hour, come from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai work and from independent home tutors' own advertising, with the October 2026 research date. Three of the six strongest pages in this search publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars.

whyPoints.title: Verification questions you can use anywhere
whyPoints.description: The permit to ask about, the code to ask for, the paper question to request in a trial: all of it works on any provider, including this one. A page that hands you a filter it might fail is more use than one that explains why it cannot be compared.

whyPoints.title: Sessions that fit an apartment evening
whyPoints.description: No parking, no building access, no lift, and no approximate arrival time. A session starts when your child sits down, can shift by half an hour on the day, and can be sixty minutes rather than two hours because nobody has to justify a journey to The Greens.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed
whyPoints.description: Computer Science, Additional Mathematics, first-language Arabic and the smaller humanities have fewer specialists, and the eight weeks before a series are the most contested. When nobody suitable is free you are told with a date. No competitor page examined in this research discloses a coverage limit at all.

faqs.question: Are home tutors available in The Greens for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: In-home tuition is a real and widely advertised service in Dubai, with published rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour and the travel inside that figure. IB Gram does not provide it: we do not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, because home visits are a service we run only in India. Everything we teach UAE families is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. The reason is subject depth rather than cost, since the pool of people who will drive to a Greens apartment is not the pool who know your child's syllabus.

faqs.question: Is a tutor on a screen really as useful as one in the apartment?
faqs.answer: For most IGCSE work, yes, and for some of it more so. Grades at this level move through repeated practice against mark schemes, and a shared screen lets a past paper, the mark scheme and the student's own answer sit side by side while a tutor marks it live. Where physical presence genuinely wins is attention management: a student who cannot stay off a phone without an adult beside them has a different problem, and it is worth naming honestly rather than solving with a platform. Everything else, including practical-paper technique, teaches well remotely.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE syllabus code my child is sitting?
faqs.answer: Email your school's exams officer and ask for the board, the syllabus code, the tier where one applies, and the series for every subject your child takes. Schools mix boards across departments more often than parents expect, especially after a transfer, so ask for the full list rather than assuming. Cambridge Mathematics is 0580 and Pearson Edexcel Specification A is 4MA1; Cambridge Physics is 0625 and Edexcel is 4PH1. Keep the reply, because it is the brief for every tutoring conversation you will have for the next two years.

faqs.question: The school has put my child on Core. Is that decision still open?
faqs.answer: Potentially, but only before the entry deadline, which falls months ahead of the examinations. For a UAE candidate the series that matters is June — the February and March series is offered to India only — and Cambridge entries for June close in the spring, well before the final term of teaching, with the exact date given on the centre's statement of entry rather than in any public announcement. So the window to change a placement is the term before that date rather than after it. Ask the school which tier your child is entered for, when the decision is finalised and what evidence of attainment would support a change. Once entries close it is not practically reversible for that series, and the realistic remedy becomes the November series as a resit, which is a different conversation and a different cost. That is what makes this a deadline worth diarising.

faqs.question: What does a home visit add to the hourly rate in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The travel sits inside the rate, which is why visiting tuition is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 450 for online one-to-one depending on specialism. The clearer comparison is monthly: advertised Dubai packages run around AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visiting sessions. That is roughly double the outlay for half the contacts, because long visits are how a travelling tutor makes the journey viable. All figures are other providers' published rates as of October 2026.

faqs.question: Which schools do children living in The Greens attend?
faqs.answer: Regent International School sits inside the community itself and runs the British curriculum, so a large share of local primary and lower-secondary children never leave the neighbourhood for the school run. Secondary students more often travel to the Al Barsha and Barsha Heights cluster, which includes GEMS Dubai American Academy, Nord Anglia International School Dubai and Kings' School Al Barsha, or across Sheikh Zayed Road to the Emirates Living schools. Schools are named here as context only; confirm current provision with the school and the published record with KHDA.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit to teach in someone's home?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued by MoHRE and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: How can I check a tutor is permitted before the first paid session?
faqs.answer: Ask directly, before money changes hands. A permitted tutor will name the permit and the eligibility category they applied under without hesitating, because it is an ordinary government process with a two-working-day turnaround and no fee. Also ask where they currently teach, since permit conduct rules and school ethics policies restrict a teacher from taking paid private work with students from their own school. Reluctance to answer either question is itself informative. None of this is an aggressive line of enquiry; it is the same diligence you would apply to anyone working with your child.

faqs.question: My child has eight weeks until the exams. Is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: Eight weeks is enough to move a grade and not enough to rebuild two years, and the difference lies in what the time is spent on. Begin with one full past paper per subject, to time and unaided, marked against the official mark scheme. That usually shows a third of lost marks came from running out of time, a third from misread command terms and the rest from genuine content gaps. Only the last category needs teaching. Working them in that order, timing first, is what makes eight weeks productive rather than frantic.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Maths and Physics IGCSE for the same child?
faqs.answer: Often yes, because the two overlap heavily in formula handling, rearrangement and graph work, and a mathematically strong tutor can carry both at Core and lower Extended level. At the top of Extended, or where a student is chasing the highest grade in one of them, a subject specialist is the better use of the hour. The arrangement many Greens families settle on is one tutor maintaining the stronger subject and a specialist for the one costing grades, booked as sequential slots on the same evening since nothing has to travel between them.

faqs.question: Where should a child revise in a two-bedroom apartment?
faqs.answer: Somewhere with a door, a table and no television, which in a two-bedroom apartment usually means negotiating rather than choosing. A bedroom desk works if the bed is out of sight; a dining table works if the room is declared quiet for a fixed hour. What rarely works is a sofa with a laptop. For an online session the practical requirements are small, headphones, a charged device and a surface for paper, and the headphones matter more than people expect in a flat where somebody else is cooking or watching something fifteen feet away.

faqs.question: How quickly can an IGCSE tutor be matched for a family in The Greens?
faqs.answer: For Mathematics, the sciences and English, usually within a few days outside peak season, because those specialisms are the best covered. For Computer Science, Additional Mathematics, first-language Arabic or a smaller humanities subject it takes longer, and in the eight weeks before a series every good evening slot is already committed. You will be given a date rather than a reassurance. The fastest route is to send the syllabus codes and two genuinely free evening windows in the first message, because availability rather than willingness is what sets the timeline.

faqs.question: My child takes Maths with Cambridge and a science with Edexcel. Does that cause problems?
faqs.answer: It is more common than families realise and it causes no problem as long as everybody knows. Schools mix boards by department, so a single candidate can sit Cambridge in one subject and Pearson Edexcel in another, with different paper formats, different grading scales and different practical arrangements. The risk is a tutor assuming one board across both subjects and using the wrong past papers. Send the full list of codes rather than the subject names, and each tutor works from the correct specification from the first session.

faqs.question: Does my child need five IGCSE subjects for a UAE-recognised certificate?
faqs.answer: On the British track the Ministry of Education requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. At least one page ranking for UAE tutoring searches states six subjects, which is wrong. Equivalency is a Ministry process that no tutoring provider performs or expedites, so verify the current rule through the Ministry's own channels before dropping any subject.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-greens.closingBody: The useful next step costs nothing and takes ten minutes. Email the school for your child's boards, syllabus codes, tiers and entry deadline, and keep the reply. Then ask any prospective tutor, including us, one narrow question about that specific syllabus, and listen to whether they answer it or talk around it. Those two steps will tell you more than any amount of browsing, and they work equally well on a visiting tutor, a centre or a platform. When you have the codes and two evenings that are genuinely free, a free trial lesson with the tutor who would teach the course is the sensible way to test the rest.

Send the code from the entry sheet and the match becomes a two-minute job instead of a guess.

intro.heading: The board and tier question comes before the tutor question
paragraphs: Most Lakes families searching for IGCSE help start with a subject and a worry. The more useful starting point is a piece of paper: the examination entry sheet or the school's subject confirmation, which carries the board and the syllabus code. Cambridge Mathematics is 0580 and splits into Core papers graded C to G and Extended papers graded A* to E. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A is 4MA1 and splits into Foundation, which caps at grade 5, and Higher, which runs 9 to 4 with an allowed 3. Those are four different jobs, not one.

The same fork runs through every subject. Cambridge Physics is 0625 and offers a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper depending on what the centre enters. Pearson Physics is 4PH1 with practical skills assessed inside the written papers. Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences is 0654, a double award covering three sciences in two grades, and a student sitting it is doing something quite different from a student taking 0610, 0620 and 0625 separately. A tutor who has not asked which of these applies is about to teach the wrong content confidently.

What that has to do with The Lakes is supply. The schools Emirates Living children attend do not all use the same board, and several split boards by department - Edexcel for mathematics, Cambridge for sciences, in the same Year 11. Inside a twenty-minute drive of Hattan or Maeen the chance of finding an available tutor who teaches your exact code, at your exact tier, in all the subjects you need, is low. That is the practical reason this page argues for online delivery rather than a geographic search.

Say the position plainly, since the search phrase invites the opposite reading. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE - home visits are a service offered only in India, and nobody arrives at a Lakes address under any arrangement sold here. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the paper open on a shared screen and marked while you watch. The in-home market exists and is priced at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour; this page prints those figures rather than hiding them.

You can check the prices yourself, and that is the point of printing them. Three of the Dubai tutoring pages researched for this project publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars rather than dirhams. The figures used here are read from the providers' own pages and from a 2026 Dubai rate study, in October 2026, and attributed line by line in the table below. Open any of those pages and compare. A rate you can verify is worth more than a rate you are asked to accept.

Pearson 4MA1: Foundation caps at grade 5, Higher runs 9 to 4 with an allowed 3
Cambridge 0625 Physics offers a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper
Cambridge runs June and November series; Pearson runs May/June and November
MoE equivalency for the British route asks for five subjects at no less than E or 3
Arabic and Islamic Education are excluded from that five-subject count

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-lakes.programmesIntro: A Lakes teenager on the British route meets three examination systems between 14 and 18, and the IB sits alongside them as the alternative. Here is what each is, and what it demands of a tutoring plan.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses with syllabus codes on every paper - 0580 Mathematics, 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics, 0500 First Language English. Most syllabuses are tiered into Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C and Extended reaching A*. Examinations run in a June series and a November series, and centres are allocated to one of six administrative zones with timetables that differ by zone.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge is the most common board in the schools Lakes children attend, and the zone rule matters practically: Cambridge states that the correct version of the timetable for your centre's zone must be used and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask the examinations officer which zone your school sits in before building a revision calendar.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other major international route, coded 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology, 4EA1 English Language A. Grading runs 9 to 1. Mathematics A is tiered Foundation and Higher; the sciences assess practical skills inside the written papers rather than through a separate practical examination. Series run in May/June and November each year.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so a revision plan should link the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

programmes.name: A Level and AS Level
programmes.description: The two-year route most Lakes students take after IGCSE, with three or four subjects studied in depth. Pearson's modular structure allows assessment in stages while Cambridge and others are largely linear, and that difference changes how a Year 12 tutoring plan is built. Grades run A* to E.
programmes.countryNote: The Ministry of Education equivalency route for British-curriculum students asks for one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, alongside the five IGCSE or GCSE subjects. That is the rule that makes IGCSE grades a regulatory matter and not only a school one.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The alternative at 16 for students at the IB schools near Emirates Living. Six subjects at Higher and Standard Level plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, examined in the May session for UAE schools. The step up from IGCSE is in breadth and in independent coursework rather than in content difficulty alone.
programmes.countryNote: A Lakes student holding Extended IGCSE grades in mathematics and two sciences has the usual prerequisites for Higher Level sciences in the Diploma. A student who sat Core papers generally does not, and discovering that in Year 11 rather than Year 10 is the most expensive sequencing mistake available on this route.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-lakes.subjectsIntro: Syllabus codes first, because the code decides the papers. These are the IGCSE subjects Lakes families ask about most, with both boards' codes and the component where marks are usually lost.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Cambridge Core sits on papers graded C to G and Extended on papers graded A* to E; Pearson Foundation caps at 5 while Higher runs 9 to 4. Marks are lost in the multi-step problems at the end of each paper, in surds and algebraic fractions, and in failing to show working that would have earned method marks.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Cambridge centres enter either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical written paper, so ask which. Pearson assesses practical skills inside the theory papers. Electricity circuits and the moments and momentum topics carry most of the lost marks, usually through unit errors and unstated assumptions rather than missing content.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Qualitative analysis, mole calculations and organic reaction conditions are the three reliable mark-losers. Students who can recite the reactivity series still lose marks writing ionic equations and stating observations precisely. Practice has to be written and marked, not read.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the problem rather than difficulty. Command terms do the real work: describe, explain and compare each demand a different answer shape, and a well-informed student can lose half a question's marks by answering the wrong one. Fast marks sit in data interpretation and in graph work.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences
subjects.description: A single course covering biology, chemistry and physics, reported as two grades for the double award. Students sitting it are often tutored from separate-science material by mistake, which adds content they will never be examined on. Confirm the code before the first lesson; this is the most common misdiagnosis in Dubai IGCSE tutoring.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0500 First Language · Cambridge 0510 ESL · Pearson 4EA1
subjects.description: Directed writing and the reading comprehension question carry the marks and both are technique-led. Students lose marks for retelling a passage where the question asked for analysis of how the writer achieves an effect. Six to eight marked pieces of writing move this grade more reliably than any amount of reading.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Quotation accuracy and a sustained argument are the two differentiators, and the unseen poetry component is where unprepared students lose most. Timed essay practice marked against the published criteria is the only format that works; discussion of texts alone does not transfer to a paper.

subjects.name: Business and Economics
subjects.description: Case-study application rather than definition recall. The high-tariff evaluation questions ask for a judgement supported by the stimulus material, and students who write everything they know score in the middle band. Diagram accuracy in economics is worth more than most students believe.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Pseudocode and trace tables in computer science, and practical application skills in ICT, assessed in ways that reward precision. Students who can code in a real language still lose marks on the board's own pseudocode conventions, which are a notation to be learned rather than a programming skill.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Source evaluation in history and case-study specificity in geography. Both subjects reward named examples with figures attached and punish generic answers, so the tutoring work is usually about building a small, well-rehearsed bank of examples rather than covering more content.

sections.heading: Which board and tier your child is actually entered for
paragraphs: Answer this before anything else. The board and the syllabus code sit on the examination entry sheet, and the tier sits next to them. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 runs Core papers graded C to G and Extended papers graded A* to E, so a student on Core cannot reach an A no matter how well they are taught. Pearson Mathematics A 4MA1 runs a Foundation tier capped at grade 5 and a Higher tier from 9 down to 4 with an allowed 3. Four distinct ceilings, and the ceiling decides what tutoring can do.

The sciences fork too. Cambridge 0625 Physics centres enter either the practical test or the alternative-to-practical written paper, and the preparation for those is not the same. Pearson 4PH1 assesses practical skills inside the written papers instead. A student on Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 is sitting a double award across three sciences and should not be tutored from separate-science 0610, 0620 and 0625 material, which is the single most common misdiagnosis in Dubai IGCSE tutoring.

A Lakes complication worth naming: schools in the Al Barsha corridor frequently split boards by department. Edexcel for mathematics and Cambridge for the sciences in the same Year 11 is a normal arrangement, which means a family can need two boards' worth of tutoring expertise in one household. That is manageable with two tutors matched by code. It is not manageable by hiring one person who lives nearby and teaches generally.

The table sets out the main codes side by side so the entry sheet can be read against it. sections.heading: Nine subjects, one evening: choosing which two to fund
paragraphs: A Year 11 student at a British-curriculum school in the Al Barsha corridor is typically sitting eight to ten IGCSEs. A Lakes household has perhaps three usable hours a week in the evening after the bus, dinner and homework, and funding all nine subjects is neither affordable nor physically possible. So the real question is which two subjects deserve the hours, and it has a method rather than an answer.

Start with the ceiling. A subject where the student is entered on Core or Foundation has a capped grade, so tutoring there buys a secure pass rather than a top grade. If the capped subject is a required one - mathematics or English for a sixth-form entry condition - securing it is the priority. If it is not, the hours are better spent on an Extended or Higher subject where the ceiling is open and the student is two or three grades below their profile.

Then look at the dependency. Mathematics and English carry forward into almost every sixth-form and university condition, and a weak mathematics grade closes A Level and Higher Level science routes that a weak geography grade does not. For a student intending the IB Diploma afterwards, Extended mathematics and two Extended sciences are the ones that determine what Higher Level choices exist. Fund the subjects that keep doors open before the subjects where the student is merely unhappy.

Finally, look at the distance. A subject three grades below profile is usually a technique problem with a fast fix: command terms, answer structure, showing working. A subject six grades below is a content problem that needs two terms. In a household with three hours, two fast fixes beat one slow one, and the slow one usually needs a conversation with the school about tier rather than a tutor. Ask which it is before you buy anything.

sections.heading: The entry deadline sits months before the exam
paragraphs: Nobody in this market writes about examination administration, and it causes more avoidable damage than weak teaching does. Entries close long before papers are sat, forecast grades are submitted on a separate date, results arrive in stages to centres and then to students, and every one of those dates is set by the board rather than by the school. A family that learns this in February of Year 11 has already lost options.

For a UAE candidate the series are June and November — Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only — and the counting-backwards shape is the same in both. Entries for June close in the spring, roughly four months ahead of the first paper, and the date is confirmed on the centre's statement of entry rather than publicly announced. Forecast grades are submitted on their own, earlier deadline. Results reach centres in August and students immediately after, with certificates following later still. The gap at either end is the whole point: a final entry deadline months before the first paper, and a results date months after the last one.

Pearson's calendar behaves the same way with different dates. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables in advance of each series, including for future November sittings, which is why a revision plan should link the live official timetable rather than copy dates that can be revised.

Two Cambridge mechanics deserve their own sentence. Centres are each allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states plainly that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. For the IB, no session or results date appears anywhere on this page: ibo.org is the source and your school's IB coordinator is the person to confirm with.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks are actually lost, subject by subject
paragraphs: Lost marks are specific and diagnosable, and the diagnosis is usually not what the student thinks. In mathematics the losses cluster in the final multi-step questions on each paper, in surds and algebraic fractions, and in unshown working that forfeits method marks a correct-but-unexplained answer would have earned. None of those are content gaps. All three respond to six weeks of marked written practice.

In the sciences the pattern is about precision rather than knowledge. Chemistry students lose marks writing ionic equations and stating observations loosely - a colour change described as 'it went darker' earns nothing where 'colourless to pale blue' earns the mark. Physics students lose marks on units and on unstated assumptions. Biology students lose them by answering the wrong command term: describe, explain and compare each demand a different answer shape and a well-informed student can halve a question's marks by choosing wrongly.

In the essay subjects the loss is structural. English Language candidates retell a passage where the question asked how the writer achieves an effect. English Literature candidates write about what happens rather than about how it is written, and the unseen poetry component punishes that hardest. Business and Economics candidates write everything they know on a high-tariff evaluation question and score in the middle band because no judgement was reached.

The reason this matters to a tutoring budget is that technique losses are cheap to fix and content losses are not. A student losing marks on command terms can be taught the five that matter in two sessions and then drilled for four weeks. A student missing two terms of chemistry content needs two terms. Ask any tutor to look at a marked mock paper and say which of the two they are looking at. A tutor who answers from the paper rather than from the subject is worth the rate.

Chemistry: ionic equations, mole calculations, imprecise observations

sections.heading: Practical and applied skills when the tutor is on a screen
paragraphs: The honest answer first: an online tutor cannot supervise a titration. What an online tutor can do is prepare every mark that the practical assessment actually awards, which for most Lakes students is the larger part of the problem. The school runs the laboratory work; the examination tests whether the student can plan an investigation, record data properly, process it, evaluate method and identify sources of error. Those are written skills and they are taught well over a shared screen.

What this looks like in practice depends on the code. A Cambridge centre entering the alternative-to-practical written paper is asking students to answer about experiments on paper, and that paper is almost entirely teachable remotely: reading a measuring instrument from a diagram, spotting an uncontrolled variable, suggesting an improvement in method. A centre entering the practical test needs the school's own laboratory sessions for the manipulation marks, with the recording, processing and evaluation marks prepared in tutoring.

Pearson's model folds practical skills into the theory papers, which removes the question entirely: there is no separate practical examination to supervise, and the skills appear as written questions about method and data. For either board the most valuable remote work is the same - taking a set of real results, processing them with the right number of significant figures, plotting them, drawing the line that the data supports rather than the one the student expected, and writing an evaluation that names a specific error rather than 'human error'.

One boundary to state. Past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables belong to the boards, and we reference and link them rather than reproducing or supplying them. A provider offering to send you a pack of mark schemes is distributing someone else's copyright material, and for unreleased papers it is a malpractice exposure for the student as well. Official past material is available through your school's examinations officer and the boards' own sites.

sections.heading: Five subjects at grade E or 3: what the Ministry actually requires
paragraphs: This is the regulatory fact that turns IGCSE grades from a school matter into a documentation matter, and almost nobody in this market writes about it. For the British track, equivalency requires proof of passes in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade.

Two details carry real weight. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count, which means a student with exactly five passes including Arabic does not yet meet the requirement. And at least one tutoring page ranking in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced rule is five. Publishing the correct count is a small thing that beats a ranking page on accuracy, and a parent planning a subject load should plan from the right number.

The American track works differently and is included here because Lakes families move between systems. English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB there is no points threshold published in the source consulted, so no IB equivalency figure appears on this page; verify any such number on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority directly.

Finally, what this process is not. Equivalency and attestation are performed by the Ministry and the relevant authority, not by a tutoring provider, and no tutoring is required for it. Nothing about hiring a tutor speeds up, guarantees or affects an equivalency decision, and any provider implying otherwise is making a false-urgency claim about a regulatory process. Describe it, check it at the source, and use the official channel.

sections.heading: The Lakes timetable through mock season and study leave
paragraphs: Mock season is where a Year 11 tutoring plan either earns its money or exposes itself. The mocks are the last honest diagnostic before entries harden and forecast grades are submitted, so the sessions immediately after them are the most valuable of the year. What matters is not the grade but the paper: which questions were left blank, where method marks were forfeited, which command terms were misread. That analysis takes a full session and it should be booked before the mocks, not after.

Timing in a Lakes household during mock fortnight is different from the rest of the year. Students are often released early on examination days, which opens slots that do not normally exist - a 14:00 session on a day with a morning paper is both possible and useful. Equally, the evening of a paper is the worst possible slot, because the student is spent. Plan the fortnight in advance against the school's mock timetable rather than defending the usual weekly hour through it.

Study leave is the other block worth planning deliberately. Those weeks contain more usable study hours than the whole of the preceding term, and they are almost always wasted on re-reading notes. The useful structure is a timed paper every other day, marked, with the gaps it exposes worked on in between - which is exactly what a ninety-minute session plus a marking conversation provides. Two sessions a week through study leave is usually the right volume; more produces fatigue rather than marks.

If Ramadan falls near the mocks or the examination series in a given year, front-load the timed work into the weeks before it and use the month itself for shorter, lighter, more frequent sessions. School days shorten, so an early-afternoon slot becomes available for a fasting student, and a post-iftar slot works for older students who have eaten. Agree the shift before the month starts rather than improvising in its first week.

sections.heading: Getting started from The Lakes, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Send four things: the school, the year, the syllabus codes with their tiers, and a photograph of one marked piece of work. That last item does more than the other three combined, because it shows whether the problem is technique or content. We come back with a tutor who teaches that code at that tier, a proposed focus for the first three lessons, and a rate. The trial lesson is free, covers one subject, and takes no card details.

The limit is availability for narrow combinations. Mainstream IGCSE subjects match within a few days. A specific code at a specific tier in a less common subject - 0452 Accounting, a second-language option, a combined-science double award with a particular paper entry - can take longer, and the tutor may be based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time. We state which, and from where, before anything is agreed. No competitor page researched in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

What we will not claim is as important as what we will. No grade promise, no improvement figure, no statistic about past students, because none of those can be evidenced here. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry, IB, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation or partnership, and no tutor is described as an examiner unless their current status can be shown. The regulators are named on this page to explain what each one governs.

On the legal side, one thing a Lakes parent should ask any provider. Private tuition in the UAE runs on the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, granted free of charge for two years, with a stated two-working-day processing time and a wide list of eligible categories. Tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts has been published, so disregard any figure you see quoted.

A commonly repeated six-subject figure in this market is wrong, and planning a subject load from it costs money.

faqs.question: Which exam board will my child in The Lakes actually be entered for?
faqs.answer: Only the school can tell you, and the answer is often split by department. Schools in the Al Barsha corridor that Lakes children attend commonly enter Pearson Edexcel for mathematics and Cambridge for the sciences in the same Year 11. The authoritative document is the examination entry sheet, which carries the board and the syllabus code - 0580 or 4MA1 for maths, 0620 or 4CH1 for chemistry - along with the tier. Ask the examinations officer rather than relying on the school's curriculum page, which usually names one board for the whole school.

faqs.question: Will an IGCSE tutor come to a villa in The Lakes, or is this all online?
faqs.answer: All online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The in-home market does exist in Dubai and is published at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, against AED 150 to AED 300 for an equivalently qualified tutor working online. The practical argument for video in an IGCSE context is supply: a tutor who teaches your exact code at your exact tier is rarely the one living within twenty minutes of Hattan.

faqs.question: Should a Year 10 student in The Lakes be entered for Core or Extended?
faqs.answer: That is a conversation with the school and it has a hard financial consequence. Cambridge Core papers are graded C to G and Extended A* to E, so a Core entry caps the grade below the level most sixth-form science routes require. Pearson Foundation caps at grade 5 while Higher runs 9 to 4. The decision is effectively locked at the board's final entry deadline, which falls months before the papers. If the tier is wrong, the fix is a school conversation before that deadline, not more tutoring afterwards.

faqs.question: We are sitting nine IGCSEs. Which two deserve a tutor?
faqs.answer: Work through three filters. First the ceiling: a capped tier in a required subject such as mathematics or English is the first priority, because securing the pass protects every later option. Second the dependency: mathematics and the Extended sciences determine which A Level and Higher Level routes stay open, so they outrank a subject the student merely dislikes. Third the distance: a subject two or three grades below profile is usually a technique problem with a six-week fix, while a six-grade gap needs a tier conversation with the school rather than a tutor.

faqs.question: How far ahead of the exam does the entry deadline close?
faqs.answer: Months, at both ends. For a UAE candidate the live series is June with November as the resit route, and entries for June close in the spring — roughly four months before the first paper, with the exact date on the centre's statement of entry rather than in a public announcement. Forecast grades are submitted separately and earlier than most parents expect, so the school's prediction is fixed well before revision peaks. Pearson works the same way with its own dates: the November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and entries for it closed long before the autumn term was underway. Pearson publishes provisional timetables in advance, so plan against the live official timetable page rather than a restated date, and treat the entry deadline as the one that decides what grade is reachable.

faqs.question: Why does Cambridge give our centre a zone-specific timetable?
faqs.answer: Because examinations are sat across many time zones and Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones to manage that. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. The practical instruction for a Lakes family is to ask the examinations officer which zone the school sits in, then build the revision calendar from that zone's timetable and nothing else.

faqs.question: How do we prepare for a practical-skills paper from a villa in The Lakes?
faqs.answer: By preparing the marks the paper actually awards, which are mostly written. Planning an investigation, controlling variables, recording data to the right precision, processing it, plotting it and evaluating method are all taught well over a shared screen. A Cambridge centre entering the alternative-to-practical written paper can be prepared almost entirely remotely. A centre entering the practical test needs the school's laboratory sessions for the manipulation marks, with everything else done in tutoring. Pearson folds practical skills into the theory papers, which removes the question.

faqs.question: A tutoring site told us six IGCSEs are needed for equivalency. What does the rule actually say?
faqs.answer: Five. The reported Ministry requirement for the British track is proof of passes in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. At least one tutoring page ranking in this market publishes six, which is wrong and which would change how a family plans a subject load. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae before relying on either figure.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education count towards the Ministry's five-subject requirement?
faqs.answer: No. The reporting of the Ministry's clarification states that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. The practical consequence for a Lakes family is arithmetic: a student holding exactly five passes where one of them is Arabic does not yet meet the requirement and needs another accredited subject. Both subjects remain mandatory on the school timetable in Dubai regardless, under KHDA's requirements for all private schools, so this is a counting rule rather than a reason to drop them.

faqs.question: Cambridge runs a November series and Pearson runs one too. Are they the same thing?
faqs.answer: Same month, different administration. Cambridge runs its International GCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and allocates centres to one of six administrative zones. Pearson Edexcel runs May/June and November series; its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. The dates, the entry deadlines and the results releases differ, so a household sitting both boards in November is managing two calendars rather than one.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE results actually reach students, and how long is the wait?
faqs.answer: Roughly two to three months after the last paper, in two stages. For Pearson, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge follows the same rhythm on the series UAE candidates actually sit: June results land in August and November results in the following January, with certificates arriving later again. Schools frequently see results a day before students do. Review and remark windows open from the student release date, which is why knowing the exact date for your series matters practically.

faqs.question: Our school uses Edexcel for maths and Cambridge for sciences. Does that complicate tutoring?
faqs.answer: It complicates finding one tutor, which is the main practical argument for matching by code rather than by proximity. The papers are built differently: Pearson 4MA1 is tiered Foundation and Higher with its own paper structure, while Cambridge 0620 and 0625 offer Core and Extended papers plus a choice between a practical test and an alternative-to-practical paper. Two tutors matched to two codes works cleanly. One tutor covering both boards generally means one subject taught well and one taught from the wrong specification.

faqs.question: During mock season, what time can a Year 11 student in The Lakes start a lesson?
faqs.answer: Earlier than usual, and the opportunity is worth taking. Students are often released after a morning paper, which opens a 14:00 or 15:00 slot that does not exist in a normal week - and a Lakes household whose child is normally bussed back from Al Barsha at 16:20 should use it. Avoid the evening of a paper entirely; the student is spent and nothing sticks. Plan the whole fortnight against the school's mock timetable in advance, including the post-mock analysis session, rather than defending the usual weekly hour through it.

faqs.question: Eight weeks from the series with two weak subjects, what is worth doing?
faqs.answer: Triage, then technique. Eight weeks is enough to fix answer structure, command terms, working-out discipline and timing, and it is not enough to learn two terms of missing content in two subjects. So pick the subject where the gap is technique and drill it with timed papers marked immediately; in the other, secure the topics that appear on every paper rather than attempting the whole specification. Two timed sessions a week with marking conversations is the right volume. More produces fatigue, and fatigue costs marks in the series itself.

faqs.question: Do we keep paying for lessons during study leave?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and this is the period where the hours are worth most. Study leave contains more usable study time than the preceding term and is almost always spent re-reading notes, which does not transfer to a paper. A better structure is one timed paper every other day, marked, with the gaps it exposes worked on in between - two ninety-minute sessions a week plus marking conversations fits that. Beyond two, fatigue sets in. If the household needs to cut cost somewhere, cut Year 10 rather than study leave.

That tells us whether the loss is technique or content and lets us match a tutor to the exact code rather than to a subject label. The trial lesson is free, covers one subject, and takes no card details. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so nobody arrives at a Lakes address; home visits are a service we offer only in India. If the real answer is a tier conversation with the school, we will say so.

intro.heading: What a Meadows parent is really asking when they search for a home tutor
paragraphs: The phrase typed into Google is "IGCSE home tutor in The Meadows". The question underneath it is almost never about geography. It is: can I find somebody who has actually taught the paper my child is going to sit, and can I tell the difference between that person and a confident generalist? Distance is a proxy parents use because it is the only filter a search box offers. It is a poor proxy. A tutor nine minutes away in The Springs who last taught maths to a British Year 11 cohort in 2014 is a worse match than a Cambridge 0580 Extended specialist on a screen.

The Meadows sits inside Emirates Living, a villa community bounded by Sheikh Zayed Road, Al Khail Road and the Emirates Hills golf course. It is residential by design: there are no tuition centres inside the gates, and the nearest cluster of them sits in Al Barsha and Tecom, between twelve and thirty minutes away depending on which side of the 4pm school-run peak you leave. That geography is why in-home tutoring became the default here, and why its real cost is counted in evenings rather than dirhams.

IB Gram does not take part in that market. We do not send tutors to addresses in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service our India operation runs, and saying so plainly is more useful than implying otherwise. What we do instead is match a student in Meadows 4 to the tutor who knows Pearson 4MA1 Higher tier, or Cambridge 0620 Extended, or First Language English 0990, and teach one-to-one over live video at a time that survives a 3:15 bell and a fifty-minute bus ride.

The rest of this page is written to make that choice checkable rather than persuasive. There is a table of the Cambridge and Edexcel codes for the subjects taught in schools around Emirates Living, so you can compare the code on your child's timetable against the tutor's claim. There is a table of what the Dubai market charges, attributed to the providers who published each figure. There is the Cambridge entry calendar counted backwards from the exam, because the deadline that actually traps families sits in November for a February exam.

There is also what a tutor may and may not do with coursework, what the MoHRE private tuition permit is and how to ask about it without being awkward, and what the Ministry of Education counts when a family eventually applies for certificate equivalency. None of that is marketing. All of it is the sort of thing you would otherwise discover three weeks before an entry deadline, from a WhatsApp group, in a form you cannot verify.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-meadows.programmesIntro: Schools around Emirates Living run three or four recognisable routes through the secondary years, and a tutoring plan only makes sense once you know which one your child is on. The notes below describe each route as it is actually timetabled in this part of Dubai, including where the handover points sit.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: A two-year course assessed almost entirely by terminal written papers, with each subject entered separately and in some cases tiered. Most British-curriculum schools enter eight to ten subjects. Cambridge splits many syllabuses into Core and Extended, which cap at grade C and grade A* respectively; Pearson tiers maths into Foundation and Higher and leaves most other subjects single-tier. The tier decision is usually taken in Year 10 and is hard to reverse late.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools inside and around Emirates Living, including Dubai British School Emirates Hills, Kings' School Al Barsha and Safa Community School, run IGCSE as the Year 10-11 qualification before students split towards A Level or the IB Diploma. Dubai's UK-curriculum sector accounted for 37 per cent of private-school enrolment in 2024-25, which is why this is the single busiest tutoring demand in the neighbourhood.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 and Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE, where the content is broad and the assessment is internal. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests sit in March, May and October and are the first externally marked signal most families see. Weak algebra, unreliable scientific notation and an inability to structure a paragraph are all cheaper to fix here than in Year 11, because there is no entry deadline pressing on the work.
programmes.countryNote: Families in The Meadows tend to arrive at tutoring in Year 11, which is the most expensive moment to arrive. A Year 8 student in Meadows 2 who cannot rearrange a formula will meet that gap again in 0580 Extended, in 0625 Physics and in 0455 Economics. One hour a fortnight at this stage replaces three hours a week two years later.

programmes.name: AS and A Level
programmes.description: The most common post-16 route out of IGCSE in Dubai's British schools. Three or four subjects, linear or modular depending on the board, with Pearson offering modular assessment that lets a student bank units and Cambridge assessing most subjects at the end. For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, one A Level at grade E or two AS Levels at the same grade must be shown alongside the IGCSE count.
programmes.countryNote: The IGCSE-to-A-Level step inside Emirates Living schools usually happens on the same campus, so parents assume continuity. The content jump in Maths and Physics does not respect that assumption: 0580 Extended rewards method marks, while A Level punishes unexplained steps. Students who coasted on a grade 7 at IGCSE are the ones who ask for help in the November of Year 12.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across three Higher Levels and three Standard Levels, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internal assessment carries real weight in every subject, which changes the nature of tutoring from exam drilling to deadline management and feedback on draft work. The IB accounted for 7 per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment in 2024-25.
programmes.countryNote: Emirates International School Meadows and Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills both run the IB continuum, so a family in Meadows 5 with two children can genuinely have one on IGCSE and one on the Diploma. The two need different tutors and different session rhythms, and parents who try to buy one solution for both usually end up paying for a compromise that suits neither.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-meadows.subjectsIntro: Every subject below is matched on the syllabus code, not the subject name. "IGCSE Physics" is three different courses depending on whether your child sits Cambridge 0625 Core, Cambridge 0625 Extended or Pearson 4PH1, and the papers, the practical assessment and the grade ceiling all differ.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 · Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two written papers, no coursework. Extended and Higher tier reach grade 9; Core caps at C and Foundation at 5. Marks leak in algebraic manipulation, in bearings and trigonometry in non-right-angled triangles, and in the last two parts of long structured questions where method marks are available but never claimed because nothing is written down.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Pure Mathematics (0606 · 4PM1)
subjects.description: Taken alongside the main maths course by students heading for A Level Maths or Further Maths. Calculus, matrices, series and trigonometric identities arrive a year early. The common failure is treating differentiation as a rule to apply rather than a rate of change, which collapses the moment a question asks for a stationary point in context.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 · Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: Cambridge candidates sit three papers, including either a practical or an alternative-to-practical paper; Pearson assesses practical skills inside two written papers. Electricity and electromagnetism are where grades are made or lost, followed by anything requiring a graph to be read rather than drawn. Unit conversion errors cost more marks here than conceptual misunderstanding.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 · Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic reaction pathways account for most of the gap between a 6 and an 8. Students who can recite a definition often cannot apply it to an unfamiliar substance, which is exactly what the Extended paper tests. Practical method questions reward precise language about control variables and nothing else.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 · Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: The highest-content syllabus in the science group and the one students most often try to memorise whole. Transport in plants, homeostasis and inheritance are the usual weak points, and extended-response questions are marked on linked reasoning rather than keyword presence. Writing three correct facts in no logical order scores one mark out of four.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0654 · Pearson 4SD0)
subjects.description: Two IGCSE grades from one timetable block covering biology, chemistry and physics. It is the route most students in Dubai take when they do not need three separate sciences, and it is frequently tutored badly because a biologist is asked to cover the physics content. Each discipline needs its own specialist hour.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500 · 0990 · Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Reading response and directed writing, with a composition component. The marks sit in selection and in control of register, not in vocabulary size. Students who write fluently but answer a different question than the one asked are the standard case, and the fix is a rehearsed reading routine rather than more practice essays.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 · 0511 · Pearson 4ES1)
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and, at 0511, an assessed speaking component. For many families in Emirates Living this is the subject that decides whether a Year 11 report looks balanced. Tutoring works on exam-specific listening technique and on the summary task, which rewards compression and is almost never taught explicitly.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455 · Pearson 4EC1)
subjects.description: Two papers, with diagram accuracy carrying more marks than most students expect. Elasticity, market failure and the circular flow are the recurring difficulties. Eight-mark evaluation questions need a judgement supported by a condition, and answers that list advantages and disadvantages without concluding anything sit permanently in the middle band.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450 · Pearson 4BS1)
subjects.description: Case-study driven, which means marks go to candidates who use the stimulus material rather than general knowledge. Break-even analysis, cash-flow forecasts and motivation theory are the technical core. The most common lost marks are on application: a correct definition that never touches the business described in the case earns the definition mark only.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478 · 0984)
subjects.description: Theory paper plus an algorithms and programming paper. Pseudocode discipline, trace tables and an understanding of how data is represented are where the grade lives. Students who have written working Python often lose marks because the mark scheme wants a trace table completed row by row, not a correct final answer.

subjects.name: Geography and History (0460 · 0470 · 4GE1 · 4HI1)
subjects.description: Both reward structured argument and specific case-study detail, and both punish generalities. Geography's skills paper needs confident map and graph work; History needs source evaluation that addresses provenance rather than content alone. These are the subjects where a weekly hour on technique moves a grade faster than content revision does.

sections.heading: The search is for proximity; the problem is syllabus
paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor in The Meadows is, for most families who search that phrase, the answer to a question about trust rather than distance. You want somebody who has taught the exact paper your child will sit, and distance is simply the only filter a search box offers. IB Gram matches that tutor and teaches one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to addresses in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service our India operation provides. The trade you make is a narrower drive radius for a much wider pool of subject specialists.

Consider what the proximity filter actually returns. Emirates Living is a villa community with no tuition centres inside it, so the nearest available tutor is whoever happens to live in The Springs, The Lakes or Emirates Hills and advertises locally. The number of adults within a two-kilometre radius of Meadows 6 who have taught Cambridge 0620 Extended Chemistry to a Year 11 cohort within the last three years is small. The number who will say they can teach it is considerably larger. Geography does not help you tell those two groups apart, and that is the whole problem with searching by it.

Syllabus code does help. Ask for the code, not the subject: 0580 or 4MA1, 0625 or 4PH1, 0500 or 0990. Ask which papers the tutor has taught towards and which tier. Ask them to describe where candidates lose marks on that specific paper, and listen for whether the answer is about the paper or about motivation. A tutor who knows the assessment will talk about method marks, command terms and the alternative-to-practical paper. A generalist will talk about confidence. Both matter, but only one of them is the thing you cannot get from the school.
bullets: Ask for the syllabus code and tier, not the subject name
Ask which papers the tutor has prepared students for, and when
Ask where marks are lost on that paper, and judge the specificity of the answer
Ask what the tutor will not do with coursework, and check the answer is a real boundary

sections.heading: Find the code before you find the tutor
paragraphs: Every IGCSE entry your child's school makes carries a syllabus code, and that code is the most useful single piece of information a parent in The Meadows can hold. It is printed on the statement of entry the exams officer issues, usually in January or February for a summer series, and it is normally visible on the subject pages of the school's own curriculum booklet. If you cannot find it, the exams officer will tell you in one email. Nothing else about tutoring can be decided properly until you have it.

The code settles three things at once. It tells you the board, which determines the number of papers and how practical science is assessed. It tells you whether the subject is tiered, which sets the grade ceiling your child is working towards. And it tells a tutor which mark scheme to teach against, because Cambridge and Pearson reward different things in an extended answer even when the content is identical. A tutor who asks for the code in the first conversation is reading the assessment. One who does not is reading the subject name.

The table below lists the codes used by the subjects most commonly taken in schools around Emirates Living. Use it to check what you are told rather than to decide anything on its own: schools do change boards between cohorts, and a few run different boards in different subjects within the same year group. Verify against the statement of entry, and treat any mismatch as a question for the school rather than an error in the table.

sections.heading: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel are not interchangeable
paragraphs: Parents in Emirates Living swap tutor recommendations across school gates and WhatsApp groups constantly, and the recommendation that travels rarely carries the board with it. That is how a family ends up paying for twelve weeks of Cambridge practical-paper technique for a child entered on Pearson 4PH1, where practical skills are assessed inside the written papers and there is no separate practical component to rehearse. The content overlap between the two boards is high. The assessment overlap is not, and tutoring lives in the assessment.

The differences that change a weekly plan are specific. Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended, with different papers and different grade ceilings; Pearson tiers maths into Foundation and Higher and leaves most other subjects single-tier, so the same conversation about ceilings does not apply. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a timetable per zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone's timetable was used. Pearson runs a single international timetable with provisional versions published well ahead of each series.

The practical consequence for a Meadows family is that you should never let a tutor plan a term before confirming the board, and you should never accept a date for an exam from a tutor at all. Dates come from the school's exams officer and from the live timetable PDF on the board's own site, because provisional timetables are revised. Everything below the board-and-code line, from paper order to the way an eight-mark question is marked, follows from this one piece of information.

A single weekly hour with a mid-range qualified tutor is estimated by Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table at AED 600 to 1,200 a month, with budget options at AED 240 to 600 and specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more. Published monthly packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are the numbers to compare against each other, because they are the ones you will pay twelve times.

Convert them to hourly rates and the structure becomes visible. Online budget and university-student tutoring is advertised from AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits including travel run AED 180 to 500, on Bestimate's AED 180 to 350 band plus independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500. IGCSE and IB specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named tutors higher still, with BartyED published at AED 650.

sections.heading: The three ways tutoring money is wasted in this neighbourhood
paragraphs: The first is paying a premium for travel and calling it quality. An in-home rate of AED 350 an hour in Emirates Living is not AED 350 of teaching; a meaningful share of it is the drive, and the tutor has priced the drive because they cannot sell that hour to anybody else. The same money spent on an online specialist buys either more hours or a better-matched tutor. This is not an argument that in-home tutoring is worthless. It is an argument that you should know what portion of the invoice is petrol and traffic before you sign up for it.

The second is buying hours before buying a diagnosis. Families commonly book a package of ten sessions in a subject described as "weak", with no idea whether the weakness is content, technique or exam behaviour. A child who understands electricity but cannot read a question stem needs four sessions, not ten, and they need them on a different thing. A single diagnostic session that produces a written list of gaps by topic is the cheapest money in tutoring, and it is the step most often skipped because it feels like a delay.

The third is starting too late and then paying for panic. Demand for Year 11 tutoring in Emirates Living peaks in January and February, which is weeks before a summer series and months after the content gap opened. At that point you are competing for the same small pool of specialists as every other family on the same bus route, at the highest rates of the year, for the fewest available slots. Starting in Year 10, at one hour a week, costs less in total and works better, and nobody does it because in Year 10 nothing has gone visibly wrong yet.
bullets: Ask what share of an in-home quote covers travel; the answer is informative either way
Buy one diagnostic session before any package of hours
Book exam-term support before the autumn term ends, not in the new year
Check whether the tutor will mark timed papers against the published scheme, or only teach content

sections.heading: The entry deadline sits months before the exam
paragraphs: The single most expensive administrative fact in IGCSE is that entries close long before the papers are sat, and that tier decisions are locked at entry. In the UAE the series are June and November; the February and March sitting is offered to India only, so it is the June calendar a Dubai family should be counting backwards from. Entries for June close in the spring, roughly four months before the first paper, with the exact date confirmed on the centre's statement of entry. Forecast grades are submitted on their own, earlier deadline. Results reach centres in August and certificates follow months after that. A family who decides in the final term of teaching that Extended was the wrong call is already well past the moment that decision could have been changed.

Read that calendar backwards and the tutoring implications are obvious. The Core-or-Extended conversation has to be settled before entries close in the spring, which means the evidence for it, mock results and marked past papers, has to exist through the autumn and winter terms rather than appearing in the weeks before the papers. The forecast grade a school submits is a professional judgement based on work it has already seen, so the period that influences it is the months before submission, not the weeks after. And the resit question, November series or move on, is decided in the days around August results, when parents are least prepared to decide anything.

Dates differ by board and by series, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables that are revised before they become final, so treat the table below as a worked example of the shape rather than a calendar for your child. The authoritative dates for your child's entries are the ones your school's exams officer holds, read against the live timetable PDF on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com. For context on how long results take to travel: Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.
