sections.heading: Is the tutor legally permitted to teach your child in Dubai?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted by licence, not by default. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. On u.ae the permit is described as granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws.

There are two things a Meadows parent should take from this. The first is that asking a prospective tutor whether they hold the permit is a normal, reasonable question, not an accusation; the permit is free and takes a stated two working days through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services system under the service name Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing. The second is that no amount of fine has been published. Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, so any figure circulating in a parents' group should be treated as rumour.

A related rule catches families who think they have found the perfect arrangement. Abu Dhabi's ADEK professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the permit holder's own school. Treat that as press-reported and verify it against the current policy document, but do not build a plan around hiring your child's own classroom teacher privately. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal again, requiring a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram is not such an institute, holds no KHDA permit, and does not describe itself as approved by any regulator.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks actually leak, subject by subject
paragraphs: Grades at this level are lost in predictable, diagnosable places, and naming them is more useful than any general promise about improvement. In maths, the leak is method marks on long structured questions: a student who writes only the final answer to a four-mark question and gets it wrong scores zero, where showing the rearrangement would have earned two. In physics, it is unit conversion and graph reading, in that order. In chemistry, it is applying a memorised definition to an unfamiliar substance, which is precisely what the Extended paper is built to test.

In biology, the leak is structure rather than knowledge. Extended-response questions are marked on linked reasoning, so three correct facts in no causal order score far below two facts correctly connected. In English, it is answering a question adjacent to the one asked, usually because the reading routine is unrehearsed. In economics and business studies, it is evaluation: an answer that lists advantages and disadvantages and declines to reach a conditional judgement sits permanently in the middle band, regardless of how much content it contains.

The reason this matters for choosing a tutor is that every item on that list is visible in a marked past paper and invisible in a conversation about confidence. A tutor working properly will keep an error log by topic and command term, will mark timed work against the published mark scheme rather than impression, and will be able to tell you in week three which of these failure modes your child actually has. If after a month nobody can tell you that, you are paying for company rather than teaching, and the honest move is to change tutor.
bullets: Maths: unwritten method on multi-step questions
Physics: unit conversion, then reading values off a graph
Chemistry: applying definitions to unfamiliar substances
Biology: unlinked facts in extended-response answers
English: answering the adjacent question, not the set one
Economics and business: no conditional judgement in evaluation marks

sections.heading: Five subjects at grade E or 3: what the Ministry counts
paragraphs: Families in The Meadows who intend their children to apply to UAE universities, or to need a UAE-recognised school certificate at any point, eventually meet Ministry of Education equivalency. On the British track the requirement reported by Gulf Today in July 2026 is that students pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

That last clause is the one that surprises people, and at least one ranking tutoring site publishes the wrong subject count, stating that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. The sourced rule is five, excluding Arabic and Islamic education from the count. On the American track the same reporting sets English proficiency at an IELTS academic score of 5, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold appears in that source, so no IB figure is published here.

Two cautions belong with this. Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs, not something a tutoring service performs, applies for or guarantees, and nothing on this page should be read as a promise about an outcome of it. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, university admission or school progression; anybody telling you otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process. Verify the current rules on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation authority before planning around them, because reported requirements change and this page is a signpost rather than an authority.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside IGCSE
paragraphs: A British-curriculum school in Dubai does not teach only the British curriculum. Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. Federally, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. These subjects sit on your child's timetable in parallel with 0580 and 0620, and they take real hours.

KHDA's guidelines are specific about how they run. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies is taught in Arabic for Arab students, and in the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and moral, social and cultural studies. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes.

Two practical consequences follow for a tutoring plan in The Meadows. The first is timetable arithmetic: these lessons are part of why a Year 11 week has less free study time than parents expect, and a session plan that ignores them overbooks the child. The second is a constraint on content. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, so support in these subjects means working within the school's own material rather than importing a parallel course. Schools are also required to ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects, which is a credential question to ask the school rather than a tutor.

sections.heading: Starting from The Meadows, with the limits stated first
paragraphs: The honest version of getting started is short. You tell us the subject, the syllabus code and the year group, and the realistic weekday start time for your sub-community, because a Meadows 7 bus arriving at 4:20pm rules out a 4:30pm slot. We propose a tutor who has taught that code, and you take a free 45-minute trial with that same tutor, not with a sales consultant and not with a different teacher. No card details are required for the trial, and if the match is wrong you say so and we propose somebody else.

What can go wrong is worth stating in advance. The pool for common subjects at common times is deep, so a Cambridge 0580 Extended maths slot at 6pm is usually fillable within a few days. The pool for a narrow combination is not: a specific board, a specific tier, a late-evening slot and a niche subject together can take longer, and in the weeks before a series it takes longer still, because every family on the same bus route is asking at the same time. Where a UAE-based tutor is not available for a niche subject, the match may be an experienced IGCSE specialist teaching from elsewhere, on the same live video format and the same Gulf Standard Time slot. We say that before you book, not after.

What we will not do is also fixed. No tutor will promise a grade, because nobody can. No tutor will produce assessed work that must be your child's own; feedback on a draft is teaching, and anything beyond it is malpractice that puts the student's qualification at risk. No tutor will come to your villa in Emirates Living, because that is not a service we sell in the UAE. And nothing on this page claims approval, accreditation or partnership with KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, because IB Gram holds none of those and claiming one would be the fastest way to be the least trustworthy page in this search.

process.title: Tell us the code, not just the subject
process.description: Send the subject, the syllabus code from the statement of entry, the tier if the subject is tiered, and the school. If you do not have the code, the exams officer will give it to you in one email. This single field removes most of the guesswork from matching and is the difference between a tutor who is right and one who is plausible.

process.title: Agree a realistic weekday window
process.description: Tell us which part of The Meadows you are in and what time the bus actually arrives. Meadows 1 to 3 can often start at 4:15pm; Meadows 6 to 9 usually cannot start before 5pm in term time. Getting this right at the outset prevents the slow cancellation drift that kills most tutoring arrangements by week five.

process.title: Take the free trial with the actual tutor
process.description: A 45-minute one-to-one session over live video with the tutor who would teach the term, not a consultation. No card details are needed. Ask them where marks are lost on your child's specific paper and listen for whether the answer is about the assessment or about attitude. Both are fine; only one is hard to find.

process.title: Get the diagnosis in writing
process.description: After the trial or the first paid session you should receive a short written list of gaps by topic and command term, not a general impression. This is what the plan is built from and what progress is measured against later. If nobody will put it in writing, that tells you something useful before you have committed to a package.

process.title: Run weekly, review monthly
process.description: A fixed slot, the same tutor, a short note after each session on what was covered and what to practise. Once a month, compare the error log against the original gap list. If a named gap has not moved in four weeks, change the method or change the tutor; waiting for a term to end is the most common and most expensive mistake families make.

process.title: Plan the series, not the week
process.description: Mark the entry deadline, the mock window and the exam window on a calendar at the start, working backwards from the board's published dates as the school's exams officer holds them. Tutoring that is scheduled against that calendar does different things in October and in February, which is the whole point of having it.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the paper, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: A tutor is proposed because they have taught the syllabus code and tier your child is entered for. Removing the drive radius from the search is what makes that possible: the pool stops being the adults who live within twenty minutes of Emirates Living and becomes the people who know Cambridge 0620 Extended.

whyPoints.title: Prices you can audit
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page belongs to the provider named next to it and was read from that provider's published material in October 2026. None of them is our price. You can check each one yourself, which is more than any page currently ranking for this search allows you to do.

whyPoints.title: A stated boundary on coursework
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches method, reads drafts and gives feedback against the published criteria. The student produces every word that is submitted. That boundary is written here because the alternative is sold openly in this market, and a student who buys it risks the qualification rather than the tutoring fee.

whyPoints.title: Calendar-aware from the first session
whyPoints.description: Entry deadlines, forecast-grade submission, exam windows and results dates all sit months apart, and a plan that ignores them optimises the wrong weeks. Sessions are scheduled against the board's published calendar as your school holds it, so October work and February work are genuinely different work.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated before you book
whyPoints.description: If no UAE-based tutor covers a narrow subject and tier at the time you need, you are told that before booking, along with what the alternative is. Concealing a coverage limit until after payment is standard in this market, and it is the single fastest way to lose a family's trust.

whyPoints.title: No regulator borrowed for credibility
whyPoints.description: KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE and the Ministry of Education are described on this page because understanding them helps you. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by any of them, holds no KHDA training-institute permit, and operates no office in the UAE.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE home tutor in The Meadows who will teach in our villa?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We deliver one-to-one IGCSE tuition over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and we do not send tutors to addresses in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service our India operation runs. Independent tutors and agencies in Dubai do visit Emirates Living, and the market rate for an in-home hour including travel runs roughly AED 180 to 500 depending on the provider. If an in-home arrangement is what you want, that is a legitimate choice and this page tells you what it costs. What we offer is a tutor matched to your child's syllabus code rather than to a drive radius.

faqs.question: Where on a school report would I find my child's IGCSE syllabus codes?
faqs.answer: The reliable place is the statement of entry, which the school's exams officer issues ahead of each series and which lists every subject with its board and four-character code. Many schools also print codes in the Key Stage 4 options booklet or on the subject pages of the curriculum guide. A termly report usually does not carry them. If you cannot find a code, one email to the exams officer naming your child and the series will produce it. Get this before you shortlist tutors: it decides the board, the number of papers, whether the subject is tiered and which mark scheme applies.

faqs.question: Are Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE the same qualification?
faqs.answer: They are equivalent qualifications from different awarding bodies, not the same course. Content overlaps heavily; assessment does not. Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended with different grade ceilings and, in sciences, sets a separate practical or alternative-to-practical paper. Pearson tiers maths into Foundation and Higher, leaves most other subjects single-tier, and assesses practical skills inside the written papers. Cambridge also allocates centres to one of six timetable zones, warning that the correct zone timetable must be used. For tutoring the difference is practical: the same topic is rehearsed differently depending on which mark scheme the student will be marked against.

faqs.question: Can my child sit different IGCSE subjects with different exam boards?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in Dubai it is common. Schools pick the board subject by subject, so a Year 11 student can sit Cambridge 0580 maths and Pearson 4PH1 physics in the same series. It is why collecting codes matters more than asking which board the school uses: the answer may be both. For tutoring it means one tutor covering two subjects needs to be fluent in two mark schemes, and that is a fair question to put directly in the trial lesson. The exams officer's statement of entry is the document that settles which board applies to which subject.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE tutor charge per hour around Emirates Living?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates in October 2026 ran roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget or university-student online tutoring, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit including travel, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IGCSE specialist, with premium named tutors quoted higher. Those bands come from EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, TutorChase and BartyED respectively. None is an IB Gram price; we offer a free trial lesson and a consultation instead of a rate card, because session length and subject change the answer.

faqs.question: Is a monthly tutoring package better value than paying per hour?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether you will use the hours. Monthly packages published in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, and Bestimate estimates AED 600 to 1,200 a month for a weekly hour with a mid-range tutor. A package is cheaper per hour and more expensive per hour actually taught, because unused sessions during school trips, exam weeks and travel rarely roll over. Ask what happens to a missed session before you compare the headline figures, and start with a short block rather than a term.

faqs.question: When does the entry deadline for an IGCSE exam series close?
faqs.answer: Months before the exam, which catches families out every year. For a UAE candidate the series is June, with November as the resit route, and Cambridge entries for June close in the spring - roughly four months ahead of the first paper, with the exact date held by your school's exams officer and printed on the statement of entry rather than announced publicly. Forecast grades are due on a separate, earlier deadline again. Pearson behaves the same way with its own dates and publishes provisional timetables for each series that are revised before they become final; its November 2026 International GCSE papers ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Your child's actual dates come from the school's exams officer, read against the live timetable PDF on the board's own site. The planning consequence is that tier decisions must be evidenced in the autumn term, not argued in the spring.

faqs.question: How do I check that a private tutor is permitted to work in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Ask them directly whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, the official service is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing on mohre.gov.ae with a stated two working days to complete, and eligible applicants include registered teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so treat any amount quoted in a parents' group as rumour.

faqs.question: Should my child take Core or Extended for a Cambridge IGCSE subject?
faqs.answer: The honest answer is that it depends on evidence you should already have by the autumn term of Year 11, because the decision is locked at entry. Core caps at grade C and uses different papers; Extended reaches A* or 9. A student consistently scoring in the lower bands on Extended past papers may convert more marks on Core, and a student near the Core ceiling is being limited by the tier rather than by ability. Decide it on marked timed papers rather than on classwork impressions, with the subject teacher's view, and decide it before the entry deadline rather than after mocks.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the UAE Ministry of Education count?
faqs.answer: On the British track, reporting in July 2026 set the requirement at five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from those five, plus one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. One ranking tutoring site publishes six, which does not match the sourced rule. Equivalency is a Ministry process, not something a tutoring service performs or guarantees, and tutoring is not required for it. Verify the current rules on moe.gov.ae before planning around them.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 10 and coping. Is it too early for a tutor?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is the cheapest and most effective place to spend tutoring money, and almost nobody does it. One hour a week while the content is still being taught holds the pace of the syllabus instead of rebuilding it later, and it puts marked timed work in front of you in time to make the Core or Extended decision on evidence. Demand from Emirates Living peaks in January of Year 11, when rates are highest, specialists are booked and the gap is a year old. Starting early costs less in total and asks less of the student, which is the only argument that matters in Year 11.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover maths, physics and English for the same child?
faqs.answer: Maths and physics together is a common and usually sound pairing, because the overlap in algebra, graph work and unit handling is real. Adding English to the same tutor is rarely a good trade: the assessment objectives, the mark schemes and the teaching methods have almost nothing in common, and a tutor comfortable across all three is more likely to be a generalist than a specialist. Two tutors for three subjects, splitting sciences from humanities, is the arrangement that usually works. It also makes progress attributable, because you can see which subject is moving.

faqs.question: What happens in the free trial before we commit to an IGCSE tutor?
faqs.answer: Forty-five minutes, one-to-one over live video, with the tutor who would teach the term rather than a consultant. The tutor works on something real, usually a past-paper question in the weak topic, and the purpose is for you and your child to judge the fit while the tutor forms a first view of where the marks are going. No card details are required to book it. Useful questions to ask at the end: which paper does this topic appear on, where do candidates lose marks on it, and what would the first four sessions cover? Vague answers are informative.

faqs.question: Is an online lesson weaker than a tutor sitting beside my child?
faqs.answer: For one-to-one IGCSE work the format matters much less than the match. A shared screen with a graphics tablet shows working line by line, past papers can be annotated live, and the session recording or written note lets a parent see what happened without being in the room. What online removes is the travel premium and the drive radius, which is what lets a family in Meadows 8 work with a specialist in a specific syllabus rather than the nearest available tutor. Where face-to-face genuinely wins is with very young children and with students who need physical supervision to stay on task.

faqs.question: What if nobody covers the IGCSE subject we need, like Business Studies?
faqs.answer: You are told before you book, with the alternative named. Common subjects at common times fill within a few days. A narrow combination of board, tier, niche subject and a late evening slot can take longer, and in the weeks before a series everything takes longer because demand across Dubai peaks at once. Where no UAE-based tutor covers a niche subject, the match may be an experienced IGCSE specialist teaching from outside the UAE on the same live video format and the same Gulf Standard Time slot. Disclosing a coverage limit up front is the whole point; concealing it until after payment is the market norm.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a Geography fieldwork write-up without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary that should be stated before the work starts. A tutor may explain the assessment criteria in plain language, teach the methods, discuss the data, read a draft and give feedback on structure, evidence and clarity. The student plans, writes and submits every word themselves. No tutor should produce, rewrite or edit assessed work to completion, because the qualification belongs to the student and malpractice puts that qualification at risk rather than the tutoring fee. Ask any prospective tutor where their line sits; a tutor who cannot describe one is a risk to your child.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-meadows.closingHeading: Get the syllabus code, then get the right tutor
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-meadows.closingBody: If you take one thing from this page, make it the code. Ask the exams officer for your child's statement of entry, note the board and the four characters beside each subject, and use them to interrogate every tutor you speak to, including ours. Then tell us the code, the year group and what time the bus actually reaches your part of The Meadows, and take the free 45-minute trial with the tutor who would teach the term. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. If the match is wrong, say so and we will propose somebody else.

Each is matched by board and syllabus code before anything else is discussed.

intro.heading: Nearby is easy to check. Knowing the paper is not.
paragraphs: There are a lot of people within fifteen minutes of The Springs who will teach your child maths. There are considerably fewer who can tell you, without looking it up, that Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Extended is examined on two papers with a calculator allowed on one of them, that Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1 Higher tier splits the content differently across its two papers, and that a student entered for the wrong tier has a grade ceiling they cannot climb above no matter how well they perform. The gap between those two groups is the real subject of this page.

Proximity is a proxy, and it is a weak one. A parent in Springs 4 asking neighbours for a recommendation gets a shortlist of people who live nearby and are willing to drive at five in the afternoon. That is a perfectly sensible way to find somebody to supervise homework. It is a poor way to find somebody who has marked Paper 4, knows which command words carry method marks, and can look at a mock script and say which of the eight lost marks were content and which were technique.

The honest version of the answer is that IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Springs address. In-home visits in the UAE are not part of what we sell; that service exists only in our India operation. UAE tutoring is delivered one-to-one over live video, with the same tutor each week, work shared on screen, and sessions timed to Gulf Standard Time. The reason to prefer that is not the saved journey. It is that the shortlist becomes everyone who teaches 0580 Extended rather than everyone who teaches 0580 Extended and lives near Emirates Living.

First, though, you need to know what your child is actually entered for, and a surprising number of families do not. Two schools on the same bus route from The Springs can run different boards for the same subject. Some schools split boards by department, so maths is Pearson and the sciences are Cambridge. Tiering decisions are made by the school, sometimes without a conversation. The statement of entry, not the textbook cover, is the document that settles it.

So this page is built as a diagnosis rather than a sales pitch. How to find the syllabus code in ten minutes. What differs between Cambridge and Pearson for the same subject, with the codes side by side. The questions to ask a prospective tutor and what a weak answer sounds like. Where marks are actually lost, subject by subject. What the Dubai market charges, attributed. And what to do if your child is in Year 10 rather than Year 11, because the right plan is not the same.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-springs.programmesIntro: An IGCSE page needs three stages in view at once: the years that build the foundation, the two years that are examined, and the post-sixteen route the grades open. Springs families usually arrive at the middle one in a hurry and discover the first one mattered.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: No external grades, which is why this stage gets neglected and why so much IGCSE repair work traces back to it. Cambridge offers Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests, sat in March, May and October, as an external read on where a cohort actually is. Algebra fluency, scientific notation, graph reading and extended writing are the four things that decide how hard Year 10 feels.
programmes.countryNote: A Springs household with a Year 8 child has the cheapest possible intervention available: one session a week on algebraic manipulation for two terms removes most of what later becomes a crisis in Year 11. It is also the stage where families discover whether their school will enter the child for Core or Extended, which is worth asking about well before the decision is made.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Years 10 to 11
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight to ten subjects, examined in a June or a November series. Most subjects are tiered: Core covers grades C to G in the legacy scale, Extended reaches the top grades. Papers carry named components with fixed weightings, and the syllabus document for each code lists exactly what is assessable. Nothing outside it can be examined, which makes the syllabus the single most useful document a parent can read.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Ask your school which zone it sits in before building a revision calendar from a PDF found online.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other board several schools near The Springs use, with its own codes, its own paper structures and its own tiering. Pearson International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and in November each year. Some Pearson qualifications are structured so that units can be sat in different series, which changes revision planning in a way Cambridge's structure does not.
programmes.countryNote: The practical consequence for a Springs family is that a tutor who taught Cambridge for ten years is not automatically fluent in Pearson's mark schemes, and the reverse is equally true. We ask for the code before proposing anybody. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so plan from the live document on its site rather than from a date on a tutoring page.

programmes.name: A Level, IB Diploma or BTEC afterwards
programmes.description: IGCSE grades are the entry currency for whatever comes next, and the thresholds are set by the receiving school rather than by the board. Most Dubai sixth forms ask for a minimum grade in the subject a student wants to continue, often a 6 or a 7 for Higher Level or A Level sciences and maths. A grade 5 in Year 11 maths closes some doors quietly.
programmes.countryNote: Several British-curriculum schools near Emirates Living run IGCSE at sixteen and then split into A Level or the IB Diploma. Families should find out which route their school offers before Year 11 subject conversations, because an IB Diploma entry needs a broader grade spread than three strong A Level subjects do.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-springs.subjectsIntro: Below are the IGCSE subjects Springs families request most, with the Cambridge and Pearson codes where both are commonly taught in Dubai. Ask a prospective tutor which of these they have actually taught, and notice whether they answer with a code or with a topic.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended / Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The most requested subject in Dubai and the one where tiering matters most. Extended and Higher tier questions in the last third of each paper demand multi-step reasoning rather than recall. Most lost marks sit in algebraic manipulation, bearings and vectors, and in failing to show the method a mark scheme is looking for before writing an answer.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken by stronger cohorts as a bridge towards A Level or Diploma mathematics. It introduces calculus, logarithms and trigonometric identities earlier than the standard syllabus. Students who coast through 0580 often meet their first real difficulty here, and it is a good predictor of how Higher Level maths will feel.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and magnetism generate most requests, closely followed by waves. Students can usually recite formulae and cannot explain the physics the formula describes, which is exactly what the longer questions test. Practical assessment arrangements differ by board and by centre, so check whether your child sits a practical paper or an alternative-to-practical.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles calculations and organic chemistry are where grades are made and lost. The qualitative analysis and ionic-equation questions reward precision in wording that students treat as optional. Extended-tier content on electrolysis and rates of reaction needs deliberate question practice rather than re-reading notes.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content volume is the difficulty. Marks are lost through imprecise terminology and through answers that describe when the command word asked for an explanation. Data and graph interpretation questions carry a meaningful share of the paper and are routinely attempted without reading the axes or the units.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Science (Cambridge 0654 / 0653)
subjects.description: The double or single award route taken where a school does not run three separate sciences. The content is a genuine subset of the separate syllabuses, which means a tutor must know exactly which sections are excluded. Teaching from a separate-science textbook wastes a student's time on material that cannot be examined.

subjects.name: English First Language (Cambridge 0500 / Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Reading response and directed writing carry most of the risk. Students lose marks by summarising a passage rather than analysing how the writer achieves an effect, and by writing in a register the task did not ask for. The improvement here is technique rather than vocabulary, which makes it one of the fastest subjects to move.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: A different qualification from First Language, with different expectations and a speaking component. Many Dubai students are entered for it appropriately and some are entered for it defensively, which can cap what a sixth form will accept later. Worth checking which one your child is sitting and why.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the hidden mark-earner: a correctly labelled and correctly shifted diagram carries marks that a paragraph of prose cannot replace. Students lose marks by defining terms loosely and by giving evaluation that lists two views without weighing them. A strong subject for a student who writes clearly.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: The case-study paper rewards application to the specific business in front of the student, not general business knowledge. Answers that could have been written about any company score poorly. Command words such as analyse, evaluate and recommend have precise mark implications that are teachable in two or three sessions.

subjects.name: Geography (Cambridge 0460)
subjects.description: Case-study recall plus skills questions on maps, graphs and photographs. The skills paper is learnable and is often where a grade is gained, because many students revise content and never practise the skills component. Fieldwork-style questions need a method vocabulary students are rarely taught explicitly.

subjects.name: History (Cambridge 0470 / Pearson 4HI1)
subjects.description: Source evaluation technique separates grades more than knowledge does. Students who learn to interrogate provenance, purpose and audience outperform students who simply know more dates. The depth-study choices vary by school, so a tutor must teach your child's chosen options rather than the ones they know best.

regions.note: Apartment living with Regent International School on the doorstep. A high proportion of children here follow a British curriculum from primary onwards, so Cambridge codes dominate conversations at the school gate.

regions.name: The Views
regions.note: Mid-rise blocks beside The Greens, with a younger family profile. Many households here are still three or four years from IGCSE and are the ones best placed to fix algebra before it becomes expensive.

regions.name: The Meadows
regions.note: Villas north of The Springs. Children split between the IB continuum at Emirates Hills and British-curriculum campuses in Al Sufouh, which is exactly why board confusion is common in this cluster.

regions.name: The Lakes
regions.note: Close to Emirates Hills and its school cluster. Families here often have one child on Pearson and another on Cambridge, because different schools made different departmental choices.

regions.name: Jumeirah Park and Jumeirah Village
regions.note: Across Sheikh Zayed Road, with their own British-curriculum campuses including Sunmarke and Arcadia. Pearson Edexcel appears more often in these households than in the Emirates Living core.

regions.name: Al Barsha South and Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: The southern expansion, where several newer British schools have opened. New schools frequently make fresh board choices, so assume nothing from an older sibling's experience at a different campus.

regions.note: Reachable along Al Khail Road and sharing several of the same sixth-form destinations. Households here ask the same tiering questions and face the same November-series retake decisions.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-springs.modesIntro: Three shapes of IGCSE support cover nearly every request from this part of Dubai. All of them run one-to-one over live video, and the choice between them depends on how far your child is from a series.

modes.title: Syllabus repair, Year 10
modes.description: Weekly sessions working through the syllabus document in order, closing gaps while there is still time for them to matter. This is the cheapest and least stressful version of IGCSE tutoring and the one families regret not starting. The tutor works from the official syllabus for your child's code, marking what has been covered in school and what has not.

modes.title: Paper technique, Year 11

Sessions are built around past questions on your child's own board.

sections.heading: Find the syllabus code before you look for anybody
paragraphs: Ten minutes of paperwork will save you a term of mismatched teaching. Your child's board and code appear in three reliable places: the statement of entry the school issues before a series, the subject information sheet most Dubai schools publish for Years 10 and 11, and the front of the examination paper from any school mock that used real past material. Ask the subject teacher directly if none of those is to hand. A textbook cover is not evidence, because schools regularly teach from one publisher's book while entering candidates with another board.

A code is four digits for Cambridge and an alphanumeric string for Pearson. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, First Language English 0500, Economics 0455 and History 0470. The Pearson International GCSE equivalents include 4MA1 for Mathematics, 4PH1 for Physics, 4CH1 for Chemistry, 4BI1 for Biology and 4EA1 for English Language. Two things travel with the code: the component structure and the tier. Both change what good teaching looks like.

Once you have the code, the search changes character. Instead of asking whether somebody teaches IGCSE maths, you are asking whether they have taught 0580 Extended, which components their students found hardest, and what they would do about a mock script that lost marks across the non-calculator paper. Those are answerable questions, and the answers tell you quickly whether the person in front of you has sat in these rooms. This is the single highest-value thing a parent in The Springs can do before spending a dirham.
bullets: Statement of entry, subject information sheet or mock paper front cover
Cambridge codes are four digits; Pearson codes are alphanumeric
The code carries both the component structure and the tier
Ask about components, not about the subject

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: what actually differs for the same subject
paragraphs: Parents are often told the boards are interchangeable. They are not, and the differences are concrete enough to change a revision plan. The two boards divide content across papers differently, label tiers differently, and set questions in recognisably different house styles. A student who has practised one board's past questions all year and then sees the other board's paper will feel the difference within the first ten minutes.

Session structure is the other difference. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and allocates centres to six administrative zones with zone-specific timetables. Pearson International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables for future series in advance. Neither board's dates should ever be copied from a tutoring page; both publish the live documents themselves.

The table below is deliberately about structure rather than difficulty, because claiming one board is easier is the kind of assertion that gets repeated for years without evidence. What a parent needs is simpler: know which board, know which tier, and make sure the person teaching your child has the matching mark schemes in their head. Where a school has split boards across departments, your household may need two tutors with two different specialisms, and that is a normal arrangement rather than a sign of something going wrong. Two tutors in one household sounds expensive until the alternative is priced, which is one tutor guessing at the half of the syllabus they were never trained on.

sections.heading: Ten minutes of questions that identify a real syllabus specialist
paragraphs: You do not need to be a teacher to run this conversation. You need six questions and a sense of what a confident answer sounds like. The purpose is not to catch anybody out; it is to separate people who teach the qualification from people who teach the subject. Both exist in Dubai in large numbers, they charge similar rates, and only one of them can tell you what your child's mock script actually shows.

Listen for specificity and for willingness to say what they do not know. A tutor who says they cover all boards for all sciences at all levels is describing an availability calendar, not an expertise. A tutor who says they teach 0620 and 0625 well, have not taught Pearson chemistry recently, and would rather you found somebody who has, is telling you something far more useful about how they will handle your child's weak topic.

The second half of the conversation should be about evidence rather than promises. Ask what you will receive after each session. Ask how progress will be measured against the school's own assessments rather than an internal scale invented by the provider. Ask what happens if the match is wrong. And ask about the permit position, because private tutoring in the UAE requires a private tuition work permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, granted free of charge for two years, and a tutor who is vague about it is telling you something.

sections.heading: What a syllabus specialist is worth in this market, in AED
paragraphs: Rates in Dubai are public if you look, and the spread is wide enough that a parent should know where a quote sits before accepting it. Everything in the table below is a figure published by a named provider or by Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table for 2026, read in October 2026. None of it is IB Gram's price list. Three of the six competitor pages ranking for searches like this one publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars, which is not the currency any family here transacts in.

The useful way to read the table is by what the money buys rather than by the number. At the bottom of the range you are buying supervision: somebody present while homework happens. In the middle you are buying subject teaching. At the top you are buying board-specific examination technique, which is a narrower skill and the one that moves a grade in the final two terms. A family in The Springs paying a mid-range rate for supervision has not overpaid by much; a family paying a specialist rate for supervision has.

In-home arrangements sit higher on published rates than online ones, and the premium is the journey rather than the teaching. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. Monthly packages circulating in the Dubai market include about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Ask what any package includes before comparing it with an hourly figure.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher: the decision with a ceiling
paragraphs: Tier entry is the most consequential administrative decision in an IGCSE, and in most Dubai schools it is made by the department rather than negotiated with the family. Cambridge tiered subjects offer Core and Extended routes; Pearson tiered subjects offer Foundation and Higher. The lower tier caps the grade a candidate can be awarded. That cap is not a judgement about potential, but it is a hard limit on an outcome, and it is set before the student sits anything.

The arguments on both sides are real. A student placed on Extended who cannot access the back third of each paper may finish with a lower grade than they would have achieved comfortably on Core, and will spend a year feeling lost. A student parked on Core who could have handled Extended loses access to sixth-form courses that specify a grade above the Core ceiling. Neither error is rare, and both are usually visible in Year 10 mock data if anyone looks.

What a parent in The Springs can usefully do is ask three questions by the middle of Year 10. Which tier is my child currently expected to sit, on what evidence, and when is the last date that decision can change? Tier decisions interact with entry deadlines, and once a centre has submitted entries, changes are not assumed to be possible. A tutor's job here is diagnostic rather than persuasive: establish from timed work which tier the student can actually access, and give you something concrete to take to the department.
bullets: Core and Foundation entries carry a grade ceiling
Both over-placement and under-placement are common and visible in mock data
Ask which tier, on what evidence, and by when it can change
Timed past questions settle the argument faster than opinion does

sections.heading: Year 10 and Year 11 need different plans, term by term
paragraphs: The most common mistake in this market is buying the Year 11 product in Year 10 or the Year 10 product in Year 11. In Year 10 the problem is coverage: there are syllabus sections the student has met once and does not own. In Year 11 the problem is almost always conversion: the student knows more than the grade shows, and the lost marks are procedural. The same tutor can do both, but not in the same way, and a family paying for content delivery in the final term is buying the wrong thing.

Entry administration sits months ahead of the papers, which is why the planning column in the table matters. The clearest way to see the lag is to count the June series forwards: entries close in the spring, roughly four months before the first paper, forecast grades go in on their own earlier deadline, the papers themselves run through June by zone timetable, results reach centres in August and certificates arrive months later again. Cambridge's February and March sitting is not part of this picture in the UAE at all - it is offered to India only - so a Dubai family planning against it would be planning against the wrong calendar entirely. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and its June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026.

Read the table as a planning instrument rather than a promise. Your school's internal deadlines will be earlier than the board's, and those internal dates are the ones that actually govern your child's autumn. Ask for them in writing at the start of the year, put them in a shared calendar, and treat any tutoring block as something scheduled backwards from them. Families in The Springs who do this find the final term far less dramatic than neighbours who did not.

sections.heading: Past papers, mark schemes and the line nobody should cross
paragraphs: IGCSE has less assessed coursework than the IB, so the academic-honesty question takes a different shape here. It shows up around material rather than around authorship. Families ask for packs of past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and syllabus documents, and a certain kind of provider supplies them as downloads. That is somebody else's copyright being redistributed, and for unreleased material it is worse than a copyright problem.

The correct approach is simple and costs nothing. Past material, syllabus documents and specimen papers are published by the boards themselves, and your school has access to the secure materials that are not public. A tutor should reference and cite those official sources, teach from them in a live session, and point you to the board's own site rather than hand over a folder. If a prospective tutor offers a drive full of papers as a selling point, that is information about how they operate.

The authorship line still exists where coursework is assessed, and in a handful of IGCSE subjects it is. The rule is the same as anywhere: the student produces the work, and the tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on what the student has produced. No supplied text, no sections drafted on the student's behalf, no editing a piece until it is no longer theirs. A parent can test this easily by asking their child to explain a paragraph of their own work without notes. If the explanation comes back fluently, the work is theirs and the tutoring is doing its job. If it does not, the problem is not the mark; it is that nobody has learned anything worth keeping.
bullets: Boards publish syllabus and specimen material themselves; link, do not redistribute
Schools hold the secure material a tutor should not be supplying
Where coursework is assessed, the student writes it and the tutor gives feedback
A folder of papers offered as a selling point is a warning sign

sections.heading: Retakes, private candidates and the November series
paragraphs: Not every IGCSE story ends in June. A student who misses a grade threshold for sixth form, or who was entered at the wrong tier, has a second route, and the Dubai market handles it badly because almost nobody writes about it. Cambridge runs a November series as well as June; Pearson International GCSE is available in May/June and November. A November retake gives roughly five months of focused work and lands in time for most post-16 decisions to be revisited.

The administration is where families come unstuck. A student retaking may be entered by their own school, or may need to sit as a private candidate at a registered examination centre, which is a different arrangement with its own deadlines, fees and identification requirements. Entries close months ahead. The subject must be checked against the series, since not every syllabus is available in every series. All of this belongs on a calendar before any teaching is bought.

Teaching for a retake is also a different job from teaching the course. The student has already met the content once, so the work is diagnostic: find out precisely which components and which question types produced the lost marks, then rebuild those alone. A retake block that re-teaches the syllabus from the start wastes most of the available time. We ask for the breakdown by component before proposing anybody, because without it a retake plan is guesswork wearing a timetable. A Springs family deciding between a November retake and a full June resit should settle that question on the component breakdown alone, because the two routes cost very different amounts of time.

sections.heading: How to start from The Springs, and what we will not pretend
paragraphs: Bring three things to the first conversation: the subject and the syllabus code, the most recent mock or report with the component breakdown if you have it, and the evenings that genuinely work once school and activities are accounted for. With those we can usually name a specialist for your child's board in the same conversation. Without the code we will ask you to find it first, because matching on the subject name is how mismatched tutoring starts.

The first lesson is free, one per family, with no card details taken beforehand. It is a working session rather than a consultation: the tutor looks at where the understanding actually stops and teaches something, and you get a short written note afterwards. If the person is wrong for your child, say so and we will propose someone else. Nobody benefits from defending a bad match for three weeks out of politeness.

The things we will not pretend are worth stating plainly. We do not send tutors to UAE addresses. We hold no approval, accreditation or partnership from Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA or the Ministry of Education, and any provider implying otherwise should be asked for the certificate number. We do not promise a grade, because nobody honest can. And if no specialist for your child's board and tier is free in your preferred slot, we will tell you that and offer a different time, a short wait, or a tutor outside the UAE teaching the same syllabus, rather than quietly sending a generalist.
bullets: Bring the syllabus code, the mock breakdown and your free evenings

process.title: Confirm the board and the code
process.description: Before anything else we ask which syllabus your child sits: Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1, Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher. If you do not know, we tell you exactly where to find it. Matching on the subject name instead of the code is the root cause of most wasted tutoring.

process.title: Read the evidence you already have
process.description: The most recent mock script, the component breakdown and the school report tell us more in five minutes than a conversation does in an hour. We want to know which paper lost marks and whether those marks were content or technique, because the answer changes who we propose.

process.title: Match on syllabus, then on timing
process.description: The shortlist is drawn from tutors who have taught that code at that tier, and only then filtered by your available evenings. Online delivery is what makes that order possible; an in-home search reverses it and takes availability first, which is why specialist cover is so often missing.

process.title: One free diagnostic lesson
process.description: A real lesson with the proposed tutor, free, one per family, no card details in advance. Your child should learn something and you should receive a short written note: what was covered, what the gaps look like, and what the next few sessions would target.

process.title: Work backwards from the series
process.description: Sessions are planned against your school's internal deadlines and the board's published dates, not against a generic programme. In Year 10 that means syllabus coverage; in Year 11 it means timed questions and command words; before a retake it means rebuilding only the components that actually failed.

whyPoints.title: Codes, not subject names
whyPoints.description: A tutor is matched to 0580 Extended or 4CH1, not to maths or chemistry. That single discipline removes the most common failure in this market, which is a capable teacher working from the wrong board's mark schemes for a whole term without anybody noticing.

whyPoints.title: Honest about where we are not
whyPoints.description: IB Gram does not visit homes in the UAE, holds no office here, and claims no board or regulator approval. Everything on this page about permits, equivalency and inspection is explanation, cited to the authority that published it, rather than an implied endorsement.

whyPoints.title: Rates on the page with sources
whyPoints.description: Published AED bands appear here with the provider named and the month they were read, so you can judge any quote you receive, including ours. Most pages competing for this search either publish nothing or quote in dollars.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before teaching
whyPoints.description: We ask for the mock breakdown before proposing a tutor, because a student losing marks on method notation needs a different intervention from a student who has not covered electrolysis. Starting without that is how families buy the wrong product for two terms.

whyPoints.title: Official material, properly cited
whyPoints.description: Syllabus documents, specimen papers and mark schemes belong to the boards. We reference and link them and teach from them live; we do not redistribute packs of them, which is both a copyright matter and a sign of how a provider works.

whyPoints.description: If the match is wrong, we change it. The free first lesson exists so that judgement happens before money does, and a family that says the chemistry is fine but the rapport is not gets a different tutor rather than a defence of the first one.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE board and syllabus code my child is sitting?
faqs.answer: Three documents settle it. The statement of entry the school issues before a series lists every syllabus code. The subject information sheet most Dubai schools publish for Years 10 and 11 usually names the board. The front cover of any past paper used in a school mock carries the code directly. If none is available, email the subject teacher and ask for the code rather than the board, because some schools run different boards in different departments and a general answer can be wrong for one of your child's subjects.

faqs.question: For a Springs family, is Cambridge IGCSE equivalent to Pearson Edexcel International GCSE?
faqs.answer: No. They are separate qualifications from separate awarding bodies, with their own codes, paper structures, tiering labels and mark schemes. Cambridge Mathematics is 0580 with Core and Extended routes; the Pearson equivalent is 4MA1 with Foundation and Higher tiers, and the content is divided across papers differently. Both are recognised by universities. What matters for tutoring is that past-question practice and mark-scheme familiarity must match the board your child is actually entered for, which is why we ask for the code before proposing anyone.

faqs.question: Can an IGCSE tutor visit our villa in Emirates Living?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in our India operation. UAE lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video with the same tutor each week and work shared on screen. The reason we prefer it is not the saved journey: it is that the shortlist for Cambridge 0620 Extended becomes everybody who teaches that syllabus on a compatible timezone, instead of everybody who teaches it and is willing to drive into the Emirates Living clusters at five in the afternoon.

faqs.question: What should I ask a prospective IGCSE tutor in the first five minutes?
faqs.answer: Ask which syllabus code they have taught and for how long, and listen for whether they answer with a code or a topic. Ask which paper your child loses most marks on and how they would find out; a strong answer asks to see the mock script first. Ask what you will receive in writing after each session, how progress will be measured against school assessments, and whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. Vagueness on any of those is information.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Core and Extended entry, and can it be changed?
faqs.answer: Core and Extended are different entry routes for the same Cambridge syllabus, and the Core route caps the grade a candidate can be awarded. Pearson uses Foundation and Higher tiers in the same way. The decision is usually made by the school department on the basis of classwork and mock performance. It can be revisited, but only up to the point at which the centre submits final entries to the board, which falls months before the examinations. Ask your school which tier is planned, on what evidence, and by when it can change.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE specialist cost per hour in Dubai right now?
faqs.answer: On figures published by named providers and read in October 2026: homework supervision runs around AED 33 to 65, with Tutopiya from AED 33 and EdFlik from AED 45. Online subject teaching sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 once travel is priced in, per Bestimate and independent tutors. Board-specific examination technique in an exam year runs AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase quoting AED 270. Those are their numbers, not ours.

faqs.question: My child studies Co-ordinated Science, not three separate sciences. Does that change the tutoring?
faqs.answer: Significantly. Co-ordinated and Combined Science syllabuses cover a defined subset of the separate-science content, so a tutor must know exactly which sections are excluded from your child's code. Teaching from a separate-science textbook means spending sessions on material that cannot appear on the paper, which is the most common way time is wasted in this subject. Ask any prospective tutor which award your child sits, double or single, and whether they have taught that specific code rather than the three separate sciences.

faqs.question: Should we start tutoring in Year 10 or wait until Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10 if the problem is coverage, Year 11 if the problem is conversion. In Year 10 there are syllabus sections a student has met once and does not own, and one weekly session across two or three terms closes them cheaply. By Year 11 most students know more than their grade suggests, and the lost marks are procedural: method not shown, command word misread, time mismanaged on the last question. Buying content delivery in the final term is the most common misallocation in this market.

faqs.question: Can my child retake an IGCSE in November rather than waiting a year?
faqs.answer: Usually yes. Cambridge runs a November series alongside June, and Pearson International GCSE is available in May/June and November, though not every syllabus appears in every series, so that has to be checked. A November retake gives roughly five months of focused work. The administration matters more than the teaching: entries close months ahead, and a student may need to be entered by a registered examination centre as a private candidate rather than by their former school. Put those deadlines on a calendar before buying any sessions.

faqs.question: Will a tutor give us a folder of past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be wary of anyone who offers that as a selling point. Past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and syllabus documents belong to the boards, which publish them on their own sites, and schools hold the secure material that is not public. A tutor should reference and cite the official source and teach from it live in a session. Redistributing packs of board material is a copyright problem, and for unreleased material it is considerably more serious than that.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Year 11 student in The Springs usually need?
faqs.answer: Two sixty-minute sessions a week in the subject causing the problem, through the term before the series, is the common pattern. Families supporting two subjects normally give each its own two slots rather than splitting one hour, because switching subject mid-session wastes the first ten minutes twice. If the diagnosis is narrow, such as electricity in Physics or moles calculations in Chemistry, a defined block of three to eight sessions with an agreed end date often does the job without an open-ended commitment.

faqs.question: Does my child's school decide which board, or can we choose?
faqs.answer: The school decides, and it decides campus by campus and sometimes department by department. That is why two children in the same Springs household can sit different boards for the same subject, and why an older sibling's experience at a different school tells you nothing reliable. Parents cannot usually pick a board, but they can and should find out which one applies to each subject, because every piece of past-question practice and every mark scheme a tutor uses needs to match it.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE grades matter for UAE university entry and Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: They matter for both. For the British track, published equivalency requirements ask for five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus either one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the count of five. One ranking tutoring site tells UAE parents six subjects are needed, which is wrong. Verify on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation channel before making subject decisions.

faqs.question: Our mock results were much worse than classwork. What does that usually mean?
faqs.answer: Most often it means technique rather than knowledge, and that is good news because technique moves faster. The usual culprits are showing no method on multi-mark questions, answering a different command word from the one printed, and spending too long on early questions so the last page is rushed. Ask the school for the component breakdown rather than the overall percentage. A tutor who sees which marks were lost, and where on the paper, can target that in a handful of sessions.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor for our exact board and tier is free in our slot?
faqs.answer: We say so in the first conversation. Some combinations, particularly a specific board at Extended or Higher tier in a narrow evening window, are genuinely contested in a given week. The options we put forward are a different time, a short wait for the right specialist, or a tutor based outside the UAE who teaches the same syllabus on a compatible timezone. What we will not do is propose a general subject tutor for a board they have not taught and let you discover it in week three.

faqs.question: Does a private IGCSE tutor in Dubai need a licence to teach my child?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, anyone giving private lessons in the UAE needs a private tuition work permit through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without the permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts is published, so treat any figure you read with scepticism.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-springs.closingHeading: Send us the code, not just the subject
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-springs.closingBody: The fastest way to get this right is to find your child's syllabus code before you contact anybody, ours included. With the code, the tier and a recent mock breakdown, we can usually name a specialist who has taught that exact paper in the same conversation, run one free lesson for you to judge, and give you a written note of what the next few sessions should target. Without it, every provider in Dubai will sell you a tutor for the subject and some of them will be teaching the wrong board's mark schemes. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with the same tutor each week.

intro.heading: The IGCSE question is nearly always a question about which term it is
paragraphs: An IGCSE course is two years long and the grade is decided in about three weeks of it. That asymmetry is what makes the examination calendar the right place to start. A student in the first term of Year 10 can afford to build slowly. A student in the second term of Year 11 is working inside a window that is already closed at one end, and the useful question changes from what should we improve to what can still be rescued in the time left.

The boards fix the outer edges. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series — the February and March series is offered to India only, so it is not a route open to a candidate sitting in Dubai. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Both boards split centres into administrative zones and publish separate timetable versions, and Cambridge states plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used. The school handles that, but a parent who knows it exists asks a better question at parents' evening.

Inside those edges, your child's own school sets everything that actually constrains tutoring: the mock window, coursework and practical deadlines, the date predicted grades are finalised, and the point at which entry decisions for tiered papers stop being reversible. That last one catches families out. The choice between Core and Extended in a Cambridge subject, or between a Foundation and Higher tier where one applies, is an entry decision with a deadline, not an opinion that can be revised in May.

The Sustainable City is a convenient place to run this kind of plan, for a reason that has nothing to do with teaching. The community sits off Al Qudra Road with a school inside its own gates, so children at that school are home early and the late-afternoon hours are real rather than theoretical. Children travelling outward to British-curriculum schools in Motor City, Dubai Sports City or Arabian Ranches are home considerably later, and a plan that pretends a 4pm start works for them collapses within a fortnight.

What we do not do is drive to your villa. IB Gram runs no home visits in the UAE at all; every lesson here is live, one-to-one and over video, with past-paper questions shared on screen and a recording available if the family wants one. Household visits exist only in our India operation, and no page of ours will suggest otherwise. The honest case for that model in this neighbourhood is made in a table further down the page, alongside what visiting tutors in this part of Dubai actually charge once travel is priced in. The short version is that an online booking removes the two journeys nobody teaches during, and that the time saved is what makes a late-afternoon session possible at all for a Year 11 student with a full school day behind them.
