dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-sustainabl.programmesIntro: Most students in this community reach IGCSE through one of three routes, and the route changes what the first term of Year 10 needs to look like. These are the stages we tutor and where the calendar bites in each.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9, before the IGCSE course begins
programmes.description: The years nobody tutors and everybody later wishes they had. Nothing is examined externally, so a gap in algebraic fluency or in writing an extended explanation is invisible until IGCSE marks start arriving. The work here is narrow and unglamorous: negative numbers, fractions, rearranging formulae, and the habit of reading a question twice before answering it.
programmes.countryNote: Families arriving in Dubai mid-phase are the common case in The Sustainable City and the newer Dubailand communities. A child joining a British-curriculum school in Year 8 from an American or CBSE system usually has a specific, closable gap rather than a general weakness, and one term of focused work in Year 9 is worth four terms of catch-up later.

programmes.name: Year 10, the first IGCSE year
programmes.description: Content is being covered for the first time and the papers are still a year away, which makes this the cheapest year in which to fix anything. Coursework and practical components in several subjects begin here, and in modular Edexcel subjects some units can be sat early. The common failure is treating Year 10 as a rehearsal and then compressing two years of content revision into the final two terms.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools often hold internal Year 10 examinations at the end of the year that feed directly into tier and entry decisions for Year 11. For a student in this community, those internal results are the moment to decide whether Extended is realistic in a subject, while there is still a year of room to make it so.

programmes.name: Year 11, the examination year
programmes.description: Three terms, one mock block, and a set of entry deadlines that sit months before the papers. Grades are reported on the 9-1 scale by both boards. Nearly all of the measurable improvement in this year comes from paper technique rather than from new content: command-term discipline, showing method, and answering the question asked rather than the question revised for.
programmes.countryNote: The November series is the resit route for a Dubai student who misses a grade in June, and knowing it exists changes how a family reacts to a disappointing result rather than how they prepare for it. Pearson results history is a useful guide to timing: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

programmes.name: After IGCSE: the A Level or Diploma decision
programmes.description: IGCSE grades function as entry requirements for whichever route follows, and schools in Dubai set their own thresholds for Higher Level or A Level subjects. A student aiming at a mathematics-heavy route needs a specific grade in a specific paper, not a good overall profile. Working out which grade the target route requires, early, is worth more than a general push on every subject.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE university plans, Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track requires five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject requirement; the sourced figure is five.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-sustainabl.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects families in The Sustainable City and the surrounding communities ask about most, with the syllabus codes where they help and the specific place marks go missing. A tutor booked against a named paper works faster than a tutor booked against a subject.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Extended and Higher tier questions reward method marks even when the final answer is wrong, so students who write nothing down lose marks they had earned. Algebraic manipulation, not topic knowledge, is the usual bottleneck. Non-calculator fluency is assumed in parts of both specifications.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and the moment-and-equilibrium questions are where Extended candidates reliably drop marks. Practical skills are examined on a written paper rather than in a laboratory, which rewards students who have practised reading apparatus diagrams and spotting the controlled variable.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles and reacting-mass calculations are the single largest source of lost marks, followed by qualitative analysis tests described imprecisely. Students who learn the ionic equations as patterns rather than as recipes answer unfamiliar questions far better.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A content-volume subject where precise terminology decides the band. Diffusion and osmosis answers lose marks for omitting the word concentration gradient; genetics questions lose them for incomplete Punnett square notation. Data questions reward reading the axes before the stem.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and the extended response carry most of the marks, and the common failure is writing well in the wrong register for the stated audience. Reading questions require quotation plus comment rather than quotation alone.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A different course from English Language with different papers, and students entered for the wrong one lose far more than a few marks. Listening and speaking components need rehearsal, not revision. Accuracy in writing outweighs ambition in vocabulary.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Case-study subjects where command terms govern the mark. An answer that explains when the question said evaluate caps itself in the lower bands however accurate the content. Numerical questions on ratios and elasticity need separate drilling from the written ones.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Algorithm and pseudocode questions reward a consistent, legible convention more than clever code. Data representation and networking answers need exact vocabulary. The practical component in ICT is a skills examination and improves with repetition rather than with reading.

subjects.name: Arabic and the UAE mandatory subjects
subjects.description: KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. These grades sit on the report card beside IGCSE subjects and are frequently the weakest line for a family that arrived mid-phase.

sections.heading: Which series your child sits, and why the March one does not apply here
paragraphs: This is the first thing to establish and the thing most tutoring pages get wrong. Cambridge International examines IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series. It also runs a February and March series, which is offered to India only. A candidate sitting in Dubai sits June, with November as the resit and alternative route. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. If a tutor, a website or a revision plan refers your Dubai child to a March examination window, that plan was written for a different country.

The second thing to establish is the board, because parents routinely do not know it and the papers differ. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel are separate qualifications with separate syllabus codes, separate paper structures and separate tiering conventions. Cambridge splits many subjects into Core and Extended; Pearson uses Foundation and Higher tiers in some subjects and a single tier in others, and offers modular assessment in several specifications where Cambridge does not. A tutor who teaches 0580 fluently is not automatically fluent in 4MA1, and the past papers are not interchangeable.

Both boards allocate centres to administrative zones and publish a timetable version per zone. Cambridge's exams officers guide states that every centre is allocated to one of six zones, that it is essential the correct version is used, and that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination because the wrong one was followed. Your school manages this. The reason it belongs on this page is that it explains why a start time you read on a forum may not match your child's, and why the school's own published timetable is the only one to revise against.

sections.heading: The Year 11 year counted backwards from the June series
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes this table, which is odd, because the sequence it shows is the entire basis on which a family should decide when to start tutoring. Work from the bottom up. The series dates are fixed by the board. Study leave is fixed by the school. Mocks sit a term before study leave because predicted grades depend on them. Entries, including tier decisions, close well before any of it. Coursework and practical deadlines sit earlier still.

The consequence is that the useful starting point for tutoring is not the same for every goal. A family trying to move a borderline grade needs to be in before the mock block, because mocks set predicted grades and predicted grades affect sixth-form and Diploma offers. A family trying to secure a specific grade for a specific post-16 route can start later and still succeed, because the final ten weeks are the highest-yield weeks for paper technique. A family trying to change a tier decision has the tightest deadline of all, and it is usually earlier than they think.

One thing to avoid: building a revision plan around dates copied from a website. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, and Cambridge zone versions differ. Treat your child's school timetable as the authority and the board's live timetable page as the backup. What the table below gives you is the order of events and what should be finished by each one, which does not change from year to year even when the dates do.

sections.heading: What the next eight weeks can actually deliver in an IGCSE subject
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the block most families here commit to, and in IGCSE it buys more than it does at Diploma level, because the papers are more pattern-driven. A student who understands the chemistry but cannot lay out a moles calculation can move a full grade in that time. A student who has never properly met half of the Extended specification cannot, and a tutor who implies otherwise is selling hope at an hourly rate.

What works is narrow. Pick the two or three topics that recur most heavily across recent papers for that syllabus code and that the student currently fails, and work only on those until the failure stops. In Cambridge 0580 that is usually algebraic manipulation and multi-step problems; in 0620 it is moles and qualitative analysis; in 0625 it is circuits and moments. The temptation to re-teach the whole course in eight weeks is the single most common way a block gets wasted.

The other half is what happens between sessions. One hour a week is a rounding error in a student's time; the session has to change the other six days. Each of ours ends with a specific task and a named output — three past-paper questions attempted under timing and self-marked against the official mark scheme, with the student's own corrections brought to the next session. Families who treat the hour as the whole intervention get a fraction of the result families who treat it as a weekly planning meeting get.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition costs in Dubai, cheapest tier first
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market rather than the top, because that is where most families start looking. Budget online tutoring, commonly delivered by university students, advertises from around AED 33 to AED 65 an hour, with Tutopiya publishing from AED 33 to AED 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65. That tier can be genuinely useful for homework supervision and for keeping a Year 9 student moving. It is a poor fit for an Extended-tier paper eight weeks out, because the thing you are buying at that point is examination judgement rather than subject knowledge.

The next tier up is where most IGCSE tutoring actually happens: a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Above that, subject specialists in IB, IGCSE and A Level are quoted from AED 200 to AED 450 and beyond, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home one-to-one visits run AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is included, and a premium named tutor has been advertised at AED 650 an hour. Monthly packages in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour home visits.

Every figure in those two paragraphs belongs to the company or rate guide that published it, read in October 2026. They are not IB Gram's prices, and we do not publish an hourly list on these pages, because the right number depends on the subject, the level and how many weeks remain. What a parent should take away is the shape of the market: the step from AED 65 to AED 200 buys subject depth, and the step from AED 200 online to AED 400 in-home mostly buys a car journey down Al Qudra Road.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor off Al Qudra Road against an online specialist
paragraphs: The case for a tutor in the room is real and worth stating before the argument against it. Some students focus better with an adult physically present, and a reluctant fifteen-year-old does treat a laptop differently from a person sitting at the same table. Compass-and-ruler constructions, diagram labelling and handwriting legibility are all easier to correct when someone can point at the page. For a student who has to be kept at the desk as much as taught, physical presence does part of the work.

The case against, in this neighbourhood specifically, is traffic and supply. A tutor travelling to The Sustainable City is on Al Qudra Road or the E311 in the late afternoon, and that journey is unpredictable in exactly the hours a Year 11 student should be working. The cost appears as a higher hourly rate, a two-hour minimum, or a cancelled session. More importantly it narrows the choice of tutor to those willing to make the drive, and in Extended-tier maths and the separate sciences that pool is thin in this part of Dubai.

Our position is not neutral and should not be read as such. IB Gram delivers online one-to-one only and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE. The argument we would make to a parent here is that the model buys subject match instead of proximity: a Year 11 student entered for Cambridge 0625 gets a tutor who teaches 0625, rather than a generalist who happens to live fifteen minutes away. The table compares models rather than companies, with the travel column written for this community.

sections.heading: Coursework, practicals and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: Several IGCSE subjects carry non-examination assessment, and a few in this market will offer to do it for your child. That offer should be refused every time. Work submitted under a board's coursework rules must be the student's own, authenticated by the school, and a submission that is not is a malpractice matter with consequences that land on the candidate rather than on whoever was paid. One operation in this market sells completed Internal Assessments for a different qualification at AED 3,750; the same logic and the same risk apply to IGCSE coursework.

The boundary is workable once it is said out loud. A tutor may teach the content a coursework task draws on, explain the assessment criteria, question whether a method is reproducible, point out an unsupported conclusion, and comment on writing the student produced. A tutor may not write any part of the submission, redraft a paragraph into final form, select and carry out the investigation, or provide a model to be edited. Our test is whether a sentence in the final submission exists because a tutor wrote it.

Practical science assessment at IGCSE is examined on paper in both boards' international specifications, which is good news for an online tutor and worth understanding properly. What is assessed is the ability to read apparatus diagrams, identify variables, criticise a method, and handle results tables and graphs — all of which can be taught and practised over a screen using the boards' own past papers. What cannot be replicated online is laboratory handling, and that is the school's job rather than a tutor's.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory subjects and what equivalency actually requires
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. The scale is worth knowing: 227 private schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25 across 17 curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37% of enrolment. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for the following academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package.

Two regulator facts change an IGCSE family's planning. First, KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and combined classes prohibited; instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Those subjects sit on the report alongside IGCSEs. Second, for UAE university plans, Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade.

That five-subject figure is worth stating precisely because a ranking competitor publishes six. Equivalency and attestation are processes your family manages with the Ministry, not services a tutoring company performs or guarantees, and nobody should imply that tutoring is required for them. On the tutoring side, the honest statement is the narrow one: IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, no ADEK or Ministry approval, no Cambridge or Pearson partnership and no UAE office. An individual tutoring privately in the UAE needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued free of charge for two years.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the Gulf week and protecting a Year 11 slot
paragraphs: A revision plan that ignores the UAE calendar is abandoned by week three. The working week runs Monday to Friday with a half-day Friday, which leaves Saturday and Sunday as the only full days and also as the days families travel and host. During Ramadan, school hours shorten and the productive study window moves to the evening; a session after Iftar often works better than any afternoon slot, and scheduling against a fasting teenager's afternoon is a waste of an hour.

Position in the community changes what is possible. A student at school inside The Sustainable City is home early enough for a 3.30pm or 4pm session, which is the band where concentration is still available. A student travelling to Motor City, Dubai Sports City or Arabian Ranches is realistically not available until 5.30pm, and in a sports-heavy household that slot competes with training four evenings a week. The Year 11 families who succeed are the ones who decide in September which evening belongs to tutoring and then defend it.

We hold slots in Gulf Standard Time, move them to post-Iftar timing through Ramadan without changing tutor, and pause blocks during a school's own examination fortnight when adding sessions produces fatigue rather than marks. What we will not do is shuffle a student between tutors to keep a diary full. For a Year 11 student eight weeks from a series, continuity with one tutor who already knows which questions go wrong is worth more than a perfectly packed calendar.

process.title: Name the board and the series
process.description: The first useful message tells us Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel, the subject, the tier if one applies, and which series your child is entered for. If you do not know the board, the school's examinations officer does, and finding out before the first session saves an hour of the wrong past papers.

process.title: A short diagnostic conversation
process.description: Fifteen minutes on what has been sat, what the last marked paper scored, which topics are avoided and what the school has predicted. Specific answers produce a specific first session. This is also where we say plainly whether the time remaining supports the grade you are aiming at.

process.title: A free trial lesson on a real topic
process.description: Run by the tutor who would continue, on a genuine weakness rather than a demonstration topic, ending with that tutor naming what they would tackle first and why. If the match is wrong, tell us and we will propose a different tutor rather than defend the first one.

process.title: A written plan built backwards from a date
process.description: You receive the sequence of sessions, the between-session work, and the date it is all counted back from, whether that is the mock block or the series. It is specific enough to disagree with, which is the point; a plan nobody can challenge is a plan nobody owns.

process.title: Weekly sessions and a note each time
process.description: Every session ends with a written note: covered, fixed, still weak, owed before next week. Progress shows up as the same question type stopping going wrong, not as a satisfaction score. If four weeks pass without that happening, we change the method or the tutor.

whyPoints.title: Matched to a syllabus code, not a subject name
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different papers with different conventions, and past papers do not transfer between them. Because delivery is online, your child is matched to someone who teaches their specific code rather than to whoever is nearby.

whyPoints.title: The calendar drives the plan
whyPoints.description: Sessions are sequenced from the school's mock block, coursework deadlines and the board's series rather than from a generic revision schedule. For a Year 11 student that is the difference between arriving before predicted grades are set and arriving after.

whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page belongs to the company or rate guide that published it, dated to when it was read. We publish no invented statistics, no self-asserted ratings and no price we have not quoted you for your child's actual subject.

whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question and critique the student's own work. They do not write, redraft to completion or supply assessed material, and we will not source it. Feedback is recorded in case the school asks what external support was received.

whyPoints.description: If the weeks remaining do not support the grade you want, we say so and discuss the November series as a planned route instead of a failure. A booking taken on an unachievable target damages the student more than it helps the business.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE exams held for a student at school in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International examines IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and its February and March series is offered to India only, so it is not open to a candidate sitting in Dubai. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Both boards split centres into administrative zones with separate timetable versions, so your child's exact dates come from the school rather than from a general timetable. Treat the school's published timetable as the authority and the board's live timetable page as the backup.

faqs.question: How do we find out whether our child sits Cambridge or Edexcel IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's examinations officer, not the subject teacher, and ask for the syllabus code rather than the subject name. A Cambridge mathematics entry will be 0580; the Pearson equivalent is 4MA1. The codes matter because the papers, the tiering and in some subjects the option of modular assessment differ between the boards, and past papers are not interchangeable. Booking a tutor without knowing the code risks spending the first sessions on the wrong question style, which is an expensive way to discover an administrative detail.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Core and Extended in a Cambridge subject?
faqs.answer: Core and Extended are different papers covering different amounts of the syllabus, with different grade ceilings: Core caps the achievable grade, while Extended reaches the top grades but contains harder content. The choice is an entry decision made by the school ahead of the board's entry deadline, not something adjustable in the examination hall. In practice, Year 10 internal results are where a realistic view is formed. If a family wants to keep Extended open in a subject, the work has to happen in Year 10 rather than in the final terms.

faqs.question: Will an IGCSE tutor come to our home in The Sustainable City?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE, and no tutor will arrive at an address in this community. Lessons are one-to-one and live over video, with past-paper questions shared on screen and a recording available on request. Home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. The benefit here is that a Year 11 student entered for a specific syllabus code gets a tutor who teaches that code, instead of whichever generalist is willing to drive down Al Qudra Road at five in the afternoon.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE tutor cost in Dubai at the cheaper end?
faqs.answer: Published budget rates in this market start at around AED 33 to AED 65 an hour, with Tutopiya advertising from AED 33 to AED 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65, usually delivered by university students. That tier suits homework supervision rather than examination judgement. Qualified subject tutors working online sit at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Those are market figures read in October 2026, not our prices; we quote after a free trial against your child's actual subject, board and tier.

faqs.question: Is it worth entering the November series if a June grade disappoints?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the decision is time-pressured because a November entry closes months before the papers. It is usually worth it when the gap is one or two marks' worth of technique in a subject that a post-16 route specifically requires, and rarely worth it when the student has moved on to a programme that does not need that grade. Pearson's published history gives a sense of timing: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Ask the school about entry deadlines the week results arrive, not a month later.

faqs.question: How are science practicals assessed if our child only studies online with a tutor?
faqs.answer: In both boards' international IGCSE specifications, practical skills are assessed on a written paper rather than in a laboratory. What that paper tests — reading apparatus diagrams, identifying independent and controlled variables, criticising a method, handling results tables and plotting graphs — can be taught and practised over a screen using the boards' own past papers. Actual laboratory handling remains the school's responsibility. So an online tutor can genuinely prepare a student for the practical paper, which is the component the grade depends on.

faqs.question: My son is in Year 10 and coasting. Is it too early for tutoring?
faqs.answer: It is the cheapest time to start. Year 10 is where IGCSE content is met for the first time, where coursework components begin in several subjects, and where internal results feed tier and entry decisions for Year 11. Fixing algebraic fluency or calculation layout before it meets examination questions costs a fraction of unpicking it under deadline pressure a year later. One weekly session through Year 10, sequenced against the school's topic order, usually removes the need for an intensive block in the final terms.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we tutor at once for a Year 11 student?
faqs.answer: One, in most cases, and two only where there is a real reason. A Year 11 student already has school, coursework, the mandatory UAE subjects and usually sport; adding three weekly tutoring hours produces fatigue and a student who prepares for nothing properly. The better approach is to identify the subject where the grade gap costs the most for the post-16 route being targeted, fix that, and then reassess. We would rather start at one session a week and increase it when a diagnosis justifies it.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education included in the five IGCSE subjects the Ministry counts?
faqs.answer: No, and the rule is specific enough to be worth stating. Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. A separate requirement covers Advanced Level: one subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong. Verify current rules on moe.gov.ae, because equivalency is a process your family manages rather than a service we perform.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan without losing the tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we recommend planning for it rather than reacting to it. School hours shorten during Ramadan and the productive study window moves to the evening, so a post-Iftar session is often the most useful hour of the day for a fasting teenager. The slot moves and the tutor stays, because continuity with someone who already knows which questions go wrong is worth more than a tidy calendar. The same applies to a school's own examination fortnight, when pausing usually serves a student better than adding sessions.

faqs.question: What if our child needs a subject you do not cover well?
faqs.answer: We will say so rather than fill the slot. Coverage is strong in mathematics, the three separate sciences, English Language, English as a Second Language, Business Studies, Economics, Computer Science and ICT across both boards. It thins in some modern foreign languages and in a few minority subjects, and in those cases we tell you what we can offer, how long a match would take, and when availability is likely. A tutor who is a year out of date on a specification is worse for a Year 11 student than a clear no.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a UAE licence, and can we verify it?
faqs.answer: An individual providing private tuition in the UAE needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so be sceptical of any specific figure quoted online. Ask a tutor directly, and ask any UAE agency how it verifies permits.

faqs.question: How quickly can a first session happen after we get in touch?
faqs.answer: For mainstream subjects on either board, usually within a few days: a short diagnostic conversation, then a free trial lesson with the tutor who would continue, then a written plan. Niche subjects and unusual tier combinations take longer, and we will tell you how long rather than book a placeholder. If the deadline is close enough that waiting matters, say so in the first message, because that changes which tutors we approach and in what order.

faqs.question: Why should we believe a page like this rather than a tutoring site with reviews?
faqs.answer: Judge it on whether the claims are checkable. Every AED figure here names who published it and when it was read. The series information comes from Cambridge's and Pearson's own timetable pages. The equivalency rule is quoted at five subjects because that is what the published source says. We publish no star rating, no satisfaction percentage and no improvement statistic, because figures without a sample size, a date and a method are marketing. Several competitors in this market publish self-asserted ratings that differ from their own page text.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-sustainabl.closingHeading: Tell us the board, the subject and the date
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-sustainabl.closingBody: If your child is in Year 10 or Year 11 in or around The Sustainable City, the most useful first message names three things: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel, the subject and tier, and the date everything is counted back from. We will arrange a free trial lesson with the tutor who would actually teach, then send a short written plan built backwards from that date. Lessons are one-to-one and live over video to this community, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with no home visits anywhere in the UAE. If the weeks remaining do not support the grade you are aiming at, we will say so before you book anything.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-valley.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects to students living in The Valley and the communities along the Al Ain road. Each is matched to a syllabus code and tier, because the two boards differ in paper structure, tiering and calculator rules.

intro.heading: Two directions, several schools, and two different exam boards
paragraphs: The Valley sits at the southern edge of Dubai along the road to Al Ain, and at the time of writing it has no school inside its own boundary. Every school run from here goes outward, in one of two broad directions: towards Dubai Silicon Oasis, Academic City and Nad Al Sheba, or across the Dubailand corridor towards Arabian Ranches and Mira. That produces a situation families in older communities do not face — the neighbours' children are at different schools, on different assessment calendars, and sometimes on different exam boards entirely.

For IGCSE that last point is the one that costs money. Cambridge International Mathematics is 0580; the Pearson Edexcel equivalent is 4MA1. They are separate qualifications with separate paper structures, separate tiering conventions and, in the current Cambridge specification, different calculator arrangements. Past papers are not interchangeable. A parent in The Valley who assumes the board from a neighbour's conversation can easily buy a tutor who teaches the wrong specification, and the first two sessions are then spent on the wrong question style.

The second thing this community changes is time. Adding a commute at both ends of a full school day pushes the first realistic session to about half past five for a secondary student. That matters for a Year 11 student who has mock examinations in view, because a slot agreed at four in the afternoon because it sounds better will be abandoned inside a fortnight. The structures that survive here are one protected weekday evening and a weekend block, not two weekday hours.

The honest answer on home tutoring itself begins with published figures. In-home one-to-one visits in Dubai are advertised at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. For a community at the city's southern edge, a good part of that gap is a long peak-direction drive rather than a difference in teaching. It also shows up as a two-hour minimum booking and as cancellations when the road fails.

So, stated before anything else: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and nobody will arrive at an address in The Valley. Lessons are one-to-one and live over video, with past-paper questions on screen, a shared whiteboard and an optional recording. Household visits exist in our India operation only. What the model buys here is a tutor chosen for the syllabus code your child sits rather than for a willingness to drive the Al Ain road at five in the afternoon. It also removes the two unpaid journeys at either end of a visit, which is what makes an early-evening start possible at all in a household where the school run has already taken an hour out of the day.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-valley.programmesIntro: Families here are at one of three points, and in a community where children attend several different schools the right question is which stage your own child is at rather than what the neighbourhood is doing.

programmes.name: Year 9, before the course begins
programmes.description: Nothing is externally assessed, so the gaps that matter later are invisible. The ones that cost IGCSE marks are specific and narrow: rearranging a formula, handling negatives and fractions, reading a question closely enough to notice what it asks, and writing an explanation that gives a reason. All are cheap to close at this stage.
programmes.countryNote: The Valley fills largely with families moving within Dubai or arriving in the emirate, which means mid-phase school changes are common. A child joining a British-curriculum school in Year 9 from another system usually has two or three specific missing topics rather than a general weakness, and a diagnostic before the IGCSE course starts is the cheapest intervention available.

programmes.name: Year 10, the first IGCSE year
programmes.description: Content arrives for the first time and coursework begins in some subjects. Internal examinations at the end of the year feed tier and entry decisions for Year 11. The signal that something has slipped is precise: a student who cannot do last term's work now, rather than one finding this term's work hard.
programmes.countryNote: Because Valley students attend several different schools, the point at which tier decisions are taken varies between households in the same street. A family hoping to keep Extended or Higher tier open in a subject should ask its own school when entries close rather than assuming the neighbourhood timetable applies to them.

programmes.name: Year 11, the examination year
programmes.description: One mock block, entry deadlines months ahead of the papers, predicted grades drawn from the mocks, then study leave and the series. Both boards report on the 9 to 1 scale. Nearly all measurable improvement in this year comes from technique rather than new content, because technique is what has not been practised.
programmes.countryNote: The commute is the practical constraint for Year 11 students here. A protected weekday evening slot plus a weekend block for whole papers is the structure that lasts; two weekday hours in a commuting household usually ends with the second being cancelled and the between-session work left undone.

programmes.name: After the results
programmes.description: IGCSE grades act as thresholds for A Level or IB Higher Level study, and schools set their own requirements, often per subject rather than overall. A student heading for a mathematics-heavy route needs one named grade in one named subject, which is a far narrower and cheaper target than lifting a whole profile.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE university plans, Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects. Verify current rules on moe.gov.ae.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-valley.subjectsIntro: The subjects Valley families ask about most, with syllabus codes where they help and the specific failure that recurs. Booking against a named paper and a named weakness is faster than booking against a subject.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Method marks sit on nearly every multi-step question and students who write only an answer forfeit them. Algebraic manipulation is the bottleneck far more often than any single topic, and the current Cambridge specification includes assessment without a calculator.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Circuits, moments and equilibrium questions are where higher-tier candidates reliably drop marks. A large share of physics losses are mathematical rather than scientific, which is a diagnosable distinction from a marked paper.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles and reacting-mass calculations cost the most marks, followed by qualitative analysis answers written imprecisely. Students who learn ionic equations as patterns rather than recipes handle unfamiliar questions considerably better.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume rather than difficulty is the problem and terminology precision decides the band. Osmosis answers lose marks for omitting concentration gradient; enzyme answers lose them for saying killed rather than denatured.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and the extended response carry most of the marks, and the recurring failure is strong writing in the wrong register for the stated audience. Reading questions need quotation plus comment, never quotation alone.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A separate qualification from English Language with different papers, and an incorrect entry costs far more than a few marks. Listening and speaking components need rehearsal rather than revision, and accuracy outranks ambitious vocabulary.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Command terms govern the ceiling more than content does. An answer that explains where the question said evaluate caps itself whatever its accuracy. Ratio and elasticity calculations need drilling separately from the written responses.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Algorithm and pseudocode questions reward a consistent, legible convention more than clever code. The ICT practical component is a skills examination and improves with repetition rather than with reading about it.

subjects.name: Arabic and the UAE mandatory subjects
subjects.description: KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. These grades sit beside IGCSE subjects on the report and often slip for mid-phase arrivals.

sections.heading: Establish the board before you book anybody
paragraphs: In a community where children attend schools in two different directions, this is the single most useful piece of administration a parent can do. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel are separate qualifications. Cambridge mathematics is 0580 with Core and Extended tiers; the Pearson equivalent is 4MA1 with Foundation and Higher tiers and two two-hour papers of 100 marks each. The sciences follow the same pattern: 0610, 0620 and 0625 against 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1.

The practical differences are not cosmetic. Cambridge papers tend to carry more, shorter questions moving quickly between topics, which penalises a student slow to switch context. Pearson papers more often build several parts on one scenario, which penalises a student who loses the thread between parts. The current Cambridge specification includes assessment without a calculator, while Pearson permits one throughout its two papers. A student revising from the wrong board's past papers is practising the wrong skill.

Ask the school's examinations officer rather than the subject teacher, and ask for the code rather than the subject name. It takes a day to establish and it determines which past papers every session uses for the next two years. In The Valley specifically, do not infer the board from a neighbour: the child next door may be at a school in an entirely different direction, entered for an entirely different specification in the same subject. The table below is the short version to take into that conversation with the school.

sections.heading: What the two school-run directions do to a tutoring plan
paragraphs: This is the comparison that actually applies to The Valley, because it is the one that decides whether a session happens at all. Families travelling towards Silicon Oasis, Academic City or Nad Al Sheba face one set of timings; families crossing the Dubailand corridor towards Arabian Ranches or Mira face another. Both are long at four in the afternoon, and both mean a student is home later than the school day's published end time suggests.

The consequence is structural rather than motivational. A Year 11 student who arrives home at a quarter past five has perhaps forty minutes before a tutoring session becomes an imposition rather than an opportunity, and in a household with siblings on different runs the practical window is narrower still. Plans that assume a 4pm start in this community are not optimistic; they are describing a different neighbourhood. The honest planning position is one weekday evening and a weekend block.

There is one upside worth naming. Because the weekday window is tight, families here tend to use weekends properly, and weekend sessions suit the highest-value IGCSE work: whole papers under timing, mark-scheme dissection, and practical paper practice. A student who does one weekday hour on content and one weekend block on papers is running a better programme than a student in a shorter-commute community doing two unfocused weekday hours. sections.heading: The in-home premium, taken apart
paragraphs: Most providers fold travel into the hourly rate without mentioning it, which makes an in-home quote look like a premium for quality when a good part of it is a premium for distance. The published Dubai in-home band is AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, with Bestimate quoting AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors AED 200 to AED 500. A qualified subject tutor working online is published at AED 150 to AED 300, and budget online tutoring at AED 33 to AED 65, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65.

For a community at the southern edge of the city the gap is mostly the journey, and it shows up in three further ways. A tutor making a long round trip will reasonably want a two-hour minimum, so a family needing one focused hour buys two. They will want the slot that suits their route rather than your child's concentration. And when the road fails the session is cancelled rather than shortened. Those are consequences of distance, not failings, and a parent should see them before week three.

What the premium genuinely buys is physical presence, which matters for younger children, for ruler and compass work, and for a student who treats a laptop differently from an adult at the table. For a Year 11 student working through a past paper, it buys very little that a shared whiteboard and a screen-shared question do not already provide. sections.heading: The grade that decides the next course
paragraphs: IGCSE is a gateway qualification and the gate is narrow. Schools in Dubai set their own entry requirements for A Level and IB Higher Level subjects, usually in the top bands and sometimes with a condition on the Extended or Higher tier paper rather than on the overall grade. A student aiming at A Level Mathematics or Analysis and Approaches needs one named grade in one named subject, which is a much smaller problem than lifting nine subjects by half a grade.

That narrowness is useful because it tells a family where to spend. Ask the head of sixth form or the Diploma coordinator for the threshold in writing while there is still time to act on it. In The Valley the answer varies by household, because children here attend several different schools with different thresholds, so one neighbour's requirement tells you nothing reliable about your own child's. This is one more area where the community's spread of schools makes direct enquiry necessary.

There is a separate minimum worth knowing for UAE university plans. Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from the count, plus one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. One ranking competitor publishes six subjects, which is wrong. That is a floor, not a competitive standard, and equivalency is a process your family manages with the Ministry.

sections.heading: What eight weeks can do, and what it cannot
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the commonest commitment and in IGCSE it buys more than at Diploma level, because the papers are more strongly patterned. A student who understands the chemistry but cannot lay out a moles calculation can move a full grade in that time. A student who has never properly met half an Extended specification cannot, and a tutor implying otherwise is selling hope by the hour. The target has to be set in the first conversation rather than the sixth week.

The work that pays is narrow. Pick the two or three topics that recur most heavily in recent papers for that specific syllabus code and that the student currently fails, and stay on them until the failure stops. In Cambridge 0580 that is usually algebraic manipulation and multi-step problems; in 0620 it is moles and qualitative analysis; in 0625 it is circuits and moments. Re-teaching a whole course in eight weeks is the standard way a block gets wasted.

The other half is what happens between sessions, and in a commuting household this is where plans fail. One tutored hour is roughly one per cent of a student's week, so the hour has to change what the other days contain. Each session here ends with a named output: three past-paper questions attempted under timing and self-marked against the official scheme, with the student's own corrections brought back. A family treating the hour as the whole intervention gets a fraction of the result.

sections.heading: Coursework, practicals and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: Several IGCSE subjects carry assessed work completed outside the examination hall, and parts of this market will offer to complete it for your child. That offer should be refused without discussion. Work submitted under a board's rules must be the student's own and is authenticated by the school; a submission that is not is a malpractice matter whose consequences fall on the candidate. One operation in this market sells completed internal assessments for a different qualification at AED 3,750, which tells you both that the trade exists and what it costs.

The boundary is workable once stated plainly. A tutor may teach the content a task draws on, explain the assessment criteria, question whether a method is reproducible, point out a conclusion that outruns the evidence, and comment on writing the student produced. A tutor may not write any part of a submission, redraft a paragraph into final form, select and carry out an investigation, or provide a model to be edited. The test is whether a sentence in the final piece exists because a tutor wrote it.

Practical science in both boards' international specifications is examined on a written paper rather than assessed in a laboratory, which has a useful consequence here. Everything that paper tests — reading apparatus diagrams, identifying independent and controlled variables, criticising a method, completing results tables, plotting graphs — can be taught over a screen using the boards' own past questions. Laboratory handling stays with the school, and no online tutor should claim otherwise.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory subjects and what we do not claim
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. The market is substantial: 227 private schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25 across 17 curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37% of enrolment. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for the following academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package.

Two regulator facts bear directly on an IGCSE plan. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and combined classes prohibited; instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Those lessons are part of why a Year 11 week has less room than a tutoring plan assumes. The emirate also determines the regulator: ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

On our own standing the position is narrow and deliberate. IB Gram holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, no ADEK or Ministry approval, no Cambridge or Pearson partnership, and no office, branch or centre in the UAE. An individual providing private tuition in the UAE needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, and those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure quoted online with suspicion.

sections.heading: Scheduling around the commute, Ramadan and the Gulf week
paragraphs: A revision plan in this community is abandoned for scheduling reasons far more often than for teaching ones. The UAE working week runs Monday to Friday with a half-day Friday, which leaves Saturday and Sunday as the only full days and also as the days families travel and host. Add an outbound school run at both ends of the day and the number of genuinely usable weekday evenings is usually one, not four.

During Ramadan school hours shorten and the productive study window moves to the evening. For a Valley student with a long commute, a post-Iftar session is frequently the most useful hour available in that month, while an afternoon slot is largely wasted on a tired, fasting teenager. Planning for that in advance works considerably better than reacting to it in the second week, and the slot can move while the tutor stays the same.

Our side is straightforward. Slots are held in Gulf Standard Time and can sit wherever in the evening the household needs; they move after Iftar through Ramadan with the same tutor retained; and a block can pause during a school's own examination fortnight, when adding sessions produces fatigue rather than marks. What we will not do is move a student between tutors to fill a diary, because for a Year 11 student continuity with someone who already knows which questions go wrong is worth more than a full calendar, and rebuilding that knowledge with somebody new takes weeks the examination year does not have.

faqs.question: Will one of your tutors come to our house in The Valley?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE, and nobody will arrive at an address in The Valley. Lessons are one-to-one and live over video, with past-paper questions on screen, a shared whiteboard and an optional recording. Home tutoring is a service we operate in India only. The gain in a community at the city's southern edge is substantial: your child is matched to a tutor who teaches their exact syllabus code rather than to whoever will drive the Al Ain road at five in the afternoon.

faqs.question: How do we find out which exam board our child's school uses?
faqs.answer: Email the school's examinations officer, not the subject teacher, and ask for the syllabus code rather than the subject name. Cambridge mathematics is 0580 and the Pearson equivalent is 4MA1; the sciences are 0610, 0620 and 0625 against 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. In The Valley this matters more than in older communities, because children here attend schools in two different directions and a neighbour's answer may be entirely irrelevant to your own child's entry.

faqs.question: Why is a 4pm tutoring slot unrealistic in this community?
faqs.answer: Because there is no school inside The Valley at the time of writing, so every school run is outbound and a commute is added at both ends of a full day. A secondary student is realistically home around a quarter past five, which makes 5.30pm the first honest start. A slot agreed at 4pm because it sounds better tends to be abandoned within a fortnight. The structures that survive here are one protected weekday evening and a weekend block for whole-paper work.

faqs.question: How much of an in-home tutoring rate is the drive?
faqs.answer: A significant share. Published Dubai figures put in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. For a long peak-direction run to the city's southern edge, much of that gap is distance rather than teaching quality. It also appears as two-hour minimum bookings and as cancellations when the road fails. Those figures were read in October 2026 and belong to the companies that published them.

faqs.question: Does the Cambridge March series apply to a student in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge International's February and March series is offered to India only, so a candidate sitting in Dubai is not entered for it. UAE candidates sit the June series, with November available as the resit and alternative route. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. If a revision plan, a website or a tutor refers your child to a March examination window, that plan was written for a different country and its dates should not be acted on.

faqs.question: Which year should we start tutoring in for the best value?
faqs.answer: Year 10, as early in it as possible. Fixing algebraic fluency or calculation layout while content is still new takes a handful of sessions; the same gap discovered in the final terms has to be closed while five other subjects compete for the hours and a predicted grade is already recorded. The gap itself does not change, only the cost of closing it. Starting in Year 10 usually removes the need for an intensive block in the examination year altogether, which is the cheaper outcome.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor prepare our son for the science practical paper?
faqs.answer: Yes, completely, because in both boards' international specifications practical skills are examined on a written paper rather than assessed in a laboratory. That paper asks students to identify independent and controlled variables, read apparatus diagrams, criticise a method and suggest improvements with their effects, complete results tables with correct units, plot graphs and comment on anomalies. All of it can be practised over a screen from the boards' own past questions. Laboratory handling remains the school's responsibility.

faqs.question: Our daughter has two subjects she is worried about. Should we tutor both?
faqs.answer: Usually one first, and in this community that is partly a logistics answer. A Year 11 student here already has a long school day, the KHDA-mandated Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies lessons and often a sport, so two tutored hours plus the between-session work for both is more than the week holds. Identify the subject where the grade gap most affects the intended post-16 route, address that, and reassess after a month. Two half-used engagements achieve less than one used properly.

faqs.question: Is a weekend session as effective as a weekday one?
faqs.answer: For IGCSE, often more so, and in a commuting household it is frequently the better option. Whole papers under timing, mark-scheme dissection and practical paper practice all need uninterrupted time rather than a squeezed evening hour, and that time genuinely exists only at the weekend here. A student doing one weekday hour on content and one weekend block on papers is running a better programme than one doing two tired weekday hours in a shorter-commute community.

faqs.question: What grade does my child need for A Level Maths?
faqs.answer: That is set by your child's own school rather than by the board, usually in the top bands and sometimes with a condition on the higher tier paper specifically rather than the overall grade. Ask the head of sixth form for the threshold in writing while there is still time to act on it. In The Valley the answer genuinely varies between neighbours, because children here attend several different schools with different thresholds, so one family's requirement tells you nothing reliable about another's.

faqs.question: We moved here mid-year and our son is behind in two subjects. How bad is that?
faqs.answer: Usually less bad than it looks. Schools teach the same specifications in different topic orders, so a mid-year arrival typically has two or three genuinely unmet topics and two or three covered twice, rather than a general weakness. A short diagnostic names which, and the gap often closes within a term. The important thing is doing it in the first term rather than the examination year, when the identical repair has to compete with five other subjects and a mock block.

faqs.question: Do you cover English as a Second Language as well as English Language?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they are genuinely different qualifications rather than easier and harder versions of one. Cambridge English as a Second Language is 0510 or 0511 with its own papers including listening and speaking components, while English Language is 0500 or 0990. A student entered for the wrong one loses far more than a few marks. Listening and speaking need rehearsal rather than revision, and accuracy outranks ambitious vocabulary throughout. Confirm with the examinations officer which your child is entered for.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan without changing tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and planning for it beats reacting to it. School hours shorten during Ramadan and the productive window moves to the evening, so for a student with a long commute a post-Iftar session is often the most useful hour of the day while an afternoon slot is largely wasted. The slot moves and the tutor stays, because continuity with someone who already knows which questions go wrong is worth more than a tidy calendar. The same applies during a school's own examination fortnight.

faqs.question: If we get in touch this week, when could lessons realistically start?
faqs.answer: For mainstream subjects on either board, usually within a few days: a short diagnostic conversation, a free trial lesson with the tutor who would continue, then a written plan anchored to a date. Less common subjects and unusual tier combinations take longer, and we will say how long rather than book a placeholder session. If a school deadline makes the timing urgent, say so in the first message, because it changes which tutors we approach and in what order.

faqs.question: Why does this page not show reviews or a success rate?
faqs.answer: Because a figure without a sample size, a date and a method is a marketing claim rather than evidence. Several providers in this market publish self-asserted ratings that differ from their own page text, and one shows a review count that cannot be reconciled with its stated student numbers. Self-serving review markup is also a structured-data policy problem. What this page publishes instead is checkable: AED figures with their publisher and the month read, and regulator descriptions quoted from u.ae.

intro.heading: Nine subjects, two free evenings, and the choice nobody explains
paragraphs: The honest answer first, because it shapes everything after it. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in The Views or anywhere else in the UAE; visiting students at home is something we do in India only. For a family in Fairways, Travo, Turia, Mosela, Panorama, Golf Towers or The Links, lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the same tutor each week and a written note afterwards.

The reason that arrangement wins here has little to do with technology and everything to do with arithmetic. A Year 10 student in this community carries eight or nine IGCSE subjects. Each one has homework. Each one has a mock in January and a terminal paper in May or June. The school day ends and the bus reaches Emirates Living somewhere between 15:40 and 16:20 depending on the route, and from that point there are roughly four usable hours before a teenager stops absorbing anything. Mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education homework takes one of them. Dinner and a sibling take another.

What is left is two, maybe three, genuinely free weekday evenings in a seven-day week. That is the budget. Every decision a Views parent makes about tutoring is a decision about how to spend it, and the question is not which tutor is best in general but which single subject moves furthest per hour spent. A tutor arriving by car at 18:15 after finding a visitor bay has already spent part of that budget before the first question is asked.

This page is written around that constraint. It maps the real Views weekday hour by hour. It works through which of nine subjects repays funding first and which will not move whatever you spend. It publishes the Dubai market rates for in-home and online IGCSE hours with the sources that printed them, cheapest band first, so you can see where the money actually goes. It covers the mock season and the Ramadan shift, how a science practical is handled when the teaching is on a screen, and the difference between homework supervision and tutoring, which is the single most expensive confusion in this market.

It also tells you what we will not do. We do not reproduce or supply Cambridge or Pearson past papers, mark schemes or syllabus documents, because that is their copyright; we reference them and link out. We publish no grade guarantee. We claim no approval from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, because IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and holds none.

The practical first step is a free lesson of about thirty minutes, one per family, with no charge and no card details taken. Its job is to find out whether your child's problem is content, technique or timing. Those three need completely different responses, and most families have been quietly buying the wrong one.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Four-digit syllabus codes such as 0580 for Mathematics, 0625 for Physics and 0620 for Chemistry, with Core and Extended tiers in many subjects. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for IGCSE and O Level, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and must use the timetable version for its own zone.
programmes.countryNote: Most British-curriculum schools serving The Views enter the majority of subjects with Cambridge, which is why the syllabus codes above are the ones a Views parent sees on a school letter. Cambridge states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used, so checking the zone is a five-minute job worth doing once.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes run 4MA1 for Mathematics A, 4PH1 for Physics, 4CH1 for Chemistry. Exams are available in May or June and in November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools frequently split entries across both boards, so a Views student can sit Cambridge sciences and Pearson mathematics in the same June. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official timetable is the only version worth planning around rather than a date restated on a tutoring page.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme, the other feeder
programmes.description: Some Views children are at IB continuum schools and meet criterion-based assessment rather than IGCSE grades. Eight subject groups, four lettered criteria each, no percentage marks. Students who transfer from MYP into a British school in Year 10 arrive strong on inquiry and investigation and weak on timed, mark-scheme-driven writing, which is exactly what IGCSE papers reward.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP-to-IGCSE transfer mid-Year 10 is one of the most common requests out of Emirates Living, because places open at different times across the Meadows and Al Barsha schools. The support needed is almost entirely exam technique rather than content, and it usually takes six to ten sessions rather than a year.

programmes.name: A Level or IB Diploma after the IGCSEs
programmes.description: The grades your child takes in Year 11 decide the post-16 options. A Level entry is subject-by-subject and typically needs a grade 6 or 7 in the related IGCSE; the IB Diploma takes six subjects at once and asks for breadth rather than depth at entry. Mathematics is the subject where the two routes diverge most sharply.
programmes.countryNote: An Extended grade 7 in Cambridge 0580 does not prepare a student for Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, and the shortfall appears in the first proof and calculus unit. Views families planning the Diploma route are better served by bridging work in the summer after Year 11 than by extra IGCSE drilling in the spring.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-views.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Views families fund most often, with what each one actually needs rather than a general description. The level column shows the tier or route, because the tier is where the grade ceiling is decided.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The subject that gets funded first in almost every household, and reasonably so, since it gates post-16 options. Marks disappear in algebraic manipulation, in multi-step problems where the method mark depends on showing a line of working, and in the non-calculator paper where arithmetic confidence has quietly eroded.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and magnetism cost more marks than any other topic, followed by moments and the equations of motion. Students who can recite a formula still lose the explanation marks because they describe what happens instead of saying why, which is a trainable habit rather than a knowledge gap.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles arithmetic is the first cliff and organic chemistry the second. The practical and alternative-to-practical papers reward a student who can read a method critically and identify the controlled variable, a skill most candidates have never been taught explicitly.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume rather than difficulty. The grade usually turns on command-term discipline: describe, explain and compare need different answer shapes, and a student writing everything they know about a topic scores less than one answering the question asked.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and the reading summary carry most of the available marks and are the most coachable parts of any IGCSE. A student who learns to plan for four minutes before writing typically gains more here per hour of tutoring than anywhere else on the timetable.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Quotation accuracy and argument structure, not opinion. The commonest failure is a well-read student writing a narrative retelling of the text rather than an argument answering the question, which no amount of additional reading fixes on its own.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram precision and data-response technique. Labelled axes, correctly shifted curves and a conclusion that actually weighs the evidence are what separate a grade 6 from a grade 8, and all three are teachable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Case-study application. Students who can define a term still fail to apply it to the specific business in the paper, which is where the higher-band marks live. Calculation questions on break-even and cash flow are reliably under-practised.

subjects.name: Additional and International Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by students heading for Higher Level mathematics or A Level. Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 is assessed with a graphic display calculator assumed, which makes it a very different preparation from 0580 and a better bridge towards Applications and Interpretation.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Pseudocode and trace tables are where marks are lost, not the programming itself. The theory paper rewards precise vocabulary about data representation and networks, which students consistently approximate rather than learn.

sections.heading: The Views weekday, from the bus door to the last worked question
paragraphs: Scheduling advice in this market is usually written as though a child comes home at 15:30 and has an empty evening. No Year 11 student in Emirates Living does. The useful version counts backwards from the point a teenager stops learning, which is somewhere around 21:00, and asks what is already occupying the hours in between.

The bus into The Views arrives at different times depending on which school and which route, and that single variable decides more about a tutoring arrangement than anything else. A child at Regent International School in The Greens is through the door by about 15:50. A child at Emirates International School Meadows is home by 16:20 on most routes. A student at Dubai College or GEMS Wellington International School in Al Sufouh, crossing Sheikh Zayed Road on the way back, is realistically not settled before 17:00 and sometimes not until 17:30.

Then the fixed costs. Homework across eight or nine IGCSE subjects runs ninety minutes to two hours on a normal Tuesday. Mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education work sits on top of that, and KHDA requires those subjects of every Dubai private school whatever curriculum it is licensed to teach. Activities take two evenings a week in most households. Dinner takes one slot that moves depending on when a parent gets back from Media City or Internet City.

The result is the table below, and the row that matters is the third one. There is a usable window of roughly sixty to seventy-five minutes in the late afternoon, and a second shorter one after dinner that works for some children and not at all for others. An in-home tutor driving in cannot reliably use the first window, because visitor parking in the Fairways and Links clusters is filling by 18:00 and the drive across Interchange 5 is unpredictable from 17:15. An online session can use it, because the only travel involved is from one room to another.

sections.heading: Nine subjects and one budget: which one to fund first
paragraphs: Parents rarely ask this question out loud, and it is the most important one on the page. If there is money and time for one subject, which subject? The answer is not the one with the lowest grade. It is the one where an hour a week moves the most marks, which depends on how the subject is assessed rather than on how badly it is currently going.

Mathematics sits at the top for a structural reason. It gates post-16 choices, the content is cumulative so a gap in Year 10 compounds through Year 11, and the marks are heavily method-based, which means technique coaching converts directly into score. English Language sits second and surprises people: directed writing and the reading summary are formulaic in the best sense, and a student who learns to plan before writing often gains a grade band within a term. Sciences come next, but only where the problem is a named topic. A general feeling that physics is hard converts poorly into paid hours; electricity and magnetism specifically converts very well.

At the other end are the subjects where tutoring is the wrong purchase. A student who has not read the set texts for English Literature needs to read them, and no tutor can substitute for that. A student failing Business Studies because they are not learning the case study needs supervision rather than teaching. And a subject the child has simply decided to abandon will not recover through an imposed weekly hour, which is a difficult thing for a parent to hear and a cheaper thing to hear in October than in April.

The table sets out the realistic return per funded hour across the subjects Views families ask about, and names the term in which starting makes the most difference. Nothing in it is a promise about grades. It is a ranking of where an hour is least likely to be wasted, which is the decision actually in front of you.
