sections.heading: What a Dubai IGCSE hour costs, cheapest band first
paragraphs: Price lists in this market tend to start at the top, because the premium figure makes everything below it look reasonable. It is more useful to read the Dubai IGCSE market from the bottom, since that is where most families start and where the disappointments happen.

The cheapest published rates in Dubai are online and staffed largely by university students. Tutopiya advertises from roughly AED 33 to AED 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65. That band buys supervision: somebody keeping a child at the desk, checking homework, re-explaining a worked example. For a Year 10 student who is coping but drifting, it is often enough, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest. It is not enough for a Year 11 student who needs a mock script diagnosed topic by topic against a mark scheme.

The next band up is where qualified subject teaching begins. Unitors publishes IGCSE tutoring from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200, online. Named IGCSE and A Level specialists are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table reaching AED 450 or more at the specialist end. Above that sit premium and former-examiner tutors, with BartyED quoted at AED 650. In-home one-to-one visits run across the middle of that range at AED 180 to AED 500 including travel, with Bestimate putting the usual Dubai band at AED 180 to AED 350.

Two things follow for a Views household. First, the jump that matters is not from AED 300 to AED 650; it is from AED 50 to AED 150, which is the step from supervision to teaching. Second, the in-home premium buys travel rather than expertise, and in a tower community a meaningful part of the booked hour disappears into parking, the security desk and an early departure for the next family. Every figure here is somebody else's published rate, dated to October 2026. IB Gram publishes no fixed price list on these pages; you get a quote before anything is booked, after a free first lesson.

sections.heading: The mock season, Ramadan, and when the hour actually counts
paragraphs: Dubai schools run a three-term year, and the IGCSE pressure points in it are not evenly spaced. Knowing where they fall is how a family spends two evenings a week sensibly instead of spreading them thinly across ten months.

The entry deadline is the first thing most parents have never heard of. In the UAE a Cambridge candidate sits the June series or the November series, and entries for June close in the spring, months before the first paper, on a date the centre confirms on the statement of entry. Pearson Edexcel works the same way: its November 2026 International GCSE timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and entries for it were settled long before term started. What the gap means in practice is that the decision about which tier and which subjects your child sits is taken by the school while there is still a full year of teaching left. If a Core or Foundation entry is going to cap your child's grade, autumn is when that conversation is useful, not the week the timetable is pinned up.

January mocks are the second pressure point and the honest start of most Year 11 tutoring. A marked mock script is the best diagnostic any family will get for free, and it is routinely wasted. The script shows which topics lost marks and, more usefully, whether the marks were lost to content, to method or to running out of time. Those three have different fixes, and a tutor who looks at the script in the first session is worth more than one who begins with a generic assessment.

Ramadan falls inside the spring term and changes the shape of the week rather than cancelling it. School hours shorten, evenings fill, and most Views families shift sessions to after Iftar or drop from two a week to one. Planning for that in advance is better than losing four weeks to it. The long Dubai summer matters for the opposite reason: a student going into Year 11 who keeps one session a week through July and August starts the final year without the usual six-week regression in mathematics.

sections.heading: Science practicals when the teaching happens on a screen
paragraphs: This is the question every science enquiry from The Views eventually reaches, and it deserves a real answer rather than reassurance. Most Dubai schools enter candidates for the alternative-to-practical paper rather than a timetabled laboratory examination. That paper does not test whether a student can use a burette. It tests whether they can read a method, identify the independent and controlled variables, spot the flaw in somebody else's procedure, read a scale correctly, process a table of results and draw a conclusion that the data actually supports.

Every one of those is a paper skill, and paper skills are taught better on a shared screen than at a dining table. A tutor can put a past-paper method on screen, have the student annotate it live, and show the mark scheme's own wording for what counted as a valid improvement. Graph work is the clearest case: plotting by hand on a shared document, with the line of best fit redrawn three times and the gradient read off properly, is exactly the exercise that moves marks in both Cambridge and Pearson science papers.

What online teaching cannot do is replace laboratory time. If your child has never set up a titration, that is the school's job and the school's equipment, and a tutor who claims to substitute for it is selling something that does not exist. The useful division of labour is that the school supplies the hands and the apparatus, and the tutoring supplies the analysis, the vocabulary and the practice at reading an experiment critically.

One constraint on materials is worth stating plainly, because this market breaks it constantly. We do not reproduce or supply Cambridge or Pearson past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents or grade-boundary tables. Those are the boards' copyright. We reference them, cite the official page, and work from material the student legitimately has from school or from the boards' own public sites.

sections.heading: Homework supervision is not tutoring, and the gap costs real money
paragraphs: The most expensive mistake a Views family makes is buying the wrong product for two terms. Supervision and tutoring look identical from the kitchen: a person, a laptop, an hour, a cooperative child. They do completely different things, they cost roughly three times apart, and parents frequently buy one while needing the other.

Supervision keeps a student working. It is somebody present while homework gets finished, who re-explains a worked example and checks that the answers are not invented. For a Year 9 or Year 10 student who is capable but disorganised, it is genuinely the right purchase, and the market prices it from roughly AED 33 to AED 65 an hour online. Nobody should pay AED 300 for it.

Tutoring does something different. It diagnoses why a specific category of mark is being lost, and changes a habit. The physics student who writes what happens instead of why; the maths student who leaps to an answer and forfeits three method marks; the English student who begins writing in the first thirty seconds of a directed-writing task. None of those is a knowledge gap, none of them is visible in a homework exercise, and none of them is fixed by supervision, however diligent. Fixing them needs somebody who knows the mark scheme well enough to name the pattern.

The test for which one your child needs is simple enough to run this week. Look at a recent marked assessment. If the lost marks are on work that was never attempted, you have a supervision problem. If the lost marks are on work that was attempted and came out wrong in the same way three times, you have a teaching problem. Buying the second remedy for the first problem is how a family spends AED 1,200 a month and sees nothing move.

sections.heading: Two boards in one household, and why that is normal here
paragraphs: A Views parent will sometimes discover that their child is sitting Cambridge sciences and Pearson Edexcel mathematics in the same June, and assume something has gone wrong. Nothing has. Dubai schools choose specifications subject by subject, and splitting across awarding bodies is ordinary practice across the British-curriculum schools serving Emirates Living.

It does matter for tutoring, though, more than most families expect. Cambridge 0580 Mathematics and Pearson 4MA1 Mathematics A cover similar ground with different paper structures, different question styles and different conventions about what working earns a method mark. A tutor who prepares a student for the wrong one will teach largely useful mathematics and still leave the student unprepared for the specific paper in front of them. The first thing we ask for is the specification code from the school, not the subject name.

The series calendars differ too. Cambridge runs June and November series for IGCSE and O Level, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version. Pearson offers May or June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026, and publishes provisional timetables for future series, the International GCSE November window among them. The practical instruction is the same for both: work from the live official timetable on the board's own site, because dates can be revised and a date restated on a tutoring page cannot be trusted.

For a family planning retakes or a private-candidate entry, the board difference becomes a logistics question about which centre accepts which qualification in which series. That is a conversation with the school and the centre rather than with a tutor, and we will point you there rather than guess.

sections.heading: Starting from The Views, and the things we will not pretend to do
paragraphs: The first step is a short conversation and three pieces of information: the school, the subjects with their specification codes if you have them, and the two evenings that are genuinely free rather than the two that look free on paper. If you have a marked mock script or a recent assessment, that is worth more than any description of the problem, because it shows where the marks went rather than how it felt.

Then the free first lesson, one per family, about thirty minutes, no charge and no card details taken. The tutor's task is to come out of it able to name the specific pattern costing marks and to say what the first four sessions would do about it. If they cannot, that is useful information about the tutor and you have spent nothing finding it out.

From there it is deliberately unglamorous. Same tutor, same evenings, a short written note after each session recording what was covered and what to practise. The notes are what let you judge in week six whether the same weakness is still being described, which is a far better signal than a general sense of whether things are improving. If the match is wrong, say so after the second session and we will change it.

The limits, stated up front. No tutor travels to a UAE address; that service exists in India only. No grade is guaranteed, by us or by anybody honest in this market. We do not reproduce board papers or mark schemes. We claim no approval from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, because we hold none. And where no specialist is free for a particular subject in your slot, you get the realistic start date rather than a substitute who will waste a term.

faqs.question: Can an IGCSE tutor visit our flat in The Views?
faqs.answer: Not one arranged by IB Gram. Visiting students at home is a service we run in India only, and nobody we match travels to a UAE address. Lessons for Views families run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time with the same tutor weekly. Independent in-home tutors do operate across Emirates Living, and the Dubai market quotes them at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included. For a younger child who needs an adult physically present, hiring locally is a sensible choice and we will tell you so.

faqs.question: Which of my child's nine subjects should we actually pay for?
faqs.answer: Start with mathematics in most households, because the content is cumulative, it gates post-16 options, and the marks are heavily method-based so technique converts straight into score. English Language is the surprising second, since directed writing and the reading summary respond quickly to coaching. Sciences repay funding where there is a named topic failing, such as electricity or moles arithmetic, and repay it poorly where the complaint is general. Subjects where the student has not done the reading or the case study need supervision, not teaching, and that costs a third as much.

faqs.question: What time can a session start for a Year 11 student living in The Views?
faqs.answer: That depends on the school rather than the community. A child at Regent International School in The Greens is usually home by about 15:50 and can be working by 16:30. Emirates International School Meadows routes get in by roughly 16:20. Students travelling back from Dubai College or GEMS Wellington International School in Al Sufouh are realistically not settled until 17:00 to 17:30. The early window is the valuable one, and it is only reachable when no tutor has to drive in and find a visitor bay first.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE specification my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Ask the school directly, or look at an exam entry letter or statement of entry, which carries the awarding body and the four-character code. Cambridge uses numbers such as 0580 for Mathematics, 0625 for Physics and 0620 for Chemistry; Pearson Edexcel uses forms such as 4MA1, 4PH1 and 4CH1. Dubai schools frequently split entries across both boards, so your child may be sitting one board for sciences and another for mathematics. The code matters because the papers differ in structure and in what working earns a method mark.

faqs.question: Is a group class in Barsha Heights better value than a one-to-one hour?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth being honest about when. A group works where several students share the same specification, the same tier and roughly the same weakness, and where the saving is real after you count the drive. For one child with one specific problem it is poor value, because the teaching cannot follow their particular pattern of lost marks and a parent spends two hours delivering a one-hour lesson. Centres also teach to their own scheme of work rather than to your school's assessment calendar, which matters most in Year 11.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE entries actually close, and why does that matter now?
faqs.answer: Months before the exam, and for a UAE candidate the exam is the June series or the November series; the February-March series Cambridge runs is offered to India only. Entries for June close in the spring, well before the papers, and Pearson's November window is set long before its late-October start. The reason that matters in autumn is tiering: if your child is entered for Core rather than Extended, the grade ceiling is fixed before revision begins, and that is a conversation to have with the school while the entry can still be amended. Ask the centre for the statement of entry and read the board, the syllabus code and the tier off it.

faqs.question: How is the science practical handled if the tutoring is online?
faqs.answer: Most Dubai schools enter candidates for the alternative-to-practical paper, which tests paper skills rather than laboratory technique: reading a method, identifying controlled variables, finding the flaw in a procedure, processing a results table and drawing a supported conclusion. All of that is taught well on a shared screen, and graph work especially so, with the line of best fit redrawn and the gradient read off properly. What online teaching cannot replace is time with real apparatus, which is the school's job and its equipment.

faqs.question: My child's mock results were poor. Is February too late to start?
faqs.answer: No, but the shape of the work changes. From February there is no time to reteach a two-year syllabus, so the honest plan is to pick the three topics the mock script shows are costing the most marks and work only on those, with past-paper questions done to time. A marked mock script is the best free diagnostic a family gets, and it is usually wasted. Bring it to the first lesson. A tutor who starts with your child's own script rather than a generic assessment will save two sessions immediately.

faqs.question: Does Arabic or Islamic Education homework really eat into the tutoring slot?
faqs.answer: It does, and families arriving from the UK are often unprepared for it. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum they are licensed to teach, with the requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. For a Year 11 with nine IGCSEs, that is real homework competing for the same two evenings, which is why most Views households fund one subject properly rather than three thinly.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE grades will the UAE recognise later?
faqs.answer: Five. The Ministry of Education's British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One competing page in this market publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong. Equivalency is a Ministry process that no tutoring platform performs, so verify anything decisive on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: Can my child sit papers from two different awarding bodies?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in Dubai it is common rather than unusual. Schools choose specifications subject by subject, so a Views student may sit Cambridge sciences alongside Pearson Edexcel mathematics in the same series. It changes nothing about the validity of the grades. It changes a great deal about preparation, because the two boards structure papers differently and reward working differently. Tell a prospective tutor the code, not just the subject, and ask which board's papers they normally teach from before the first lesson.

faqs.question: Is it worth continuing sessions through the Dubai summer?
faqs.answer: For a student going into Year 11, usually yes, and one session a week is enough. Mathematics is the subject that regresses most over six weeks away, and the cost of rebuilding fluency in September is higher than the cost of holding it in July. Online delivery is what makes this practical: a family in the UK, India or Europe for the summer keeps the same tutor and the same slot where the time zone allows. For Year 9 and Year 10 students, a break is usually the better choice.

faqs.question: Does the person tutoring my child privately in Dubai need a licence?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, whose service page lists it as private tutor licensing with a two-working-day completion time. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen and university students. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: Will the tutor use my child's own school materials and deadlines?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the main reason to prefer one-to-one over a centre. Sessions follow the school's scheme of work and its assessment calendar, so revision happens in the order the school teaches rather than in the order a syllabus is printed. We work from material your child legitimately holds. We do not reproduce or supply Cambridge or Pearson past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents or grade-boundary tables, because those belong to the boards; we reference the official pages and link to them instead.

faqs.question: What if no tutor is free for the subject and evening we need?
faqs.answer: You are told, with a date. Some combinations are genuinely tight, particularly separate sciences at Extended tier in the 17:00 window when every Emirates Living family wants the same hour. The alternative to saying so is placing a general tutor in a specialist slot, which costs a term before anybody admits it. Usually the fix is an adjacent evening or a weekend block. Occasionally it is a wait of a week, and you decide whether to hold the slot. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-views.closingHeading: Fund one subject properly rather than three thinly
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-the-views.closingBody: The search that brought you here was about access, and the answer is that nobody drives to a Views tower, which turns out to free up the best hour of the evening. The decision actually in front of you is narrower and more useful: which one of eight or nine subjects gets the two free evenings, and whether your child needs teaching or supervision. Send the school, the specification codes if you have them, a marked mock script if there is one, and the evenings that are genuinely available. We will propose a tutor matched to that exact paper, arrange a free first lesson of about thirty minutes with no card details taken, and tell you honestly if the specialist is a few days out.

intro.heading: Every useful IGCSE decision has a deadline attached
paragraphs: The hardest thing to explain to a family hiring an IGCSE tutor in a hurry is that most of the decisions they want to make are no longer available. Subject entries closed months ago. The tier was fixed before that. A resit cannot be taken next month, only in the next series. A remark has a deadline measured in weeks after results. None of this is obscure and almost none of it is explained to parents, who reasonably assume that effort can be applied whenever they decide to apply it.

So this page is organised around dates rather than topics. It sets out which series a UAE candidate actually sits, how the November series works as a resit route, what happens between a result arriving and a decision having to be made, and what each term of Year 11 has to deliver before the next one starts. The intention is that a Tilal Al Ghaf family reading it in October knows what is still changeable and what is not.

Tilal Al Ghaf helps with one part of this. The community has a school inside its boundary and sits beside DAMAC Hills and Dubai Sports City, which also have their own provision, so the school run here is short by Dubailand standards and pupils are home earlier than in villa communities with no school. That means a four-thirty or five o'clock weekday session is realistic, which matters when a revision plan has to fit inside a fixed number of weeks.

The second thing to establish before hiring anyone is which qualification your child actually sits. Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE are separate awarding bodies with different codes, different tiering language and, in several subjects, different calculator rules. Ask the school's exams officer for the board, the syllabus code and the tier in writing. A tutor working from the wrong specification can teach excellently for a term and leave your child unprepared for the paper in front of them.

There is one date-related error worth correcting immediately, because UAE-facing tutoring pages repeat it. Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only. A candidate in Dubai sits the June series or the November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. If you have read a November entry deadline attached to a February exam window on a page aimed at UAE parents, that page is wrong about your country, and it is the kind of error a family acts on.

IB Gram delivers IGCSE tuition to Tilal Al Ghaf as live one-to-one lessons over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. The phrase 'home tutor' is what parents search for, so this page uses it and answers the home-tutoring question properly below, with the market figures and the travel arithmetic set out.

programmes.name: Year 9, before anything is fixed
programmes.description: Everything is still open: subjects, provisional tier, and the fluency the specification assumes. Work here is algebraic manipulation, written stamina in the sciences and reading-response technique. It is the cheapest intervention per mark available and the least often booked, because nothing feels urgent yet.

programmes.description: The year the grade is built and the last point at which a tier entry can realistically be challenged. A tutor consolidates content as the school teaches it, drills method and units, and can produce a marked higher-tier paper as evidence if the entry looks wrong. After this the conversation gets much harder.

programmes.description: The most common booking. The series date is fixed, the entry is in, and the work is paper technique and targeted topic repair driven by a marked mock. dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-tilal-al-ghaf.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Tilal Al Ghaf families ask about, with both boards' codes. The codes matter because a tutor matched to the subject but not the specification wastes exactly the weeks you cannot replace.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Edexcel 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two papers on each board. Edexcel permits a calculator in both; Cambridge's current structure pairs a non-calculator paper with a calculator one, so confirm which your child sits. Method marks are forfeited by unshown steps even where the answer is right.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken alongside the main course by pupils heading for A Level Mathematics or IB Analysis and Approaches. Calculus, logarithms and trigonometric identities arrive early, and differentiation is usually where fluency and understanding separate.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity is the reliable weak point because circuit reasoning requires holding three relationships together. Cambridge sets a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper depending on the centre's entry; Edexcel assesses practical skills inside the written papers.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations decide the grade because they recur and compound, and concentration units cost more marks across a paper than conceptual gaps do. Qualitative analysis is pure learned content and the cheapest marks available, reliably skipped in revision.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Large content load with exact terminology, where diffusion, osmosis and active transport are separated in the mark scheme and conflated under pressure. Inheritance questions want the cross drawn rather than reasoned in prose.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Reading response and directed writing, marked on comprehension, summary skill and control of register. The summary question is the most coachable task on the paper because it rewards selection and compression rather than style.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and, where entered, speaking. Text-type conventions are assessed, so an email, a report and an article each carry format and register marks that confident speakers routinely lose.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Case-study assessment where context carries the marks. Answering with textbook theory and never referring to the business in the stimulus is the standard loss, and the cost, revenue and ratio calculations get skipped under time pressure.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Markets, the macro economy and trade. A mislabelled diagram axis undermines every sentence built on it, and evaluation marks require an explicit stated judgement which pupils omit after writing a strong explanation.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Systems, data representation, algorithms and programming. Binary, hexadecimal and logic gates are learnable in a handful of sessions and recur every series. Hand-tracing pseudocode is the missing skill, because pupils learn to run code rather than predict it.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Physical and human geography with a skills component on maps, graphs and data. Case-study specificity carries the top marks: a named place with named figures beats a general description, and the skills questions reward practice rather than revision.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.levels: First language and additional language, plus mandated strands
subjects.description: Compulsory in Dubai private schools alongside the licensed curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, and tutoring splits along the same line.

sections.heading: Which series, and the dates that are actually verifiable
paragraphs: Start with the series, because everything else hangs off it. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series. It also runs a February and March series, and that series is offered to India only — a candidate in Dubai does not sit it. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Those are the options for a Tilal Al Ghaf pupil, and any page offering a UAE parent a February exam window is describing a different country.

Cambridge adds a complication worth knowing about. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone's timetable. Parents who download a timetable themselves and plan study leave around it are taking a risk that costs nothing to remove: ask the exams officer which zone the centre is in.

The verifiable Pearson dates are worth quoting precisely because they show the scale of the lag between sitting a paper and acting on the result. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are backward-looking citations and carry their dates for that reason. For any series still ahead, use the month and check the live official timetable, since Pearson publishes provisional timetables that can be revised.

The practical consequence for a family is that the decision points are not where they feel like they should be. Entries close months before papers. A November resit entry has to be made before November results from the previous year are even relevant. And a remark request has a deadline measured in weeks after a result arrives, not months. The table below lays the sequence out so that a family can see which door is open today.

sections.heading: The fortnight after results, and the decisions inside it
paragraphs: This is the part of the IGCSE calendar that nobody prepares for and the part where families lose options. A result arrives. It is below what a sixth-form place or a parent's expectation required. Three courses of action exist and two of them expire.

The first is to accept the grade, which is frequently the right answer and deserves to be stated as a real option rather than a failure. A grade a little below target in a subject that nothing depends on is not worth a term of a child's life to improve. The second is to ask the school to request an enquiry upon results from the awarding body, a process schools initiate rather than families, with its own deadline shortly after results and a fee structure the school will explain. It is worth considering where a grade sits one or two marks below a boundary, and the school can usually tell you whether it does.

The third is to re-enter for the next series. For a May or June result the next series is November, which in practice means a short window: results arrive in August, entry has to go through a centre, and the papers are sat in late October and November, with results reaching students in the following January. That is a compressed sequence and it only works if the decision is made quickly, which is why a family should know the shape of it before results day rather than discovering it afterwards.

What a tutor contributes in that fortnight is diagnosis rather than reassurance. Where did the marks actually go? A candidate who lost them to timing and unfinished papers is a very different proposition in a resit from one who never understood a third of the specification. The first is a strong candidate for a November block; the second may be better served by a different subject choice at sixteen. We will say which we think it is, and saying the second costs us the booking.

sections.heading: Year 11, term by term, with what closes at each point
paragraphs: Having set out the series, here is the year inside it. The purpose of this table is to let a family see, from wherever they are reading, what is still available and what has already been decided. Year 11 is not one undifferentiated stretch of revision; it has distinct phases with different possibilities.

The first term is the last point at which content teaching is genuinely realistic. There is enough time to cover a topic properly, and the mock series at the end of it will produce the evidence everything afterwards is planned from. Families who book in the first term get a tutor who can teach; families who book in the third term get a tutor who can only triage.

The second term is where most bookings actually happen, and it is the technique term. Command terms, method shown for marks, unit discipline, finishing the paper. Those are habits and they respond within weeks, which is why a second-term booking can still move a grade materially even without much content teaching. This is also the point at which three or four weak topics can be repaired, chosen from a marked mock rather than from the student's impression of what is difficult.

The final weeks are about papers and pacing. Nothing new gets taught, and attempting to teach new content at that point does active harm, because it displaces the practice that would have consolidated what the student already knows. One timed paper a week, marked against the scheme with losses categorised, is the whole of a sensible plan. Any provider offering to cover remaining syllabus content in the final fortnight is selling comfort rather than marks.

sections.heading: Where the marks go when time runs out
paragraphs: Because this page is about the calendar, the loss pattern worth examining is the one caused by time rather than by ignorance. In a marked mock, a large share of lost marks typically belongs to candidates who knew the material and did not convert it, and every one of those losses is a scheduling or technique problem rather than a content gap.

Unfinished papers come first. A candidate who spends fourteen minutes on a six-mark question has bought a small improvement on that answer with the entire value of a later question, and unanswered questions score nothing regardless of understanding. This only becomes visible under full-length timed conditions, which is why the first session of any Year 11 block is a paper rather than teaching, and why a student who has never sat a complete paper before the mock discovers the problem at the worst possible moment.

Unshown method comes second. Mark schemes award credit for steps, so a correct answer with nothing written scores below a wrong answer with sound working. The candidates most affected are the quick ones who have been praised for mental arithmetic since primary school. Third is the command term: 'describe', 'explain', 'compare' and 'evaluate' want different structures, and writing everything known satisfies none of them while consuming the time the next question needed.

The fourth is a scheduling failure rather than an exam one: work set between sessions that does not get done. In a commuting household this has a real cause, and the fix is design rather than exhortation. One short timed question set per subject per week, rather than an hour of open revision, fits into an evening and produces more. Tilal Al Ghaf's short school run makes this easier here than in most of the belt, and it is worth using.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs now against what a resit costs later
paragraphs: This is the cost comparison that actually matters in a calendar-led decision, and nobody makes it. Market rates in Dubai, read in October 2026 from competitors' own published figures: EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65 an hour, Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52, Unitors from AED 150 for IGCSE, TutorChase at AED 270, BartyED at AED 650. Bestimate's table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 and IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above.

Now the arithmetic. A standard Year 11 block of two sessions a week for twenty weeks is about forty hours, which at the qualified subject tutor band of AED 150 to AED 300 is roughly AED 6,000 to AED 12,000. A November resit block is shorter — perhaps twenty-four hours over eight to ten weeks — so roughly AED 3,600 to AED 7,200 at the same band, plus the private candidate entry fees the centre charges, plus a term in which your child is preparing for an exam instead of starting their sixth-form course properly.

The resit route therefore looks cheaper in tutoring terms and is usually more expensive in every other respect. It consumes the autumn of Year 12, it arrives with results in January when sixth-form courses are already a term in, and it carries no guarantee of a better outcome since the candidate is working alone rather than inside a taught course. None of that makes it wrong — for a subject a university route actually requires, it is clearly worth doing — but a family should see the whole cost rather than the hourly one.

For context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for Dubai private schools for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package, valued at AED 1.5 billion. The fee line is flat; tutoring is the variable. IB Gram publishes no hourly rate here, because the right figure depends on board, tier and weeks remaining, but the band above lets you judge any quote including ours, and the first lesson is free.

sections.heading: Private candidates, and entering outside your own school
paragraphs: Some Tilal Al Ghaf families end up needing to enter a subject their child's school does not offer, or to re-enter after leaving a school, or to sit a subject earlier than the school's timetable allows. That means entering as a private candidate through a centre that accepts them, and it is worth understanding how that changes the picture.

The administrative reality is that entry is made through a centre rather than directly with the awarding body, the centre sets its own deadlines inside the awarding body's, and fees are the centre's. We do not arrange entries and this page does not pretend to: ask centres directly, and ask early, because private candidate places for a given series close well before the series.

The teaching reality is the one a tutor is relevant to. A private candidate is not inside a taught course, so everything the school would normally do — pacing, coverage, mock papers, access to practical facilities where the subject requires them — falls to the family to arrange. For a written-only subject that is manageable with a weekly tutor and a disciplined timetable. For a science where the centre enters candidates for a practical test rather than an alternative-to-practical paper, it is a genuine problem, and the answer is to establish which paper the centre enters before committing.

The honest guidance is that private candidacy works well for a motivated student in a written subject with a clear reason for taking it, and poorly as a way of avoiding a difficult school situation. If your child is sitting a subject privately because something went wrong at school, deal with the something first. A tutor cannot substitute for a taught course, and we will say so rather than taking a booking that was never going to work.

sections.heading: The home-tutoring question, answered properly
paragraphs: In-home tuition is widely available in Dubai and the market rate runs roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel, against roughly AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. Published monthly packages show AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits against around AED 799 for eight online sessions — roughly double the money for half the sessions. IB Gram does not offer in-home tuition anywhere in the UAE, and this page is not going to pretend the option does not exist.

What the premium buys is presence: an adult physically in the room, no dependence on a connection, and no screen. For a young or distractible pupil those are real benefits and sometimes the deciding ones. What the premium does not buy is better teaching, a wider choice of tutor or more reliable attendance, and in a calendar-led plan the last of those matters most. A tutor crossing Dubai to reach Tilal Al Ghaf is exposed to traffic twice, and two cancellations in a Year 11 spring term are two weeks removed from a countdown that does not move.

Tilal Al Ghaf's own geography makes an interesting point here. Because the community has a school inside it and sits beside others that do, your child's commute is short and their evening starts early. The only long journey in an in-home arrangement would be the tutor's, which means the premium is entirely their travel rather than a cost shared across the arrangement. Online delivery simply removes that journey and the risk attached to it.

Where in-home genuinely wins, we say so. Early primary pupils and children who need an adult beside them to stay on task are better served in person, and since we do not offer that here the useful thing we can do is tell a family to look elsewhere. For Year 10 and Year 11 work, where a session is a marked past paper and a conversation about where the credit went, the screen is not the limitation.

sections.heading: Equivalency, permits and the claims to distrust
paragraphs: If a UAE university application is in prospect, the Ministry of Education's equivalency requirements matter alongside the university's own and almost no tutoring page mentions them. For the British track, students must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five.

That exclusion is the detail that catches families out, and at least one competitor page ranking for UAE tutoring searches states that six IGCSE subjects are required, which does not match the published rule. Count five excluding those two, verify the current requirement on the Ministry's own channel, and note that IB Gram neither performs nor guarantees equivalency or attestation. We describe the process and point you to the official route.

On the regulation of tutors: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE is subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

No fine amount appears here. Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, and the figure circulating online could not be verified. Equally, IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and we do not reproduce or distribute awarding-body papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, which belong to the boards. Any provider claiming a regulator's endorsement should be asked for a permit number.

process.title: Establish the series and the entry
process.description: Ask the exams officer which series the school enters, when the entry closed or closes, which tier each subject is entered at and, for Cambridge, which administrative zone the centre sits in. Those four answers tell you what is still changeable, which is the only sound basis for a plan with a fixed end date.

process.title: Convert the plan into weeks
process.description: Count the weeks between today and the first paper, and write the plan in those terms rather than as a list of topics. Twenty weeks has room for content teaching; eight does not. Saying so in the first session is more useful than discovering it in week six, and it changes what a family should be buying.

process.title: One full timed paper, categorised
process.description: The diagnostic is a complete past paper at the correct tier under exam timing, marked against the published scheme, with every lost mark categorised as content, method, units, command term or timing. Candidates who lost marks to timing and those who lost them to content need entirely different blocks.

process.title: A free first lesson with the named tutor
process.description: One full lesson, no charge, with the person who would continue. Ask them which series your child sits and which papers the syllabus sets. A tutor who knows the specification answers instantly. Then watch whether they located the real losses and set work your child can attempt alone.

process.title: Use the early evening this community allows
process.description: Tilal Al Ghaf's school provision inside and beside the community means pupils are home earlier than in most of this belt, so a four-thirty or five o'clock start is realistic. In a plan with a fixed end date, an earlier session catches a student with attention left, which is worth more than any change to the lesson plan.

process.title: Decide about results before results day
process.description: Know in advance what the three options are — accept, enquire, or re-enter for November — and which has a deadline. A family that understands the sequence in May makes a calm decision in August. A family that meets it for the first time on results day usually discovers a door closed while they were deciding.

whyPoints.title: Plans written in weeks, not topics
whyPoints.description: A fixed exam date means the honest unit of planning is weeks remaining. We say in the first session what the available weeks can and cannot reach, which sometimes means telling a family that content teaching is no longer realistic and the hours belong in technique instead.

whyPoints.title: The right series, with the right dates
whyPoints.description: UAE candidates sit June and November; the February and March series is India-only, and pages telling UAE parents otherwise are wrong about their country. We also flag Cambridge's zone-specific timetables, because using the wrong zone's version is a risk Cambridge explicitly declines to carry.

whyPoints.title: Taught by syllabus code and tier
whyPoints.description: Board, code and tier are established before the first lesson. Cambridge 0620 and Edexcel 4CH1 are different qualifications, and the calculator rules in mathematics differ between the boards, so a tutor matched to the subject but not the specification wastes weeks that cannot be replaced.

whyPoints.title: An honest account of the resit route
whyPoints.description: This page sets out what a November resit actually costs — fewer tutoring hours, plus entry fees, plus the autumn of Year 12, plus working outside a taught course. It also says that accepting a grade is sometimes the right answer, which no provider has an incentive to tell you.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published with their sources
whyPoints.description: The dirham figures here are competitors' own published numbers with the month they were read, so any quote including ours can be checked. Three of the six pages ranking for these searches publish no price at all, and one asks its own pricing question and declines to answer.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what we are not
whyPoints.description: No home visits in the UAE. No entry administration; that is the centre's. No distribution of awarding-body papers or mark schemes. No examiner claims we cannot evidence. No guaranteed grades. No approval or accreditation from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson.

faqs.question: Which exam series does a Tilal Al Ghaf pupil sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Those are what UAE candidates use. The February and March series is offered to India only, so any page giving UAE parents a February exam window or an entry deadline attached to it is describing a different country. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for the zone.

faqs.question: Can my child resit an IGCSE in Dubai whenever they want?
faqs.answer: No. A resit is an entry for a series, not something taken on demand, so a May or June result is resat in November and a November result in the following May or June. The sequence is compressed: results arrive, entry must go through a centre, and papers follow within weeks. In the last cycle Edexcel's November 2026 timetable ran to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Knowing that shape before results day is what makes a calm decision possible.

faqs.question: What are the options when an IGCSE grade comes back low?
faqs.answer: Three, and two have deadlines. Accept the grade, which is often the right answer where nothing depends on the subject and is worth stating as a real option. Ask the school to request an enquiry upon results from the awarding body, which schools initiate rather than families and which is worth considering where the grade sits a mark or two below a boundary. Or re-enter for the next series through a centre. Start with a diagnosis of where the marks actually went, because timing losses and content gaps point to different answers.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our house in Tilal Al Ghaf?
faqs.answer: No. All UAE tuition is delivered live and one-to-one over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service we run only in India. The phrase 'home tutor' is what parents search for, so the page uses it and answers the question directly. In this community the point is sharper than usual: because there are schools inside and beside Tilal Al Ghaf, your child's commute is short and the only long journey in an in-home arrangement would be the tutor's.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the series is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: It is never too late to gain marks, but what the weeks can reach changes. Twenty weeks has room for genuine content teaching. Eight weeks moves technique — command terms, method shown for credit, unit discipline, finishing the paper — and repairs three or four topics chosen from a marked mock. Two weeks is papers and pacing only, and any provider offering to cover remaining syllabus content in a final fortnight is selling comfort. We will say which case you are in after the first session.

faqs.question: What does a November resit block cost compared with tutoring now?
faqs.answer: A Year 11 block of two sessions a week for twenty weeks is about forty hours, roughly AED 6,000 to AED 12,000 at the qualified subject tutor band of AED 150 to AED 300 read in October 2026. A November resit block is shorter, perhaps twenty-four hours, so roughly AED 3,600 to AED 7,200 at the same band, plus the centre's private candidate entry fees and the autumn of Year 12 spent preparing for an exam rather than starting a sixth-form course. Cheaper in tutoring and more expensive in everything else.

faqs.question: How does a private candidate entry work in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Entry is made through a centre that accepts private candidates, not directly with the awarding body, and the centre sets its own deadlines inside the board's and charges its own fees. Places for a given series close well before the series, so ask early. We do not arrange entries. The teaching consequence matters too: a private candidate sits outside a taught course, so pacing, coverage and mock papers fall to the family, and in a science you must establish whether the centre enters the practical test or the alternative paper.

faqs.question: Why do candidates lose marks on topics they actually knew?
faqs.answer: Because of time and technique rather than knowledge. Unfinished papers come first: a candidate spending fourteen minutes on a six-mark question has traded a later question for a small improvement, and unanswered questions score nothing. Then unshown method, since mark schemes credit the steps and a correct answer with no working scores below a wrong one with sound working. Then command terms, where writing everything known satisfies no verb while consuming the time the next question needed.

faqs.question: What should a Year 11 do between sessions in a commuting household?
faqs.answer: One short timed question set per subject per week, marked against the published scheme, rather than an hour of open revision. Timing is the operative constraint, and twenty-five minutes with a clock running teaches more than ninety minutes without one. Marking against the scheme is what changes results, because it shows where credit actually sits rather than whether the answer felt right. Tilal Al Ghaf's short school run makes this easier here than in villa communities with no school inside them.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education counted in the MoE subject total?
faqs.answer: For the British track the Ministry of Education requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one subject at Advanced Level at E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five, which is the detail families miss. At least one ranking competitor states six subjects are needed, which the published rule does not support. Verify on the Ministry's own channel; we neither perform nor guarantee equivalency.

faqs.question: Should we challenge my child's tier entry, and when?
faqs.answer: If your child is on Core or Foundation in a subject they intend to continue at A Level or IB Higher Level, raise it as early as possible, because entries close months before papers and the lower tier caps the grade that can be awarded regardless of performance. Ask the school which tier they are entered at and what evidence would support a change. The most persuasive thing you can bring is a full higher-tier past paper worked under timing and marked against the scheme, which is a legitimate use of a tutor.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle two subjects in the weeks before the series?
faqs.answer: Often, and in Year 11 it can be the better arrangement where mathematics and a science are both weak, because the shared cause is frequently quantitative rather than subject-specific. A single tutor across both will recognise that a chemistry difficulty and a physics difficulty are the same rearranging problem. The sessions remain separate one-to-one lessons in consecutive slots. The limit is specialism: at the higher tier in two sciences, two specialists usually beat one generalist.

faqs.question: Does Ramadan change an exam-term revision plan?
faqs.answer: It changes the shape of the week rather than the amount of work. School hours shorten and the usable evening moves, so sessions shift to the earlier afternoon or to a post-Iftar slot. The adjustment that works in a fixed countdown is a shorter session at the same frequency rather than skipped weeks, because continuity is what holds a revision sequence together. Where Ramadan falls close to the series, plan the block before it starts. An online slot is far easier to move than a drive across Dubai.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE tutors in Dubai need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no fine schedule is published, so be sceptical of pages quoting amounts. Ask to see the permit rather than accepting a verbal assurance.

faqs.question: Will a tutor supply past papers for the series we are preparing for?
faqs.answer: No. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and reproducing or distributing them is copyright infringement. A tutor works through questions from legitimately obtained material and teaches your child to read a mark scheme themselves, which matters more in a fixed countdown than being handed answers: a candidate who understands where credit sits writes differently on every remaining paper, whereas one given solutions does not.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-tilal-al-ghaf.closingHeading: Find the date, then count the weeks
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-tilal-al-ghaf.closingBody: Email your child's exams officer for four things: which series the school enters, when the entry closed, which tier each subject is at, and which administrative zone the centre sits in if the board is Cambridge. Then count the weeks between today and the first paper and let that number set the plan. Twenty weeks can still teach content; eight moves technique and repairs a handful of topics; two is papers and pacing. Also decide now what you would do with a disappointing result in August, because two of the three options have deadlines. Tilal Al Ghaf sessions run live and one-to-one over video at Gulf Standard Time. We make no home visits in the UAE and promise no grades.

intro.heading: What IGCSE tutoring costs in Town Square, with sources
paragraphs: Start with the state of the market, because it explains why this page exists. Of the six most visible competitor pages in this search cluster, three publish no price whatsoever and two quote US dollars — a currency no Town Square family pays school fees in. One ranking agency's own frequently-asked-questions section raises the price question and then declines to answer it. The ordinary experience of shopping for an IGCSE tutor in Dubai is therefore to receive a number over the phone with no way to judge it.

Here is the published market. Budget online tutoring advertises from AED 33-65 an hour, with Tutopiya from AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65. Qualified online subject tutors run AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialist IGCSE, IB and A Level tutors run AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate research giving the specialist band as AED 200-450 plus. At the premium end BartyED publishes AED 650. In-home visiting runs AED 180-500 an hour including travel. All read from the publishing provider's own page in October 2026.

Monthly is the figure a household budget actually registers. Bestimate estimates a weekly one-hour arrangement at AED 240-600 a month for budget tutoring, AED 600-1,200 for mid-tier and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Advertised packages include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four in-home two-hour visits.

Context helps too. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a Town Square family, that means the school-fee line is flat while the tutoring line is entirely discretionary — which makes it worth spending deliberately rather than reactively.

None of the figures above are IB Gram prices. We publish no rate card on these pages, because an honest number depends on the board, the tier, the year group and how many weeks remain, and a price quoted before those are known is a marketing device. What this page does instead is set out the bands, list the extras that get added after the headline rate, and name the four patterns that waste money in this community.

One delivery note, because it affects the cost comparison directly. Lessons for Town Square families are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and we make no home visits anywhere in the UAE — in-home tutoring is a service we run in India only. From Al Qudra Road, a visiting tutor's rate carries seventy to ninety minutes of driving inside it, and that portion of the invoice teaches nobody anything.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-town-square.programmesIntro: What you are buying changes with the year group, and so does the cost of leaving it late. These are the stages we cover for Town Square IGCSE families.

programmes.name: Year 9, the cheap year
programmes.description: Nothing is externally examined, so nothing feels urgent, which is exactly why this is the least expensive place to fix a problem. Written explanation, algebraic fluency and the habit of showing method cost a fraction here of what they cost in Year 11, when they have to be repaired under time pressure alongside new content.
programmes.countryNote: Town Square has a young population and plenty of mid-stage arrivals, so a child joining in Year 9 from another system meets a different topic order partway through. A short diagnostic block at this point is the best-value purchase in the entire sequence, and almost nobody makes it because nothing looks wrong yet.

programmes.name: Year 10, where the grade is bought
programmes.description: The first examined year. Most syllabus content is delivered, tier placement is confirmed, and the habits that earn or forfeit method marks settle. One session a week here is unurgent and inexpensive, and it is the last point at which a tier change is realistically available.
programmes.countryNote: Do the totals rather than the hourly comparison. A weekly mid-band session across Year 10 at the published AED 600-1,200 monthly range costs less over the year than a Year 11 specialist block at AED 1,000-2,000 a month plus the extra subjects such blocks usually pull in. Families compare rates and almost never compare totals.

programmes.name: Year 11, the expensive year
programmes.description: Mocks, entries, then the series. Work shifts from content to producing marks: timing, command-term discipline, showing method, reading a question for what it asks. This is when most families buy, at the highest rates, for the shortest remaining window.
programmes.countryNote: By February the honest conversation is triage rather than coverage. We would rather name the two subjects where a grade can realistically move than take a fee across five, because five dilutes every session and the student is too tired to use any of it. That conversation costs us money and it is the one worth having.

programmes.name: November entry and resits
programmes.description: The cheapest purchase in the sequence: one subject, a defined topic list, a fixed endpoint at the November papers. Six to ten sessions is frequently the entire requirement, which makes it far better value than an open-ended arrangement running all year.
programmes.countryNote: Before planning anything: UAE candidates sit the June and November Cambridge series, and the February/March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, with November results reaching students in January.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-town-square.subjectsIntro: IGCSE is many subjects with very different cost profiles. These are the ones Town Square families buy help with, and what each is genuinely worth paying for.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The most commonly bought and the one where tier matters most, because Core and Foundation cap below the top grades. Paying specialist rates inside a capped tier buys something undeliverable. Algebraic manipulation is the highest-return topic in the subject.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Formula rearrangement, units carried through and precise definitions. Electricity and waves recur as weak areas. Where the Alternative to Practical route applies, it is reliably where the most marks are available relative to the effort of preparing for it.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry are the wall, and the required ion tests and qualitative analysis are heavily examined and quick to secure. A student who can balance an equation may still fail multi-step conversions under time pressure.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Recall volume plus command-term precision. The cheapest improvement available is teaching the difference between describe, explain and suggest, which takes weeks rather than terms and is almost never taught explicitly.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and the extended response carry the marks, and both are won on structure and register. Reading questions reward precise textual reference against the mark scheme, so retelling the passage is effort spent for nothing.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Good value for targeted work because the component skills are discrete and measurable. A short block aimed at one weak strand produces visible movement, which makes a fixed-scope purchase more sensible than an open-ended arrangement.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Diagrams must be drawn and then used. Data-response questions reward applying a concept and reaching a judgement, so money spent on memorising terminology is wasted while money spent on case practice is not.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Theory carries more weight than families expect, covering data representation, logic and networks. Students comfortable at a keyboard still lose marks hand-tracing algorithms, which is a narrow and inexpensive thing to fix.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.levels: Cambridge first and additional language routes
subjects.description: Mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Support must match the stream the student sits.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: A bridge to A Level or Higher Level Diploma maths. Worth paying for only if the intended post-16 route needs it, in which case it is worth paying for properly, because residual algebraic weakness is exposed immediately.

sections.heading: The extras nobody quotes you
paragraphs: The headline hourly rate is not the cost of tutoring, and the gap between the two is where families feel misled even when nobody lied to them. Here is what commonly gets added, and what to ask about before you agree anything.

Session length versus hour. A rate quoted per session rather than per hour is not comparable to one quoted per hour, and a fifty-minute session priced as an hour is a ten per cent increase nobody mentioned. Ask whether the figure is per hour or per lesson, and how long a lesson is. Then there is the minimum commitment: some providers quote a rate that assumes a block of ten or twenty sessions paid up front, and the single-session price is higher. Ask what happens if you stop after one.

Cancellation and rescheduling terms matter more in a community with a long school run, because traffic and illness genuinely cause late changes. A twenty-four hour cancellation policy with a full charge inside it is normal and worth knowing about; so is whether a missed session can be made up at all. Travel surcharges apply to in-home arrangements and are frequently quoted as a separate line into outer communities, which is honest but needs asking for.

Then the ones that are easy to forget. Assessment or diagnostic fees charged separately. Report or progress-review charges. Materials fees, which should make you ask what is being supplied, because awarding-body past papers and mark schemes are copyright and should not be sold to you by anybody. And VAT treatment — we will not state the UAE VAT position on tuition as fact without a Federal Tax Authority citation, so ask any provider plainly whether their quoted figure includes it.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context for a Town Square household
paragraphs: Tutoring is the discretionary line in an education budget that already has several non-discretionary ones, and seeing it in that context changes how it gets spent. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. So the fixed line is flat this year, which is a reason to spend the discretionary line deliberately rather than reactively.

The Dubai market is also expanding rather than contracting. KHDA reported 387,441 pupils across 227 private schools in 2024-25 offering seventeen curricula, with UK curriculum at 37% of enrolment, and the emirate is adding seven new private schools for 2026-27 — four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate — creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. A growing UK-curriculum cohort is why this market has so many general tutors advertising into it.

The practical question for a household is not what an hour costs but what a decision costs across two years. A fixed-scope block in Year 9 at published mid-band rates runs to perhaps AED 1,500-3,000 for six to ten sessions. A weekly session across Year 10 runs to roughly AED 6,000-12,000 at the mid band. A Year 11 specialist intensive across two subjects for five months can reach a similar total on its own, from a worse starting position.

The table below sets those out as indicative totals built from the published market bands rather than from our prices. They are not quotes. The purpose is the last column, which is the thing an hourly rate cannot tell you.

sections.heading: Four ways Town Square families waste money on IGCSE tutoring
paragraphs: These are the patterns we see most often when a family arrives after a year of paying somebody else, and each has a question that would have prevented it.

First, a budget generalist handed an exam-year student. At AED 33-65 an hour a capable graduate genuinely helps a Year 8 with homework. Put the same person in front of a Year 11 entered for Extended tier and they will teach plausible material that is not the specification, agreeably, for a term, with no change in paper performance. The low hourly rate is precisely what stops anyone examining the total. The preventing question: which specification do you teach, and at which tier?

Second, the wrong board. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1, or 0625 and 4PH1, set different papers with different tiering and practical routes. A term of the wrong board's past papers trains the wrong instincts about what a question wants, and it is invisible until the real paper arrives. One email to the school office prevents it.

Third, paying the travel premium for proximity when proximity was not the problem. In-home visits are published at AED 180-500 an hour including travel, and from Al Qudra Road a real share is driving. For a younger child who needs presence, that is money well spent. For a Year 11 working past papers it buys a journey. Fourth, buying five subjects in February when two could move and three could not — spending the specialist exam-year rate across a load that dilutes every session and exhausts the student.

sections.heading: The tier decision changes the value of every dirham
paragraphs: No amount of tutoring lifts a student above the ceiling of the tier they are entered for, which makes tier the first thing to establish and the thing parents are least often told clearly. Cambridge offers many subjects in Core and Extended versions; Pearson runs Foundation and Higher tiers. Core and Foundation cover a reduced syllabus and cap below the top grades.

Spending in the wrong direction is easy here, and invisible on an invoice. A family paying specialist rates for a child on Core, aiming at a grade the Core paper cannot award, is buying something that cannot be delivered. A family paying budget rates for a child on Extended who needs the full syllabus covered is buying something too thin to work.

The decision is usually taken by the department during Year 10 on class performance and is often reversible for a while. That window is where tutoring has its maximum financial leverage, because moving tier opens grades no amount of later practice can reach. Once the centre confirms entries, months before the papers, the question is closed and the money can only buy technique.

So the sequence that spends well is: establish the tier per subject, check it against the post-16 route your child actually wants, change it in Year 10 if there is a mismatch, and only then buy teaching. Reversing that order is how a family spends a year of fees inside a ceiling nobody mentioned.

sections.heading: Why the thing that tells you most is free
paragraphs: The trial lesson is one full lesson with the specialist who would actually continue, with no card required and no obligation. It is not taught by a salesperson and it is not a shortened sample.

It is free because explanation style decides whether the money works, and nothing written down predicts it. A tutor with exactly the right specification knowledge and the wrong pace for your child produces a term of pleasant sessions and no movement — and you cannot tell which you have hired from a profile, a qualification list or a phone call. One hour tells you. Charging for that hour would mean families commit on worse information, which is bad for them and, over time, bad for us.

The diagnostic sits before it. The student works through real questions from the correct board at the correct tier while a specialist watches. That is where the genuine gap appears, and it is usually narrower than the school report implies: method not written down, a command term misread, one topic missed during a move between schools.

Being precise about the word free matters, because it is misused in this market. Ours means one full lesson, with the proposed tutor, no card, no obligation to continue, and no condition attached. Where any provider attaches a condition to something described as free — a minimum block, a card on file, an eligibility rule — that condition should appear on the same screen as the word, and frequently it does not.
