sections.heading: Is the tutor you are paying permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: This belongs in a cost discussion because it is a risk you are carrying without being told. Private tuition in the UAE requires a permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits and issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. MoHRE's own service is Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through its smart app, website or e-services, with a stated two-working-day completion time.

The permit is granted free of charge for two years. That matters commercially: because it costs the tutor nothing and takes two working days, there is no price reason for anybody to lack one, and a tutor who cannot produce it has made a choice rather than faced an obstacle. Eligibility is wide — teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

MoHRE states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, and Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the amounts or detail the penalties, so any specific figure circulating informally should be disregarded. We are not going to repeat an unverified number on a page a parent might act on.

The permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, as do Abu Dhabi's ADEK professional-ethics rules for school staff there according to press reporting. Separately, an organisation operating tutoring from premises in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation or partnership, claims none, and has no UAE office or centre.

sections.heading: What we will not sell you
paragraphs: No guarantee of a grade, a tier change or an improvement. In a market where several ranking pages do offer guarantees, declining is information rather than modesty, and any guarantee worth the word would need published refund terms honoured on the same page.

No statistics without a sample size, a date and a method, which in practice means none at all. No average grades achieved by students we have taught, no percentage improved, no satisfaction score, no self-generated star rating. Competitors publish figures like 4.9 from several hundred reviews, occasionally in two conflicting versions on the same page, and none states how the number was produced. Self-asserted review markup is also against Google's structured-data policy.

No awarding-body material as downloads. Past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson; we cite and link them rather than hosting them, and you should ask why any provider charging a materials fee is supplying them. No description of tutors as examiners either, because current examiner status is not something we can evidence.

And no home visits anywhere in the UAE at any price, because there is no UAE visiting service to buy. What we will sell you is the smallest thing that solves the problem — if the diagnostic shows eight sessions on one topic, that is what we propose, even though a weekly arrangement running to the series would be worth considerably more to us. The scope goes in writing before the first session, and the review at the end is an honest review rather than a renewal conversation wearing a review as a costume.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE tutor cost for a Town Square family?
faqs.answer: The published Dubai spread, read in October 2026, runs from AED 33-65 an hour at the budget end (Tutopiya AED 33-52, EdFlik AED 45-65), through AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor (Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150), to AED 200-450 and above for a specialist (TutorChase AED 270, Bestimate AED 200-450+), with BartyED at AED 650 premium. In-home visits run AED 180-500 including travel. Those belong to the providers named, not to us. We quote after a diagnostic, because board, tier and year group change the answer.

faqs.question: What extras get added to a tutoring quote in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Seven things worth asking about before you agree anything. Whether the figure is per hour or per lesson and how long a lesson is. The single-session price with no block. What happens if you stop after one. The cancellation and reschedule policy, which matters with a long school run. Any travel surcharge into outer Dubailand. Whether diagnostics, reports or materials are charged separately. And whether the quoted figure includes VAT — nobody should state the UAE treatment as fact without a Federal Tax Authority citation, so ask about their own price.

faqs.question: Should a provider charge a materials fee for past papers?
faqs.answer: It should prompt a question. Past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables are the awarding bodies' copyright, and reproducing or selling them is infringement; for unreleased material there is a malpractice exposure too. We do not host or supply them — we cite the official source and teach from it. If a provider is charging you for awarding-body material, ask what exactly is being supplied and under what licence, because the value was never in owning the paper.

faqs.question: What should we budget monthly for IGCSE help in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's Dubai research puts specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000-2,000 or more a month for one weekly hour, with mid-tier at AED 600-1,200 and budget at AED 240-600. In practice Year 11 families often buy two or three sessions a week in the final term, which multiplies that figure, and frequently across more than one subject. Advertised packages include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four in-home two-hour visits. Buying the same total earlier across Year 10 generally costs less.

faqs.question: Is a cheap tutor ever good value for a Year 11 student?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and it is the most common expensive mistake in this market. At AED 33-65 an hour a capable graduate genuinely helps a Year 8 with homework and keeps them company through it. Handed a Year 11 entered for Extended or Higher tier, the same person teaches plausible material that is not the specification, agreeably, for a term, and the paper performance does not move. The low hourly rate makes the total feel small, which is exactly why nobody examines it until results day.

faqs.question: Does the in-home premium buy anything useful in Town Square?
faqs.answer: It buys physical presence, which is genuinely valuable for a younger or less self-managing child — somebody to take a phone off the table and notice attention going. For a Year 11 working through correct-board past papers it buys a drive down Al Qudra Road. In-home rates are published at AED 180-500 an hour including travel, and from this community a real share of that is the journey. There is also the apartment problem: in most Town Square homes the only available venue is the dining table.

faqs.question: When is IGCSE tutoring cheapest to buy?
faqs.answer: Year 9, which is when almost nobody buys it. A fixed-scope block of six to ten sessions on written explanation or algebraic fluency costs perhaps AED 1,500-3,000 at published mid-band rates and addresses the layer struggling Year 11 students usually turn out to need. It feels unnecessary because nothing is examined yet. Year 10 is next best, at roughly AED 6,000-12,000 across the year for a weekly mid-band session, and it arrives in Year 11 with content secure and the tier chosen deliberately rather than by default.

faqs.question: Can tutoring lift my child above their tier's grade ceiling?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge Core and Pearson Foundation tiers cover a reduced syllabus and cap below the top grades, so no amount of teaching inside that entry produces an uncapped grade. This is why tier is the first thing to establish and why paying specialist rates inside a capped tier buys something undeliverable. The decision is usually taken by the department during Year 10 and is often reversible for a while, which is where tutoring has its maximum financial leverage. Once the centre confirms entries, the question is closed.

faqs.question: How much does practising the wrong exam board cost?
faqs.answer: A term, usually, and it is invisible until the real paper arrives. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1, or 0625 and 4PH1, are different specifications with different tiering, paper structures and practical routes, and past papers are not interchangeable. A tutor drilling the wrong board teaches correct material while training the wrong instincts about what a question wants and how much to write. The preventing step is free: one email to the school office asking for the board and syllabus code per subject.

faqs.question: Are Dubai school fees going up, and does that affect tutoring budgets?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a household budget that means the fixed line is flat this year while tutoring remains entirely discretionary. The practical implication is to spend the discretionary line deliberately — a fixed-scope block with a written endpoint rather than an open-ended weekly arrangement that renews by default.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we actually pay for?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most Year 11 families start with. Three sessions a week across five subjects produces shallow coverage of all of them and a student too tired to use any. We would rather diagnose, name the two or three subjects where a grade can realistically move in the time available, concentrate there, and say plainly that the rest are better served by a November entry or the student's own revision. That conversation is unpopular, it costs us revenue, and it is the honest one.

faqs.question: Why is the trial lesson free and what is the condition?
faqs.answer: There is no condition: one full lesson with the specialist who would actually continue, no card required, no obligation. It is free because explanation style decides whether the money works and nothing written down predicts it — a tutor with the right specification knowledge and the wrong pace produces a pleasant term and no movement. Charging for the hour would mean families commit on worse information. If something elsewhere is described as free, check whether its conditions appear on the same screen as the word.

faqs.question: Does a higher hourly rate mean a better IGCSE tutor?
faqs.answer: Not reliably. The published Dubai top end is AED 500-650 and above, with BartyED at AED 650, and a premium rate reflects scarcity and reputation rather than demonstrated outcomes. Treat any claimed examiner status as a claim until it is evidenced, and note that examiner status gives nobody access to marking, boundaries or paper content whatever is implied. We do not describe our own tutors as examiners, because current examiner status is not something we can demonstrate. Specification knowledge plus the right pace is what you are paying for.

faqs.question: Do we have to keep paying once the gap closes?
faqs.answer: No, and we will tell you when it has. A fixed-scope block ends when the agreed topic list is covered, with a review and a deliberate stop rather than an automatic rollover into open-ended tutoring. An arrangement that continues by default is the quietest way a household overspends, and it is easy for any provider to let happen. If you want to continue weekly afterwards, that should be a decision you make rather than a drift you notice six months later.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need a permit, and does that cost us anything?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and costs the tutor nothing, so there is no price reason for anybody to lack one. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with MoHRE listing a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website or e-services. Eligibility covers school and sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Ask to see it. dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-umm-al-sheif.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach one subject each and work from the mark scheme rather than from a textbook. Ask one how a six-mark evaluate question is built; a specialist answers in the scheme's own terms, and that is the test worth applying.

intro.heading: Correct is not the same as credited
paragraphs: The most common complaint from a capable IGCSE student is that an answer was right and the mark was not. Usually both are true. Examination mark schemes do not pay for correctness in the abstract; they pay for specified things in specified amounts, and a student who has never read a mark scheme has never seen what those things are. They are writing to an audience whose rules they have not been shown, which is a strange way to spend two years.

The rules are not secret. Command words are defined and they differ: state wants a bare fact, describe wants an account, explain wants a reason linked to a consequence, compare wants both sides in the same sentence, evaluate wants a judgement supported by both sides. A student who answers all five with the same kind of paragraph will be credited on some and not on others, and will conclude that marking is arbitrary rather than that the instruction changed.

The second rule is development. In most written subjects a mark scheme credits a point, then credits what the point leads to, then credits the judgement built on it. A student who lists four correct points earns four marks where a student who makes two points and develops each earns six. On a paper with several extended questions that difference is a grade, and it is a writing habit rather than a knowledge gap.

The third rule is that the scheme rewards specificity. A named example, a figure, a precise term where a vague one would do. In economics that is a named country or policy; in business a named company or tool; in history a named individual, date or source; in English a quoted word rather than a paraphrased idea. Students supply the general version because it feels safer, and the scheme has nothing to credit.

Umm Al Sheif is an established villa district between Al Safa and Umm Suqeim, reached from Al Wasl Road and Sheikh Zayed Road, with no secondary school inside it. Children travel to schools along the Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim corridor and out toward Al Sufouh, home between about 3.45pm and 4.20pm. Teaching is one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run in India only, and for mark-scheme work a shared screen carrying the scheme, the question and the student's own answer side by side is the better instrument anyway. What follows is the command vocabulary in full, what a scheme credits and why listing loses, the answer structures for English, economics, business and history, the self-marking method, and which subjects convert technique into marks fastest.

sections.heading: The command words, and what each one is paying for
paragraphs: Command words are defined terms in both boards' specifications and they are the clearest example of a rule students are marked against without being taught. State wants a fact and nothing else, and a paragraph of context around a correct fact wastes time rather than earning marks. Describe wants an account of what happens without requiring a reason. Explain wants a reason linked to a consequence, which means the word because or its equivalent should appear in the answer.

Compare wants both items addressed in relation to each other, which in practice means a sentence containing both rather than two separate paragraphs. Suggest allows a reasoned possibility rather than a known fact, which students find uncomfortable and which is often the easier mark. Justify wants a choice defended against an alternative. Evaluate and discuss want a judgement with both sides weighed, and a conclusion that merely restates one side scores lower than one that acknowledges what has been set aside.

To what extent, which appears in several subjects, is the one students handle worst. It is asking for a degree rather than a yes or no, and an answer that argues entirely one way has not addressed the instruction even if every point is correct. The structural answer is to establish the strongest case for one position, establish the strongest case against, and then state which carries more weight and why, which is a shape rather than a content problem.

A student can be taught this in four to six sessions, practised on their own subjects, and the gains appear across every written paper simultaneously. That makes it the highest-leverage purchase in IGCSE tutoring and one that almost nobody sells, because it is not a subject and therefore does not look like a product. Ask a prospective tutor to explain what evaluate requires; the answer will tell you whether they work from mark schemes or from textbooks.

sections.heading: What a mark scheme actually rewards
paragraphs: A mark scheme is a list of creditable things, usually with an indication of how many of them earn how much. Reading one changes a student's behaviour permanently, which is why the first self-marking session is often the most useful hour of a year. The pattern across written subjects is consistent: a point earns something, the development of that point earns more, and a judgement built on developed points earns the top band.

The arithmetic consequence is that listing is a losing strategy. Four correct unconnected points on a six-mark question typically earn four marks and cannot earn six, because the scheme has nothing to credit beyond the points. Two points, each developed into its consequence, reach the same four and then access the remaining two. Students resist this because listing feels safer and faster, and because nobody has shown them the scheme that disagrees.

The second consequence is that specificity is creditable in its own right. Schemes in economics, business, geography and history frequently allocate a mark for application to a named context: the country, the business in the case material, the place in the case study, the source's provenance. Students supply a general version because it cannot be wrong, and in doing so forfeit a mark that was available for free to anyone who named something.

The third is that the scheme's language tells you the shape of the expected answer. A scheme that says one mark for identification and two for development is describing a three-part sentence. A scheme with level descriptors rather than point marks is describing a quality of argument rather than a quantity of content, and in those subjects more writing does not help while better-organised writing does. Teaching a student to read that distinction is a session, not a term.

sections.heading: English: the two papers and where the marks sit
paragraphs: In English as a first language, the reading response rewards the use of specific textual detail in service of a point about the writer's effect, and the directed writing rewards doing exactly what the task set out in the form and register it specified. Students lose marks in the first by paraphrasing rather than quoting, and in the second by writing a good piece that is not quite the piece requested. Both are task-handling problems rather than writing-ability problems.

The highest-return habit in English is planning, and three minutes is enough. A plan that fixes the order of points and the single idea each paragraph will carry produces an answer worth several marks more than the same student writing for three minutes longer unplanned, because structure is credited and volume is not. Students skip it because the clock feels hostile, and the clock is in fact the reason to do it.

In English literature the discriminator is close reading. A paragraph that quotes one word and says what that specific choice does outscores a paragraph that accurately retells a scene, because the scheme credits analysis of language rather than knowledge of plot. Students who have revised by rereading the text know the story thoroughly and have nothing to analyse under pressure, which is why past questions matter more than rereading in the final weeks.

In English as a second language the scheme is more mechanical and therefore more fixable. Accuracy, range, register and task completion each have their allocation, and the speaking component has its own. Speaking rehearses unusually well over video, because the examination format is already a structured conversation through a limited channel, and a recording made with consent lets a student hear their own hesitation and register in a way no amount of advice conveys.

sections.heading: Economics and business: the four-step answer
paragraphs: These two subjects are the clearest case of marks following structure rather than knowledge, which makes them the fastest subjects to improve under mark-scheme work. The standard extended answer has four moves. Define the term precisely, because the definition mark is free and routinely skipped. Apply the idea to the named context, which is a second mark available for naming something. Analyse the mechanism, which means tracing the consequence through at least one step. Then evaluate, weighing the alternative before stating a judgement.

Students typically perform moves one and three and omit two and four. They know what elasticity is and can explain what happens to revenue, and they do not tie it to the business in the case material or weigh the counter-argument. On a paper with several extended questions that pattern costs more than any content gap, and it is corrected in two or three sessions because it is a template rather than a body of knowledge.

Diagrams carry their own marks in economics and are treated as decoration by many candidates. A diagram with axes labelled, curves labelled, the shift arrowed and the new equilibrium marked earns its allocation; the same diagram drawn hastily with unlabelled axes earns nothing and has cost the same time. Students should be practising drawing them to a fixed routine until it is automatic, which takes a fortnight.

In business specifically, the application mark is the one to chase. The case material exists to be used: the business's size, sector, market and stated problem should appear in the answer. A general point about cash flow is worth little; the same point referring to the seasonal retailer in the case is worth the application mark as well. Students withhold the specific because it feels riskier, and the scheme rewards exactly the risk they are avoiding.

sections.heading: History: using a source rather than reading it
paragraphs: History mark schemes reward a specific move that students are rarely taught explicitly: using the provenance of a source rather than only its content. Who wrote it, when, to whom and for what purpose determines what the source is useful for, and an answer about utility that discusses only what the source says has missed the question. This is a technique rather than knowledge, it takes about two sessions to install, and it changes marks on every source question on the paper.

The second move is cross-referencing. Where two sources agree, the agreement itself is evidence; where they disagree, the disagreement is a question about purpose and audience rather than about truth. Candidates treat sources as a set of facts to be summarised, and the scheme is asking them to treat them as a set of claims with authors. Once a student makes that shift, source questions become among the most reliable marks on a history paper.

On extended essay questions the usual problem is organisation rather than content. A student who knows a great deal about a period writes everything they know in the order they learned it, and the scheme is asking for an argument that answers the question asked, which is frequently a to what extent question demanding a degree rather than a side. The fix is the three-minute plan: the strongest case one way, the strongest case the other, then a stated judgement.

Specificity matters more in history than almost anywhere. A named individual, a date, a named policy, a figure. Candidates revise narratives and arrive able to describe a process without being able to name anything inside it, and the scheme has nothing to credit for a well-written paragraph with no content markers in it. The practical revision instruction is to attach three names or figures to every topic, which is a memorisation task and finishes faster than students expect.

sections.heading: Self-marking: the method that makes a tutor unnecessary
paragraphs: The aim of mark-scheme teaching is for the student to stop needing it, which is a strange thing for a tutoring page to say and is the honest description of the work. The method is simple and has to be done rather than explained. The student answers a question under timed conditions. The student then marks their own answer against the scheme, writing a mark and a reason for each decision. Only then does the tutor mark it, and the discussion is about the gap between the two marks rather than about the answer itself.

That gap is the whole lesson. A student who gives themselves five and receives three has a specific misunderstanding about what the scheme pays for, and naming it once usually corrects it permanently. A student who gives themselves three and receives five is under-confident and is probably writing too much to compensate. Either way the conversation is about the scheme rather than about the student's ability, which is also a far easier conversation to have with a teenager.

The schemes themselves need translating at first. Bullet points in a scheme are not a required list but a set of creditable options, and students who believe they must hit every bullet write far too much. Level descriptors are not a checklist but a description of quality, and students who try to tick them off produce mechanical answers that sit in the middle band. A session on how to read a scheme is a prerequisite for the rest of the method.

We do not host or supply past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. They belong to Cambridge International and Pearson, the boards publish specifications on their own sites, and your child's school has legitimate access to the assessment material, including the schemes. A tutor working from that material inside a session is ordinary practice; a website offering a download library of it is distributing someone else's property. Ask the school first; in most cases the material a student needs is already available to them.

sections.heading: Which subject deserves the hours, by mark-scheme leverage
paragraphs: A Year 11 candidate carrying nine or ten subjects has to choose, and mark-scheme leverage is a better criterion than current grade. Some subjects convert technique into marks quickly because the knowledge is already present and simply uncredited; others need content and will not move in a hurry whatever the technique. Knowing which is which turns a limited budget into a better result.

The fast movers are economics and business, where the four-step structure is a template and the gains appear within a fortnight. English directed writing moves quickly for the same reason, because planning and task handling are mechanical. History source technique moves fast because provenance handling is a single learnable move. Geography case-study specificity moves fast once a student accepts that memorising three figures per topic is the work.

The slow movers are the sciences, where experimental and quantitative skills take longer, and mathematics, where a missing topic is a missing topic. That does not mean technique is irrelevant in those subjects; command words and accuracy routines pay there too. It means that if a choice has to be made between a slow mover and a fast mover at the same distance below target, the fast mover returns more for the same money.

The honest implication is that a family should often buy the subject that is not the worst. A student two grades below target in economics and two grades below in chemistry should probably buy economics, because the economics gap closes faster and the chemistry gap needs more weeks than remain. That is advice against our own interest in selling more hours, and it is the arithmetic.

sections.heading: What this costs, and what not to pay for
paragraphs: Mark-scheme work is unusually cheap relative to its effect, because it is bounded. A command-word block is four to six sessions. A self-marking block is three or four. A single-subject structure block is four to six. None of them is a subscription, and all of them end with the student able to do something they could not do before, which is the test of whether tutoring was worth buying.

The market figures, each published by the provider named and read in October 2026: budget online platforms advertise from AED 33 to 65 an hour, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. A qualified subject tutor online is quoted at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. IGCSE specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is absorbed, with Bestimate at AED 180 to 350.

For technique work the middle band is the right place to buy. Command words, answer structure and self-marking do not require a premium specialist, and a qualified subject tutor who works from schemes will do it as well as anybody at AED 500 an hour would. Where seniority earns its premium is content teaching in a difficult area and advice about tier or subject choice, neither of which is what this page is about.

What not to pay for: an open-ended weekly arrangement with no stated end point, a premium rate for marking practice papers, or three subjects at once when the mark-scheme work would pay in all of them simultaneously. The command-word block is the clearest example of a purchase that improves several subjects for the price of one, and it is worth asking for explicitly because almost nobody offers it as a product.

faqs.question: Why does our child write good answers and still lose IGCSE marks?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the answer is correct and not creditable. Mark schemes pay for specified things in specified amounts: a point, then the development of that point, then a judgement built on it. A student who lists four correct unconnected points on a six-mark question will score four and cannot score six, because there is nothing further to credit. Two points, each developed into its consequence, reach the same four and then access the remaining two. It is a writing habit, not a knowledge gap.

faqs.question: Our child answers describe and explain the same way. Does that cost marks?
faqs.answer: Describe wants an account of what happens and does not require a reason. Explain wants a reason linked to a consequence, which in practice means the word because or its equivalent should appear. A student who answers both with the same paragraph will be credited on one and not the other, and will conclude that marking is arbitrary. The same applies to compare, which wants both items in one relationship rather than two separate descriptions, and to justify, which needs the alternative addressed.

faqs.question: How do we handle a to what extent question properly?
faqs.answer: By giving a degree rather than a side. An answer that argues entirely one way has not addressed the instruction however correct each point is. The structure is to establish the strongest case for one position, establish the strongest case against it, and then state which carries more weight and why, naming what has been set aside. It is a shape rather than a content problem, which is why it can be fixed in two or three sessions and then applies to every such question.

faqs.question: What exactly is the application mark in Business Studies?
faqs.answer: A mark allocated for tying your point to the business in the case material rather than making it in general. The case exists to be used: its size, sector, market and stated problem should appear in the answer. A correct general point about cash flow earns the knowledge mark; the same point referring to the seasonal retailer described in the case earns the application mark as well. Students withhold the specific because it feels riskier, and the scheme rewards precisely the specificity they are avoiding.

faqs.question: Do economics diagrams really carry their own marks?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they are the most commonly wasted marks in the subject. A diagram with axes labelled, curves labelled, the shift arrowed and the new equilibrium marked earns its allocation. The same diagram drawn hastily with unlabelled axes earns nothing while costing the same time. The fix is a fixed drawing routine practised until automatic, which takes about a fortnight and then applies to every diagram question on every paper your child sits.

faqs.question: How do history source questions actually earn marks?
faqs.answer: Through provenance rather than content. Who wrote the source, when, to whom and for what purpose determines what it is useful for, and an answer about utility that discusses only what the source says has not answered the question. The second move is cross-referencing: where two sources agree the agreement is itself evidence, and where they disagree the disagreement is a question about purpose and audience. Both are single learnable techniques that take about two sessions to install.

faqs.question: Is three minutes of planning really worth it in an English exam?
faqs.answer: Reliably, yes. A plan that fixes the order of points and the single idea each paragraph will carry produces an answer worth several marks more than the same student writing unplanned for three minutes longer, because structure is credited and volume is not. Students skip planning because the clock feels hostile, which is exactly backwards: the clock is the reason to plan. The same three minutes pays in history and economics extended answers too.

faqs.question: What is the self-marking method and why does it work?
faqs.answer: The student answers a question under timed conditions, marks their own answer against the scheme with a mark and a reason for each decision, and only then does the tutor mark it. The discussion is about the gap between the two marks rather than about the answer. Over-marking reveals a misunderstanding of what the scheme pays for, which usually corrects permanently once named. Under-marking reveals under-confidence and over-writing. It also turns the conversation away from the student's ability.

faqs.question: Can we get the mark schemes and past papers from you?
faqs.answer: No. Past papers, mark schemes, specifications and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge International and Pearson. The boards publish specifications on their own sites and your child's school has legitimate access to the assessment material, including the schemes, so in most cases what a student needs is already available to them through school. A tutor working from that material inside a session is ordinary practice; a website hosting a download library of it is distributing someone else's property.

faqs.question: If we can only pay for one subject, which should it be?
faqs.answer: Often not the worst grade. Technique converts to marks at very different speeds: economics, business, history source questions and English directed writing move within two to four weeks because the knowledge is present and uncredited, while the sciences and mathematics need content and move slowly. A student two grades below target in economics and two below in chemistry should usually buy economics, because the gap closes within the weeks that remain. Better still, buy the command-word block, which pays in all of them.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our villa for these sessions?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time and does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run in India only. For mark-scheme work the screen is genuinely the better instrument, because the scheme, the question and your child's own answer sit side by side and can be annotated in place, with the annotated version surviving the session. A kitchen table cannot do that.

faqs.question: How long before we see mark-scheme work show up in results?
faqs.answer: On school assessments, two to four weeks in the fast-moving subjects, which is unusually quick for anything in education. Economics and business respond within two or three weeks because the four-step structure is a template. History source technique responds in two or three. English planning takes three or four. The sciences and mathematics take longer because command-word gains sit alongside content that may also need work. Measure it on marks for extended questions rather than on overall grades.

faqs.question: Is there any point starting this in Year 9?
faqs.answer: It is arguably the best time, and almost nobody does it. A student who enters Year 10 already distinguishing describe from explain, and already developing points rather than listing them, spends two years being credited for work they would otherwise have produced unrewarded. Four to six sessions in Year 9 is a small purchase with a two-year return, and it also keeps a higher-tier entry available by making the student's written work look stronger to the teachers deciding it.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-umm-al-sheif.closingHeading: Learn the scheme, then mark your own work
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-umm-al-sheif.closingBody: Most IGCSE students know more than their papers show, and the document that explains the difference is the mark scheme. Teach the command words, teach development rather than listing, insist on the named example, and then teach the student to mark their own answers against the scheme until their marks agree with a tutor's. That sequence is four to twelve sessions, it ends rather than continuing, and it pays in every written subject at once. Teaching is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; home tutoring is an India-only service. Last reviewed 22 October 2026.

intro.heading: The Umm Suqeim evening, and why it decides what tuition is possible
paragraphs: Umm Suqeim runs from Jumeirah Beach Road inland to Al Wasl and Sheikh Zayed Road, in three numbered sections of mostly villas. It has school gates of its own and sits a short drive from several more in Al Safa, Al Sufouh and Jumeirah. On paper that is convenient. In practice it means that between 2:45pm and 3:45pm the same two or three roads carry every family in the area in opposite directions at once, and the window a parent is trying to protect - homework, food, one useful hour of study - starts shorter than they expect.

That is the real constraint on IGCSE tuition here, and it is why this page is organised around the timetable rather than around subjects. A Year 11 student who gets home at 3:40pm, eats at 4:15pm and has football at 6pm has one workable slot, and it is narrow. Adding a tutor's drive across Dubai to that evening does not just cost money; it costs the slot. A session advertised for 5pm that starts at 5:20pm because Al Khail Road was slow is a session that finishes at 6:20pm, by which point the student has stopped absorbing anything.

Which brings the home-tutor question into the open. In-home tuition is a real and well-established part of the Dubai market, charged at roughly AED 180-500 an hour with travel included, and for some families it is worth it. IB Gram does not sell it. Home visits are a service we offer in India only, and there is no UAE address we will send anybody to. What we sell into Umm Suqeim is one-to-one tuition over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, which is the same teaching without the drive and without the premium that pays for the drive.

The gain is not only logistical. The pool of people who can teach Pearson Edexcel 4CH1 Chemistry to a student aiming at grade 8 is small in Dubai, and shrinks to almost nothing if you also require them to reach Umm Suqeim 2 by 5pm on a Tuesday. Removing the travel requirement puts the whole pool back in play, which matters most in exactly the subjects where families struggle to find anybody: Further Pure Mathematics, Computer Science, separate sciences at the top end.

What follows: the school-run timetable for the gates this area feeds, which board each of them is likely to be running and why you must check rather than assume, the market rates from cheapest upwards, the June and November series counted backwards from the exam to today, where marks actually disappear in Years 10 and 11, the Ministry of Education equivalency rule that should influence your child's subject choices, and the honest version of how to start - including when the answer is that your child does not need a tutor at all.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Years 10-11
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight to ten subjects, assessed by terminal written examinations with practical or coursework components in some subjects. Students usually sit in the June series, with November available as a resit or an early-entry route.

That is the detail most families get wrong when buying revision material, and it is the first thing a tutor should establish. Dubai's UK-curriculum schools are inspected annually by KHDA on a six-band scale.

programmes.name: International A Level, Years 12-13
programmes.description: Three or four subjects studied in depth over two years, with AS and A2 structures depending on the board. For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, the published requirement is one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside the five IGCSE subjects.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving Umm Suqeim run A Levels, and the subject your child drops at the end of Year 11 is the one they cannot pick up at AS. That makes Year 10 subject performance a gatekeeping issue rather than just a grade issue, which is a better reason to add tuition early than any marketing argument.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme, Years 12-13
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three Higher Level and three Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. UAE schools sit the May session. The DP demands breadth where A Levels demand depth, so an IGCSE student with no weak subject is better placed for it than one carrying a single collapse.

Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds three new International Baccalaureate schools. An IGCSE student switching to the DP needs Mathematics and a second language in reasonable shape, since both are compulsory.

programmes.name: Pearson BTEC and applied routes
programmes.description: Vocationally weighted qualifications assessed largely through units and assignments rather than terminal examinations. Available at some Dubai centres and occasionally the right answer for a student whose IGCSE profile is strong in practical subjects and weak under examination conditions.
programmes.countryNote: Availability in Dubai is patchy and changes, so check the current KHDA school listing rather than an older guide. For equivalency and university purposes a BTEC route needs checking with the Ministry of Education and with the target university directly, because the published equivalency rules on the British track are written around GCSE, IGCSE and A Level.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-umm-suqeim.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Umm Suqeim families book most often, with the syllabus codes to confirm with the school. The code matters more than the subject name: 0580 and 4MA1 are both called Maths and are assessed differently.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Cambridge 0580 Extended is examined through a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper. Pearson 4MA1 Higher runs two calculator papers. That single difference changes revision completely, and a student drilling the wrong one loses marks on arithmetic they were never asked to do without a calculator.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: In Cambridge 0625 the multiple-choice paper carries 30% of the grade, the theory paper 50% and the practical or alternative-to-practical component 20%. Marks concentrate in the theory paper, but the practical component is where unprepared students give away the easiest fifth of the qualification.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Same component weightings as Physics in the Cambridge version. The predictable losses are in moles calculations, electrolysis half-equations and organic reaction conditions, all of which reward drilled procedure rather than understanding, and all of which are teachable in a short block.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The highest-content science and the one where students lose marks to command words rather than to knowledge. 'Describe', 'explain', 'suggest' and 'compare' each demand a different answer shape, and a correct biological fact written in the wrong shape earns nothing.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences
subjects.description: A double or single award covering all three sciences rather than three separate qualifications. Content per science is reduced, which suits a student with a full subject load, but it closes some A Level and university doors. Check the target course before choosing it.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0500 First Language; Pearson 4EA1 English Language A
subjects.description: Assessed on reading comprehension and directed writing in both boards, with coursework options at some centres. The marks are in technique: inference questions have a mark-per-point structure, and a long beautiful paragraph answering the wrong question scores the same as a blank.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A different qualification from First Language English with different grading implications for university applications, and a common source of confusion when a family moves between school systems. Confirm which one your child is entered for before buying any revision resource.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Both reward structured evaluation, which is the single hardest skill to self-teach. High-mark questions need a judgement supported by two sides and a stated reason for preferring one; students who write everything they know and stop score in the middle every time.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Case-study subjects where the specified examples are not optional. A student who revises the concepts and invents the case studies loses the application marks, and that pattern is visible in almost every mock paper we see from Year 11.

subjects.name: Computer Science and Further Pure Mathematics
subjects.description: The two subjects Dubai families most often cannot staff locally. Further Pure Mathematics in particular has a small teaching pool across the whole emirate, which is the clearest practical case for taking tuition over video rather than by driving distance.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE home tutor in Umm Suqeim means in practice
paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor in Umm Suqeim, as the market sells it, is a qualified subject teacher who drives to your villa, teaches for an hour or ninety minutes, and leaves. Dubai rates for that service run roughly AED 180-500 an hour with travel included, and advertised monthly packages reach AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour visits. It is a legitimate product and plenty of families here use it. Three things about it are worth knowing before you buy.

The first is that you are paying for mileage. The in-home band overlaps almost exactly with the online specialist band of AED 200-450, and the gap at the bottom - AED 180 in-home against AED 150 online for a qualified subject tutor - is fuel, parking and unpaid driving time rather than better teaching. The second is that the tutor's journey becomes your timetable. If the drive from Al Barsha to Umm Suqeim 2 takes fifty minutes on a Tuesday, the session starts when the car arrives, and the student loses the end of their best hour. The third is selection: requiring a tutor who can reach your gate by 5pm reduces the pool to whoever lives nearby and is free, which in a subject like Further Pure Mathematics may be nobody at all.

IB Gram's answer is to drop the driving and keep the teaching. Lessons into Umm Suqeim are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the real school release time, with the student's own marked work on screen. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India, and we would rather say that in the second paragraph than in a footnote. The honest comparison is in the table further down this page, with the rates attributed.

What that buys an Umm Suqeim family is access rather than convenience. A Year 11 student sitting Pearson Edexcel 4CH1 gets a tutor who teaches that specification, rather than a generalist who teaches Cambridge 0620 and will adapt. For a grade-8 target those are not interchangeable, because the papers are structured differently and the mark schemes reward different phrasing.

sections.heading: The Umm Suqeim school run, hour by hour, and where a session actually fits
paragraphs: Everything about tuition scheduling in this area follows from one hour of the afternoon. Gates around Umm Suqeim, Al Safa and Al Sufouh release in a narrow band between roughly 2:45pm and 3:30pm, with secondary year groups generally later than primary. Jumeirah Beach Road and Al Wasl Road absorb all of it simultaneously, in both directions, and the inland exits to Sheikh Zayed Road queue at the same time.

A realistic reconstruction of a Year 10 weekday looks like this. Out of the gate at 3:15pm. Home between 3:30pm and 3:55pm depending on which section of Umm Suqeim and whether there is a younger sibling on a second run. Changed and fed by 4:30pm. Genuinely able to think between 4:45pm and 6:30pm, then declining. Anything booked before 4:30pm is booked against the child's attention, and anything starting after 7pm competes with dinner and fatigue.

That leaves a usable window of roughly ninety minutes to two hours, four or five days a week, and it is already contested by sport, Arabic homework, Islamic Education homework and whatever the school set. The practical consequence is that the most valuable thing a tutoring arrangement can do in Umm Suqeim is not add time but protect it. A session that starts exactly on the hour, every week, in the same slot, with no travel variable attached, is worth more over two years than a nominally longer session that starts late twice a month.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Edexcel: establish this before you buy anything
paragraphs: The single most common wasted expense in IGCSE tutoring in Dubai is work done against the wrong specification. Both Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel are widely used in this area, a single school frequently uses one board for sciences and another for mathematics or English, and the revision guides on the shelf in a Dubai bookshop cover both without making the distinction loud. Ask the school for the subject code in writing. Not the board name - the code.

The differences are not cosmetic. Cambridge 0580 Extended Mathematics is examined through a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper, while Pearson 4MA1 Higher runs two calculator papers; a student drilling the wrong pattern practises arithmetic they will never be asked to do unaided, or neglects the one thing that will catch them out. Cambridge sciences split into Core and Extended tiers with a grade ceiling on Core, and carry a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper worth a fifth of the grade. Pearson's International GCSE sciences are structured differently again, and Pearson reports on a 9-1 scale while Cambridge IGCSE reports A*-G.

There is an administrative trap worth knowing too. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. A parent in Umm Suqeim downloading a timetable from a search result rather than from the school has a real chance of reading the wrong one.

A tutor who asks for the codes in the first five minutes is doing the job. A tutor who does not ask is about to teach your child a competent lesson on the wrong paper structure, and you will not find out until a mock paper comes back with marks lost in places that make no sense.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition costs around Umm Suqeim, cheapest option first
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market rather than the top, because the bottom is where most of the waste happens. Published budget rates in Dubai begin at around AED 33-52 an hour from Tutopiya and AED 45-65 from EdFlik, putting the budget online band at roughly AED 45-150. For a Year 10 student who understands the content and will not sit down to work, that can be money well spent: supervision is a real service. For a Year 11 student who needs a 4CH1 paper marked against the mark scheme, it is not, because the tutor at that rate usually cannot do it.

The next band up is where IGCSE tuition actually lives. A qualified subject tutor working online runs AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Above that, IB and IGCSE specialists sit at AED 200-450 and upwards, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai guidance putting specialists at AED 200-450 or more. Premium named or examiner-led tutors reach AED 500-650, BartyED publishing AED 650. In-home one-to-one visits, travel included, sit at AED 180-500, with Bestimate quoting AED 180-350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200-500.

Monthly, that translates into Bestimate's own estimates for weekly one-hour sessions: AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Advertised packages include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Against school fees, which KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package, a single subject at mid-market online rates is a modest addition; four subjects is not.

Every figure above is another provider's published rate, read during the October 2026 research round, and is quoted as the market rather than as an IB Gram price. What to ask before you commit, in this order: the rate per 60 minutes rather than per lesson, whether VAT is included, the cancellation terms, whether the tutor teaches your child's exact syllabus code, and the tutor's MoHRE private tuition work permit position. The permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, so a provider treating it as an expensive obstacle has not read it.

sections.heading: The June series counted backwards from exam day
paragraphs: Nobody in this search cluster publishes a calendar, so here is one, built from the boards' own documents rather than from memory. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year. UAE candidates sit June and November; the February/March series is offered to India only, and a page quoting it to a Dubai parent is quoting a timetable from the wrong country.

Working backwards from the June series, the fixed points that matter to a family are these. Results: Pearson's June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026 - which tells you a November entry means waiting until the following January to know. Final entry deadlines sit months before the papers, set by the centre rather than by the family, so the school's internal deadline is the one to diary. Coursework and practical components are completed and internally marked well before the written papers begin.

For tuition planning the useful arithmetic runs the other way. From the June series, count back three weeks for timed full papers under conditions, eight to twelve weeks for a structured past-paper block, two terms for content repair in a subject that has gone wrong, and the whole of Year 10 for foundations. A family in Umm Suqeim starting tuition in February for a June series can realistically fix technique and the highest-mark topics. A family starting in May is buying reassurance, and should be told so.

Two practical cautions. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which means dates can be revised, so always work from the live official timetable rather than from a restated date on any website including this one. And for Cambridge, the zone allocation is not a formality: use the version of the timetable for your centre's zone, because Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam through using the wrong one.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks actually disappear in Years 10 and 11
paragraphs: The losses are predictable enough to list. First, command words. 'State', 'describe', 'explain', 'suggest', 'compare' and 'evaluate' each require a specific answer shape, and a factually correct response in the wrong shape scores nothing. This is the largest single source of avoidable loss in IGCSE sciences and humanities, and it is fixed by marking a student's own answers against the official mark scheme until they can predict the marks themselves.

Second, case studies and specified examples. Geography and History award application marks for named, specified material, and a student who revises the concept and improvises the example loses those marks every time. Third, arithmetic without a calculator, which on Cambridge 0580 Extended is an entire paper and on Pearson 4MA1 Higher is not - another reason the code matters more than the subject name.

Fourth, the practical component in Cambridge sciences, worth 20% of the grade through either the practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper. Students treat it as the easy part and lose marks on variables, repeats, table headings with units and graph conventions - all of which are learnable in two or three sessions and almost never revised. Fifth, evaluation in Economics and Business Studies, where the top band needs a judgement with two sides weighed and a reason given for the preference, and where writing more content instead reliably caps a student in the middle.

Sixth, and least discussed, the mock paper that never gets properly read. A marked mock is the most informative document a family will see in two years, and it is usually glanced at for the grade and filed. Going through it question by question against the mark scheme - what was the question asking, what did the mark scheme want, what did you write - takes an hour and typically identifies three recurring technique errors worth more marks than a term of re-teaching.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency and how it should shape subject choices
paragraphs: If there is any chance your child will apply to a UAE university or need their certificate attested locally, the equivalency rules should influence Year 10 subject choices, and almost no tutoring page in this market mentions them. On the British track, the published requirement is that students pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The detail that catches families out is the exclusion: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. A student taking eight subjects of which two are Arabic and Islamic Education has six that count, not eight, and a weak result in one of those six matters more than the headline subject count suggests. One competitor page currently ranking in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced rule is five, and getting this wrong in either direction leads to real decisions being made on bad information.

For the American track, the same source gives English proficiency as a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold is published in that source, so any page quoting one for IB equivalency is quoting something unverified - including, if it did, this one.

Two boundaries matter here. Equivalency and attestation are processes run by the Ministry of Education and the emirate authorities, not by a tutoring provider, and nothing on this page should be read as IB Gram performing or guaranteeing them. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, university admission or school progression; any provider implying that it is has invented an urgency the regulation does not contain. Verify the current rules on moe.gov.ae before acting.

sections.heading: Starting from Umm Suqeim, and the cases where tuition is the wrong answer
paragraphs: The starting sequence is short and the first step is free. Tell us the subject, the year group, the syllabus code if you have it and the school's release time. Send the most recent marked mock or assessment if one exists. We match a tutor who teaches that specification, you take a full-length trial lesson at no cost with your child's own work on screen, and you judge one thing: whether this person explains where the marks are rather than re-explaining the topic. If the match is wrong, say so and we change it.

Sessions then sit in a fixed weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time, set against the release time for your child's gate rather than a default hour. Lessons can move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan, holiday weeks often work better in the morning, and a slot can pause through a school's heaviest assessment week. Tell us the school assessment calendar at the start and the plan gets built around it.

Now the part a tutoring page is not supposed to include. Tuition is the wrong answer in several common situations. If a Year 10 student is coping with the content but not doing the work, a tutor becomes an expensive supervisor and the underlying problem survives into Year 11. If four subjects are weak at once, the issue is usually sleep, timetable load or something going on that no subject tutor can reach, and adding four tutors makes the week worse. If a mock grade dropped once in a subject that was previously fine, wait for the next assessment before spending anything. And if the exam is four weeks away and the content was never learned, the honest service is to help the student protect the grades they can still get, not to sell them a rescue.

What we will not do, stated plainly. We do not send anyone to a UAE address; home visits are an India-only service. We do not claim KHDA, ADEK, Ministry of Education, Cambridge, Pearson or IB approval or partnership, because IB Gram holds none of them. We do not supply or reproduce syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes - we reference and link the official sources and work from the school's own copies. We do not write coursework. And we publish no grade promises, because nobody honest can make one.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to our villa in Umm Suqeim for IGCSE lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. IGCSE tuition into Umm Suqeim is one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with your child's own marked work on screen. The reason is on this page rather than hidden: the Dubai in-home band of roughly AED 180-500 an hour overlaps the online specialist band almost exactly, so the premium pays for driving rather than teaching, and requiring a tutor who can reach your gate by 5pm cuts the available pool to whoever happens to be nearby and free.

faqs.question: What time should we book an IGCSE session if my child is in a school near Umm Suqeim?
faqs.answer: Plan for 4:45pm as the default and 5:00pm if the gate is in Al Sufouh or Al Barsha. Secondary year groups around Umm Suqeim, Al Safa and Al Sufouh release roughly between 2:45pm and 3:30pm, the beach road and Al Wasl Road absorb all of it at once, and a child is home between about 3:30pm and 4:25pm depending on which section you live in and whether there is a second school run. Add changing and food and the useful working window starts around 4:45pm and closes around 6:30pm.

faqs.question: Which syllabus code should I ask an Umm Suqeim school for before booking?
faqs.answer: Ask the school for the syllabus code in writing for each subject, not just the board name. A single Dubai school commonly uses Cambridge for sciences and Pearson for mathematics or English, and the codes are what resolve it: 0580 and 4MA1 are both called Maths and are examined differently, since Cambridge 0580 Extended includes a non-calculator paper and Pearson 4MA1 Higher does not. Cambridge sciences also carry a practical or alternative-to-practical component worth 20% of the grade. Buying revision material before you have the codes is the commonest wasted expense in this market.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest sensible way to get IGCSE help for a Year 10 student here?
faqs.answer: Published budget rates in Dubai start around AED 33-52 an hour from Tutopiya and AED 45-65 from EdFlik, and at that level you are buying supervision rather than subject expertise. For a Year 10 student who understands the content but will not sit down and work, supervision is genuinely useful and probably enough. For technique and mark-scheme work the band you need is a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. The cheapest real saving is starting in Year 10 rather than in Year 11, because repair under time pressure costs far more hours.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE exams sat by students in Dubai, and when do results arrive?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November. UAE candidates sit June and November; the February/March series is offered to India only. On results timing, Pearson's June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Always work from the live official timetable, since Pearson publishes provisional timetables that can be revised before a series.

faqs.question: My child's mock grade dropped in one subject. Should we start tuition straight away?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and a provider telling you otherwise is selling rather than advising. A single dip in one subject that was previously fine is often a bad paper, a missed topic or an off week, and the next assessment will tell you which. What is worth doing immediately and costs nothing is reading the marked mock question by question against the mark scheme: what the question asked, what the mark scheme wanted, what your child wrote. If that exercise shows the same technique error three times, a short block of tuition will fix it. If it shows one unlearned topic, the school can usually handle it.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are hardest to find a tutor for in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Further Pure Mathematics and Computer Science are the thinnest, followed by separate sciences at grade 8-9 level and Arabic as a first language. These are exactly the cases where insisting on someone who can drive to Umm Suqeim by 5pm leaves you with nobody, because the small pool that exists in the emirate is distributed by where people teach rather than by residential area. Over live video the request is answered from everyone qualified. If we genuinely cannot cover a combination at the time you need it, we will tell you that instead of placing a generalist.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we take tuition in at once?
faqs.answer: One, usually, and rarely more than two. Four weak subjects at the same time is almost never four subject problems; it is sleep, timetable load, or something else going on, and adding four weekly sessions makes a full week worse rather than better. One subject taught properly also tends to lift the others, because command-word discipline and mark-scheme awareness transfer. If your child genuinely needs help across the board, the more useful conversation is with the school about load and support, not with a tutoring provider about volume.

faqs.question: Does the Cambridge science practical component matter if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: It matters a great deal and it is where easy marks go missing. In Cambridge sciences the practical test or alternative-to-practical paper carries 20% of the grade, and the marks are awarded for controlled variables, repeats, table headings with correct units, graph conventions and conclusions that reference the data. Those are written skills assessed on paper, and they are teachable over video using the student's own past-paper responses. The hands-on laboratory work itself belongs to the school. What tuition adds is the discipline of writing up an experiment the way the mark scheme wants it written.

faqs.question: Can an Umm Suqeim session shift during Ramadan or an internal assessment week?
faqs.answer: Yes, and arranging it in advance works better than improvising. Sessions can shift to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan, and holiday weeks often suit a morning slot, which is useful for concentrated past-paper work. A slot can also pause through a school's heaviest internal assessment week, when an extra evening commitment reliably makes things worse. Send the school's assessment calendar when you book and the plan is built around it. The one thing we would not recommend is pausing through the eight weeks before the June series, which is when structured past-paper work pays most.

faqs.question: How should subject choices account for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. The detail families miss is that Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. A student taking eight subjects of which two are Arabic and Islamic Education has six that count. Verify the current rules on moe.gov.ae; equivalency is run by the Ministry and emirate authorities, and no tutoring provider performs or guarantees it.

faqs.question: What does a tutor need from us before the first IGCSE lesson?
faqs.answer: Four things, and they take ten minutes to gather. The subject and year group. The exam board and syllabus code, from the school in writing. The most recent marked paper, with the marks on it. And the time your child is realistically home and fed. The marked paper is the important one: it shows whether marks are going on content, on command words or on timing, and those need different first sessions. Without it a tutor spends the first hour on a diagnostic your child has already effectively sat at school, which you have then paid for twice.

faqs.question: Is an online lesson really as useful as someone sitting at the table?
faqs.answer: For IGCSE work it is, because almost all of the work is on paper and on screen. The tutor sees the student's written answer, annotates it live, and works through the mark scheme line by line - which is in practice easier shared on a screen than read upside down across a kitchen table. What online delivery does not provide is a physical presence to keep a reluctant student in the chair, and that is a real limitation worth naming. For a student who needs supervision rather than teaching, a parent in the next room during the session achieves more than a higher hourly rate.

faqs.question: What happens if the first tutor is not right for my child?
faqs.answer: You say so and we change the match, without a case to argue. The trial lesson exists precisely so this decision is made before money changes hands, and the thing to watch in it is whether the tutor can point at a specific question on your child's own paper and explain where the mark scheme awards the point. A tutor who re-teaches the topic instead is doing something the school already does. Mismatches are usually about pace and manner rather than competence, and a second match on the same subject code normally settles it.

faqs.question: Is an IGCSE tutor teaching an Umm Suqeim student required to hold a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists it as 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing'. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat quoted amounts sceptically.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-umm-suqeim.closingHeading: Fit the tuition to the clock you actually have
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-umm-suqeim.closingBody: The useful question in Umm Suqeim is not who can get to your door. It is what happens in the ninety minutes between the school run finishing and your child's attention going, and whether the person using that time knows the exact specification on the paper. Send the subject, the syllabus code and the time your child gets home, take a free trial lesson, and judge it on whether the tutor can show you where the marks are on your child's own work. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with no drive attached to either end.

intro.heading: Nobody near you needs to know your syllabus — your tutor does
paragraphs: Villanova is a townhouse and villa community off Al Qudra Road in the Dubailand belt, and its children attend schools scattered from The Sustainable City to Al Barsha. Those schools do not all teach the same IGCSE. Some run Cambridge, some run Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, a few run both across different departments, and a handful add Oxford AQA for one or two subjects. A tutor who lives four streets away and 'does IGCSE' may never have taught your child's specification.

This is the gap that makes the local search frustrating. Parents type 'IGCSE home tutor in Villanova' expecting a geography problem and discover a specification problem. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 cover similar content but assess it differently: 0580 is tiered into Core and Extended with two written papers, while 4MA1 is tiered Foundation and Higher and has its own paper structure and formula provision. Teaching one as if it were the other costs marks in exactly the places that are hard to diagnose afterwards.

So the useful filter is not distance. It is whether a tutor can tell you, without looking it up, which papers your child sits, what the tier ceiling is, and where that specification hides its marks. That filter does not care where the tutor sleeps, which is why IB Gram matches on board and tier and teaches the lesson live online, one-to-one. No tutor travels to a Villanova address — home visits are a service we run only in India — and the lesson reaches your child's desk instead.

Being clear about that upfront saves everyone a week. Independent in-home tutors do work in Dubailand and some are excellent; market rates for home visits run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel. If a person in the room is what your child needs, that is the market to approach. If what you need is a Chemistry 0620 specialist who has marked a hundred Paper 4s, geography is the wrong way to find one.

What follows is the information you would need to run that check yourself: how to find your child's board, the syllabus codes worth asking about, what the Dubai market charges from the cheap end upwards, who is legally permitted to tutor here, what the Ministry of Education actually requires for equivalency, and how the June and November series work for a UAE candidate. Sources are named throughout so you can verify rather than trust.

One framing point before the detail. Dubai has 227 private schools teaching 17 different curricula to 387,441 students, with the UK curriculum accounting for 37 per cent of enrolment, according to figures published by Dubai Media Office for 2024-25. That is a large and genuinely varied market, and it is why two Villanova neighbours can both say their child does IGCSE and mean materially different courses. The variation is the reason the specification question matters more here than it would in a single-board national system.
