sections.heading: Tutoring cost in the context of a Dubai school bill
paragraphs: Maths tutoring is bought out of a household budget that is already carrying school fees, and the Dubai fee position is unusually clear. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family modelling two years of IGCSE support, that holds one large variable still.

The sector around that decision is large. Dubai served 387,441 private school students across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with UK schools taking 37% of enrolment, Indian 26%, US 14% and the International Baccalaureate 7%. Seven new private schools join for the 2026-27 intake, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places; six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%.

The UK-curriculum share is why IGCSE maths tutoring is the most competitive segment of this market and the one where a family has most choice. That is good for price and bad for selection: the number of providers is large and the proportion who will ask which syllabus code your child sits is small. The screening question is cheap and it eliminates most of the field.

A closing caution about the regulators. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai and inspects schools; it does not license individual private tutors, which is MoHRE's responsibility through the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. That permit is granted free of charge for two years with a stated two-working-day completion time. No tutoring service should present a regulator's name as a credential it does not hold.

process.title: Get the syllabus code and tier from the school
process.description: Cambridge 0580, Cambridge 0607 or Pearson 4MA1, and Core, Extended, Foundation or Higher. Both facts in writing. Everything else, including which past papers are worth doing, depends on them, and no tutor can supply them for you.

process.title: Send a marked maths paper
process.description: A mock, a school assessment or a topic test with the teacher's marks visible. The patterns that cost marks are visible on a script in five minutes: method not shown, rounding too early, units missing, the same two topics failing repeatedly.

process.title: Agree a topic list and a session count
process.description: A named list of topics and habits, with an estimated number of sessions. A list can be crossed off, which is a progress record a parent can read. An open-ended commitment to improve at maths cannot.

process.title: Book short frequent sessions over live video
process.description: Two shorter slots a week generally beat one long block, particularly before mocks. Sessions sit around the Dubai school day, mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons, sport and prayer times, with no journey to arrange.

process.title: Re-test from the correct past papers
process.description: Every few weeks, a timed past-paper question set from the right specification, marked properly. The list shrinks or it does not. If it does not, the plan changes rather than continuing on hope.

whyPoints.title: Priced by the gap, not by the hour
whyPoints.description: The modelled table shows what a one-grade or two-grade gap costs at each published band and session count, so a Dubai family can sanity-check any quote. Three of the main competitors in this market publish no price at all.

whyPoints.title: Syllabus codes named
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580, Cambridge 0607 and Pearson 4MA1 are different examinations with different calculator rules. Exactly one syllabus code appears across the entire researched area cluster, which is why a 4MA1 candidate ends up revising 0580 papers.

whyPoints.title: Tier ceilings stated
whyPoints.description: Core and Foundation entries cap the grade available, and that cap can close A Level Mathematics and IB Analysis and Approaches. Families should know it in Year 10, not discover it with results in August.

whyPoints.title: The November series named as an option
whyPoints.description: UAE candidates sit June and November with Cambridge, and May/June and November with Pearson. The India-only February and March series does not apply here. A late gap has a real second route, and most pages never mention it.

whyPoints.title: Method marks insisted on
whyPoints.description: Written method is the habit that protects a candidate from arithmetic slips, and it is the largest single category of avoidable loss. It is unpopular to enforce and worth more than any additional topic coverage.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated plainly
whyPoints.description: One-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared writing surface and the correct past papers to hand. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India.

faqs.question: How much does it cost to raise an IGCSE maths grade in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It depends far more on when you start than on who you hire. A one-grade gap worked on from the start of Year 10 typically needs twelve to sixteen sessions, which at published Dubai rates of AED 150 to 250 an hour comes to roughly AED 1,800 to 4,000. The same gap addressed after a Year 11 mock usually needs more sessions and delivers less, because the work becomes triage. A two-grade gap in the spring of Year 11 is a different purchase and should be discussed alongside the November series.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths syllabus does my child's Dubai school use?
faqs.answer: You have to ask the school, and it matters. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A 4MA1 are all used across the emirate. They differ in paper structure, question style and calculator rules, so past-paper practice must match the code on the entry. A student revising 0580 papers for a 4MA1 examination is practising the wrong examination, and that is the commonest avoidable error in IGCSE maths revision here.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Core and Extended in Cambridge maths?
faqs.answer: Content and grade ceiling. Extended covers the full syllabus including the harder algebra, trigonometry and functions material and carries the upper grade range. Core covers reduced content and is capped below the top grades. The cap is the consequential part: a Core candidate can achieve the maximum available and still not meet an A Level Mathematics entry requirement. The tier decision rests with the school, which has two years of evidence, and any conversation about it belongs in Year 10 rather than Year 11.

faqs.question: When do UAE students sit their IGCSE maths exams?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February and March series is offered to India only, so it does not apply here, and material quoting it at a UAE family is wrong for their country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that candidates must use the correct zone timetable, so work from the school's own version.

faqs.question: Does anyone come to our home in Dubai for maths lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Maths support for Dubai families is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared writing surface both parties can write on. The in-home market here is real and quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the rate, and advertised in-home packages run AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month against AED 799 for eight online sessions.

faqs.question: Why does my child understand maths but lose marks in the exam?
faqs.answer: Usually because nothing is written down. Method marks exist so that a candidate who sets out a correct approach and then slips on arithmetic still collects most of the credit, and a student who writes only a final answer forfeits that protection entirely. In a multi-step question that converts a one-mark slip into a four-mark loss. The second common cause is rounding at each stage rather than at the end, which produces a final answer outside the accepted range after perfectly correct mathematics.

faqs.question: Can a tutor move my child from Core to Extended tier?
faqs.answer: A tutor can help a student acquire the content, but the school enters candidates and the school decides the tier. Moving from Core to Extended means learning material that was never taught, which is typically twenty or more sessions, and it has to be settled before entries close. The useful question to the school is not a demand but this: what would my child need to demonstrate, and by when, for the higher tier to be viable? Sometimes the honest answer is that it is not, and a secure lower-tier result is better.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths topics cost Dubai students the most marks?
faqs.answer: A small recurring set. Reverse percentages and compound interest get confused with one another. Area and volume scale factors are applied as though they were length scale factors in similar shapes questions. Bearings are mishandled. Histograms with unequal class widths are treated as bar charts. Graph transformations are half-remembered. None of these is conceptually difficult; they share a profile of being taught once, usually late in Year 10, and never revisited, which is exactly what makes a topic fail under examination pressure.

faqs.question: Is the non-calculator paper a problem for my child?
faqs.answer: It can be, and it catches students who prepared assuming a calculator throughout. The current Cambridge 0580 structure includes a non-calculator paper at both tiers, while Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator on both papers and Cambridge 0607 requires a graphical calculator. Non-calculator fluency, meaning confident work with fractions, decimals, index laws and standard form by hand, is a separate skill that needs separate practice. Confirm the current paper structure and permitted equipment with the school rather than from summaries found online.

faqs.question: Should we plan for the November series instead of June?
faqs.answer: It is a real option and worth considering rather than dismissing. A student whose January mock sits two grades below target can push for the summer series or plan for November with several additional months of preparation. The decision belongs with the school, because it affects post-16 applications and entry administration, but it exists. A provider that sells a compressed programme of sessions without mentioning that the second series is available is not giving a Dubai family complete advice.

faqs.question: How early is too early for IGCSE maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: Year 9 is not too early, and it is the best value in the whole course. The IGCSE syllabus assumes fluency with fractions, negative numbers, index laws, rearrangement and proportional reasoning, and a student who starts Year 10 shaky on those carries the deficit through two years of new content. Fluency work also suits the lower published rate bands, because the job is clear explanation and repetition rather than criteria-level marking, so it is both the cheapest and the most effective intervention available.

faqs.question: Does my child need Additional Mathematics as well?
faqs.answer: Only if the Year 10 evidence supports it. Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 is taken alongside IGCSE Mathematics by stronger candidates in some Dubai schools as a bridge towards A Level, and it is genuinely useful preparation. It is also a substantial extra load in an examination year. The decision should rest on a marked Year 10 mock rather than on ambition, because a weakened main maths grade is a worse outcome than no Additional Mathematics at all.

faqs.question: Will maths tutoring help my child's physics and chemistry too?
faqs.answer: Frequently, yes, because a lot of what looks like science weakness is maths weakness wearing a lab coat. Rearranging equations, standard form, units and graph gradients are maths skills assessed in a physics paper. Moles, concentration and percentage yield are proportional reasoning. A student losing calculation marks across three sciences usually has one underlying problem, and fixing it in a maths session is cheaper than hiring three science tutors to work around it.

faqs.question: Do maths tutors in Dubai need a government permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Any individual providing private tuition in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, and warns that tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: What if no tutor is free for our specification and tier?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than substituting quietly. IGCSE maths is the busiest segment of the Dubai market, so availability is usually good, but demand concentrates sharply in the weeks after mock results and a specific match on 0607 or on a particular tier can be narrower. The options are a start date in the future, a tutor who covers the content but not that exact specification for interim fluency work, or a recommendation to wait. Families should know which of those is on offer.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor.closingHeading: Get the code and the tier, then price the gap
dubai/igcse-maths-tutor.closingBody: Ask the school for two things in writing: the syllabus code your child is entered for and the tier. Then send a marked paper and take the free trial session, which will produce a named list of topics and habits and an honest estimate of how many sessions it takes. A list can be crossed off and checked; a promise to improve at maths cannot. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time with a shared writing surface; home visits are not part of our UAE service. Every AED figure here was published by the provider named and read in October 2026.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-barari.tutorsIntro: These tutors cover Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE mathematics for Al Barari and the surrounding Dubailand communities. Each teaches a named syllabus and tier, and you meet the tutor who would take every session before committing.

intro.heading: Two qualifications, two sets of rules, one street
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject Dubai parents most often seek a tutor for, and it is also the subject where picking the wrong tutor is hardest to detect. A good mathematician can teach a competent lesson on any IGCSE topic. What they cannot do, without knowing the specification, is tell your child which paper a topic appears in, whether a calculator will be available when it does, and where that board's mark scheme awards method credit. Those are the things that move a grade in Year 11.

In Al Barari this is not an abstract risk. The community has no school inside its gates, so pupils commute out — north to Nad Al Sheba, west to Motor City and the Arabian Ranches, or deeper into Dubailand. Those schools do not all use the same awarding body. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580, tiered as Core and Extended. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A is 4MA1, tiered as Foundation and Higher. A tutor recommended by a neighbour may be excellent on the one your child does not sit.

The calculator rule is the clearest illustration. Edexcel 4MA1 allows a calculator in both papers. Cambridge's current 0580 structure pairs a non-calculator paper with a calculator paper at each tier, and that structure was revised relatively recently, so confirm with the school which papers your child actually sits. A student who has spent two years with a calculator in hand and then meets a non-calculator paper loses marks across the whole thing, not in one topic.

The second decision that matters more than families realise is the tier. A Core or Foundation entry caps the grade that can be awarded no matter how well the paper is answered. The Extended and Higher tiers reach the full range and are effectively prerequisites for A Level Mathematics and for IB Analysis and Approaches. If your child is on the lower tier in a subject they intend to continue, that is a conversation with the school now, while the entry can still move, and a marked higher-tier past paper is the most persuasive thing you can bring to it.

One more thing worth knowing before you hire: a school report that says mathematics is weak does not distinguish between a missing topic and algebraic fluency that was never secure. Those look identical on a report card and need entirely different responses. A missing topic is a session or two. Fluency built on sand is a holiday block of four or five sessions a week, because fluency comes from volume rather than from being explained again. Establishing which one you are dealing with is the first hour of useful work, and it is the hour most tutoring skips.

IB Gram delivers mathematics tuition to Al Barari as live one-to-one lessons over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For mathematics that costs almost nothing — a session is worked problems on a shared screen with the student's own working visible — and it widens the shortlist to every tutor who teaches your child's exact syllabus and tier.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-barari.programmesIntro: An IGCSE maths tutor is wanted at one of four points in a Dubai school career, and the job is different each time. These are the stages, with what is still changeable at each.

programmes.name: Year 9, before the course begins
programmes.description: The cheapest intervention available and the rarest booking. Work here is algebraic fluency: expanding, factorising, rearranging and solving with confidence rather than with effort. The IGCSE specification assumes this fluency and spends no time building it, so a pupil who enters Year 10 shaky spends two years paying for it.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this coincides with option choices and the provisional tier decision, which most families do not realise is happening. A marked assessment from a tutor at this point gives you something concrete to bring to the school's conversation about which tier your child is placed in.

programmes.name: Year 10, building the grade
programmes.description: The year the grade is made. A tutor consolidates each topic as the school teaches it, builds method and units discipline before questions lengthen, and introduces past-paper questions from the first term so that the paper is familiar long before a mock. The marks gained per hour are higher here than at any later point.
programmes.countryNote: Al Barari commutes make a five o'clock weekday start realistic, so many Year 10 families here do better with a weekend morning. Dubai school breaks also allow four or five sessions a week, which is the only practical way to rebuild fluency that was never secure.

programmes.name: Year 11, after the mocks
programmes.description: The most common booking. The first session reads the marked mock question by question to establish whether marks went to content, method, units or timing, and teaching then follows the mark distribution rather than the syllabus order. Two sessions a week to the series is typical, with one timed paper every fortnight.
programmes.countryNote: The series matters. Cambridge runs June and November for UAE candidates and Pearson Edexcel runs May/June and November, with entries closing months in advance through the centre. A resit after results is entered for the next series rather than taken whenever suits, so the decision window is narrower than families expect.

programmes.name: Bridging into A Level or IB mathematics
programmes.description: The summer after IGCSE is the most underused tutoring window in the whole school career. A Level Mathematics and IB Analysis and Approaches both assume algebraic fluency well beyond what a comfortable Extended pass demonstrates, and both start at pace. Six sessions across a summer prevents a term of catching up.
programmes.countryNote: Schools near Al Barari split both ways at sixteen, into A Levels or the IB Diploma. Either route rewards having taken Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 or Pearson Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1, and a pupil who took neither benefits most from a bridging block before Year 12 begins.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-barari.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE mathematics topics Al Barari families ask about, with where the marks actually go. Topic weakness repeats across both boards, which is why this list is organised by content rather than by syllabus.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging and simplifying. The strongest single predictor of a mathematics grade, because every later topic is carried by it. A pupil who hesitates over rearranging a formula will lose marks in physics and chemistry too, which is why maths tutoring often improves three subjects.

subjects.name: Equations and inequalities
subjects.levels: Both boards, extended at the higher tier
subjects.description: Linear, simultaneous and quadratic equations, then inequalities and regions. Quadratics by completing the square and by formula are higher-tier staples, and the error pattern is sign management rather than method. Showing the substitution step earns marks the final answer alone does not.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.levels: Both boards, extended at the higher tier
subjects.description: Sketching, transformations, intersections and, at the higher tier, inverse and composite functions. Students lose marks by plotting rather than sketching, which wastes time, and by failing to label intercepts and asymptotes that the question explicitly asks for.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.levels: Both boards, extended at the higher tier
subjects.description: Right-angled trigonometry, then the sine and cosine rules and bearings. Bearings questions are reliably lost through diagram errors rather than trigonometry errors, and the habit that fixes it is drawing north lines at every point before any calculation begins.

subjects.name: Geometry and circle theorems
subjects.description: Angle reasoning, similarity, congruence and circle theorems. Circle theorems are learnable in two sessions and then yield marks every series, but only if the student names the theorem used. Unnamed reasoning loses the communication marks even when the answer is right.

subjects.name: Mensuration and compound measures
subjects.description: Area, volume, surface area, arcs and sectors, plus speed, density and pressure. The dominant loss is unit conversion, especially between volume units, and it costs a mark at a time across the whole paper rather than failing one question.

subjects.name: Number, ratio and proportion
subjects.description: Percentages, reverse percentages, compound interest, direct and inverse proportion, standard form and bounds. Reverse percentage questions are the most commonly failed topic on the lower tiers, and upper and lower bounds the most commonly failed on the higher ones.

subjects.name: Sequences
subjects.levels: Both boards, extended at the higher tier
subjects.description: Linear and quadratic nth terms, and geometric sequences at the higher tier. Quadratic nth term is a procedure that can be taught once and used forever, and it is a frequent source of free marks for students who have simply never been shown the method.

subjects.name: Probability and set notation
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, Venn diagrams, conditional probability and set language. Conditional probability is the standard trap: students multiply along the wrong branch or forget that the denominator has changed. Drawing the tree before reading the question again is the fix.

subjects.name: Statistics
subjects.description: Averages from tables, cumulative frequency, histograms and box plots. Histograms with unequal class widths are the reliable higher-tier loss, because frequency density is a step students skip. Interpretation questions want a comparison in context, not a restatement of a figure.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, vector geometry proofs and the four transformations. Vector proof questions reward writing the route algebraically before attempting a conclusion, and students who try to reason from the diagram alone generally lose the method marks.

subjects.name: Non-calculator arithmetic
subjects.description: Fractions, surds, indices, standard form and exact values worked by hand. For pupils sitting a non-calculator paper this is a skill set in its own right, and it decays quietly over two years of calculator use. The only way to find out whether it is intact is to take the device away in a session.

sections.heading: 0580 against 4MA1, paper by paper
paragraphs: The two qualifications are not interchangeable and the differences are operational rather than philosophical. Both tier the course, both sit two papers, and both cover broadly similar mathematics. Where they diverge is in calculator access, paper length and how topics are distributed between the papers, and each of those changes how a student should prepare.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, 4MA1, sets two papers of two hours each with a calculator permitted in both. That makes efficiency with the device a genuine skill worth teaching, and it means the written method is where the marks are protected, because a calculator answer with no working is exposed. Cambridge 0580's current structure pairs a non-calculator paper with a calculator paper at each tier, which adds an entire skill set — hand arithmetic, surds, indices and exact values — that an Edexcel candidate never needs.

That single difference is the most common reason a recommended tutor underperforms in this neighbourhood. A tutor who has taught Edexcel for years has never had to prepare a candidate for a non-calculator paper, and will not instinctively remove the device in a session. The student discovers the gap in a mock, which is late. The reverse is milder but real: a Cambridge-trained tutor may under-teach calculator efficiency to an Edexcel candidate who could be saving minutes per question.

Cambridge's paper structure was revised relatively recently, so confirm with your child's school which papers they actually sit before planning around any description, including this one. The table sets out the comparison as a structural guide; the current specification on the awarding body's own site is the authority and should be checked for the series your child is entered for.

sections.heading: The tier decision, and how to argue it with evidence
paragraphs: The tier entry is the most consequential administrative decision of the two years and it is usually made quietly, in Year 10, on the basis of a school assessment. A Core or Foundation entry caps the grade that can be awarded regardless of performance on the day. The Extended and Higher tiers reach the full range, and they are effectively prerequisites for A Level Mathematics and for IB Analysis and Approaches at either level.

Schools make these decisions for sound reasons: a student placed on a tier they cannot cope with will underperform badly, and a secure grade on the lower tier is better than a poor one on the higher. The failure mode is not that schools decide badly, it is that they decide early, on limited evidence, and families do not realise a decision has been made until the entry has gone in. Entries close months before papers are sat.

So the useful move is evidential rather than argumentative. Ask the school directly which tier your child is provisionally entered for and when the entry closes. If the answer is the lower tier and your child intends to continue mathematics, ask what evidence would support a change. In almost every case the answer is performance on a higher-tier paper, which is exactly what a tutor can produce: a full past paper at the higher tier, worked under timing and marked against the published scheme, with the mark breakdown attached.

That document does two honest jobs. If the mark is respectable, you have a concrete case to put to the school rather than a parental opinion. If it is not, you have found out in Year 10 that the lower tier is the right call, which is also worth knowing, because it redirects the tutoring towards securing a strong grade on the tier your child will actually sit rather than chasing one they will not.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE maths marks actually go
paragraphs: Mark a paper rather than asking the student and the picture changes. In IGCSE mathematics a large share of lost marks comes from four repeated behaviours rather than from absent content, and all four respond quickly to deliberate practice with someone watching.

Unshown method comes first. Mark schemes award credit for steps, so a correct answer with nothing written scores below a wrong answer with sound working. The pupils most affected are the quick ones who have been praised for mental arithmetic since primary school, and they are usually surprised to learn that their strength is costing them. Units and conversions come second: a mark at a time across the paper, concentrated in volume and compound-measure questions, adding up to a grade boundary.

Third is incomplete answers to questions that ask for more than a number. Circle theorem questions want the theorem named. Statistics questions want a comparison in context. Vector proofs want the route written algebraically. In each case the student knows the mathematics and loses the communication marks. Fourth is timing, which only becomes visible under full-length conditions: a pupil who spends fourteen minutes on a six-mark question will not finish, and unanswered questions score nothing however well the material is understood.

Genuine content gaps do exist and are usually narrow and nameable: reverse percentages, upper and lower bounds, histograms with unequal class widths, conditional probability, quadratic nth term, vector proof. Each is a session or two. What takes a year is algebraic fluency that was never secure, which is why a Year 10 diagnosis is worth so much more than a Year 11 one.

sections.heading: What the top grades actually require
paragraphs: Parents in this part of Dubai frequently ask what it takes to reach the top of the scale, and the honest answer is less dramatic than expected. It is not a different kind of mathematics. It is the same content executed with almost no leakage, plus genuine competence on the handful of topics that only appear at the higher tier.

Leakage is the operative word. A student who understands everything and drops a mark for units here, an unnamed theorem there, a sign error in the third line and an unfinished final question has lost enough to sit two grades below their understanding. Closing that gap is unglamorous work: full papers under timing, marked against the published scheme, with every lost mark categorised rather than merely corrected. Most students have never had their losses categorised, so they revise content they already know.

The higher-tier-only topics are the second half. Depending on the board and tier these include upper and lower bounds, histograms with unequal class widths, vector proof, function notation, and the harder algebraic manipulation. These are each teachable in a session or two and then reliable, which makes them unusually good value late in Year 11 when content teaching has stopped being realistic.

What we will not do is tell you a block of sessions produces a particular grade. Nobody can control that, and any provider offering it is guessing or guaranteeing something outside their power. What a tutor can honestly say, after a marked diagnostic paper, is where the marks are currently going and which of those categories the remaining weeks can realistically close. That is a more useful sentence than a promise, and it is checkable against the next mock.

sections.heading: Supply in Al Barari against the communities next door
paragraphs: A proximity search is how most families begin, so it is worth saying what it delivers here. For IGCSE mathematics at the lower tiers and for Year 9 support, local supply across the Dubailand communities is genuinely reasonable. Mathematics is the most commonly taught subject and plenty of competent teachers in Dubai will travel. At the higher tier, and particularly for non-calculator preparation on Cambridge or for tier-change evidence, the pool narrows.

Group tuition centres are the other local option and they deserve an honest mention. A group class at a centre costs considerably less per hour than one-to-one and works well for a student whose problem is pace and practice rather than a specific gap. It works poorly for a student with an identifiable weakness, because a group cannot stop for one person's algebra. If your child's mock losses were spread evenly across the paper, a group may be enough; if they were concentrated in three topics, it will not be.

What differs between these communities is scheduling, not supply. A Nad Al Sheba pupil can start at half past four; an Al Barari or Arabian Ranches 3 pupil realistically starts at five. For mathematics that matters more than in most subjects, because full-length timed papers need a rested student and a clear two hours. A paper attempted at seven in the evening after a commute produces a misleadingly poor result and knocks confidence for no useful reason.

In-home rates also rise with distance from the centre, so the further out the community, the worse the value a proximity search returns. The premium buys presence rather than specialism. For mathematics, where the session is worked problems on a shared screen with the student's own working visible and a paper marked in front of them, presence is the component least needed.

sections.heading: Permits, papers and the limits of what we will supply
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permit-regulated and most Dubai parents have not been told. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE is subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws.

MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website and e-services system, so a tutor who says the permit is expensive or optional is wrong on both counts. No fine amount appears on this page: Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, and the figure circulating online could not be verified. Nor is IB Gram approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and nobody in this market should imply such a thing without a permit number.

On materials, the limit is firm. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and reproducing or distributing them is copyright infringement. A tutor works through questions from legitimately obtained material and teaches the student to read a mark scheme themselves, which is the more durable outcome: a student who understands where credit is awarded writes differently on the next paper, whereas one handed answers does not.

Two claims to be sceptical about wherever you meet them. Examiner status, which we do not use as a selling point for anyone whose current status cannot be evidenced, and which in any case gives no access to marking, boundaries or unseen papers. And grade guarantees, which we will not offer because nobody can control the outcome. What we will give you after a marked diagnostic is a categorised list of where the marks are going and an honest view of which categories the remaining weeks can close.

faqs.question: Does my child's IGCSE maths paper allow a calculator?
faqs.answer: It depends on the board. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, 4MA1, permits a calculator in both papers. Cambridge 0580's current structure pairs a non-calculator paper with a calculator paper at each tier, and that structure was revised relatively recently, so confirm with the school which papers your child sits. The difference matters more than it sounds: a student who has used a calculator for two years and then meets a non-calculator paper loses marks across the whole paper rather than in a single topic.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge 0580 and Edexcel 4MA1?
faqs.answer: They are separate qualifications covering broadly similar mathematics with different paper structures, different tier names and different calculator rules. Cambridge tiers as Core and Extended and sets a non-calculator paper alongside a calculator one. Edexcel tiers as Foundation and Higher and allows a calculator throughout. Cambridge reports some syllabuses on A* to G and others on 9 to 1, while Edexcel reports on 9 to 1. A tutor who has taught only one will not instinctively prepare a candidate for the other's demands.

faqs.question: How do I get my child moved from Core to Extended maths?
faqs.answer: Ask the school which tier your child is provisionally entered for, when the entry closes, and what evidence would support a change. In almost every case the answer is performance on a higher-tier paper, which a tutor can produce: a full past paper at the higher tier worked under timing and marked against the published scheme, with the breakdown attached. That document is honest in both directions. If the mark is weak, you have learned in Year 10 that the lower tier is the right call and the plan should change accordingly.

faqs.question: What does a full Year 11 maths tutoring block actually cost?
faqs.answer: Take two sessions a week from a January mock to a June series, around twenty weeks or forty hours. At Dubai market rates read in October 2026 that is roughly AED 1,800 to AED 6,000 at the budget tier, AED 6,000 to AED 12,000 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 8,000 to AED 18,000 or more for a specialist, and AED 7,200 to AED 20,000 for in-home delivery including travel. Those are published market figures, not IB Gram prices. Seeing the block total rather than the hourly rate is how families make this decision properly.

faqs.question: Is a group class at a Dubai tuition centre good enough for maths?
faqs.answer: It depends on the shape of the losses. A group class costs considerably less per hour and works well for a student whose problem is pace and practice volume rather than a specific gap, because the content is being covered again at a manageable speed. It works poorly where losses are concentrated in three or four topics, since a group cannot stop for one student's algebra. Look at the marked mock: evenly spread losses suit a group, concentrated ones need one-to-one attention on those topics.

faqs.question: Which topics are worth most late in Year 11?
faqs.answer: The higher-tier-only topics, because each is teachable in a session or two and then reliable. Depending on board and tier these include upper and lower bounds, histograms with unequal class widths, vector proof, function notation, quadratic nth term and the harder algebraic manipulation. Alongside them, the leakage categories: unshown method, unit conversions and unnamed reasoning in circle theorems and statistics comparisons. Content teaching stops being realistic late in Year 11, but those two groups together often move a grade.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor to houses in Al Barari?
faqs.answer: No. All UAE tuition is delivered live and one-to-one over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are a service we run only in India and no tutor is sent to any UAE address. For mathematics this costs very little, because a session consists of worked problems on a shared screen with the student's own working visible and a paper marked in front of them. What it gains is a shortlist of tutors who teach your child's exact syllabus and tier rather than those who will drive to a villa community at five.

faqs.question: My child's answers are right but the marks are low. Why?
faqs.answer: Because mark schemes award credit for method, so a correct answer with no visible working scores below a wrong answer with sound working. The students most affected are the quick ones who have been praised for mental arithmetic since primary school and are genuinely surprised that their strength is costing them. The other common causes are unit errors in volume and compound-measure questions, and unnamed reasoning where a circle theorem question wants the theorem stated. All three are habits and all three respond to a few weeks of enforced working.

faqs.question: Should we start maths tutoring in Year 10 or wait for the mocks?
faqs.answer: Year 10, and the argument is financial as well as educational. Weekly sessions across Year 10 and Year 11 typically need fewer total hours to reach the same grade than a compressed Year 11 rescue, because nothing has to be undone and no content is being taught against a deadline. Sixty weeks at one session a week costs roughly what forty hours of panic costs, and produces a calmer household. Year 10 is also when a mismatched tier entry can still be challenged with evidence.

faqs.question: What should we do in the summer after IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: Six to eight bridging sessions, which is the most underused window in a school career. Both A Level Mathematics and IB Analysis and Approaches assume algebraic fluency well beyond what a comfortable Extended or Higher pass demonstrates, and both start at pace in the first week of Year 12. A short summer block covering manipulation, logarithms and early calculus notation prevents a difficult first term. It is cheaper than the catch-up tutoring that otherwise starts in October.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths topics do UAE students lose most marks on?
faqs.answer: Reverse percentages at the lower tiers, and upper and lower bounds plus histograms with unequal class widths at the higher ones. Conditional probability is a consistent trap because students multiply along the wrong branch or forget the denominator has changed. Bearings questions are lost through diagram errors rather than trigonometry, and vector proofs through trying to reason from the diagram instead of writing the route algebraically. Each of those is one or two sessions of work, which is why a categorised diagnostic is worth so much more than general revision.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does IGCSE maths need?
faqs.answer: One a week through Year 10, rising to two in the term before the series if the mock evidence supports it. Beyond two in term time the limiting factor becomes whether the student can complete the problem sets, and the problem sets are where the improvement happens rather than in the session itself. Holiday periods are the exception: four or five sessions a week in a school break is the only realistic way to rebuild algebraic fluency, because fluency comes from volume rather than from explanation.

faqs.answer: Yes. The private tutor work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no fine schedule is published, so be sceptical of pages quoting amounts. Ask to see the permit rather than accepting a verbal assurance, and ask any agency the same.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give us the mark schemes to work through at home?
faqs.answer: No. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and reproducing or distributing them is copyright infringement. What a tutor does instead is work through questions from legitimately obtained material and teach your child to read a mark scheme themselves, so they can see where credit is awarded rather than being handed answers. That skill changes how they write on the next paper, which a set of answers does not.

faqs.question: Which exam series will an Al Barari pupil sit for maths?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. UAE candidates use those. The February and March series is offered to India only, so a UAE-facing page quoting a March window is wrong about your country. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for the zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise.

intro.heading: The question to settle before anything else: which maths is this?
paragraphs: There are at least three qualifications called IGCSE Maths in use across Dubai schools, and they are assessed differently enough that preparing for the wrong one wastes most of the preparation. Cambridge 0580 Mathematics runs a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper, each worth half the grade. Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Mathematics A runs two papers, both calculator, each worth half. Cambridge 0607 International Mathematics expects a graphics calculator and has a different component structure again. A student drilling one pattern and sitting another will find marks disappearing in places that make no sense to them.

Al Barsha is a good place to make this point, because the cluster of schools between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road is large and uses more than one board. A family here can get a confident recommendation from a neighbour whose child sits a different specification at a school two streets away. The revision guides on sale locally cover Cambridge and Pearson side by side without making the distinction loud. The result is predictable: two terms of competent teaching aimed at the wrong paper structure, paid for in full.

So the first useful act costs nothing. Email the school and ask for the syllabus code and the tier for mathematics, in writing. Not the board name - the code. Then everything on this page becomes usable, because the topic lists, the paper structures and the mark-scheme conventions below are organised by code.

What follows is deliberately about the subject rather than about the service. There is the paper structure for each specification and what the non-calculator paper actually demands. There are eleven topics where IGCSE maths marks reliably disappear, with what the mark scheme wants in each. There is an explanation of method marks, accuracy marks and follow-through, which is the single most useful thing a maths student can understand about their own marking. There is a past-paper routine you can run at home without paying anybody. And there is a short section on tiering, which sets a ceiling on the grade before any teaching happens.

On delivery: IB Gram teaches Al Barsha students one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer in India only. For maths this matters less than for any other subject - the work is a shared page of working, annotated live, which is easier on a screen than upside down across a table - and it keeps Further Pure Mathematics and Additional Mathematics requests fillable, which a locally bounded search often does not. One more thing is worth saying before the detail starts. Nothing on this page requires a tutor to act on. The three-pass past-paper routine, the category count, the eleven mark losses and the mark-scheme conventions are all things a parent and a student can work through together with the papers the school already holds, and a family that does so will know within an hour whether they need to buy anything at all. That is the sequence we would recommend to our own relatives, so it is the sequence published here.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-barsha.subjectsIntro: The topic areas below are where IGCSE maths grades are decided. Each note names the specific trap rather than describing the topic, because the topic is in the textbook and the trap is not.

subjects.name: Number, bounds and standard form
subjects.description: Upper and lower bounds are the most reliably lost marks in the whole qualification: students add bounds when they should subtract, and divide by the wrong bound in a rate calculation. Standard form loses marks through index arithmetic rather than through the concept.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation and fractions
subjects.description: Simplifying algebraic fractions requires factorising both numerator and denominator before cancelling, and students cancel across addition. Rearranging a formula where the subject appears twice is a distinct skill that must be taught explicitly; it is never guessed correctly.

subjects.name: Simultaneous and quadratic equations
subjects.description: One linear and one quadratic simultaneously is a standard high-mark question and a standard loss, usually through substituting into the wrong equation. Completing the square is examined for its own sake and for finding a turning point, and the sign errors are predictable.

subjects.name: Inequalities, regions and graphs
subjects.description: Shading the correct side of a boundary and knowing when the line is dashed rather than solid carries easy marks that go missing. Graph sketching questions want intercepts and asymptotes shown, not a smooth curve.

subjects.name: Mensuration, similarity and scale factors
subjects.description: Area scales by the square of the length factor and volume by the cube, and students apply the length factor to all three. Compound shape questions lose marks when a radius is treated as a diameter, which happens most often under time pressure.

subjects.name: Trigonometry, bearings and 3D
subjects.description: Sine and cosine rule selection is the first decision and the first error. Bearings must be measured clockwise from north and given as three figures. Three-dimensional trigonometry questions require a named right-angled triangle to be identified before any calculation begins.

subjects.name: Circle theorems and geometric reasoning
subjects.description: A correct angle without the named reason scores partial marks at best. The mark scheme wants the theorem named - angle at centre, angles in the same segment, cyclic quadrilateral - and students who know the geometry routinely lose the reasoning mark.

subjects.name: Probability, trees and conditional cases
subjects.description: Without replacement is the whole question, and the denominator change on the second branch is where marks go. Conditional probability expressed in words rather than notation catches out students who have only practised the diagram.

subjects.name: Statistics: histograms and cumulative frequency
subjects.description: Unequal class widths mean frequency density, and a histogram drawn with frequency on the vertical axis loses the question. Cumulative frequency questions want values read at specific points and the interquartile range calculated, not estimated by eye.

subjects.name: Functions, sequences and differentiation
subjects.description: Composite and inverse function notation is examined directly and is often never practised. Quadratic sequences need the second difference method. Differentiation of simple polynomials appears on both major specifications at the higher tier, including gradient at a point and turning points.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Pure Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken alongside the main qualification by students heading to A Level Mathematics. The hardest maths request to staff locally anywhere in Dubai, and the clearest case for working with a tutor who does not need to be nearby.

subjects.name: Calculator technique
subjects.description: A neglected source of marks: storing exact values rather than rounding mid-calculation, using the table function to check a graph, and knowing the specific keystrokes for standard form and statistical functions on the model your child actually owns.

sections.heading: The paper structures, and what the non-calculator paper really demands
paragraphs: Cambridge 0580 Mathematics at Extended tier is examined through a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper, each carrying 50% of the grade. At Core tier the same pattern applies with a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper. Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Mathematics A runs two papers at each tier, both calculator-permitted, each carrying 50%. Cambridge 0607 International Mathematics expects a graphics calculator and distributes its assessment differently again. Those are three materially different preparations.

The non-calculator paper is the part families underestimate. It is not an arithmetic test; it is a test of whether a student can work in exact form. That means surds left as surds, answers left in terms of pi, fractions kept as fractions rather than converted to decimals, index laws applied rather than evaluated, and standard form manipulated symbolically. A student who has spent two years typing everything into a calculator has not practised any of that, and will lose marks on questions whose mathematics they understand completely.

It also changes what good practice looks like. On a calculator paper the sensible habit is to store intermediate values and round only at the end, because premature rounding loses accuracy marks. On a non-calculator paper the sensible habit is to keep everything exact and never approximate at all. Those are opposite instincts, and a student sitting Cambridge 0580 Extended needs both, switched on and off by which paper is in front of them. A student sitting Pearson 4MA1 Higher needs only the first, and time spent on the second is time taken from something that counts.

This is the clearest example on this page of why the syllabus code has to come before the teaching. Everything in this section is correct for one specification and wrong for another, and the difference is not subtle. A tutor who starts teaching before establishing the code has made a fifty-fifty bet with your child's preparation.

sections.heading: Eleven places IGCSE maths marks go, and what the scheme wants instead
paragraphs: These are the specific losses, in the order they tend to appear across a marked paper. The list is deliberately concrete, because 'revise algebra' is not an instruction anybody can act on and 'you add the lower bound and divide by the upper bound in a rate question' is.

Upper and lower bounds come first because they are the most reliable loss in the whole qualification. To maximise a quotient you take the largest numerator and the smallest denominator, and students do the opposite roughly half the time. Then algebraic fractions, where cancelling requires both numerator and denominator to be factorised first and students cancel across addition. Then rearranging a formula where the subject appears twice, which is a distinct technique that has to be taught rather than inferred.

Then the geometry group. Similar shapes: area scales by the square of the length factor and volume by the cube, and the length factor gets applied to all three. Circle theorems: a correct angle without the named theorem loses the reasoning mark, and the scheme wants the theorem named. Bearings: measured clockwise from north, given as three figures, and marks go on the three-figure convention alone. Three-dimensional trigonometry: identify and name the right-angled triangle before calculating anything.

Then the data group. Histograms with unequal class widths require frequency density on the vertical axis; drawing frequency instead loses the question rather than a mark. Cumulative frequency wants values read at stated points and an interquartile range calculated. Probability without replacement is the whole question, and the second-branch denominator is the mark. Finally, functions and sequences: composite and inverse notation is examined directly and often never practised, and quadratic sequences need the second difference method rather than inspection.

sections.heading: How a maths mark scheme actually works, and why it matters to your child
paragraphs: Most IGCSE maths students believe a question is either right or wrong. Mark schemes do not work that way, and the gap between those two beliefs is worth several grades over two papers. Marks are split into method marks and accuracy marks. A method mark is awarded for a correct approach even if the arithmetic that follows is wrong. An accuracy mark is awarded for the correct value. On a four-mark question a student with a correct method and one slip can score three, and a student who writes only a wrong final answer scores none.

The practical consequences are immediate. Show every step, because an unshown correct method cannot be credited. Never erase working; cross it out if you must, because crossed-out work is still marked if nothing replaces it. If you cannot finish a question, write the method anyway. And if an early part goes wrong, carry on - follow-through means a later part can still earn full credit using your own incorrect earlier value, provided the method is right.

Then the conventions. Unless a question says otherwise, Cambridge 0580 answers are generally required to three significant figures, with exact answers given exactly - and premature rounding mid-calculation loses accuracy marks even when the final figure looks close. 'Show that' questions require every step to be visible and the stated result reached, with no credit for working backwards from the answer. Units are marks. Degrees rather than radians. Correct notation for vectors and for inverse functions.

Teaching a student to mark their own paper against the official scheme is, in our experience, the highest-value single intervention available in IGCSE maths. It takes two to four sessions. After it, the student can predict their marks, which means they can tell when they have finished a question and when they have not - and they stop writing bare answers to four-mark questions. Families can do a version of this themselves with the official mark schemes their school holds, which is why it is on this page rather than kept as a selling point.

sections.heading: A past-paper routine that works, and the three-pass method
paragraphs: Doing past papers is not the same as learning from them, and most students do the first and skip the second. A paper attempted, scored, and filed produces a number and no information. The routine below produces information, takes about twice as long per paper, and is worth roughly five times as much. It can be run at home at no cost, using the papers and schemes your school holds.

First pass: attempt the paper untimed, in pencil, with nothing to hand. Leave blanks rather than guessing, because a blank is data and a guess is noise. Second pass: with a different colour and still no mark scheme, go back and attempt everything left blank, with notes and textbook allowed. What gets completed on the second pass is content the student knows but could not retrieve under exam conditions - a different problem from content they do not know, and it is solved by retrieval practice rather than re-teaching. Third pass: mark against the official scheme, awarding marks exactly as written, and categorise every lost mark as unknown content, retrieval failure, method shown but arithmetic slipped, misread question, or ran out of time.

Then count the categories. That count is the revision plan. A student losing fifteen marks to arithmetic slips and three to unknown content should be practising accuracy under time pressure, not learning new topics. A student losing twelve marks to unknown content in two topics should be learning those two topics and nothing else. Most students and most tutors do the opposite of whichever is indicated, because the default instinct is to work through the syllabus in order.

Timing comes last and only in the final three weeks. Practising under time pressure before technique is secure trains a student to make mistakes faster. The sequence is: learn the content, learn the mark scheme, then learn the clock. Any revision plan that starts with timed full papers in January has the order backwards.

sections.heading: Tiering: the ceiling that is set before any teaching happens
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject where tiering bites hardest, because both major specifications tier it and the grade ranges do not overlap at the top. Cambridge 0580 Core papers are graded C to G and Extended papers A* to E. Pearson 4MA1 Foundation awards grades 5 to 1 and Higher awards 9 to 4. A student entered at the lower tier cannot be awarded a top grade no matter how well they perform or how much tuition they have received.

The entry is made by the school, to the board's deadline, usually on the basis of internal assessment performance in Year 11. That timing means the tier is effectively determined by Year 10 and early Year 11 work, even though nobody frames it as a decision at the time. A parent who discovers in February that their child is entered at the lower tier has discovered it after the point at which tuition could have changed anything.

So the conversation to have, and to have in Year 10, is: which tier is my child currently heading for in mathematics, and what specifically would need to change for the higher tier to be viable? Schools answer that question constructively when it is asked early and defensively when it is asked late. The answer also tells you exactly where tuition has a structural return rather than a marginal one, because a student on the tier boundary has far more to gain from a term of work than one comfortably inside either tier.

One more consequence worth knowing. The tier interacts with what comes next. Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track requires five accredited IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, which the lower tier can satisfy. A Level Mathematics entry requirements set by schools are frequently a 7 or an A, which the lower tier cannot reach. Those are two different numbers, and planning against the lower one produces a student who is technically qualified and practically blocked from the subject they wanted.

sections.heading: What maths tuition costs around Al Barsha, and the hour that is free
paragraphs: Start with the hour that costs nothing, because it is the one most families skip. Marking a past paper properly against the official scheme and counting the categories of lost mark is free, takes about an hour, and produces a better revision plan than most paid first sessions. The schemes are held by the school. The three-pass routine earlier on this page is the method. Do that once before buying anything and you will know whether you need content teaching, technique work or timed practice - three different purchases.

Then the market. Published Dubai rates run from AED 33-52 an hour at Tutopiya and AED 45-65 at EdFlik in the budget band, through AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. IGCSE and IB specialists sit at AED 200-450 and upwards, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai guidance putting specialists at AED 200-450 or more. In-home one-to-one with travel included runs AED 180-500, Bestimate quoting AED 180-350. Premium named or examiner-led tutors reach AED 500-650, BartyED publishing AED 650.

For maths specifically, the mid band is where the useful work happens, with one exception. Mark-scheme literacy, bounds, circle theorem reasoning and the other items in the eleven-loss table are all procedural and are taught just as well at AED 200 as at AED 600. The exception is Further Pure Mathematics and Additional Mathematics, where the pool is small enough across the whole emirate that specialist rates are simply what the subject costs, and where an online arrangement is often the only way to get anybody at all.

Monthly, Bestimate's estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, with advertised packages at AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Set against school fees, which KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package, maths tuition for one subject at the mid band is a modest addition - and the cheapest version of it starts in Year 10 rather than in the January of Year 11. All figures are other providers' published rates read in October 2026, quoted as market context rather than as an IB Gram price list.

sections.heading: Starting from Al Barsha, and when a maths tutor is the wrong purchase
paragraphs: Send three things: the syllabus code and tier from the school in writing, the most recent marked maths paper, and the category count from the three-pass routine if you have run it. With those we can tell you in one message whether the useful purchase is content teaching, mark-scheme literacy, timed practice or nothing at all. Then we match a tutor who teaches that exact specification, you take a full-length trial lesson at no cost worked on your child's own paper, and you decide.

Sessions run weekly in Gulf Standard Time. For Al Barsha the honest start time is 5:00pm for a student at a local gate and 5:15pm if the commute runs to Al Sufouh, the Marina or Jumeirah Village, because Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road at release time are the binding constraint in this part of the city. Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar timing and holiday weeks often work better as morning slots, which suit full timed papers.

When a maths tutor is the wrong purchase. If a student understands the content and will not do the practice, a tutor becomes an expensive supervisor and the gap reappears. If the category count shows fifteen marks lost to arithmetic slips, the fix is accuracy practice the student does alone, not more teaching. If the problem is Year 8 algebra, say so and let the tutor start there rather than at Year 11 content - and expect a term, not a month. If the paper is four weeks away and three topics are missing entirely, the honest plan is to secure the highest-mark topics and the technique marks rather than to attempt the syllabus. And if a student is already comfortably at their target grade with no higher target, there is nothing to buy.

The fixed limits. No home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. No claimed approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB, because IB Gram holds none of them. No reproduction or supply of specifications, past papers or mark schemes - they are the boards' copyright material, which we reference and link while working from your school's own copies. No coursework written or completed. No grade promises, and no statistics about our own results, because we cannot publish the sample, date and method that would make such a figure mean anything.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths specification does my child in Al Barsha actually sit?
faqs.answer: You have to ask the school, in writing, for the code rather than the board name. At least three qualifications are in use across Dubai schools: Cambridge 0580 Mathematics, which examines a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper at 50% each; Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Mathematics A, which runs two calculator papers at 50% each; and Cambridge 0607 International Mathematics, which expects a graphics calculator and is structured differently again. Those are three different two-year preparations. The Al Barsha school cluster uses more than one, sometimes within a single school across subjects, so a neighbour's recommendation means nothing without the code attached.

faqs.question: How should my child prepare differently for a non-calculator maths paper?
faqs.answer: By working in exact form, which is a distinct skill rather than mental arithmetic. Surds stay as surds, answers stay in terms of pi, fractions stay as fractions, and index laws are applied rather than evaluated. The habit is the opposite of calculator-paper habit, where the right instinct is to store intermediate values and round only at the very end. A student sitting Cambridge 0580 Extended needs both instincts and has to switch between them by paper. A student sitting Pearson 4MA1 Higher needs only the calculator habit, and exact-form drilling would be time taken from something that counts.

faqs.question: What are method marks and why do they change how my child should write answers?
faqs.answer: A method mark is awarded for a correct approach even when the arithmetic that follows is wrong; an accuracy mark is awarded for the correct value. So on a four-mark question a student with a sound method and one slip can score three, while a student who writes only a wrong final answer scores none. The practical rules follow directly: show every step, never erase working because crossed-out work is still marked, write the method even when you cannot finish, and carry on after an early error because follow-through lets later parts earn full credit from your own wrong value.

faqs.question: Which maths topics lose the most marks for IGCSE students here?
faqs.answer: Upper and lower bounds are the most reliable loss in the whole qualification - to maximise a quotient you take the largest numerator and the smallest denominator, and students do the opposite about half the time. Then algebraic fractions, where cancelling requires both parts fully factorised first. Then similar areas and volumes, where the length factor gets applied to all three instead of being squared and cubed. Then circle theorems, where a correct angle without the named theorem loses the reasoning mark. Then histograms with unequal class widths, which need frequency density rather than frequency.

faqs.question: How do we use past papers properly rather than just doing them?
faqs.answer: Use three passes. Attempt the paper untimed with nothing to hand, leaving blanks rather than guessing because a blank is data. Then revisit every blank in a different colour with notes allowed - what gets completed on this pass is content your child knows but cannot retrieve under pressure, which needs retrieval practice rather than re-teaching. Then mark against the official scheme exactly as written and categorise each lost mark as unknown content, retrieval failure, method shown but slipped, misread question or out of time. The category count is the revision plan.

faqs.question: When should timed practice start?
faqs.answer: In the last three weeks, and not before. Practising under time pressure while technique is still insecure trains a student to make the same mistakes faster, and it produces a demoralising score that tells nobody anything useful. The correct order is content, then mark scheme, then clock. A revision plan that opens with timed full papers in January has the sequence backwards. Once technique is secure, timed full papers are genuinely valuable for pacing - knowing when to leave a question and come back is worth several marks on a two-hour paper and cannot be learned any other way.

faqs.question: Does the tier entry really cap my child's maths grade?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in mathematics the ranges do not overlap at the top. Cambridge 0580 Core papers are graded C to G and Extended papers A* to E; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation awards 5 to 1 and Higher awards 9 to 4. The school makes the entry to the board's deadline, usually on Year 11 internal performance, which means the tier is effectively determined during Year 10. Ask in Year 10 which tier your child is heading for and what would change it. A student on the boundary gains structurally from a term of focused work, because the ceiling itself moves rather than just the grade.

faqs.question: My child wants A Level Maths. Is extra IGCSE tuition the right investment?
faqs.answer: Sometimes the better investment is Additional or Further Pure Mathematics instead. A Level entry requirements are set by schools and are frequently a 7 or an A in IGCSE maths, sometimes with a grade in Additional Mathematics as well, and the Additional qualification is also the best available preparation for the algebraic fluency A Level assumes. If your child is already secure at the higher tier, extra hours on the main qualification have diminishing returns while the additional specification opens a route. Ask the school what its own A Level maths entry requirement is before deciding where the hours go.

faqs.question: Can a tutor over video really teach maths working?
faqs.answer: For maths it is arguably easier than in person. The work is a shared page of working annotated live, which both people see the same way up, and a tutor can write on the student's own scanned paper rather than reading it across a table. What online delivery does not provide is a physical presence to keep a reluctant student in the chair, which is a genuine limitation worth naming. For a student who needs supervision rather than teaching, a parent in the next room during the session achieves more than a higher hourly rate does.

faqs.question: What should maths tuition cost for an Al Barsha family?
faqs.answer: The mid band of AED 150-300 an hour is where the useful work happens, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists sit at AED 200-450 and upwards, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and premium named tutors reach AED 500-650 with BartyED at AED 650. Bounds, circle theorem reasoning and mark-scheme literacy are procedural and taught just as well in the mid band. The genuine exception is Further Pure or Additional Mathematics, where the pool across the emirate is small enough that specialist rates are simply what the subject costs. Monthly, a weekly hour runs AED 600-1,200 mid-market.

faqs.question: My child keeps making careless mistakes. Can tutoring fix that?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the honest answer is that most of the fix is practice the student does alone. Run the category count: if fifteen marks are going on method-shown-but-slipped and three on unknown content, the problem is accuracy under pressure, and the remedy is short frequent accuracy sets rather than more teaching. What a tutor genuinely adds here is the discipline of checking strategy - re-reading the question against the answer, estimating before calculating, keeping exact values until the end on a calculator paper. Two sessions on that, then the student does the volume. Paying weekly for carelessness is paying for something you cannot buy.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting maths tuition in Year 9?
faqs.answer: It is the cheapest maths intervention available and almost nobody buys it. A gap in Year 8 algebraic manipulation does not announce itself - the student compensates and scores adequately on topic tests - and then fails to carry Year 10 quadratics. At that point a tutor has two jobs, teach the new and repair the old, while the school moves on. By Year 11 exam technique joins the list and it is three jobs at exam-year rates. Same gap, roughly three times the hours. A term of Year 9 algebra is the single best-value purchase in this subject.

faqs.question: Can you help with Further Pure Mathematics or Additional Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Yes, and these are the requests where delivery method genuinely changes what is available rather than just what it costs. Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics and Pearson 4PM1 Further Pure Mathematics have a small teaching pool across the whole emirate, distributed by where people teach rather than by residential area, so requiring someone who can also reach Al Barsha by 5pm frequently leaves nobody. Expect specialist-band rates, because that is what the subject costs. If we cannot cover it in the window you need, we will say so rather than place a general maths tutor.

faqs.question: What time should an Al Barsha maths session start?
faqs.answer: 5:00pm for a student at a local Al Barsha gate and 5:15pm if the commute runs out to Al Sufouh, the Marina or Jumeirah Village. Secondary gates across this cluster release roughly between 2:45pm and 3:15pm, and Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road take the whole corridor's traffic at once, so a child is home between about 3:40pm and 4:35pm. Changing and food take the rest. Online delivery protects that window because nothing in the arrangement depends on how either road happens to be moving at the time.

faqs.question: How quickly should we expect maths marks to move?
faqs.answer: Faster than most subjects, because much of what is lost is procedural. Bounds, bearings, similar-shape scale factors, histogram frequency density and quadratic sequences are single-session fixes that show up on the next paper. Mark-scheme literacy takes two to four sessions and improves every answer thereafter. Algebraic fluency that was never secure takes a term, because it has to be rebuilt rather than corrected. Re-run the category count on a fresh paper after six to eight weeks: if the targeted category has not shrunk, change the focus or the tutor rather than continuing on faith.
