dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-garhoud.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE Mathematics to Al Garhoud and wider Deira-side families: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended, Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Foundation and Higher, and the Year 9 groundwork that decides which tier a pupil is entered for.

intro.heading: The school run is what makes or breaks a maths tutoring plan here
paragraphs: Al Garhoud is a small, old residential pocket wedged between Dubai Creek, Garhoud Bridge and the northern perimeter of Dubai International Airport. It is quiet, it is low-rise, and it is twenty minutes from more private schools than almost any other patch of Dubai. That proximity is the reason parents here rarely complain about distance to school. It is also the reason an afternoon tutoring slot is so hard to place: the child is at school nearby, not at home, until mid-afternoon, and the gap between the gate opening and dinner is narrower than most families expect when they start looking.

Work the clock backwards and the arithmetic is unforgiving. A British-curriculum secondary around Al Garhoud, Oud Metha or Festival City typically finishes between 14:00 and 15:00, with co-curricular clubs running to 16:00 on two or three days. A school bus that loops Al Garhoud, Al Rigga and Al Mamzar before dropping adds twenty-five to fifty minutes. Add the walk upstairs, a meal and a change of clothes and the earliest honest start for a Year 10 pupil is 16:15 on a club-free day and 17:15 otherwise. Push the lesson later than 19:30 and you are teaching simultaneous equations to a tired teenager, which is money spent on attendance rather than learning.

Now add travel for the tutor. An in-home maths tutor crossing from Barsha or the Marina to Al Garhoud between 15:30 and 17:30 is in the worst traffic Dubai produces, because Garhoud Bridge and Al Maktoum Bridge carry the Creek crossing at exactly those hours. Published in-home rates in Dubai sit at AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor online, and a good part of that gap is the car. The family also inherits the risk: if the Sheikh Rashid Road approach is blocked, the lesson starts twenty minutes late and the pupil loses the end of the session, not the tutor.

An online one-to-one lesson removes the journey from both sides of the booking. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, because in-home visits are a service offered only in India; what an Al Garhoud family gets instead is a 16:30 slot that holds every week and a tutor chosen for the syllabus rather than for proximity to the Creek. For IGCSE Mathematics that distinction is sharper than it sounds: a specialist who teaches Extended 0580 and Higher-tier 4MA1 all week is a different proposition from a general maths graduate who lives nearby and takes on whatever walks through the door.

The rest of this page is written around that timetable. It names the schools the neighbourhood actually feeds, sets out when a session can realistically start on each weekday, explains the two exam board routes your child is likely on and what the tier decision caps their grade at, and shows what the Dubai market charges so you can judge a quote. If you read nothing else, read the tiering section. Choosing between Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher, is the single decision that most often costs a Garhoud family a grade it had already paid for.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-garhoud.programmesIntro: An IGCSE maths tutor is usually brought in at one of four points: late MYP or Year 9, the start of the two-year IGCSE course, the final two terms before the papers, or the bridge from IGCSE into A Level or the IB Diploma. Each needs a different plan.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 and MYP maths groundwork
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE decide which tier a pupil is entered for. Fractions, negative indices, rearranging formulae, ratio and basic algebraic manipulation are the gatekeepers. A Year 9 pupil who still counts on a calculator for 7 x 8 or who cannot expand two brackets reliably will be placed in Core or Foundation, and that placement is usually made in the spring term of Year 9 on the strength of one internal paper.
programmes.countryNote: Al Garhoud and Deira-side schools set tiers earlier than many Dubai parents realise, often in February or March of Year 9, using an internal assessment rather than a public exam. Families who want an Extended or Higher entry are better served by two terms of Year 9 work than by a rescue attempt in Year 11, when the syllabus gap is already two years wide.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
programmes.description: Cambridge splits candidates into Core and Extended. Core candidates sit Paper 1 and Paper 3; Extended candidates sit Paper 2 and Paper 4. The current syllabus includes a paper sat without a calculator, which has changed what revision has to look like: arithmetic fluency and surd manipulation now carry marks that a calculator used to absorb. Confirm your child's entry codes and the live syllabus on cambridgeinternational.org before building a plan around them.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit the June and November series. The February and March series is offered to India only, so a Garhoud family planning a resit is planning for November, not for the spring. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable for each, so the dates that matter are the ones on your own school's zone timetable.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1
programmes.description: Specification A is the route most Edexcel centres use: two papers of two hours and 100 marks each, weighted equally, with a calculator permitted throughout. Candidates are entered at Foundation or Higher tier. Specification B (4MB1) is a shorter, more compressed alternative, and strong candidates may also be entered for Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 alongside the main award.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and November results have reached students in January in recent series. Always open the live timetable on qualifications.pearson.com rather than trusting a date copied onto a tutoring page, because provisional timetables are revised.

programmes.name: The IGCSE to A Level or IB Diploma bridge
programmes.description: A grade 7 or an A at IGCSE does not automatically carry a pupil into A Level Mathematics or into IB Maths Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. The step up is in algebraic stamina and in proof: students who passed by pattern-matching question types hit a wall in the first term. Six to ten weeks of bridging work on indices, surds, functions and trigonometric identities over the summer is the cheapest intervention available in the whole sequence.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools around Al Garhoud and Festival City run both an A Level and an IB Diploma route after Year 11, so the bridging target differs by sibling even inside one family. Students heading for engineering at a UAE university should check whether the department expects Analysis and Approaches rather than Applications and Interpretation before the DP subject choice is locked.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-garhoud.subjectsIntro: IGCSE maths is one subject with a dozen separable failure points. Tutoring is efficient when it attacks the specific ones a pupil loses marks on, and wasteful when it re-teaches the whole syllabus from chapter one. These are the strands Garhoud-area families most often ask for.

subjects.name: Number, surds and standard form
subjects.description: Where the non-calculator marks live. Pupils lose them on index laws with negative and fractional powers, on rationalising a denominator, and on converting between standard form and ordinary numbers under time pressure. Fixable in three or four sessions because the content is narrow and the technique is drillable.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation and rearrangement
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, simplifying algebraic fractions and changing the subject of a formula. This is the strand that quietly sets the tier: a pupil who cannot rearrange reliably cannot do mechanics-style questions later, and examiners award method marks for correct rearrangement even when the final answer is wrong.

subjects.name: Quadratics: factorising, formula and completing the square
subjects.description: Three methods, each worth knowing for a different reason. Completing the square is the one most pupils skip and the one that makes turning points tractable and the sketching questions. Marks are lost by using the formula on a question that asked for the completed-square form, which earns nothing.

subjects.name: Simultaneous and non-linear equations
subjects.description: Linear pairs are rarely the problem; one linear and one quadratic is. Pupils substitute the wrong way round, lose a solution pair, or forget to give both x and y values. Writing both solutions explicitly is a one-mark habit that is worth building early.

subjects.name: Trigonometry, sine and cosine rules
subjects.description: Right-angled trigonometry is secure for most candidates. The sine rule in its ambiguous case, the cosine rule rearranged for an angle, and three-dimensional trigonometry questions are not. Bearings questions combine the trigonometry with a diagram pupils have to draw themselves, which is where most of the loss happens.

subjects.name: Mensuration, similar shapes and area and volume scale factors
subjects.description: Length, area and volume scale factors behave differently and candidates apply the linear factor to all three. A single worked contrast between k, k squared and k cubed usually fixes it permanently. Compound solids also demand an accurate sketch before any formula is used.

subjects.name: Graphs, transformations and function notation
subjects.description: Sketching reciprocal, exponential and cubic graphs, reading a gradient from a tangent, and interpreting translations and stretches in function notation. Pupils confuse the direction of a horizontal translation almost universally, and the mark scheme does not forgive it.

subjects.name: Probability, tree diagrams and set notation
subjects.description: Conditional probability without replacement is the standard trap: the denominator changes on the second branch and candidates leave it alone. Venn diagrams with set notation appear on both boards and reward precise reading of union, intersection and complement symbols.

subjects.name: Statistics: cumulative frequency, histograms and averages from tables
subjects.description: Histograms with unequal class widths require frequency density, which a surprising share of candidates never meet properly. Estimating the mean from a grouped table needs midpoints, and the interquartile range read off a cumulative frequency curve needs the right axis read at the right value.

subjects.name: Vectors and geometric proof
subjects.description: Column vector arithmetic is straightforward; writing a path around a figure in terms of two base vectors and then arguing that two vectors are parallel is not. These questions sit late in the paper, carry several marks, and are routinely left blank by candidates who could have earned two of them.

subjects.name: Non-calculator arithmetic and estimation
subjects.description: The non-calculator paper has made long multiplication, division of decimals, fraction arithmetic and sensible estimation examinable again. Pupils who learned maths with a calculator in hand from Year 7 need deliberate practice here, and it is the quickest win available in the final two terms.

subjects.name: Exam technique and working under a two-hour clock
subjects.description: Showing method, rounding only at the end, answering in the units asked for, and abandoning a stuck question after ninety seconds. Technique work typically moves a borderline candidate more than new content does in the last six weeks, and it is the cheapest thing a tutor can teach.

sections.heading: What an Al Garhoud weekday actually allows
paragraphs: A search for an IGCSE maths tutor in Al Garhoud is usually made in the evening, after a parent has looked at the week and realised there is no obvious hour in it. So start with the hour rather than the tutor. The secondary schools in and around this neighbourhood finish between 14:00 and 15:00, with activity clubs extending two or three afternoons to around 16:00. Bus routes that serve Al Garhoud, Al Rigga, Al Mamzar and Al Qusais take between twenty-five and fifty minutes depending on where the stop sits on the loop.

That gives most families a usable window between 16:15 and 19:30, narrowing on club days and narrowing again if a younger sibling has a fixed activity. The table below is the honest version of that window by day, based on how a standard UAE school week falls. Sunday is the first school day and the one on which pupils are freshest; Thursday is the last, which makes it the natural home for a longer or double session because Friday mornings start later at most schools.

Prayer times move with the season and the family, and Maghrib is the practical boundary for an evening session in many Garhoud households. During Ramadan the school day is shortened by regulation across Dubai private schools, which counter-intuitively makes afternoon tutoring easier rather than harder: the pupil is home by early afternoon. The sensible pattern then is a late-morning or early-afternoon lesson, or a post-Iftar slot for an older candidate who prefers it.

None of this works if the tutor is driving. The whole point of placing the lesson online is that the window you identified is the window that gets used, with no twenty-minute erosion at the front for a Creek crossing and no rescheduling because Sheikh Rashid Road stopped moving.

sections.heading: Which schools this neighbourhood feeds, and why that changes the plan
paragraphs: Al Garhoud does not have a single catchment school. It has a ring of them, split across the Creek, and the pupil's school matters more than the home address for every practical decision about maths tutoring. The immediate cluster runs from Deira International School and Universal American School in and around Dubai Festival City to Dubai Scholars Private School and Al Mawakeb's Garhoud campus. Across Al Maktoum Bridge, St Mary's Catholic High School, Dubai English Speaking School, Dubai Gem Private School and The Indian High School in Oud Metha take a substantial share of Garhoud secondary pupils.

The first thing that changes is the exam board. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1 cover similar content, but the paper structures, the calculator rules and the grading scales are different enough that past-paper practice on the wrong board wastes the session. A pupil entered for 4MA1 who spends six weeks on Cambridge non-calculator technique has prepared for a paper they will not sit. Ask the school for the entry codes in writing; most will supply them without fuss.

The second is the timetable, which the table in the previous section covers. The third is the tier decision, which almost every school makes internally and communicates late. Schools with a large Extended or Higher cohort tend to tier early and move pupils down; schools with a mixed intake often tier later and move pupils up. Knowing which pattern your child's school follows tells you whether Year 9 or Year 10 is the moment to intervene.

Dubai's private school sector gives some scale to this. KHDA-reported figures for 2024-25 put 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula, with UK-curriculum schools at 37 per cent of enrolment and the IB at 7 per cent. The Deira side of the Creek holds a disproportionate share of the older, long-established schools in that count, which is why the curriculum mix inside a single Garhoud apartment block can be wider than in a newer community out on Sheikh Zayed Road.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher: the decision that caps the grade
paragraphs: Tiering is the part of IGCSE maths that parents in Al Garhoud discover too late. Both boards split candidates, and both put a ceiling on the lower route. Cambridge Core candidates on 0580 cannot be awarded above a grade C; Extended candidates can reach A*. Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Foundation candidates cannot be awarded above a grade 5; Higher runs 9 down to 4, with a safety grade 3 available. A pupil capped at C or 5 who needed a 6 for an A Level Mathematics place has lost that place in Year 9, not in Year 11.

The argument for the lower tier is real, not merely defensive. A pupil placed on Extended who is not ready sits two harder papers, gets fewer marks on each and may come away with a lower grade than a confident Core candidate would have achieved. Schools are not being cautious for the sake of it. The question is whether a particular pupil is genuinely at their ceiling or whether two or three specific weaknesses, usually algebraic rearrangement, indices and fraction arithmetic, are holding down a result that is otherwise within reach.

That distinction is diagnosable in one sitting. Give the pupil a Core or Foundation paper and an Extended or Higher paper on the same afternoon and compare where the marks fall. A pupil who scores well on the lower paper but collapses on specific question types in the higher one has a repairable gap. A pupil who loses marks evenly across both is at their level, and the honest advice is to secure a strong grade on the lower tier rather than gamble on the higher.

sections.heading: The non-calculator paper, and why Garhoud pupils find it hardest
paragraphs: The most consequential recent change to Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is that one of a candidate's two papers is now sat without a calculator. For a cohort that has had a calculator in hand since Year 7, this reaches further than it looks. It is not only that long multiplication and division of decimals are examinable again. It is that fraction arithmetic, index laws, surd simplification and sensible estimation have to be fluent enough to use inside a bigger question, under time pressure, without a safety net.

The failure pattern is consistent. A pupil who knows the method for a compound interest question loses the marks because they cannot evaluate the arithmetic cleanly. A pupil who can state the index laws cannot apply them to a negative fractional power at speed. A pupil who has never had to estimate cannot tell that an answer of 0.0032 is implausible for a question about the area of a classroom floor. All three are repairable, and all three respond to short daily practice rather than long weekly sessions.

This is where a tutor earns the rate quickly, because the repair is measurable. Ten minutes of mental arithmetic at the start of each lesson, a weekly ten-question non-calculator set, and one timed non-calculator paper a fortnight in the final term will move a borderline candidate. It requires no new content and no new textbook. Pearson Edexcel candidates on 4MA1 have a calculator on both papers and so face a different priority list, which is another reason the board question has to be settled first.

Parents can check progress on this without any specialist knowledge. Ask to see the pupil's non-calculator working on a past paper question. If the page shows a clear method and arithmetic laid out in steps, the technique is landing. If it shows an answer with no working, the method marks are being left on the table regardless of whether the answer is right.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the paper: the June and November series
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit the June and November series. The February and March series is offered to India only, which matters because a resit plan built around a spring sitting does not exist for a pupil in Dubai. If the June papers go badly, the next opportunity is November, and the work has to be planned across the summer rather than crammed into the autumn.

Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable for each. The guidance is explicit that using the wrong zone's timetable is the candidate's risk and that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for a missed exam on that basis. The practical instruction for an Al Garhoud parent is to take the timetable from the school's exams officer, not from any tutoring page, and to put the actual paper dates in the family calendar in September.

Pearson's published pattern is clearer to cite because the dates are on their support pages. International GCSE runs in May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables well ahead, including for each November series to come, and those are revised, so the live PDF is the only version worth acting on.

sections.heading: Permits, verification and what you can check yourself
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories are wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists the route as private tutor licensing, with no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE app, website or e-services.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any page quoting a specific amount is quoting something unverified. The useful point for a parent is simpler: the permit is free and quick, which removes every excuse for not holding one, and it is reasonable to ask.

There are boundaries worth knowing in the other direction too. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. So the apparently attractive arrangement of hiring your child's own maths teacher privately is the one to avoid. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal again, requiring a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute; IB Gram does not hold one and does not operate premises in the UAE.

What a parent can check without any of this: ask the tutor which board and tier they teach most often, ask them to talk through one mark scheme on a past paper question, and watch the free trial lesson. A maths specialist will tell you within ten minutes where the pupil is losing marks. Someone who cannot name a single question type the pupil is weak on after an hour has not diagnosed anything.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, coursework and the limits on what a maths tutor may do
paragraphs: IGCSE Mathematics on both the Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 routes is examined entirely by written paper, with no coursework component, so the academic-honesty question is narrower here than in subjects with an internal assessment. It still matters, for two reasons. The first is that many Garhoud pupils are taking maths alongside subjects that do carry coursework, and the household's working assumption about what a tutor does needs to be consistent. The second is that pupils who go on to the IB Diploma will face a Mathematics exploration, where the line is sharp.

The line is this: the work submitted for assessment must be the student's own. A tutor may teach the content, explain a mark scheme, model a method on a different question, ask the questions that help a student find their own approach, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not write, complete, redraft to completion or supply the assessed work. Breaching that is academic malpractice under IB rules and puts the student's own award at risk, not the tutor's.

This matters commercially as well as ethically, because the UAE tutoring market contains operators who sell completed Internal Assessments outright. A page in this search results set advertises finished IAs at a fixed price. Any family tempted by that convenience should understand that an IB malpractice finding can cost the whole Diploma, and that the student carries the consequence alone.

For maths specifically, the honest version of help is less glamorous and more effective: past papers from the correct board, timed, marked against the published mark scheme, with the loss points named and repaired. That is what moves a grade. Nobody can promise a particular grade, and a tutor who does is telling you something about their own judgement rather than about your child.

faqs.question: What time can an IGCSE maths lesson realistically start for a family in Al Garhoud?
faqs.answer: On a club-free day, 16:15 or 16:30. Secondary schools around Al Garhoud, Festival City and Oud Metha finish between 14:00 and 15:00, and a bus loop through Al Garhoud, Al Rigga or Al Mamzar adds twenty-five to fifty minutes. Add a meal and a change of clothes and 16:15 is the earliest honest start. On the two or three afternoons a week with activity clubs, 17:15 is more realistic. Thursday is the best day for a longer session because Friday mornings start later at most schools, and Saturday morning is the only slot where a full timed past paper plus review fits comfortably.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE maths tutor to a villa in Al Garhoud?
faqs.answer: No. Lessons for UAE families are delivered one-to-one over live video, and IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. That is a deliberate choice rather than a limitation. Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online tutor, and much of that gap is the car. Online delivery also means your child can be matched with a specialist who teaches Extended 0580 or Higher 4MA1 every week, rather than whoever happens to live within a short drive of the airport perimeter.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child sits Cambridge 0580 or Pearson Edexcel 4MA1?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's exams officer for the entry code in writing. Schools around Al Garhoud and Oud Metha split between the two boards, and some enter different cohorts differently. The distinction is not cosmetic: 0580 now includes a paper sat without a calculator, while 4MA1 Specification A permits a calculator on both papers, and the grading scales differ. Six weeks of non-calculator drilling is wasted on a 4MA1 candidate, and past papers from the wrong board teach the wrong question styles. Settle this before buying any past-paper work, because everything else in the plan depends on it.

faqs.question: What grade is the highest my child can get on Cambridge IGCSE Core maths?
faqs.answer: A grade C. Cambridge 0580 splits candidates into Core and Extended, and the Core route caps the award at C while Extended reaches A*. Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 works the same way: Foundation tier caps at grade 5 and Higher runs 9 to 4 with a safety grade 3. This is the most consequential decision in the whole course and it is usually made internally by the school in the spring term of Year 9. A pupil capped at C or 5 who needed a 6 for A Level Mathematics has lost that option two years before anyone notices.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my child is genuinely a Core candidate or just has gaps?
faqs.answer: Sit both papers on the same afternoon and compare where the marks fall. Give the pupil a Core or Foundation past paper and an Extended or Higher one, then look at the pattern rather than the totals. A pupil who scores well on the lower paper but collapses on specific question types in the higher one, typically algebraic rearrangement, indices and fraction arithmetic, has a repairable gap. A pupil losing marks evenly across both papers is at their level, and the honest advice is to secure a strong grade on the lower tier. One diagnostic session answers this; a term of guessing does not.

faqs.question: Why has the non-calculator paper made IGCSE maths harder for Dubai pupils?
faqs.answer: Because a cohort that has used a calculator since Year 7 has never had to be fluent without one. The current Cambridge syllabus examines one of a candidate's two papers without a calculator, which puts long multiplication, decimal division, fraction arithmetic, index laws, surd simplification and estimation back on the paper. The failure is rarely the method. A pupil who knows how to do compound interest loses the marks on the arithmetic, or cannot evaluate a negative fractional power at speed, or cannot tell that an answer is implausible. Short daily practice fixes it faster than long weekly sessions do.

faqs.question: Which maths topics should we spend tutoring hours on first?
faqs.answer: Start with whatever the last paper shows, not with the hardest topic on the syllabus. In practice the highest-yield strands for Extended and Higher candidates are algebraic rearrangement, quadratics including completing the square, graph transformations and function notation, and the sine and cosine rules in their awkward forms. For Core and Foundation candidates it is fraction and ratio arithmetic, reading the question accurately, and showing method so partial marks survive a slip. Vectors in geometric proof are worth two or three marks late in an Extended paper and are routinely left blank, which makes them cheap to recover.

faqs.question: How much should I expect to pay for IGCSE maths tuition around Al Garhoud?
faqs.answer: Market bands in Dubai, as published by the providers themselves: budget online tutoring from around AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik quoting AED 45 to 65; a qualified subject tutor online at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150; in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate's 2026 table showing AED 180 to 350; specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more; and premium named tutors higher still, with BartyED publishing AED 650. Those are market figures, not IB Gram's price. The first lesson here is a free trial.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to use a tuition centre in Deira than a one-to-one tutor?
faqs.answer: Per hour, usually yes, because the cost is shared across a group. The question is what the hour buys. A group class moves at the group's pace and cannot spend twenty minutes on your child's specific index-law problem, which is often the whole reason you went looking. A centre also puts a journey back into an afternoon that was already tight, and the Creek crossing at 16:30 is the exact traffic you were avoiding. Group teaching suits content coverage; one-to-one suits diagnosis and repair. Many families use a centre in Year 10 and switch to one-to-one for the final two terms.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Year 11 maths candidate usually need?
faqs.answer: One 60-minute lesson a week through Years 10 and 11 is the common pattern, rising to two or three a week for six to ten weeks before the papers. More than three weekly sessions rarely helps, because the limiting factor becomes how much independent past-paper work the pupil does between lessons rather than how much teaching they receive. A pupil who sits one timed paper a fortnight and reviews it properly will improve faster on one lesson a week than a pupil taking three lessons and doing nothing in between. The homework is where the grade moves.

faqs.question: My child has eight weeks until the maths paper. Is starting now worth it?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a narrower plan. Eight weeks is not enough to re-teach a two-year syllabus and is plenty to fix exam technique and three or four specific loss points. The sequence that works: a timed past paper from the correct board and tier in the first session, a line-by-line review against the published mark scheme, then six weeks of targeted repair on the strands that actually lost marks, with a full mock in the final week. Technique work alone, showing method, rounding at the end, answering in the right units, abandoning a stuck question, often moves a borderline candidate more than new content does.

faqs.question: Which exam series do IGCSE maths candidates in Dubai actually sit?
faqs.answer: June and November. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and the February and March series is offered to India only, so there is no spring resit route for a pupil in Dubai. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with a separate timetable for each, and warns that using the wrong zone's timetable is the candidate's risk. Take the dates from your school's exams officer, not from a tutoring page.

faqs.question: Do private maths tutors in Dubai need a government permit, and can I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists the application as private tutor licensing with no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so ignore any page quoting a figure.

faqs.question: Can we hire my child's own school maths teacher for private lessons instead?
faqs.answer: It is the arrangement to avoid. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Beyond the rules, there is a practical problem: the person who set the internal assessment that decided your child's tier is not a neutral second opinion on whether that tier was right. A separate specialist gives you an independent read on where the marks are going.

faqs.question: What can a maths tutor do about coursework, and where does the line sit?
faqs.answer: IGCSE Mathematics on both the 0580 and 4MA1 routes is examined entirely by written paper, with no coursework component, so there is nothing to submit. The question matters for pupils taking other subjects, and for anyone heading to the IB Diploma and its Mathematics exploration. The line is that the assessed work must be the student's own. A tutor may teach content, explain a mark scheme, model a method on a different question and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not write, complete or supply the work. Operators in this market who sell finished assessments put the student's award at risk.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change a maths tutoring schedule in Al Garhoud?
faqs.answer: It usually makes afternoon tutoring easier rather than harder. Dubai private schools run a shortened day during Ramadan, so pupils are home by early afternoon and the 16:15 bottleneck disappears. Two patterns work well: a late-morning or early-afternoon lesson while concentration is best, or a post-Iftar slot for an older candidate who prefers to work in the evening. Fasting students should not be scheduled in the hour before Iftar, when attention is at its lowest. Tell the tutor which pattern the household is following before the month starts, so the slot moves once rather than being renegotiated weekly.

intro.heading: Eight weeks, two papers and one grade: what Al Habtoor City parents are really asking
paragraphs: Almost nobody searches for an IGCSE maths tutor in Al Habtoor City in September. The searches cluster at two points in the year: the fortnight after a mock paper comes home, and the six to eight weeks before a Cambridge or Pearson series opens. By the time a parent in Noora, Amna or Meera Tower is typing that phrase, a date already exists on the calendar, and the only question that matters is what can realistically be fixed before it.

That is why this page is built as a countdown rather than a brochure. Your child sits two papers in IGCSE Mathematics, not one, and the two reward different work. On Cambridge 0580 Extended, Paper 2 is the short-answer, non-calculator-free structured paper and Paper 4 is the long structured paper, each carrying half the marks. Cramming topics helps Paper 4. Cleaning up notation, units and rounding helps Paper 2. A tutor who does not know which of the two is the weaker half is guessing, and guessing is expensive at eight weeks out.

Al Habtoor City adds its own constraint. This is a vertical community: three hotels, La Perle, the Dubai Water Canal frontage and a cluster of residential towers wedged between Business Bay and Al Safa on Sheikh Zayed Road. There is no school inside the development, so every family here commutes out of it. Children attend schools in Al Safa, Al Wasl, Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim, and the drive home between 15:00 and 17:00 on Sheikh Zayed Road is the single biggest reason an in-home session gets cancelled. The first appointment a tutor should be asked to hold is the one at 18:00 on a Tuesday, not the one that looks best on paper.

IB Gram works with Al Habtoor City families online, one-to-one, over live video. Home visits are something we offer in India only; we do not send tutors to UAE addresses, and the page you are reading will never promise one. What online buys a tower family is specific rather than vague: your child gets a tutor who has taught Extended 0580 to examination repeatedly, instead of whoever is free to drive to Sheikh Zayed Road at 18:30 for a fee that includes their travel. The screen is shared, the working is written out on a tablet or on paper held to the camera, and the session recording lets a student re-watch the one explanation they did not catch.

The rest of this page does four things. It counts the term backwards to the series your child is entered for, so you can see which weeks are already spoken for. It sets Cambridge 0580 against Pearson 4MA1 so you can tell which syllabus the school has actually entered them for. It publishes what Dubai providers charge, with the source beside the figure, because three of six ranking pages in this market publish no price at all. And it answers the questions parents in this part of Dubai send us, including the uncomfortable ones about what a tutor is allowed to do.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-habtoor-ci.programmesIntro: Al Habtoor City children are spread across British, IB and Indian-curriculum schools within a ten-kilometre radius, so the level a maths tutor is working at varies more here than the single search phrase suggests. These are the four stages we are asked for most from this postcode.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: The two-year course that ends in the June or November series. Cambridge 0580 splits into Core and Extended tiers; Pearson 4MA1 splits into Foundation and Higher. Both sit two papers, both allow a calculator on at least one of them, and both reward disciplined method marks over clever shortcuts. Tutoring at this stage is usually half syllabus repair and half examination technique.
programmes.countryNote: Most British-curriculum schools near Al Habtoor City enter the bulk of their cohort for Extended or Higher tier, and a parent often discovers the tier only when a mock result arrives. Ask the maths department which code appears on the entry: 0580, 0607, 4MA1 or 4MB1. The answer changes which past papers are useful, and it is the first thing a tutor should establish.

programmes.name: Additional and Further Pure Mathematics
programmes.description: Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics and Pearson 4PM1 Further Pure Mathematics sit alongside the main qualification for students heading towards A Level Maths, IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, or an engineering degree. Calculus, series and trigonometric identities arrive a year earlier than they otherwise would, which is precisely why these courses are the ones most often dropped in panic in the spring term.
programmes.countryNote: Families along the Dubai Water Canal corridor ask about 0606 for one reason: a sibling found the jump into IB Mathematics HL brutal. Taking Additional Mathematics is the cheapest insurance available against that jump, but only if the main grade is secure first. A tutor should say plainly when the answer is to drop it.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary and pre-IGCSE maths
programmes.description: Cambridge runs Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests, and most schools near Al Safa use Years 7 to 9 to decide tiering for the IGCSE course. Work at this stage is about fractions, negative indices, algebraic manipulation and proportional reasoning - the four things that, left unfixed, become the Paper 2 ceiling three years later. It is unglamorous and it is the cheapest point in the whole journey to intervene.
programmes.countryNote: Al Habtoor City has a high proportion of families who arrived in Dubai mid-phase, from CBSE, American or French systems. A Year 8 arriving from CBSE is typically ahead on arithmetic and behind on worded, context-heavy questions. That is a three-month gap, not a three-year one, and naming it early prevents a Core-tier entry nobody intended.

programmes.name: A Level, IB DP and the post-16 decision
programmes.description: Schools in Al Safa, Al Sufouh and Umm Suqeim split after IGCSE into A Level and IB Diploma routes. The maths decision is the one with the longest shadow: A Level Mathematics, IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at HL or SL, or IB Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation. Grade 7 to 9 at Extended tier generally keeps every door open; a grade 5 closes the HL door quietly.
programmes.countryNote: UAE universities and the UK admissions cycle both treat the two IB maths routes differently, and the published prerequisites for engineering and economics courses are where this gets decided. Check each target university's own entry page rather than relying on a school corridor rumour, and make the choice in the spring of Year 11 while the IGCSE grade is still movable.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-habtoor-ci.subjectsIntro: A maths request from this postcode usually arrives attached to one or two others, because the Year 11 timetable crowds everything into the same eight weeks. These are the syllabuses we are asked to cover alongside IGCSE Mathematics, with the code that decides which past papers are worth opening.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: Two papers. Extended reaches grade 9, Core is capped. Marks drain away on rounding instructions, exact-form answers, and the structured multi-step questions at the back of Paper 4 where method marks are available even when the final answer is wrong.

subjects.name: International Mathematics (Cambridge 0607)
subjects.description: The graphic-display-calculator syllabus used by many IB-continuum schools, with an investigation paper that 0580 does not have. Students moving between the two codes lose marks simply from being trained on the wrong paper style.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Pearson's main route, two papers of equal weight, calculator allowed throughout. The question wording differs noticeably from Cambridge, and students who revise on the wrong board's papers arrive in the hall fluent in a dialect nobody is speaking.

subjects.name: Mathematics B (Pearson 4MB1)
subjects.description: A more compressed, more algebraic alternative used by a minority of schools, usually for faster sets. Fewer past papers exist, so a tutor has to build practice from the specification rather than relying on volume.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Calculus, binomial expansion, logarithms and trigonometric identities a year early. Taken well it removes most of the shock from IB Mathematics HL; taken badly it eats the revision time the main grade needed.

subjects.name: Further Pure Mathematics (Pearson 4PM1)
subjects.description: Pearson's accelerated option, heavy on proof, series and coordinate geometry. Useful evidence for a competitive engineering application, and only sensible once 4MA1 Higher is comfortably secure.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: The subject that punishes weak algebra hardest. Rearranging formulae, handling standard form and reading a gradient off a graph are maths skills examined in a physics paper, which is why these two are so often tutored together.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles, concentration and percentage yield are proportional reasoning in a lab coat. Students who are shaky on ratio lose marks in chemistry long before they lose them in maths, and the repair work is identical.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Less arithmetic, but the data-handling and magnification calculations still catch students out, and the long six-mark answers need the same structured approach a maths method mark needs.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Science (0653 / 0654)
subjects.description: Three disciplines compressed into two or three papers. Timing is the main enemy, and timing is trainable: the fix is almost always a paper-pacing routine rather than more content.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and precise definitions carry the marks. Students who are confident in maths often over-explain in prose here and run out of time on the data-response paper.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Ratio analysis, break-even and cash-flow forecasts are examined arithmetic. A student who is secure in IGCSE maths can lift a business grade quickly by treating the calculation questions as free marks.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE maths tutor in Al Habtoor City is being hired to do
paragraphs: An IGCSE maths tutor in Al Habtoor City is almost always hired to close a measurable gap inside a fixed number of weeks. The gap is usually visible on a mock paper: a student who can do every topic in isolation and still loses fifteen marks across two papers to rounding, unfinished method, misread instructions and running out of time. That is not a knowledge problem and it does not respond to more content. It responds to being shown, in the student's own handwriting, where the marks went.

The second thing the job involves is translation. Dubai schools near Al Habtoor City use at least four maths codes between them, and the mark schemes differ in what they reward. A student trained to show full working on Cambridge 0580 Paper 4 will keep method marks when the final answer is wrong. A student who writes only answers will not. Pearson 4MA1 allows a calculator on both papers, which changes revision priorities entirely: estimation and mental arithmetic matter less, and interpreting a calculator display to the right degree of accuracy matters more.

The third part is scheduling discipline, which sounds administrative and is actually the difference between a block that works and one that quietly collapses. A family in these towers has a school run that crosses Sheikh Zayed Road twice a day, activities in Jumeirah or Al Safa, and in many cases a parent travelling for work. An eight-week block needs sixteen sessions to happen. Booking them at a time that survives a bad traffic evening is worth more than booking a nominally better tutor at a time that does not.

What the job is not: a guarantee. No tutor can promise a specific grade, and any provider in this market who does should be asked to publish the refund terms on the same page. What can be promised is a named diagnosis in week one, work set and marked every week, and an honest answer in week four about whether the target is still realistic.
bullets: Week-one deliverable: a marked paper with every lost mark categorised
Two named priority topics, written down and not quietly changed

sections.heading: The term counted backwards from the June series
paragraphs: Entry deadlines sit months before examinations, and results arrive months after, which means the useful calendar for a Year 11 family is longer than the examination window suggests. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. For UAE candidates those are the two windows that exist. The February/March series is offered to India only, and a page that tells a Dubai parent otherwise is handing them a date they will act on and then miss.

The table below is the shape of a term read from the examination backwards rather than from the syllabus forwards. The dates themselves move each year and are set by the school and the board, not by us, so treat the milestones as fixed and the dates as something to confirm against your school's examinations officer and the board's own published timetable. One Cambridge detail deserves special attention: every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential that you use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. A printout from an internet search is not a timetable.

Reading the term this way changes what you buy. If there are sixteen weeks left, content repair is still sensible and a weekly session is enough. At eight weeks, content repair has to be rationed to two topics and the rest of the time goes to full papers under time. At four weeks, adding new content is actively harmful: the only work left with a positive return is error-pattern clean-up on topics the student already half-knows. Parents in Al Habtoor City most often arrive at the eight-week point, which is late enough to need structure and early enough for structure to work.

Results day belongs on this calendar too, because it is when the next decision gets made. Pearson's published pattern is a useful anchor: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. If a resit is on the table, the November entry has to be lodged long before the June result is understood, so the conversation happens in the spring, not in August.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1: which papers your child actually sits
paragraphs: Parents are often surprised to learn they do not know which maths qualification their child is taking. The school letter says IGCSE Mathematics. The entry says 0580, 0607, 4MA1 or 4MB1. Those are four different examinations with different paper structures, different calculator rules and different past-paper libraries, and revising on the wrong one is the most common avoidable waste of time we see from this part of Dubai.

Cambridge 0580 is the most widely sat in the emirate. It is tiered into Core and Extended, with Extended reaching the top grade and Core capped lower, and the tier decision is usually made by the department in Year 10 based on set performance. Cambridge 0607 International Mathematics is the graphic-display-calculator syllabus, more common in IB-continuum schools, and it includes an investigation element that 0580 does not. Pearson 4MA1 Mathematics A is tiered Foundation and Higher, sits two equally weighted papers and allows a calculator throughout. Pearson 4MB1 Mathematics B is a single-tier, more algebraically compressed alternative with a much smaller past-paper bank.

The practical consequences are concrete. A 0580 Extended student must drill non-calculator fluency because one paper demands it. A 4MA1 Higher student must drill calculator accuracy and rounding instead, because the examiner assumes the arithmetic is done for them and marks the interpretation. A 0607 student needs to be fluent with a graphic display calculator as an investigative tool, not merely as a calculator. None of these are preferences; they are what the specification says, and the published specification is the document to read rather than a revision website's summary.

One more reason to confirm the code: tier. Where a student is entered at Core or Foundation, the grade available is capped, and a capped grade can quietly close a post-16 door that the family assumed was open. If your child is aiming at A Level Mathematics or IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, the tier conversation belongs in Year 10 while it is still changeable, not in the spring of Year 11 when it is not.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE maths marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Across marked papers, lost marks cluster in a small number of repeatable places, and almost none of them are exotic topics. The largest single category is instruction-reading: an answer given to two decimal places when three significant figures were asked for, a length given when an area was wanted, a question answered in the wrong units. These are not knowledge failures and they are the fastest marks in the paper to recover, which is why a tutor should start there rather than with circle theorems.

The second cluster is unfinished method. On the long structured questions at the back of Cambridge 0580 Paper 4, method marks are available even when the final answer is wrong, and a student who abandons a question because the number looks ugly forfeits marks they had already earned. Training a student to write the next line even when they expect to be wrong is worth several marks a paper and takes about three sessions to establish as a habit.

The third is algebraic fluency under pressure: sign errors when expanding, dropped negatives, incorrect index laws, and the inability to rearrange a formula with the unknown on both sides. This is where a genuine content gap usually lives, and it usually traces back to Years 7 to 9. It is repairable in six to eight weeks of consistent short practice, and it is not repairable in a fortnight, which is the honest answer a parent deserves to hear in week one rather than week six.

The fourth is pacing. Many students lose more marks to the questions they never reached than to the ones they got wrong. The fix is procedural: a known order of attack, a watch on the desk, a rule for abandoning a question and returning to it, and enough full papers sat under time that the rule has become automatic. Pacing is trainable, measurable and almost never taught, which makes it the highest-return item on most eight-week plans.

sections.heading: What Dubai charges for IGCSE maths, and what eight weeks of it costs
paragraphs: Pricing in this market is unusually opaque. Of the competitor pages examined for this project, three published no figure at all, and the two that did quoted in US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family transacts in. The bands below are market rates collected from published provider pages and from the Bestimate tutoring-cost table for Dubai. They are not IB Gram's price list; they exist so you can tell whether a quote you have been given is normal.

Read the table by monthly cost rather than by hourly rate, because that is the number that actually lands on a family budget. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run roughly AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. Published package pricing in this market includes around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. The gap between those two numbers is almost entirely travel.

That travel premium is worth naming precisely, because it is what an Al Habtoor City family is deciding about. In-home one-to-one visits in Dubai are quoted at roughly AED 180-500 an hour once the tutor's drive is priced in, against roughly AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The difference does not buy better teaching. It buys a car journey along Sheikh Zayed Road at the worst hour of the day, and it narrows the available tutor pool to whoever happens to live within range of your tower.

An eight-week block, two sessions a week, is sixteen sessions. At the middle of the online band that is a four-figure commitment in dirhams, and it is worth doing the arithmetic before you start rather than discovering it in week five. For context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Tutoring is the part of the education budget that is still moving, which is a good argument for deciding the size of the block up front.

sections.heading: Al Habtoor City evenings: towers, the Canal and when a session can realistically start
paragraphs: Al Habtoor City is a cluster of residential towers and hotels on the Sheikh Zayed Road frontage of the Dubai Water Canal, between Business Bay and Al Safa. It has no school of its own. Every secondary student living here travels out of the development in the morning and back into it in the afternoon, and both journeys cross or run along Sheikh Zayed Road at its least cooperative hours. That single fact shapes the tutoring week more than any pedagogical preference does.

Working backwards from a realistic evening: a school day that ends at 15:00 in Al Safa or Umm Suqeim puts most students back in the tower between 15:45 and 16:45 depending on the day and the route. Add the lift, a change of clothes and something to eat, and the first session slot that survives a bad traffic day is 17:30 or 18:00. Families who book 16:30 in optimism tend to rebook by week three. Families who book 18:00 complete the block. An online session also removes the second journey entirely, which on a Tuesday in term time is not a small gain.

The tower layout matters in a smaller way too. Study space in a high-rise apartment is often a shared dining table rather than a dedicated room, and an online maths session works considerably better with a specific setup: a hard surface, squared paper, the student's own calculator rather than a phone, headphones so the household is not a factor, and the camera angled so the tutor can see the working being written rather than only the student's face. Ten minutes of setup before the first session is worth more than a change of tutor.

Ramadan reshapes the calendar for a few weeks each year, and the schools adjust their hours. Sessions move to late morning or to the post-Iftar window, and families usually want fewer, shorter sessions rather than the same timetable pushed later. We plan that shift in advance rather than cancelling through it, because for a Year 11 student those weeks frequently fall close to a mock series.

sections.heading: The schools nearby, the regulator and what an inspection letter tells you about maths
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a judgement on a six-band scale running from Outstanding down to Very Weak. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are regulated by ADEK, Sharjah by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah by the federal Ministry of Education. Knowing which body publishes the report tells you where to read it.

The scale of the market is worth holding in mind: KHDA figures for 2024-25 record 387,441 students across 227 private schools in Dubai, offering seventeen different curricula, with UK-curriculum provision accounting for the largest share of enrolment, Indian curricula next, then American, then the International Baccalaureate. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK-curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 new places. For a parent, that density is the reason the maths code varies so much between two children living in the same tower.

An inspection band is useful to a tutoring decision only if you read past the headline. A school rated Outstanding overall can still have a specific department under strain, and the published report breaks judgements down by subject and phase. If the report names mathematics attainment or progress in the secondary phase as the area needing improvement, that is a stronger signal than the overall letter, and it is a legitimate reason to put support in place early rather than waiting for a mock result.

Alongside the licensed international curriculum, KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools, and its guidance requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Those subjects sit on the same timetable as maths, and they are part of why a Year 11 week is as full as it is.

sections.heading: Permits, honest limits and the resit route nobody plans for
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

There are things a tutor must not do, and they are worth stating plainly because this market contains providers who do them. A tutor teaches, explains, sets work, marks it and gives feedback on the student's own working. A tutor does not produce assessed work. For IGCSE Mathematics there is no coursework component, so the question arises less often than it does at IB, but the principle holds for any school-assessed task: if a provider offers to supply finished work, that is a malpractice trigger for your child, not a service. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules have been reported as barring school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries its own code of conduct in the same direction.

IB Gram holds no accreditation or approval from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and no page here will claim otherwise. We are a tutor-matching platform. We do not operate a centre, office or branch in the UAE, we do not sell in-home visits anywhere in the Emirates, and we do not administer examinations or perform Ministry equivalency. Those are things to verify with the school, the board and the authority directly, and the official pages are the place to do it.

The resit route deserves a plan rather than a panic. Cambridge candidates in the UAE who need a second attempt use the November series; Pearson candidates use November as well. Entries close well before the examination, which means the decision is taken months earlier than most families expect. If equivalency is on the horizon, the Ministry of Education's British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education not counted among those five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject figure; the published rule is five. Verify your own case on the Ministry's own channel before acting on any page, including this one.

process.title: A free trial lesson that diagnoses rather than sells

You receive a short written note afterwards naming the two priority topics and the error patterns, and that note is yours whether or not you book anything.

process.title: Agree the slot that survives a bad traffic evening
process.description: We fix a weekly time in Gulf Standard Time, chosen to sit after the school run rather than inside it. For Al Habtoor City that usually means 17:30 or later. A slot that works on a good day and fails on a bad one costs more in rescheduled sessions than it saves in convenience.

process.title: Work the block backwards from the paper
process.description: Weeks one and two diagnose and attack the two named topics. Weeks three to six alternate content and full timed papers. The last two weeks add nothing new and work only on error patterns and pacing. Every paper is marked against the published mark scheme so the progress you are shown is a mark count, not an impression.

process.title: Review honestly at the halfway point
process.description: At week four you get a straight answer about whether the target is still in reach, based on marked papers rather than optimism. If a different tutor is a better fit, we change tutor rather than defending the match. If the honest answer is that the target needs the November series instead, we say so while there is still time to enter.

whyPoints.title: The tutor pool is not limited to who can drive to your tower
whyPoints.description: An in-home arrangement in Al Habtoor City selects from tutors willing to make the journey at 18:00. For a specific need - Additional Mathematics 0606, or 0607 with a graphic display calculator - that difference is the whole decision.

whyPoints.title: Marking against the published mark scheme

whyPoints.title: A clear line on what a tutor may do

We plan blocks around those windows, around the entry deadlines that sit months earlier, and around Ramadan and the Dubai school calendar. whyPoints.title: One child, one tutor, one plan you can read
whyPoints.description: You get the same tutor each week, a written note after each session, and a named plan with two priority topics rather than a general promise of improvement. If the match is wrong, changing it early is cheaper than hoping. Nothing here depends on you being in a particular part of Dubai.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE maths tutor cost for a family in Al Habtoor City?
faqs.answer: Dubai market rates for a qualified subject tutor working online run roughly AED 150-300 an hour, with IGCSE and IB specialists quoted from about AED 200 to 450 or more. Published monthly figures are a better guide for a household budget: around AED 240-600 for budget weekly support, AED 600-1,200 in the mid band, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist examination-year work. In-home visits in Dubai are quoted higher, roughly AED 180-500 an hour, because the fee includes the tutor's journey. Those are market figures from published provider pages and the Bestimate Dubai rate table, not an IB Gram price list; ask us for a quote after the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor to our tower in Al Habtoor City?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family's address is a service we run in India only. Every lesson for an Al Habtoor City family is delivered one-to-one online over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. In practice that is an advantage rather than a compromise here: you are choosing from tutors who have taught your child's exact syllabus to examination rather than from those willing to drive to Sheikh Zayed Road in the evening peak, you are not paying a travel premium, and nobody loses a session to traffic. Screen sharing, a shared whiteboard and session recordings cover the things a kitchen table used to.

faqs.question: Which maths syllabus has my child's school actually entered them for?
faqs.answer: Ask the examinations officer for the code on the entry, not the subject name. Dubai schools near Al Safa and Jumeirah use Cambridge 0580 Mathematics, Cambridge 0607 International Mathematics, Pearson 4MA1 Mathematics A or Pearson 4MB1 Mathematics B, and some add Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics or Pearson 4PM1 Further Pure Mathematics. The code determines the paper structure, the calculator rules and which past papers are worth sitting. A student revising on the wrong board's papers is working hard in the wrong dialect, and it is the most common avoidable mistake we see. Get the code, the tier and the series in one email, then build the revision plan around all three.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE candidates in Dubai sit the June series or the November one?
faqs.answer: Both exist for UAE candidates. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Most Dubai schools enter their main Year 11 cohort for the summer window and use November as the resit route. The February/March Cambridge series is offered to India only, so a UAE family should ignore any date they see for it. One Cambridge rule matters practically: every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and you must use the timetable version for your zone, because Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one.

faqs.question: Is eight weeks long enough to change an IGCSE maths grade?
faqs.answer: Eight weeks is enough to recover marks that are being lost to technique, instruction-reading, pacing and unfinished method, and those are usually the largest category on a marked mock paper. Eight weeks is not enough to rebuild three years of missing algebra, and a tutor who tells you otherwise is selling rather than teaching. The honest process is to sit a full paper in week one, categorise every lost mark, name two priority topics, and review at week four against a second marked paper. No tutor can promise a specific grade, and if the mid-block evidence says the target needs the November series instead, that is better heard in week four than in August.

faqs.question: Should my child take Core or Extended tier, and when is that decided?
faqs.answer: Extended on Cambridge 0580, or Higher on Pearson 4MA1, reaches the top grades; Core and Foundation are capped. The department usually decides from set performance during Year 10, and many parents discover the tier only when a mock result arrives. That timing matters because a capped grade can quietly close a post-16 route: A Level Mathematics and IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches both assume the higher tier. If your child is aiming that way, raise the tier question in Year 10 while it is still changeable, and ask what specifically would need to improve for an Extended entry to be considered.

faqs.question: For an Al Habtoor City student, how do Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 differ?
faqs.answer: Paper structure and calculator rules. Cambridge 0580 sits two papers where one is taken without a calculator, so non-calculator fluency, exact-form answers and notation carry real weight. Pearson 4MA1 sits two equally weighted papers with a calculator allowed throughout, which shifts the risk to rounding, accuracy and interpreting what the display means. Question wording differs noticeably between the boards as well. Both are respected qualifications and neither is easier in any general sense, but revision has to match the one your child is entered for, which is why the syllabus code is the first thing a tutor should ask you for.

faqs.question: When in the term should an Al Habtoor City family start maths support?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most do. The cheapest intervention is a weekly session running alongside school teaching from early Year 10, because it prevents gaps rather than repairing them. The most common real starting point is the fortnight after a Year 11 mock result, which leaves roughly eight weeks and makes structure essential. At three or four weeks out, adding new content stops helping and the only work with positive return is error-pattern clean-up and pacing. If you are reading this with more than twelve weeks left, you have the comfortable version of the problem.

faqs.question: Can my child resit IGCSE maths in the November series after a summer result?
faqs.answer: Yes, November is the UAE resit route for both Cambridge and Pearson. The practical difficulty is timing: entries close well before the examination, and summer results arrive late in August, which leaves a narrow window for a decision many families have not thought about. Pearson's published pattern shows June 2026 results reaching centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, with November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026. If a resit is even possible, discuss it with the school in the spring, confirm the entry deadline with the examinations officer, and diary it the week results land.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does Ministry equivalency count for a Dubai school leaver?
faqs.answer: For the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among the five required subjects. One competitor page currently states six subjects, which does not match the published rule. Equivalency is a Ministry process, not something a tutoring platform performs or guarantees, so verify your own case on the Ministry's own channel before making any decision.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics 0606 worth taking alongside the main maths grade?
faqs.answer: It is worth taking when the main grade is already secure and the student is heading for A Level Mathematics, IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, or an engineering or economics degree. Cambridge 0606 brings calculus, logarithms, binomial expansion and trigonometric identities forward by a year, which removes most of the shock from the post-16 jump. It is not worth taking when it is competing for revision time with a main grade that is not yet safe. The honest sequence is to secure Extended or Higher first, then add 0606 if there is genuine capacity, and a tutor should tell you when the answer is to drop it.

faqs.question: How do online maths lessons handle written working on paper?
faqs.answer: Working is the whole point of a maths session, so the setup is built around it. The student writes on squared paper or a tablet, the camera is angled at the page rather than the face, and a shared digital whiteboard carries anything the tutor needs to demonstrate. The tutor watches the working appear line by line, which is where diagnosis happens: a sign error, a dropped negative or an abandoned method is visible as it occurs. Papers are photographed and marked against the published mark scheme between sessions. Ten minutes of setting up the camera, calculator and paper before the first lesson prevents most of the friction people expect.

faqs.question: Can Al Habtoor City sessions move into the post-Iftar window during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we plan the shift in advance rather than cancelling through it. Dubai schools adjust hours during Ramadan, and most families want fewer and shorter sessions rather than the same timetable pushed later. Late-morning slots work well for students whose school day has been compressed, and the post-Iftar window suits households that prefer the evening. For a Year 11 student the weeks matter because they often sit close to a mock series, so we agree the revised timetable before the month starts and set lighter work between sessions.

faqs.question: What happens if no IGCSE maths specialist is free at the slot we want?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than filling the slot with whoever is available. For common requests - Extended 0580, 4MA1 Higher - matching is usually quick. For narrower needs such as 0607 with a graphic display calculator, 4MB1 or Additional Mathematics 0606, the pool is smaller and the honest options are a different time, a short wait for the right tutor, or a marking clinic in the meantime. We would rather lose a booking than place a generalist on a specialist paper eight weeks before a series. If a UAE-based tutor is not available for a niche paper, we say where the tutor is based before you book.

faqs.question: Does a maths tutor working with an Al Habtoor City household need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount you read as unverified. The application runs through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, and MoHRE lists a two-working-day completion time.
