intro.heading: Price the tutoring against everything else you are paying
paragraphs: A tutoring budget looks reasonable on its own and often looks different beside the rest of the education spend. So start with the context. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Dubai had 227 private schools serving 387,441 students in 2024-25, and seven more schools join for the 2026-27 intake, creating 16,846 places. School costs are flat and capacity is growing.

Against that backdrop, a maths tutoring line that rises every term deserves a direct question: what did the last block of hours actually move? For a household in Al Jaddaf the honest version of that question has a testable answer, because mathematics is the subject where marks are most diagnosable. A timed paper marked against the published scheme before a block and after it will say whether the money worked. Almost nobody runs that test, which is why so much is spent without anybody knowing.

The published rates are the second piece of context. Budget online tutoring in Dubai is advertised from AED 33 to AED 52 by Tutopiya and from AED 45 to AED 65 by EdFlik. A qualified subject tutor online is quoted at roughly AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialist rates run from around AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650 at the top. In-home visiting rates are quoted at AED 180 to AED 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to AED 500 by home-tutor providers. Each figure belongs to the provider named and was read in October 2026.

Monthly, which is how families actually budget, Bestimate's estimates for a weekly one-hour session run roughly AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle band, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are per subject. Monthly packages seen in the market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Al Jaddaf or anywhere else in the UAE. Tuition for UAE families is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; home visiting is a service we operate only in India. We also print no IB Gram hourly rate on this page, because the right figure depends on the specification, the tier and how close the series is, and a single number on a landing page would be wrong for most of the people reading it. The free trial comes first and the quote follows it.

What follows prices maths support in context, ranks interventions by what they move per dirham, explains why a tier decision is a spending decision, does the resit arithmetic, and sets out why Additional Mathematics 0606 is simultaneously the most expensive hour in this market and often the best value in it.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-jaddaf.programmesIntro: An Al Jaddaf family buying IGCSE maths support is at one of three decision points, each with a different cost profile. These are the routes we cover.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: A two-year course entered at Core or Extended, assessed by written papers with no coursework. Core is capped below the top grades; Extended carries the full range and adds algebraic fractions, vectors, circle theorems and harder trigonometry. Paper durations and calculator arrangements have been revised across syllabus versions, so the current syllabus document is the only safe reference.
programmes.countryNote: The cost-relevant detail is the ceiling. A Core entry made for safety is cheaper to prepare for and closes the top grades, which can mean paying later for a post-16 route that was foreclosed at sixteen. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with a separate timetable each, and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: Specification A, tiered Foundation and Higher, assessed by two written papers of two hours each at 100 marks apiece with a calculator permitted. Specification B, 4MB1, has a different structure and is entered by fewer schools. Foundation carries a grade ceiling, so the tier decision is a grade decision taken a year ahead of the paper.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. That January timing is a budgeting fact: a November resit decision is taken in August and paid for in the autumn, when demand is already peaking.

programmes.name: Cambridge Additional Mathematics
programmes.description: A separate award alongside 0580 Extended, covering functions, quadratics in depth, binomial expansion, differentiation, integration, advanced trigonometry and vectors. There is no Core tier and no lower-tier fallback, and schools frequently teach it in less curriculum time than the content warrants.
programmes.countryNote: Within any single Dubai district the number of tutors who have taught 0606 through to a June series is small, so the rate reflects scarcity. It is also the subject with the clearest financial payoff, because a student who has done 0606 meets almost nothing new in the first term of A Level Mathematics or IB Analysis and Approaches, where support is considerably more expensive per hour.

programmes.name: The November resit
programmes.description: Both boards offer a November series available to UAE candidates, which is the standard retake route. Entry is made through the school's exam office shortly after June results, and results arrive in the new year rather than in August.
programmes.countryNote: This is the most commonly unbudgeted cost in an Al Jaddaf IGCSE year and it carries three charges at once: an entry fee, a compressed autumn of intensive tuition bought at peak demand, and a results date that may land after sixth-form conversations have moved on. Deciding in advance what June result would trigger a resit converts a surprise into a line you have already priced.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-jaddaf.subjectsIntro: Within IGCSE mathematics, some topics are cheap to fix and some are not. These are the areas Al Jaddaf families buy support for, ranked loosely by what an hour achieves in each.

subjects.name: Reverse percentage and proportional reasoning
subjects.description: The most reliably failed question type at the lower tiers and the cheapest thing on this list to fix. The student knows what a percentage is and multiplies where they should divide. Twenty minutes of deliberate practice removes it from every subsequent paper.

subjects.name: Area and volume scale factors
subjects.description: Similar shapes with the linear factor applied to an area or a volume instead of being squared or cubed. One of the highest-value single corrections available, because the same error recurs across mensuration, similarity and ratio questions throughout the paper.

subjects.name: Writing claimable method
subjects.description: The dominant loss at the top tiers. A correct answer reached in three lines forfeits marks a five-line scheme would have awarded, and a wrong answer with no working rescues nothing. A fortnight of enforced habit is worth more than a month of new content.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, algebraic fractions, changing the subject and simultaneous equations with one non-linear. Expensive to fix relative to the items above, because fluency is built by repetition rather than by a single correction, but it underpins everything else.

subjects.name: Histograms and grouped data
subjects.description: Unequal class widths read as frequency rather than frequency density. A standing trap, cheap to correct, and worth doing before any broader statistics work because it appears in most papers in some form.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Sine and cosine rules, the ambiguous case, bearings and three-dimensional problems. Moderate cost. Half the lost marks here are a calculator left in the wrong angle mode, which is a habit rather than a knowledge problem.

subjects.name: Circle theorems and geometric reasoning
subjects.description: Requires a written reason alongside each step, and most students give the answer without it. Moderate cost to fix and high value, because the reasoning marks are predictable and the question type appears every series.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, vector geometry, and the four transformations with full descriptions. A rotation without a centre and a direction earns part marks at best, which makes this another cheap correction with a visible return.

subjects.name: Calculus in 0606
subjects.description: Differentiation of products, quotients and trigonometric functions, stationary points, rates of change and integration. The most expensive hour in this market because specialist supply is thin, and the one with the clearest post-16 payoff.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: the whole education line
paragraphs: Tutoring is usually assessed against other tutoring, which is the wrong comparison. The useful comparison is against the rest of what the household already pays for this child's education, because that is how the decision actually feels when the invoice arrives. School fees are the dominant item, and in Dubai they are currently stable: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package.

Tutoring, by contrast, tends to grow without anybody deciding that it should. A weekly hour in one subject becomes two subjects, then three, then an intensive block before the series, and the annual figure arrives at something nobody chose. The mechanism is not greed on anybody's part; it is the absence of a stopping rule. A block without a stated endpoint renews by default, and a renewal that nobody evaluated is a renewal nobody can justify.

Two further items belong in the same line and are routinely left out. Examination entry fees apply where a student sits as a private candidate rather than through their school, which happens for a resit or for a subject the school does not offer; those are quoted by the centre rather than published centrally, so ask the exam office. And the resit itself, which is the expensive surprise because it lands after a full year of spending.

The table below sets the items beside each other with what is actually known about each. Where a figure is not published, it says so rather than guessing, because an invented number in a cost table is worse than an empty cell.

sections.heading: What moves a maths mark per dirham spent
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject where return on a tutoring hour is most measurable, because the errors are specific and the mark scheme is published. That makes it possible to rank interventions by what they move rather than by how reassuring they feel, and the ranking is not what most families expect. The cheapest interventions are corrections, and they are cheap because the same error is costing marks on every paper the student sits.

Top of the list is reverse percentage at Core and Foundation tier. The question gives a price after a discount and asks for the price before; the student multiplies instead of dividing. Twenty minutes removes it permanently. Second is area and volume scale factors, where the linear factor is applied to an area or a volume instead of being squared or cubed, which recurs across mensuration, similarity and ratio. Third is histograms with unequal class widths read as frequency rather than frequency density.

At Extended and Higher tier the highest-return item is writing claimable method. A correct answer reached in three lines forfeits marks that a five-line scheme would have awarded on a question the student fully understood, and a wrong answer with no working rescues nothing at all. This is a habit rather than a topic, it takes about a fortnight of enforced practice, and it is worth more than a month of new content for most students at a middle grade.

Expensive interventions are the ones where fluency has to be built rather than an error corrected: algebraic manipulation at the top tiers, and the calculus content in Additional Mathematics 0606. Those genuinely need weeks, and they are where a weekly arrangement rather than a short block is justified. Buying a weekly arrangement for a problem that was three corrections is the commonest waste in this market, and a marked timed paper tells you which situation you are in for the price of one session.

sections.heading: The tier decision is a spending decision
paragraphs: Cambridge Core and Pearson Foundation both carry a grade ceiling, and a student entered at the lower tier cannot be awarded the top grades however well they perform. Extended and Higher carry the full range with harder content and a steeper paper. Schools normally decide on Year 10 evidence, and a parent who does not ask will often learn the decision after it has been made. That is a financial decision as much as an academic one, and it is made a year before the money is spent.

The cheaper path is the lower tier. Preparation is narrower, the content load is lighter, and a safe pass is more likely. The cost sits later. A Level Mathematics, Physics and Economics and IB Higher Level sciences assume the Extended or Higher tier content, so a ceiling accepted at sixteen can close a post-16 route, and reopening it means buying bridging support at post-16 rates, which are higher than IGCSE rates in every band of this market.

There is a specific window where tutoring money does unusual work, and it is narrow. Between a provisional tier decision and the final entry, a borderline student who gets focused work on the exact Extended or Higher topics the department doubts can move the decision. A student who gets generalised extra maths usually does not, because the department is watching particular evidence: algebraic fluency, confidence with the harder geometry, and performance on the longer structured paper under timed conditions.

So the advice for an Al Jaddaf family is to ask the maths department two questions in Year 10. Which tier are they planning, and what evidence would change it. Both answers are free and both are more useful than any amount of hours bought in ignorance of them. If the department names specific topics, that is the spending target and a short block is enough. If they name general confidence, that is a slower and more expensive problem and worth knowing early.

sections.heading: The resit arithmetic, done in advance
paragraphs: A November resit is the cost families discover rather than plan, and it arrives at the worst possible moment: after a full year of spending, at the point when demand across the Dubai market peaks. It carries three charges at once. An entry fee, made through the school's exam office shortly after June results. A compressed block of intensive tuition in the autumn, bought when specialist availability is thinnest. And a results date in the new year, which Pearson's November 2025 series illustrates: those results reached students on 22 January 2026.

The way to defuse it is to set a decision rule in advance. Before the June series, agree what result would trigger a resit in which subject. That single conversation converts a panicked August into an executed plan, lets the autumn block be booked while slots exist, and removes the scramble that makes the whole thing expensive. It also prevents the opposite error, which is resitting a grade that was actually sufficient for the destination the student is heading to.

There is a calendar point that matters for a maths resit specifically. A November entry means the autumn term contains both the resit preparation and, for a student who has moved into a post-16 course, the start of A Level or IB Diploma mathematics. Those two compete directly for the same evenings, and the post-16 course is the one with longer-term consequences. A resit plan that ignores this buys hours into a week that has no room for them.

One correction worth making while on the subject of series. Cambridge's February and March series is offered in India only. UAE candidates sit the June and November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Several pages aimed at Gulf parents quote a February or March window with an Indian entry deadline, and a family budgeting intensive tuition towards it would be paying for revision ahead of an exam their school cannot enter them for.

sections.heading: Additional Mathematics 0606: most expensive hour, often best value
paragraphs: Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 is the most expensive subject to support in this market and frequently the best purchase in it, which is an unusual combination worth explaining. The expense is supply. It is taken by a minority of IGCSE students, so within any single Dubai district the number of tutors who have taught it through to a June series is small, and the rate reflects scarcity rather than difficulty.

The value is forward-looking. 0606 introduces differentiation, integration, binomial expansion, composite and inverse functions and advanced trigonometric identities a full year before A Level Mathematics or IB Analysis and Approaches would. A student who has done it meets almost nothing genuinely new in the first term of a post-16 maths course. A student arriving from 0580 Extended alone meets several things at once, in a term that also contains five other subjects, and the support needed then is bought at post-16 specialist rates.

There is also a structural reason 0606 benefits disproportionately from one-to-one work. It has no Core tier and no lower-level fallback, and schools frequently teach it in less curriculum time than the content warrants, sometimes as an option outside the main timetable. That produces a cohort of capable students covering calculus quickly, with the department moving on before fluency has settled. The gap is narrow and specific, which is exactly what an hour of one-to-one time addresses well and a group class does not.

The practical advice for a family in Al Jaddaf weighing it. If post-16 plans point towards A Level Mathematics, Physics, Engineering or IB Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, 0606 is worth the extra load and worth the scarcity premium on support. If they do not, the same money spent raising an Extended grade in 0580 is the better purchase, and we will say so rather than selling the harder option.

sections.heading: Group classes, centres and the cost per usable minute
paragraphs: A tuition centre group class is the cheapest format per hour in Dubai because the teacher's cost divides across the room, and that saving is real. It is the right purchase where the problem is practice volume and a student who works better with others present. For an Al Jaddaf family it fails for two reasons that are specific rather than general, and both are worth checking before paying for a term.

The first is the mixed room. A class advertised as IGCSE Mathematics may contain Cambridge Core candidates, Cambridge Extended candidates, Pearson Foundation and Pearson Higher candidates simultaneously, because centres draw from several schools. The content overlaps enough to make the class deliverable and differs enough to make it imprecise, and the highest-value interventions in maths are corrections caught as they happen, which a teacher managing eight students cannot deliver.

The second is the journey. Tuition centres cluster in commercial districts, so a class at 17:00 suits a student who finished school nearby and not an Al Jaddaf student arriving home from Nad Al Sheba at 17:15. Travel to the centre reinserts a journey that online delivery had already removed, and that is a cost in time and in attention rather than in money. It is also the usual reason a centre arrangement lapses by the middle of term.

The honest arithmetic is cost per usable minute rather than cost per hour. A cheap class the student reaches tired, in a mixed room, with no individual correction, may deliver fewer useful minutes than a shorter one-to-one session at a higher rate. Al Jaddaf's short commutes make the early one-to-one slot genuinely available, which is the district's main financial advantage and the one most families never use.
bullets: Group classes are the cheapest per hour and suit practice volume genuinely

sections.heading: Claims and prices to discount before comparing
paragraphs: Part of what gets quoted in this market is a claim rather than a capability. Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. A KHDA inspection rating judges a school and does not transfer to any tutor. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson, and a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation for training institutes with premises and staff that we do not hold.

The permit is the one claim that is checkable and free. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's own Private Tutor Licensing service, listed with no fee and a two-working-day completion time. A provider citing permit costs to justify a rate is citing a cost that does not exist.

Discount self-asserted ratings when comparing prices. Competitors in this market publish star ratings and review counts that contradict each other on the same page, and one shows a figure in its structured data that differs from the one a reader sees. A rating with no countable, attributable, dated reviews behind it should be treated as decoration. The same applies to any statistic quoted without a sample size, a date and a method, and to examiner claims that cannot be evidenced.

Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published; a figure circulating in this market could not be verified against any official source, and the ministry was reported as not having specified amounts or detailed penalties. So no amount appears here, and a provider quoting one to you has told you something useful about their other figures.
bullets: KHDA regulates schools; a rating judges the school and never a tutor

sections.heading: Getting started, and the stopping rule
paragraphs: Send the board, the specification code, the tier, whether 0606 is being taken, and two evening windows that genuinely work from Al Jaddaf after the school run. We match a specification specialist and run one free trial lesson in the slot you intend to keep. One trial per student, nothing charged beforehand, no card details needed to book it, and the tutor writes a short note on what the diagnostic showed.

Then agree the stopping rule before the first paid session, because that is the single discipline that keeps this budget honest. A block of six to eight sessions, a named target, and a school assessment as the finish line. At that assessment, the question is whether the targeted error moved and what evidence shows it. If the answer names a mark, there is a case for continuing while there is more to gain. If the answer is general improvement in confidence, the block ends.

We will also recommend a cheaper tier where it fits, which is worth stating because few providers do. For reverse percentage corrections, recall discipline and Core homework support, budget online tutoring at AED 33 to AED 65 is genuinely adequate and buying a specialist would be reassurance rather than teaching. The specialist tier earns its rate on 0606 calculus, on a scarce specification, and on compressed pre-series work where experience of what moves marks quickly has real value.

Two limits, because the stopping rule above only works if the destination is honest. The sourced equivalency threshold on the British track is lower than most Al Jaddaf parents assume: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level at E or two Advanced Subsidiary Levels. A student aiming at grade 7 in mathematics is working well above that floor, and nothing on this page implies tutoring is required for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency, for university admission or for school progression - verify your own case with the Ministry rather than with us. The second limit is simpler: nobody can promise a grade, and this page does not.

faqs.question: How should I judge whether an IGCSE maths tutoring budget is reasonable?
faqs.answer: Against the rest of your education spend rather than against other tutoring quotes. Dubai private school fees are not increasing for the 2026-27 academic year, which KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026, so a tutoring line that grows every term deserves a stated reason. Published monthly bands, per subject, run roughly AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget tier, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are Bestimate's estimates for a weekly one-hour session.

faqs.question: Which maths fixes give the most improvement for the least money?
faqs.answer: Corrections, because the same error costs marks on every paper. Reverse percentage at Core and Foundation tier leads: the student multiplies where they should divide, and twenty minutes removes it permanently. Area and volume scale factors applied linearly instead of being squared or cubed come second, recurring across mensuration, similarity and ratio. Histograms with unequal class widths read as frequency rather than frequency density come third. At the top tiers, writing claimable method is the highest-return habit available.

faqs.question: Why is writing out the method worth a fortnight of practice?
faqs.answer: Because it is where Extended and Higher tier marks disappear. A student reaches a correct answer in three lines where the published scheme awards marks across five, and forfeits two on a question they fully understood. In the reverse case, an early arithmetic slip with no working written down rescues nothing, when method marks would have been available. The instruction is simple and the habit takes about two weeks to embed: write the line you were about to do in your head.

faqs.answer: Yes, and it is made a year before the money is spent. Cambridge Core and Pearson Foundation carry a grade ceiling that performance cannot exceed. The lower tier is cheaper to prepare for and the cost arrives later, because A Level Mathematics, Physics and Economics and IB Higher Level sciences assume the Extended or Higher content. Reopening a closed route means buying bridging support at post-16 rates, which are higher in every band. Ask the department which tier they plan and what evidence would change it.

faqs.question: What does a November maths resit actually cost a family?
faqs.answer: Three things at once, which is why it hurts. An entry fee made through the school's exam office shortly after June results. A compressed block of intensive tuition in the autumn, bought when demand across Dubai peaks and specialist availability is thinnest. And a results date in the new year rather than August: Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Agreeing in advance what June result triggers a resit converts the surprise into a line you have already priced.

faqs.question: Does a November resit clash with starting A Level or IB maths?
faqs.answer: Directly, and families rarely plan for it. A November entry means the autumn term contains both resit preparation and the opening weeks of a post-16 maths course, and the two compete for the same evenings. The post-16 course has the longer-term consequences, so a resit plan that ignores the collision buys hours into a week with no room for them. If both are unavoidable, the honest answer is fewer, better-placed sessions rather than more of them.

faqs.question: Why does Additional Mathematics support cost more than 0580 support?
faqs.answer: Supply rather than difficulty. 0606 is taken by a minority of IGCSE students, so within any single Dubai district the number of tutors who have taught it through to a June series is small and the rate reflects that scarcity. The offsetting value is forward-looking: a student who has done 0606 meets almost nothing new in the first term of A Level Mathematics or IB Analysis and Approaches, where support is bought at higher post-16 rates. It is worth the premium only if post-16 plans point that way.

faqs.answer: Per hour, yes, because the teacher's cost divides across the room, and it genuinely suits a student whose problem is practice volume. It fails on two specifics. A class advertised as IGCSE Mathematics may hold Cambridge Core, Cambridge Extended, Pearson Foundation and Pearson Higher candidates at once, and a teacher managing eight cannot deliver the corrections that move maths marks. And centres cluster in commercial districts, which reinserts a journey online delivery had removed. Compare cost per usable minute, not per hour.

faqs.question: Does an earlier session really produce better value in maths specifically?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the reason is working memory rather than general tiredness. A multi-step algebraic rearrangement requires holding intermediate states while applying a rule to one of them, and an error at step two is invisible until step five. A long school day degrades exactly that capability. Al Jaddaf's short commutes often allow a 16:30 start, which is unusual in Dubai. The real unit price of an hour is the rate divided by the fraction of it that works, so an earlier slot is cheaper at the same rate.

Whether VAT is included in the figure you were given. What the cancellation notice window is, because a slot that cannot be resold is normally charged. intro.heading: Two boards, two tiers, four different qualifications
paragraphs: IGCSE mathematics in Dubai is not one qualification. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 splits into Core and Extended, with different paper pairs and grades running A* to G, where a Core entry cannot exceed grade C. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1 splits into Foundation and Higher, grades 9 to 1, and uses two papers rather than four across the tiers. A student described as doing IGCSE maths is doing one of those four, and the four need different past papers, different expectations and in some respects different teaching.

The tier is the more consequential of the two variables because it is a ceiling rather than a difficulty setting. A Cambridge Core candidate is not sitting an easier version of the Extended paper; they are sitting different papers over a smaller syllabus, and the grade they can reach is capped. The same is true at Foundation on Pearson, where the accessible grade range sits below what most A Level mathematics courses and Higher Level Diploma mathematics ask for.

The board is the second variable and it changes the feel of the paper more than the content. Pearson stems run longer with more to read before the mathematics starts. Cambridge Extended papers tend to use shorter multi-part structures with precise instructions. The supplied formula conventions differ. None of that makes one harder, and all of it means that practising the wrong board's papers produces a student who walks into a mock feeling the paper is strange when every topic on it is known.

Beyond board and tier, IGCSE mathematics marks are lost in a small number of predictable places, and the largest single cause has nothing to do with mathematical understanding. Mark schemes award credit for the method and the substitution separately from the final answer. A student who calculates mentally and writes one number down loses two or three marks a paper on slips that cost them nothing conceptually. Making the working mechanical is the cheapest available grade movement in the subject.

Then come the question types. Multi-step problems where the student abandons rather than banking partial credit. Bounds and rounding, where the method is simple and the precision is marked strictly. Algebraic fractions, where a single sign error propagates. Vectors and transformations, where the notation itself carries marks. Probability trees, where the structure earns credit before any arithmetic. Each is a short, teachable fix rather than a long programme.

One caution about specifications: boards revise paper structures and content between series, so the authoritative description of what a student will sit is the specification document for their own series on the board's website, read against the code on the statement of entry. Where this page names a code or a structure, treat it as a prompt to check that document rather than a substitute for it.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-khail-gate.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE mathematics topics where Extended and Higher tier marks are concentrated, described by the specific error that loses them.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation and fractions
subjects.description: Simplifying and combining algebraic fractions, and rearranging where the subject sits on the denominator. A single sign error propagates through every later line, and the method marks are only available to a student whose intermediate steps are written down.

subjects.name: Quadratics and the formula
subjects.description: Factorising with a leading coefficient, completing the square and applying the quadratic formula. Marks go missing where the formula is quoted incorrectly from memory rather than read from the supplied sheet, and where only one root is given.

subjects.name: Simultaneous equations including non-linear
subjects.description: The non-linear pair, a line against a curve, is a reliable Extended discriminator. Students find one solution and stop, losing the marks attached to the second, and frequently do not substitute back to produce the paired values.

subjects.name: Bounds, rounding and estimation
subjects.description: Conceptually simple and marked strictly. Upper and lower bounds for a calculated quantity require choosing the right combination of bounds for the operation involved, and students who guess rather than reason lose the whole question.

subjects.name: Trigonometry beyond right angles
subjects.description: Sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle, bearings and three-dimensional applications. The commonest losses are the ambiguous case of the sine rule and bearings measured from the wrong reference direction.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vector notation, vector geometry and describing transformations fully. A transformation described without all its required elements, such as a centre or a scale factor, scores partially however correct the picture is.

subjects.name: Probability and tree diagrams
subjects.description: The structure of the tree earns credit before any arithmetic, and conditional branches without replacement are where the structure usually goes wrong. Drawing it fully rather than working mentally is worth marks in itself.

subjects.name: Functions, graphs and gradients
subjects.description: Reading gradients and intercepts, sketching with asymptotes and intercepts labelled, and interpreting a graph in context. Sketches lose marks for unlabelled features that the student knew and did not mark on the diagram.

subjects.name: Statistics: averages from tables and cumulative frequency
subjects.description: Estimated means from grouped data, cumulative frequency curves, quartiles and box plots. The errors are procedural rather than conceptual: midpoints not used, or readings taken from the wrong axis scale.

subjects.name: Multi-step problem solving
subjects.levels: Extended and Higher, heavier on Pearson
subjects.description: Long questions combining several topics, where a student who cannot see the whole route abandons rather than completing the first step for credit. Banking partial marks is a teachable behaviour and worth several marks a paper.

sections.heading: Which board and which tier, and how to find out in ten minutes
paragraphs: The statement of entry the school issues names the board, the syllabus code and the tier for every subject. For mathematics that single line settles what a student should be practising, what grade is achievable and which past papers are relevant. Families frequently do not have it to hand, and schools will provide the codes on request well before the document itself is issued.

Inferring the board from the textbook is unreliable. Schools sometimes teach from one publisher's material and enter candidates with the other board, and revision guides bought for an older sibling may describe a specification since revised. The specification document on the board's website, for the student's own series, is the authority on paper structure and content, and it is free to read.

Knowing the tier matters more than most parents realise because of what it does to planning. A student entered for Cambridge Core should not be spending Saturdays on Extended content they will never be examined on, and a student entered for Extended should not be practising Core papers that will leave them unprepared for the structure of Paper 4. The same applies to Pearson Foundation and Higher. Mismatched practice is the commonest invisible waste in this subject.

There is one more line on the statement of entry worth checking: whether the subject entry is what the family expects at all. Errors happen, including tier changes agreed verbally and never processed. Reading each line, confirming board, code and tier, and querying anything inconsistent in writing takes ten minutes and the correction window is narrow, because entries close months before the papers.

sections.heading: Method marks: the mechanical habit worth a grade
paragraphs: The largest single source of avoidable loss in IGCSE mathematics is not a topic. It is the gap between what a student did and what they wrote down. Mark schemes allocate credit for identifying the correct approach and for substituting correctly, separately from the final answer. A student who works mentally and records a single number is gambling the whole question on getting the arithmetic right first time, and loses everything when they do not.

The habit that fixes it is mechanical and slightly tedious: write the relationship or the formula, substitute the given values, then state the answer with its units. Three lines where one used to be. On a question worth four marks, that converts a wrong answer from zero into two or three, and a strong student does it eight or ten times a paper. The arithmetic becomes less important, which is exactly the point.

Students resist this for understandable reasons. It feels slower, it feels like being treated as less capable, and in class a teacher has usually accepted the right answer without comment. The persuasive move is to show it on their own script: find three questions where the method was sound and the answer wrong, and count what writing the working would have earned. That calculation changes behaviour more reliably than instruction does.

There is a second presentational habit worth the same attention: stating the units and the degree of accuracy the question asked for. Questions specifying three significant figures or two decimal places mark it, and an otherwise perfect answer given to the wrong precision loses the accuracy mark. Reading the final line of the question before writing the answer is a two-second check with a measurable return across a paper.

sections.heading: Six question types that account for most of the loss
paragraphs: Across Extended and Higher papers the same half-dozen question types recur as the places marks go missing, and each has a short fix rather than a general one. Multi-step problems are the first: long questions combining topics where a student who cannot see the whole route writes nothing. The behaviour to teach is banking, doing the first step that is clearly available, which earns credit and often reveals the next step.

Bounds and rounding are the second. The mathematics is simple and the marking is strict: an upper bound for a quotient requires the upper bound of the numerator and the lower bound of the denominator, and a student who applies the same bound to both loses the question. Teaching the reasoning rather than a memorised rule is what makes it stick, because the rule flips with the operation.

Algebraic fractions are the third, where a sign error in the second line destroys the rest. Non-linear simultaneous equations are the fourth, where students find one solution and stop rather than producing both paired values. Vectors and transformations are the fifth, where a transformation described without its centre or scale factor scores partially however correct the understanding. Probability trees are the sixth, where the structure earns credit before the arithmetic and conditional branches without replacement are where it goes wrong.

Working through these one at a time, to reliability, is a six-week block rather than a term. The sequence matters less than the discipline of finishing each before moving on, and of re-testing it inside a full paper question afterwards rather than on isolated practice. A student who can do bounds in a dedicated exercise and fails them inside a longer question has not finished the topic.

sections.heading: Moving tier, and the evidence that makes it possible
paragraphs: A tier that is set too low is the most consequential fixable problem in IGCSE mathematics, and the window to fix it is short. Schools place students on Core or Foundation from Year 10 performance, and the placement caps the grade: Cambridge Core at C, Pearson Foundation below the range most A Level mathematics courses require. A student heading for A Level mathematics, Higher Level Diploma mathematics or most science routes needs the higher tier.

The decision is not arbitrary and schools are not being obstructive. A student who would score across the bottom of an Extended paper can come away with a secure C from Core rather than an insecure E, and for a student who will not need mathematics beyond sixteen that is the better outcome. The problem is that the decision is often made without the family understanding the consequence, and without the student understanding that it closes doors two years away.

What makes a reconsideration possible is raw marks on higher-tier papers. Six weeks of Extended or Higher papers sat to time and marked against the published scheme without generosity gives a head of department something concrete. If the marks support the move, the conversation is short. If they do not, the family has chosen on evidence rather than hope, which is also a result worth having.

Timing is everything and it is the part that catches people. Entries close months before the papers and the school's internal collation deadline sits earlier still. A conversation opened in the spring of Year 11 has usually missed the window for the next series. Opened in the spring of Year 10 or the first weeks of Year 11, it is routine administration. Families in this belt with a child currently in Year 10 have the most room and the least urgency, which is precisely why it gets postponed.

sections.heading: A past-paper routine built for mathematics specifically
paragraphs: Mathematics past papers are abundant and badly used. The standard pattern, working through a paper with the answers beside you, teaches almost nothing because nothing about it resembles the examination. A paper is diagnostic only when it is sat to time, without notes, and then marked against the published scheme by someone unwilling to be generous.

A workable weekly routine for a Year 11 student in this belt: one full paper from the right board and tier at the weekend, phone in another room, timed strictly. Self-marking the same day against the published scheme, with every lost mark labelled as content, method, misread or clock. Then the paid session spends its hour on the dominant label rather than starting at question one. Then one short targeted task midweek, ten or fifteen minutes on exactly that weakness.

The labelling is what makes the routine work, and it is the step families skip. Twelve lost marks that are two content, seven method and three clock call for a working-out habit and a timing plan, not more revision. The same twelve all in content call for teaching. A fortnight of labelled papers tells a parent more about their child's mathematics than a year of reports.

Volume is the other thing to get right. Three or four papers a week produces fatigue, careless marking and no improvement, because the student stops treating each one as a real attempt. One properly sat and properly marked paper a week, plus midweek targeted work, is sustainable through a whole exam term, and sustainability is what moves a grade over twelve weeks.

sections.heading: Budgeting a two-year mathematics plan rather than a crisis term
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject families most often buy support for, and the way they buy it is usually the most expensive available: nothing for eighteen months, then intensive help in the final term at peak demand. Spread as a planned two-year line, the same total spend covers considerably more hours and lands them where they are worth more.

The published Dubai rates frame it. At the budget end, Tutopiya advertises from around AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. Qualified subject tutors working online are published at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at around AED 270, and BartyED charges AED 650 for premium named tutors. In-home one-to-one is AED 180 to 500 with travel included. Monthly packages in the market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

A planned shape for mathematics across Years 10 and 11 might be a tier-evidence block in Year 10, nothing for two terms, a six-week technique block after the winter mocks, and a weekly session through the final term. That is perhaps thirty sessions across two years rather than twenty-four crammed into one term, and it includes the one intervention, the tier evidence, that the crisis version cannot deliver at all.

Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-band and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under an incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total, which makes a flat fee year the natural moment to commit to a planned line rather than an emergency one.

sections.heading: Online delivery for a handwritten subject
paragraphs: The fair objection to online mathematics tutoring is that the work is handwritten. The practical answer is a shared writing surface, a document camera or a phone propped over the page, with the student writing while the tutor watches each line appear. For mathematics that is better than reviewing a finished answer, because the error is almost always earlier than the last line, and a tutor watching can stop at the line where it happened rather than reconstructing it afterwards.

It also supports the single most important habit on this page. Method-mark discipline is about what reaches the page, and a tutor who can see the page as it is written can insist on the relationship and the substitution appearing in real time. That is harder to enforce through a photograph of completed homework, which is how a lot of remote tutoring actually operates.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and no tutor will arrive at an address in Al Khail Gate or anywhere else in the Emirates. All UAE lessons are one-to-one and delivered live over video on Gulf Standard Time. The published in-home band in Dubai is AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150 to 300 for comparable online work, and the difference largely reflects the journey rather than the teaching.

Two honest caveats. A student who will not work unless somebody is physically present is not fixed by the format, and for that household a local option deserves serious consideration. And full timed papers need an uninterrupted block, which for students travelling back along the Al Khail corridor usually means a weekend morning rather than a weekday evening, whichever format is chosen.

sections.heading: What we claim, and the regulatory position
paragraphs: Stated plainly: IB Gram holds no permit, licence, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and has no office, centre or branch in the UAE. The phrase approved circulates loosely in this market, and the only thing it could properly refer to for a tutoring business with premises is a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which requires initial approval, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry.

Individual private tutoring in the UAE is regulated separately and the facts are public. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's own service page lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without the permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so any figure quoted is unverified.

On materials and honesty: syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and should be referenced and linked at source rather than distributed. A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on a student's own work and does not write it, complete it or supply model answers for submission. Those boundaries are stated here rather than discovered later.

We publish no statistics about our own outcomes, no star ratings and no student counts, because we cannot produce the underlying data and a figure without its sample, date and method is decoration. Every AED band on this page is a market rate published by a named provider or rate study, credited as such, and every regulatory statement is drawn from the authority's own published material.

faqs.question: How do I find out which maths syllabus my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Read the statement of entry the school issues, or ask the school for the codes before it arrives. It names the board, the syllabus code and the tier: Cambridge 0580 Core or Extended, or Pearson 4MA1 Foundation or Higher. Do not infer the board from the textbook, because schools sometimes teach from one publisher's material and enter candidates with the other board. The specification document for your child's own series on the board's website is the authority on paper structure and content.

faqs.question: What grade can my son get if he is on Cambridge Core maths?
faqs.answer: Grade C is the ceiling. A Core entry sits a different paper pair over a smaller syllabus, so he has not merely been assessed more gently, he has not been taught several topics the Extended syllabus examines. That ceiling closes most A Level mathematics courses and Higher Level Diploma mathematics. If either is in the plan, the tier needs revisiting with timed Extended paper evidence before entries close, which means Year 10 or the first weeks of Year 11 rather than the spring.

faqs.question: Is Pearson Foundation tier the same as Cambridge Core?
faqs.answer: Similar in function, different in detail. Both are lower tiers with a restricted grade range, but Pearson grades 9 to 1 while Cambridge grades A* to G, and the paper structures differ: Pearson 4MA1 uses two papers across the tiers while Cambridge 0580 uses separate paper pairs. The practical point is the same either way: the lower tier caps the achievable grade below what most post-16 mathematics routes require, and the decision window closes with the entry deadline.

faqs.question: Why does my daughter lose marks when her final answers are right?
faqs.answer: If the answers are right she is probably losing accuracy and units marks rather than method marks. Questions specifying three significant figures or two decimal places mark the precision, and an otherwise perfect answer given to the wrong accuracy loses that mark. Units are marked where the question asks for them. Both are fixed by reading the final line of the question before writing the answer, which is a two-second check with a measurable return across a whole paper.

faqs.question: What is the fastest way to gain marks in IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: Writing the working. Mark schemes award credit for the correct relationship and the correct substitution separately from the final answer, so a student who calculates mentally and records one number loses everything on an arithmetic slip. The habit is mechanical: write the relationship, substitute the values, state the answer with units. Three lines where one used to be. The persuasive way to install it is to find three questions on the student's own script where the method was sound and count what the working would have earned.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths topics cause the most trouble at Extended level?
faqs.answer: Six recur. Multi-step problems, where a student who cannot see the whole route writes nothing instead of banking the first step. Bounds and rounding, marked strictly, where the right combination of bounds depends on the operation. Algebraic fractions, where a sign error in line two destroys the rest. Non-linear simultaneous equations, where one solution is found and the pair never completed. Vectors and transformations, where a description missing a centre or scale factor scores partially. And probability trees, where the structure earns credit before any arithmetic.

faqs.question: How do we get the school to move my child up a tier?
faqs.answer: With raw marks from higher-tier papers, not with a request. Have the student sit six weeks of Extended or Higher past papers under timed conditions and mark them against the published scheme without generosity, then bring the marks to the head of department. If they support the move the conversation is short. If they do not, the family has decided on evidence rather than hope. Crucially this has to happen before entries close, which is months before the papers.

faqs.question: How many maths papers a week should a Year 11 student do?
faqs.answer: One, properly. Sat to time from the right board and tier, no notes, phone in another room, then self-marked against the published scheme the same day with every lost mark labelled content, method, misread or clock. Three or four papers a week produces fatigue and careless marking, and the student stops treating each as a real attempt. One paper plus a short targeted midweek task on the dominant weakness is sustainable across a whole exam term.

faqs.question: Can we practise with the other board's past papers if ours run out?
faqs.answer: It is less useful than it looks and can be actively misleading. The content overlaps heavily, so it feels efficient, but the question shapes differ: Pearson stems run longer with more to read before the mathematics begins, Cambridge Extended uses shorter multi-part structures, and the supplied formula conventions are not identical. A student trained on one who sits the other tends to find the paper unfamiliar even when every topic is known. Exhaust your own board's archive, including older series, first.

faqs.question: Will a maths tutor come to our home in Al Khail Gate?
faqs.answer: Not from us. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and no tutor will arrive at an address anywhere in the Emirates. All UAE lessons are one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time, with the working visible line by line as the student writes. The published Dubai in-home band is AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150 to 300 for comparable online work.

faqs.question: How should we budget for maths support across Years 10 and 11?
faqs.answer: As a planned line rather than a crisis purchase. A tier-evidence block in Year 10, nothing for two terms, a six-week technique block after the winter mocks and a weekly session through the final term is around thirty sessions across two years, and it includes the tier evidence a final-term scramble cannot deliver at all. At published rates, Bestimate estimates roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-band and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work.

faqs.question: When are the IGCSE maths papers sat in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series and UAE centres sit those two; the February/March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with a separate timetable per zone and states that using the correct one is essential, since it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise. Use the timetable your school's exams officer issues.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics worth taking alongside Extended?
faqs.answer: For a student already secure on Extended and heading for A Level or Higher Level Diploma mathematics, yes: it bridges the gap in algebraic fluency and calculus foundations that otherwise lands in the first term of Year 12. For a student still insecure on Extended content it is a poor use of hours, because it adds a second syllabus before the first one is reliable. The deciding question is the current Extended paper mark, not enthusiasm, and one timed paper answers it.

faqs.question: Does an online tutor really see enough to help with maths?
faqs.answer: More than with a photograph of finished homework, which is how a lot of remote tutoring works in practice. With a shared writing surface, a document camera or a phone over the page, the tutor watches each line appear and can stop at the line where the error happened rather than reconstructing it afterwards. For method-mark discipline specifically it is the stronger format, because the relationship and substitution can be insisted on in real time as the page fills.

faqs.question: What if nobody is free who teaches our board and tier?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than substituting someone teaching the other specification. A particular board and tier at a particular hour does occasionally come up empty, especially in the weeks before a series when demand peaks across the city. The honest options are a different time, a different tutor with a handover of the labelled loss list, or a wait with a date attached. A tutor working from the wrong specification sets practice on question shapes the student will not meet.

intro.heading: Two syllabuses, two sets of rules, one word on the report
paragraphs: A school report that says mathematics tells you almost nothing about what your child will sit. In the schools around Al Khawaneej, two different international syllabuses are common: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics, code 0580, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, code 4MA1. They cover broadly similar content, which is why a mismatch does not announce itself in week one, and they differ in the things that decide marks: the number and structure of the papers, the names and arrangement of the tiers, and the rules about calculators.

That last point is the one that catches families out most sharply. The arrangement of calculator and non-calculator assessment is not the same across these syllabuses, and a student who has practised exclusively with a calculator to hand will find a non-calculator paper a different experience from the one they prepared for. Confirm your own syllabus's current arrangement against the board's published documentation rather than from memory or from a parent group, because these specifications are revised.

The tier question is equally consequential and uses different words on each syllabus. Cambridge divides 0580 into Core and Extended. Pearson divides 4MA1 into Foundation and Higher. In both cases the lower tier limits the grade a candidate can be awarded, and in both cases the entry becomes a permanent fact once the series has been sat. Families regularly discover the ceiling two years later, when a sixth-form requirement or a Diploma mathematics prerequisite turns out to sit above it.

So the first task is administrative rather than academic: establish the board, the code and the tier from the statement of entry or the front page of an issued past paper, and ask the school in writing what the grade ceiling is at your child's tier. Ten minutes of this is worth more than a fortnight of asking around for a tutor, because it is what turns a search for maths help into a search for the right maths help. Ask for it by email rather than at the school gate, so that you have the answer in writing and can forward it to anybody you are considering as a tutor.

The rest of this page is the syllabus detail: how the two compare, which topic areas carry the marks, what method marks are and why they are silently discarded, how to handle calculator and non-calculator work differently, the past-paper procedure that produces improvement in maths specifically, and the gap between IGCSE maths and what comes next. Teaching is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, because in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. Read it with your child's own statement of entry open, because several sections only become useful once the code is known.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-khawaneej.subjectsIntro: The topic areas an IGCSE maths candidate is examined on, with a note on what each costs students in practice. The point is to show where the recoverable marks actually live.

subjects.name: Number
subjects.description: Fractions, ratio, percentages, standard form, bounds and estimation. The highest-frequency source of avoidable loss across both syllabuses, because errors here are arithmetic slips inside questions the student understood, and they are fixable by practice rather than by teaching.

subjects.name: Algebra and graphs
subjects.levels: Both tiers, far deeper at the higher tier
subjects.description: Manipulation, equations, inequalities, sequences, functions and graph transformations. The decisive topic area: weakness here limits the whole paper and shows up in physics and chemistry marks as well as in maths.

subjects.name: Geometry
subjects.description: Angle reasoning, circle theorems, congruence and similarity. Marks are lost when a student reaches the right answer without stating the reason, since geometric reasoning questions award the justification and not only the figure.

subjects.name: Mensuration
subjects.description: Perimeter, area, surface area and volume, including compound shapes and parts of circles. Reliable marks for students who keep units straight and convert carefully, and a steady drain for students who do not.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.levels: Both tiers, extended at the higher tier
subjects.description: Right-angled trigonometry, then sine and cosine rules and three-dimensional work at the higher tier. Students lose marks by rounding too early in multi-step problems, which changes the final answer enough to fall outside the accepted range.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Vector arithmetic, geometric reasoning with vectors, and describing transformations fully. Description questions are routinely under-answered: a transformation needs every defining detail, not just its name.

subjects.name: Probability
subjects.description: Single and combined events, tree diagrams and conditional reasoning at the higher tier. Tree diagrams earn method marks generously, which makes them an efficient place to recover marks for a student short of time.

subjects.name: Statistics
subjects.description: Averages, spread, charts, cumulative frequency and histograms. Histogram questions involving frequency density are among the most consistently mishandled on either syllabus and are worth a session on their own.

subjects.name: Additional or Further Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken alongside the main syllabus by stronger candidates and genuinely useful preparation for A Level or Diploma mathematics. Worth considering for any student aiming at Higher Level Analysis and Approaches.

subjects.name: Physics and Chemistry
subjects.description: Listed here because they are where IGCSE maths weakness is first visible. Rearrangement failures and standard-form errors cost science marks, so maths work frequently shows up in a science grade before it shows up in a maths grade.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 against Pearson Edexcel 4MA1
paragraphs: These are the two syllabus codes an Al Khawaneej family is most likely to encounter, and the differences between them are structural rather than cosmetic. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 splits candidates into Core and Extended, each sitting its own pair of papers. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, code 4MA1, splits candidates into Foundation and Higher, each sitting two papers. The words are different, the paper numbering is different, and the arrangements around calculators are not identical.

Content overlap is substantial: number, algebra, geometry, mensuration, trigonometry, probability and statistics appear on both, with the higher tier on each syllabus extending into material the lower tier does not assess. What differs is the shape of the assessment and therefore the shape of effective practice. A student who has spent a term on past papers from the wrong code has practised real mathematics in the wrong format, which is a frustrating and invisible way to lose preparation time.

Both specifications are revised periodically, including the arrangements for calculator use, so the table below should be read alongside the board's own current syllabus document rather than instead of it. The instruction that matters is the simple one: get the code from the statement of entry, confirm the tier with the school, and then ask any prospective tutor which code they teach. A tutor who answers with a code is a different proposition from one who answers with reassurance about years of experience. Ask the school as well, since a centre occasionally changes board between year groups.

sections.heading: The tier decision, and the ceiling nobody mentions at the time
paragraphs: Whichever syllabus a school uses, the tier decision is the most consequential administrative fact of the two years. The lower tier assesses a defined subset of the content and caps the highest grade available. The higher tier assesses the full content with the full grade range accessible. These are not two difficulty settings on one exam; they are different papers, and preparing for one does not prepare a student for the other.

There are sound reasons to enter at the lower tier. A student who would be overwhelmed by the full content and score very little is better served by a tier they can succeed in, and a secure lower-tier grade is a real qualification that a collapsed higher-tier attempt is not. The problem is not the decision. The problem is that it is often made quietly, without the ceiling being explained, and then discovered when a sixth-form science requirement or a Diploma mathematics prerequisite turns out to sit above it.

Three questions, asked in writing, settle it. Which tier is my child entered for. What is the highest grade available at that tier under the grading scale in use. And what would have to change for the other tier to be appropriate. The third question is the useful one, because it converts a verdict into a plan: if the answer is that algebraic fluency and confidence with multi-step problems need to improve by a specific point in the year, that is a tutoring brief rather than a disappointment.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually are, topic by topic
paragraphs: Revision time is finite, particularly for an Al Khawaneej student who travels out of the community to school and has a short weekday evening. Spending it evenly across the syllabus is a mistake, because the topic areas are not equally weighted and the student's losses are not evenly spread. The table sets out where the recoverable marks usually sit, and the pattern is consistent enough across both syllabuses to plan from.

Two observations matter more than the table itself. Algebra is the decisive area on both syllabuses: it carries substantial marks directly, it is embedded inside questions labelled as other topics, and weakness there shows up in physics and chemistry papers too. Any student short of time should secure algebraic manipulation before anything else, because the return appears in several places at once.

The second observation is that number work, which looks trivial, is the largest source of avoidable loss. Students who understand a question perfectly and mishandle a percentage, a bound or a conversion lose marks that no amount of further teaching will recover, because the issue is reliability rather than knowledge. Those marks come back through short frequent practice rather than through explanation, which makes them well suited to the fifteen-minute slots an eastern-suburbs evening can actually accommodate. There is a third point, specific to this catchment. A student with ninety usable minutes on a weekday evening cannot work evenly across six topic areas, so the choice is not whether to prioritise but whether to do it deliberately. Working from a loss log built out of marked scripts turns that into a decision rather than a guess, and it is the one piece of preparation that makes a short evening productive.

sections.heading: Method marks: the marks given away in silence
paragraphs: Maths mark schemes award method as well as answers. A student who sets out the working, shows intermediate values and reaches a wrong final answer can score most of the available marks. A student who writes only the final answer, correct or not, scores either everything or nothing. Across a whole paper this difference is large, and it is entirely about how solutions are written rather than how well the mathematics is understood.

Three habits recover most of it. Write the working in a way somebody else could follow, which is also how a student catches their own slips. Keep intermediate values at full accuracy and round only at the end, because premature rounding puts a final answer outside the accepted range even when every step was right. And on geometry and vector questions, state the reason or the full description, since those marks are for the justification rather than the figure.

This is the part of maths tutoring with the best return and the least glamour. It does not involve learning anything new, which makes students resistant to spending sessions on it, and it recovers marks on questions they can already do, which is why it works. The practical version in a session is straightforward: the student writes a solution, the tutor marks it against the scheme exactly as written, and the student sees where the scheme awarded nothing for work that was in their head and not on the page.

sections.heading: Calculator and non-calculator work are two different skills
paragraphs: Where a syllabus assesses some work without a calculator, students need to prepare for that condition deliberately, and most do not. Practice almost always happens with a calculator within reach, because that is how homework is done, so the non-calculator condition arrives as an unfamiliar experience in the examination hall rather than a rehearsed one. Confirm which arrangement applies to your child's syllabus with the board's current documentation, since this has changed on at least one major specification.

Non-calculator work rewards a small set of specific skills: confident multiplication and division by hand, fraction arithmetic without converting to decimals, surd manipulation where the tier requires it, and estimation good enough to notice an implausible answer. None of these is difficult and all of them decay without use. Ten minutes of mental and written arithmetic twice a week through Year 10 removes an entire category of problem before Year 11 begins.

Calculator work has its own discipline, which students assume they already have. Entering a long expression in one go rather than in stages, using the memory functions rather than writing intermediate values down and retyping them, knowing the statistical functions well enough to use them under pressure, and keeping full accuracy in the machine while writing rounded values on the page. A specialist notices in a marked script which of these a student lacks; a generalist usually sees only a wrong answer. Both sets of habits are worth a session each and neither appears in most tutoring plans.

sections.heading: The past-paper procedure for maths specifically
paragraphs: Past papers in maths are frequently used as a scoring exercise, which wastes most of their value. The useful procedure has four steps after the paper is sat, and the paper itself is the least important part. Timed conditions first, with no notes and the correct paper for the right code and tier, because practising on the wrong tier's paper teaches the wrong pacing.

Then the student marks their own script against the published scheme, before anyone else looks at it. In maths this is especially instructive, because the student sees method marks awarded for working they nearly did not write down, and marks withheld for answers that were right but rounded early. That discovery changes behaviour in a way that being told cannot. The tutor's job is to audit the marking rather than the mathematics, which catches generous self-marking and misread schemes.

Then the loss log, by cause rather than by topic. Marks lost to premature rounding, to unstated geometry reasons, to arithmetic slips, to running out of time, to not writing working down. Causes transfer across every paper; topics only pay if they reappear. And finally, re-answer only the questions that were lost, immediately, while the correction is fresh. Practice material should come from the school and the boards' own published pages; IB Gram does not reproduce or distribute past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents or grade-boundary tables. Two papers handled properly in a fortnight is a reasonable rhythm for a student with a short evening.

sections.heading: The gap between IGCSE maths and what comes next
paragraphs: Whatever route a student takes at sixteen, the step up from IGCSE mathematics is the one families most consistently underestimate. A Level Mathematics assumes the higher tier's algebra as a starting point and moves quickly through material only briefly encountered at IGCSE. Diploma Analysis and Approaches assumes confident manipulation from the first term. Applications and Interpretation assumes comfort with technology and with interpreting data, which is a different but equally real assumption.

The specific gap is almost always algebraic fluency rather than content coverage. A student who can rearrange, factorise, handle indices and manipulate fractions algebraically without thinking about it will cope with either route. A student who can do all of those things slowly and with effort will spend the first year of the next course using their attention on the manipulation rather than on the new ideas, and will appear to be struggling with the new ideas as a result.

This matters for how the final IGCSE term is used. Once the papers are sat, there is a window before the next course begins, and it is the cheapest time in a student's school career to close an algebra gap. A short block of deliberate fluency work in that window, with no content to cover and no deadline pressure, repeatedly turns out to be worth more than a term of tutoring in the following year. Very few families use it, because the exams are over and the summer has started, which is exactly why it is available.

sections.heading: Starting, and how coverage is disclosed
paragraphs: Send three things and the first session does real work. The statement of entry showing the board, the syllabus code and the tier. The most recent marked maths paper with the teacher's annotations intact. And the realistic weekday time your child is genuinely able to work, which for a student travelling home across eastern Dubai is later than the end of the school day suggests.

Then a free trial lesson, one-to-one over live video. Ask the tutor to mark a page of your child's script against the published scheme and explain what the scheme awarded and withheld. That is the test of whether they know the syllabus as a marker rather than as a past candidate, and it is the distinction that decides whether method marks get recovered. A specific answer about rounding, unstated reasons or missing working is what you are listening for.

Coverage is held by syllabus code and tier rather than by the word maths, and that is how availability is reported to you. In some weeks no UAE-based specialist in your child's exact code holds a slot that fits an Al Khawaneej timetable. Where that is the case you will be told, and offered a specialist in the same code teaching over the same live video on Gulf Standard Time from elsewhere. A tutor for the other syllabus will not be presented as a match, because that is the failure this entire page is written to prevent.
