faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths syllabus is my child sitting?
faqs.answer: Check the statement of entry, the entry confirmation, or the front page of any past paper the school has issued. The two most common codes in this catchment are Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1. They differ in tier names, paper structure and calculator arrangements. If the paperwork is unclear, email the school's exams officer rather than the class teacher, and ask for the tier in the same message, because that answer matters just as much.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Core, Extended, Foundation and Higher?
faqs.answer: They are tier names from two different syllabuses. Cambridge 0580 uses Core and Extended; Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 uses Foundation and Higher. In both cases the lower tier assesses a defined subset of the content and caps the highest grade a candidate can be awarded, while the upper tier assesses the full content with the whole grade range available. The two tiers sit different papers, so practice must match the tier as well as the syllabus, and the entry becomes permanent once the series has been sat.

faqs.question: What are method marks and why do students lose them?
faqs.answer: Maths mark schemes award credit for working as well as for answers, so a student who sets out their method and reaches a wrong final answer can still score most of the marks on a question. Students lose them by writing only the final answer, by keeping intermediate steps in their head, and by rounding too early so that a correct method produces an answer outside the accepted range. Recovering method marks raises scores on questions the student already understands, which makes it the fastest available improvement.

faqs.question: Does my child need to practise without a calculator?
faqs.answer: Where the syllabus assesses any work under non-calculator conditions, yes, and deliberately. Homework is almost always done with a calculator to hand, so the non-calculator condition arrives in the examination hall as an unrehearsed experience. The skills it needs are specific: multiplication and division by hand, fraction arithmetic without decimals, surds where the tier requires them, and estimation good enough to spot an implausible answer. Confirm the current arrangement for your child's code against the board's own documentation.

faqs.question: Which maths topic should we fix first with limited time?
faqs.answer: Algebraic manipulation, on both syllabuses and at both tiers. It carries substantial marks directly, it sits inside questions labelled as other topics, and weakness there costs physics and chemistry marks as well. Context-free rearrangement practice, perhaps twenty minutes twice a week, produces returns in several subjects at once. Number reliability is the second priority, because errors there occur inside questions the student has understood and respond to short frequent drills rather than to further teaching.

faqs.question: How should my child use past papers in maths?
faqs.answer: Sit the correct tier's paper under timed conditions with no notes. Then mark it against the published scheme personally, before anyone else sees it, which is where the method-mark lesson lands. Have a tutor audit the marking rather than the mathematics, log the losses by cause rather than by topic, and re-answer only the questions that were lost while the correction is fresh. Four papers handled this way are worth more than twelve papers scored and filed away.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks on geometry questions they got right?
faqs.answer: Because geometric reasoning marks are awarded for the reason rather than for the figure. A correct angle with no stated justification scores less than the student expects, and the same applies to transformation questions, where the description must contain every defining detail rather than just the name of the transformation. The fix is mechanical: write the reason every time, even when it feels obvious, and have it marked strictly against the scheme until the habit is automatic.

faqs.question: Can a tutor who teaches 0580 prepare a 4MA1 candidate?
faqs.answer: On content, largely yes, since the two syllabuses cover similar mathematics. On the paper, with real caution. The tier names differ, the paper structures differ, the calculator arrangements are not identical and the pacing is therefore different. A tutor working from the wrong code will set practice in the wrong format, which is a frustrating and invisible way to lose preparation time. Ask which code they teach and treat a general answer about IGCSE experience as a no for this subject.

faqs.question: How big is the jump from IGCSE maths to A Level or IB maths?
faqs.answer: Larger than families expect, and the gap is algebraic fluency rather than content coverage. A Level Mathematics assumes the higher tier's algebra and moves quickly past it; Diploma Analysis and Approaches assumes confident manipulation from the first term. A student who can rearrange and factorise slowly will spend the next year using their attention on the manipulation rather than on the new ideas, and will look as though they are struggling with the ideas themselves.

faqs.question: When is the cheapest time to close an algebra gap?
faqs.answer: The window after the final IGCSE papers and before the next course begins. There is no content to cover, no deadline pressure, and the work is purely fluency, which is exactly the condition in which fluency work succeeds. A short block there repeatedly proves worth more than a term of tutoring in the following year. Almost no family uses it, because the exams are over and the summer has started, which is precisely why the window is available.

faqs.question: Is a Year 10 student too early for maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is the better year of the two. The problem at that stage is usually a foundation rather than a topic, and foundations take a term rather than a fortnight, which is time Year 10 has and Year 11 does not. A syllabus audit against the actual code, marking each statement as secure, shaky or unmet, takes two or three sessions and usually shows the gap is narrower than it feels. It also establishes the paper procedure before the pressure arrives.

faqs.question: Where should we get maths past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: From the school, which holds what it is entitled to use, and from the boards' own published pages. Files circulating in parent groups are frequently from the wrong code, the wrong tier or an outdated version of the specification, and an outdated syllabus is worse than none because it looks authoritative. IB Gram does not reproduce or distribute past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents or grade-boundary tables; sessions work from the official material the school provides.

faqs.question: Why does my child run out of time on the maths paper?
faqs.answer: Usually one of three causes, and they need different fixes. Spending too long on two difficult questions early, which needs a skip rule and a per-question clock. Doing arithmetic the long way where a shorter method exists, which needs technique rather than speed practice. Or writing nothing down and then having to redo work they lost track of, which is the same habit that costs method marks. Timed practice with the cause logged afterwards identifies which within two papers.

faqs.question: What should an Al Khawaneej family send before the first maths session?
faqs.answer: Three things. The statement of entry showing board, syllabus code and tier, because practice has to match all three. The most recent marked maths paper with the teacher's annotations left on, which tells a specialist whether the losses are content, method or reliability. And the measured weekday time your child is genuinely able to work, taken from a week of noting when the first page was actually open rather than estimated from the end of the school day.

intro.heading: In Al Mamzar the maths hour has to survive the end of the school day
paragraphs: Al Mamzar is a narrow strip at the top of the Deira peninsula - Corniche towers on the beach side, older villas inland towards Abu Hail, and the Sharjah boundary a few minutes north. Almost no family here sends a child to a school within walking distance. The buses run out to Al Garhoud, Al Qusais, Al Nahda and Mirdif, and they come back between the early and late afternoon depending on which route the child is on. That single fact decides more about whether tuition works than the tutor's qualifications do.

A Year 10 or Year 11 student in this neighbourhood typically gets home somewhere between 3.10pm and 4.05pm, is carrying homework in eight or nine IGCSE subjects, and has a maths paper to practise that nobody has told the household is tiered. The hour you book has to fall after the bag is down and before concentration has gone, and it has to survive a parent who may still be on Al Ittihad Road at 6pm. A tutor driving in from elsewhere in Dubai adds the worst part of that journey to the cost of the lesson.

IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in Al Mamzar or anywhere else in the UAE - visiting tutors are offered only in India. Lessons here run live, one-to-one, over video, with a shared whiteboard and the student's own past paper on screen. The practical gain is specific: the slot can be 3.45pm on a Tuesday and 6.30pm on a Thursday if that is what the bus timetable and a parent's commute actually allow, and nobody loses forty minutes to the Al Ittihad Road queue in either direction.

The academic half of the question is tiering, and it is the thing most Al Mamzar families discover late. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 is entered at Core or Extended; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 is entered at Foundation or Higher. The two tiers are different papers with different grade ranges, and a student prepared on the wrong one wastes months. Before booking anybody, ask the school's maths department for the syllabus code and the tier, in writing.

What follows is the detail that makes a maths hour in this neighbourhood productive: how the two boards structure their papers, what each tier can and cannot award, where Deira-schooled students drop marks, how the June and November series are counted backwards, and what Dubai tutors charge in AED. All of it is checkable with the school or against the board's own published syllabus, and a parent who reads nothing here but the tier table will already be asking the department a sharper question than most tutoring enquiries in this neighbourhood begin with.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The paired subject where weak maths costs marks that look like physics marks. Rearranging a formula, handling standard form and reading a gradient off a graph are all IGCSE maths skills being assessed under a physics heading.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations, concentration, percentage yield and empirical formulae are arithmetic problems in chemical clothing. A student who is insecure with ratio and proportion in maths will be insecure here, and the fix belongs in the maths hour.

subjects.description: Lighter on calculation, heavier on data interpretation: magnification, rate calculations, and reading experimental results off a table. Precision in units and significant figures is where the marks sit.

subjects.description: Percentage change, index numbers, break-even and simple ratio analysis. Students often meet the arithmetic as a surprise, having chosen the subject expecting written answers only. The numeracy transfers directly from maths work.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Binary and hexadecimal conversion, logic and algorithmic reasoning. The number-base work is the part students arrive at unprepared, and it is a short, teachable block rather than a long-running weakness.

subjects.description: Not a maths subject, but the one most likely to be competing for the same evening hour. Families planning a weekly maths slot in Year 11 should decide the whole week's shape at once rather than adding subjects one at a time.

sections.heading: The Al Mamzar weekday, and where the maths hour actually fits
paragraphs: The short answer: in Al Mamzar a workable IGCSE maths slot usually starts between 3.45pm and 4.30pm for a student on an early bus route, or between 6.15pm and 7.15pm in households where a parent is driving back through the Sharjah-bound traffic. Lessons are delivered live over video, so the slot is set by the child's day rather than by a tutor's route across Dubai.

The reason the window splits in two is the school spread. Al Mamzar has almost no secondary provision of its own, so children travel out in several directions. A student bussed to Al Qusais is often home before 3.30pm. A student at a school on the airport side, going through or around the Garhoud bottleneck, may not be back before 4pm. The same street can therefore have two households needing slots forty-five minutes apart, which is impossible to serve with a tutor driving between them and trivial to serve online.

The second constraint is the late-afternoon road. Al Ittihad Road towards Sharjah and the Al Nahda approaches fill from roughly 5pm, and a tutor coming in from Jumeirah or Business Bay in that window is quoting you for the journey as well as the hour. The market rate for in-home visits reflects it: Bestimate puts Dubai in-home tutoring at AED 180-350 an hour and independent home tutors at AED 200-500, against online bands starting far lower for comparable qualifications.

The third is simpler and more often ignored: a Year 11 student with nine subjects has a finite amount of evening. A maths hour placed at 8.30pm because that is when the tutor could come is an hour of tired practice. Placing it earlier, even on a day when the parent is not yet home, is the single cheapest improvement available to most Al Mamzar households, and online delivery is what makes it possible.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher: the entry that decides everything
paragraphs: Every IGCSE maths syllabus is tiered, and the tier caps the grade. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 is entered at Core or Extended. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, syllabus code 4MA1, is entered at Foundation or Higher. A student entered at the lower tier cannot be awarded the top grades no matter how well they perform, and a student entered at the higher tier can fall off the bottom of its range. The decision belongs to the school, but a parent is entitled to ask what it is and why.

Cambridge Core candidates sit papers leading to grades C to G; Extended candidates sit papers leading to A* to E. On the Pearson side, Foundation runs to grade 5 and Higher from 9 down to 3 with an allowed grade 2 below that. The practical consequence is blunt: a student who needs a grade 6 or better for a sixth-form maths course cannot get there on Cambridge Core or Pearson Foundation, and no amount of tuition changes that. If the tier looks wrong, that conversation needs to happen with the department in Year 10, not in the spring of Year 11.

Tier also changes what tuition should do. An Extended or Higher candidate needs depth and speed on the harder topics, with time spent on the question types that carry four or five marks each. A Core or Foundation candidate needs accuracy and completeness across the whole paper, because the marks are spread more evenly and leaving the last page blank costs proportionally more. Teaching one as if they were the other is the most common waste of money in this market.

Ask the school three things in writing: the syllabus code, the tier, and whether the entry is still reviewable. Then give all three to any tutor you are considering and see whether they can describe the paper structure back to you without looking it up. The current syllabus document on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com is the authority, and it is worth reading the two pages at the front of it yourself.

sections.heading: The calculator paper, and the one that is not
paragraphs: The clearest structural difference between the two main boards used by Deira schools is calculator access. Pearson's International GCSE Mathematics A permits a calculator in both papers. Cambridge 0580 does not: one of the two papers is sat without one. A student who has learned every method through a calculator screen and then meets a non-calculator paper loses marks on arithmetic they genuinely understand, which is the most frustrating kind of mark loss there is.

This has a direct consequence for how an Al Mamzar household should use its weekly hour. A Cambridge candidate needs deliberate non-calculator practice built in from Year 10 - long multiplication and division, fractions without decimals, percentages of awkward amounts, surds where the syllabus requires them, and estimation to check an answer is plausible. Fifteen minutes of it a week for a year beats a month of panic in the spring, because it is fluency rather than knowledge, and fluency only builds with repetition.

On the calculator paper, the opposite discipline applies. Students lose marks by trusting a display: typing a long expression in one go, misplacing a bracket, and writing down a number that is wrong by a factor of ten without noticing. The habit that saves those marks is writing the method down line by line before touching the keys, which also protects the method marks when the final answer is wrong. Most students have never been taught it explicitly.

For a Pearson candidate, calculator access in both papers is an advantage that gets squandered in a specific way: speed. With a calculator always available, students under-practise mental estimation and so lose the ability to spot an implausible answer. The fix is the same habit in reverse - a quick estimate written beside each answer, so a transposed digit announces itself before the paper is handed in.
bullets: Cambridge candidates: fifteen minutes of non-calculator arithmetic weekly, all year
Write the method in lines before touching the calculator keys
Estimate every calculator answer so a factor-of-ten error is visible
Learn the specific calculator model the school teaches, not a different one
Practise both papers of the entered tier, not only the one the student prefers

sections.heading: Where Deira-schooled IGCSE students lose maths marks
paragraphs: Across the Al Qusais and Al Nahda schools the pattern is consistent, and it is almost never the hardest topic on the syllabus. Marks go in four places, all of them trainable in a term.

First, algebraic manipulation. Expanding and factorising reliably, handling negative and fractional indices, and rearranging a formula where the subject appears twice. These are Year 9 skills, and when they are shaky every later topic takes longer and costs more. Second, ratio, proportion and percentage in multi-step word problems, where students get the arithmetic right and answer a slightly different question from the one asked. Reverse percentage - finding the original amount after an increase - is the single most reliably dropped question type in the whole syllabus.

Third, geometry reasoning. Circle theorems and angle chasing require a written reason for each step, and students who can see the answer lose the marks attached to saying why. Fourth, presentation under time: unlabelled diagrams, working crossed out and then needed, final answers not stated separately, and rounding to the wrong degree of accuracy. That last category can be worth a grade on its own in a paper where several questions ask for an answer to three significant figures.

A useful first session produces a written list specific to the student rather than a reteaching of last week's topic. If the list says indices, reverse percentages, circle-theorem reasons and rounding, then those four things drive every hour until they are gone. That is the difference between tuition that moves a grade and tuition that comfortably revisits what the school already covered.

sections.heading: The IGCSE maths year counted backwards from the June series
paragraphs: Cambridge runs IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, and UAE centres sit both; the February/March series is offered to India only and is irrelevant to a candidate in Dubai. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Every centre is allocated to one of six Cambridge administrative zones, and the board states plainly that using the wrong zone timetable is the candidate's risk - it cannot accept responsibility for a missed examination. The school's exams officer holds the correct version for your centre.

Counting backwards from the June window gives a workable plan. Around eight months out, the content should be on track and the tier settled. Five to six months out, mocks arrive and give the first honest read of paper technique. Three months out is the last comfortable point for closing a content gap. Eight weeks out, the work should be full papers under time with an error log, because at that distance the available marks are in technique rather than in new material. Two weeks out, nothing new should be introduced at all.

The November series is the resit route rather than a first sitting for most school candidates, and it is worth knowing the shape of it before results day rather than after. On the Pearson side, the November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results for a November series reach students in January - November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day. Always check the live timetable on the board's own site rather than relying on a restated date, since provisional timetables are revised.

For an Al Mamzar family the practical use of all this is deciding when to start. A Year 11 student beginning in January has about eight to twelve usable weeks before study leave, which is enough for technique and not enough for a missing topic. A Year 10 student starting in October has the whole arc, and pays less per grade for it.

sections.heading: What IGCSE maths tuition costs around Al Mamzar, and what the travel premium buys
paragraphs: Taking the cheapest end first: Tutopiya advertises online tuition from around AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65, both at the university-student level. That band is real and useful for homework support, and it is not where a Year 11 Extended candidate chasing a grade 7 should be looking. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour. TutorChase quotes around AED 270 for specialist work. Bestimate's Dubai research puts specialist exam-year support at AED 200-450 and above, and BartyED advertises AED 650 for a premium named tutor.

In-home visits sit apart from all of that. Bestimate puts them at AED 180-350 an hour and independent home tutors at AED 200-500, and monthly packages seen in the market run AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions against AED 799 for eight online sessions. Comparing those two packages honestly, the in-home arrangement delivers eight hours a month for roughly twice the price of eight online hours, and the difference is paying for a car in Deira traffic.

That is the whole case for online delivery in a neighbourhood like Al Mamzar, and it is why IB Gram offers no home visits anywhere in the UAE; visiting tutors are an India-only service. The money that would go to travel goes instead into matching a tutor who marks your child's specific tier, and into booking the hour when your child is actually able to use it.

Where the money is most often wasted: paying a specialist rate for homework supervision that a cheaper tutor could do; buying a long package before a diagnosis has established how many hours are needed; booking a second subject in the same hour; and starting in April. All four are avoidable, and all four are more expensive than they look. These figures are market rates from the sources named, read in October 2026, and not IB Gram's own price list.

sections.heading: Checking a tutor is permitted to teach, and three questions that settle the rest
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE requires a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any specific amount quoted to you should be treated as unverified. Applications go through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service.

Dubai's schools themselves are overseen by KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi has ADEK, Sharjah the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to training institutes with premises. IB Gram holds no such permit and claims no approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, Cambridge or Pearson. Treat any tutoring service that implies otherwise with scepticism.

Three questions then do most of the work. First: which syllabus code and tier have you taught to final examinations? A tutor who says "IGCSE maths" rather than "0580 Extended" or "4MA1 Higher" has not been asked often enough. Second: how will you mark a past paper, and will I see method marks separately from answer marks? Third: what is the plan for the non-calculator paper, if the student is on Cambridge?

One Al Mamzar-specific check is worth adding. Fix the hour in Gulf Standard Time in writing, and agree in advance what happens when a school event or a late commute kills it. A session that moves silently to 8.45pm because nobody set a rule is a session nobody learns anything in.

process.description: Mock dates and the school's teaching order set the plan. A Year 10 student gets content-alongside-school with non-calculator fluency built in; a Year 11 student gets technique from the mock onwards and full papers from eight weeks out.

whyPoints.description: Sessions are booked to the half hour after school transport actually reaches Al Mamzar, with later options for families driving back through the Sharjah-bound queue. Online delivery is what makes a 3.45pm Tuesday and a 6.30pm Thursday possible in the same week.

whyPoints.description: A 0580 Extended request goes to someone who marks 0580 Extended papers. Tier decides what the papers look like and what the grade ceiling is, so a tutor matched only on "maths" is being matched on the least informative part of the brief.

whyPoints.description: Past papers come back with method marks separated from answer marks, so a student can see that a correct answer scored two marks out of five. That distinction is where IGCSE grades actually move, and it is invisible in most homework help.

faqs.question: What time can an IGCSE maths session realistically start on an Al Mamzar school day?
faqs.answer: Two windows work in this neighbourhood. For a student on an early bus route from the Al Qusais side, anywhere between 3.45pm and 4.30pm is comfortable. For households where a parent drives back through the Sharjah-bound traffic, or where the child is at a school on the airport side, 6.15pm to 7.15pm is more realistic. Because lessons run live over video rather than depending on a tutor's journey, the two can coexist in the same week - one slot early, one later - which is not possible with a visiting tutor.

faqs.question: Is my child on Cambridge 0580 Core or Extended, and how do I find out?
faqs.answer: Ask the maths department directly, in writing, for the syllabus code and the tier. Most families assume they know and are wrong, because school reports rarely name it. The tier matters more than almost anything else you will discuss with a tutor: Cambridge Core leads to grades C to G and Extended to A* to E, so the entry sets the ceiling before any teaching happens. Ask at the same time whether the entry is still reviewable, which it usually is in Year 10 and rarely is late in Year 11.

faqs.question: Can a Core candidate still be awarded a top IGCSE maths grade?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge 0580 Core papers lead to grades C to G, and Pearson 4MA1 Foundation runs to grade 5. A student entered at the lower tier cannot be awarded the top grades however well they perform, which is why the entry decision deserves more attention than it usually gets. If your child needs a higher grade for a sixth-form course, the conversation to have is with the department about moving tier in Year 10, not with a tutor about extra hours in Year 11. A tutor can tell you honestly whether the move is realistic.

faqs.question: Our school teaches 0580 but my nephew sits 4MA1 - which maths syllabus is harder?
faqs.answer: Both are two-paper tiered syllabuses with each paper worth half the grade, and both are widely taught in Dubai. The difference that changes how a student prepares is calculator access: Pearson's International GCSE Mathematics A permits a calculator in both papers, while Cambridge 0580 sits one paper without one. Grade ranges differ too - Cambridge uses A* to G and Pearson the 9 to 1 scale. Question wording and layout differ enough that a student switching boards mid-course loses marks to unfamiliarity rather than to mathematics.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths paper allows a calculator?
faqs.answer: On Cambridge 0580, one of the two papers in each tier permits a calculator and the other does not, so a candidate must be fluent both ways. On Pearson 4MA1 a calculator is permitted in both papers. Check the current syllabus document on the board's own site, because paper structures are revised periodically and a tutor working from an older version will prepare the wrong thing. The practical rule for a Cambridge student is fifteen minutes of deliberate non-calculator arithmetic each week from Year 10 onwards.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the June series should IGCSE maths tutoring start?
faqs.answer: If the aim is technique rather than content, eight to twelve weeks of weekly work before study leave is enough to make a real difference, because at that distance the marks on offer are in paper discipline rather than new material. If there is a missing topic, start sooner: three months out is the last comfortable point to close a content gap without eating into revision. Starting in Year 10 rather than Year 11 is cheaper per grade, because fluency builds over months and cannot be compressed.

faqs.question: My daughter is in Year 10 at a school in Al Qusais. Is it too early for maths tuition?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is the most cost-effective year to do it. The content arrives at pace, a mis-set tier is still reviewable, and there is time for arithmetic fluency to build rather than be patched. A single weekly hour from October to the summer closes more ground than a double block in the spring of Year 11 and costs less in total. The work should run alongside the school's teaching order rather than ahead of it, so the student is consolidating what was taught that week rather than meeting it twice.

faqs.question: Does the evening traffic towards Sharjah affect our tutoring slot in Al Mamzar?
faqs.answer: It affects the slot rather than the lesson. Al Ittihad Road and the Al Nahda approaches fill from around 5pm, so households where a parent is driving back often cannot supervise a 5pm start. The usual answer here is a 6.15pm or later booking on those days and an earlier one on days when the child is home alone after an early bus. Because sessions run over live video, the tutor's own journey is not part of the equation, which removes the larger half of the problem.

faqs.question: How much do IGCSE maths tutors charge per hour around Deira?
faqs.answer: Dubai rates read in October 2026 band fairly clearly. Tutopiya advertises from around AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65 at the university-student end. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150. TutorChase quotes about AED 270 and Bestimate puts specialist exam-year work at AED 200-450 and above, with BartyED at AED 650 for a premium named tutor. In-home visits run AED 180-500 including travel. Those are market figures from the sources named, not IB Gram's prices; our own arrangement begins with a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Can my child resit IGCSE maths in November if the June result is disappointing?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a November series and Pearson runs November alongside May/June, so a re-entry is possible, and for many students it is the right call rather than a defeat. The sequence matters: results, then a decision with the school's exams officer about entry, then a plan with a realistic number of weeks in it. Pearson's November results reach students in January - the November 2025 series landed on 22 January 2026. Check entry deadlines with the exams officer early, because they sit well before the examination itself.

faqs.question: What does the 9 to 1 IGCSE grade scale mean against the older A* to G letters?
faqs.answer: Pearson's International GCSE uses numbers, where 9 is the highest and 1 the lowest, while Cambridge 0580 is reported in letters from A* to G. They are different reporting scales rather than different standards, and sixth forms in Dubai are used to reading both. What matters for a tutoring plan is the tier ceiling rather than the scale: Pearson Foundation runs to 5 and Higher from 9 down to 3 with an allowed 2, while Cambridge Core runs C to G and Extended A* to E. Ask the school which scale appears on your child's certificate.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE maths tutor who will come to our flat in Al Mamzar?
faqs.answer: Independent tutors who travel do exist in Dubai, and the market rate for them is AED 180-500 an hour including travel, with monthly in-home packages around AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour sessions. IB Gram does not offer that service anywhere in the UAE; visiting tutors are available only in India. Our lessons are live, one-to-one and over video, which keeps the budget in the match rather than in the journey and lets a tier specialist teach your child rather than whoever can reach your building by 5pm.

faqs.question: How many hours of maths tutoring a week is realistic alongside nine IGCSE subjects?
faqs.answer: One hour is the sensible default, and it is enough for most students through Year 10 and the first half of Year 11. Two shorter sessions on different days works better than two consecutive hours in the final term, because concentration after a full school day is finite. More than two hours a week in maths usually signals something else - a mis-set tier, a gap several years old, or hours being used as reassurance. A diagnosis should name the cause before extra hours are bought.

faqs.question: What should my child have ready for the first online IGCSE maths session?
faqs.answer: The syllabus code and tier, the most recent marked piece of work or mock paper, the calculator the school teaches on, and a pen and paper - the writing still happens on paper, with the camera on it. If a past paper has been attempted, send it beforehand so the tutor arrives knowing where the marks went rather than spending the first twenty minutes finding out. The session ends with a short written note to the parent naming what was covered and what has been set for the week.

intro.heading: The maths money most Al Manara families lose is not spent on tutoring
paragraphs: It is lost at entry. Tiered IGCSE mathematics caps the grade available at the lower tier: a student entered for Cambridge 0580 Core cannot reach the top grades however well they sit the paper, and the same logic applies to Pearson Mathematics A at Foundation. Families spend a year buying hours to lift a grade that the entry decision has already ceilinged, and nobody tells them, because the entry is a school matter and the tutoring is a separate transaction. That is the most expensive thing on this page and it costs nothing to check.

So begin there. Ask the school, in writing, which board and syllabus code your child is entered for and which tier. Cambridge Mathematics is 0580, with 0606 Additional Mathematics as the harder extra. Pearson Edexcel runs 4MA1 Mathematics A, tiered Foundation and Higher, plus 4MB1 Mathematics B as a single harder tier and 4PM1 Further Pure. Those are different qualifications with different papers and different calculator permissions, and the tier within them governs what is arithmetically reachable before any teaching happens.

With that settled, IGCSE mathematics is genuinely the best-value subject in the Dubai tutoring market, for a reason worth understanding. Most lost marks in it are technique rather than content: unshown working, premature rounding, a correct method abandoned because the student cannot rearrange under time pressure, a command word misread. Those are habits, and habits move faster than knowledge. A grade step in biology may need a term of content; a grade step in maths often needs six to ten well-aimed hours and homework between them.

The market prices, with the name attached to each. Tutopiya advertises from roughly AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65. A qualified subject tutor online is quoted around AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150. Named specialists run AED 200-450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270, Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table at 200-450+, with BartyED at AED 650. In-home one-to-one visits are quoted AED 180-350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 independently. Monthly, published packages run about AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

Al Manara's position shapes the in-home end of that range. The neighbourhood sits inland on Al Wasl Road and Umm Suqeim Street between two school clusters, so a tutor driving to a villa here comes from Al Barsha, Umm Suqeim or further through late-afternoon traffic. One hour of teaching takes about two and a half to deliver, and the quote reflects that honestly rather than greedily. IB Gram does not sell it: home visits are a service we run only in India, and for an Al Manara family lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.
What follows is the arithmetic - hours per grade step by topic, the tier cap in numbers, the five places the money goes missing, and what a resit actually costs if the first series goes wrong.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-manara.programmesIntro: An Al Manara maths enquiry sits somewhere in a British-curriculum sequence, and the spending logic changes at each stage. These are the four, with the honest value of an hour at each.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 mathematics
programmes.description: Negative numbers, fractions, indices, basic algebra and the habit of showing working. The IGCSE syllabuses assume all of it, which means a gap here is not a Year 9 problem - it is a Year 11 problem that has not arrived yet. Teaching at this stage sits at the lower end of the rate card and requires no syllabus specialism at all.
programmes.countryNote: The best-value maths purchase available to a Dubai family, and the one least often made. A Year 8 who cannot handle negatives reliably becomes the Year 11 whose physics and chemistry marks are also being eaten by rearrangement errors, and by then three subjects are being paid for instead of one.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE mathematics
programmes.description: Cambridge 0580, tiered Core and Extended, with two written papers per tier. Pearson 4MA1 Mathematics A, tiered Foundation and Higher, with two equally weighted papers and a calculator permitted throughout. Pearson 4MB1 Mathematics B is a single harder tier. Exams are sat as a June or November series for UAE candidates.
programmes.countryNote: This is the stage nearly all Al Manara enquiries concern, and the stage where the entry decision quietly governs the return on any tutoring spend. Confirm the code and tier in writing before buying hours, because the two facts together determine what is reachable.

programmes.name: Additional and Further Pure Mathematics
programmes.description: Cambridge 0606 and Pearson 4PM1, taken by stronger candidates alongside the main qualification and genuinely useful preparation for A Level or IB Higher Level mathematics. The algebraic demand jumps sharply, which makes performance here a reliable early signal of whether an advanced post-16 maths course is realistic.
programmes.countryNote: Worth paying for only where the post-16 destination needs it. For an Al Manara family whose child is heading for a non-mathematical pathway, hours spent on Additional Mathematics are hours taken from subjects that will decide the outcome.

programmes.name: A Level and IB Diploma mathematics
programmes.description: The two destinations from Al Manara's schools. A Level Mathematics assumes fluency the IGCSE only begins; the IB splits into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each at Higher and Standard Level, with an internally assessed exploration in all four.
programmes.countryNote: The financial reason to fix IGCSE maths properly rather than to grade-hunt. Specialist post-16 maths tuition in Dubai is quoted at AED 200-450 and above, so fluency built at IGCSE rates is fluency that does not have to be bought again at Higher Level rates.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-manara.subjectsIntro: IGCSE maths is best budgeted topic by topic, because the hours a grade step needs differ enormously between them. Below, what each topic costs in attention.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Rearrangement, expanding, factorising, indices and surds. The highest-return topic in the subject because every other topic depends on it, and because failures here show up as lost marks in physics and chemistry too. Usually a handful of hours of drilled practice under time rather than explanation.

subjects.name: Equations and inequalities
subjects.description: Linear, simultaneous and quadratic, with inequalities and number lines at the higher tiers. Marks go on solutions presented without checking, and on quadratics solved by formula when factorising was faster and less error-prone. Technique work, moves quickly.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.description: Transformations, domains, inverse and composite functions, and sketching. Students lose marks by sketching without key points labelled and by giving a domain they have not checked. A conceptually demanding topic that still responds to a defined number of hours.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled work at the lower tiers, then sine and cosine rules and non-right-angled triangles. The commonest loss is a calculator in the wrong angle mode, which costs whole questions and takes one session to eliminate permanently.

subjects.name: Geometry and circle theorems
subjects.description: Angle reasoning where marks are awarded for naming the theorem rather than for the number. Students who get the right answer with no reasoning shown lose most of the marks available, which makes this a cheap fix with a visible effect on a paper total.

subjects.name: Mensuration and similarity
subjects.description: Areas, volumes, arcs, sectors, and similar shapes with length, area and volume scale factors. Scale factors are the classic error - applying a length factor to an area - and it is a single misconception rather than a body of content.

subjects.name: Vectors
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, and geometric arguments using vector paths. Usually taught late and rushed, which is why it is overrepresented in dropped marks. A well-spent two sessions for a student aiming at the top grades.

subjects.name: Probability and statistics
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, conditional probability, averages from grouped data, cumulative frequency and histograms. The marks are procedural and sit close to the surface, which makes this one of the quickest topics to lift for a student currently guessing at it.

subjects.name: Number and ratio
subjects.description: Percentages, reverse percentages, compound interest, ratio and proportion, standard form, bounds. Heavily weighted at the lower tiers and routinely under-practised by students who consider it beneath them, which is where Core and Foundation grades are actually won.

subjects.name: Calculus, where the syllabus includes it
subjects.description: Differentiation and its applications where the route covers them. For most IGCSE candidates this is the smallest slice of the paper and the largest slice of the anxiety, which makes it a common place to overspend relative to the marks available.

subjects.name: Calculator technique
subjects.description: Pearson Mathematics A permits a calculator throughout, which changes the balance of skills against some Cambridge components. Memory use, mode discipline and sensible rounding are worth one session and recover marks across every topic on the paper.

subjects.name: Exam technique and timing
subjects.description: Allocating minutes by marks, decoding command words, showing working that earns method marks, and leaving nothing blank. Not a topic, and frequently the single highest-return thing in a six-hour block for a student who already knows the content.

sections.heading: What the tier cap costs, in numbers
paragraphs: This section exists because it is the largest sum on the page and almost no competitor page in this market mentions tiering at all. In tiered IGCSE mathematics the lower tier caps the maximum grade: a candidate entered for Cambridge 0580 Core cannot be awarded the top grades, and the same is true of Pearson Mathematics A at Foundation. The paper is pitched so that the ceiling is a feature of the entry, not of the performance.

So the first question is not how many hours a grade step takes but whether the grade you are aiming at is available. A family spending AED 800 a month for eight months to lift a Core candidate into the top band is spending money on an outcome the entry has excluded. Conversely a student entered for Extended or Higher who is not yet fluent enough faces questions pitched above their current level across a whole paper, and loses marks that no content teaching recovers - a different error with the same financial shape.

The decision belongs to the school and that is correct, because the school holds the data. But it is interrogable, and the window is Year 10 into early Year 11 rather than March. The question worth asking is: what does my child's current performance predict on each tier, and what specifically would have to change by the entry deadline for the higher tier to be the better bet? A school with a view will answer that; a school without one has told you something useful too.

Where a tutor genuinely earns their fee here is in the evidence rather than the opinion. A specialist reading a marked mock can separate marks lost to fixable technique from marks lost to the paper being pitched above the student's fluency, and that distinction is the whole decision. It takes one session, which makes it the cheapest consequential hour available in this subject.

sections.heading: Hours per grade step, by where the marks are going
paragraphs: Parents ask how many sessions it will take and are usually given a number designed to sound reassuring. The honest answer depends entirely on where the marks are being lost, and a marked paper tells you that in ten minutes. Three categories cover almost every IGCSE maths student, and they have very different price tags.

The first is technique on known content: working not shown so method marks are forfeited, premature rounding, calculator in the wrong mode, a command word misread, time mismanaged so the last questions are blank. This is the cheapest and fastest category. Six to ten hours with practice between sessions changes a paper total visibly, because the knowledge is already there and only the harvesting is broken.

The second is a specific topic gap - circle theorems never properly taught, vectors rushed at the end of Year 10, similarity scale factors misunderstood. These are bounded: two to four hours each, diagnosed and fixed, and they stay fixed. The third is fluency: the student cannot rearrange, cannot handle indices, loses the thread of multi-step algebra. That one is not a term's worth of content but it is not two hours either, and it is the category families most often misdiagnose as the first.

The table puts indicative hours against each so a budget can be built rather than guessed. Treat it as a planning range from a marked script, not a promise - every student starts somewhere different, and no specific grade outcome can be predicted by anybody. What can be said honestly is which category you are in and roughly what it takes.

sections.heading: The Dubai rate card, read against hours needed
paragraphs: Rates only mean something multiplied by hours, so here they are with the name attached to each figure, ready to be put against the table above. Tutopiya advertises from roughly AED 33-52 an hour. EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65. A qualified subject tutor working online is quoted around AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Named specialists are quoted AED 200-450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270, with Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table showing 200-450+ and BartyED publishing AED 650.

Now combine them. A technique problem needing six hours at a qualified-tutor rate is a one-off spend rather than a monthly commitment. A fluency problem needing twelve to fifteen hours at the same rate is a defined block over a term. Neither needs the AED 200-450 specialist band, because IGCSE mathematics is a widely taught syllabus and the premium at the top of this market is largely about scarcity in post-16 and IB work rather than about IGCSE content.

That is a genuine saving and worth saying plainly: for IGCSE maths specifically, the qualified subject tutor band is usually the right tier. Where specialism does add value is board knowledge - a teacher who knows whether your child sits 0580 or 4MA1, what the tiering caps, and how the papers differ - and that is a question rather than a price. A tutor at AED 180 who names the code is more useful than one at AED 400 who does not.

The in-home band is the exception to the whole argument. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors at up to AED 500, against AED 150-300 online. Published monthly packages run about AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits: half the contact days for roughly twice the outlay. For maths, where the work is annotated calculation both parties need to see, that premium buys a drive from Al Barsha rather than better teaching. Where supervision is the real need it is worth paying for, and plenty of Dubai providers deliver it - IB Gram does not, because home visits are a service we run only in India.

sections.heading: Five places IGCSE maths money goes missing in Dubai
paragraphs: First, buying hours before checking the tier. It bears repeating because it dwarfs the others. Confirm the board, the code and the tier in writing from the school, then decide what to buy. The check is free and the mistake is a year of fees.

Second, the past-paper mill. A tutor who works through paper after paper without marking them diagnostically is charging you to supervise something your child could do alone. Past papers are essential and they are only useful when someone reads the script and says why a mark was lost. If the session is mostly the student working in silence, you are paying AED 200 an hour for a study room.

Third, paying for content when the problem is arithmetic. The commonest pattern in Year 11 is a student who understands the topic and still drops marks because a sign flipped or a fraction went wrong under time pressure. Teaching the topic again does nothing. Rearrangement and number work under time does, and it is cheaper per hour than any specialist content teaching.

Fourth, group classes for a tiered, two-board subject. A centre class containing Core and Extended candidates on two different boards receives generic mathematics; nobody can teach to one student's tier and code in that room. It is cheaper per hour and often worth less per hour. Fifth, the in-home premium for a screen-friendly subject: AED 180-500 against AED 150-300, where the difference is a car in Al Wasl Road traffic rather than better mathematics.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson: what actually changes
paragraphs: A parent does not need to know the syllabuses, but does need to know that they are different, because a tutor's familiarity is board-specific in practice even when their mathematics is not. Across the entire researched area cluster for this market, exactly one syllabus code appears anywhere - yet the code is the qualification, and it is printed on your child's entry confirmation.

Cambridge Mathematics 0580 is tiered Core and Extended, with two written papers per tier and calculator permissions varying by component. Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A 4MA1 is tiered Foundation and Higher, with two equally weighted papers and a calculator permitted throughout - which shifts the balance of skills noticeably, since a candidate who leans on the calculator is less exposed on arithmetic and more exposed on method and interpretation. Pearson Mathematics B 4MB1 is a single harder tier with no lower safety net.

The practical consequence is that past-paper work has to be on the right board. A student preparing with the wrong board's papers is practising unfamiliar question styles and timing, which wastes the most valuable preparation tool in the subject. It happens more often than it should in Dubai, usually after a school move, and it is one of the easiest mistakes to catch early.

For the harder extras, Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics and Pearson 4PM1 Further Pure serve a similar purpose as preparation for A Level or IB Higher Level mathematics, and both involve a steep jump in algebraic demand. Always check the live syllabus document on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com rather than any summary, including this one, because boards revise content between cycles.

sections.heading: Counting backwards to the June or November series
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only and does not apply to a candidate in Dubai - which matters because a wrong exam window handed to a parent wrecks a real revision budget.

One Cambridge detail affects planning directly. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your child's exams officer which zone the centre sits in, in writing, before building a plan around any date.

For Pearson, International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so any plan should work from the live official timetable rather than from restated dates, including those here.

Counted backwards, the budget phases are clear: the tier and entry conversation first, then steady work or a diagnosed block, then the mock round as the last honest diagnostic, then timed papers in the final weeks, then results with a resit series available if needed. The table below adds the ownership column, because knowing who sets a deadline is most of meeting it.

sections.heading: If the first series goes wrong: resits and private entry
paragraphs: A resit is a real financial decision and one nobody plans for in advance. Both boards offer a second series each year, which means a disappointing June result can be addressed in November, and a disappointing November result in the following May or June. Entry fees are set by the board and the examination centre, not by a tutor, and they differ between centres, so the figure to work with comes from your child's school or from the centre you would enter through.

The first thing to do after a disappointing result is read the breakdown rather than the grade. Where the marks were lost tells you whether a resit is a sensible proposition: a candidate who was close and lost marks to timing and working across the paper is in a very different position from one who was a long way off across most topics. The second position may be better served by a different qualification route or a different tier, which is a conversation with the school rather than a tutoring purchase.

The resit window is short, which is the practical trap. Entries for the next series close weeks after results in some cases, so the decision has to be made quickly and the preparation block scoped immediately. For a close-miss candidate, a short diagnosed block on the specific question types that cost the marks is usually a better buy than a repeat of the whole year's teaching.

A note on private candidacy, which comes up in Dubai after mid-year moves and school changes. Private candidates enter through an examination centre rather than a school, and the board and the centre set what subjects and components are available - practical science arrangements in particular constrain what a private candidate can sit. Ask the centre directly, in writing, before building any plan around it, because a tutor cannot change those arrangements.

sections.heading: Checking the tutor costs nothing
paragraphs: Two free checks before any money moves. The permit first: private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals offering private tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted at you by anybody - including by a tutor explaining their rate.

MoHRE's own service page is "Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing", lists no fees, states a two-working-day completion time, and runs through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Since it is free and quick, a working tutor without one has chosen not to have one.

The second check is the arrangement itself. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat it as press-reported and verify against the current policy document, but decline the arrangement where your child's own maths teacher is paid privately, however helpfully it is offered.

And one claim to refuse outright, because it circulates widely in Dubai and sometimes carries a premium: no individual tutor in Dubai is KHDA-approved, because that status does not exist for individuals. KHDA regulates and inspects private schools and issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises in the emirate. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no premises in the UAE and claims no regulator or board accreditation. Paying extra for an approval that does not exist is the clearest overpayment in this market.

sections.heading: What a well-spent first block looks like
paragraphs: Concrete beats reassuring, so here is the shape of eight sessions that earn their fee for an Al Manara student. Session one is diagnosis and nothing else: the marked paper is read together, the lost marks are sorted into technique, topic gap and fluency, and the honest category is named. If a tutor proposes a plan before seeing marked work, that plan is guesswork however confident it sounds.

Sessions two to six address the named thing in order of yield. Technique first, because it is cheapest and shows fastest - working shown, minutes allocated by marks, calculator discipline. Then the diagnosed topic gaps, one at a time, each with practice set between sessions and marked at the next. Fluency work runs alongside rather than instead, as short drilled sections rather than whole lessons, because rearrangement improves with frequency rather than with duration.

Sessions seven and eight are full papers on the correct board, under time, marked and dissected with an error list kept. That error list is the deliverable: a page naming the specific mistakes this student makes, which the student can reread before the real paper. It is worth more than any number of completed past papers nobody analysed.

Then the block ends and a decision is made, which is the part that distinguishes a purchase from a subscription. Some students need a second block on different topics. Some need nothing further until the pre-series phase. Some turn out to be in a tier conversation rather than a tutoring one, and should be told so. The free trial lesson means the diagnostic session costs nothing, and no block is agreed until after it.

process.title: Get the board, code and tier in writing
process.description: Before any hours are bought, ask the school for the board, the four-character syllabus code and the tier. That is the free check that determines whether the grade you are aiming at is arithmetically available, and it is the single most valuable thing on this page.

process.title: Send the last marked paper
process.description: Not a description of the problem - the script, with whatever the teacher wrote on it. Marks lost to working, to timing, to a topic gap and to fluency look completely different on a page, and they carry completely different price tags. Ten minutes of gathering saves a session of discovery.

process.title: See who is proposed and what they ask for
process.description: You get a named tutor with the boards and codes they have taught. The signal worth watching is whether they ask for the code and the tier before proposing anything. A plan offered without those two facts has not been built from your child's situation.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson as the diagnosis
process.description: One lesson at no cost with the marked paper on screen, ending with the problem sorted into technique, topic gap or fluency, and an indicative number of hours. If the honest answer is that this is a tier conversation with the school rather than a tutoring purchase, you will be told.

process.title: Buy a defined block, not a subscription
process.description: A fixed number of sessions aimed at named topics, with practice set between them and a decision at the end. IGCSE maths rewards finite well-aimed blocks, and an open monthly commitment tends to drift into supervised past papers at a specialist rate.

process.title: Review against the school's next mark
process.description: Judge the spend on the next assessed paper or mock, on the same topics. If the mark moved, buy the next block. If it did not after a fair run, the diagnosis was wrong and should be revised rather than repeated at greater length.

whyPoints.title: The tier gets checked before the hours
whyPoints.description: Core and Foundation entries cap the grade available, and almost no page in this market mentions it. A diagnosis that starts with the entry decision can save an Al Manara family a year of fees aimed at an outcome the entry has already excluded.

whyPoints.title: You are told which tier of tutor you need
whyPoints.description: IGCSE mathematics is a widely taught syllabus and the qualified subject tutor band at AED 150-300 is usually the right tier. Where somebody says so rather than selling the AED 200-450 specialist band, the diagnosis came from marked work rather than from a sales conversation.

whyPoints.title: Hours are estimated from the marked script
whyPoints.description: Technique problems run two to five hours, topic gaps two to four each, fluency rebuilds eight to fifteen. Those are ranges from evidence rather than reassurance, and they let a parent build a budget instead of guessing at one.

whyPoints.title: Rates come with their publisher
whyPoints.description: Tutopiya, EdFlik, Unitors, TutorChase, Bestimate and BartyED each published a figure quoted here, and you can check them. Three of six researched competitor pages in this market publish no price at all and two quote in a currency UAE families do not use.

whyPoints.title: Board-correct past papers
whyPoints.description: Preparation happens on the board your child actually sits - 0580 or 4MA1 - because practising unfamiliar question styles and timing wastes the best tool in the subject. That is a free improvement and one of the easiest errors to catch after a school move.

whyPoints.title: No travel inside the rate
whyPoints.description: In-home maths tuition is quoted at AED 180-500 in Dubai because a drive from Al Barsha or Umm Suqeim is priced into the hour. Lessons here are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; home visits are a service we run only in India.

faqs.question: What is the most expensive mistake in buying IGCSE maths help in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Buying hours before checking the tier. Tiered IGCSE mathematics caps the grade at the lower tier: a Cambridge 0580 Core candidate cannot be awarded the top grades, and the same applies to Pearson Mathematics A at Foundation. Families spend months of fees aiming at a grade the entry has already excluded, because the entry is a school matter and the tutoring is a separate transaction so nobody joins them up. Ask the school in writing for the board, the syllabus code and the tier before buying anything. The check is free.

faqs.question: How many hours does a grade step in IGCSE maths actually take?
faqs.answer: It depends on where the marks are going, and a marked paper shows that in ten minutes. Technique problems - working not shown, timing, calculator mode, misread command words - typically run two to five hours, because the knowledge is there and only the harvesting is broken. A single diagnosed topic gap runs two to four hours. An algebraic fluency rebuild runs eight to fifteen. Whole-paper weakness is twenty hours or more, and at that point the tier conversation matters more than the hours. Nobody can promise a specific grade from any of it.

faqs.question: Do we need a specialist, or will a qualified subject tutor do for IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: For IGCSE mathematics the qualified subject tutor band is usually the right tier. The market prices it at around AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150, while named specialists at AED 200-450 and above command that premium largely for post-16 and IB work where the pool is smaller. What you do need is board knowledge: a tutor who knows whether your child sits 0580 or 4MA1, what the tier caps, and how the papers differ. A tutor at AED 180 who names the code beats one at AED 400 who does not.

faqs.question: Why does the same subject cost AED 50 at one provider and AED 500 at another?
faqs.answer: Because they are selling different things, and all the figures are real. Tutopiya advertises from roughly AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65, which buys somebody who was good at maths recently - genuinely useful for content. A qualified subject teacher is AED 150-300. Named specialists are AED 200-450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. In-home visits are AED 180-500 because a cross-city drive is priced into the hour. Match the tier to the diagnosis rather than to the anxiety.

faqs.question: Is paying for past-paper practice worth it?
faqs.answer: Only if somebody marks them diagnostically. Past papers are the best tool in this subject and they are worthless as supervised silence - if the session is mostly your child working while a tutor watches, you are paying AED 200 an hour for a study room. What earns the fee is a marked script and a conversation about why each mark went: method marks forfeited for unshown working, a command word misread, three minutes overspent on a two-mark question. The deliverable should be a written error list your child can reread before the real paper.

faqs.question: My child knows the topic and still drops marks. What do we buy?
faqs.answer: Arithmetic and rearrangement under time, not more content. The pattern is unmistakable on a marked script: the method is right, the concept is understood, and the question is abandoned two lines in or finished with a wrong value because a sign flipped. Re-teaching the topic achieves nothing, which is why families can buy a term of content revision and see the same marks. The fix is short drilled sections on rearrangement, indices, fractions and number work, run frequently rather than in long sessions, and it costs less per hour than specialist content teaching.

faqs.question: Does the board my child sits change how we should prepare?
faqs.answer: Yes, more than most families expect. Cambridge 0580 is tiered Core and Extended with calculator permissions varying by component. Pearson Mathematics A 4MA1 is tiered Foundation and Higher with two equally weighted papers and a calculator permitted throughout, which shifts the skill balance - a candidate leaning on the calculator is less exposed on arithmetic and more exposed on method and interpretation. Pearson Mathematics B 4MB1 is a single harder tier. Practising with the wrong board's past papers wastes the best preparation tool available, and it happens often after a school move.

faqs.question: Is a maths group class at an Al Quoz or Al Barsha centre good value?
faqs.answer: It is cheaper per hour and frequently worth less per hour for a tiered, two-board subject. A centre class containing Core and Extended candidates on Cambridge and Pearson syllabuses can only deliver generic mathematics, and nobody in that room can address one student's tier, code or command-term habits. For common content revision before mocks it can work. Note also that a centre with premises in Dubai operates under a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a different licence from an individual tutor's MoHRE permit, and it is reasonable to ask for the number.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor to an Al Manara villa?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and nobody is sent to a UAE address. For an Al Manara family lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing so the marked paper, the right board's past paper and the mark scheme are visible to both sides, and the annotated script stays with the student. For mathematics that is no compromise: the work is annotated calculation both parties need to see, and a shared screen does that as well as a shared table and costs no drive.

faqs.question: Why is in-home maths tuition quoted so much higher here?
faqs.answer: Because an hour of teaching takes about two and a half hours to deliver. Al Manara sits inland on Al Wasl Road between two school clusters, so a tutor is driving in from Al Barsha, Umm Suqeim or further through late-afternoon traffic, parking on a villa street, and reversing the journey. Bestimate's 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors up to AED 500, against AED 150-300 online. The premium is the price of a car, not of better mathematics - though for a younger or easily distracted student the supervision is worth paying for.

faqs.question: What does a resit cost if the June result is disappointing?
faqs.answer: Entry fees are set by the board and the examination centre rather than by any tutor, and they differ between centres, so the figure has to come from your child's school or the centre you would enter through. Both boards run two series a year, so a June result can be addressed in November and a November result in the following May or June. Read the mark breakdown before deciding: a close-miss candidate who lost marks to timing and working across the paper is in a very different position from one who was a long way off across most topics.

faqs.question: How quickly do we have to decide on a resit?
faqs.answer: Fast, which is the practical trap. Entry windows for the next series can close within weeks of results in some cases, and the entry is submitted by the school to the board rather than by you. So the sequence is: read the breakdown immediately, have the conversation with the school within days, and if a resit is entered, scope the preparation block at once. For a close-miss candidate a short diagnosed block on the specific question types that cost the marks is usually better value than repeating the whole year's teaching.

faqs.question: Which series will an Al Manara candidate be entered for?
faqs.answer: The June series or the November series. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only and does not apply to a candidate in Dubai. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. Plan from the live official timetable on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com rather than any restated dates, including these, because provisional timetables are revised.

faqs.question: We moved schools mid-course - can maths be entered through an exam centre instead?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and the arrangements are set by the board and the examination centre rather than by a tutor. Private candidates enter through a centre instead of a school, and what subjects and components are available depends on that centre - practical science arrangements in particular constrain what a private candidate can sit, though mathematics is usually less affected. Ask the centre directly and in writing before building any plan around it. This comes up in Dubai more than elsewhere because of mid-year school moves and changes of board.

faqs.question: What should a first block of eight sessions actually contain?
faqs.answer: Diagnosis, then yield, then measurement. Session one reads the marked paper and sorts the lost marks into technique, topic gap and fluency without teaching anything. Sessions two to six take the named problems in order of return: technique first because it shows fastest, then diagnosed topic gaps one at a time with practice set and marked, with short fluency drills running alongside. Sessions seven and eight are full papers on the correct board under time, dissected into a written error list. Then the block ends and a decision is made rather than rolling on.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-manara.closingHeading: Check the tier, read the script, then buy hours
dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-manara.closingBody: If you are pricing an IGCSE maths tutor in Al Manara, the sequence matters more than the rate. Get the board, the syllabus code and the tier from the school in writing, because that decides what grade is reachable. Then send the last marked paper so the lost marks can be sorted into technique, topic gap or fluency - three problems with three different price tags. You will get a named tutor who has taught that board, an honest view of how many hours it needs and at which rate tier, and a free trial lesson that functions as the diagnosis. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; home visits are a service we run only in India.
