Work is scoped from the series the student is entered for and the weeks genuinely remaining before it, rather than from an open-ended weekly commitment.

intro.heading: Two calendars, and only one of them negotiates
paragraphs: Every IGCSE mathematics plan runs against two schedules. The school's is the one families see: terms, mocks, revision clinics, reports. It bends. Teachers reschedule, clinics move, a mock gets pushed a week. The board's schedule does not bend at all, and it is the one that decides when your child sits the paper, when the entry had to be made, and when the result arrives.

That second calendar is almost absent from the local tutoring conversation. Entry deadlines sit months ahead of the examinations, so by the time a family decides in March that a subject needs a different tier or an additional entry, the window has closed. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates. Those are the only two windows, and each has an administrative tail behind it.

The results gap is the other piece families misjudge. Pearson's June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. So a November resit is not a quick repair if a school or university deadline falls in December - the result simply is not available. Knowing that in October changes the decision; discovering it in January does not.

There is a warning worth putting early on any page aimed at Gulf parents. The Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit June and November. A considerable amount of tutoring content written for this region quotes a February or March examination window and an autumn entry deadline that belongs to a different country, and a family who plans around it loses months. Cambridge's Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests do run in March, May and October, which is a separate thing and is part of why the confusion persists.

Reading your own position is harder in this district than it should be, for a mundane reason. Several schools around Al Mankhool and Bur Dubai split entries between boards by subject or by teaching group, so a student can be on Cambridge in mathematics and Pearson in a science, with two administrative timelines running in the same household. Parents who assume one set of dates covers everything find out otherwise at an inconvenient moment, and the entry statement is the document that settles it.

So what follows is a mathematics plan organised by distance from a series. The administrative timeline first, so nothing closes while you are deciding. Then a week-numbered run-in for the final ten weeks, because an open-ended weekly hour is the wrong instrument at that range. Then how to triage topics when the weeks are counted rather than assumed. Then what a resit genuinely costs in money and in weeks, and finally the mock-to-paper gap, which is where most of the recoverable marks in this subject are sitting.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-mankhool.subjectsIntro: In a counted run-in, topics stop being equal. Below are the IGCSE mathematics areas students around Al Mankhool most often need, ranked by how well each responds to a short, dated block of work.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Underpins everything and repays work at any distance from the series, because a gap here costs marks in topics that look unrelated. In a ten-week run-in it is the one area worth revisiting even when the student believes it is secure.

subjects.name: Number, ratio and percentages
subjects.description: Bounded, high-frequency and often neglected because it feels like earlier work. In a short run-in it is among the best value available: the questions are plentiful, the techniques are few, and accuracy improves quickly under timed practice.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.description: Responds well to a dated block provided the algebra underneath is sound. Where it is not, a block aimed at graphs becomes an algebra block within two sessions, and it is better to name that at the start than to discover it in week four.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Self-contained enough to be made reliable in three or four sessions, which makes it a sensible target late. Marks are lost on choosing the wrong relationship for the information given rather than on executing it.

subjects.name: Geometry and circle theorems
subjects.description: Highly drillable and frequently examined, with a small finite set of results to recognise. A late block here converts recognition into reliability, and students often gain more marks per session on this than on anything else.

subjects.name: Probability and statistics
subjects.description: Bounded and commonly left until last, so it is usually the highest-yield late target. Diagrams - tree, Venn, frequency - do most of the work, and students who draw them consistently stop losing marks they understood.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: A smaller topic that rewards a focused session or two. Worth including in a late plan precisely because it is small: a topic that can be finished inside the available weeks is worth more than one that cannot.

subjects.name: Mensuration and compound shapes
subjects.description: Mark-rich and mechanical, with losses coming from premature rounding and from unit slips rather than from method. Fixing the rounding discipline alone recovers marks across several other topics at the same time.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Calculus, logarithms and matrices at pace. Poorly suited to a short late block, because it assumes algebraic fluency and moves quickly. If this is the subject in trouble, the honest conversation is about the entry rather than about tuition.

subjects.name: Non-calculator accuracy
subjects.description: Not a topic but a skill, and the one most reliably ignored. Students practise everything with technology to hand and then sit a paper without it. Twenty minutes of timed written arithmetic a week, from early in the run-in, changes more than another topic.

sections.heading: The administrative timeline, which closes earlier than you think
paragraphs: The decisions that most affect an IGCSE mathematics grade are administrative and they are taken months before anyone revises. Which board. Which tier. Whether an additional entry such as Additional Mathematics 0606 is made. Whether a student sits as a school candidate or, in some circumstances, as a private candidate through an approved centre. Each of those has a window, and each window closes while the family is still thinking about the exam itself.

The entry fee question belongs here too. Where a student sits as a private candidate rather than through their own school, the entry is arranged through an approved examination centre and the fee is set by that centre rather than by the board. Those fees vary by centre and by subject, so the only honest instruction is to ask centres directly and get the figure in writing before the deadline. Nobody can quote you a single number for this in good faith.

Then there is the Cambridge zone point, which is administrative rather than academic and has caught out real candidates. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, the board states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and it says plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. A revision schedule built from a timetable found through a search engine rather than from the school's own entry statement has an avoidable failure in it.

The table below sets out the shape of the administrative year. The exact dates belong to your school and to the board's live timetable, which is what you should link and check rather than trusting a restated version.

sections.heading: The final ten weeks, with a job for each one
paragraphs: At ten weeks out an open-ended weekly hour is the wrong instrument. The student has a finite number of sessions left and an infinite amount of syllabus to feel anxious about, and without a dated plan the hour drifts to whatever topic was most recently frightening. A week-numbered plan removes that drift, and it also tells a family at week five whether the thing is working.

The shape that works is consistent. The early weeks go on triage and on the habits that pay across every topic: writing method, reading the command verb, and a pacing rule for how long a question gets before moving on. The middle weeks go on the two or three bounded topics identified as recoverable. The closing weeks go almost entirely on full timed papers and the audit of them, with repair work only where an audit names something specific.

Non-calculator accuracy runs throughout rather than appearing at the end. It is a separate skill from the mathematics, it decays without practice, and twenty minutes a week of timed written arithmetic from week one of the run-in produces a different student by week ten. Left to the final fortnight it cannot be built in time.

The table gives the shape. Adjust it to the weeks you actually have after term breaks, holidays and the school's own mock window are accounted for - which in the UAE academic year is usually fewer than the calendar suggests.

sections.heading: Triage: which topics to drill and which to leave
paragraphs: With the weeks counted, topics stop being equal and the decision becomes uncomfortable. Some topics the student nearly knows and could make reliable in three sessions. Some they have no grasp of and could not secure in the weeks available. Some are small enough to finish; some are large enough to swallow the whole run-in. Ranking by recoverable marks rather than by anxiety or syllabus order is the single most valuable judgement in a late plan.

The high-yield late targets in IGCSE mathematics are consistent across cohorts. Probability and statistics, because they are bounded and usually left until last. Circle theorems and geometry, because the set of results is finite and recognition converts to reliability quickly. Mensuration, because it is mechanical and mark-rich and the losses are rounding slips rather than method. Number, ratio and percentages, because the questions are plentiful and accuracy improves fast under timed practice.

The poor late targets are equally consistent. Anything that assumes algebraic fluency the student does not have, because the block becomes an algebra block under another name. Additional Mathematics 0606 at short notice, because it moves too quickly. And any topic the student has genuinely never understood, where three sessions produce partial recognition and no reliable marks. Deciding to leave a topic alone is a legitimate plan, and saying so out loud is part of an honest one.

Running alongside all of it are the habits, which pay in every topic simultaneously and are therefore the best use of a short run-in. Writing out method so partial credit is earned. Reading the command verb before answering. A pacing rule. Rounding discipline. These feel like administration to a student and they are worth more than any single topic at ten weeks out.

sections.heading: The resit decision, costed in weeks as well as dirhams
paragraphs: A subject that goes wrong in the June series is recoverable in November, and that is genuinely good news that families underuse. The decision has three components, and only one of them is money. The first is the entry: a second entry fee, set by the centre where the student sits as a private candidate rather than by the board, which is why the figure has to be confirmed in writing with the centre rather than estimated.

The second is weeks. A November resit means a block of work through the autumn, competing with the start of a post-sixteen course at a new school, which is the busiest possible term for the student. Realistically that is a shorter and more targeted block than the original run-in, and it should be: the student has sat the real paper, knows exactly what it felt like, and can usually name where the time went. That experience makes the block more efficient, not less.

The third is the result date, which is where decisions go wrong. Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. If a receiving school or a university deadline falls in December, a November resit does not meet it, however well the student does. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026 - so the summer series' result arrives in time for a September start and the autumn series' does not.

sections.heading: The gap between the mock and the paper
paragraphs: Between a mock and the real series sits the largest pool of recoverable marks in the subject, and most of it is left untouched. The mock produces a marked script under genuine time pressure - the only one the student will see before the real thing - and the standard response is to discuss the grade and file the paper.

Use it properly and the audit takes one session. Assign every lost mark to one of four causes: the content was not known, the method was not shown, the question was misread, or the time ran out. Then count them. In most IGCSE mathematics scripts the content category is not the largest, which is awkward because it is the one families have been buying sessions to address. Method, misreading and the clock between them usually account for more marks than any topic gap.

Each of those three has a specific repair. Method is a writing habit, installed by refusing to accept an answer without working for several weeks until it becomes automatic. Misreading is fixed by a mechanical routine: underline the command verb, state what is being asked before starting. The clock is fixed by a pacing rule and by practising abandoning a question and returning to it, which students find psychologically hard and which recovers more marks than almost anything else.

The scale of this is worth being concrete about. A student forfeiting two method marks per structured question across a paper is losing a substantial fraction of the total on work they had already done correctly in their head. That is not a knowledge problem and it is not fixed by teaching. It is fixed by a habit built over six to eight weeks, which is exactly the length of a well-planned run-in.

Misreading is fixed mechanically: underline the verb, restate the demand

sections.heading: What the weeks cost, and why the market firms up
paragraphs: Two cost effects run in the same direction as a series approaches. Specialist availability narrows, because every family in the city is looking in the same eight weeks. And rates across this market tend to firm up, for the ordinary reason that demand concentrates. A dated run-in booked in January is a different purchase from the same run-in sought in April, and the difference is not the quality of the teaching.

For reference, the published bands, each attributed to the provider that published it and read in October 2026. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts qualified online tuition at AED 150 to 300, in-home one-to-one including travel at AED 180 to 350, and specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level provision at AED 200 to 450 or more. TutorChase publishes AED 270 and BartyED AED 650. Home tutors are quoted up to AED 500 an hour including travel. None of those is an IB Gram price.

The right way to budget a run-in is by the block rather than by the hour, because the block is what is being bought. Ten weeks at one session a week is ten hours; the closing fortnight at two sessions a week adds two more. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to 600 for budget provision, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, and the exam-year band is the one that applies to a dated run-in. One Dubai provider publishes AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, which is near AED 100 an hour.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Sessions for Al Mankhool students run one-to-one over live video. In a counted run-in the format matters practically: session volume has to rise in the closing weeks, and an hour that can be moved inside the week is worth more than one tied to somebody's driving route on a specific evening.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and the periods that compete for the week
paragraphs: Two checks a parent can make without anybody's permission. First, the tutor's permit position: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, covering teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the smart app, website and e-services system with a two-working-day completion time. Because the permit costs nothing, no part of a quoted rate is a permit fee. Operating without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule is published, nobody should be quoting you an amount.

Second, the school's inspection report. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai and publishes reports on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. If mathematics attainment is named as a strength at your child's school, the school's own revision provision may cover part of what you were about to buy. Elsewhere in the country ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulates there, and the Ministry of Education supervises Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

A tutoring business with premises in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, no regulator accreditation and no UAE office, and does not describe itself as approved by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

Finally, the periods that compete with a run-in for timetable space. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA's requirements due from the start of the 2025-26 academic year or April 2026 where the year begins in April. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises at least twenty-five minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson. Those periods sit inside the school day, which is part of why the ten weeks a family counts on a calendar contain less study time than they appear to.

process.title: Get the entry statement and the series
process.description: Board, code, tier, candidate status and the series the student is entered for. That tells us which calendar applies, which papers to work from, and whether any administrative window is still open. It is one line from the school and it governs everything else.

process.title: Count the weeks that actually remain
process.description: Term breaks, public holidays, Ramadan, travel and the school's mock window all remove sessions. A notional ten-week run-in in the UAE academic year often delivers seven or eight, and the plan should be built for the real number rather than the calendar one.

process.title: Audit a marked paper before planning
process.description: One timed paper, marked against the official scheme, with every lost mark assigned to content, method, misreading or the clock, and the four counted. The triage list and the week-by-week plan both come out of that count rather than out of the syllabus.

process.title: Agree a job for every week
process.description: Each week of the run-in carries a named task written down at the start, with non-calculator accuracy running throughout. An open-ended weekly hour drifts to whatever topic frightened the student most recently, which is the opposite of triage.

process.title: Re-audit at the midpoint and adjust
process.description: A second timed paper around week seven, audited against the first. If the four-way split has not shifted, the plan or the match changes then rather than at week ten. In a dated run-in there is no time to discover a problem at the end.

whyPoints.title: Planned from the board's calendar, not just the school's
whyPoints.description: Entry deadlines, series windows and result dates are the inflexible part of an IGCSE year and the part local tutoring content most often gets wrong. We plan from them, name the February and March series as India-only, and link the live official timetable rather than restating dates.

whyPoints.title: A dated run-in, not an open-ended hour
whyPoints.description: At ten weeks out every week needs a job. We write them down at the start, raise paper volume toward the end, and keep non-calculator accuracy running throughout rather than leaving it to the final fortnight when it cannot be built.

whyPoints.title: Triage instead of coverage
whyPoints.description: With the weeks counted, topics stop being equal. We rank by recoverable marks - probability, circle theorems, mensuration, ratio - and will say plainly when a topic should be left alone because three sessions cannot make it reliable.

whyPoints.title: The mock script used, not filed
whyPoints.description: Every lost mark assigned to content, method, misreading or the clock, then counted. In most scripts content is not the largest category, and the plan that follows looks nothing like the one a family expected to buy.

whyPoints.title: Resits costed in weeks and result dates
whyPoints.description: A November sitting is a real option, with a second entry fee set by the centre and a result that, on Pearson's own precedent, reached students on 22 January 2026. If a December deadline is in play, we will tell you the resit does not meet it.

whyPoints.title: Figures attributed, nothing claimed we cannot show
whyPoints.description: Every dirham band belongs to the provider that published it with the month read. No regulator approval, no UAE office, no grade guarantees, no board papers or mark schemes supplied, and no statistic without a source.

faqs.question: Which exam series will my child in Al Mankhool actually sit?
faqs.answer: June and November. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only, so any revision schedule pointing a Dubai student at a February or March window is using the wrong country's calendar. Cambridge's Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests do run in March, May and October, which is a separate thing and part of why the confusion persists.

faqs.question: Why do entry deadlines matter if the exam is months away?
faqs.answer: Because the decisions that most affect the grade are administrative and they close first. Which board, which tier, whether an additional entry such as Additional Mathematics 0606 is made, and whether the student sits through the school or as a private candidate at an approved centre - each has a window that shuts while a family is still thinking about revision. By the time a parent concludes in the spring that the tier is wrong, the amendment is no longer available. Ask the school for the entry deadline in the autumn.

faqs.question: How should the final ten weeks before the papers be organised?
faqs.answer: With a job written down for each week rather than an open-ended hour. Early weeks go on triage and on the habits that pay in every topic: writing method, reading the command verb, and a pacing rule. Middle weeks make two or three bounded recoverable topics reliable. Closing weeks are full timed papers and the audit of them, with repair only where an audit names something. Non-calculator accuracy runs throughout, twenty minutes a week, because it cannot be built in the last fortnight.

faqs.question: Which topics are worth drilling when only a few weeks remain?
faqs.answer: The bounded, mark-rich ones that respond fast. Probability and statistics, because they are diagram-led and usually left until last. Circle theorems and geometry, because the set of results is finite and recognition converts quickly to reliability. Mensuration, because it is mechanical and the losses are rounding slips. Number, ratio and percentages, because accuracy improves rapidly under timed practice. What to avoid is anything assuming algebraic fluency the student lacks, because that block becomes an algebra block by week two under a different name.

faqs.question: Is it ever right to stop revising a topic altogether?
faqs.answer: Yes, and an honest plan says so. A topic the student has genuinely never understood will, in three sessions, produce partial recognition and no reliable marks, while the same three sessions on a bounded topic they nearly know produce marks that count. Ranking by recoverable marks rather than by anxiety is uncomfortable and it is the most valuable judgement in a late plan. The habits - method writing, command verbs, pacing, rounding discipline - should be protected in every case, because they pay across all topics at once.

faqs.question: What should we do with the mock paper once it comes home?
faqs.answer: Audit it rather than discuss the grade. Assign every lost mark to one of four causes - content not known, method not shown, question misread, time ran out - and count them. In most IGCSE mathematics scripts the content category is not the largest, and method, misreading and the clock together usually account for more marks than any topic gap. Each has a specific repair, and each is faster than teaching. Then build the week-by-week plan from that count rather than from the syllabus order.

faqs.question: How many marks is unwritten method actually costing?
faqs.answer: More than most families believe. A four-mark question typically awards two or three marks for a correct approach, so a student who works mentally, writes one line and makes an arithmetic slip scores nothing on work they had already done correctly. Across a full paper, two forfeited method marks per structured question adds up to a substantial fraction of the total. It is a habit rather than knowledge, installed by refusing to accept an answer without working for six to eight weeks - which is exactly the length of a well-planned run-in.

faqs.question: If June goes badly, is November a real option?
faqs.answer: Yes, with three things to settle. A second entry, with the fee set by the approved examination centre where the student sits as a private candidate rather than by the board, so confirm the figure in writing. A block of work through the autumn, which competes with the start of a new post-sixteen course and should be short and targeted. And the result date: Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so a November sitting does not meet a December deadline however well it goes.

faqs.question: Does a resit block need to be as long as the original preparation?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and it is more efficient. The student has sat the real paper, knows what it felt like, and can generally say where the time went and which questions they recognised and could not finish. That turns the block into targeted repair rather than general preparation. Scope it from the actual experience plus the triage list, confirm the entry with the centre before starting, and plan it around the new term's workload rather than pretending the autumn is free.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE exam entry cost for a private candidate in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The fee is set by the approved examination centre rather than by Cambridge or Pearson, so it varies by centre and by subject and no honest single figure can be published. Contact centres directly, ask for the per-subject fee in writing, and get it before the entry deadline rather than after. Where the student sits through their own school the entry is handled by the school, and the school's own fee arrangements apply. Either way, settle the number before the window closes, not while deciding whether to use it.

faqs.question: Why does Cambridge mention timetable zones, and does it affect us?
faqs.answer: It can, and it is worth two minutes of attention. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. A family in Al Mankhool should therefore take the dates from the school's entry statement and the board's live timetable rather than from a PDF found through a search engine, because a plan built on the wrong zone has an avoidable failure in it.

faqs.question: Does our ten-week plan really have ten weeks in it?
faqs.answer: Usually fewer. Term breaks, public holidays, Ramadan, family travel and the school's own mock window all remove sessions, and the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies periods sit inside the school day on a forty-minute lesson unit, so study time is tighter than the subject list suggests. Counting the genuinely available weeks on a calendar at the start takes five minutes and changes what should be promised. If the real answer is seven weeks, the run-in should be built for seven.

faqs.question: Is it more expensive to book a tutor close to the series?
faqs.answer: In two ways. Rates across this market tend to firm up as a series approaches, because every family in the city is looking in the same eight weeks. And genuine specialists on a specific code and tier become scarce at precisely that point, so the choice narrows as well as the price moving. A dated run-in booked in January is a different purchase from the same run-in sought in April, and the difference is not the quality of the teaching you receive.

faqs.question: What does a dated IGCSE maths run-in cost in this market?
faqs.answer: Budget by the block rather than the hour. Published Dubai rates run AED 33 to 65 at the budget end from Tutopiya and EdFlik, AED 150 upward from Unitors for IGCSE, AED 150 to 300 for qualified online tuition and AED 200 to 450 or more for specialist provision on Bestimate's Dubai table, with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650. Bestimate's monthly estimate for specialist exam-year support is AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more. All read October 2026, all the providers' own figures.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor to our building in Al Mankhool?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. In a counted run-in that is a practical advantage: session volume has to rise in the closing weeks, an hour that can move inside the week is worth more than one fixed to a driving route, and the pool becomes every specialist on your child's exact code and tier rather than the few prepared to travel here.

faqs.question: How soon will we know whether the run-in is working?
faqs.answer: Around week seven, because the measurement is built in. The student sits a second full timed paper and it is audited exactly as the first was: every lost mark assigned to content, method, misreading or the clock, then counted and compared. If the split has not shifted, the plan or the match is wrong and that is the moment to change it. In a dated run-in there is no room to discover a problem in the final fortnight, which is why the midpoint audit is not optional.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-mankhool.closingHeading: Find the dates, count the weeks, then plan
dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-mankhool.closingBody: Ask the school for the entry statement and the series your child is entered for, then look up the board's live timetable for that series rather than trusting any restated date. Count the weeks that genuinely remain once term breaks, holidays and the mock window are removed. Bring one marked paper to a free trial lesson with a specialist on the right code and tier, let the audit produce the triage list, and agree a job for every week before the first session. If a resit is on the table, settle the entry fee and the result date with the centre first. Sessions run one-to-one over live video.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-mizhar.tutorsIntro: These are mathematics specialists rather than general science-and-maths tutors. The test is simple: ask one what a question means when it says "give an exact answer", and the answer should arrive without hesitation and with an example attached.

intro.heading: Why extra practice has not moved the grade
paragraphs: A Year 11 in Al Mizhar sitting at 58 per cent on a Cambridge 0580 Extended Paper 4 is not short of mathematics. Look at the script and the pattern is almost always the same: the method is right, the answer is nearly right, and the marks have gone to rounding, to missing units, to an unlabelled graph, to a transformation described as a reflection without naming the mirror line, and to two questions left blank at the end because the first six took too long. None of that is fixed by another worksheet.

This is the gap a subject specialist closes and a generalist usually does not, because it requires knowing the mark scheme rather than the mathematics. A mark scheme awards method marks for working the examiner can follow and accuracy marks for an answer in the form the question asked for. A student who writes down the final number and erases the working loses marks they had already earned. Nobody tells them this in a class of twenty-six.

Al Mizhar sits north of Mirdif in the eastern suburbs, a low-density villa district with schools on its own edges and the Mirdif cluster a short run away. Students here attend British, Indian, American and IB schools within a few kilometres of each other, which means two children in neighbouring villas can be sitting Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 and revising from each other's past papers without realising the papers are different. That happens more often in this cluster than families expect.

So the first thing a tutor should establish is the code. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are both IGCSE mathematics. They tier differently, they structure the papers differently, and they reward slightly different things. Cambridge's current 0580 arrangement pairs a non-calculator paper with a calculator paper at each tier, which changed what revision has to cover; Pearson 4MA1 runs two papers with a calculator available on both, tiered Foundation and Higher. Confirm your child's own paper structure against the current syllabus document before building a plan on it.

There is a second reason the code matters in Al Mizhar specifically. The schools on this district's edges and in the Mirdif band next door do not share a board, so the study group your child revises with on a Thursday may be working from a different paper structure entirely. We have seen a Year 11 arrive with a folder of Higher-tier questions for a Cambridge Extended sitting, having done four weeks of conscientious work on the wrong archive. Nobody was careless; the papers simply look alike from the outside.

Everything below works outwards from the content. The topic list and where the supplement sits. The paper structures side by side. The mark-scheme conventions, written out as a checklist. How a past paper should be used, which is not the way most students use it. Then the market rates in AED, the permit position, and what a tutor may and may not do. Lessons are delivered as live one-to-one video; IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE, and home visiting is a service we run only in India.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-mizhar.programmesIntro: IGCSE mathematics sits inside a longer sequence, and the tier chosen at 16 decides what is available at 17. These are the stages either side of it for a student in this part of Dubai.

programmes.name: IGCSE Mathematics, Years 10-11
programmes.description: Two years covering number, algebra, coordinate geometry, geometry and mensuration, trigonometry, vectors and transformations, probability and statistics. Assessment is by terminal written papers with no coursework in the main syllabus. Cambridge tiers it Core and Extended; Pearson tiers it Foundation and Higher. The tier fixes the grade ceiling before the paper is sat.
programmes.countryNote: Schools around Al Mizhar and Mirdif make the tiering decision through the autumn term of Year 11, often on the strength of one mock. That is early, and it is reversible for a window afterwards, so a student who improves sharply in November has a case to make if somebody makes it in writing.

programmes.name: Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606
programmes.description: An extension course taken alongside 0580 by stronger mathematicians, covering functions, quadratics, surds and indices, logarithms, trigonometric identities, series, calculus including differentiation and integration, and kinematics. Effectively a bridge into AS Mathematics, and the point at which students who coasted through Extended first meet genuine difficulty.
programmes.countryNote: Not every school in the eastern suburbs offers it. Where it is available, taking it is the single clearest signal that a student is ready for AS Mathematics or Diploma Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and the calculus introduction removes most of the shock in Year 12.

programmes.name: Advanced Subsidiary Mathematics
programmes.description: Pure mathematics with mechanics or statistics, depending on the board and the school's choice of modules. The step up from IGCSE Extended is in the length of reasoning expected: questions build over several parts and partial credit depends on a clean argument rather than on a correct final figure.
programmes.countryNote: No school in this corridor will admit a Core or Foundation pass to AS Mathematics. That single fact is the strongest argument for fighting for the Extended or Higher tier in Year 10, and it is the one most often discovered in Year 12 when the option has already closed.

programmes.name: IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
programmes.description: The algebraic and proof-oriented Diploma maths route, available at Standard and Higher Level, with an exploration worth roughly a fifth of the grade. Assumes algebraic fluency from the outset, and at Higher Level moves into calculus and proof quickly enough that gaps from IGCSE do not survive the first term.
programmes.countryNote: The IB schools reachable from Al Mizhar include options in Mirdif and Nad Al Sheba. A student heading for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level should treat the Extended supplement content, and particularly the algebra and the differentiation, as foundation work rather than as the final topic of Year 11.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-mizhar.subjectsIntro: The topic areas below are where a maths tutor in this cluster spends almost all of their time, with the specific failure attached to each. Nothing here is a syllabus substitute; confirm the content list against your child's own syllabus document.

subjects.name: Number and accuracy
subjects.description: Standard form, bounds, percentages, ratio and reverse percentages. The recurring loss is rounding during the calculation rather than at the end, which makes a correct method produce an answer outside the accepted range.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging and algebraic fractions. Extended candidates lose most on sign errors in expansion and on cancelling terms that are added rather than multiplied, both of which respond to deliberate slow practice.

subjects.name: Equations and inequalities
subjects.description: Linear, simultaneous, quadratic by factorising and by formula, and simultaneous pairs where one equation is quadratic. Inequality notation is a steady source of lost accuracy marks because students answer with an equals sign.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.description: Function notation, composite and inverse functions, and sketching. Sketches are marked on intercepts, asymptotes and shape; an unlabelled curve that is geometrically perfect can still earn nothing.

subjects.name: Coordinate geometry
subjects.description: Gradient, midpoint, length, parallel and perpendicular lines, and the equation of a straight line. Perpendicular gradients are the commonest single error, and it is a two-minute fix that students keep repeating.

subjects.name: Mensuration
subjects.description: Area, surface area, volume, arcs and sectors, and similar shapes with area and volume scale factors. Units are the mark killer here: a volume answer in square centimetres loses the accuracy mark however good the method.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled trigonometry, then the sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle, bearings and three-dimensional problems at Extended. Bearings must be given as three figures, and the ambiguous case of the sine rule is routinely missed.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, and the four transformations. A transformation description needs the type plus the full defining information: mirror line, centre and angle, centre and scale factor, or translation vector. Partial descriptions score partially.

subjects.name: Probability
subjects.description: Single and combined events, tree diagrams, and conditional probability without replacement. Students round intermediate probabilities and then produce totals that cannot be right, which an examiner notices immediately.

subjects.name: Statistics
subjects.description: Averages from frequency tables, cumulative frequency, and histograms with unequal class widths at Extended. Frequency density is the single most reliably mishandled topic on the Extended paper and the easiest to repair in one session.

subjects.name: Differentiation
subjects.description: Gradient functions, tangents and normals, and stationary points with their nature. It arrives late in Year 11 at many schools and is often taught at speed, which is why it appears as blank space on mock papers.

subjects.name: Sequences and exponential change
subjects.description: Linear and quadratic sequences, nth terms, and exponential growth and decay. Quadratic nth terms are a small, learnable procedure that most students have never been shown systematically.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-mizhar.modesIntro: Maths support divides by what is actually broken: content that was never secure, or technique that loses marks on content the student knows. The formats below target those separately, because mixing them wastes the hour.

Algebra before functions, functions before differentiation. The order matters more than the pace, and a tutor who teaches topics in the order the textbook prints them is wasting a third of the block.

modes.description: For the student whose maths is sound and whose grade is not. The hour is spent on a marked script rather than on new content: why that answer scored one of three, what the mark scheme wanted, and what to write next time. Four of these shift more marks than a term of general tuition for this type of student.

sections.heading: Find the syllabus code before anything else
paragraphs: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 are both IGCSE mathematics, and in this cluster both are common. The syllabus code is printed on your child's statement of entry and on the front of every past paper. Until a tutor has it, any plan they make is a guess, and any revision guide you buy has a reasonable chance of being for the other board.

The differences are not cosmetic. Cambridge tiers the qualification Core and Extended, with a separate paper pair at each tier; Pearson tiers it Foundation and Higher. Cambridge's current 0580 arrangement pairs a non-calculator paper with a calculator paper at each tier, which changed what revision has to include. Pearson 4MA1 runs two papers of equal weight with a calculator available on both, which rewards a different kind of preparation entirely.

Cambridge also runs an administrative detail that matters to this household and almost nobody mentions. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series, and every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones. Cambridge's own exams officers' guide states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. A timetable downloaded from a search result is not a timetable.

Do this in ten minutes. Get the code, check the tier, download the current syllabus document from the board's own site, and check the paper structure against what your child believes it to be. A surprising number of Year 11 students are revising for a paper structure that changed before they started the course.

sections.heading: Core, Extended, and the supplement that decides Year 12
paragraphs: The tier is not a difficulty setting; it is a different content list and a different grade ceiling. The Core content is the shared foundation. The Extended content is that foundation plus a supplement, and the supplement is where a disproportionate share of the catch-up hours go, because it contains the topics that arrive latest and are taught fastest.

Look at what sits in the supplement and the consequence becomes obvious. Functions with composite and inverse notation. Histograms with unequal class widths and frequency density. The sine and cosine rules and three-dimensional trigonometry. Simultaneous equations where one equation is quadratic. Differentiation, tangents and stationary points. A student entered at Core has not met most of that, and a student entered at Extended has usually met differentiation in about three lessons in March.

The decision matters beyond the grade because of what comes next. No school in this corridor admits a Core or Foundation pass to AS Mathematics, and Diploma Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level assumes the Extended algebra from the first week. A tier chosen in Year 10 to protect a child from difficulty can close two subject options in Year 12, and the family usually finds out when the options form arrives.

The practical test takes an afternoon. One full past paper at each tier, marked properly. If the student is within a grade of a solid Extended pass, the tier is worth fighting for and eight to ten focused weeks is usually enough to settle it. If they are consistently below the Core ceiling, Extended will produce a worse outcome and the honest answer is to take the Core grade and build from there.

sections.heading: The mark-scheme conventions that quietly cost a grade
paragraphs: This is the section that matters most and the one almost no tutoring page writes. A mark scheme awards method marks for working an examiner can follow, and accuracy marks for an answer in the form the question asked for. Those are two separate things, and a student can earn the first and lose the second repeatedly without ever being told why.

Take rounding. Cambridge expects answers to three significant figures unless a question specifies otherwise, and expects full accuracy to be carried through the working. A student who rounds a trigonometric value to two decimal places in line three and then rounds again at the end produces a final answer outside the accepted range, having done the mathematics correctly. That is one of the most common two-mark losses on the Extended calculator paper and it is purely procedural.

Then the instruction words. "Show that" requires the stated result to appear at the end of the argument, not merely to be approached. "Give an exact answer" means surd or pi form, and a decimal scores nothing. "Give a reason" in a circle-theorem question wants the theorem named. A transformation description needs its full defining information. Bearings are given as three figures. Units belong on mensuration and on rate answers. None of this is mathematics, all of it is marks, and it is learnable in four sessions.

The last convention is the hardest to teach because it is a habit. Do not erase working. A crossed-out method that is correct still earns method marks; an erased one earns nothing and cannot be recovered. Students tidy their scripts out of neatness and hand in less evidence than they produced.

sections.heading: How to use a past paper, as opposed to how students use one
paragraphs: Most students do a past paper, check the answers, count the score and feel either relieved or bad. Nothing is learned in that cycle because the information is in the mark scheme, not in the answer, and they never open it.

The method that works is slower and produces far more. Sit the paper under timing, in one sitting, with the correct calculator or without one depending on the paper. Mark it against the official mark scheme rather than an answer list, awarding marks the way the scheme awards them. Then classify every lost mark into one of four types: content not known, method known but misapplied, convention error, or ran out of time. That classification is the whole point, and it takes longer than sitting the paper.

What the classification gives you is a plan. Content gaps go into teaching sessions. Misapplied methods go into targeted drills. Convention errors go onto a checklist the student reads before the next paper. Running out of time goes into pacing targets per section. Four different problems with four different fixes, where the raw score told you only that there was a problem.

Do this with two papers six to eight weeks apart and the comparison is genuinely informative. The score may move slowly while the error profile changes completely, and the changing error profile is the earlier signal. A convention error list that has shrunk from nine items to two is the thing that shows up in the real paper.

sections.heading: The non-calculator paper and why it changed revision
paragraphs: A paper sat without a calculator tests different things from one sat with it, and students who have spent two years with a calculator in their hand find out in the exam hall. Arithmetic with fractions, surds, standard form by hand, percentage work without a decimal shortcut, and estimation all become load-bearing rather than incidental.

The specific failure is not that students cannot do the arithmetic. It is that they are slow at it, and slowness on a timed paper costs the last two questions. A student who takes forty seconds over a fraction addition that should take ten has given away four minutes across a paper, and four minutes is a full question at the end where the marks are densest.

The fix is unglamorous and it works: short, frequent, timed arithmetic drills separate from the topic teaching. Ten minutes at the start of a session, every session, on fractions, indices, surds and mental percentage work. Over a term that becomes speed, and speed on the non-calculator paper converts directly into attempted questions.

There is a related habit worth building at the same time: estimation as a check. A student who can see in two seconds that an answer of 0.42 metres for the height of a building is wrong recovers a mark that would otherwise be lost silently. Estimation is on the syllabus, it is quick to teach, and it does double duty as an error trap on both papers.

Confirm which of your child's papers permits a calculator before planning any of this, because it differs by board and by syllabus version. If the structure includes a non-calculator paper, treat it as a separate skill with its own practice diet rather than as the same paper minus a tool.

sections.heading: What maths tutoring costs in Dubai, and what the travel premium buys
paragraphs: Begin with the premium rather than the base rate, because it is the part parents in this district can act on. In-home one-to-one in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to 350 an hour by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent home tutors. A qualified subject tutor working online is quoted from AED 150 by Unitors for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB. The gap between those two numbers is the travel premium, and it does not buy better mathematics. It buys a car journey through Al Khawaneej Road at the hour it is busiest.

Below that, the budget end is real and has its uses. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, both figures published by those providers and read in October 2026. For a Year 9 who needs homework supervision rather than mark-scheme coaching, that may be exactly the right spend. It will not fix a convention error list, because identifying one requires somebody who has marked to the scheme.

At the specialist end, the band across Bestimate and TutorChase runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and BartyED reaching AED 650 at the examiner end. Monthly packages circulating in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour home visits. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly hour are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support.

sections.heading: Is the tutor permitted to teach privately in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, which is why no amount appears here; an amount circulating online could not be verified against any official source. MoHRE's own service is listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, showing no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Two related points. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry, which is a different thing from an individual's permit. Separately, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

So the question to put to any provider is narrow. Does this individual hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit, and does my child attend the school where they teach? IB Gram holds no permit, licence, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none. The official channels are where any status claim should be checked.

sections.heading: Materials, honesty and what a maths tutor will not do
paragraphs: IGCSE mathematics carries no coursework in the main syllabus, which removes the sharpest academic-honesty question. The boundary still exists and it is worth stating, because families in this cluster often have a sibling on the Diploma where it bites hard. A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own work. A tutor does not produce assessed work, in any subject, at any level.

The materials question applies directly to maths. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson. We reference them and link to the official source; we do not reproduce or distribute them. There is a practical reason as well as a legal one: revision sites circulate superseded papers and outdated syllabus versions, and a student revising from a withdrawn paper structure is working hard in the wrong direction.

One provider ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. That is an academic-integrity breach and the malpractice consequence falls on the student rather than the seller. If any tutor offers to produce assessed work for your child, in maths or anything else, you have the only piece of information about them that you need.

What this leaves is the thing one-to-one is actually for. A student working a question on screen while somebody who knows the mark scheme watches the working appear and asks why line three was written that way. There is no document and no package that substitutes for it, and it is why four technique sessions can move more marks than a term of general tuition.

sections.heading: Starting, and what the first three sessions should produce
paragraphs: Send the syllabus code, the tier if it is set, the year group, and two evenings that work after the bus. We match a mathematics specialist to that code, you take a free trial lesson with your child's own current paper in front of them, and you decide afterwards. Nothing is booked before the trial.

The first three sessions should produce three specific things rather than a general feeling of progress. One marked diagnostic paper with every lost mark classified as content, method, convention or timing. A written convention checklist, in your child's own words, listing what they keep missing. And a topic order for the content gaps, in dependency order, so the sessions after that are not improvised.

If the specialist for a narrow requirement is not free in the slot you need, we say so and give you the options. Maths is a deep pool in this cluster, so this is rarely an issue at 0580 or 4MA1 level; Additional Mathematics 0606 on a tight weekday slot occasionally is. The options are to wait a week, to take a Saturday morning, or to start with a tutor at the level below and hand over with the session notes travelling.

Then set the measure before you need it. A second comparable paper six to eight weeks in, marked the same way, with the two error profiles side by side. That comparison is checkable and it belongs to you. What we will not supply is a predicted grade after three sessions, because nobody can produce one honestly and a reassuring number is not information.

faqs.question: My child practises constantly and the maths grade has not moved. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the lost marks are not where the practice is aimed. Look at a marked script and the pattern is usually method marks earned and accuracy marks lost: rounding during the working, missing units, a decimal where an exact answer was required, a transformation named without its defining information, and two questions left blank at the end. None of that is content, so more content practice cannot fix it. It needs a tutor working from the mark scheme rather than the answer, and it typically takes four sessions rather than a term.

faqs.question: Where is the maths syllabus code printed, and why does the board make a difference?
faqs.answer: It is printed on the statement of entry from the school, and on the front cover of any past paper the school has issued. Ask the exams officer or the subject teacher if you cannot find it. The reason it matters is that the two tier differently, structure the papers differently and treat calculator use differently, so revision guides and past papers from the wrong board look plausible and waste weeks. A school can also use different boards for different subjects in the same year group.

faqs.question: Does the non-calculator paper change how my child should revise?
faqs.answer: Substantially, where the structure includes one. Arithmetic with fractions, surds, indices, standard form and mental percentage work stops being incidental and becomes load-bearing. The failure is rarely inability; it is slowness, and slowness on a timed paper costs the final questions where the marks are densest. The fix is ten minutes of timed arithmetic drill at the start of every session, separate from topic teaching. Confirm which of your child's papers permits a calculator against the current syllabus document before planning around it.

faqs.question: Which Extended topics should we put the first sessions into?
faqs.answer: Usually the supplement topics that arrive latest and are taught fastest, because those are the ones that show up as blank space on a mock. In practice that means differentiation with tangents and stationary points, histograms with unequal class widths and frequency density, the sine and cosine rules with three-dimensional work, composite and inverse functions, and simultaneous equations where one equation is quadratic. Underneath all of them sits algebraic manipulation, so a student insecure on algebraic fractions should start there regardless of what the mock said.

faqs.question: What does three significant figures actually mean for my child's working?
faqs.answer: Cambridge expects answers to three significant figures unless a question specifies otherwise, and expects full accuracy to be carried through the working rather than rounded at each stage. A student who rounds a trigonometric value in line three and again at the end can do the mathematics perfectly and still produce an answer outside the accepted range. The habit to build is to keep the unrounded value on the calculator, use it, and round only the final figure. It is a two-mark saving on multi-step questions, repeated across a paper.

faqs.question: Why does the school's tier decision matter after Year 11 is over?
faqs.answer: Because no school in this corridor admits a Core or Foundation pass to AS Mathematics, and IB Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level assumes the Extended algebra from the first week. A tier chosen in Year 10 to shield a child from difficulty can quietly close two Year 12 options, and families usually discover it when the options form arrives. Ask the school in writing which tier is pencilled in and when it is fixed, then sit one marked paper at each tier before accepting the answer as final.

faqs.question: How should a past paper be marked at home?
faqs.answer: Against the official mark scheme from the board's own site, not an answer list, awarding marks the way the scheme awards them. Then classify every lost mark into one of four types: content not known, method known but misapplied, convention error, or ran out of time. That classification is the useful output. Content gaps become teaching sessions, misapplied methods become drills, convention errors become a checklist, and timing becomes pacing targets per section. The raw score on its own tells you only that something is wrong.

faqs.question: Can a tutor in Al Mizhar come to the villa for maths lessons?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run in India only. Lessons here are live one-to-one video with a shared screen and a graphics tablet, so the tutor sees your child's working appear line by line, which is what matters in mathematics. The published Dubai market rate for in-home visits is AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 independently, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor online, if you want to compare the two routes.

faqs.question: Should a strong Al Mizhar student add the 0606 extension course in Year 11?
faqs.answer: For a student heading towards AS Mathematics or Diploma Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, yes, because it introduces calculus, logarithms, trigonometric identities and series a year early and removes most of the Year 12 shock. It is also genuinely demanding, and a student who is working hard for a mid grade on 0580 Extended should not add it. Not every school in the eastern suburbs offers it. If yours does and your child is comfortably above the Extended pass, it is the clearest readiness signal available.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions a week does a Year 11 in this area need?
faqs.answer: One a week through autumn and winter while content gaps are being closed, rising to two in the final eight to ten weeks when the work becomes full timed papers. One session cannot both teach content and drill technique properly, so the phases should be separated rather than blended. Families in this cluster more often fail by booking three subjects at one session each than by under-booking maths, because the week cannot hold three and two get cancelled by November.

faqs.question: Which exam series will my child sit for IGCSE maths in the UAE?
faqs.answer: UAE candidates sit the June and November series. Cambridge runs IGCSE and O Level in those two series and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, stating in its exams officers' guide that using the correct zone timetable is essential and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November; its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Always use the board's live timetable.

faqs.question: When do results arrive and how quickly must a resit be decided?
faqs.answer: Timings differ by board and series. For Pearson, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. That gives a sense of the loop length from paper to certificate. The practical point is that a resit decision made within a fortnight of results leaves a workable run-up to the next sitting, while one made in September has already lost a third of it. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series.

faqs.question: Do private maths tutors in Dubai need a licence?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligibility covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific figure you read online as unverified. MoHRE's own service page is the authority on the current route.

faqs.question: What should the first three maths sessions actually produce?
faqs.answer: Three concrete things rather than a general sense of progress. One marked diagnostic paper with every lost mark classified as content, method, convention or timing. A written convention checklist in your child's own words, listing what they keep missing. And a topic order for the content gaps arranged in dependency order rather than textbook order. If after three sessions you have none of those, the tutoring is being improvised, and that is worth raising before another month goes by.

faqs.question: Can lessons move during Ramadan or the school's mock fortnight?
faqs.answer: Yes to both, and both are worth planning for. Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar, so it drifts across the UAE school year; sessions move to after Iftar and heavy timed-paper work shifts to either side of the month. During the school's own mock fortnight, pausing is often the right call because the student needs the evenings to revise. Holidays work the other way: a ninety-minute session at 10:00 with nothing before it is the most productive hour available.

faqs.question: How will I know it is working before the real paper?
faqs.answer: Two comparable past papers six to eight weeks apart, marked the same way against the official scheme, with the error classification from each set side by side. Watch the convention list rather than the score: a list that has shrunk from nine recurring errors to two will show up in the real paper even if the raw mark has moved only a little. We will not give you a predicted grade after three sessions, because no tutor can produce one honestly and a reassuring number is marketing rather than information.

intro.heading: Al Muteena, Deira and the next street over: one shortlist, not five
paragraphs: Al Muteena sits in the older, denser half of Dubai, a few minutes from Deira's main spine and within a short drive of Hor Al Anz, Al Mamzar, Al Nahda and Al Qusais. Families here rarely use only one neighbourhood. The flat is in Al Muteena, the school bus collects from Abu Baker Al Siddique Road, the grandparents live in Karama and the orthodontist is in Al Garhoud. When a parent searches for an IGCSE maths tutor in Al Muteena, the honest answer is that the useful shortlist is identical to the one a family two streets away in Hor Al Anz would build, and this page is written to prove that rather than pretend otherwise.

The reason is the syllabus. Almost every British-curriculum school serving this part of Dubai enters Year 11 for one of two mathematics specifications: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A, code 4MA1. Both split the grade across two written papers. Both tier students into a lower and an upper route with different grade ceilings. Neither cares where the candidate lives. A student losing marks on bounds and upper limits in Al Muteena is losing them for exactly the reason a student in Al Nahda is, and the fix is the same twenty minutes of work on the same question type.

What does change by neighbourhood is logistics, and that is where the in-home tutoring market in Old Dubai gets expensive. A tutor driving from Jumeirah to Al Muteena at five in the afternoon spends most of an hour on Al Ittihad Road before teaching anything, and that hour is priced into the rate. Market figures for in-home visits in Dubai run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, against roughly AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor teaching online. The gap is not a quality difference. It is a traffic difference, and it is the single clearest argument for the format IB Gram actually delivers.

IB Gram teaches UAE students one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard and the student's own paper on screen. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. That constraint turns out to be an advantage in Al Muteena specifically, because the pool stops being whoever is prepared to drive into Deira on a weekday evening and becomes whoever actually teaches the student's paper. A Year 11 on Extended 0580 who needs Paper 3 non-calculator drill gets someone who marks that paper, not the nearest available generalist.

This page compares Al Muteena with the neighbourhoods around it on the things that genuinely differ, then sets out the board-by-board detail that does not: paper structures, tier ceilings, where marks are lost, what the market charges by month rather than by hour, how the June and November series count backwards from results day, and what the Ministry of Education actually requires of an IGCSE transcript. Where a figure comes from a published source, the source is named so a parent can check it.
