dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-muteena.programmesIntro: Al Muteena students arrive at IGCSE mathematics from three directions: a British primary and lower secondary, an Indian-curriculum school switching board at Year 9, or an IB Middle Years Programme. The route changes what has to be rebuilt before Year 11 work makes sense.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 into IGCSE
programmes.description: The three years before the IGCSE course starts decide the tier a student is offered. Schools around Deira typically set mathematics from Year 7 and use Year 9 attainment to sort Core from Extended entries. Work here is about number fluency, negative indices, algebraic manipulation and the fraction and ratio arithmetic that Extended questions assume rather than teach.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools run a British academic year from late August to early July, so a Year 9 setting decision is usually made in the spring term. A student in Al Muteena who wants the Extended route should be visibly secure on algebraic fractions and rearranging formulae by February, because that is the evidence a head of maths uses.

programmes.name: IGCSE Mathematics, Years 10-11
programmes.description: Two years, two written papers, no coursework. Cambridge 0580 Extended is examined on a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper, each carrying half the grade. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator in both of its two-hour papers. The content overlap is large; the examination behaviour required is not, and that is what a specialist tutor works on.
programmes.countryNote: Most Al Muteena families will be entered through their own school as internal candidates, which means the school holds the entry and the tier decision. Private candidates in Dubai sit at an approved examination centre instead, and need to confirm their own entry deadline with that centre well before the series opens.

programmes.name: MYP Mathematics into IGCSE
programmes.description: Students transferring from an IB Middle Years Programme into a British-curriculum school meet a different assessment culture. MYP mathematics is marked against four criteria out of eight each, with investigation and real-life application weighted heavily. IGCSE replaces that with timed, method-marked written papers, so the transfer work is almost entirely about speed, layout and showing method.
programmes.countryNote: The Deira and Al Garhoud cluster contains both IB and British schools within a few kilometres of each other, so mid-year transfers between the two are common in this part of Dubai. A student moving across in Year 10 usually needs six to eight weeks of focused past-paper work before their mock reflects what they actually know.

programmes.name: Indian curriculum into IGCSE
programmes.description: Old Dubai has a dense Indian-curriculum school population, and families move to a British-curriculum school for Year 10 and 11 more often here than in newer districts. CBSE mathematics is strong on algebraic technique and weaker on the statistics, probability tree and transformation geometry content IGCSE examines, so those three topics usually need building from scratch.
programmes.countryNote: The academic calendars do not line up: an Indian-curriculum school year in Dubai commonly runs April to March, a British one late August to July. A student transferring in Al Muteena may lose or repeat a term, and the maths plan has to account for which topics the previous school had not yet taught.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-muteena.subjectsIntro: Mathematics is the request, but the specific topic matters more than the subject name. These are the areas Al Muteena and Deira students most often bring to a first session, with what each one is actually testing.

subjects.name: Number, bounds and limits of accuracy
subjects.description: Upper and lower bounds appear in almost every Extended paper and are among the most reliably dropped marks in the subject. The question is rarely hard arithmetic; it is deciding which bound to use in a division and giving the answer to an appropriate degree of accuracy. Half an hour of structured practice usually fixes a two-mark habit.

subjects.name: Algebraic fractions and rearranging
subjects.description: Adding algebraic fractions, simplifying by factorising and changing the subject of a formula where the subject appears twice. These are method-marked questions, so a correct answer with no visible working still loses marks. Tutors work on layout as much as on technique.

subjects.name: Quadratics: factorising, formula and completing the square
subjects.description: Three solution methods, and the paper usually signals which one it wants. Completing the square is also how turning points are found, which links this topic to sketching. Students who only know the formula lose the marks that ask for exact surd answers.

subjects.name: Trigonometry beyond right angles
subjects.description: The sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle using one half ab sine C, and three-dimensional problems where the hard part is drawing the correct right-angled triangle inside a solid. Bearings questions sit here too and are lost on diagram labelling rather than calculation.

subjects.name: Probability trees and conditional probability
subjects.description: Two-stage trees with and without replacement, and the without-replacement branch is where denominators change. Marks come from the tree being drawn and labelled, so a student who works mentally and writes one answer forfeits most of the question.

subjects.name: Statistics: histograms and cumulative frequency
subjects.description: Unequal class widths and frequency density separate grades here. Cumulative frequency work asks for medians, quartiles and interquartile range read from a curve, and the reading has to be accurate to the grid. This is a drawing skill as much as a statistical one.

subjects.name: Transformations and vectors
subjects.description: Describing a transformation fully, including centre and scale factor, and combining two into a single equivalent one. Column vectors, magnitude and vector geometry proofs follow on. Descriptions lose marks for being incomplete rather than wrong.

subjects.name: Functions, graphs and sketching
subjects.description: Function notation, composite and inverse functions, and sketching quadratics, cubics, reciprocals and exponentials with intercepts and asymptotes marked. Graph sketching questions reward a small number of correct labelled features, which is a technique a tutor can teach in two sessions.

subjects.name: Core-tier number and ratio
subjects.description: Percentage change, reverse percentages, compound interest, direct and inverse proportion and currency conversion. On the lower tier these carry a large share of the paper, and securing them is usually worth more than reaching for the hardest questions on the paper.

subjects.name: Non-calculator arithmetic for Paper 3
subjects.description: Cambridge's Extended non-calculator paper is the single clearest difference from Pearson's specification, where a calculator is allowed throughout. Long multiplication, surd manipulation, standard form by hand and fraction arithmetic all have to be reliable under time pressure, and that is trained, not taught.

sections.heading: Al Muteena against the next neighbourhood over: what actually differs
paragraphs: Searching for a tutor by neighbourhood assumes that neighbourhood changes the answer. In this cluster it changes four things, and none of them is the mathematics. It changes the drive time a visiting tutor would bill for, the time the school bus gets home and therefore the earliest realistic session, the regulator involved if the school sits over the Sharjah line, and the dominant curriculum of the nearest secondaries. Everything else, from the syllabus code to the grade boundaries, is shared.

That matters because the in-home market prices travel. An agency quoting a visit to Al Muteena at five in the afternoon is quoting for the Al Ittihad Road crawl as much as for the teaching. Published market rates for in-home one-to-one in Dubai sit at roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, and the Bestimate rate survey for Dubai puts the ordinary band at AED 180 to AED 350. Online one-to-one from a qualified subject tutor is quoted lower, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour. The difference is largely the car.

The table below sets the cluster out honestly. The feeder-school column is the reason the shortlist is shared; the session-start column is the only operational difference worth planning around. A family in Al Nahda cannot realistically start before 5.45pm on a weekday in term time, while an Al Muteena student attending a Deira school often can start at 4.30pm. That is a scheduling decision, not a tutoring one.

The practical conclusion for a parent comparing addresses: choose on the school and the schedule, and treat the maths plan as portable. A student who moves from Al Muteena to Al Qusais mid-year keeps the same tutor, the same specification and the same weekly slot, because nothing about the arrangement depends on where the furniture is.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are not interchangeable
paragraphs: The first question a tutor should ask an Al Muteena parent is which board the school enters. Nobody in the competitor set asks it, and it changes the preparation completely. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics carries the code 0580. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A carries the code 4MA1. Both appear on Year 11 timetables in this part of Dubai, sometimes within the same school for different sets.

The structural differences are concrete. Under the current 0580 syllabus the Extended route is assessed on a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper of equal weight, which means a Cambridge candidate has to be fluent in surd manipulation, standard form and fraction arithmetic by hand. Pearson's 4MA1 allows a calculator in both of its two-hour papers, which shifts the pressure from arithmetic to interpretation and to showing method for the method marks. A student who prepares for one board as though it were the other will find the paper harder than it is.

Tiering differs too. Cambridge splits 0580 into Core and Extended with different grade ranges and separate question papers. Pearson splits 4MA1 into Foundation and Higher tier with an overlap grade. Because the tier caps the grade, the entry decision made by the head of mathematics in the spring term is more consequential than any number of tutoring hours. A tutor's first job is often to help a family understand what tier their child is on and whether the evidence supports moving.

Syllabus versions change, so the only safe instruction is to confirm the code and the version on the school's own examination entry letter, then check the paper structure against the board's published specification before building a revision plan around it.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE maths marks are actually lost
paragraphs: Mark loss in IGCSE mathematics is not spread evenly and it is not usually about missing knowledge. Reading through marked mock papers from this cluster, the same small set of behaviours accounts for most of the gap between a student's apparent ability and their grade. The useful consequence is that a tutor can name them in a first session and work on them specifically, instead of reteaching a two-year course.

The first is working not shown. Both boards award method marks, and a correct answer with no visible method scores less than an incorrect answer with correct method. Students who have been praised for mental arithmetic are the most exposed to this. The second is rounding at the wrong point: rounding mid-calculation and carrying the rounded value forward turns a correct method into a wrong answer. The third is incomplete descriptions, which is why transformation questions bleed marks even when the student can see exactly what has happened to the shape.

The fourth is time allocation. A two-hour paper rewards finishing, and a student who spends twenty minutes on a four-mark question has already lost more than that question is worth. Timed sections, marked honestly against the official mark scheme, is the only reliable way to train this. The fifth is equipment discipline: a protractor and a pair of compasses are required for construction and locus questions, and a surprising number of candidates arrive without them.

None of this is exotic, which is the point. A diagnostic built on the student's own last two mock papers finds their personal version of this list within one session, and the first month of tutoring is then spent on four named habits rather than on a syllabus sweep.

sections.heading: What maths tuition costs around Al Muteena, by the month
paragraphs: Parents budget monthly, not hourly, so this section starts there. One sixty-minute session a week for a month is four sessions. At the lower online band that is a monthly figure in the low hundreds of dirhams; at specialist exam-year rates it reaches four figures. The Bestimate rate survey for Dubai estimates monthly spend on a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240 to AED 600 for budget tutoring, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle band, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are market figures, published by a third party, not an IB Gram price list.

Reading the market from the cheapest end upwards is instructive. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 an hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to AED 52, which buys a university student or a general tutor rather than a subject specialist. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist work. BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. The spread across that list is more than fifteenfold for something all five describe as one-to-one tuition, which tells a parent that the label carries almost no information.

The in-home premium is the part worth isolating, because it is the only cost that buys no teaching. Published in-home rates in Dubai run from about AED 180 to AED 500 an hour against about AED 150 to AED 300 online for a comparable subject tutor. A family paying the difference across a two-year IGCSE course is paying a substantial sum for a car journey into Deira. Set against the KHDA confirmation on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, tutoring is now the fastest-moving line in a Dubai education budget.

IB Gram's own position is deliberately not a published hourly table on this page. The model is a free trial lesson first, then a plan built from what the trial shows, because an Extended candidate eight weeks from a paper and a Year 10 repairing algebra need different numbers of hours. Any figure above should be read as the market, with its source named, and checked against the provider's current page before a parent relies on it.

sections.heading: Online or a tutor on the doorstep in Deira: the comparison in full
paragraphs: A parent in Al Muteena asking for a home tutor is asking a reasonable question, and it deserves a straight answer before any pitch. In-home tutoring in this part of Dubai does exist, it is delivered by independent tutors and by agencies, and it costs more per hour than online for the reasons set out above. What it buys is a person in the room, which some students genuinely need, particularly younger ones and those who will not stay on task without physical presence.

What it costs, beyond money, is the tutor pool. Al Muteena's realistic catchment for a visiting tutor is whoever will drive into Deira on a weekday evening and get home afterwards. That is a small group, and it is selected for willingness to travel rather than for teaching Cambridge 0580 Extended non-calculator technique. Online removes the constraint entirely, and the selection becomes the specification the student is actually sitting.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE. Lessons for Al Muteena families are taught one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own paper shared on screen and a whiteboard both sides can write on. Home visits are offered only in India. Stating that plainly is better than implying otherwise and disappointing a family after they have paid, which is what two of the pages ranking for this query do by routing UAE parents to a non-UAE phone number.

sections.heading: The June and November series, counted backwards
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, and both are available to UAE candidates. The February/March series is offered to India only, so it is not a route an Al Muteena student can use. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year. Those four windows are the entire calendar a Dubai IGCSE family needs to plan around.

Counting backwards from results is the useful direction. For Pearson, the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November results reach students in the following January; November 2025 results landed with students on 22 January 2026. June results come far sooner after the papers: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. Those are published dates with a source, which is why they keep their year here.

Working back from that, entry deadlines sit months before the papers, because a centre has to declare candidates, tiers and options before timetables are finalised. A family that wants to change tier, add a subject or enter as a private candidate has to act in the term before the series, not in the weeks before the exam. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the correct zone timetable must be used, stating that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong version.

sections.heading: What the Ministry of Education asks of an IGCSE transcript
paragraphs: Equivalency is the step most Dubai tutoring pages skip, and it is the one with the clearest rules. For students on a British track, the UAE Ministry of Education requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects.

That detail matters when a family is choosing a tier. A Core or Foundation entry has a lower grade ceiling, but the equivalency floor is grade E or grade 3, which a well-prepared Core candidate can clear. The risk is different: a university course with a mathematics prerequisite may ask for a higher grade than equivalency does, and a Core entry can close that door before the student has chosen a subject. The tier conversation should therefore involve both the school and the intended destination, not just the current mark.

One page ranking for these queries states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. The sourced figure is five, excluding Arabic and Islamic education. Getting that right is worth more to a parent than any amount of reassurance, and it is checkable against the public reporting of the Ministry's clarification.

IB Gram does not perform or guarantee equivalency or attestation, and no page here should suggest that tutoring is required for it. The process belongs to the Ministry of Education and the emirate's attestation channel, and a family should verify current requirements on moe.gov.ae before making a subject decision that depends on them.

sections.heading: Is your tutor permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated, which is a sentence very few pages in this market write. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no figure should be quoted, and anyone quoting one to an Al Muteena parent is inventing it. The official application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Two further points apply to Dubai specifically. A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal matter from an individual tutor, and requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no centre in Dubai and should never be described as KHDA approved. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars the same arrangement, so a family should not try to engage their child's own class teacher privately.

The practical advice for a parent is short. Ask the tutor directly whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition permit. Ask which board and which syllabus code they teach. Ask what happens if the match does not work. A tutor who answers all three clearly is a safer choice than one with a longer list of adjectives.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the IGCSE timetable
paragraphs: A Year 11 in Al Muteena is not only sitting IGCSEs. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 the equivalent date for schools whose year begins in April. That is timetable pressure on a mathematics revision plan, and it is almost entirely absent from the tutoring pages in this market.

The rules are specific. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, and Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, while non-Arab students follow the school's licensed-curriculum language in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

Schools must also ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, and mandatory-subject instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with schools permitted to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met and advised to keep any mandatory subject lesson to at least 25 minutes. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited.

What this means for a maths tutoring plan is practical. The mandatory subjects occupy real weekly hours that cannot be moved, so the realistic window for independent mathematics practice in an Al Muteena household is the weekend and two weekday evenings. Planning for that honestly produces a schedule a family keeps, which is worth more than an ambitious one they abandon in week three.

sections.heading: Starting from Al Muteena, including what happens if nobody is free
paragraphs: The first step is a conversation, not a payment. A parent sends the year group, the school, the board and syllabus code from the entry letter, the current working grade, the last two mock papers if they exist, and two or three weekday windows that work once the bus is back. That is enough to decide whether the problem is content, technique or timing, and those three need different tutors.

A free trial lesson follows, taught by the tutor proposed for the ongoing slot rather than by a demonstrator. The trial has a specific job: to produce a short written diagnosis of where the marks are going and what the first month should attack. A family that reads that and decides not to continue has still gained something useful, which is the only fair way to run a trial.

On availability, the honest position matters more than the reassuring one. Mathematics at IGCSE is the best-covered request in this set, so a match for 0580 or 4MA1 is usually straightforward within a few days. A narrow request - Extended non-calculator technique in a 7am slot before school, for instance - can take longer, and the right answer is to say so and offer a realistic date rather than to fill the slot with whoever is free. If no suitable specialist is available for a student's board and tier, IB Gram says that rather than substituting someone who teaches a different specification.

Progress reporting is deliberately plain: what was covered, what was practised, what the mark-scheme evidence shows and what changes next week. No scores are invented and no outcome is promised. A tutor can change how a student handles a non-calculator paper; nobody can promise a grade, and any provider offering one to an Al Muteena parent is selling something they cannot deliver.

process.title: Send the entry letter details
process.description: Year group, school, board and syllabus code, tier, current working grade and two or three weekday windows that work after the Deira school run. The syllabus code is the single most useful line, because it decides whether non-calculator drill is part of the plan at all.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: Taught by the tutor proposed for the weekly slot, using the student's own mock paper. The output is a short written diagnosis naming where marks are being lost and what the first four sessions should cover. No payment is required to reach this point.

process.title: Agree the plan and the slot
process.description: Sixty or ninety minutes, once or twice a week, held for the term so the family can plan around it. Longer sessions suit full-paper work; shorter ones suit topic repair. The plan names three question types to attack first rather than promising a grade.

process.title: Work through marked papers weekly
process.description: Timed sections marked against the official mark scheme, with the student's own errors as the agenda. Each session ends with a short practice set and a written note of what to bring back, so the next session starts from evidence rather than memory.

process.title: Review before the series
process.description: Six to eight weeks before the June or November papers, the plan shifts from content to examination behaviour: timing, method presentation, accuracy instructions and equipment. If a tier or entry decision is still open, it is raised with the family in time to act on it.

whyPoints.title: The board is identified before the teaching starts
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 differ on calculator use, paper length and tiering. A tutor who does not know which one a student sits is guessing at the preparation. The first question here is always the syllabus code on the school's entry letter.

whyPoints.title: Al Muteena's tutor pool stops being a driving radius
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means the shortlist is built from people who teach the student's specification and tier, not from people willing to drive into Deira at five in the afternoon. For a narrow request like Extended non-calculator technique, that is the whole difference.

whyPoints.title: Rates are quoted as the market, with sources named
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider or survey that published it, so a parent can check it. IB Gram's own arrangement starts with a free trial lesson and a plan, because hours needed vary too much for a single published rate to be honest.

whyPoints.title: Academic honesty is a stated boundary
whyPoints.description: A tutor here teaches, reviews and gives feedback on the student's own work. Nobody writes, completes or produces assessed work for a student. On a mathematics page that mostly means practice and method; on coursework subjects it is the difference between support and malpractice.

whyPoints.title: What we do not do is said plainly
whyPoints.description: No home visits in the UAE, no office in Dubai, no regulator approval claimed, no grade promised and no invented statistics. The pages competing for this query do several of those, and a parent comparing them should notice which ones state their limits.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling is built around the real school day
whyPoints.description: A session slot is agreed after the bus is actually back, with Deira traffic and prayer times accounted for, and held through the term. A plan a family keeps for twelve weeks beats a more ambitious one abandoned in week three.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether we live in Al Muteena or Hor Al Anz when choosing an IGCSE maths tutor?
faqs.answer: For the teaching, no. Both neighbourhoods feed the same Al Garhoud and Al Qusais secondaries, which enter students for the same two specifications, Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1. The grade is decided by paper technique and tier, not by address. Location changes two practical things: how long the school bus takes, which sets the earliest realistic weekday session, and how much a visiting in-home tutor would charge for travel. Since IB Gram teaches online, the second disappears and only the timing matters. A family moving between the two mid-year keeps the same tutor and the same slot.

faqs.question: Which maths specification does my child's school in Deira actually use?
faqs.answer: The entry letter from the school names it, and it is worth finding before booking any tutoring. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is code 0580 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A is 4MA1. Both appear in this part of Dubai, and some schools use different specifications for different sets. The difference is not cosmetic: on the Cambridge Extended route one paper is taken without a calculator, while Pearson permits a calculator in both papers. A tutor preparing for the wrong board will drill the wrong skills, so confirm the code and the syllabus version with the head of mathematics.

faqs.question: Can an IGCSE maths tutor in Al Muteena help us decide between Core and Extended?
faqs.answer: A tutor can give you evidence; the school holds the decision. The useful contribution is two marked papers on the intended tier, which shows what the student actually scores rather than what they feel capable of. The stakes are the grade ceiling: the lower tier caps the maximum grade available, so an entry made for comfort can close off a university course with a mathematics prerequisite. Equivalency itself only needs grade E or grade 3, so the risk is about destinations rather than about the Ministry. Raise the question in the term before entries close, not after.

faqs.question: How much should we budget monthly for IGCSE maths tuition in Old Dubai?
faqs.answer: Think in sessions rather than hours. One sixty-minute session a week is four a month. The Bestimate rate survey for Dubai estimates roughly AED 240 to AED 600 a month for budget tutoring on that pattern, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle band, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are market figures with a published source, not an IB Gram price list. In-home visits sit higher because travel is billed, and that premium buys no additional teaching. Our own arrangement starts with a free trial lesson and then a plan sized to what the diagnosis shows.

faqs.question: Why does online tutoring work for a subject as visual as maths?
faqs.answer: Because the paper is the shared object. A session runs with the student's own question paper on screen, a whiteboard both sides can write on, and the tutor watching the working appear rather than seeing a finished answer. Method marks are where IGCSE maths is won and lost, so watching a student lay out a solution line by line is exactly the right view. Sessions are recorded, so a method can be revisited later in the week. What online does not provide is physical presence, which some younger students need, and that is worth saying honestly.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our flat in Al Muteena?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; that service exists only in India. UAE lessons are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The URL you arrived on uses the phrase parents search, and the honest answer to it is this one. In-home tutoring in Al Muteena is available from independent tutors and agencies at published market rates of roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, and that is a legitimate choice. What it costs beyond money is the size of the tutor pool, which narrows to whoever will drive into Deira on a weekday evening.

faqs.question: When can a weekday session realistically start if our child goes to school in Al Qusais?
faqs.answer: Most families in this cluster land on something between 4.15pm and 5.45pm, depending on the bus route. A student attending a school within Al Qusais itself is often home soonest; a family on the Al Nahda side crossing border traffic is latest. Al Muteena to the Al Garhoud cluster typically means a 4.30pm start is workable. The practical advice is to pick a slot that survives a bad traffic day rather than the earliest one that works in theory, because a slot missed twice stops being a habit. Weekend mornings are the most reliable option for ninety-minute paper work.

faqs.question: Is a tutor teaching an Al Muteena student legally required to hold a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published, so treat any quoted amount with suspicion. Ask the tutor directly whether they hold it. The official route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service through its app, website and e-services.

faqs.question: Which exam series will our child sit, and is the February session an option?
faqs.answer: UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series with Cambridge, and May/June or November with Pearson Edexcel. The February/March series is offered to India only, so it is not available to a student in Dubai, and any page telling a UAE parent otherwise is giving them a date they cannot use. June results arrive quickly after the papers; Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day. November results come in the following January, with November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026. Always check the board's live timetable rather than a restated date.

faqs.question: What are the most common reasons a capable student still drops IGCSE maths marks?
faqs.answer: Five behaviours account for most of it. Working not shown, which forfeits method marks even on correct answers. Rounding mid-calculation and carrying the rounded figure forward. Incomplete descriptions in transformation and vector questions. Spending too long on low-mark questions and not finishing the paper. Arriving without compasses and a protractor for construction and locus work. None of these is a knowledge gap, which is why a diagnostic on the student's own marked mocks is more useful than a syllabus sweep. The first month of tutoring then targets four named habits rather than two years of content.

faqs.question: Is five IGCSE subjects really the equivalency count, or is it six as one site claims?
faqs.answer: Five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited A Level subject at grade E or better or two AS Level subjects at the same grade. One competitor page ranking for these queries states six, which is wrong. Verify the current requirement on moe.gov.ae or through the emirate's attestation channel before making a subject decision that depends on it. IB Gram does not perform equivalency or attestation, and tutoring is not required for it.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover maths and a science for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. A physics specialist usually teaches mathematics well, and the overlap in algebra, graphs and units is genuine. The combination that works less often is mathematics plus a humanities subject, where the mark schemes reward completely different behaviour. Where one tutor can cover both, scheduling gets simpler and the student builds one working relationship. Where they cannot, two specialists beat one generalist. The answer depends on the specific tutor's subject depth at the level required, so it is settled during matching rather than promised in advance.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not the right fit after two or three sessions?
faqs.answer: You say so and the match changes. The free trial exists to reduce the chance, but fit is partly about personality and pace and a trial cannot test everything. A reasonable test after three sessions is whether the student can name what they are working on and whether the written session notes match what you see at home. If either is missing, raise it. No provider should make changing a tutor awkward, and a page that does not mention the possibility at all is quietly hoping you will not ask.

faqs.question: Will Arabic and Islamic Education lessons leave time for maths practice?
faqs.answer: They occupy real timetable hours, so the honest answer is that a plan has to be built around them. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum licensed, with KHDA requiring implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. For most Al Muteena households that leaves the weekend and two weekday evenings as the realistic window for independent mathematics work, which is enough if the practice is targeted rather than open-ended.

faqs.question: Our child has six weeks before the paper. Is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: It is late for new content and useful for examination behaviour, which is where most of the recoverable marks sit anyway. A six-week block works best as two sessions a week built entirely from the student's own marked papers: timed sections, method presentation, accuracy instructions, and the three question types they most reliably drop. Expect to leave some topics alone deliberately, because a sweep at this point does less than securing what is nearly there. Nobody can promise a grade in six weeks, and anyone who does should be questioned. What is realistic is fewer avoidable marks lost.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-muteena.closingHeading: One shortlist for Al Muteena, Deira and the streets between
dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-muteena.closingBody: If you are comparing addresses, compare them on the school and the school run. The mathematics does not change between Al Muteena, Hor Al Anz and Al Nahda, because the same two specifications are sitting in every Year 11 classroom in this cluster and the same mark schemes decide the grade. Send the syllabus code from your child's entry letter, the last two marked mock papers and two weekday windows that survive a bad traffic day. A free trial lesson with the proposed tutor will tell you where the marks are actually going, in writing, before you commit to anything.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-nahda.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE mathematics to Al Nahda families one student at a time over live video. Each works from the specification printed on your child's entry statement, so the paper being practised has the same structure, timing and calculator rules as the paper being sat.

intro.heading: Work out the month before you argue about the hour
paragraphs: An hourly rate tells an Al Nahda family almost nothing. Two sessions a week at AED 200 is AED 1,600 a month and about AED 14,000 across a two-year IGCSE course. One session a week at AED 300 is AED 1,200 a month. The cheaper hourly rate is the more expensive arrangement, and the difference is large enough to pay for a term of university accommodation. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai estimates for a single weekly hour run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are monthly numbers, and they are the ones to compare.

Al Nahda adds a specific wrinkle to this arithmetic. The neighbourhood sits on the Dubai side of the Sharjah boundary, and a large share of households there run split logistics: a school place in Dubai, relatives or a second school in Sharjah, and a commute that crosses the emirate line at the exact hour tutoring wants to happen. A tutor who agrees to drive into Al Nahda for 5pm is pricing that crossing into the quote, and the published in-home band of AED 180 to AED 500 an hour reflects it.

IB Gram removes the journey rather than discounting it. Al Nahda lessons are one-to-one over live video, screen-shared, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. A family who specifically wants somebody at the dining table should hire locally, and the published rates for doing that are set out below rather than hidden.

The second thing that decides your total spend has nothing to do with rates. It is the tier your child is entered for. Cambridge 0580 splits into Core and Extended; Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 splits into Foundation and Higher. Extended and Higher reach grade 9. Core and Foundation stop at grade 5. A family paying for weekly tutoring towards a 7 while their child is entered for Core is buying something arithmetically impossible, and the entry has a deadline. Checking the tier costs one email and is the highest-value unpaid step on this page.

The third is which maths. From the 2025 examination Cambridge 0580 sits one non-calculator and one calculator paper at each tier, which changed how much arithmetic fluency has to be rebuilt before anything else works. Pearson 4MA1 sits two papers of two hours each with a calculator permitted throughout. A student drilled for a calculator-permitted paper and then handed a non-calculator one loses marks on competence they genuinely possess.

What follows is costed: the monthly scenarios, the tier decision, the paper structures side by side, the six topics that consume the most paid hours, where Al Nahda families most often waste money, and what a November resit should and should not cost. Every AED figure belongs to the provider named next to it and was read in October 2026. None is an IB Gram price.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-nahda.programmesIntro: Al Nahda households often span two emirates and two curricula, so the maths a 15-year-old is sitting varies street by street. These are the programmes most often tutored here and what each one does to a maths budget.

programmes.name: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 Mathematics
programmes.description: Two linear years ending in two written papers at the entered tier. The syllabus is number, algebra, coordinate geometry, mensuration, trigonometry, transformations, probability and statistics. Marks concentrate in multi-step problems worth four to six marks each, where a student who knows every individual step still loses the chain. Tier choice sets the ceiling before teaching begins.
programmes.countryNote: Al Nahda's British-curriculum feeder schools run IGCSE at 16 before splitting towards A Level or the IB Diploma. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak and the published report comments on subject performance, which is a free way to find out whether a weak maths cohort is the school or the child.

programmes.name: Cambridge Additional Mathematics
programmes.description: Taken alongside 0580 by schools preparing students for A Level Mathematics. It brings in differentiation, logarithms, matrices and the factor theorem a year early. Single tier, so there is no ceiling decision. Students who struggle here almost always struggle because 0580 algebra was never secure, which is why paying for both at once is usually the wrong order.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Al Nahda school offers 0606, and whether it appears on a timetable is a school decision rather than a parent one. If your child is entered for it, confirm with the school whether it is taught in curriculum time or expected as independent study, because the answer changes how many paid hours it needs.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Criterion-marked on a 0-8 scale across four criteria rather than examined against a content list. A student arriving in an IGCSE maths class from MYP has usually met the concepts and never met a tiered written paper under timed conditions. The teaching gap is assessment literacy, not mathematics, and it is cheap to close if diagnosed early.
programmes.countryNote: Families moving between Deira and Garhoud schools inside a single academic year can cross this boundary mid-course. It is one of the two commonest reasons an Al Nahda parent books maths support in Year 10, and the other is a Core entry nobody explained.

programmes.name: IB Diploma mathematics: AA and AI
programmes.description: The route out of IGCSE maths for Diploma students, split into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each at Standard and Higher Level. AA is the proof-and-calculus route; AI is the modelling-and-statistics route. Which one a student can realistically take is largely decided by how secure their IGCSE algebra was, which makes Year 11 maths spending an investment in Year 12 options.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma places for Al Nahda families sit mostly in Garhoud, Mamzar and Festival City. A student aiming at Analysis Higher Level with an insecure Extended algebra base should fix that in Year 11, when an hour is cheaper in effect than the same hour spent firefighting in Year 12.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-nahda.subjectsIntro: Maths is one subject and eight different spending problems. These are the strands an IGCSE maths tutor in Al Nahda actually bills time against, ordered roughly by how many paid hours each tends to consume.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging and simplifying. The single largest consumer of paid hours, because every other topic uses it. A student who hesitates here pays for it in trigonometry, in mensuration and in every physics and chemistry calculation as well, which is why fixing it once is the cheapest intervention available.

subjects.name: Number and non-calculator arithmetic
subjects.description: Fractions, surds, indices, standard form, percentages and reverse percentages. Cambridge's non-calculator paper from the 2025 examination raised the cost of neglecting this. Reverse percentage questions are a reliable four-mark loss for students who have only ever seen percentages in the forward direction.

subjects.name: Multi-step problem solving
subjects.description: Questions worth four to six marks that chain two or three topics together. This is where the gap between a 5 and a 7 actually lives. The skill is planning a route before calculating, and it is taught by marking attempts rather than by explaining methods, which is why written feedback between sessions matters more than lesson time.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and bearings
subjects.description: Right-angled trigonometry, the sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle, three-dimensional problems and bearings. Bearings questions lose marks on diagram conventions rather than on trigonometry, which makes them unusually cheap to fix with a short targeted block.

subjects.name: Graphs and functions
subjects.description: Sketching quadratics, reciprocals and exponentials, finding gradients, solving graphically and interpreting rates of change. Students who can solve algebraically and cannot read a graph lose marks twice: once in maths and again in science data questions.

subjects.name: Mensuration and compound shapes
subjects.description: Area, volume, surface area, arcs and sectors, and similar figures with the length, area and volume scale factors. The scale-factor relationship is the most reliably forgotten fact in the whole specification and appears in both tiers most years.

subjects.name: Probability and statistics
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, conditional probability, cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal intervals and averages from grouped data. Marks go on frequency density and on reading a cumulative frequency curve precisely, both of which are technique rather than understanding.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, vector geometry proofs, and the four transformations with full descriptions. Transformation questions demand complete descriptions, so a correct image drawn without naming the centre or the scale factor scores partial marks at best.

subjects.name: Sequences and iterative methods
subjects.description: Linear, quadratic and geometric sequences, nth-term rules and, on some specifications, iteration. Quadratic nth-term questions are routinely skipped in school revision because they are fiddly, which makes them good value for a targeted session.

subjects.name: Calculator discipline
subjects.description: Not a topic, but a billable skill. Mode settings, bracket discipline, storing intermediate values and avoiding premature rounding are worth several marks a paper. A single session on the specific model your child owns often returns more marks per dirham than any content lesson.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-nahda.modesIntro: Three ways to buy IGCSE maths support in Al Nahda, with the monthly consequence of each. IB Gram teaching is one-to-one and delivered live online; the other models appear because they are what a local quote gets compared against.

modes.description: The default and usually the right starting shape. One fixed slot on Gulf Standard Time plus a marked problem set in between, which is where most of the measurable movement happens. paragraphs: Families compare hourly rates because that is what providers advertise. Providers advertise hourly rates because the monthly number is less flattering. Working the month out first reorders the whole decision, and it takes about two minutes.

Bestimate's 2026 Dubai figures for a single weekly hour are AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Published package rates in this market include roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, which is around AED 100 a session at two a week, and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits, which is eight contact hours plus eight journeys.

The budget online tier underpinning the lowest monthly numbers is real and has a real limit. Tutopiya advertises from about AED 33 to AED 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65. At that level you can buy homework supervision and drilling, which genuinely helps a Year 10 student rebuilding fractions and indices. You cannot buy a reading of a marked Extended script that identifies which four topics are costing nine marks each.

sections.heading: The tier decision that caps the grade before you spend anything
paragraphs: No amount of tutoring lifts a student above the ceiling of the tier they are entered for. Cambridge 0580 Core awards grades up to 5; Extended reaches 9. Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Foundation awards up to 5; Higher reaches 9. A family paying for weekly maths towards a 7 while the entry sits on Core is buying an arithmetic impossibility, and it happens more often than it should because the tier is set quietly by the school and rarely explained at home.

The decision is not simply higher is better. A student entered for Extended who can reliably access only the first half of each paper may score a 3 or a 4, whereas the same student on Core, where the questions sit in their range, may convert the same knowledge into a 5 and keep the subject alive for Ministry of Education equivalency purposes. Equivalency on the British track asks for five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, so a secure 5 can be worth more to a family's plan than a risky 4.

What makes the decision cheap to get right is evidence. Two or three paid sessions producing a timed paper at each tier, marked against the published criteria, tells you which paper the student can actually work through. That costs between AED 300 and AED 900 at the published mid band and it is the highest-return purchase in an IGCSE maths budget, because it determines whether every subsequent hour is aimed at an achievable grade.

Timing matters because entries close months before the papers. The conversation to have with the school is before the entry deadline, not after results. Ask for the tier in writing, ask what evidence the decision rests on, and ask what would have to change for it to be revisited. A school that can answer all three has made a considered decision; a school that cannot has made an administrative one.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 against Pearson 4MA1, paper by paper
paragraphs: Two Al Nahda students can both be doing IGCSE maths and sit genuinely different examinations. The content overlaps heavily. The papers do not, and preparing for the wrong structure wastes the fee completely while looking like diligent work the whole way through.

Cambridge 0580 is the specification most Al Nahda British-curriculum schools use, and from the 2025 examination it sits one non-calculator and one calculator paper at each tier. That changed the preparation economics: arithmetic fluency, surds, indices and fraction work that a calculator previously absorbed now has to be secure, and a student who has spent two years reaching for a calculator needs a dedicated block to rebuild it.

Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 sits two papers of two hours each, 100 marks apiece, with a calculator permitted in both. The consequence is that preparation weight shifts away from mental arithmetic and towards calculator discipline: bracket handling, storing intermediate values, mode settings and avoiding premature rounding, each of which is worth marks on a two-hour paper. Pearson also offers the specification in a November series as well as May and June, which matters to resit planning.

Finding out which applies costs one email. The specification number appears on the exam entry statement the school issues, on every past paper handed out in class, and the examinations officer will confirm it. Do that before the first paid session, because a tutor briefed with a code gives different lessons from a tutor briefed with a subject name.

sections.heading: Six topics that consume the most paid hours
paragraphs: Maths tutoring money does not spread evenly across the specification. It concentrates, and it concentrates in predictable places. Knowing which six topics absorb the hours lets a family buy a short targeted block instead of a long general one.

Algebraic manipulation comes first and by a distance. Expanding, factorising, rearranging and simplifying appear inside almost every other topic, so insecurity here is paid for repeatedly in trigonometry, in mensuration, in graphs and in every physics and chemistry calculation the student attempts. One tutor fixing this once is cheaper than three subject tutors each discovering it separately.

Second is reverse percentages and compound change, which fail because students have only ever met percentages in the forward direction. Third is multi-step problem solving, the four-to-six-mark questions that chain topics together, which is where the gap between a 5 and a 7 genuinely lives and which responds to marked attempts rather than to explanation. Fourth is similar figures and the length, area and volume scale factors, the most reliably forgotten relationship in the specification.

Fifth is histograms with unequal class intervals and cumulative frequency, where the marks go on frequency density and precise curve reading rather than on understanding. Sixth is vectors and full transformation descriptions, where a correct drawing without a named centre or scale factor scores partial marks. Each of those last three is a technique problem, which means a single well-aimed session can return more marks per dirham than a month of general coverage.

sections.heading: Where Al Nahda families waste maths money
paragraphs: Waste here is rarely a weak tutor. It is a capable tutor pointed at the wrong target, bought in the wrong month, for a student whose real gap sits two years upstream. Four patterns account for most of it and all four are visible before the money moves.

The first is paying for the school's current topic every week. A tutor who follows the scheme of work re-teaches whatever was covered on Tuesday, which feels responsive and leaves the Year 8 foundations untouched underneath. Those foundations are what the papers actually test, and they do not appear on this term's plan. A diagnosis reorders the sessions around marks lost rather than around the timetable.

The second is buying 0606 Additional Mathematics alongside a 0580 rebuild. Additional Maths assumes secure algebra. A student who does not have it will consume hours in both courses and improve in neither, at roughly double the monthly cost. Fix 0580 algebra, then let 0606 follow; the order is the saving.

The third is the two-hour session. In-home packages use two-hour visits because the journey has to be amortised, and families then carry that shape into online tutoring where there is no journey to amortise. For a 15-year-old, two sixty-minute sessions on separate days produce more than one two-hour session, because the marked homework in between is where the learning lands.

The fourth is the group class bought on headline price. A centre advertising IGCSE maths at a fraction of the one-to-one rate is excellent value at four students and worthless at fourteen, and the group size is usually unpublished. Ask for the current enrolment of the specific class in writing. A centre with premises and staff in Dubai should also hold a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, and the permit number is a fair thing to request.

sections.heading: Fitting a maths session into an Al Nahda week
paragraphs: Scheduling is a cost, even when nobody invoices for it. A slot that keeps collapsing gets rebooked, and rebooked sessions are either lost or crammed, and crammed sessions are the least productive hours a family buys. Al Nahda's position against the Sharjah boundary makes this sharper than in most Dubai neighbourhoods.

A Dubai school day typically ends in the early-to-mid afternoon, and the drive home across Al Nahda Street or Al Ittihad Road at that hour is slower than the distance suggests. Allow for arrival, a meal and some decompression, and the first genuinely useful weekday slot is early evening rather than late afternoon. An online lesson can start the moment the student is at a desk, which is often forty minutes earlier than an in-home tutor could physically arrive.

Three fixed pressures then shape the week. Dubai private schools carry Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside the licensed curriculum regardless of the international programme, with KHDA calculating instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, so the school week is already full. School assessment fortnights come round two or three times a year and are the wrong weeks to add hours. Ramadan moves the usable evening window, and sessions shifting to a post-Iftar slot is a normal accommodation rather than a special request.

The practical answer is one protected weekday evening slot, one marked problem set due before it, and an agreed policy for exam weeks and travel. Over a two-year course that policy is worth more than a small discount on the hourly rate, because it determines how many of the hours you paid for actually happened.

sections.heading: The November resit route, costed
paragraphs: Resits are where families either spend well or spend twice. The reason to spend well is that a resit candidate holds the single best diagnostic available anywhere in this process: component-level marks. You are no longer guessing which topics cost the grade; the statement of results tells you which paper lost the marks.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, and UAE centres sit those two. The February and March series is offered to India only, so it is not a route from Al Nahda and should be left out of any plan. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in May and June and again in November. Pearson's own record gives a feel for the lag: the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Always work from the live official timetable, because provisional ones are revised.

Costed at the published mid band, a targeted resit campaign of six to ten hours across eight weeks is AED 900 to AED 3,000, plus whatever the centre charges for entry. Anything materially above that usually means the hours have drifted back into general revision, which is precisely what the component marks exist to prevent. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one.

One decision belongs to the family rather than to the tutor: whether a resit is the right purchase at all. If a grade 5 on a capped tier already satisfies the plan, the money may be better spent protecting two fragile subjects than lifting one adequate grade. Equivalency on the British track counts five subjects at no less than grade E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, and a plan is only as strong as its weakest five.

sections.heading: What a maths tutor may and may not do with your child's work
paragraphs: This matters financially as well as ethically, because work produced by somebody else can end a candidacy and make every hour already bought worthless. The boundary is clearer than families expect, and it is worth testing before the first payment.

A tutor may teach content, explain the assessment criteria, question a student's reasoning, work through a parallel example, and mark the student's own attempts against the published mark scheme. A tutor may not supply solutions to be submitted, complete assessed work, or edit a piece into a finished state. For IGCSE maths the assessment is external, so the exposure is smaller than in a coursework subject, but the same rule governs any school-assessed task and any Diploma exploration the student goes on to produce.

Materials carry a parallel rule. IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are copyright works. A tutor should cite and link the official versions rather than distributing copies, and a provider advertising a bundle of mark schemes as an inducement is offering something it has no right to distribute. One page found in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright; that is a malpractice trigger whose consequences fall on the student.

There is also a rule about who may be asked. Abu Dhabi's ADEK professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Asking your child's own maths teacher to tutor them privately is therefore the wrong favour to request, however convenient it looks on a Tuesday.

process.title: Send the code and the tier, not the subject name
process.description: Email the examinations officer for the specification number and the entered tier, then send both. Cambridge 0580 Extended and Pearson 4MA1 Higher need different first lessons, and a tutor briefed with a code prepares differently from one briefed with the words IGCSE maths.

process.description: One session on real material, no payment and no commitment, ending in a written view of where the marks are going. If that view contradicts what school has said, the disagreement is worth having before any money moves rather than after three months of sessions.

process.title: Buy the diagnosis before the programme
process.description: Two or three sessions producing a timed paper at the relevant tier, a marked script with mark-scheme references, and a ranked list of topics by marks lost. At the published mid band that is AED 300 to AED 900 and it decides whether the next twelve weeks are aimed or general.

process.title: Fix the monthly number and the review date
process.description: Agree hours per month, the total for the first phase, the Gulf Standard Time slot, and the date the arrangement gets reviewed. A review date is what stops a monthly fee outliving the problem it was bought to solve, and it costs nothing to insist on.

process.title: Require marked work between sessions
process.description: A weekly problem set returned with criteria references rather than a grade. Most of the measurable movement in IGCSE maths happens in the student's response to marking, which is why the marking rather than the lesson time is the thing to hold a provider to.

process.title: Taper into the series deliberately
process.description: Switch from content to timing and technique around eight weeks out, drop frequency after the final mock, and stop when the papers start. Hours bought in the last fortnight cost the same as any others and can add the least.

Bestimate's 2026 bands, the AED 799 online package rate and the AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 in-home package rate are all named and dated rather than implied.

whyPoints.title: Tier checked before money is spent
whyPoints.description: Core and Foundation cap the grade at 5. Confirming the entered tier in writing before buying weekly sessions is free, takes one email, and prevents the most expensive misunderstanding available in IGCSE maths tutoring.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the specification, not the subject
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 differ on calculator rules, paper length and where marks are lost. Matching on the code is what stops an Al Nahda family paying for preparation aimed at a paper their child will never sit.

whyPoints.description: No promised grade, no success percentage, no self-asserted rating. Where a figure appears it carries the source that published it and the month it was read. A number without those two things is not evidence and is not used here.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE maths tuition cost per month in Al Nahda?
faqs.answer: Work from monthly bands rather than hourly rates. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai estimates for one weekly hour are AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Published packages in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are the market's published figures read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list, which is discussed only after a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Is Extended maths tuition priced higher than Core?
faqs.answer: Not reliably by the hour, but materially by the term. The published bands do not split by tier; what changes is how many hours each tier needs. Extended and Higher candidates aiming above grade 6 are chasing the last four marks of each question, which is specialist work spread thinly across a year. Core and Foundation candidates are usually consolidating fewer topics to a secure 5, which is a shorter engagement. The bigger cost difference is the tier itself, because Core and Foundation cap the grade at 5 regardless of spend.

faqs.question: How much of an IGCSE maths budget goes on topics the school already covered?
faqs.answer: More than most families realise, and it is the commonest avoidable waste. A tutor who follows the school's scheme of work re-teaches whatever was covered that week. It feels responsive and leaves the Year 8 and Year 9 foundations untouched underneath, which is where the papers actually probe. A diagnosis reorders the sessions around marks lost rather than around the timetable. One marked timed paper, costing a single session at the published band, usually relocates half the planned hours to a different topic entirely.

faqs.question: Does paying more per hour buy a better IGCSE maths grade?
faqs.answer: It buys a narrower kind of help, which is only worth it if that is the help needed. The premium tiers in this market, with BartyED publishing AED 650 an hour, deliver scarcity and senior marking experience. That suits a student already scoring well and losing only the hardest marks in each paper. A student missing Year 9 algebra needs volume and patience rather than seniority, and would convert the same money into more progress at the mid band. Match the tier of tutor to the diagnosis, not to the ambition.

faqs.question: Is 0580 the same specification as 4MA1?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 are separate International GCSE mathematics specifications with heavily overlapping content and different papers. Cambridge tiers into Core and Extended and, from the 2025 examination, sits one non-calculator and one calculator paper per tier. Pearson tiers into Foundation and Higher and sits two papers of two hours with a calculator permitted throughout. Preparation differs accordingly: Cambridge candidates need arithmetic fluency rebuilt, Pearson candidates need calculator discipline and pacing. The code is printed on your child's exam entry statement.

faqs.question: What is the grade ceiling on IGCSE Core maths?
faqs.answer: Cambridge 0580 Core awards grades up to 5, and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Foundation does the same. No amount of tutoring moves a candidate above that, because the papers do not contain the questions that carry the higher grades. This is why confirming the entered tier in writing is the first thing to do and the cheapest. It also explains why a secure 5 on the lower tier can serve a family's plan better than a fragile 4 on the higher one, particularly where Ministry of Education equivalency counts five subjects at no less than grade E or 3.

faqs.question: Can my child move from Core to Extended maths in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the window is the entry deadline rather than the end of the course. Entries close months before the papers, so the conversation belongs with the school well before results. Ask three questions in writing: what tier is my child entered for, what evidence does that rest on, and what would have to change for it to be revisited. Bring evidence of your own by having a timed paper at each tier marked against the published criteria. A school that can answer all three has made a considered decision rather than an administrative one.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths paper is the calculator paper?
faqs.answer: It depends on the board. From the 2025 examination Cambridge 0580 sits one non-calculator paper and one calculator paper at each tier, which raised the cost of weak arithmetic considerably. Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 permits a calculator in both of its two-hour papers, so the preparation weight shifts towards calculator discipline: bracket handling, storing intermediate values, mode settings and avoiding premature rounding. Confirm the arrangement with the examinations officer rather than assuming, because preparing for the wrong rule costs marks on competence your child already has.

faqs.question: How many hours before the exam should we stop buying new topics?
faqs.answer: Around eight weeks out the useful work changes character. Before that, new content can still be learned and consolidated. After it, the realistic job is timing, command-word discipline and recovering the marks the student already half-earns, because a topic met for the first time in the final fortnight rarely survives into the hall. Practically: switch to whole timed papers marked against the published criteria at the eight-week point, reduce frequency after the final mock, and stop entirely when the papers start. The last fortnight is for rest and rehearsal.

faqs.question: Is one two-hour maths session cheaper than two single hours?
faqs.answer: Occasionally per hour, rarely per unit of learning. Two-hour blocks exist because in-home packages have to amortise a journey over more teaching, which is why four two-hour visits appear at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month. Online there is no journey to amortise and concentration becomes the binding constraint. For a 15-year-old, two sixty-minute sessions on separate days beat one two-hour session, because the gap between them is where the marked problem set gets done, and the problem set is where most of the movement happens.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE maths retake in the November series cost us twice?
faqs.answer: It costs a board entry fee through the centre plus a short block of tutoring, and it should cost considerably less than the original campaign. A resit candidate holds component-level marks, which is the best diagnostic in the whole process: you know which paper lost the marks rather than guessing. Six to ten targeted hours across eight weeks at the published mid band is AED 900 to AED 3,000. Spending much beyond that usually means the sessions have drifted back into general revision, which the component marks exist to prevent.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest useful thing to buy for IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: A single marked timed paper at the entered tier. One session at the published band of AED 150 to AED 300 produces a script marked against the real criteria, a ranked list of topics by marks lost, and a view on whether the tier is right. That one purchase routinely redirects half of the hours a family was about to buy. Two free steps belong alongside it: email the examinations officer for the specification code and tier, and read your school's published KHDA inspection report for its subject-level comments.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE maths tutors charge more during mock season?
faqs.answer: Rates in this market are not published as seasonal, but availability tightens sharply from the mock window onwards, and scarcity shapes what you can actually book rather than what you are quoted. The planning consequence matters more than the price: the fortnight after mocks is the single best moment to buy a diagnosis, because a marked mock script is free evidence the school has already generated. Families who book a diagnostic session in that window spend the following term aimed, and families who wait until spring spend it generally.

faqs.question: Should we pay for tuition in both maths and additional maths?
faqs.answer: Rarely at the same time. Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics assumes secure 0580 algebra and introduces differentiation, logarithms and matrices on top of it. A student whose algebra is not yet secure will consume hours in both courses and improve in neither, at roughly double the monthly cost. The cheaper sequence is to fix 0580 algebraic manipulation first and let 0606 follow, because almost every 0606 difficulty traces back to it. If both are genuinely needed, stagger them across terms rather than running them in parallel.

faqs.question: How do we check an IGCSE maths tutor's claimed marking experience?
faqs.answer: Ask for specifics and treat vagueness as an answer. Which board, which specification code, which component, and in which years. Then ask them to mark one of your child's existing scripts and show the mark-scheme references for every deduction. A tutor with real marking experience does that quickly and in the mark scheme's own language. Nobody should describe themselves as a current examiner without evidence, and examiner status must never be presented as access to marking, boundaries or paper content, which is a claim no legitimate provider makes.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor to an address in Al Nahda?
faqs.answer: No, and it is better to say so plainly than to let a family find out after paying. IB Gram delivers one-to-one teaching to UAE families over live video, screen-shared and scheduled on Gulf Standard Time; home visits are offered only in India. The gain is that an Al Nahda family chooses from everyone who knows their child's specification and tier rather than from everyone who can cross Al Nahda Street by five o'clock. The honest cost is that a family who wants a person in the room should hire locally, where the published band is AED 180 to AED 500 an hour.

Only after that does a monthly figure mean anything, because until somebody has marked your child's maths, every quote in Al Nahda is a guess about a problem nobody has measured.
