intro.heading: The comparison worth running, and the one that changes nothing
paragraphs: Al Quoz parents looking for IGCSE maths support usually compare districts first. Al Barsha has schools inside it. Al Safa and Jumeirah have long-established tuition centres. Al Quoz has warehouses, showrooms, workshops and the Alserkal Avenue arts spaces, with housing in Al Quoz 1, 2 and 3 between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road. On a map it looks underserved, and the conclusion drawn from that is usually the wrong one.

Here is what the district comparison genuinely decides: the length of the school run, and therefore the earliest hour a weekday session can start. Al Quoz sits around 5pm to 5.30pm; Al Barsha manages 4.30pm. That matters when a pre-series block needs two sessions a week. It decides nothing at all about the mathematics itself, or about who is able to teach it.

Here is the comparison that does decide something. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1 are different papers with different structures and different tier vocabulary. Cambridge sets Core and Extended; Edexcel sets Foundation and Higher. A tutor working from the wrong board's past papers is giving your child confident, well-organised practice in a format they will not sit, and the student cannot tell the difference until results day.

The second decisive comparison is the tier. A capped entry limits the grade available whatever the student achieves, and an over-ambitious entry can produce a worse grade than the capped tier would have. The decision sits with the school to a school deadline, it is often presented as administrative, and it reaches forward: a Core or Foundation entry does not position a student for A Level Mathematics or Higher Level Analysis and Approaches two years later.

The third comparison is the one families almost never run, and it is the cheapest. Compare the problems rather than the providers. A grade of 5 can be produced by weak algebra, by one catastrophic topic, by method marks leaking out of every question, or by running out of time on every paper. Those are four different problems with four different plans, three of which take three or four sessions and one of which takes a term. Nobody can tell them apart from a report card, and one marked script usually separates them in minutes.

So this page compares boards, compares tiers, compares topics by where the marks actually go, and compares the real cost of the options including the extras that nobody mentions until the invoice. One premise first: IB Gram delivers one-to-one IGCSE mathematics into Al Quoz homes as live online video sessions on Gulf Standard Time, with working shared and annotated on screen. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home visits are a service we run in India only.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics

Papers reward method, so unshown working forfeits marks even where the final answer is correct, and premature rounding breaks multi-step answers that were otherwise sound.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A
programmes.description: Tiered Foundation and Higher, with a different paper structure from Cambridge and different mark allocation conventions. Content overlaps heavily, which is exactly why families mix the two up, and the overlap does not help a student who has practised the wrong format all term.

programmes.description: Taken alongside 0580 by stronger cohorts as a bridge to A Level or Higher Level IB, introducing calculus and more formal function work. A student comfortable in 0580 Extended who finds 0606 hard usually has a speed and fluency gap rather than a conceptual one, which responds well to short regular practice.

Mathematics is the subject where the IGCSE decision constrains post-16 choice most sharply, because a capped tier removes a prerequisite regardless of the grade achieved within it.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-quoz.subjectsIntro: IGCSE mathematics is best organised by topic, because that is where the marks are lost and where a block of sessions can be aimed. Below is what each area demands and the error that recurs most in marked scripts.

subjects.name: Number and the four operations in context
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Fractions, percentages, ratio, standard form and bounds. The dominant error is premature rounding, which produces an answer just outside the acceptable range and loses marks on work that was otherwise correct from start to finish.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging and solving. Fluency here determines performance everywhere else, because a student slow at manipulation spends their working memory on mechanics and has none left for the question being asked.

subjects.name: Equations, inequalities and simultaneous systems
subjects.description: Quadratics by factorising, formula and completing the square, plus simultaneous equations including one linear and one non-linear at the higher tiers. Marks go missing when a correct solution set is found and not checked against the original condition.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.description: Sketching, transformations, gradients, intercepts and interpreting graphical information. Students lose marks on sketches that are qualitatively right but missing the labelled features the question specifically asked for, which is a reading problem rather than a mathematical one.

subjects.name: Geometry and mensuration
subjects.description: Angle reasoning, circle properties, similarity, area and volume of composite solids. Reasons are marked as well as answers: an unstated angle fact forfeits the explanation mark even where the numerical answer is right.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled and non-right-angled triangles, bearings and three-dimensional problems. The recurring failure is a calculator left in the wrong angular mode, which yields a confidently wrong answer that looks like carelessness and is actually a habit.

subjects.name: Statistics and data handling
subjects.description: Averages from grouped data, cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal intervals and scatter graphs. Histograms are reliably the worst-answered topic in this part of the syllabus because frequency density is treated as optional.

subjects.name: Probability
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, conditional probability and set notation at the higher tiers. Errors cluster around failing to adjust for non-replacement, and around answers left as unsimplified products when the question asked for a value.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude and geometric reasoning with vectors. Marks are available for the reasoning chain rather than the final vector, so answers given without the intermediate statements score below their apparent worth.

subjects.name: Calculator technique and the formula list
subjects.description: Not a topic and worth marks throughout. Knowing which functions the calculator provides, which formulae are given and which must be recalled, and how to report a calculator result with supporting method, is trainable and usually left to accident.

Three facts have to be established before any teaching is useful, and a tutor who does not ask for them is guessing. The board and code, because Cambridge 0580 and Edexcel 4MA1 are different papers. The tier, because a Core or Foundation candidate practising Extended or Higher material is learning content that will not appear and losing confidence to no purpose. sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 against Edexcel 4MA1
paragraphs: Across the competitor pages researched for this market, exactly one syllabus code appeared in an entire seven-page cluster. That omission is why so many Dubai families end up with a tutor using the wrong papers: nobody told them the distinction existed, and the content overlap is large enough that the error is invisible from inside a session.

What differs is not the mathematics but the examination. Paper structure, the number and length of papers, mark allocation conventions, how heavily certain topics are weighted and the tier vocabulary itself all vary. Cambridge sets Core and Extended; Edexcel sets Foundation and Higher. A parent translating between those terms in a phone call can agree to the wrong entry without anyone noticing.

Check this per subject rather than per school, because departments choose independently. A single Al Quoz student can sit Cambridge 0580 Mathematics and Edexcel 4CH1 Chemistry in the same year. The code is printed on the school's assessment paperwork and the subject teacher will confirm it in one line, which is the single most valuable email a parent can send this term.

On dates, both boards publish provisional timetables in advance and revise them, so use the live official document. For a candidate sitting in the UAE, Cambridge runs June and November, with the February and March series offered to India only. Edexcel runs May and June, and November. Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

sections.heading: The tier decision, and the door it closes
paragraphs: This is the highest-leverage decision in IGCSE mathematics and it is routinely made for the wrong reason. The capped tier protects a student from a grade collapse, which is a legitimate aim. It also removes a prerequisite, which is a different and longer-lasting consequence that rarely gets raised in the same conversation.

The honest test is a timed paper from the harder tier, taken now, with no help and no notes. If the score sits near the bottom of that tier's range, there is a real decision about whether a block of work closes the gap or whether the capped tier produces the better outcome. If it sits in the middle, the conversation is over. What should not decide it is which tier the student finds more comfortable in class, because comfort and capability diverge under timed conditions.

The forward consequence is specific. A Core or Foundation mathematics entry does not position a student for A Level Mathematics or for Higher Level Analysis and Approaches in the IB Diploma, whatever grade they achieve inside the cap. In a school offering both post-16 routes, which several in this part of Dubai do, that is a Year 12 limitation created by a Year 10 form.

The deadline belongs to the school. Ask the subject teacher when the tier must be confirmed, and bring evidence to that meeting rather than opinion. A recent marked paper from the harder tier is worth more than any amount of discussion about potential.

sections.heading: Topic by topic: where the marks actually go
paragraphs: Marked scripts are repetitive. The same five or six failures account for most lost marks in IGCSE mathematics, and almost none of them is an inability to do mathematics. They are habits, and habits respond to short targeted work rather than to a term of general revision.

The largest single category is method marks forfeited by omitted working. A student who sees the answer writes the answer, and the scheme pays for the steps. This usually costs more marks across a paper than any individual topic does, and it responds to four sessions of marking their own scripts against the scheme until they can predict the mark before it is given.

After that come the specific topics that are reliably taught in a hurry: histograms with unequal class widths, where frequency density is treated as optional; conditional probability without replacement; three-dimensional trigonometry; and vector reasoning where the marks sit in the intermediate statements rather than the final answer. Each of these is a three to five session fix when identified, and an expensive mystery when not.

Premature rounding deserves its own mention because of how unfair it feels. A student carries a value rounded to two decimal places through four further steps and arrives just outside the accepted range, losing the mark on work that was correct throughout. It takes two sessions and a rule: carry full precision and round only on the final line.

The last category is timing, which disguises itself as weakness. A student who scores well with unlimited time and poorly under examination conditions does not need more teaching; they need a per-question time budget and practice holding it. You can test for this at home in one evening with a past paper taken twice, and the result changes the plan entirely.

sections.heading: The cost comparison, including the extras nobody mentions
paragraphs: Published hourly rates are the easy part of a cost comparison. The hard part is everything attached to them, which is where Al Quoz families most often find the real total diverging from the quote. So this section compares options on both.

The market first, attributed and dated October 2026. Budget online tutoring starts at Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 per hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. A qualified subject tutor online runs roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650. In-home one-to-one visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel, per Bestimate's 2026 Dubai cost table. Monthly packages seen in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. None of this is an IB Gram price list; ours is set after the free trial.

Now the extras. Minimum commitments that convert a trial into a term. Travel surcharges on in-home visits outside a stated radius, which matters in a district bordered by two motorways. Two car journeys per session for a centre class, which is a real cost in time even when it is not billed. Materials charges where a provider sells its own workbooks. Cancellation windows that charge for a session your child spent in a school detention. And rates that rise in the weeks before a series, which is the point at which switching is hardest.

Ask about each one before the first session rather than after the third. A provider who answers all six plainly is telling you something useful about how they operate, and a provider who deflects is also telling you something.

sections.heading: Calculators, formula provision and what the student is allowed
paragraphs: This is a small subject that costs real marks, and no competitor page in this market addresses it. A student who does not know which formulae are provided will either memorise things unnecessarily or, worse, assume something is given and find it is not. Both show up as content failure in a mock and are neither.

The provision differs between boards and is stated in the current syllabus documents your child's school holds. We do not reproduce those documents, because they are the boards' copyright, so the practical instruction is to ask the subject teacher for the formula provision for the specific paper and tier your child sits, and then build the memorisation list from what is not provided. That list is usually much shorter than students assume, which is itself reassuring.

Calculator technique is the other half. Knowing which functions the machine offers, which are permitted, how to check an angular mode before starting, and how to report a calculator result with the supporting method line, are all trainable skills worth marks across every paper. Most students acquire them accidentally and incompletely. Thirty minutes of explicit teaching early in Year 10 is worth more than the same time spent on content.

One related point on materials: we do not publish or supply Cambridge or Pearson past papers, mark schemes, grade boundary tables or syllabus documents as downloads. We reference them, cite the official source and link to it. Your child's school has proper access, and a provider offering those files as a selling point is distributing someone else's copyright.

sections.heading: Why the maths grade carries extra weight in the UAE
paragraphs: Mathematics does more work than other IGCSE subjects in this market, for two reasons that families often meet separately and should see together. The first is post-16 progression, already covered: a capped tier closes A Level Mathematics and Higher Level Analysis and Approaches. The second is equivalency, which is about what a UAE university or employer will accept.

The published British-track rule requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One competitor page currently ranking in this market tells parents six subjects are needed, which is wrong and could change what a family makes their child sit.

On the American track, mathematics appears explicitly: at least 450 in the SAT Math test is required before applying, with English proficiency satisfied by a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section. For the IB, no points threshold appears in the source we read, so none is published here.

Two cautions. IB Gram does not perform, submit or expedite equivalency, and tutoring is not required for it; it is a process families complete through the official channel. And requirements change, so verify the current position on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority before planning a subject list around any number, including the ones on this page.

No satisfaction percentages, because a statistic without its sample, date and method is decoration.

A limit stated in advance: in the weeks before a series, early-evening slots are genuinely constrained, because much of Dubai's Year 11 cohort wants the same hour. When it happens you are told, offered the nearest workable alternative and given a realistic view of when the slot opens. Nobody general is quietly substituted for the specialist you asked for.

Individuals offering private tuition in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023; it is granted free of charge for two years, eligible categories include school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents and university students, and those operating without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We teach IGCSE mathematics one-to-one into Al Quoz homes over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with working shared and annotated on screen, and send no tutors to UAE addresses; in-person home visits are an India-only service for us. Other Dubai providers do visit homes at roughly AED 180 to 500 per hour with travel included, per Bestimate's 2026 cost table. For mathematics the shared screen is generally a better working surface than one sheet of paper.

faqs.question: Should my child be entered for Core or Extended maths?
faqs.answer: Settle it with a timed paper from the harder tier, taken now with no notes and marked honestly. Mid-range or above and the conversation is over. Near the bottom of the range and you have a genuine decision about whether a block of work closes the gap. What should not decide it is which tier feels more comfortable in class, because comfort and capability separate under examination timing. The confirmation deadline belongs to the school, so ask the subject teacher when it falls.

faqs.question: Does a capped maths tier really affect university options?
faqs.answer: It affects post-16 options, which then affect university ones. A Core or Foundation mathematics entry does not position a student for A Level Mathematics or for Higher Level Analysis and Approaches in the IB Diploma, whatever grade they achieve inside the cap. Several schools in this part of Dubai offer both post-16 routes, so the Year 10 form can quietly close a Year 12 door. Raise it explicitly in the tier conversation, because it is frequently presented as an administrative matter.

faqs.question: My child understands the maths but keeps losing marks. Why?
faqs.answer: Most often method marks forfeited by omitted working. The scheme pays for the steps, and a student who can see the answer writes only the answer, collecting one mark where four were available. Across a paper this usually costs more than any single weak topic. The fix is mechanical: have them mark their own scripts against the published scheme wording until they can predict the mark before it is given. That is typically four sessions, not a term.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths topics cause the most trouble in Dubai schools?
faqs.answer: Histograms with unequal class widths come first, because frequency density gets treated as optional and the topic is often taught in a hurry. Conditional probability without replacement is second, where the second branch is not adjusted. Three-dimensional trigonometry is third, compounded by calculators left in the wrong angular mode. Vector reasoning is fourth, where the marks sit in the intermediate statements rather than the final vector. Each is a three to five session fix once identified from a marked script.

faqs.question: How do we know if the problem is timing rather than knowledge?
faqs.answer: Test it at home in one evening. Give your child the same past paper twice, once under strict examination timing and once with unlimited time and no notes. If the untimed score is substantially higher, the problem is pacing, and the plan becomes a per-question time budget practised under pressure rather than more teaching. If both scores are low, the marked script will show whether it is content or technique. This single test prevents a term of tutoring aimed at the wrong thing.

faqs.question: What extra charges should we ask about before booking a tutor?
faqs.answer: Six, and ask all of them before the first session. Minimum block commitments that convert a trial into a term. Cancellation windows, which decide who pays when your child is kept at school. Travel surcharges on in-home visits outside a stated radius, which matters in a district bordered by two motorways. Materials charges where a provider sells its own workbooks. Class size, if a group is involved. And whether rates change in the weeks before a series, which is when switching is hardest.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre in Al Safa a reasonable alternative?
faqs.answer: For broad syllabus coverage, yes. For repairing one topic, it is poor value, because a group class teaching a fixed sequence cannot stop for your child's specific error, which is usually the entire problem. Add two car journeys per session from Al Quoz and the real cost in time exceeds the headline. If the marked script points at histograms and conditional probability, three one-to-one sessions will get further than a term of general class work.

faqs.question: Which formulae does my child have to memorise?
faqs.answer: Fewer than they assume, and the exact provision differs between boards and tiers. It is stated in the current syllabus documents your child's school holds, which we do not reproduce because they are the boards' copyright. The practical step is to ask the subject teacher for the formula provision for the specific paper and tier, then build the memorisation list from what is not given. Students routinely over-memorise and under-practise, which is the wrong way round.

faqs.question: Can we start maths support in the middle of Year 11?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families do, though earlier is cheaper. Mid-Year 11 work has to be targeted rather than broad: pick one component or topic from marked scripts, fix it, verify it on a timed paper, then decide whether a second block is justified. What mid-year starting cannot do is rebuild two years of algebraic fluency, so if the diagnosis points there, the honest plan is to secure the achievable grade rather than to chase the one that needed starting in Year 10.

faqs.question: Does my child need separate tutors for Maths and Additional Maths?
faqs.answer: Usually not, because 0606 Additional Mathematics is a direct extension of the algebra and functions work in 0580 Extended and the same tutor can hold both. The thing to check is that the tutor has taught 0606 specifically, since it introduces calculus and more formal function work that a general IGCSE tutor may not have covered. A student comfortable in Extended but struggling in 0606 usually has a fluency and speed gap rather than a conceptual one.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week during the eight weeks before the series?
faqs.answer: Two, and no more. The student needs days between sessions to attempt timed papers independently, because that attempt is where the gain is produced and the session is where it is diagnosed. Three or four sessions a week leaves no room for the practice and produces a tired student with the same error log. If two subjects both need work, one session each beats two in whichever feels most alarming this week.

faqs.question: Is the November series a realistic option if June goes badly?
faqs.answer: Yes. Both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel run a November series, and for a candidate in Dubai that is the resit route; the February and March series is offered to India only. Planning a November attempt is actually easier than first-attempt work, because you have the real script and the real grade, so the two or three topics that cost it can be identified precisely. Entry is arranged by the school's exams officer and should be discussed as soon as results arrive.

intro.heading: Two questions to answer before anyone teaches your child a thing
paragraphs: The first question is the board. Dubai schools enter IGCSE candidates with Cambridge International or with Pearson Edexcel, and the mathematics syllabuses are not interchangeable. Cambridge International Mathematics carries the code 0580 and splits into a Core and an Extended tier, each with its own pair of papers. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A carries the code 4MA1 and splits into Foundation and Higher tiers. A tutor who has only taught one of these will still be useful, but they will be teaching from the wrong paper layout unless somebody checks first, and a surprising number of parents cannot say which board their child's school uses.

The second question is the tier. This is the decision with a hard consequence attached, because the lower tier carries a grade ceiling. A Core or Foundation entry caps the achievable grade, and no amount of tutoring lifts a result above the ceiling of the paper sat. Schools make this call in Year 10 or early Year 11 on the basis of mock performance, and it is reversible for a while and then it is not. A parent who finds out in March that their child was entered for the capped tier has lost the chance to argue the case.

Those two answers shape everything a tutor should do. Extended and Higher tier candidates need algebraic fluency, functions, transformations of graphs and the harder trigonometry; they also need to handle multi-step problems where the method carries the marks. Core and Foundation candidates need accuracy, number work and the confidence to finish a paper, and they lose marks to carelessness far more often than to missing content. The two students need almost opposite sessions.

Al Quoz 4 adds its own constraint, which is time rather than content. This is a residential pocket off Al Khail Road with no secondary school inside it, so children travel out to Al Barsha, Al Quoz 1 and the central corridor and come home by bus somewhere between 3.50pm and 4.20pm. Year 11 students are carrying nine or ten subjects and the evening fills fast. A tutoring plan that ignores the arrival time will be a plan that gets cancelled in week four of a term.

IB Gram teaches this online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service and we would rather say so on the page than in an email after you have booked. What the online model buys an Al Quoz 4 family is a tutor chosen by syllabus code and tier rather than by driving distance, and a 6pm start that is not at the mercy of the Al Khail Road traffic at 5.40pm.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-quoz-4.subjectsIntro: IGCSE mathematics is one subject on a timetable and several distinct skills under examination. These are the topic areas where Al Quoz 4 students most often need a specialist, with what each one actually demands.

subjects.name: Algebra and manipulation
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging, indices and surds. The gatekeeper topic: weakness here shows up as poor marks in every other topic, because almost every multi-step question passes through an algebraic step on the way to the answer.

subjects.name: Functions and graph transformations
subjects.description: Domain, range, inverse and composite functions, and the translation, reflection and stretch of graphs. Absent from the Core tier, and the single most common reason an Extended candidate scores well below their class impression.

subjects.name: Trigonometry beyond right angles
subjects.description: Sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle, bearings and three-dimensional problems. Students who learned SOHCAHTOA securely often freeze when the triangle is not right-angled, and the recovery is a matter of two or three worked session hours.

subjects.name: Probability and set notation
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, conditional probability and Venn notation. Marks are usually lost not to the probability but to the reading: students miss the words without replacement and solve a different question correctly.

subjects.name: Statistics and data presentation
subjects.description: Cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal intervals, box plots and averages from grouped data. Histograms with unequal class widths are the reliable mark-shedder, because frequency density is a concept rather than a formula to recall.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, vector geometry proofs and combined transformations. The proof-style questions are worth full marks and routinely left blank, which makes them the cheapest marks on the Extended paper to recover.

subjects.name: Number, ratio and percentages
subjects.description: Reverse percentages, compound interest, standard form, bounds and ratio problems. The highest-volume topic on the Core paper and the one where accuracy, not understanding, decides the grade.

subjects.name: Mensuration and circle work
subjects.description: Arcs, sectors, surface area and volume of compound solids, and at Extended the circle theorems. Circle theorems are learnable in a fortnight and are worth a grade boundary on their own to a borderline candidate.

subjects.name: Calculator technique
subjects.description: A skill rather than a topic. Fraction entry, stored answers, statistical modes and degree settings decide whether a student finishes the paper. Ten minutes per session on the model your child will actually take into the hall is time well spent.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 or Edexcel 4MA1: find out which before you book
paragraphs: Ask the school, or look at the statement of entry. Dubai British-curriculum schools split between Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel, and the choice is made by the school, not the family. Cambridge International Mathematics is syllabus 0580, with a Core tier sitting Papers 1 and 3 and an Extended tier sitting Papers 2 and 4. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A is 4MA1, with Foundation and Higher tiers each sitting two papers. Edexcel also runs Specification B, which some schools use for stronger cohorts.

What differs in practice is the style of question rather than the content list, and the style is what a student has to be trained for. Cambridge Extended Paper 4 runs long multi-part structured questions where later parts depend on earlier ones, so an early error is expensive. Edexcel Higher papers tend to present a greater number of shorter items, which rewards pace and punishes a student who dwells. A tutor who has taught both will tell you which pattern your child is losing marks to.

There is also a practical difference in past-paper supply. A student preparing for 0580 who works through 4MA1 papers will be practising similar mathematics in an unfamiliar format, and the time cost of that mismatch is real in the eight weeks before a session. Matching the practice material to the entry code is basic and frequently not done, usually because nobody established the code at the start.

We do not host or supply syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes for either board. They belong to Cambridge International and Pearson, your child's school has legitimate access, and the boards publish specifications on their own sites. A tutor works from them; a tutoring page that offers them as downloads is handing you somebody else's copyright.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that sets the grade ceiling
paragraphs: This is the part of IGCSE mathematics that parents in Al Quoz 4 most often discover too late. The lower tier of either board caps the grade available. A Cambridge Core entry cannot reach the top grades, and a Pearson Foundation entry has its own ceiling. The cap is a property of the paper, not of the candidate, so a student who performs superbly on a capped paper still receives a capped result. Tutoring cannot lift a grade above the ceiling of the paper sat.

Schools make the entry decision on evidence, usually Year 10 mock performance and classwork, and they are generally right. Where they are sometimes wrong is with a student whose difficulty is confidence or examination technique rather than content, because that student looks like a Core candidate in October and could be an Extended candidate by March with the right work. The conversation to have with the school is a specific one: what would my child need to show, and by when, for the Extended entry to stay open.

The honest counterweight is that an inappropriate Extended entry is also damaging. A student placed on the harder paper who cannot access the back half of it will come out of the examination with fewer marks and less confidence than they would have had on the tier that suited them, and the grade can be worse in absolute terms. The decision is about the right fit, not about ambition, and a tutor who tells you to push for Extended regardless is not giving advice.

For a family in Al Quoz 4 the practical timeline is this. Have the diagnostic done in the autumn of Year 10, not Year 11. The topics that separate the tiers, functions, graph transformations, the sine and cosine rules, vectors and circle theorems, take months rather than weeks to build. By February of Year 11 the entry has usually been made and the question has changed from which tier to how many marks.

sections.heading: What a grade on the certificate actually tells you
paragraphs: Both boards report on a nine-to-one numeric scale for International GCSE, where grade 9 is the highest, and older certificates and some subjects still carry the A star to G letters. Parents moving to Dubai from a system that used letters, or from India, reasonably want a translation, and the honest answer is that the two scales do not map cleanly onto each other because the boundaries were redrawn when the scale changed. Grade 4 is generally treated as a standard pass and grade 5 as a strong pass, and that is about as far as a safe generalisation goes.

Grade boundaries move between series. They are set after the papers are marked, against the difficulty of that particular paper and the performance of that cohort, which is why a student who scored sixty-two marks in one series and sixty-two in another can receive different grades. Anyone telling you the mark needed for a grade 7 next series is guessing. The boards publish the boundaries after each series and the school has them; we do not reproduce them here because they are the boards' material.

For UAE families there is a second scale that matters more than the first, and it is the Ministry of Education equivalency threshold. For the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. A grade 3 in mathematics therefore clears the equivalency bar while being nowhere near enough for A Level Mathematics. Those are two different questions and they get confused constantly.

The practical reading for a parent is to stop asking what grade is good and start asking what the grade is for. If the target is equivalency, the bar is low and the subject count matters. If the target is A Level Mathematics or IB Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, the school's own threshold is the number to ask about, and it will be well above the equivalency floor.

sections.heading: The Al Quoz 4 weeknight: Year 10 against Year 11
paragraphs: The two years need different slots, and families usually plan them the same way. A Year 10 student has lighter evening work and more tolerance for a session at 5.30pm. A Year 11 student in the autumn term is carrying coursework in other subjects, mock preparation and nine or ten subject homeworks, and a 5.30pm maths session competes with all of it. Pushing the Year 11 slot later, to 6.30pm or 7pm, after some homework is cleared, produces a student who can actually use the hour.

Door times in Al Quoz 4 run from about 3.30pm for a car journey from Al Quoz 1 to about 4.20pm for a bus from Al Barsha, with the variation driven by stop order rather than distance. Activity days push that to 5.30pm. None of this is unusual for Dubai and all of it is invisible to a booking page that offers a 4pm slot. The useful planning move is to pick the slot that works in a busy week in November, not the one that works in a quiet week in September.

Session length is worth deciding deliberately too. Sixty minutes is right for weekly term-time work. Ninety minutes is right in a pre-mock block where timed paper work needs a full sitting plus review, and is too long for a tired Year 11 on a Tuesday. Two shorter sessions in a week beat one long one for a student who is losing marks to accuracy rather than knowledge, because the drilling needs frequency.

A note on siblings, since many Al Quoz 4 households have two or three children in the same school run. One-to-one means one student in the session; two children cannot share an hour. What works is sharing an evening, with consecutive slots at 6pm and 7.15pm, which keeps the household pattern intact and means only one evening a week is given over to tutoring.

sections.heading: The June and November series, counted backwards
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes a calendar, which is odd, because the calendar is what a parent is actually trying to plan against. Two points of fact first. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only, so a Dubai parent who reads a page quoting a late-November entry deadline for a February examination is reading advice written for another country.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. For the most recent completed cycles: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those dates are stated because they are backward-looking and checkable. For a future series, name the month and check the live timetable, because the boards publish provisional timetables that get revised.

There is one administrative trap worth knowing. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and the timetable differs by zone. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Your child's school knows its zone; a parent working from a timetable found online may not be looking at the right one.

Counted backwards from any series, the shape of the year is stable even though the dates are not. Entries close months before the papers. Mocks sit a term before. Any decision about tier has to be made before the entry closes. And a resit route exists through the following series, which is why a disappointing June is a setback rather than an ending.

sections.heading: Five subjects at grade E or 3: the equivalency rule parents get wrong
paragraphs: If your child will apply to a UAE university or needs a UAE certificate equivalency, the Ministry of Education sets out what the British track must show. Students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

That last clause is where a ranking competitor page in this market gets it wrong, stating that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. The sourced rule is five, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from the count rather than added to it. A parent planning a subject set on the wrong number will either over-enter, at real cost per entry, or mis-plan the timetable. The number to work from is five.

For the American track the requirements are different: English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL internet-based test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics through at least 450 in the SAT Math test. No IB points threshold appears in the source, so we do not publish one; an IB family should check moe.gov.ae or the emirate attestation authority directly rather than trusting a figure on a tutoring page.

Two honest caveats. Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs and we do not perform, guarantee or expedite any part of it, and tutoring is not required for it. What a tutor can do is make sure mathematics is not the subject that falls below the threshold, which for a struggling Core candidate is a genuinely useful and quite modest goal.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE maths marks actually disappear
paragraphs: Four patterns account for most of the gap between what a student knows and what the paper awards. The first is unfinished papers. A Core or Foundation candidate who leaves the last page blank has usually not run out of ability but out of minutes, often because the first few questions were done too carefully. Timed practice with a visible clock fixes this faster than any amount of content teaching, and it is measurable from one week to the next.

The second is accuracy. Rounding too early, dropping a unit, mis-transcribing a figure from the calculator, answering in centimetres when the question asked for metres. Each costs one mark and together they can cost a grade boundary. The correction is a routine rather than a lesson: a fixed thirty-second check at the end of each question, practised until it is automatic.

The third is the reading of the question. Without replacement in a probability question, correct to three significant figures, give your answer in terms of pi, hence rather than find. Students solve a nearby question correctly and receive nothing. A tutor who makes a student underline the instruction before working will see this shift within a fortnight. The fourth, specific to Extended and Higher, is the topics that only appear on that tier: graph transformations, circle theorems, vector proofs, the sine and cosine rules in three dimensions. These are left blank rather than attempted badly, which means they are pure recoverable marks.

Circle theorems deserve a separate mention because of the arithmetic of it. They are a bounded, learnable set, they appear reliably, and a borderline Extended candidate who masters them in a fortnight can move a grade on that alone. Any tutor who has taught the tier will go there first, and if they do not, ask why.

sections.heading: After IGCSE maths: which doors the grade opens
paragraphs: The IGCSE maths grade is a branching point at sixteen rather than a final result, and schools near Al Quoz 4 offer both A Level and the IB Diploma afterwards, which means the branch is real. A strong Extended or Higher grade keeps A Level Mathematics and IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches open at Higher Level. A middling grade points toward IB Applications and Interpretation, A Level subjects without a heavy mathematical load, or Mathematics at Standard Level.

Thresholds are set by schools, not nationally, and they vary. Some sixth forms require a grade 7 at Extended for A Level Mathematics and some accept a 6 with conditions. Some IB schools require a 6 for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. The only reliable version of this information is your own school's published entry criteria, and the question is worth asking in Year 10 rather than after results.

The transition itself is where students are caught out. A Year 11 candidate who achieved a good grade through procedural fluency meets A Level or Diploma mathematics and finds that the questions ask for justification, proof and sustained multi-step reasoning. Schools in Dubai see this every autumn in Year 12. The gap is not the content; it is that nobody has asked these students to explain why a method works. Six to eight weeks of bridging work over the summer closes most of it, and it is cheap compared with repairing a failing first term.

If the plan is IB Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, the specific preparation is algebraic manipulation without a calculator, because Paper 1 is non-calculator and the hand fluency that IGCSE never demanded becomes the binding constraint. If the plan is A Level, the pure algebra and trigonometry of the first term is the same problem by a different name.

faqs.question: Which maths syllabus code is my child entered for, and why does it matter?
faqs.answer: It is on the statement of entry the school issues, and the exams officer will confirm it in one email. The school chooses the board, not the family, and schools in the same Dubai community often differ. The code matters because it determines which past papers are worth practising: a 0580 candidate working through 4MA1 papers is doing similar mathematics in an unfamiliar format, and that mismatch costs real time in the last eight weeks before a series. Establish the code before any tutoring plan is written.

faqs.question: Can tutoring get my child a grade 8 if they are entered for the Core tier?
faqs.answer: No, and anyone who says otherwise is misleading you. The lower tier of either board carries a grade ceiling that is a property of the paper, not the candidate. A student who performs outstandingly on a capped paper still receives a capped grade. What tutoring can do is maximise the result within the tier, and more usefully, if there is still time, build the case for an Extended or Higher entry. That case has to be made in Year 10 or very early in Year 11, because the entry closes months before the examinations.

faqs.question: What time does an IGCSE maths session work for a Year 11 student in Al Quoz 4?
faqs.answer: Usually 6.30pm. The bus from the Al Barsha cluster reaches Al Quoz 4 between 3.50pm and 4.20pm, and a Year 11 student in the autumn term is carrying nine or ten subject homeworks plus mock preparation. A session at 5.30pm competes with all of that and gets cancelled by November. Clearing some homework first and starting at 6.30pm produces an hour the student can use. Online delivery makes that start time reliable because nobody is driving across Al Khail Road at 6.15pm to reach you.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying AED 250 an hour rather than AED 50 for IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what is wrong. A Core tier candidate who needs accuracy drilling and timed practice can get real value from a budget tutor at the AED 33 to 65 band that Tutopiya and EdFlik advertise. An Extended candidate who cannot do graph transformations needs somebody who has taught that tier, and those sit at AED 150 to 300 online, with specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. Pay for specialism where the problem is specific content, and for hours where the problem is practice volume.

faqs.question: When are the IGCSE maths exams in Dubai, and is there a February series?
faqs.answer: There is no February series for UAE candidates. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series, and the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Any page offering a Dubai parent a February examination window or a late-November entry deadline for it has copied advice written for India. Check the live official timetable through your child's school, and note that Cambridge timetables differ by administrative zone.

faqs.question: My child failed maths in the June series. What does the resit actually involve?
faqs.answer: A retake in the following November series, entered through the school or a private centre, with results reaching students in January. The useful work between results and the examination is not a full re-teach. It starts from the paper that was sat, identifies whether the loss was pacing, accuracy, question-reading or specific topics, and targets that. Two timed mocks inside the block are worth more than ten topic lessons. Plan the block as a fixed number of sessions ending on a date, so the cost is known from the start.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does my child need for a UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five. The Ministry of Education requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. A page in this market states six, which is wrong and will cost a family in unnecessary entries or a misplanned timetable. Equivalency also requires one A Level at grade E or better, or two AS-Levels at the same grade. Verify on moe.gov.ae; IB Gram does not perform or expedite any part of the process.

faqs.question: Does my child's maths tutor need a UAE permit if the lessons are online?
faqs.answer: Anyone providing private tuition in the UAE needs the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued by MoHRE. It is free of charge and granted for two years, and eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no fine schedule is published. If you hire independently, ask to see the permit and check the name matches the person teaching.

faqs.question: Which schools near Al Quoz 4 enter students for IGCSE mathematics?
faqs.answer: The British-curriculum schools in Al Barsha, Al Quoz and along the central corridor that Al Quoz 4 children travel to, including Kings' School Al Barsha, Dubai American Academy, Nord Anglia International School Dubai, GEMS Our Own Indian School in Al Quoz, Safa British School and Jumeirah College. Entry boards differ school by school, so two children on the same bus can sit different syllabuses. Dubai had 227 private schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25. faqs.question: Can a tutor fix circle theorems in a few weeks before the exam?
faqs.answer: Circle theorems are one of the genuinely good answers to a short timescale. They are a bounded, learnable set, they appear reliably on Extended and Higher papers, and borderline candidates routinely leave them blank rather than attempting them badly. A fortnight of focused work can move a grade on that alone. The same arithmetic applies to vector geometry proofs. A tutor who has taught the tier will go to those topics first in a short block, because they are the cheapest recoverable marks on the paper.

faqs.question: Will sessions move during Ramadan, and how does that work?
faqs.answer: School days shorten during Ramadan, so the Al Quoz 4 door time comes forward and the whole evening changes shape. Families generally either pull the session into the early afternoon or move it after Iftar, and both are straightforward on video in a way they would not be with a tutor travelling across the city at Iftar. Tell us which pattern your household keeps and the slot is rebuilt for the month rather than paused. For a Year 11 candidate, plan for the Ramadan weeks to be lighter and move revision earlier.

faqs.question: Should we use a tuition centre group class instead of one-to-one?
faqs.answer: A group class is the cheapest option per head and suits a student whose problem is practice volume and motivation rather than a specific gap. It works badly for the student who needs the one topic they cannot do explained three different ways, because the class moves at the scheme's pace. The honest test: if you can name the topic that is wrong, buy one-to-one time on it. If you cannot name anything beyond the grade, a structured group programme plus timed practice at home may be enough to start.

faqs.question: How does a tutor handle calculator technique over video?
faqs.answer: Your child keeps the handheld model they will take into the examination, and the tutor shares the matching emulator or software on screen so every keystroke is visible at a readable size. For fraction entry, stored answers, statistical modes and degree settings, this is clearer than sitting beside someone, because the menu path is projected rather than glimpsed. Ten minutes of each session on the student's own model is time well spent: a competent candidate who navigates slowly will not finish the paper, and that alone can cost a grade.

faqs.question: What does the trial IGCSE maths lesson cover, and is payment needed?
faqs.answer: Forty-five minutes over live video, no card details collected and no obligation. The tutor works from a past-paper question in your child's actual syllabus code and tier, then watches how the student approaches it rather than only whether the answer is right. Afterwards you get a plain note naming the three things the tutor would work on first. The trial exists to test the match, so if the pace or the style is wrong for your child, say so and we propose a different tutor.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 9. Is it too early to think about IGCSE maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: Year 9 is arguably the highest-value point in the whole sequence, because this is when the tier decision is quietly being made. The topics that decide whether Extended or Higher is viable are algebraic fluency, rearrangement, indices and negative numbers, and they are built in Years 8 and 9. Two short sessions a month aimed narrowly at manipulation is modest, cheap and changes what is possible in Year 11. Remediation in Year 11, by contrast, is expensive and runs into an entry deadline that has already closed.

intro.heading: Start with the monthly number, not the hourly rate
paragraphs: An hourly rate tells an Al Qusais family almost nothing, because nobody buys one hour. What a household actually commits to is a line in the monthly budget running from October to the June series, and that is the number worth comparing. Bestimate's Dubai rate table, read in October 2026, puts a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month for budget tutoring, AED 600 to 1,200 a month mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000-plus a month for specialist exam-year support. Published monthly packages in the market sit alongside those estimates: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Those two in-home and online monthly figures are the clearest signal in the whole Dubai tutoring market. Roughly double the money buys half the sessions, and the difference is not teaching quality - it is a car. An independent tutor coming into Al Qusais from Barsha or the Marina at 16:30 is absorbing forty to seventy minutes each way on Al Ittihad Road and Damascus Street, and that time is billed inside the fee whether anybody itemises it or not. Al Qusais sits awkwardly for this: close to the Sharjah boundary, fed by the evening peak, and far from where most freelance tutors advertise.

The second thing worth knowing before any money is spent is that the biggest financial decision in IGCSE maths is not which tutor you hire. It is which tier your child was entered for. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 runs a Core tier capped at grade C and an Extended tier reaching A*, and the school makes that entry decision, usually in Year 10. A student wrongly parked on Core cannot be tutored to an A, however many hours are bought, because the paper does not contain the marks. A student stretched onto Extended too early can lose a safe C chasing a B.

The third is that some of the most popular purchases in this market do not move a grade. Group revision classes sold by the term, past-paper bundles, generic weekly sessions with no marking, and tutoring that starts in April. Each has a reason parents buy it and a reason it underperforms, and both are set out on this page with the cheaper alternative beside them. The intention is not to talk anybody out of spending money - it is to make sure the money buys marks rather than reassurance.

IB Gram delivers IGCSE maths tuition to UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For an Al Qusais family the practical effect is that the travel premium disappears from the price, the tutor is chosen by syllabus code rather than by driving distance, and a 16:00 Tuesday slot does not depend on traffic between Al Nahda Road and wherever the tutor happens to live.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-qusais.subjectsIntro: Families search for an IGCSE maths tutor in Al Qusais and then describe something far more specific once a tutor is on the call. These are the requests that come up most from this part of Dubai, with the cost of fixing each one.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging, solving simultaneous and quadratic equations. The highest-value topic in the specification because it appears inside questions about everything else. Cheap to fix with short daily drills and expensive to leave alone, since every later topic inherits the errors.

subjects.name: The non-calculator paper
subjects.description: Cambridge now sets a non-calculator written paper on both tiers, which changed what Year 10 needs to practise. Fractions, percentages, surds, index laws and standard-form arithmetic done by hand. Students taught with a calculator permanently available lose straightforward marks here and recover them quickly once drilled.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and bearings
subjects.description: Sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle, three-dimensional problems and bearings. Marks are lost in the setup rather than the trigonometry - a mislabelled diagram or a bearing measured from the wrong north line costs the whole question even when the calculation is correct.

subjects.name: Graphs, transformations and functions
subjects.description: Sketching quadratics, cubics and reciprocals, reading solutions from a graph, function notation, composite and inverse functions. The common failure is sketching features that were not asked for while omitting the intercepts and asymptotes that carry the marks.

subjects.name: Probability and statistics
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, Venn diagrams, cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal class widths and the interpretation sentences at the end. The histogram question is the single most reliably mishandled item on either board, because frequency density is taught once and tested in an unfamiliar form.

subjects.name: Mensuration and compound measures
subjects.description: Surface area and volume of composite solids, similar shapes with area and volume scale factors, speed, density and pressure. The scale-factor rules are two lines of theory and worth several marks a paper, which makes them one of the best hours a tutor can spend.

subjects.name: Method marks and exam technique
subjects.description: Writing a method line, keeping unrounded values in the calculator, answering in the units asked, and reading the command word. Students arriving from systems that reward only the final answer lose marks across every paper to this, and it is the cheapest thing on the whole list to repair.

subjects.levels: Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher
subjects.description: A single marked paper at each tier, before the school's entry deadline, usually answers the question the family has been arguing about for a term. It costs one session and can change the grade ceiling for two years, which makes it the highest-return hour on this page.

sections.heading: What IGCSE maths tuition actually costs in Al Qusais, cheapest option first
paragraphs: Work upwards from the cheapest thing available, because that is how the options present themselves to a parent typing into Google. At the bottom of the Dubai market sit online platforms staffed largely by university students, with Tutopiya's published rates beginning around AED 33 to 52 an hour when read in October 2026 and EdFlik listing sessions from AED 45 to 65. That money buys a competent pair of eyes on a homework sheet. It does not generally buy someone who knows that Cambridge 0580 now sets a non-calculator paper on both tiers.

One step up, a qualified subject tutor working online is quoted across Dubai at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB tuition from AED 200. This is the band most Al Qusais families settle into for IGCSE maths, and it is usually the right one: the specification is well documented, the papers are public, and a good maths graduate who has taught the board can do this work. The premium band above - roughly AED 200 to 450 and beyond, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate putting specialist exam-year rates at AED 200 to 450-plus - is better justified at Diploma or A Level than at IGCSE.

In-home visits are the expensive end and the reason this page exists. Dubai in-home one-to-one is quoted between roughly AED 180 and 500 an hour inclusive of travel, with Bestimate's table showing AED 180 to 350 and independent tutors asking AED 200 to 500. At the top of the market BartyED published AED 650 for premium named tutors. Convert all of that into monthly commitments and the picture sharpens: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Every figure above was published by the provider named and read in October 2026. None of them is an IB Gram price, and we do not print one on these pages, because the honest quote depends on the tier, the number of weeks left and how much marking is involved. The free trial lesson exists so a family can judge a tutor before any fee is discussed; its only condition is that it is one lesson with one matched tutor.

sections.heading: Five purchases Al Qusais families make that rarely move an IGCSE maths grade
paragraphs: This is the part of the budget worth auditing before adding to it. The first is the term-length group revision class, sold cheaply per head and taught to the middle of the room. It works for a student who is close to a grade boundary and needs reminding; it does very little for a student whose problem is algebraic fluency, because that problem is individual and the class cannot stop for it. Three one-to-one diagnostic hours usually beat a term of group sessions for the same money.

The second is the past-paper bundle. Past papers are free from the board's own site and from most schools, so paying for a collection buys convenience rather than content. What actually has value is marking - a paper marked against the published scheme by someone who explains why a method line earned nothing. A hundred unmarked papers teach a student their own bad habits more thoroughly.

The third is the open-ended weekly session with no written output. If nobody can say at the end of a month which three topics were fixed and what the marked evidence was, the money bought company rather than progress. Insist on a short written list after the diagnostic session and a tick against it monthly. This costs a tutor nothing and changes how the hour is used.

The fourth is tutoring that starts in April for a June series. Eight weeks is enough to repair technique and close a few named gaps; it is not enough to build two years of algebra, and a provider who implies otherwise is selling hope. The fifth is paying for the wrong tier. A student entered on Cambridge Core cannot reach a B, so money spent chasing one is wasted until the entry itself is revisited with the school.

sections.heading: The tier decision: Cambridge 0580 Core against Extended, in money terms
paragraphs: No tutoring decision in IGCSE maths matters as much as the tier, and it is the one most parents in Al Qusais discover late. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 is examined at two tiers. Core is graded C to G and sits a non-calculator written paper and a calculator written paper covering the core content. Extended is graded A* to E and sits its own non-calculator and calculator papers on the full content, including the harder algebra, trigonometry, functions and calculus-adjacent topics that a Diploma or A Level course later assumes.

The financial consequence is blunt. On Core, grade C is the ceiling. A family spending AED 1,200 a month for eight months on a Core candidate in pursuit of a B is buying something the examination cannot deliver. On Extended, the floor is lower - a student out of their depth can score an E or ungraded where Core might have secured a solid C - so pushing a borderline student up a tier carries its own cost. Both errors are expensive and both are avoidable with one marked paper at each tier before the entry closes.

Pearson handles the same problem differently. The International GCSE in Mathematics Specification A, code 4MA1, is tiered Foundation and Higher, with Foundation reaching grade 5 and Higher running 9 to 4, and a calculator permitted on both of its two-hour papers. A student who would be capped at C on Cambridge Core might reach a 5 on Pearson Foundation, which maps differently against sixth-form entry requirements. Which board your child's school uses is therefore part of the tier conversation, not a separate one.

Practically: ask the head of mathematics, in writing, which tier your child is provisionally entered for, when the entry becomes final, and what evidence the decision rests on. Then buy one diagnostic session at the tier above and one at the tier below if there is genuine doubt. That is two hours of tutoring to settle a decision that governs two years of spending.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson: the differences that change what you pay for
paragraphs: Al Qusais schools do not all use the same board, and a tutor who teaches one fluently can still cost a family marks on the other. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is syllabus 0580, with the Core and Extended tiers described above and a non-calculator paper now set on both. Cambridge also publishes Additional Mathematics and International Mathematics variants that some schools in this part of Dubai run alongside or instead of 0580, so the code on the timetable is worth checking rather than assuming.

Pearson's International GCSE in Mathematics Specification A is 4MA1, tiered Foundation and Higher, with two papers of two hours each and a calculator permitted throughout. Specification B is 4MB1, structured differently with a shorter first paper and a longer second. The practical difference for a student is the absence of a non-calculator paper on 4MA1 and the presence of one on 0580 - which means the same child, on the same content, needs a different practice regime depending on which board their school entered them for.

Session timing differs too, and this is where dates matter to a family planning spending. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, and the February and March series is offered to India only, so no Al Qusais parent should be planning around a March exam. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November; the November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

Cambridge also allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. That is a school administrative matter rather than a tutoring one, but it is the kind of detail worth knowing exists. Always work from the live official timetable on the board's own site rather than from a date restated anywhere else, including here.

sections.heading: Twelve weeks, costed three ways for an Al Qusais household
paragraphs: Abstract bands are hard to budget against, so here are three plans a family in this neighbourhood might actually run between the first mock and the June series, each built from the published market rates above rather than from an IB Gram quote. The point of setting them side by side is that the most expensive plan is not always the one that moves the grade furthest, and the cheapest is not always false economy.

The lean plan is one diagnostic session followed by one weekly hour for eleven weeks at mid-market online rates, with the student doing a marked past paper every fortnight in their own time. At roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour that lands in the region of AED 1,800 to 3,600 across the block. It suits a student sitting at a 5 or 6 whose problem is three identifiable topics and whose homework actually gets done.

The focused plan is one diagnostic session followed by two hours a week for ten weeks, aimed at a written list and with every session opening on the previous week's marked work. At the same hourly band that is roughly AED 3,000 to 6,000. This is the plan we would recommend for most students who are two grades off where they need to be, because the second weekly hour is what converts marking into correction.

The in-home plan is four two-hour visits a month at the packaged market figure of AED 1,599 to 1,799, which across three months reaches roughly AED 4,800 to 5,400 for twenty-four contact hours. Compare that with the focused plan's twenty hours at the lower end of the online band and the structural point becomes visible: in-home buys fewer, longer, less frequent sessions for more money, and frequency is what repairs algebra. A family that genuinely needs someone physically present should buy it with that trade-off in view rather than by accident.

sections.heading: Checking a tutor is permitted to teach, and what to ask before paying
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permit-regulated and a parent is entitled to ask about it. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

Two things follow from that. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published - so a figure circulating online as the penalty should be treated as unverified. A tutor who cannot answer the permit question, or who becomes evasive about it, has told you something useful for free. Ask ours the same question.

There is a second boundary worth knowing. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct has been reported as barring the same thing. Treat that as press-reported and verify against the current policy document, but the principle is sound anywhere in the Emirates: your child's own classroom teacher is the wrong person to pay privately, whatever the convenience.

The rest of the checklist is about competence rather than legality. Which syllabus code do you teach - 0580, 4MA1 or 4MB1? Which tier does my child's current work sit in and what is the evidence? Will you mark a paper against the published scheme and send me the list? What happens in week four if nothing has shifted? A tutor with real answers to those four questions is worth the mid-market rate. One without them is not worth the budget rate.

sections.heading: What IB Gram actually sells an Al Qusais family, and what it does not
paragraphs: We match an IGCSE maths tutor to the syllabus code and tier your child sits, and the lesson runs one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The first lesson is a free trial with the matched tutor - one lesson, with the fee discussed afterwards rather than before. There is no office, centre or branch in the Emirates, no tutor is sent to a UAE address, and home visits are a service we run only in India. All of that is stated the same way on every UAE page on this site, which is the only way a reader can check it.

We hold no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson, and nothing on this page should be read as implying one. Where a regulator is named here it is to explain what that body does. KHDA, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, inspects schools - not tutors - and its published school ratings belong to the school as a whole rather than to a mathematics department.

We publish no success rate, no star rating, no student headcount and no average grade improvement. Those numbers appear on competing pages in this search result, sometimes contradicting themselves within one page, and none of them can be produced on request. The figures we do publish on this page are other people's prices, attributed and dated, plus Dubai's private-school market size from the emirate's own media office: 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 curricula, with UK curriculum at 37%, Indian at 26%, US at 14% and International Baccalaureate at 7%.

One more piece of context for a budget conversation. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. School fees are therefore flat for the year ahead, which makes the tutoring line the part of an Al Qusais education budget that a family still fully controls - and the reason it is worth spending deliberately rather than reactively.
