faqs.question: How much should an Al Qusais family budget for IGCSE maths tutoring in total?
faqs.answer: Think in blocks rather than hours. Bestimate's Dubai estimates for a weekly one-hour session run roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at budget level and AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, read in October 2026. A realistic twelve-week run with a diagnostic and two hours a week at mid-market online rates lands somewhere between AED 3,000 and 6,000 in total. A packaged online bundle seen in the market sits around AED 799 a month for eight sessions. Those are other providers' published figures, not ours; we quote against the tier and the weeks remaining.

faqs.question: Why is in-home IGCSE maths tutoring in Al Qusais quoted so much higher than online?
faqs.answer: Because the travel is inside the fee. Published Dubai in-home rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of the tutor's round trip, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor online. Al Qusais sits near the Sharjah boundary and takes the full force of the Al Ittihad Road evening peak, so a tutor crossing from New Dubai is absorbing forty to seventy minutes each way. The visible result in monthly packages is around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits against about AED 799 for eight online sessions.

faqs.question: My child is entered for Cambridge Core. Can tutoring get them a B?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider who says otherwise is misleading you. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Core is graded C to G, so grade C is the ceiling that the papers can produce. If a B or above is needed for a sixth-form place, the conversation to have is with the head of mathematics about the Extended entry, not with a tutor about more hours. What tutoring can do before the entry is final is provide evidence: one marked Extended paper usually tells a school more than a term of classroom impressions.

faqs.question: Does Cambridge 0580 really have a non-calculator paper now?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it changed what Al Qusais students need to practise. Both Cambridge tiers now sit a non-calculator written paper alongside a calculator one, which means hand arithmetic, fractions, percentages, index laws and standard form are examined directly rather than delegated to a device. Students taught with a calculator always available lose straightforward marks to this and recover them quickly with short daily drills. Pearson's 4MA1, by contrast, permits a calculator on both of its papers - so the same child needs a different practice regime depending on which board their school uses.

faqs.question: Is a group IGCSE maths class in Dubai better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the problem. A group class is good value for a student who is close to a grade boundary and needs structured reminding across the whole syllabus, and it is poor value for a student whose issue is algebraic fluency, because the class cannot stop for one person's gap. For the price of a term of group sessions a family can usually buy two or three marked one-to-one diagnostics, which is more likely to identify what is actually wrong. Buy the group class second, after you know the diagnosis.

faqs.question: When is the cheapest time to spend money on IGCSE maths for my child?
faqs.answer: Year 9 and the first half of Year 10, which is almost never when families do it. Algebraic fluency, index laws, rearranging formulae and the habit of writing a method line are cheap to build early and expensive to retrofit in Year 11. Most of the tutoring budget in this neighbourhood is spent after the first Year 11 mock has made the problem visible, at which point the same money buys exam technique rather than foundations. If you are reading this with a Year 9 student, a single diagnostic now is the highest-return purchase available.

faqs.question: What should I ask an IGCSE maths tutor in Dubai before I pay anything?
faqs.answer: Four questions. Which syllabus code do you teach - 0580, 4MA1 or 4MB1? Which tier does my child's current work sit in, and what is the evidence for that? Will you mark a past paper against the published scheme and send me a written list of weaknesses? What happens in week four if nothing has shifted? Then one more: do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit? It is granted free of charge for two years, so there is no cost reason for a working tutor not to have one.

faqs.question: Which exam series will my child in Al Qusais actually sit?
faqs.answer: For Cambridge candidates in the UAE, the June series with November available as a resit route. The February and March series is offered to India only, so no Dubai family should be planning around a March exam date. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November; its November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Work from the board's live official timetable rather than any restated date.

faqs.question: How many hours of IGCSE maths tutoring does a grade actually take?
faqs.answer: There is no honest universal number, but there is an honest structure. Moving from a 5 to a 6 or 7 on a diagnosed list of three topics typically takes a block of twelve to twenty contact hours spread across eight to twelve weeks, because frequency matters more than total length - the gap between the lesson and the homework it was meant to fix is what decides whether anything sticks. Moving two grades from a low base takes longer and starting in April does not shorten it. No tutor can promise a particular grade for a particular number of hours, and a quote framed that way is not one to accept.

faqs.question: Can you help if my child's school uses a board your tutor does not know?
faqs.answer: We match on the code rather than guess. If your child sits Cambridge Additional Mathematics, Cambridge International Mathematics or Pearson Specification B rather than the common 0580 or 4MA1 route, say so in the first message and we look for a tutor who has taught that specification. If nobody suitable is free in your preferred window, you are told that at the match stage with the alternatives and a date, rather than after a payment. A disclosed wait costs an Al Qusais family less than a mismatched tutor.

faqs.question: With Dubai school fees held flat, how should an Al Qusais family rebalance the tutoring line?
faqs.answer: It changes the arithmetic of the household budget rather than the tutoring decision itself. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. With the largest line in an education budget flat for the year, the tutoring line is the part a family still controls - which is an argument for spending it deliberately, on a diagnosed list with written output, rather than reactively after a disappointing mock.

faqs.question: Are online IGCSE maths lessons effective for a student who dislikes screens?
faqs.answer: For maths the honest answer is usually yes, because the subject is written and the format carries written work well. A shared whiteboard, the student's own page photographed and annotated live, and screen-shared papers reproduce the part of a lesson that matters: watching working appear line by line and stopping at the line where it goes wrong. The variable that decides it is the tutor's habit of asking rather than telling. Use the free trial lesson to check whether your child talks for a reasonable share of the hour.

faqs.question: What does a diagnostic session for IGCSE maths actually produce?
faqs.answer: A past paper or a substantial section of one, sat under something close to timed conditions, marked against the published scheme, and turned into a written list of three to six named weaknesses with the marks lost attached to each. It will usually also give a view on whether the current tier entry is right. You keep that document whether you continue with us, take it to another tutor, or decide no weekly tutoring is needed. It is the cheapest useful thing in this market and almost nobody sells it on its own.

faqs.question: Do you offer in-home IGCSE maths tutoring anywhere in Al Qusais or Al Nahda?
faqs.answer: No. Every UAE lesson we arrange is one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service we run only in India. We say that before a family spends anything rather than after. The Dubai market does supply in-home tutors at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel, and for some households having a person in the room is worth the premium. If that is your decision, make it knowing the trade-off is fewer, longer, less frequent sessions - and ask the tutor about their MoHRE permit.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-rashidiya.tutorsIntro: These are the IGCSE Mathematics specialists currently taking students from Al Rashidiya and the eastern suburbs. Tell us the arrival-home time and the syllabus code, and the shortlist comes back matched to both.

intro.heading: The lesson that works is the one that fits the bus timetable
paragraphs: Al Rashidiya is a compact residential district pressed between Dubai International Airport, Al Garhoud and Nad Al Hamar. It has mosques, villas, a metro station and no secondary school. Every Year 10 and Year 11 student living here travels out of the district to sit their IGCSEs, and the direction they travel is the single most useful fact a tutor can know about them before the first lesson.

Two directions dominate. North across Al Rebat Street into Al Garhoud is short, and on an ordinary day a student is home soon after the bell. East along Algeria Street and Tripoli Street into Mirdif, Al Mizhar and Al Warqa is a different proposition: those bus routes collect across several communities and can take the better part of forty minutes once school finishes, which puts a child through the door closer to 4.15pm than 3.15pm, tired, hungry and not ready to factorise anything.

This matters because of what a maths course is. IGCSE mathematics is a two-year drill. It rewards a weekly habit far more than it rewards intensity, and a weekly habit only forms if the slot is one the household can actually keep. The arrangements that fail in this corridor almost never fail because the tutor was poor. They fail because the lesson was booked for the earliest time that had ever worked, then missed every third week, then rescheduled, then quietly abandoned in November.

IB Gram's part of the solution is narrow and practical. Lessons are one to one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with no tutor travelling anywhere, so the only variable left in the schedule is your child. Home visits are a service offered only in India; there is no version of this where somebody has to leave Mirdif at 4pm to reach your gate by 4.30pm. That removes the half of the scheduling problem that nobody can control and leaves the half you can measure.

There is a second reason the timetable matters more in maths than in most subjects. Maths is cumulative in a way that history is not. A fortnight missed in October is not a fortnight of content to catch up; it is a hole that every subsequent topic sits on top of, and by December the student cannot tell you where the problem started. A weekly hour that reliably happens is therefore worth considerably more than a fortnightly hour that happens twice as hard, and the slot is the mechanism that makes the weekly hour reliable rather than aspirational.

The rest of this page is the timetable in detail: what time the day actually ends by school direction, the weekday rhythm a Year 11 maths plan needs, which syllabus code your child is entered for and why it changes the past papers they should be working from, what the Dubai market charges, and the exam calendar read backwards from the entry deadline that catches families out.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-rashidiya.programmesIntro: An IGCSE maths plan in this district is really three plans joined together: the years before the course, the examined two years, and whatever comes after. These are the stages we cover either side of Year 11.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary and Checkpoint maths
programmes.description: Where the arithmetic fluency IGCSE assumes is built or missed. Index laws, fractions without a calculator, rearranging a formula and negative numbers are the four things that later show up as an inexplicable Year 11 problem. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests sit in March, May and October, and a Checkpoint result is the earliest external read a parent gets.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving Al Rashidiya use Year 9 results to stream Year 10 into Core and Extended maths. That is the moment to ask which tier your child is heading for and on what evidence, because a Core placement quietly removes the route to A Level maths two years before anybody mentions it. Fixing a fluency gap here costs a fraction of fixing it in Year 11.

programmes.name: IGCSE and International GCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: The examined course: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 at Core or Extended, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1 at Foundation or Higher. Both cover number, algebra, geometry, trigonometry, statistics and probability, with the higher tier reaching functions, harder trigonometry and transformation work the lower tier never touches. Grading differs by board and the tier caps the available grade.
programmes.countryNote: UK-curriculum schools account for roughly thirty-seven per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment, which makes this the commonest exam a sixteen-year-old in this part of the city sits. It also means the local tuition market is full of general maths tutors. The code on the statement of entry is the fastest way to tell whether a tutor has taught the exam your child is actually sitting.

programmes.name: Additional Mathematics
programmes.description: Taken alongside the main course by students heading for A Level Maths or an engineering route, covering calculus, matrices and harder trigonometric identities ahead of time. It is the cleanest way to remove the step that otherwise lands in the first weeks of Year 12, and it is a sensible use of tutoring money for a student already comfortable at Extended.
programmes.countryNote: Not every school in the eastern suburbs offers it, and some offer it only to a top set. If your child is aiming at engineering or physical sciences and the school does not run it, a short tutoring block over the summer between Years 11 and 12 covers much of the same ground without the examination.

programmes.name: A Level and IB Diploma entry
programmes.description: What the maths grade is for. A Level Maths and Further Maths typically expect a grade 7 or above at IGCSE in the same subject, and IB Diploma schools set their own bars for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. The tier and the grade decided in Year 11 set the ceiling for both routes, which is why Year 10 is the cheapest year to intervene.
programmes.countryNote: For an Al Rashidiya family, both sixth-form routes are reachable within an ordinary school run, with Diploma provision in the Garhoud and Mirdif clusters and A Level provision across the eastern corridor. The grade profile that keeps both doors open is a strong Extended or Higher maths grade, and that is worth knowing in Year 10 rather than in results week.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-rashidiya.subjectsIntro: IGCSE maths is one subject with about eight separate places to lose marks. These are the areas Al Rashidiya families most often ask about, and what each one actually needs from a tutoring hour.

subjects.name: Number and the non-calculator skills
subjects.description: Index laws, standard form, surds at the higher tier, fractions and percentages handled without reaching for a calculator. The commonest hidden cause of a disappointing Year 11 grade is a Year 8 fluency gap here, and three sessions on it often achieve more than ten on anything else.

subjects.name: Algebra and manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, solving, rearranging and, at the higher tier, algebraic fractions and the quadratic formula applied under pressure. Marks go missing to sign errors and to method that cannot be followed, which is why writing the step down is drilled rather than discussed.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.description: Function notation, composite and inverse functions, transformations and curve sketching. This is the clearest dividing line between the tiers and the content A Level maths assumes on day one, so it is the area a Core-placed student aiming higher most needs.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.description: Angle reasoning, circle theorems, Pythagoras, the sine and cosine rules and three-dimensional trigonometry at the higher tier. The recurring loss is a reason not stated: a correct answer with no named theorem leaves the reasoning marks on the table.

subjects.name: Mensuration and compound measures
subjects.description: Area, volume, surface area, similar shapes, speed, density and pressure. Mechanical marks, routinely lost to unit errors and to formulas half remembered. Entirely fixable by practice, which makes it good value for a short block of sessions.

subjects.name: Statistics and data handling
subjects.description: Averages from grouped data, cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal widths and box plots. The histogram question is a reliable mark-loser because frequency density is a step students skip; the fix is six worked examples rather than a new explanation.

subjects.name: Probability
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, conditional probability and set notation at the higher tier. Students who can draw the tree still lose marks by multiplying along the wrong branch or forgetting that the second pick is from a smaller set, which is a careless-error pattern rather than a knowledge gap.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, vector geometry and proofs using position vectors, plus the four transformations with their full descriptions. The description is where marks go: a correct rotation without a stated centre and direction scores less than it should.

subjects.name: Problem-solving and multi-step questions
subjects.description: The questions at the end of the paper that combine three topics and no longer tell the student which method to use. These are practised rather than taught, and they are the main reason a student who knows every topic individually still lands a grade below expectation.

subjects.name: Examination technique and timing
subjects.description: Reading the mark allocation to decide how much to write, showing method so partial credit survives a wrong answer, and leaving a question rather than sinking ten minutes into it. A term of weekly practice on this moves marks without covering any new content.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics bridging
subjects.description: Early calculus, matrices and harder identities for students heading to A Level Maths or an engineering route. Best taken as a defined summer block rather than an ongoing arrangement, because it has a clear finish line and a visible deliverable.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory subjects alongside maths
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside IGCSE in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum. They occupy real timetable space, which matters when a family is working out how many tutoring hours a week a Year 11 student can actually absorb.

regions.name: Mirdif
regions.note: East along Algeria Street. Bus routes here collect across several communities before heading back, so forty minutes door to door is normal rather than unlucky. Plan for 5.30pm and the slot survives; plan for 4.30pm and it will not.

regions.name: Al Mizhar
regions.note: Beyond Mirdif, villa communities with the longest collection routes in this corridor. Families here and in Al Rashidiya frequently share a school and a bus, so the arrival-home time is effectively the same and sibling slots can be booked together.

regions.name: Al Warqa

sections.heading: What time does the school day actually end here?
paragraphs: Not when the bell rings. For an Al Rashidiya student the end of the day is the moment they are through the front door with a bag on the floor, and that time varies by the better part of an hour depending on which direction they travel and whether they ride a bus or get collected.

The Garhoud direction is the easy case. A short run north, a quick exit, and a student who can reasonably sit down at a desk by 4.15pm without being asked to do something unreasonable. The eastern routes are the hard case. A bus serving a Mirdif or Al Mizhar school collects across several communities and loops back through the Algeria Street traffic, and forty minutes is a normal outcome rather than a bad one. Add a walk from the drop-off point and a student is home at 4.15pm, not sitting down at 4.15pm.

Families underestimate the recovery time. A fifteen-year-old off a forty-minute bus in Dubai heat needs food and twenty minutes of nothing before they are any use at a multi-step algebra question. A lesson that starts before that has the first ten minutes eaten by the student arriving in the room rather than in the lesson, and over a term that is a measurable amount of paid time.

sections.heading: A Year 11 maths week that a household can actually keep
paragraphs: A weekly tutoring slot is one hour out of a week that already contains school homework, the mandatory UAE subjects, eight or nine other IGCSE courses and whatever a fifteen-year-old does to stay sane. Planning the hour without planning the week around it is why arrangements collapse.

The shape that holds is simple. The lesson sits on one weekday, chosen for the direction of the school run, and the practice it sets sits on a different day, early enough that it is done rather than remembered on the way to the next lesson. Twenty to thirty minutes of practice on two separate evenings beats ninety minutes the night before, because maths retention follows repetition rather than volume. Nothing is scheduled for the evening after a long sports fixture, because that evening is not real.

The UAE week has its own rhythm and it rewards paying attention. Sunday is the first school day, which makes a Sunday evening lesson the worst-performing slot in the week for most students; they are reassembling the term rather than learning anything. Thursday evening is better than it looks because the following morning is not a school morning. Weekend mornings are the strongest slot of all for students on the long eastern routes, and the only cost is the weekend.

Build the review into the shape as well. At six lessons, look at marks on questions of the type that were going wrong rather than at how the sessions felt. If the pattern has not shifted, change the tutor or the approach rather than extending the arrangement and hoping it compounds.

sections.heading: 0580 or 4MA1: find out before you book anybody
paragraphs: Your child's statement of entry names the board and the syllabus code for every subject. Most parents have never opened it, and it is the single most useful document to have in hand before a tutoring conversation. For maths the two codes you will see in this corridor are Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1.

They are not interchangeable, and the practical consequence is about past papers. Revision material circulates through school parent groups in this part of Dubai, and a well-meaning folder of Cambridge papers handed to a child entered for Pearson is a weekend spent on the wrong question styles. Check the code printed at the top of any paper against the code on the statement of entry before your child starts work on it.

The tier is the second thing to settle, and it is more consequential than the board. Core and Foundation are capped, and the cap can close off A Level maths in the same subject. The tier is fixed at entry, which falls months before the first paper, so the conversation with the subject teacher has to happen earlier than most families expect and should be based on mock marks rather than on impressions. After entry, moving tier for that series is difficult and sometimes not possible.

We do not supply syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables ourselves. Those belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and the right route is the board's own site or the school. What we will do is teach from the code your child is entered for and confirm the current paper structure on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com rather than from memory.

sections.heading: What the eastern corridor pays for a maths hour
paragraphs: Start with the cheapest option and work up, because that is the order a family deciding on a budget actually thinks in. The entry point in Dubai is a university-student tutor working online, advertised from AED 45 to 65 an hour by EdFlik, with Tutopiya's published panel starting lower again. For a Year 9 fluency gap or Core-tier consolidation that is a genuine service.

Above it sits the qualified subject tutor working online, where Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150. Then the named IGCSE specialist at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai table reaching the top of that band. The premium tier is real: BartyED publishes AED 650. For an Extended or Higher student in Year 11 with a mock two bands low, the middle two bands are where the sensible purchase sits.

The travel premium is the number this page cares about, because it is a timetable cost dressed as a teaching cost. In-home one to one in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor online, and in this corridor the difference is paying for a car on Algeria Street at 4pm. Monthly packages show the same shape: around AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four in-home sessions of two hours.

None of these figures is an IB Gram rate, and each was read on the provider's own public page so you can verify it rather than trust it. We publish no rate card on these pages; the free trial lesson and the conversation after it is where the actual number for your child's subject and level comes from.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the entry deadline
paragraphs: The date that catches families out is not the exam. It is the entry, which a school submits months ahead of the first paper and which fixes both the tier and the series. A family who discovers in February that their child is entered at the wrong tier has discovered it too late, and no amount of tutoring undoes it for that series.

Get the series right first. UAE candidates sit the June and the November series. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in those two series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only, so any plan built around a March exam window is built for a different country. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your exams officer which zone your centre sits in.

For dated examples, Pearson's published record is the checkable one. The Pearson Edexcel International GCSE November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are past dates, which is precisely why they are safe to use as a shape. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so open the live official timetable rather than relying on any restated date, including this one.

Read the table from the bottom upwards once and you will see where the tutoring money has to go. By the time the mock window arrives, support in the weakest paper should already be running, not being arranged.

sections.heading: Ramadan, holidays and the terms that are not full terms
paragraphs: A Dubai academic year contains several periods where the ordinary weekday shape does not apply, and a tutoring plan that ignores them loses weeks it did not budget for. Planning them in advance is the difference between a two-year arrangement that delivers seventy sessions and one that delivers fifty.

During Ramadan school days are shortened and household routines shift towards the evening. A 5.30pm lesson is usually the wrong slot in that period and a post-iftar one is usually right, and because our lessons involve no travel the change costs nothing but a message. Families who plan the shift before Ramadan starts keep their continuity; families who improvise lose three or four weeks.

School holidays cut the other way. A weekly slot limping through a holiday week with a student who is travelling is worth less than a short defined block on one topic, used while there is daylight and no homework. The strongest use of a Dubai winter or spring break for a Year 11 student is three or four sessions on the single weakest paper, finishing before school resumes.

Travel is the other recurring factor in this district, given how many households here have a parent working airport-adjacent shifts or travelling frequently. Online lessons follow a student to another time zone if the slot is adjusted, which is a real advantage over any arrangement that depends on somebody driving to a particular address. Tell us the travel dates in advance and the schedule is moved rather than missed.

sections.heading: What a maths tutor may and may not do with school work
paragraphs: IGCSE maths has less assessed coursework than most subjects, which makes the honesty question simpler here than in sciences or languages, but it does not make it disappear. School assignments, projects and investigation tasks still carry marks in some schools, and the boundary is the same one the boards apply everywhere.

A tutor may teach the method, work a comparable example, question a student about their own attempt and point out where the reasoning does not hold. A tutor may not write, complete, redo or edit to completion any piece of work the student will submit. The practical test for a parent is what the feedback looks like: if it arrives as sentences your child could copy in, the line has been crossed, and if it arrives as questions they have to answer, it has not.

This matters more than it sounds in this market. One page in the researched competitor set sells completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price, which is an academic-integrity breach and an examination malpractice trigger, and the student bears the consequence rather than the seller. Any offer of that kind, from anyone, should end the conversation.

We also decline to reproduce or supply board material. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson and are available from them. Pointing a parent at the official page is both the lawful answer and the more useful one, because the official page is current and a copied PDF is not.

sections.heading: Starting, and what we will tell you about availability
paragraphs: Send three things and the match is a narrow problem rather than a broad one: the syllabus code and tier from the statement of entry, a photograph of a marked mock or school test, and the time your child is realistically through the door on a bad traffic afternoon. The third one is the item most families leave out and the one that decides whether the arrangement survives.

The trial lesson is free, lasts about forty minutes, and is a real lesson rather than a sales call. Your child works a past question from their own code while the tutor teaches, and afterwards you receive a written read on the loss pattern and the number of weeks it implies. No card details are taken and nothing is owed if you stop there.

Sometimes the honest answer is that the slot you need is not available. Late-evening weekday slots in Gulf Standard Time are the first to fill, and so are weekend mornings during exam terms. If a specialist in your child's tier and code is not free at the time that works for your household, we will say so with a realistic match time rather than offering a generalist at the right hour. The wrong tutor in the right slot is worse value than a two-week wait.

What we need from you is limited to what the matching requires: the subject, the board and code, the year group, the school if you want its sequence followed, and a contact for scheduling. We do not need a photograph of your child or a full grade history, and UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 governs the data we do hold. The privacy link on this page sets out what is kept and how to have it removed.

process.title: Get the statement of entry
process.description: The board, the syllabus code and the tier for maths, from the school's own document rather than from memory. Your exams officer will send it. This one step prevents the commonest mismatch in Dubai tutoring and takes a single message to complete.

process.title: Time the journey home for a week
process.description: Note when your child is actually through the door on five consecutive days, including the worst one. The slot is set from the worst day, not the average. This is the step that decides whether a weekly arrangement is still running in February.

process.title: Send a marked paper
process.description: A photograph of a marked mock or class test tells a maths specialist more in two minutes than a paragraph of description. We are looking for the repeating error: index laws, sign slips, method not shown, reasoning marks left unclaimed.

process.title: Choose the slot and the practice day
process.description: One weekday for the lesson, a different evening for the practice it sets, and nothing on the night after a long fixture. Thursday and weekend mornings work best for long-commute families; Sunday evening works worst for almost everybody.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: Forty minutes on a past question from your child's own code, with your child doing the work and the tutor teaching. Afterwards you get a written read on the loss pattern and a realistic number of weeks before you commit to anything.

process.title: Review at six lessons against marks
process.description: Against marks on the question types that were going wrong, not against how the sessions felt. If the pattern has not moved we change the tutor or the approach, and if the arrangement is not earning its place we will tell you so.

whyPoints.description: We schedule from your child's real arrival-home time on a bad afternoon, with recovery time built in. Garhoud-direction families can hold 4.30pm; Mirdif, Al Mizhar and Al Warqa routes need 5.30pm or later, and pretending otherwise is how arrangements die in November.

faqs.question: What time should an IGCSE maths lesson start if my child buses to Mirdif from Al Rashidiya?
faqs.answer: Plan for 5.30pm or later. A bus serving a Mirdif school collects across several communities and loops back through Algeria Street, so thirty-five to forty-five minutes once school finishes is normal rather than unlucky, putting a student home around 4.15pm. Add food and twenty minutes of recovery and a 4.30pm lesson is being taught to somebody who has not arrived yet. Families travelling north to Al Garhoud are the exception and can usually hold 4.30pm through a whole term.

faqs.question: Are there any secondary schools inside Al Rashidiya itself?
faqs.answer: No, which is the fact that shapes everything else on this page. Al Rashidiya is a residential district between Dubai International Airport, Al Garhoud and Nad Al Hamar, and its Year 10 and Year 11 students travel out of it to sit IGCSE: north to the Garhoud and Al Mamzar schools, east to Mirdif, Al Mizhar and Al Warqa, or north-east across Damascus Street to Al Qusais. That is why a tutor's address tells you nothing useful, and why the direction of your child's school run is the first thing we ask about.

faqs.question: Which weekday is the worst one to book a maths lesson on?
faqs.answer: Sunday evening, for most students. It is the first school day of the UAE week and a fifteen-year-old spends it reassembling the term rather than learning anything new, so a lesson there consistently produces less than the same hour later in the week. Wednesday is the second weakest in many schools because it carries the heaviest homework load. Monday and Tuesday are reliable, Thursday is stronger than it looks because the next morning is not a school morning, and weekend mornings are the best slot available.

faqs.question: Is a weekend morning lesson actually better than a weekday one?
faqs.answer: For students on the long eastern bus routes, usually yes. The comparison is not hour against hour; it is a rested student against one who has been awake since six and travelling since two-thirty. A Saturday or Sunday morning lesson with a fresh fifteen-year-old covers noticeably more ground than a 5pm weekday lesson with a tired one, and it leaves weekday evenings free for school homework. The cost is a piece of the weekend, and most long-route families decide that is the right trade after trying the alternative.

faqs.question: My child's school never told us the maths board. Where is it written down?
faqs.answer: The statement of entry, which the school issues ahead of each series, lists the board and the syllabus code for every subject. Your exams officer holds it and will send a copy. If the series is still some way off, the head of maths will confirm which board and tier the class is working towards. It matters practically rather than academically: past papers do not transfer between the boards, and revision folders circulating in school parent groups here regularly send a child to the wrong question styles for a weekend.

faqs.question: Can we still change from Core to Extended maths?
faqs.answer: Only before the entry is submitted, which falls months ahead of the first paper. The tier is fixed at that point and moving it for the same series is difficult and sometimes not possible. The lower tier caps the available grade, and that cap can close the route to A Level maths in the same subject, so the conversation with the subject teacher should happen in Year 10 and again early in Year 11, with marked mock papers as the evidence rather than a report comment. Ask early; it is a decision with a deadline.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE maths tutor cost around the eastern suburbs?
faqs.answer: Cheapest first: a university-student tutor online is advertised from AED 45 to 65 an hour by EdFlik, with Tutopiya's published panel lower again. A qualified subject tutor online starts from AED 150 at Unitors. A named IGCSE specialist runs AED 200 to 450 or above, with TutorChase at AED 270. The premium tier reaches AED 650 at BartyED. In-home one to one is quoted at AED 180 to 500 because the rate includes the drive. None of those is an IB Gram price; each was read on the provider's own public page.

faqs.question: Why would I pay more for in-home maths tutoring out here?
faqs.answer: You would be paying for a car journey. A tutor reaching Al Rashidiya from Al Garhoud or Mirdif between 3pm and 6pm loses a real portion of the chargeable hour to Algeria Street or the Garhoud interchange and recovers it in the rate, which is why in-home sits at AED 180 to 500 against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor online. The premium buys travel rather than teaching, and it also introduces a second unpredictable variable into the schedule. IB Gram does not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE.

faqs.question: How much practice should my child do between weekly maths lessons?
faqs.answer: Twenty to thirty minutes on two separate evenings, rather than ninety minutes the night before. Maths retention follows repetition, so two short sessions beat one long one by a wide margin, and the practice should be set to a specific day rather than left to be fitted in. Pick evenings that are actually free: nothing after a long sports fixture, nothing on the heaviest homework night. The tutor's written note after each lesson names the practice, which makes it checkable rather than aspirational.

faqs.question: My child's mock maths grade came back two bands low. What format do we need?
faqs.answer: An intensive block rather than a weekly lesson. Two or three sessions a week for six to ten weeks, built almost entirely from past questions in the right syllabus code, marked against the published mark scheme, with the repeating errors named and drilled. A mock two bands below target usually hides two or three recurring faults rather than a general absence of knowledge, and those are recoverable in weeks. Weekly general teaching from that point is too slow to reach the series.

faqs.question: Does the maths slot have to change once Ramadan starts?
faqs.answer: The slot moves, usually to after iftar, and because no tutor is travelling anywhere the change costs nothing more than a message. School days are shortened during Ramadan and household routines shift towards the evening, so the 5.30pm slot that works in October is usually the wrong one then. Families who agree the shift before Ramadan begins keep their continuity through it; families who improvise tend to lose three or four weeks and then restart from a worse position in a busier term.

faqs.question: We travel often. Can the maths lessons follow us?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the slot adjusted for the time difference. This district has a high proportion of households with airport-adjacent shift patterns or frequent travel, and an online one-to-one lesson is the format that survives that. Tell us the dates in advance and the sessions are moved rather than missed. The thing to avoid is letting a trip turn into a four-week gap, because in a drill subject like maths the restart costs more than the sessions missed. A short catch-up block on return usually settles it.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover maths and another subject for the same child?
faqs.answer: Usually we would rather two specialists than one generalist, and in maths specifically the specialism matters. A tutor who teaches 0580 Extended well is not automatically useful on IGCSE Physics 0625, and the combination offer tends to be a scheduling convenience rather than a teaching one. Where two subjects both need help and the household can only hold one slot, the better answer is to fix the subject where the gap is widest or where the grade blocks a post-16 route, then reassess, rather than splitting the hour.

faqs.question: Do you supply past papers and mark schemes for maths?
faqs.answer: No. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and reproducing or distributing them is not ours to do. We teach from the code your child is entered for and point you at cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com, where the current material lives. That is also the more useful answer, because an official page is current and a copied file circulating in a parent group is often two specifications out of date.

faqs.question: What do you need from us before the first maths lesson?
faqs.answer: Three things. The syllabus code and tier from the statement of entry. A photograph of a marked mock or class test, which tells a specialist more than any description of confidence. And the time your child is realistically through the front door on a bad traffic afternoon, which sets the slot. We do not need a photograph of your child or a full grade history across every subject; UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 governs personal data here and the privacy link explains what is held.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-rashidiya.closingHeading: Set the slot first, then the syllabus
dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-rashidiya.closingBody: Two facts decide whether IGCSE maths tutoring works for a family in Al Rashidiya, and neither of them is the tutor's rate. The first is the time your child is genuinely through the door on a bad afternoon, which sets a slot the household can keep for two years rather than two months. The second is the syllabus code and tier on the statement of entry, which decides which past papers are worth a weekend. Get both in writing, send them to us with a photograph of a marked paper, and take the free trial lesson. It runs on a question from your child's own code, with your child doing the work, and you will know by the end of it whether this is the right person.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-safa.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE mathematics to the June and November series. Every plan starts from your child's own timetable and tier rather than from a generic revision schedule, because the two produce different work.

intro.heading: A two-year maths course has four useful phases, not one
paragraphs: IGCSE mathematics runs for two years and most families treat it as a single undifferentiated stretch with a frightening bit at the end. It is better understood as four phases, each with a different purpose, a different kind of tutoring attached to it, and a hard boundary at the end that you cannot cross back over. Knowing which phase you are in answers most of the questions a parent in Al Safa arrives with, including the uncomfortable one about whether it is too late.

Phase one is Year 10, when content is being taught for the first time and the tier entry is being provisionally decided on the evidence available. Tutoring here changes outcomes rather than defending them, because it works on cause: a student who cannot rearrange a formula reliably in Year 10 will lose marks in trigonometry, in mensuration and in graphs eighteen months later, and nobody will connect those losses back to the rearranging. Phase one is also the only phase in which a Core entry can be argued up to Extended with evidence rather than with hope.

Phase two is the autumn of Year 11, when the second half of the syllabus arrives on top of whatever was left unfinished, entries are submitted and the tier locks. Phase three is the window between the mocks and the final six weeks, which is the only point in the year when a complete set of marked scripts exists and the one most families spend recovering instead of reading. Phase four is the final six to eight weeks, where the work is pace, technique and nothing else, because the time for content has gone.

Al Safa is a good place to say this from, because it has an unusual density of secondary provision. Jumeirah College, Horizon English School, Safa British School and Latifa School for Girls all sit in or beside it, with Jumeirah Baccalaureate School alongside them, and children from Al Wasl, Jumeirah 3 and Al Manara all come into the same schools. That means mock timetables here are tightly packed, study leave arrangements vary between schools on the same street, and your own school's calendar is the only one worth planning against.

Two plain statements before the detail. Cambridge runs the June and November series for UAE candidates; the February and March series is offered to India only and should play no part in a Dubai plan. And IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses: home visits are a service we provide in India only, and maths teaching for Al Safa families happens one-to-one over live video in a shared workspace where both people write. For a subject taught through multi-step working, that arrangement is better than it sounds, because a solution stays on screen and can be returned to a week later when the same slip reappears.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-safa.subjectsIntro: What each maths topic is worth in a short run-up differs sharply. These are the topics that generate the work, ranked loosely by how quickly they respond when time is short.

subjects.name: Upper and lower bounds
subjects.description: The quickest win in the subject. Students write the rounded value as the bound rather than the limit, and ten minutes of definition work plus a week of drilling recovers marks in every paper that includes it.

subjects.name: Compound growth and reverse percentages
subjects.description: Mechanical and fast to fix. Losses come from non-integer periods handled wrongly and from reverse percentage questions where the student multiplies instead of dividing.

subjects.name: Histograms and frequency density
subjects.description: One misconception costing a whole question. Frequency density treated as frequency, axes unlabelled, and the data understood perfectly well throughout. A single reteach plus two targeted papers normally closes it.

subjects.name: Similar shapes, area and volume scale factors
subjects.description: A single rule applied wrongly: the length scale factor used for an area or a volume. Worth a full question and fixable in one session followed by repetition.

subjects.name: Simultaneous and quadratic equations
subjects.description: Technique is usually sound and working is often absent, which forfeits method marks that remain available. A habit problem rather than a knowledge problem, and habits respond to being marked.

subjects.name: Trigonometry, sine and cosine rules
subjects.description: Rule selection is the taught skill. Three-dimensional questions and bearings lose marks because students try to work without drawing the diagram the question is really asking for.

subjects.name: Probability and tree diagrams
subjects.description: Marked generously when the diagram is drawn and harshly when it is not. Conditional questions fail on reading rather than on probability, with the condition missed in the wording.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Notation costs more than concepts. An ambiguously written column vector is read by the scheme as a different object, and the method credit goes with it.

subjects.name: Graphs, gradients and rates of change
subjects.description: Interpretation marks sit here. The gradient is calculated correctly and the sentence saying what it means in the context of the question is missing, which is where the mark was.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: The slowest to repair and the most consequential. Losses spread across every topic point here, and eight weeks is not enough time to rebuild it alongside nine other subjects.

subjects.name: Non-calculator arithmetic
subjects.description: A distinct examinable skill for 0580 candidates. Two years of calculator-assisted homework leaves hand arithmetic slow, and the non-calculator paper finds that out immediately.

subjects.name: Question triage and timing
subjects.description: Sizing an answer to its marks, and deciding what to leave. Students write paragraphs on two-mark questions and meet the long final question with four minutes left, which is planning rather than mathematics.

sections.heading: The four phases of a maths course, and what each one is for
paragraphs: A two-year maths course has four phases with hard boundaries between them, and the boundary you have most recently crossed determines what tutoring can achieve. This is the single most useful thing for a parent in Al Safa to establish before spending anything, because the same budget buys very different outcomes depending on where in the sequence it is spent.

The boundaries are not soft. Once entries are submitted, the tier is fixed and the grade ceiling with it. Once the content teaching finishes, a student who has not secured algebraic fluency will not acquire it alongside nine other subjects in revision season. Once study leave begins, the structure of the week disappears and self-management becomes the binding constraint. None of those boundaries can be argued with, and all of them are predictable months in advance.

What that means practically is that the honest answer to what tutoring will do changes several times across two years. In Year 10 it changes the grade. In the autumn of Year 11 it can still change the tier. After the mocks it changes the technique and the priority order. In the final six weeks it changes the pace and the number of recoverable marks that are actually recovered. All four are worth buying; only the first is worth buying as a general improvement.

The table sets the four phases out with what the job is in each, and the final column states what the phase cannot do. Families who read that column first make better decisions than families who read the first column first.

sections.heading: An eight-week maths plan, week by week
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the most common amount of time a family in this cluster has when they first make contact, and the plan below is roughly what we would write for a student whose mock showed technique losses rather than a foundation gap. It is deliberately specific, because a plan with no weekly target is a wish rather than a plan.

The principle is that every week ends with evidence. A week of revision with nothing sat and nothing marked has produced no information, so the following week has to be planned on guesswork. A week ending in a timed section marked against the scheme produces a number and a cause, and the next week can be built on both. Students resist this at first because it is uncomfortable, and then prefer it, because progress becomes visible.

The plan deliberately front-loads the quick procedural fixes. Bounds, scale factors, compound growth and histograms can each be closed in a session and a week of practice, and closing four of them in the first fortnight produces a measurable jump that makes the harder weeks survivable. Leaving them until week six wastes their motivational value as well as their marks.

One adjustment worth making in Dubai. If Ramadan falls inside the eight weeks, move the timed work to mornings where the school day is shortened and expect the evening sessions to be shorter and later. A full paper sat late at night tests endurance rather than technique, and the result is not diagnostic.

sections.heading: Reading a maths mock script properly
paragraphs: A mock produces two things: a grade, which is of limited value, and a marked script, which is the most useful document a family will see all year. Schools set mock boundaries differently, some deliberately harsh and some generously, so the grade tells you about the school's choice as much as about your child. The script tells you about your child.

Read it with a pen and five categories. Content not known. Technique not chosen, meaning the student knew the content and picked the wrong approach. Working not shown, forfeiting method marks that remained available. Accuracy or rounding, where the method was right and the value was quoted wrongly. Ran out of time. Mark every lost mark against one of the five and total the columns.

The distribution is where the surprises live. Families expect the first category to dominate and in maths it usually does not. Working-not-shown and ran-out-of-time together often account for a third or more of the losses, and both are behavioural rather than mathematical, which means they respond quickly. A student with that profile does not need more content; they need to be marked strictly on method for a fortnight and timed for another.

The profile that needs a different answer is losses spread evenly across every topic with few procedural causes. That indicates algebraic fluency was never secured, which is a longer project than eight weeks permits alongside nine other subjects. The honest response is to say so, protect the achievable grades, and plan a longer programme if the student is continuing with maths post-16. Being told that early is more useful than being sold an intensive course that cannot deliver.

sections.heading: The order of papers in the series, and what it does to a plan
paragraphs: The sequence of papers inside an examination series shapes the final fortnight more than most plans allow for. Maths papers are usually separated by days rather than sat consecutively, other subjects fall between them, and the gap between a student's two maths papers is often the single most valuable block of revision time available in the whole series.

That gap should be planned before study leave begins. A student with four days between the two maths papers has a specific and unusual opportunity: the content is at its freshest, the first paper has just shown exactly where the weaknesses are, and nothing else can usefully be revised in that window because it is maths-shaped. Students who have not planned it tend to spend it anxiously reviewing everything rather than the three topics the first paper exposed.

The zone point matters here too. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable version for each, stating that it is essential to use the correct version and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. The timetable to plan against is the one your child's school issues. Two schools in Al Safa could in principle hold different versions.

On dates that are properly sourced: the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January, and November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official PDF is always the document to use.

sections.heading: The November resit in maths, and why it plans well
paragraphs: Maths is the subject where a November resit most often makes sense, because the maths grade is the one most likely to be blocking a post-16 place. A Level Mathematics and Higher Level Analysis and Approaches both expect a strong Extended grade, and a sixth form that has declined a student on maths alone is a specific and solvable problem rather than a general one.

It also plans unusually well. The syllabus is already known, the previous script shows exactly where the marks went, and the target is a defined number of marks rather than a vague improvement. That is the clearest brief a tutor ever receives, and it is why a short focused block of sessions can work for a resit when the same block would be inadequate for a first sitting.

The decision still needs testing honestly in four steps. Establish which grade is actually the blocker, in writing, from the receiving school. Ask whether the requirement is negotiable, because inside the same institution it sometimes is. Confirm the subject is available in the November series at your centre and when the entry closes, since that deadline falls well before the papers. And assess whether the student can carry a resit alongside the start of A Levels or the Diploma, because the new course has two years of consequences attached and the resit has one grade.

Where a student is not re-entering through their own school, a private-candidate route exists and its mechanics vary by centre and board. That is a question for the school's examinations officer or an approved centre, not for a tutoring page, and it should be asked early because the arrangements take time to put in place.

sections.heading: Ramadan, holidays and the blocks that decide a maths grade
paragraphs: The UAE academic calendar has its own term and break pattern, Ramadan moves earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar, and school days shorten during it. For maths revision specifically this matters more than for essay subjects, because calculation work degrades sharply with tiredness and a timed paper sat late at night produces a result that is not diagnostic.

The adjustments are simple when planned. During Ramadan, move timed papers to mornings where the school day is shortened, and expect evening sessions to be later and shorter. Online delivery handles the shift without anybody travelling, which is one of the few genuine logistical advantages available. Keep the week after any break for revision rather than new content, because it is reliably the weakest week in any plan.

The break weeks themselves are the most valuable and most wasted study blocks of the year. A fortnight without school can absorb two full timed maths papers with proper marking and review between them, which is more diagnostic output than the preceding two months of fragmented evenings. The decision that makes the difference is booking the work before the break rather than intending to do it during the break.

The practical first step is mundane and almost nobody does it. Put the school's published term dates, the mock fortnight, the break weeks, Ramadan and the exam window on one page at the start of Year 11, then plan backwards into the gaps. Families who do find time they did not believe they had. Families who do not find that the calendar has already made their decisions for them.

sections.heading: What late maths help costs around Al Safa
paragraphs: Start with the monthly figure, since that is what a household budget registers. Bestimate's Dubai guidance for a weekly one-hour arrangement gives roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Published monthly packages in this market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Hourly, and cheapest first: Tutopiya advertises from AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65, which generally means a university student working from a textbook. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200 for a qualified online tutor. TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level work, Bestimate's specialist band is AED 200-450 and above, and BartyED publishes AED 650. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180-350 by Bestimate and AED 200-500 by independent home tutors, travel included. Those are other providers' own published figures with their own dates, not an IB Gram price list.

Booking late does not appear to raise rates much; it reduces availability, which is a cost of a different kind. A specific board at a specific tier is harder to cover in April than in September, and that is the real penalty for leaving it. Four questions make quotes comparable: per hour or per session and how long is a session, travel inside or outside the figure, what happens to the fee on a short-notice cancellation during study leave, and how many sessions am I committing to.

IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson rather than publishing a blind figure, because an eight-week technique problem and a two-year foundation rebuild are not the same product. If the trial shows that three sessions and the school's own maths clinic would do the job, that is what we will tell you, and the school clinic is free and widely underused in this cluster.

sections.heading: The tier, the deadline and the ceiling
paragraphs: A Cambridge Core entry in mathematics caps the grade available, and that cap is administrative rather than mathematical. It is the most consequential date-driven fact in an IGCSE maths year, and in this cluster it is most often discovered in Year 11 when a sixth-form requirement turns out to be unreachable on the entry that already exists.

The school decides, usually on Year 9 and early Year 10 evidence, and the decision is revisable inside the entry window that closes months before the papers. Both sides of the usual disagreement are reasonable: a school placing a borderline candidate on Extended risks them sitting papers they cannot answer, while a parent can see improvement the current data does not yet show. Impressions resolve nothing; evidence resolves it quickly.

Three questions in writing, early in Year 11 or ideally in Year 10, settle it. Which tier is my child provisionally entered at, in each subject. What evidence would move that entry. When is the final deadline for changing it. Schools answer all three readily because the answers come off the entry record, and a vague anxiety becomes a dated plan.

If the window has closed, that is unwelcome and still useful, because it changes where the remaining hours should go. A fixed Core entry means the sensible plan is to secure the top of the Core range and to look seriously at post-16 routes that do not require a strong Extended maths grade, rather than spending a spring chasing a grade the entry cannot award. That conversation is better had in February than in August.

process.title: Send the timetable and the tier
process.description: Your child's own exam timetable from the school, including the Cambridge zone version where it applies, plus the syllabus code and tier. The plan is built from those documents. Without them any schedule is guesswork, and in a spring term guesswork is the expensive option.

process.description: Not the grade. We read it question by question and sort each lost mark into content, technique choice, working, accuracy or time. In maths that distribution usually surprises families, because behavioural losses are a larger share than anyone expects and they respond fastest.

process.description: One full session online, no cost, no card, worked on a real paper in a shared workspace. Afterwards you get a written view of what the remaining weeks can realistically deliver. If that is less than you hoped, you hear it before any fee is discussed rather than after.

process.title: Receive a written plan with weekly targets
process.description: Eight rows, each with a focus and a piece of evidence that week produces. Quick procedural fixes front-loaded, the first full timed paper in week four, and the plan from week five onwards following the evidence rather than the original guess.

process.title: Weekly papers and a running error log
process.description: Timed papers marked against the published scheme, method and accuracy losses recorded separately, and the cause distribution reviewed every week. The log is how the final weeks stay pointed at the real problem and how you can judge progress independently.

whyPoints.title: Plans with dates and evidence, not topic lists
whyPoints.description: Every week in the plan ends with something sat and marked, because a week of revision that produced no information forces the next week to be planned on guesswork. Progress becomes visible, which students resist initially and then prefer.

whyPoints.title: Phase-aware advice
whyPoints.description: What tutoring can achieve changes several times across two years, and we say which phase you are in before taking a booking. Year 10 changes the grade; the autumn can still change the tier; eight weeks changes technique and pace and nothing else.

whyPoints.title: UAE-correct exam information
whyPoints.description: June and November are the series a UAE candidate sits. The February and March series is offered to India only and has no place in a Dubai plan. Handing a parent a date from another country is worse than saying nothing at all.

whyPoints.title: Quick procedural wins front-loaded
whyPoints.description: Bounds, scale factors, compound growth and histograms each close in a session plus a week of practice. Fixing four in the first fortnight produces a measurable jump that makes the harder weeks survivable, and leaving them to week six wastes that.

whyPoints.title: We will point you at the free option
whyPoints.description: Many Al Safa schools run a maths clinic at no cost and it is widely underused. Where a trial shows that three sessions plus the clinic would do the job, that is what we say. Selling a term to a student who needs a fortnight is not a service.

whyPoints.title: Explicit about limits and status
whyPoints.description: No UAE home visits, no Dubai office or centre, no regulator or board approval claimed, no grade promised, and no past papers or mark schemes supplied. Home visits are an India-only service, and the exam material belongs to Cambridge and Pearson.

faqs.question: We are eight weeks from the June series. What can maths tutoring realistically achieve?
faqs.answer: A great deal, if the losses are behavioural, and very little if they are foundational. Eight weeks reliably fixes procedural misconceptions like bounds and scale factors, builds the habit of showing working so method marks are awarded, teaches question triage so the long final question is not met with four minutes left, and improves pace through timed papers. It does not rebuild algebraic fluency alongside nine other subjects. One marked mock script tells us which situation you are in, and we tell you before any fee is discussed.

faqs.question: What should we do in the fortnight after my child's maths mock?
faqs.answer: Read the script rather than the grade, with a pen and five categories: content not known, technique not chosen, working not shown, accuracy or rounding, ran out of time. Total the columns. In maths the surprise is usually how large the working and timing columns are, because both are behavioural and both respond within weeks. Ask the school for the marked script before it is filed. That fortnight is the only point in the year when a complete set of marked papers exists at once.

faqs.question: Why do mock grades at Al Safa schools vary so much from each other?
faqs.answer: Because schools set mock boundaries themselves, and the choices differ. Some set them deliberately harshly to provoke effort before study leave, others more generously to protect confidence, and neither reflects a board boundary. Two children at two schools on the same street can receive different grades for identical performance. That is why the grade tells you about the school's decision and the script tells you about your child, and why a plan should be built on the second rather than the first.

faqs.question: How much of the final weeks should be full papers rather than topic practice?
faqs.answer: Most of it, after the first fortnight. Topic practice builds technique and tests nothing about pace, question order or the decision of what to abandon, and all three are examined. A reasonable shape is quick procedural fixes in weeks one and two, then a full timed paper roughly every fortnight with targeted work in between driven by what each paper showed. A paper is only useful if it is sat to time, in one sitting, and marked against the real scheme afterwards.

faqs.question: Is the gap between the two maths papers worth planning for?
faqs.answer: It is often the single most valuable revision block of the whole series and it is routinely wasted. The content is at its freshest, the first paper has just revealed exactly which topics are weak, and nothing else can usefully occupy that window because it is maths-shaped. Students who have not planned it spend it anxiously reviewing everything instead of the three topics the first paper exposed. Decide what goes in that gap before study leave begins rather than during it.

faqs.question: Can my child's Core maths entry still be moved to Extended?
faqs.answer: Only if the entry window is still open, and it closes months before the papers. Ask the school three questions in writing: which tier is my child entered at, what evidence would move it, and when is the deadline. If the window is open, produce the evidence: a term of direct work on the Extended-only content and a full Extended paper sat to time. If it has closed, the sensible plan changes to securing the top of the Core range and looking at post-16 routes that do not require strong Extended maths.

faqs.question: Which maths topics give the fastest improvement when time is short?
faqs.answer: Four stand out, and each closes in a session plus a week of practice. Bounds, where the student writes the rounded value rather than the limit. Similar shapes, where the length scale factor gets applied to an area or a volume. Compound growth over a non-integer number of periods. And histograms, where frequency density is treated as frequency and a whole question goes. Front-loading those four produces a measurable jump early, which matters for motivation as well as for marks.

faqs.question: Does Ramadan change how maths revision should be scheduled?
faqs.answer: Yes, and more than for essay subjects, because calculation work degrades sharply with tiredness. Where the school day is shortened, move timed papers to the morning; a full paper sat late at night tests endurance and produces a result that is not diagnostic. Expect evening sessions to be later and shorter, which online delivery accommodates without anybody travelling. And treat the week after any break as a revision week rather than a new-content week, because it is reliably the weakest in a plan.

faqs.question: Will IB Gram send a maths tutor to our home in Al Safa during study leave?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we provide in India only. Sessions here are one-to-one over live video in a shared workspace where both people write. During study leave that has a practical advantage: a session cannot be lost to traffic, a tutor cannot arrive late into a ninety-minute slot, and a paper review can happen at eight in the evening without anybody making a journey across Jumeirah.

faqs.question: Is a November maths resit worth it, and when do we have to decide?
faqs.answer: Maths is the subject where a resit most often makes sense, because the maths grade is the one most likely to block a post-16 place. Decide in four steps: establish in writing which grade is the blocker, ask whether the requirement is negotiable, confirm the subject is available in November at your centre and when the entry closes, and assess honestly whether a resit can be carried alongside the start of A Levels or the Diploma. The entry deadline falls months before the papers, so the decision cannot wait long after results.

faqs.question: How much does a short block of maths tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Monthly figures first, since that is what a budget feels: Bestimate's estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, with advertised packages including around AED 799 for eight online sessions. Hourly, Tutopiya starts at AED 33-52, EdFlik at AED 45-65, Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150, TutorChase quotes AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650. Those are other providers' own rates; we quote after a free trial.

faqs.question: Does booking in April cost more than booking in September?
faqs.answer: Not materially in price, and considerably in availability, which is the real penalty. Rates in this market are broadly stable across the year, but specialists fill up as the series approaches, so a specific board at a specific tier is harder to cover in the spring than in the autumn. Where we cannot match you promptly we say so, give a realistic estimate and suggest what to do meanwhile, which is often the school's own maths clinic. Assigning an approximate tutor in an exam term helps nobody.

faqs.question: Do the school holidays actually help with maths revision?
faqs.answer: They are the most valuable study blocks in the year and the most commonly wasted. A fortnight with no school can absorb two full timed maths papers with proper marking and review between them, which is more diagnostic output than the preceding two months of fragmented evenings. The thing that makes the difference is booking the work before the break starts. Families who plan it find time they did not believe they had; families who intend it come back having looked at some notes.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions a week should we book in the final stretch?
faqs.answer: One is normal, two in the last month if the mock showed several separable problems. The binding constraint is not money but the time left to do the work: a full paper takes around ninety minutes to sit and roughly as long to review properly, so a student booked three times a week has no space to produce the evidence those sessions exist to diagnose. Past that point extra contact hours reduce progress rather than adding to it, and we would rather say so.

faqs.question: Which timetable should we be revising against?
faqs.answer: The one your child's school issues, and no other. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable version for each, stating that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Two schools in Al Safa could in principle hold different versions. Ask which zone your centre sits in, and plan from the document the school hands out.

faqs.question: Can you provide the past papers and mark schemes for the eight weeks?
faqs.answer: No. Past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and syllabus documents belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and reproducing or distributing them is a copyright problem rather than a grey area. Your child's school has legitimate access and can supply what is needed, and sessions work from material the student already holds. Be cautious with any site offering a downloadable bundle of this material: distributing it is something they have no right to do, which is informative about the rest of the service.
