dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-satwa.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach IGCSE mathematics by syllabus code across Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel, one-to-one over live video. Sessions for Al Satwa families are scheduled around the actual school return time rather than a standard after-school block.

intro.heading: The maths lesson has to fit the Satwa afternoon
paragraphs: Almost no private school sits inside Al Satwa. The district is dense low-rise housing between Sheikh Zayed Road and 2nd December Street, and its secondary pupils travel out — to Oud Metha and Al Mankhool on the Bur Dubai side, to Al Safa and Jumeirah on the coast, or the long run to Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim. That single fact decides more about whether maths tutoring works for a Satwa family than any claim about teaching method, because a lesson that cannot reliably start does not happen.

The arithmetic is worth doing out loud. A child on the Oud Metha run finishes at around 15:00 and, on a looping bus route, reaches home somewhere between 15:40 and 16:15. The Al Safa and Jumeirah runs cross Sheikh Zayed Road, which adds ten to twenty minutes in the wrong direction at that hour. The Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim run commonly puts a child through the door after 16:30. Add changing, eating and the collapse that follows a long day in a bus and the honest earliest start for most Satwa families is 17:00, with 17:30 or 18:00 safer for the longer runs.

Parents routinely propose 16:00 because that is when school ends on paper. The slot then slips by fifteen minutes one week, half an hour the next, and is quietly abandoned by the third month. A slot chosen against the worst Tuesday of the term survives. This matters more in maths than in most subjects, because maths improvement is cumulative: a weekly session that actually runs for fourteen weeks beats a nominally twice-weekly arrangement that runs eleven times in total.

The second half of this page is about which maths your child is actually sitting, and it is not a pedantic question. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is syllabus 0580 and runs a Core and an Extended tier with different papers. Cambridge International Mathematics is 0607, a different syllabus with graphics-calculator assumptions throughout and an investigation strand. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A is 4MA1, with its own formula provision, and Further Pure Mathematics is 4PM1. These are not interchangeable. A tutor preparing a 0607 student on 0580 past papers is preparing for the wrong exam, and the student will not notice until the real paper.

The code is printed on the statement of entry the school issues, and it takes one email to the school office to confirm. Sending it with the first enquiry is the single most useful thing a Satwa parent can do, because it removes the first two sessions of guesswork from a paid arrangement.

Lessons from IB Gram are one-to-one and delivered live online to Al Satwa on Gulf Standard Time, with the first one free. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE — home visits are a service offered only in India. For a district with this commute pattern that limit cuts both ways honestly: you lose a person in the room, and you gain a tutor chosen for the syllabus code rather than for who is willing to drive into Satwa at five in the afternoon.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-satwa.programmesIntro: An IGCSE maths search usually spans three stages of a child's school life in this district, and each one needs a different kind of session. The years before Year 10 are where fluency is built cheaply; Years 10 and 11 are where it is examined; post-16 is where the gaps become expensive.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary Mathematics
programmes.description: Three years assessed internally, with optional Checkpoint tests at the end of Year 9. Nothing from this stage appears on a certificate, which is why it is skipped and why skipping it is costly. Fraction and index fluency, proportional reasoning and the habit of setting work out in lines are built here or repaired later under exam pressure.
programmes.countryNote: Satwa children at this stage are usually at a school in Al Mankhool, Oud Metha or Al Safa, and the Year 9 maths pathway conversation happens in the second term. One or two sessions before that conversation give a parent something concrete to discuss with the subject teacher about 0580 against 0607.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson International GCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: Two years to a June or November series. Cambridge 0580 runs Core and Extended tiers; 0607 runs Core and Extended with a graphics calculator assumed; Pearson 4MA1 is a different paper structure again. The entry is made by the school ahead of the series deadline and determines the grade range available to the candidate.
programmes.countryNote: Mathematics is one of the five accredited subjects most Al Satwa families will want inside the Ministry of Education equivalency count, since the British track requires five IGCSE or GCSE passes at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from the five.

programmes.name: AS and A Level Mathematics
programmes.description: Where IGCSE algebraic weakness turns into a visible problem. The step from Extended-tier manipulation to AS-level work is the most common reason a comfortable Year 11 grade becomes an uncomfortable Year 12 one. Cambridge and Pearson both run AS and A Level series in June and November.
programmes.countryNote: The British equivalency track also asks for one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary at the same grade — a constraint worth reading before a Satwa family lets a three-subject A Level block settle.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Mathematics
programmes.description: The alternative post-IGCSE route, offered by several schools within reach of this district. Students arriving from 0607 generally find the transition shorter than those arriving from 0580, because the graphics-calculator habits and the investigation strand are already familiar.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's International Baccalaureate cohort is about 7% of private enrolment against 37% on the UK curriculum, so a Satwa student moving IGCSE to Diploma is joining the smaller stream — and specialist tutoring supply in that stream is thinner, which rewards booking earlier.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-satwa.subjectsIntro: Maths does not fail as a subject; it fails in specific places. The list below is the set of topics that account for most of the lost marks on Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE maths papers, written as what a tutor would actually work on rather than as a syllabus contents page.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation and rearrangement
subjects.description: The foundation everything else sits on. Students who can solve a tidy equation lose marks the moment a subject has to be made from a formula with a fraction in it. This is the highest-yield topic in the whole course because it appears inside questions labelled as something else entirely.

subjects.name: Two-step and multi-topic problems
subjects.description: A percentage change inside a geometry question, or a ratio buried in a volume calculation. Students who know both topics separately score nothing because they do not see the join. Practising the join is a distinct skill from practising either topic.

subjects.name: Bearings, angles and geometric reasoning
subjects.description: Bearings cost marks because of convention rather than difficulty: three figures, clockwise, from north. Angle-reasoning questions require the reason to be stated in the mark scheme's language, and a correct answer without the named circle theorem does not score full marks.

subjects.name: Transformations and vectors
subjects.description: Describing a transformation fully is the mark scheme's requirement and the usual place students stop short: a rotation needs angle, direction and centre. Vector work is usually lost in notation rather than concept.

subjects.name: Trigonometry beyond the right angle
subjects.description: The sine and cosine rules, area of a non-right triangle, and three-dimensional trigonometry. Students pick the wrong rule under time pressure, and the recovery is a decision drill rather than more theory.

subjects.name: Probability, tree diagrams and set notation
subjects.description: Conditional probability is where Extended papers separate candidates. Set notation and Venn diagrams reward precise reading of the question, and students who shade intuitively rather than from the notation lose marks consistently.

subjects.name: Statistics: cumulative frequency and histograms
subjects.description: Frequency density is the single most reliably botched calculation in IGCSE statistics. Cumulative frequency graphs are usually drawn correctly and then read from the wrong point, which is a technique fix rather than a knowledge fix.

subjects.name: Functions, graphs and calculator use (0607)
subjects.description: Syllabus 0607 assumes a graphics calculator throughout and asks candidates to sketch from a calculator display, state ranges and identify asymptotes. Students taught on 0580 resources are unprepared for the format even when their mathematics is sound.

subjects.name: Formula recall and the provided sheet
subjects.description: Different papers provide different formulae. What must be memorised therefore differs by code, and the only safe way to know is to look at the formula pages of the actual paper your child will sit rather than at a generic revision list.

subjects.name: Setting out, units and accuracy
subjects.description: Method marks are awarded for visible working, and students who calculate mentally lose them even when the answer is right. Rounding instructions, units in the final line and correct accuracy conventions quietly account for several marks per paper.

sections.heading: What time a maths session can actually start in Al Satwa
paragraphs: For most Al Satwa families the earliest reliable weekday start for a maths lesson is 17:00, and for the Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim commutes it is 18:00. That is the answer, and the rest of this section is the reasoning, because parents who do not see the reasoning propose 16:00 and then lose the slot by October.

Secondary schooling in this district happens elsewhere. The bus or the car leaves Satwa in the morning and comes back in the afternoon through one of three traffic patterns: the Bur Dubai crossing, the Sheikh Zayed Road crossing, or the long coastal and inland run to Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim. Each has a different failure mode. The Bur Dubai crossing is short but reliably congested from 15:00. The Sheikh Zayed crossing is fast when it moves and stationary when it does not. The long run is simply long, and a looping bus route on top of it routinely adds twenty minutes to the map time.

The table below puts a realistic earliest start against each cluster. These are planning assumptions a family can test against their own last two weeks rather than predictions, and the useful discipline is to set the slot against the slowest of those weeks. A session that begins fifteen minutes late is a session where the first thing taught is taught to a child still unpacking a bag.

There is one more variable worth naming. Younger siblings on different school runs pull a household's afternoon in two directions, and the maths slot is usually the one that gives way. If that is your situation, the weekend-led pattern described further down this page will survive where a weekday one will not.

sections.heading: Which maths syllabus your child is actually sitting
paragraphs: There are four maths codes a Satwa IGCSE student is realistically entered for, and they are different exams. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580. Cambridge International Mathematics is 0607. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A is 4MA1, and Further Pure Mathematics is 4PM1. The code appears on the statement of entry the school issues to each candidate.

The differences are practical rather than academic trivia. Syllabus 0607 assumes a graphics calculator throughout and includes an investigation strand, so a 0607 candidate has to be fluent at reading a calculator display, stating a range and identifying an asymptote. Syllabus 0580 does not make that assumption. A student taught on 0580 past papers for a 0607 entry arrives at the real paper with sound mathematics and an unfamiliar format, which costs marks that look like carelessness and are not.

Pearson's 4MA1 provides a different formula sheet from Cambridge 0580, which changes the memorisation load directly. Any revision list that tells a student which formulae to learn is only correct for one code. The reliable method is to open the formula pages of the actual paper and work from those, and that is a five-minute job in a first session that saves weeks of misdirected effort.

Ask the school three questions and the matching problem disappears: which code is my child entered for, which tier, and which administrative zone does the centre sit in. The third one matters because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

sections.heading: Core and Extended are two different exams
paragraphs: Cambridge 0580 and 0607 each run a Core and an Extended tier. The tiers do not sit the same papers and they do not reach the same grades. The entry is made by the school ahead of the series deadline, and once it is made, the ceiling is set for that series. This is the most consequential decision in IGCSE maths and most families meet it as a line on a form rather than as a decision.

Read the tiering detail on the syllabus document for your child's specific code at cambridgeinternational.org rather than from any tutoring site, including this one, because syllabuses are revised and a stale restatement is worse than no statement. What is stable is the shape of the consequence: a student entered at the lower tier cannot reach the upper grades in that series, and the remedy after the deadline is a resit in the next series rather than a change of paper.

Where tutoring money does real work is before the entry. Two or three diagnostic sessions in the first term of Year 10, run against the actual papers for each tier, give a parent something concrete to put in front of the subject teacher. That conversation is far more productive when it is about a specific question the child could and could not do than when it is about a general impression of ability.

Pearson behaves differently. Several Pearson International GCSE subjects are untiered, and some operate modular assessment where units can be sat across series. For maths that changes when support is best concentrated — modular routes reward a push before each unit rather than an even spread across two years. Confirm with the school which structure applies before planning the year.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE maths marks actually go missing
paragraphs: A student losing marks in IGCSE maths is almost never losing them evenly. The losses cluster, and a tutor who cannot name the cluster after reading one mock script is not worth a weekly slot. The most common clusters, in rough order of how many marks they cost, are algebraic rearrangement, multi-topic problems, convention errors, and visible method.

Algebraic rearrangement is the foundation and the biggest single source of loss, because it hides inside questions labelled as geometry, mechanics or statistics. A student who can solve a tidy linear equation and freezes when the subject has to be made from a formula containing a fraction will lose marks across the whole paper rather than in one topic. Repairing it moves more marks per hour than any other intervention in the course.

Convention errors are the cheapest losses to fix and the most annoying to watch. Bearings written in two figures instead of three, or anticlockwise instead of clockwise. A transformation described as a rotation without its angle, direction and centre. An angle-reasoning answer that is numerically correct and does not name the circle theorem the mark scheme requires. Frequency density calculated as frequency. Each is worth one to three marks and each takes one focused session to eliminate permanently.

Visible method is the quiet one. Method marks are awarded for working that an examiner can see, and a confident student who calculates mentally and writes only the answer loses them even when the answer is right. Rounding instructions, units on the final line and the required accuracy conventions add to the same pile. Across a full paper this category alone regularly accounts for the difference between two grades.

sections.heading: Building a weekly pattern that survives to the series
paragraphs: A term is about fourteen teaching weeks. The pattern that works is one that still runs in week twelve, and the main threats to it in a Satwa household are the school run, school assessment weeks, Ramadan, and a parent's own work travel. Planning for all four at the start costs nothing; discovering them one at a time costs the slot.

Start with one hour a week, not two. A single session with properly set practice between sessions does more than two sessions with nothing in between, because maths is consolidated by doing rather than by watching. The practice should be short, specific and marked — fifteen to twenty-five minutes on the named topic, looked at before the next session, so the tutor starts from evidence rather than from a question about how the week went.

Protect the slot through the school's own assessment weeks instead of cancelling it. Those are precisely the weeks when a diagnosis is available for free, because a real marked script exists. The temptation is to pause tutoring to make room for revision, which removes the one person who could tell the student which revision to do.

Ramadan shifts the whole household rhythm and the school day shortens. The practical answer in this district is to move the maths slot to after Iftar, or to the late morning at weekends, and to accept a lighter week in the final days. Agree the shift before the month starts. Families who plan it keep their pattern; families who improvise lose three weeks and then try to recover them in the term before the series.

sections.heading: What IGCSE maths support costs in this market
paragraphs: Nobody in this cluster of search results publishes a price in dirhams, so here are the market bands with the providers who published them. Budget online tutoring runs from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from about AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits between AED 150 and 300, and Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above; TutorChase lists AED 270. In-home one-to-one visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, Bestimate putting the usual range at AED 180 to 350. The premium named tier starts around AED 500 and BartyED asks AED 650.

For a weekly one-hour arrangement, Bestimate's monthly estimates are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Packages seen in Dubai include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. These are market figures, not an IB Gram price list; IB Gram's own arrangement starts with a free lesson, so the diagnosis costs nothing before the rest is priced.

The travel element is where this district differs from a Dubai average. A tutor driving to Al Satwa for a 17:00 start is in the worst window of the day in both directions, and that is inside the quoted in-home rate. The dirham cost of it is visible; the invisible cost is that the pool of tutors willing to make the drive is small, so the premium can buy a weaker teacher than the mid online band would have provided for less.

One honest note on the top of the market. A premium rate is sometimes justified by describing a tutor as an examiner. Examiner status is only meaningful if it can be evidenced, and it confers no access to marking, grade boundaries or unreleased paper content. A family paying at that level should be able to see what the extra buys in teaching terms.

sections.heading: Calculator, formula sheet and the things schools assume
paragraphs: Three pieces of equipment decide a surprising number of marks, and schools tend to assume a family already knows about them. The first is the calculator. Cambridge 0607 assumes a graphics calculator throughout, and a student who owns one but has never been taught to use it under time pressure is slower than a student with a scientific calculator and better habits. Knowing how to store a value, set a window and read a point of intersection are examinable skills in practice even where they are not named as such.

The second is the formula provision. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 provide different formulae, so the memorisation list differs by code. The right move is to print the formula pages from the actual paper your child will sit and work from those, rather than from a generic revision list found online. This is a ten-minute job and it is routinely skipped.

The third is the exam rubric on each paper: which paper allows what, how many marks it carries, how long it runs. Students who have never read the front of a past paper walk into the real one with assumptions. Reading the rubric aloud once, early, removes a whole category of avoidable loss.

A note on materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson. The correct behaviour for any tutor or platform is to reference them and link to the official source rather than hosting or supplying copies, which is why this page points to cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com instead.

sections.heading: The June and November series counted backwards
paragraphs: Working forwards from today produces a vague plan. Working backwards from the series produces a schedule, because the decisions that matter are locked by entry deadlines rather than by exam dates. This is the table no competitor in this market publishes, and it is the most useful thing on the page for a Year 10 parent.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask your child's school which zone its centre sits in and then read the timetable for that zone.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. For June 2026, results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so always read the live official timetable rather than a restatement.

Working backwards from a June series, the useful milestones are these: the entry deadline, which fixes tier and subject count; the mock window, which is the first honest read on position; the point eight to twelve weeks out, after which only preparation remains; and the results release, which is when a November resit decision has to be taken quickly because that entry deadline follows soon after.

sections.heading: Starting, and what a tutor will not do with coursework
paragraphs: Getting started is four lines of information and one free lesson. The four lines are the school, the year group, the maths code and tier from the statement of entry, and what the last piece of marked work looked like. With those, the free first session can be spent on diagnosis rather than on introductions, and you finish it with a list of named topics you can price work against.

If the specialist you need is not free in the slot you need, you get told. Cover is thinner in some combinations than others — 0607 Extended and 4PM1 Further Pure are narrower pools than 0580 Extended. The honest options are a short wait, a different weekly slot that opens a wider pool, or a tutor outside the UAE working on Gulf Standard Time for the same code. What should not happen is a general maths tutor taking a 0607 student because the calendar had a gap.

On coursework and assessed work the line is firm, and it is worth stating on a maths page even though IGCSE maths has no coursework component in most codes. A tutor may teach content, explain assessment criteria in the board's own words, model a method on a different example, and give feedback on work the student has written. A tutor may not write, complete, rewrite or edit assessed work to completion. One operator in this market sells finished Internal Assessments; the consequence of that lands on the student, not on the seller.

Finally, two things nobody should be promising you. No tutor can promise a grade, a number of marks or an improvement in an externally assessed examination, and any provider claiming it is describing their marketing rather than their teaching. And tutoring is not required for Ministry of Education equivalency, for university admission or for school progression — anyone implying otherwise is selling urgency.

process.title: Send the code, not just the subject
process.description: School, year group, and the maths syllabus code and tier from the statement of entry — 0580 Extended, 0607 Core, 4MA1, 4PM1. One email to the school office produces it. Sending it with the first enquiry removes two sessions of guesswork from a paid arrangement and gets the match right first time.

process.title: Pick the slot against your worst week
process.description: Look at the last two weeks of actual arrival times rather than the published school finish. Set the lesson at least forty-five minutes after the latest of them. For most Satwa clusters that means 17:00; for Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim it means 18:00. A slot chosen optimistically is a slot abandoned by October.

process.title: Use the free lesson for diagnosis
process.description: The first session costs nothing and should end with named topics: rearrangement is the gap, bearings convention is costing marks, method is not being written down. That list is what you price work against. A trial that ends in enthusiasm and an offer of ten sessions has produced nothing you can spend against.

process.title: Agree the practice, not just the lesson
process.description: Fifteen to twenty-five minutes of specific practice between sessions, looked at before the next one. Maths consolidates by doing. A session that starts from marked evidence is worth noticeably more than one that starts from a conversation about how the week went.

process.title: Review at the entry deadline and the mocks
process.description: Those are the two points where a review changes anything: the deadline fixes tier and subject count, and the mock script is the first honest read on position. Reviewing on a monthly billing cycle reviews the invoice rather than the plan.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled around the bus
whyPoints.description: Satwa has almost no secondary schools of its own, so every lesson time has to be set against a commute. Slots are agreed against the latest realistic arrival rather than the published school finish, with a stated rule for the week the bus runs twenty minutes late.

whyPoints.title: Matched by code and tier
whyPoints.description: 0580 Core, 0580 Extended, 0607, 4MA1 and 4PM1 are different papers with different calculator assumptions and formula provision. The match is built from the code on the statement of entry, not from the phrase 'IGCSE maths'.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis in the free lesson
whyPoints.description: The first session is free and exists to produce a list of named topics. Buying a block of hours and asking a tutor to work through the syllabus teaches a student the things they could already do, in syllabus order.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published, with sources
whyPoints.description: AED bands attributed to the providers that published them, with the date. Three of the six most visible competitors in this market publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars, which is not what a Dubai family pays in.

whyPoints.title: The delivery limit is stated upfront
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one and online. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are offered only in India. If a child needs somebody physically in the room, that is a real requirement and this is not the service for it.

whyPoints.title: No promises about grades
whyPoints.description: Nobody here will tell you a grade is assured. What can be committed to is a named diagnosis, marked practice between sessions, a written note after each lesson, and an honest answer when the right specialist is not available.

faqs.question: What time should an IGCSE maths lesson start for a family living in Al Satwa?
faqs.answer: For most Satwa households, 17:00 on the Oud Metha, Al Mankhool and Jumeirah runs, and 18:00 for the Al Safa, Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim runs. Satwa has almost no secondary schools inside it, so every child commutes, and a looping bus route routinely turns a 15:00 finish into a 16:15 arrival. Set the slot at least forty-five minutes after the latest arrival you have actually seen in the past fortnight, not after the published finish time. Slots chosen optimistically slip by fifteen minutes a week and are quietly abandoned by the third month.

faqs.question: How do I find out which maths syllabus code my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: It is printed on the statement of entry the school issues for the series, and one email to the school office will produce it. The four you are likely to see are Cambridge 0580 for IGCSE Mathematics, Cambridge 0607 for International Mathematics, Pearson 4MA1 for International GCSE Mathematics A, and Pearson 4PM1 for Further Pure. Ask for the tier as well — Core or Extended — because the tier decides the grade range available in that series. Those two pieces of information are what a tutor should be matched against, rather than the phrase IGCSE maths.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge 0607 really different enough from 0580 to matter?
faqs.answer: Yes, enough to cost marks. Syllabus 0607 assumes a graphics calculator throughout and carries an investigation strand, so candidates have to read a calculator display confidently, state a range, and identify an asymptote. Syllabus 0580 makes no such assumption. A student taught on 0580 past papers for a 0607 entry arrives with sound mathematics and an unfamiliar format, and loses marks that look like carelessness. Check the code on the statement of entry and make sure the practice papers match it from the first session.

faqs.question: My son writes almost no working and still gets most answers right. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It is one of the most common reasons a capable student lands two grades below their ability. Method marks are awarded for working an examiner can see, and a student who calculates mentally forfeits them even when the final answer is correct. The moment a question gets long enough that the mental route breaks, there is also nothing on the page to earn partial credit. This is a habit problem rather than a maths problem, which means it responds quickly: a few weeks of insisting on written lines usually fixes it permanently.

faqs.question: Which single topic gives the biggest improvement if we only fix one thing?
faqs.answer: Rearranging a formula that contains a fraction. Algebraic manipulation is the foundation the rest of the paper stands on, and it hides inside questions labelled as geometry, statistics or ratio. A student who can solve a tidy linear equation and stalls when a subject must be made from a formula loses marks across the whole paper rather than in one identifiable topic. Fixing it moves more marks per hour of tutoring than any other single intervention in the course, and it is usually a matter of practised technique rather than new understanding.

faqs.question: Should my daughter be entered for Core or Extended maths?
faqs.answer: That decision belongs to the school and is made before the series entry deadline, but a parent can make the conversation far more useful. The tiers sit different papers and reach different grade ranges, and after the deadline the ceiling for that series is fixed. Two or three diagnostic sessions in the first term of Year 10, run against the actual papers for both tiers, give you a specific account of what your child could and could not do. Read the tiering detail on the syllabus document for her exact code at cambridgeinternational.org rather than from any tutoring site.

faqs.question: Is one maths session a week enough, or should we book two?
faqs.answer: One, with practice attached, is better than two without. Maths consolidates by doing rather than by watching, so an hour a week plus fifteen to twenty-five minutes of specific marked practice between sessions outperforms two unsupported hours. Two sessions also double the number of chances the school run has to break the arrangement, and in a district where every child commutes that is a real risk. Start at one, keep it consistent for a term, and add a second only if the diagnosis says the volume of content rather than the technique is the constraint.

faqs.question: We have a long commute from Umm Suqeim. Would weekend sessions work better?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. On the Umm Suqeim and Al Barsha runs a child frequently reaches Satwa after 16:30, and an evening lesson competes with homework, siblings and exhaustion. A longer weekend session carrying the teaching, plus a short midweek check-in to catch a misunderstanding before a week of practice embeds it, is a pattern that survives where a weekday-only arrangement does not. It also means the main teaching happens when nobody is watching the clock for a bus.

faqs.question: What happens to the maths slot during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: The school day shortens and the household rhythm changes, so the slot moves rather than stops. In this district the two workable options are a session after Iftar, or late morning at the weekend, with a lighter week accepted in the final days of the month. The important part is agreeing it before the month begins. Families who plan the shift keep their weekly pattern; families who improvise lose two or three weeks and then try to recover them in the term before the series, which is the most expensive place to do it.

faqs.question: Should we pause tutoring during the school's own assessment weeks?
faqs.answer: No, those are among the most valuable weeks to keep it. An internal assessment produces a real marked script, which is free diagnostic evidence of exactly where the marks went. Pausing removes the one person who could read that script and tell your child which revision to do. The usual instinct is to clear the diary to make room for revision; the better move is to keep the hour and spend it analysing the mark scheme against what was actually written.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE maths tutor cost in Dubai at the moment?
faqs.answer: Market figures as of October 2026: budget online runs about AED 33 to 65 an hour, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. A qualified online subject tutor sits between AED 150 and 300, Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase listing AED 270. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 including travel. Those belong to the providers named, not to IB Gram; the first lesson here is free, so the diagnosis costs nothing before anything is priced.

faqs.question: Why is in-home maths tutoring quoted higher for a district like Satwa?
faqs.answer: Because the travel is inside the rate and the window is bad. A tutor driving into Al Satwa for a 17:00 start crosses the city in the worst traffic of the day in both directions, and in-home rates in Dubai are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online tutor. The larger cost is not the dirhams. It is that the pool of tutors willing to make that drive is small, so a travel premium can end up buying a weaker teacher than the mid online band would have given you.

faqs.question: Does my child need a graphics calculator, and when should we buy it?
faqs.answer: If the entry is Cambridge 0607, yes, and early enough to become fluent with it rather than the week before a mock. The syllabus assumes a graphics calculator throughout, and the examinable skills in practice include storing a value, setting a sensible window and reading a point of intersection under time pressure. A student who owns one and has never used it under a clock is slower than a student with a scientific calculator and better habits. For 0580 and 4MA1, check the rubric on the front of the actual past papers for what each paper permits.

faqs.question: When do the Pearson International GCSE maths exams and results actually fall?
faqs.answer: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. For the June 2026 series, results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so read the live official timetable on qualifications.pearson.com rather than any restatement, including this one, before you plan around a date.

faqs.question: What is a Cambridge exam zone, and why should a Satwa parent care?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, and the timetable differs by zone. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. That is a real, avoidable risk sitting behind one question to the school office: which zone is our centre in. Ask it once, write the answer down, and read the timetable for that zone rather than the first one a search returns.

faqs.question: What if no tutor is free for my child's exact code and tier?
faqs.answer: You should be told, not quietly matched to whoever is available. Some pools are narrower than others — 0607 Extended and 4PM1 Further Pure are thinner than 0580 Extended. The honest options are a short wait for the right person, a different weekly slot that opens a wider pool, or a tutor outside the UAE working on Gulf Standard Time for the same code. A general maths tutor taking a 0607 candidate because the calendar had a gap is how a family pays specialist money for generalist teaching.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-satwa.closingHeading: Fix the time first, then fix the maths
dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-satwa.closingBody: Two things make IGCSE maths support work for an Al Satwa family, and neither is a teaching method. The first is a lesson time that survives the worst week of the term rather than the best — for most clusters here that means 17:00, and 18:00 on the long runs. The second is the syllabus code and tier from the statement of entry, so the practice papers match the real exam from day one. Send those two things and take the free first lesson; it exists to produce a list of named topics you can plan against. Lessons are one-to-one, live online, on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Start from the monthly number, not the hourly rate
paragraphs: Hourly rates make tutoring look cheap and monthly totals make it real. A parent in Al Sufouh quoted AED 250 an hour hears a number that feels manageable; the same parent six months later is spending AED 2,000 a month across two subjects and wondering where the decision happened. So this page runs the other way round. Bestimate's Dubai estimates for a weekly one-hour session put the budget end at AED 240 to AED 600 a month, the mid-market at AED 600 to AED 1,200, and specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above. Published packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are market figures read in October 2026, attributed to who published them, not an IB Gram price list.

Converted back to an hour, the same market splits into bands. Budget online tutoring advertises from AED 33 to AED 52 at Tutopiya and from AED 45 to AED 65 at EdFlik, usually delivered by current university students. A qualified subject tutor online is quoted from AED 150 by Unitors for IGCSE. Specialists sit at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to AED 350 by Bestimate, and independently advertised home tutors run AED 200 to AED 500. Premium named tutors reach AED 650 at BartyED.

What makes maths different from the other subjects in this catchment is that the monthly figure is partly decided by something administrative. Your child is entered for a specific syllabus at a specific tier, and that entry sets a grade ceiling and a past-paper diet. Cambridge 0580 splits into Core and Extended, and Core caps at grade C, or 5 on the numeric variant. Pearson 4MA1 splits into Foundation and Higher, with Foundation topping out at grade 5. A student sitting Core who is capable of Extended is paying for tuition against a ceiling. A student pushed onto Extended who is not ready is paying for content they will not reach.

There are four maths qualifications in common use in Al Sufouh schools and the surrounding Al Barsha and Greens clusters, and they are not interchangeable. Cambridge 0580 Mathematics is the most entered. Cambridge 0607 International Mathematics assumes a graphic display calculator throughout and includes an investigation paper. Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics sits alongside 0580 for strong mathematicians heading towards A Level. Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Specification A runs two equally weighted papers of a hundred marks each, two hours apiece, with a calculator permitted. A tutor matched to the wrong one of those spends your first month learning the difference.

IB Gram's delivery model is stated the same way on every UAE page. Tuition here is one-to-one online tuition over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is offered only in India. For a monthly budget that matters in a concrete way: the travel component embedded in the in-home band, somewhere between AED 50 and AED 150 an hour on published figures, never appears on the bill, and the money buys teaching hours instead of kilometres.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-sufouh.programmesIntro: Maths support in this catchment is bought at three points, and the price per mark differs sharply between them. The earlier the point, the cheaper the outcome, which is the one piece of financial advice this page would give if it could only give one.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary maths, before the tier decision
programmes.description: The cheapest maths tutoring a family will ever buy, because it removes gaps rather than patching them against a deadline. The work here is algebraic fluency, proportional reasoning, negative and fractional indices, and confidence with formula rearrangement. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests are available in March, May and October and give a school a cohort benchmark rather than a certificate, so they are a diagnostic rather than a qualification.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Sufouh this band is routinely skipped because nothing is at stake yet. The arithmetic is unkind: a Year 9 student who cannot rearrange a formula reliably will meet that same weakness in 0580 Paper 4, in 0625 Physics and in 0620 Chemistry at the same time eighteen months later, and will then need three tutors instead of one. Three mid-band subjects is AED 1,800 to AED 3,600 a month.

programmes.name: IGCSE mathematics, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Two years to cover a full syllabus and to build paper technique. Cambridge 0580 runs Core and Extended tiers with separate papers; Pearson 4MA1 runs Foundation and Higher with two papers of a hundred marks each. Extended and Higher carry the algebraic manipulation, the trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles, and the vectors and transformations work the lower tiers never meet. Calculator rules have been revised by Cambridge, so the current syllabus document should be checked rather than assumed.
programmes.countryNote: Most Al Sufouh families buy here, and most buy in Year 11 rather than Year 10. Buying in September of Year 10 at one session a week is roughly AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month on the mid band and covers a syllabus properly. Buying in February of Year 11 at three sessions a week costs two to three times that monthly figure and can only triage.

programmes.name: Additional Mathematics and the A Level bridge
programmes.description: Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics runs two papers of two hours each with a calculator permitted, and covers calculus, binomial expansions, trigonometric identities and vectors in a way 0580 does not. Schools enter strong mathematicians for it alongside 0580 as preparation for A Level Mathematics or IB Analysis and Approaches. It is a genuine step up in abstraction rather than a longer version of the same syllabus.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai College and the British-pathway schools around Al Sufouh use this route for students heading towards A Level Mathematics and Further Mathematics. Where a family is paying for 0606 support, it is worth establishing whether the real target is the 0606 grade or the A Level start, because those two aims produce different session plans.

programmes.name: November series resits and private candidacy
programmes.description: A maths grade that falls short in June can be retaken in the November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge runs June and November for UAE candidates; the February and March series is offered to India only. A resit decision is a budget decision taken in August with a January payoff.
programmes.countryNote: Families in this catchment usually make the resit call within a fortnight of August results, which gives roughly eight to ten weeks of preparation. At two sessions a week on the mid band that is about AED 1,200 to AED 2,400 a month. Whether it is worth buying depends on whether a January grade still helps the application it was meant to support.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-sufouh.subjectsIntro: Maths is one word and several qualifications. The entries below are the specific maths and maths-adjacent syllabuses Al Sufouh families ask about, with the code attached, because the code is what decides which past papers a session uses.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: The most entered maths syllabus in this catchment. Extended carries algebraic fractions, functions, trigonometry in non-right-angled triangles, vectors and transformations. Core caps at grade C, or 5 on the numeric variant. Most lost marks are method rather than knowledge: unsimplified answers, premature rounding, and omitted units in mensuration questions.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607
subjects.description: A separate syllabus assuming a graphic display calculator throughout, with an investigation paper that has no 0580 equivalent. Students taught from 0580 materials meet unfamiliar graphing question styles and lose marks for describing a sketch rather than reading values off it. A tutor unaware the syllabus exists will teach 0580 at a 0607 candidate for a term.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: Two papers of two hours with a calculator permitted, covering calculus, binomial expansion, trigonometric identities, logarithms and vectors. Entered alongside 0580 for students heading to A Level or IB Analysis and Approaches. The difficulty is abstraction rather than volume, and students who rely on memorised procedures stall quickly here.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, 4MA1
subjects.description: Two papers of a hundred marks each, two hours apiece, calculator permitted, with Foundation capped at grade 5. Question styles and mark-scheme conventions differ from Cambridge, so a tutor who has only taught 0580 will mark against the wrong expectations. Higher-tier algebra and the proof-style questions are where the tier gap shows most.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Further Pure Mathematics, 4PM1
subjects.description: The Pearson parallel to Additional Mathematics, taken alongside 4MA1 by students aiming at A Level Mathematics. It carries calculus, series, coordinate geometry and matrices. Families sometimes discover their child is entered for it only when a mock paper appears, which is a sign the entry list is worth asking for explicitly.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 · Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Requested alongside maths more than any other subject, because the formula rearrangement and graph-gradient work are shared. A student who manipulates equations confidently in maths and cannot convert a gradient into a physical quantity with units has a transfer problem, and fixing it once in a maths session is cheaper than fixing it twice.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 · Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: The moles work, concentration calculations and empirical formula questions sit on exactly the proportional reasoning 0580 builds. Students strong in maths who struggle in chemistry are usually weak on the qualitative material and the ionic equations rather than on calculation, which is a different tutoring job.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 · Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content volume rather than conceptual depth, with marks lost to imprecise command-term responses. The statistical and graph-reading elements reward the same care maths does, and the magnification and surface-area-to-volume calculations are straightforward marks for a numerate student who practises them.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (Cambridge 0455 · 0450)
subjects.description: Both are marked against levels rather than points, so evaluation matters more than recall. Numerate students often perform well on the calculation and diagram questions and cap out on the judgement command terms, which is a writing problem presenting as a subject problem.

subjects.name: Arabic and the UAE mandatory subjects
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run in every Dubai private school alongside the licensed international curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited.

sections.heading: A month of IGCSE maths support in Dubai, priced
paragraphs: The table below converts the market's hourly bands into the monthly figures a household plans against, using one, two and three sessions a week. Every band is attributed and every figure was read in October 2026. None of it is an IB Gram price list; Dubai has no published standard rate for private tuition, so the only honest way to show cost is to show who charges what and when it was read.

Two patterns are worth noticing. The cheapest row and the dearest row differ by roughly a factor of fifteen at the same session count. Budget online tuition from AED 33 to AED 65 an hour is a legitimate product for a Year 9 confidence problem and a poor one for Extended-tier Paper 4 technique, because the person delivering it is often a current university student working from the student's own textbook. The second pattern is that stepping from one session a week to three does not triple a grade's prospects; it triples a bill while leaving the same number of hours for everything else in the student's week.

The practical reading for an Al Sufouh family is that the sensible plan is usually one weekly session from early in Year 10 at the mid band, with a short step up before the series. That shape costs less across two years than a February panic at three sessions a week, and it buys full syllabus coverage rather than triage. Bestimate's own monthly estimates follow the same logic: AED 240 to AED 600 budget, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support, all at weekly one-hour sessions.

Package pricing is the other thing to read carefully. Published packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, which is a lower effective hourly figure, and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. A package is cheaper per hour and less forgiving: if the school's assessment calendar shifts or the family travels, unused sessions are the hidden cost, and that cost does not appear in the headline.

sections.heading: The tier decision, and the price attached to getting it wrong
paragraphs: Maths is the subject where an administrative choice sets a ceiling, and in Al Sufouh that choice is often discovered rather than made. Cambridge 0580 is entered at Core or Extended. Core caps at grade C, or 5 on the numeric variant, and its papers exclude a block of content Extended requires. Pearson 4MA1 is entered at Foundation or Higher, with Foundation capped at grade 5 and Higher running to 9. The entry is made by the centre, usually confirmed in the first half of Year 11, and it is written on the statement of entry.

Both errors cost money in different ways. A student entered at the lower tier who is capable of the higher one is paying for tuition against a ceiling: no amount of teaching produces a grade the paper cannot award. A student pushed onto the higher tier without the algebraic foundation is paying for content they will not reach in the time available, and will usually have sat a whole year of past papers at the wrong difficulty. The second error is the more common in this catchment, because ambition is cheap in September.

The question is answerable with evidence rather than opinion, and the evidence is a timed past paper at each tier marked against the published mark scheme. That is one or two sessions. On the mid band it is AED 150 to AED 600, against a decision that governs eighteen months of work and the entire post-sixteen conversation. It is the single highest-return hour available in IGCSE maths, and it has to happen before the centre's entry deadline rather than after.

Where the tier is already fixed and wrong, the honest answer is to stop paying for the ceiling and redirect. A Core candidate who is clearly stronger than the tier should have the entry discussed with the school. Where a change is not possible, the sensible plan is to secure every available mark at that tier and to spend the remaining budget on the subject where the ceiling is not the constraint.

sections.heading: Four maths qualifications, four different bills
paragraphs: A parent who asks for maths help and does not name the code is buying a lottery ticket. The four qualifications in common use around Al Sufouh are Cambridge 0580 Mathematics, Cambridge 0607 International Mathematics, Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Specification A, with Pearson 4PM1 Further Pure Mathematics appearing in some strong sets. They differ in paper structure, in calculator assumptions and in the kind of question a student has to recognise.

The 0607 case is the most expensive misunderstanding available. International Mathematics assumes a graphic display calculator throughout and includes an investigation paper that 0580 has no equivalent of. A student entered for 0607 who is taught from 0580 resources will sit unfamiliar graphing questions and will lose marks describing a sketch rather than reading values off it. Four sessions of the wrong material is roughly AED 600 to AED 1,800 at the mid and specialist bands, paid and wasted.

0606 Additional Mathematics is a different kind of mismatch risk. It is entered alongside 0580 by schools preparing students for A Level, it runs two papers of two hours each with a calculator permitted, and it covers calculus, binomial expansion, trigonometric identities and vectors. Tutors who are comfortable with 0580 are not automatically comfortable here, because the difficulty is abstraction rather than volume. A family paying for 0606 support should ask directly whether the tutor has taught the syllabus.

Pearson 4MA1 differs from Cambridge in mark-scheme conventions as much as in content. Two papers of a hundred marks each, two hours apiece, calculator permitted, Foundation and Higher tiers. A tutor who has only taught Cambridge will mark a 4MA1 response against the wrong expectations for method and presentation. The remedy costs nothing: ask for the statement of entry, read the code off it, and say the code out loud in the first conversation.

sections.heading: Which topics eat the sessions, and what each costs to fix
paragraphs: A monthly budget is really a session count, and a session count is really a list of topics. The table below is built from where Extended and Higher tier candidates in this catchment most reliably lose marks, with a realistic number of sessions to repair each and a cost at the mid-market band of AED 150 to AED 300 an hour. It is an estimate of work rather than a promise about a grade; no tutor can promise a grade and nobody should accept a quote that implies one.

The pattern across the rows is that the expensive topics are the ones built on something earlier. Algebraic fractions are not hard in themselves; they are hard for a student who is shaky on factorising, and the session count doubles because the prerequisite has to be rebuilt first. Trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles behaves the same way: the sine and cosine rules take one session to teach and three to make reliable, because reliability depends on the algebra underneath.

The cheap rows are worth as much per dirham. Rounding and accuracy, units in mensuration, and giving answers in the form the question demanded are pure technique, and they recur across every paper. A student losing six marks a paper to premature rounding is losing a grade boundary's worth of marks to something fixable in two sessions. That is the highest-return work in IGCSE maths and it is almost never what a parent asks for, because it does not feel like teaching.

What this table is for is a conversation with a tutor rather than a purchase order. Bring a marked mock paper, identify which of these rows it reveals, and agree a plan against them. A tutoring arrangement that cannot name which rows it is working on by the third session is an arrangement without a diagnosis, and that is where monthly costs drift upward without anything changing.

sections.heading: What a resit costs, in money and in months
paragraphs: Some of the most expensive maths tutoring in Dubai is bought in August, and much of it is bought without a clear view of what the November grade will be used for. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only, which matters because general advice circulating online quotes its dates to Gulf parents. Working the decision through properly takes twenty minutes and saves a month of fees.

The datable anchors are Pearson's. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November each year, the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including the International GCSE November series not yet sat, and those can be revised, so the live official timetable is the only safe reference.

The arithmetic of a resit is therefore this. Results arrive in the third week of August. The November papers sit from late October. That is roughly eight to ten weeks. At two sessions a week on the mid band it is around AED 1,200 to AED 2,400 a month, so AED 2,400 to AED 6,000 for the block, with specialist rates higher. The new grade arrives in January. If the application the grade was meant to support closes before January, the money buys a corrected transcript rather than an opened door, and that may still be worth it, but it should be a decision rather than a reflex.

Cambridge candidates should add one step. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and its exams officers' guide is explicit that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, because Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask the exams officer for the zone and the dated timetable in the same email as the entry confirmation. A paper sitting two days earlier than assumed rewrites the last fortnight of a paid intensive block.

sections.heading: Group, centre or one-to-one for maths in this catchment
paragraphs: Group tuition is the obvious way to cut a monthly bill, and for maths it works under one condition that Al Sufouh rarely satisfies. Every student in the group has to sit the same board, the same tier, and share the weakness being worked on. At AED 80 to AED 180 per student per hour against AED 150 to AED 450 for one-to-one, the saving is real when that condition holds.

It rarely holds here because the catchment splits. Within a single Year 11 cohort at a school near Al Sufouh you will find 0580 Extended candidates, 0580 Core candidates, 0607 candidates and, in schools using Pearson, 4MA1 Higher and Foundation candidates. A group containing an Extended student and a Foundation student is two lessons delivered at once, and both are delivered badly. The parent paying the lower rate has not saved money; they have bought a different product.

Tuition centres sit between the two. A centre with a fixed timetable and a rostered tutor can be effective where the student needs structure and company more than they need precision, and the published monthly packages in this market reflect that positioning. What a centre cannot usually offer is a tutor matched to 0607 or to 4PM1, because the roster is built around the commonest entries.

The honest summary is that one-to-one is the right purchase where the problem is specific and the code is unusual, and group work is the right purchase where the problem is shared and the code is common. Most Al Sufouh maths requests fall into the first category, which is why the monthly numbers in this page's first table are the ones families end up planning against.

sections.heading: Where maths tutoring money is wasted in Al Sufouh
paragraphs: The waste in this market is not usually overpayment. It is correct payment for the wrong work, and there are four recurring versions of it in this catchment.

The first is the uncoded match, already covered: a tutor teaching 0580 to a 0607 candidate, or Cambridge conventions to a Pearson entry. The second is unmarked practice. A student who completes eight past papers and marks them himself will report good scores and will keep repeating the same method errors, because self-marking cannot catch what the candidate does not know is wrong. Marking against the published mark scheme is slow and it is where the diagnostic value lives. If an arrangement contains no marked timed papers by January of Year 11, the family is buying teaching without assessment.

The third is duplication. Al Sufouh schools run their own maths clinics, intervention sets and after-school sessions, and those are inside fees already paid. A tutor repeating Thursday's clinic content is being paid to deliver free provision again. One email to the subject teacher asking what the school already runs frequently removes a weekly session from the plan without removing support, which is AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month at the mid band.

The fourth is scope creep, and it is the expensive one. A family that engages maths help in October regularly holds three weekly sessions across three subjects by February, because every new assessment produces a new worry. Three subjects at the mid band is AED 1,800 to AED 3,600 a month and eleven commitments in a student's week. Deciding in advance how many subjects will be supported, writing it down, and accepting that the other grades will be what they will be is a cost control and usually an academic improvement too.

sections.heading: What a parent can verify for nothing before paying
paragraphs: Four checks, all free, all worth more than any marketing claim. The first is the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, listing no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Because it costs nothing, a quote that itemises a licensing charge should be questioned.

The second is the accreditation claim. IB Gram holds no accreditation from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none. A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a specific document with a number on it. Any provider describing itself as approved by a regulator or a board should be asked to produce it.

The third is the rate source. Ask where a quoted market figure came from and when it was read. Three of the six competitor pages researched in this cluster publish no price at all, and two of the others quote in US dollars, which is not a currency a Dubai household transacts in. One publishes a schema price range that contradicts the figure on its own page. A provider who cannot date a number is not giving you evidence.

The fourth is the honesty boundary on coursework. A tutor teaches, explains, questions and gives feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor does not write, complete, draft or produce assessed work, and where a school requires an authenticity declaration the candidate signs it. One operator in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price; buying that places a malpractice exposure on the student rather than on the seller. For maths at IGCSE the exposure is smaller than at Diploma level but the principle is the same.

process.title: Read the code off the statement of entry
process.description: The statement of entry names the board, the syllabus code and the tier for every subject. Reading 0580 Extended or 4MA1 Higher off that document and saying it in the first conversation removes the most expensive mistake in this market before any money changes hands. The exams officer can confirm it in writing if the document has gone missing.

process.title: Sit one timed past paper first
process.description: Before buying anything, have the student sit a full past paper at the entered tier under timed conditions. Bring it to the diagnostic session unmarked. That single paper tells a tutor which of the topic rows in this page's table apply, and it converts a vague worry into a session plan with a count attached.

process.title: Take the free trial, then agree a monthly figure
process.description: One lesson, one subject, booked before any payment is taken. Afterwards, agree the monthly number rather than the hourly rate, and agree how many subjects will be supported. Writing both down is what prevents the February drift from one weekly session into three across three subjects.

process.title: Ask the school what it already provides
process.description: Maths clinics, intervention sets and after-school sessions are inside fees already paid. One email to the subject teacher establishes what is running, when, and whether your child is already on a list. This regularly removes a paid weekly session from a plan without removing any support at all.

process.title: Review tier readiness before the entry deadline
process.description: Tier is decided by the centre in Year 11 and sets a grade ceiling. A timed paper at each tier, marked against the published mark scheme, settles the question with evidence. That review has to happen before the deadline, because afterwards the only remaining choice is how to work within the ceiling.

whyPoints.title: Costs shown monthly, as a household plans them
whyPoints.description: Hourly rates understate what tutoring becomes over a term. Every band on this page is converted into one, two and three sessions a week, with the publishing source and an October 2026 reading date attached, so a figure can be checked rather than taken on trust.

whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580, Cambridge 0607, Cambridge 0606 and Pearson 4MA1 are four qualifications. Confirming code and tier before the first paid session is what stops a month of sessions running against the wrong past papers and the wrong mark-scheme conventions.

whyPoints.title: Marked papers rather than self-marking
whyPoints.description: From the point syllabus coverage is reasonable, a proportion of each session is a timed paper marked against the published mark scheme. Self-marking cannot catch what a student does not know is wrong, and without marked papers a tutoring arrangement has no diagnosis to show you.
