faqs.question: What does a month of IGCSE maths tutoring cost in Al Sufouh?
faqs.answer: At one weekly one-hour session, Bestimate's Dubai estimates put the budget end at AED 240 to AED 600 a month, the mid-market at AED 600 to AED 1,200, and specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above. Published packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are market figures read in October 2026 and attributed to who published them, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Which maths syllabus is my child actually entered for?
faqs.answer: It is written on the statement of entry the school issues, and the exams officer can confirm it in writing. The four in common use around Al Sufouh are Cambridge 0580 Mathematics, Cambridge 0607 International Mathematics, Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Specification A, with 4PM1 Further Pure appearing in some strong sets. Reading the code off that document before you agree a rate is the cheapest quality control available, because the four need different past papers and different mark-scheme conventions.

faqs.question: Does the Core or Extended tier change how much tutoring my child needs?
faqs.answer: Yes, in both directions. Core on Cambridge 0580 excludes algebraic fractions, functions, non-right-angled trigonometry and vectors, so there is less to cover and the grade caps at C, or 5 on the numeric variant. Extended covers the full syllabus and runs to A*, which takes more sessions. The expensive error is a mismatch: paying for teaching against a ceiling the paper cannot exceed, or paying for content the student will not reach. One timed paper at each tier settles it with evidence.

faqs.question: Why is Cambridge 0607 taught differently from Cambridge 0580?
faqs.answer: Because it is a different syllabus. International Mathematics 0607 assumes a graphic display calculator throughout and includes an investigation paper that 0580 has no equivalent of. A 0607 candidate taught from 0580 resources meets unfamiliar graphing question styles and loses marks describing a sketch rather than reading values off it. Four sessions on the wrong material is roughly AED 600 to AED 1,800 at mid and specialist bands. Any tutor who does not know the distinction exists should not be teaching the course.

faqs.question: Is a visiting maths tutor in Al Sufouh worth the extra monthly cost?
faqs.answer: The published in-home band runs AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel, against AED 150 to AED 450 for an online specialist, so at three sessions a week that gap is several hundred dirhams a month. What the premium buys is presence, which has real value for a younger or easily distracted student. What it does not buy is subject range: restricting the pool to people who drive to Al Sufouh at your child's free hour removes most 0607 and Pearson-trained tutors. IB Gram delivers UAE lessons online only.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week should a Year 11 maths student in Al Sufouh have?
faqs.answer: One weekly session from early in Year 10 covers a syllabus properly and costs roughly AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month at the mid band. Stepping to two or three in the eight to twelve weeks before the series is normal and useful. Running three a week from February is the pattern that produces a large bill and an exhausted student, because the time has to come from somewhere. Fewer subjects supported properly beats more subjects supported thinly, and the student's remaining week is a real limit.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE maths resit in November cost and when does the grade arrive?
faqs.answer: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results went to students on 20 August 2026, which leaves roughly eight to ten weeks of preparation. At two sessions a week on the mid band that is about AED 2,400 to AED 6,000 for the block. If the application the grade was meant to support closes before January, that is worth knowing first.

faqs.question: Which maths topics cost the most sessions to fix?
faqs.answer: The ones that depend on something earlier. Algebraic fractions typically take four to six sessions, because the real gap is usually factorising rather than fractions. Trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles takes three to five, because reliability depends on the algebra underneath. Functions and transformations take three to four. The cheapest and highest-return work is rounding, accuracy and giving answers in the form demanded, which takes one or two sessions and recurs on every paper a student will ever sit.

faqs.question: Can a small maths group work out cheaper for us?
faqs.answer: Per student, group rates run AED 80 to AED 180 an hour against AED 150 to AED 450 one-to-one, so the saving is genuine when one condition holds: every student in the group sits the same board, the same tier and shares the weakness being worked. Around Al Sufouh that condition is rare, because a single Year 11 cohort contains 0580 Core, 0580 Extended, 0607 and sometimes 4MA1 candidates. A mixed group is two lessons delivered at once and both suffer.

faqs.question: Do I still need a tutor if the school runs a maths clinic?
faqs.answer: Often not for the same content. School clinics, intervention sets and after-school maths sessions are already inside the fees you pay, and a private tutor repeating Thursday's clinic material is being paid to deliver free provision twice. One email to the subject teacher asking what is running and whether your child is on a list regularly removes a weekly paid session, which is AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month at the mid band. Private support is for what the school is not covering.

faqs.question: Does a maths tutor in Dubai need a MoHRE permit, and does it raise the price?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and it adds nothing. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

faqs.question: Is self-marking past papers good enough to save on tutoring hours?
faqs.answer: It is good for fluency and poor for diagnosis. A student who marks his own work cannot catch what he does not know is wrong, which is why self-marked scores drift upward while the same method errors repeat. Marking against the published mark scheme is slow, unglamorous and where the value sits: it shows whether a lost mark was knowledge, method, accuracy or timing, and those four need different fixes. A reasonable compromise is self-marking for routine practice and tutor marking for whole timed papers.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for Cambridge 0607 or Pearson 4PM1?
faqs.answer: You get told, with a timescale, rather than matched with somebody approximate. The scarce codes in this market are 0607 International Mathematics, 0606 Additional Mathematics and 4PM1 Further Pure Mathematics, because the entries are fewer and the teaching experience is rarer. Where no match in a suitable time zone is free, the options are a tutor working an Al Sufouh-friendly evening slot from elsewhere, a short wait with a named date, or a diagnostic hour with a generalist to establish what is actually needed. Being told costs less than being matched badly.

faqs.question: Are IGCSE maths grades enough for Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: For the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking competitor states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the published rule. Verify your own case with the Ministry of Education rather than relying on any provider's summary.

faqs.question: When is the right month to start maths support for an Al Sufouh Year 10?
faqs.answer: September of Year 10, at one session a week. That shape costs roughly AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month at the mid band, covers the syllabus rather than selecting from it, and leaves time to review tier readiness before the centre's entry deadline. Starting in February of Year 11 at three sessions a week costs two to three times as much per month and can only triage. The cheapest maths tutoring is always the earliest, which is the least satisfying advice available.

faqs.question: How do I stop a maths tutoring budget from doubling by February?
faqs.answer: Decide two numbers in advance and write them down: how many subjects will be supported, and what the monthly ceiling is. Scope creep is the largest single cost in a Dubai tutoring budget, because every new school assessment produces a new worry and a new weekly session. Three subjects at the mid band is AED 1,800 to AED 3,600 a month and eleven commitments in a student's week. Accepting that some grades will be what they will be is a financial decision and usually an academic one.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-twar.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors teaching IGCSE mathematics to Year 10 and Year 11 students in Al Twar, Al Qusais and Mirdif, on Cambridge 0580 and Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A, at the tier each student is actually entered for.

intro.heading: Does your maths tutor know which paper your child will sit?
paragraphs: IGCSE mathematics is the most tutored subject in this part of Dubai, and it is also the one where a mismatch between tutor and specification does the most damage. The reason is the proportion of time spent on past papers. By the spring of Year 11 a maths tutor is mostly working through questions from previous series, and if those questions come from the wrong syllabus the student is being trained on the wrong formula provision, the wrong calculator rules and the wrong question style while appearing to make progress.

Two specifications dominate here. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is syllabus 0580, tiered Core and Extended, with the Core and Extended candidates sitting different paper sets. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A is 4MA1, offered at Foundation and Higher tier. Both are widely taught within a short drive of Al Twar, and they differ in ways that matter: which paper permits a calculator, what is printed on the formula sheet, how much of the mark total sits in the longer questions, and the phrasing conventions a mark scheme rewards.

The formula provision is the clearest example of why this is not pedantry. A student who has spent a year assuming a particular formula will be printed on the paper, and then finds it is not, loses the question and some confidence with it. A student who has been drilled to recall formulae that are in fact provided has spent revision time on something worth no marks. Neither student has a knowledge gap. Both have a specification gap, and it was free to prevent with one email to the examinations officer.

There is a second detail specific to Cambridge candidates in the UAE. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable version for each, stating that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. UAE candidates sit the June and November series; the February and March series is offered to India only, so any date from that series is irrelevant to your child.

One thing to state plainly. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. IGCSE maths tuition for an Al Twar family is delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen for worked algebra and marked past papers. For this particular problem that is the whole advantage: the tutor can be selected for teaching 0580 Extended or 4MA1 Higher every week, rather than for being the available person willing to drive to Al Twar 3 on a weekday evening.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-twar.programmesIntro: Maths at 16 is a gateway rather than an endpoint, and what follows determines how much depth is worth building now. These are the four stages around it.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
programmes.description: Tiered Core and Extended, with each tier sitting its own pair of papers and recent versions of the syllabus separating non-calculator from calculator work. Content runs across number, algebra, coordinate geometry, mensuration, trigonometry, transformations, vectors, probability and statistics.
programmes.countryNote: In this cluster 0580 is the most common entry, and the Extended tier is the one most parents assume their child is on without checking. Ask the examinations officer for the tier in writing during Year 10, because the Core ceiling cannot be lifted by any amount of Year 11 work.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1
programmes.description: Offered at Foundation and Higher tier, with two written papers per tier and its own formula provision and question conventions. Content is comparable to the Cambridge syllabus with meaningful differences in emphasis and phrasing.
programmes.countryNote: Published dates give the shape of the year: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Read the live official timetable from Pearson for current dates.

programmes.name: Additional Mathematics 0606
programmes.description: A separate Cambridge qualification sat alongside 0580 by stronger sets, overlapping early A Level content including calculus and more advanced trigonometry. It is demanding and it is genuinely useful preparation for A Level or Higher Level maths.
programmes.countryNote: For an Al Twar student already secure on 0580 Extended material, this is usually a better purchase than more hours on the main course. It is also the entry most commonly added late, which is worth raising with the school in Year 10 rather than Year 11.

programmes.name: What follows at 16
programmes.description: Either A Level Mathematics, or IB Mathematics in one of two routes: Analysis and Approaches, the algebraic and analytical course, or Applications and Interpretation, the modelling and statistical course. Each is available at Higher and Standard Level in the Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: Al Twar has IB continuum provision locally and Diploma provision in Al Garhoud, so both routes are live options here. The practical test for the analytical routes is whether algebraic manipulation is automatic rather than merely correct, and that is decided during IGCSE rather than afterwards.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-twar.subjectsIntro: Maths tutoring in Al Twar usually arrives attached to something else. These are the subjects and components families here combine with it, and the specific overlap in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Number, algebra, geometry, trigonometry, vectors, probability and statistics. Most lost marks are algebraic slips inside correct methods, and the cure is marked volume rather than further explanation.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Calculus, advanced trigonometry, series and functions, overlapping early A Level content. Taken alongside 0580 by stronger sets and a better use of extra hours than repeating main-course topics.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The closest overlap with maths. Rearranging an equation before substituting, reading a gradient correctly and handling standard form account for a large share of physics losses, and all three are maths skills.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Proportional reasoning throughout, from reacting masses to concentration and gas volumes. A student weak on ratio work will appear weak at moles, and the correct diagnosis is arithmetic.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Percentage change, magnification calculations, scale and statistical interpretation. Easy marks are routinely lost here by students who are fine at the biology and shaky at the arithmetic.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Break-even, cash flow and ratio calculation, followed by a judgement. The numbers are seldom the problem; stating what they imply for the business in the case is.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Gradients, elasticity calculation and data interpretation, plus diagram conventions that must be learned to the specification. Maths-strong students often calculate correctly and explain nothing.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode, trace tables and binary arithmetic. The discipline of defining each step before computing transfers directly into multi-step maths problems, where errors are usually sequencing errors.

subjects.name: First Language English
subjects.description: Often the subject a maths-strong student in this cluster neglects. Worth protecting, because written explanation marks appear in several other subjects as well.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. It occupies timetable space when planning a weekly maths slot.

subjects.name: Non-calculator arithmetic
subjects.description: Long multiplication and division, fraction work, surds and exact-value trigonometry. Rarely drilled in school once calculators arrive, and heavily examined on the non-calculator paper.

subjects.name: Exam technique for maths
subjects.description: Showing enough working for method marks, reading the required accuracy, checking the units and deciding quickly which questions to leave until last. Teachable, and worth several grades for some students.

sections.heading: What is actually on an IGCSE maths paper
paragraphs: Parents hear topic names from their children and have no reliable sense of proportion between them. The useful frame is that number and algebra together carry a very large share of the marks on both specifications, geometry and trigonometry a substantial block, and probability and statistics a smaller but entirely winnable one. That matters for how a revision plan should be weighted, because a student who spends three weeks on transformations and a weekend on algebra has inverted the proportions.

Algebra is the load-bearing topic and the one where improvement spreads furthest. Rearranging formulae, solving simultaneous and quadratic equations, factorising, and working with algebraic fractions appear directly in their own questions and indirectly inside almost every other topic. A student who is slow at algebraic manipulation will be slow everywhere and will attribute the problem to whichever topic the question happened to be about. That misattribution is the commonest reason a family tutors the wrong thing for a term.

Statistics and probability are the reliably available marks that get neglected. The content is finite, the question styles repeat, and the methods are mechanical once learned: cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal intervals, tree diagrams, conditional probability. A student who is weak here is usually weak because nobody has drilled it rather than because it is difficult, which makes it the cheapest grade improvement in the subject.

The table sets out the topic areas with the common error in each. Treat the weighting column as the broad shape rather than a published figure, and confirm the detail against your child's own syllabus document from the board's site, which is also where the formula provision for their paper is set out.

sections.heading: 0580 against 4MA1, for maths specifically
paragraphs: The two specifications are not interchangeable and the differences are concentrated where tutoring time goes. Tiering is the first. Cambridge 0580 is Core and Extended, and the two tiers sit different papers with different content coverage and a different grade range. Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A 4MA1 is Foundation and Higher tier, again with its own paper structure per tier. Both therefore carry a ceiling attached to the entry, which is the fact families most often discover in the examination year.

Calculator provision is the second, and recent versions of the Cambridge syllabus make it explicit by separating non-calculator from calculator papers. A student who has learned the whole course with a calculator in hand and then meets a non-calculator paper discovers that their arithmetic and fraction work are slower than they believed. This is a practice problem, it is invisible in homework done at the kitchen table with a calculator present, and it responds quickly to short weekly drilling.

Formula provision is the third, and it is the one worth checking personally. Which formulae are printed on the paper, and which must be recalled, is set out in the syllabus document on the board's own site. Reading that page takes ten minutes and it reshapes revision: there is no point memorising what is provided, and there is considerable point in knowing what is not. A tutor who cannot tell you which list applies to your child is working from the wrong document.

Finally, question phrasing and mark-scheme convention. What counts as a complete answer for a given number of marks, how much working must be shown for method marks, and the required accuracy in a final answer are conventions learned by doing that board's papers. The table below sets out what to confirm. The source of truth in every row is the syllabus document and your examinations officer, not this page.

sections.heading: The tier, the ceiling and the Year 10 conversation
paragraphs: Both specifications attach a grade range to the tier of entry, so the entry decision sets an upper bound on the result. A lower-tier entry examines a reduced syllabus on an easier paper set and caps the achievable grade; an upper-tier entry covers the full content and opens the full range but presents questions a struggling student may not be able to attempt. Neither is the right answer in the abstract, and a student placed on a tier they cannot access will do worse than one correctly placed a tier below.

The failure mode in this district is not a wrong decision, it is an unexamined one. Entries are set by the school months before the papers, and a Year 11 parent asking why their child's maths grade appears capped is usually asking after the deadline has passed. The remedy costs nothing: ask for the tier in writing during Year 10, ask what evidence placed your child there, and ask the final date for an entry amendment. Schools answer all three.

Where tutoring legitimately helps is before that deadline. A short diagnostic engagement can establish whether a student can access upper-tier content, which is a different question from whether they currently are. A student held back by a specific missing topic, such as algebraic fractions or trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles, is a different case from a student for whom the upper-tier demand is consistently out of reach, and only the first case justifies pushing for a change.

One more point worth making to parents in Al Twar specifically, where ambition for maths runs high. Pushing a borderline student onto the upper tier to protect an idea of their ability is a bad trade. A capped grade achieved confidently supports a post-16 application better than an uncapped paper the student could not finish, and the conversation to have is with the school about evidence rather than with the tutor about effort.

sections.heading: The non-calculator paper and the arithmetic nobody drills
paragraphs: Somewhere around Year 7 most students stop practising arithmetic by hand, and nothing in the following four years asks them to resume. Then a non-calculator paper arrives and a capable mathematician loses marks on long division, on adding fractions with unlike denominators, on expressing a surd in simplest form and on exact trigonometric values. None of that is difficult content. All of it is slow and error-prone when unpractised, and slow is as expensive as wrong when the paper is timed.

The diagnosis is routinely missed because homework is done with a calculator on the table. A tutor who only ever sees calculator-assisted work will report that the student is fine, and will be right about the mathematics and wrong about the paper. The fix is mechanical: fifteen minutes of non-calculator work inside a longer weekly session, timed, with the error pattern named each week rather than merely corrected. Over a term that converts into marks you can see.

A particular Al Twar pattern is worth naming. Students from Indian-curriculum backgrounds often arrive with genuinely strong mental and written arithmetic, because that preparation drills it hard, and they are the group least likely to need this work. Students who have come through a British-curriculum primary and middle school with calculators available throughout are the group most likely to need it and the least likely to be told so. The same school, the same class, two opposite diagnoses.

Check which papers apply to your child before investing in this. Recent versions of the Cambridge syllabus separate non-calculator from calculator papers explicitly, and the Pearson specification sets out its own arrangement. If your child's entry has no non-calculator component, those fifteen minutes are better spent elsewhere, and a tutor should be able to tell you which situation you are in without looking it up.

sections.heading: Five questions that test a maths tutor on your specification
paragraphs: You do not need to be a mathematician to establish whether a tutor knows your child's paper. Five questions, all short, all specific. Ask them of everybody you consider, including us, and listen for precision instead of reassurance. A tutor working on that syllabus weekly answers all five quickly; one who teaches maths in general will answer in generalities, and that is the result of the test.

The first establishes the syllabus and tier, with the code. The second asks which of your child's papers permits a calculator, which a tutor cannot answer without knowing the entry. The third asks which formulae are provided and which must be recalled, which is the question that separates somebody who has read the syllabus document from somebody who has read the topic list. The fourth asks how much working is needed for method marks on that board, which is a mark-scheme convention question.

The fifth is diagnostic: what would you check first if my child kept arriving at nearly-right answers? A good answer is concrete, naming rounding at an intermediate stage, a sign error in expansion, or working to insufficient accuracy before the final line. A weak answer proposes more practice, which every tutor says and which tells you nothing about whether they can find the fault.

Run the same five past the nearest available tutor and an online specialist, and hire whoever answers better. The point of publishing a test is that an Al Twar parent should be able to decide on evidence rather than on which page looked more convincing. What we will say is that the test is easier to pass when a tutor was chosen for the specification rather than for the drive.

sections.heading: Why distance tells you nothing about whether a tutor knows 0580
paragraphs: Proximity is the easiest thing to verify about a tutor and almost the least informative. Whether somebody lives in Al Qusais is checkable in a sentence; whether they have marked a hundred 0580 Extended Paper 4 scripts is not, and only the second predicts anything about your child's grade. The search term says near me because that is what a search box can offer, not because it is the thing that matters.

The structural problem in a villa district like Al Twar is that the nearby pool is defined by willingness to drive rather than by specification. Within that pool, the chance of a precise match on board, tier and paper set is moderate for 0580 Extended, lower for 4MA1 Higher, and low for Additional Mathematics 0606. Across the whole population of tutors who teach a given specification weekly, it is close to certain. That is an argument about outcomes rather than convenience.

There is a second effect that is easy to overlook. A tutor working with several students on the same syllabus and tier sees the same mark-scheme traps repeatedly and builds a short list of the errors that cost most on that specific paper. That accumulated pattern knowledge is exactly what distinguishes a mid-band tutor from a budget one, and it exists only where a tutor has volume in the specification. Someone covering four boards across six subjects for a local client list has not had the chance to build it, however able they are.

IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is an India-only service. For an Al Twar family that turns the question from who is nearby into who teaches 0580 Extended, or 4MA1 Higher, every week. That is a question with a good answer, and the free trial lesson is where you check the answer is true.

sections.heading: What specification-correct maths teaching costs, and what you can verify free
paragraphs: Price and specification fit are independent, which is the useful thing to establish before comparing quotes. A tutor at the published premium end can be teaching the wrong syllabus, and a mid-band tutor can be teaching exactly the right one, so filter on the five questions above first and compare price second. The market bands, read in October 2026 and attributed to their publishers, are: Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the budget end; qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150; IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 survey agreeing on the range; in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 per Bestimate and up to AED 500 with independent home tutors; and BartyED advertising AED 650 at the premium end.

In monthly terms, which is how a household budget reads, Bestimate's survey puts a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240 to 600 for budget tutoring, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more at specialist exam-year level. Advertised packages run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. For maths the eight-point pattern generally does more than the four-point one at the same spend, because the subject rewards frequent marked practice rather than long teaching blocks. None of these figures is an IB Gram price; we publish a free trial lesson and a consultation.

Three checks cost nothing and improve the purchase more than comparing providers does. First, read your child's own syllabus document on the board's site, specifically the formula provision and the paper structure for their tier: ten minutes, and it tells you whether a tutor's revision plan is right. Second, ask about the permit. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own private tutor licensing service, which lists a two-working-day completion time. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so ignore any figure quoted at you.

Third, test the claims. Nobody selling you private maths tutoring in Dubai is accredited, approved or licensed by Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education to do it. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence for training institutes with physical premises, requiring initial approval first and annual renewal at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit and occupies no UAE premises. The boards publish their own centre lists, which is where a claim of that kind would be checkable.

sections.heading: What comes after IGCSE maths, and what to build now
paragraphs: The IGCSE maths grade opens or closes specific doors, and the useful thing to know in Year 10 is which. A Level Mathematics and IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level both assume algebraic fluency that is automatic rather than merely correct, because neither course leaves time to think about manipulation while thinking about the actual problem. IB Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation is the modelling and statistical route with technology permitted throughout, and rewards interpretation and context rather than unaided algebra.

That gives a concrete instruction for the IGCSE years. If the intended destination is an analytical route, the thing to build now is speed and automaticity in algebra, not extra topics. Additional Mathematics 0606 is a genuinely good purchase for a student already secure on 0580 Extended content, because it covers early calculus and advanced trigonometry and it exposes the student to the pace of post-16 work while there is still slack in the timetable.

If the destination is Applications and Interpretation, or a degree route that accepts either, the IGCSE priority shifts. Statistics and probability become more important than the last layer of algebraic depth, and so does the habit of saying what a figure means in context. That is a different revision plan from the analytical one, and worth distinguishing in Year 10 rather than discovering in DP1.

Check prerequisites against the specific universities your child is considering, including UAE institutions, because requirements differ by institution and by faculty within the same institution and are revised. Where the published information is ambiguous, write to admissions. Do not take a prerequisite claim from a tutoring page, this one included. On the UAE side, equivalency on the British track requires five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the count, plus one Advanced Level at E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade; verify through the Ministry of Education's own channel.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether a maths tutor teaches 0580 or 4MA1?
faqs.answer: Yes, more in maths than in most subjects, because by the spring of Year 11 a tutor is mostly working through past papers. Cambridge 0580 is tiered Core and Extended; Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A 4MA1 is Foundation and Higher. They differ in which paper permits a calculator, what the formula sheet provides, and what a mark scheme credits as working. A tutor on the wrong code drills the wrong practice for a term while appearing to make progress. Ask the examinations officer for the code and tier.

faqs.question: Will IB Gram send a maths tutor to our villa in Al Twar?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram provides no home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. IGCSE maths tuition for an Al Twar family is delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen for worked algebra and marked past papers. The practical gain here is specification fit: the tutor is selected for teaching 0580 Extended or 4MA1 Higher weekly, rather than for being the available person willing to drive to Al Twar on a weekday evening.

faqs.question: Which formulae will be printed on my child's maths paper?
faqs.answer: That depends on the specification and tier, and the authoritative answer is in the syllabus document on the board's own site, which takes about ten minutes to read. It matters in both directions. Memorising formulae that are provided wastes revision time, and assuming a formula is provided when it is not loses the question. It is also a good test of a tutor: one who has read the syllabus document can tell you which list applies, while one who has only read the topic list cannot.

faqs.question: Why did my daughter struggle on a paper with no calculator?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly unpractised arithmetic rather than weak mathematics. Most students stop working by hand years before they meet a non-calculator paper, so long division, fractions with unlike denominators, surds in simplest form and exact trigonometric values become slow and error-prone. Slow is as expensive as wrong on a timed paper. It is invisible in homework done with a calculator on the table, which is why it goes undiagnosed, and fifteen timed minutes inside a weekly session fixes it over a term.

faqs.question: Can the tier my child was entered for limit the maths grade?
faqs.answer: Yes. Both specifications attach a grade range to the tier of entry: Cambridge Core and Pearson Foundation examine a reduced syllabus on an easier paper set and cap the achievable grade, while Extended and Higher open the full range. The entry is set by the school months before the papers, so this is a Year 10 question. Ask for the tier in writing, ask what evidence placed your child there, and ask the final date for an entry amendment. All three are reasonable requests.

faqs.question: Should we push for the higher tier if our child is borderline?
faqs.answer: Only with diagnostic evidence, and often not. A student placed on a tier they cannot access performs worse than one correctly placed a tier below, because much of the paper becomes unattemptable. A capped grade achieved confidently supports a post-16 application better than an uncapped paper the student could not finish. The useful step is a short diagnostic engagement to establish whether the upper-tier content is genuinely accessible, then a conversation with the school about evidence rather than with a tutor about effort.

faqs.question: Which maths topics are worth the most revision time?
faqs.answer: Algebra first, by a wide margin. Rearranging formulae, solving simultaneous and quadratic equations, factorising and algebraic fractions appear in their own questions and inside almost every other topic, so a student slow at manipulation is slow everywhere and usually blames the wrong topic. After that, probability and statistics are the most neglected winnable marks: cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal intervals, tree diagrams and conditional probability all repeat in predictable styles and respond fast to direct drilling.

faqs.question: My son gets nearly-right answers. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Three causes account for most of it. Rounding at an intermediate stage rather than at the end, which shifts the final figure outside the accepted range. Sign errors during expansion or rearrangement, which produce a plausible wrong number. And working to insufficient accuracy before the final line, which the mark scheme may not accept. None of these is a knowledge gap and none is fixed by re-teaching the topic. Marked volume with the error pattern named each week is what changes it.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics 0606 worth taking as well?
faqs.answer: For a student already secure on 0580 Extended content, usually yes, and it is a better use of extra hours than repeating main-course topics. It covers early calculus, advanced trigonometry, series and functions, overlapping the start of A Level and IB Higher Level work, and it exposes a student to post-16 pace while the timetable still has slack. Raise it with the school in Year 10 rather than Year 11, because it is a separate entry and it is most commonly added too late.

faqs.question: Is it better to do more past papers or fewer from the right tier?
faqs.answer: Enough that the paper holds no surprises, which for most students means several full timed papers rather than a large number of selected questions. The crucial detail is that they come from your child's own code and tier, marked against that board's published scheme. Mixed-board practice teaches content correctly and mis-teaches phrasing, accuracy conventions and formula expectations at the same time. Quality of match matters considerably more here than quantity of papers completed.

faqs.question: Which series does a Dubai candidate sit, and when are the results?
faqs.answer: The June series or the November series. The February and March series is offered to India only and has no bearing on a UAE candidate. On published dates: the Pearson Edexcel November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Read the live official timetable from the board for current dates, and ask your examinations officer for your Cambridge zone.

Hourly, Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52, EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, Unitors IGCSE from AED 150, TutorChase AED 270 and BartyED AED 650. faqs.question: Does paying more guarantee the tutor knows my child's syllabus?
faqs.answer: No, and that is worth knowing before comparing quotes. Specification fit and price are independent: a tutor at the published premium end can be teaching the wrong code, and a mid-band tutor can be teaching exactly the right one. So filter first on the five questions in this page, which take ten minutes and cost nothing, and compare price only among the tutors who pass. That ordering is the single most useful habit a parent can bring to this market.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover maths and physics together?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and for IGCSE it is frequently efficient, because physics losses are largely maths losses in disguise: rearranging before substituting, reading a gradient correctly, handling standard form and units. A tutor who can see that pattern treats the cause rather than the symptom. The caveat is specification: confirm the codes for both subjects, because a tutor comfortable with one board's maths is not automatically comfortable with another board's physics practical conventions.

faqs.question: Can you supply past papers and mark schemes for us to keep?
faqs.answer: A tutor should work from them in the session and point you to the official source rather than distribute them. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the boards' copyright material, and reproducing or supplying them is not something we will do. Cambridge and Pearson publish what is publicly available on their own sites, and schools can access more through the examinations officer. A provider advertising a library of board material is telling you something about its standards.

intro.heading: How many hours of IGCSE maths does your child actually need?
paragraphs: Every tutoring comparison starts in the wrong place. Parents collect three hourly rates, pick the middle one and then find out over the following year how many hours the problem required. Reverse it. Establish the number of hours first, from marked work, and the rate becomes a small decision instead of the only one. In IGCSE mathematics the honest range of answers is wide: a tier decision needs one or two hours, a paper-technique repair needs six to ten, and a genuine two-year content gap needs something a tutor should be honest about rather than quietly monetising.

The most expensive thing in IGCSE maths is not an hourly rate at all. It is the tier. Cambridge 0580 Core candidates sit two papers and cannot be awarded above grade C. Extended candidates sit a different pair and can reach A star. Pearson 4MA1 runs Foundation, which reaches grade 5, and Higher, which runs to grade 9 with a grade 3 allowed. Enter a child for Core who needs a B for sixth form and no amount of money fixes it. Enter a child for Extended who is not ready and they can finish below where Core would have placed them.

The second most expensive thing is buying hours in response to anxiety rather than evidence. A household in Al Warqa'a 3 with a Year 10 showing a weak maths report has, in practice, three options: one weekly hour at the qualified-tutor band of AED 150 to 300, a budget supervision hour at AED 33 to 65 to make sure the set work gets done, or a short diagnostic block to find out which of those is the right purchase. The third costs least and is chosen least often.

Delivery is stated plainly here as on every page on this site: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. That service exists only in India. Al Warqa lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. For mathematics this works unusually well, because a shared screen with a student's own working annotated live, and a mark scheme open beside it, shows exactly which method marks were available and never claimed. That conversation is hard to have leaning over a notebook.

What follows is a costing document with the mathematics in it. The tier arithmetic. The papers in each board, and which of them is non-calculator. Where marks actually go, the five recurring ones. What hours cost at published Dubai rates and how many each starting point needs. Whether a group class, a budget tutor or a specialist is the right purchase for a given problem. And what a November resit costs if June goes wrong, counted from the published results dates rather than guessed at.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
programmes.description: Tiered as Core or Extended. Each tier has two written papers, one of which is sat without a calculator, and the syllabus covers number, algebra, coordinate geometry, geometry, mensuration, trigonometry, vectors and transformations, probability and statistics. programmes.countryNote: This is the most common mathematics entry among Al Warqa IGCSE students. The practical thing to establish early is which tier the school intends to enter, because that single decision caps or releases the grade and is far cheaper to influence in Year 10 than in Year 11.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, 4MA1
programmes.description: Two written papers, both calculator-permitted, sat at Foundation or Higher tier. Foundation reaches grade 5; Higher runs to grade 9 with a grade 3 allowed. Available in May-June and November each year. Because both papers allow a calculator, revision priorities differ from Cambridge, where one paper of each pair is non-calculator.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools reachable from Al Warqa run Pearson mathematics alongside Cambridge sciences, which is exactly the combination that produces a mismatched tutor. Ask for the code on the entry form: 4MA1 and 0580 need different practice, and a tutor who assumes one when the child sits the other wastes the first month.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics
programmes.description: A separate syllabus taken alongside Extended Mathematics by stronger candidates, covering functions, calculus, series, trigonometry and vectors at a level that overlaps with early A Level content. It is demanding, it is not universal, and it is excellent preparation for A Level Mathematics or Higher Level IB mathematics.
programmes.countryNote: Worth paying for only in one situation: a student comfortably on course for an A or A star in Extended who intends to take mathematics further. Buying support for Additional Mathematics while Extended Mathematics is still shaky is the clearest example of money spent in the wrong place in this whole subject.

programmes.name: International A Level Mathematics
programmes.description: The usual continuation for a Dubai IGCSE mathematician who does not move to the IB Diploma. Entry typically assumes Extended or Higher tier at a good grade, which is the practical reason the tier conversation belongs in Year 10 rather than being discovered in a sixth-form application.
programmes.countryNote: Ministry of Education British-track equivalency requires one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, alongside five GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-warqa.subjectsIntro: Mathematics is one subject on a timetable and five or six distinct skills on a paper. Each note below says what the topic demands and where Al Warqa candidates lose marks inside it.

subjects.name: Number and accuracy
subjects.description: Standard form, upper and lower bounds, percentage change, ratio and rates. The quiet killer is accuracy: a candidate who rounds early loses marks spread across a whole paper rather than in one visible place, and nobody notices because each individual loss is a single mark.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging, simultaneous and quadratic equations. Extended candidates lose most here, and almost always to abandonment: a correct method started, the expression grows, and the question is left half finished for partial credit. Fluency is built weekly, not in a weekend.

subjects.name: Coordinate geometry and graphs
subjects.description: Gradients, equations of lines, graph sketching and interpretation. Marks go on sketching from analysis rather than from a calculator, and on reading a gradient from axis values instead of counting grid squares, which is the single most common graph error at this level.

subjects.name: Geometry, mensuration and trigonometry
subjects.description: Angle reasoning, circle theorems, area and volume, Pythagoras, sine and cosine rules, and bearings. Bearings and three-dimensional trigonometry account for a disproportionate share of Extended losses because candidates do not draw the diagram before calculating.

subjects.name: Transformations and vectors
subjects.description: Translations, reflections, rotations, enlargements and vector notation. Students lose marks describing a transformation incompletely, giving a rotation without a centre or an enlargement without a scale factor, which the mark scheme treats as an unfinished answer.

subjects.name: Probability and statistics
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, conditional probability, averages from grouped data, histograms and cumulative frequency. The recurring loss is interpretation: the calculation is correct and the sentence saying what it means in context, which the scheme rewards, is never written.

subjects.name: Non-calculator technique
subjects.description: Exact fractions, surds where required, mental estimation and long-form arithmetic. Candidates who have practised everything with a calculator in hand are unprepared for half their Cambridge entry, and the gap usually surfaces in mocks rather than in classwork.

subjects.name: Calculator fluency
subjects.description: Using memory, fractions and statistical functions efficiently rather than retyping. A slow calculator user loses time rather than marks directly, which then costs marks at the end of the paper. Twenty minutes of deliberate teaching here pays for itself.

subjects.name: Problem-solving and multi-step questions
subjects.description: Questions that require two or three techniques in sequence with no signposting. These are where A and A star candidates are separated from B candidates, and they respond to practice on question types rather than to more content teaching.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: Functions, differentiation, integration, series, vectors and trigonometry at a level approaching early A Level. Only worth support when Extended Mathematics is already secure; buying 0606 help while 0580 is shaky is the commonest misallocation in this subject.

sections.heading: What a tiering mistake costs, in dirhams and in doors
paragraphs: Set the hourly rate aside and price the tier instead. A Cambridge Core candidate cannot be awarded above grade C. A Pearson Foundation candidate cannot be awarded above grade 5. If a sixth-form place, an A Level mathematics route or a university prerequisite needs more than that, the entry has already decided the answer and tutoring cannot change it. That is the only decision in IGCSE mathematics that is genuinely irreversible once the series is sat.

The opposite error costs differently. A candidate pushed into Extended or Higher who is not ready meets papers assuming content they have not secured, and can finish below where the lower tier would have placed them comfortably. Families rarely see this coming because classwork in a mixed-tier set looks reassuring, and the gap only becomes visible on a full upper-tier paper under timed conditions, which is exactly what a two-session diagnostic produces.

Both errors are cheap to avoid and expensive to repair. Two hours at the qualified-tutor band, somewhere between AED 300 and AED 600, buys an evidenced view in Year 10 that a head of department can act on. Repairing an optimistic Extended entry in the final term of Year 11 means specialist hours at AED 200 to 450 and above, under deadline pressure, with the tier fixed. The same money, spent a year apart, achieves entirely different things.

The third version of this is the one nobody budgets for: accepting the lower tier and planning around it. A grade C or grade 5 is a legitimate outcome that leads somewhere, and the honest conversation includes it. A provider who treats every Core entry as a problem to be solved with hours is selling hours. A tutor who says the tier is right and the grade is achievable has just saved you a year of payments, which is the test of whether advice is advice.

sections.heading: The papers in each board, and which one has no calculator
paragraphs: Cambridge 0580 gives each tier two written papers, and one of each pair is sat without a calculator. That structural fact shapes revision more than any topic list, because a candidate who has done every piece of practice with technology in hand has not prepared for half of their entry. The gap does not show in classwork, where calculators are usually permitted. It shows in a mock, by which point there are months rather than years left to fix it.

Pearson 4MA1 is different and simpler in this respect: two written papers, both calculator-permitted, at Foundation or Higher tier. Revision priorities shift accordingly. Where Cambridge candidates need deliberate non-calculator work, Pearson candidates need calculator fluency, because speed with fractions, memory and statistical functions decides how much of the second paper gets finished. Both are teachable, and neither is taught by accident.

Exact durations and mark totals are revised periodically by both boards, so the only reliable source is the current syllabus document and your school's examinations officer. That is not evasion; publishing a paper duration that changes next cycle would leave this page quietly wrong with nobody having touched it. What does not change often is the structure: tiers, two papers per tier, and the calculator split in Cambridge. Plan around those.

One more structural point matters for an Al Warqa family. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version of the timetable for their zone. That is an administrative risk a parent can eliminate in one email to the examinations officer, and it costs nothing.

sections.heading: The five recurring losses in Al Warqa maths scripts
paragraphs: First, illegible or absent working. Mark schemes award method marks for working an examiner can follow, so a correct final answer with unreadable working can score less than a wrong answer with clear method. This is the cheapest fix in the subject and the one students resist most, because writing more feels slower in the moment and is faster across a paper.

Second, abandoned algebra. A candidate starts correctly, the expression grows, and the question is left half completed. That is fluency rather than understanding, and fluency comes from short frequent practice over months. It is also the single strongest argument for starting in Year 10: you cannot build automaticity in a final-term intensive.

Third, graph errors. Gradients read by counting grid squares instead of using axis values, axes without units, and curves of best fit forced through the first and last points. Fourth, accuracy and rounding, which bleeds single marks across an entire paper so quietly that neither student nor parent can see it without a marked script in front of them.

Fifth, incomplete descriptions. A rotation given without a centre, an enlargement without a scale factor, a probability calculated correctly with no sentence saying what it means in context. The mark scheme treats each of those as unfinished, and the candidate believes they answered the question. All five are visible within minutes on two marked papers, which is why those two documents are worth more at the start of an arrangement than any amount of conversation about how maths makes your child feel.

sections.heading: Hours first, then rates: costing each starting point
paragraphs: Published Dubai figures give the multipliers. A qualified subject tutor working online is roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors advertising IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above in Bestimate's Dubai table, with TutorChase at AED 270. The budget tier is AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik. In-home visits across Dubai are AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's table and AED 200 to 500 from independent home tutors.

Now apply them to real starting points instead of to a generic year of support. A tier diagnostic is two hours: AED 300 to 600. A paper-technique block before a series is six to ten hours at specialist rates: AED 1,200 to 4,500. One weekly hour across Year 10 and Year 11 is roughly seventy hours at the qualified band: AED 10,500 to 21,000. Those three numbers are not variations on a theme; they are three different purchases, and most families buy the third when they needed the first.

The arithmetic also exposes the cheapest substitution available. A student who understands the content and will not practise needs supervision, and supervision at AED 45 to 65 an hour costs a quarter of what the same hours cost at the qualified band. Paying AED 250 an hour for somebody to sit with a child while they complete set work is a common, expensive and entirely avoidable mistake in this market.

IB Gram publishes no fixed UAE price list, because an honest figure depends on the tier, the board and how many weeks remain. The trial lesson is free, the estimate in hours comes with it, and there is no fixed term. What will not be offered is a promise about a grade: no provider can deliver what happens in an examination hall, and anyone who says otherwise is describing their advertising.

sections.heading: Group class, budget tutor or specialist: matching the purchase to the problem
paragraphs: Tuition centre group classes in Dubai run roughly AED 80 to 180 per student per hour, which is genuinely good value for one specific job: covering a shared syllabus at a shared pace for students at a similar level. They are poor value for the problems that actually bring Al Warqa families to a tutor, because a centre timetable cannot spend forty minutes on one child's bearings diagrams while five other students wait.

The budget online tier does one job well too. At AED 33 to 65 an hour it buys presence, question-answering and the completion of set work. For a Year 10 who understands the mathematics and will not sit down, that is precisely the right product, and it is the cheapest route to the single biggest improvement available in many households: the homework actually gets done.

The qualified band, AED 150 to 300, is where diagnosis lives. It is the tier that can look at a marked paper and say the problem is rounding rather than algebra, or legibility rather than understanding, or tier rather than effort. That ability is the whole value proposition, and it is what separates a worthwhile hour from an expensive one. Most IGCSE mathematics problems are solved at this band and nowhere else.

Specialist and premium bands, AED 200 to 450 and AED 500 to 650 and above, are defensible for a narrow task: paper technique in a short final block, or Additional Mathematics 0606 where the content approaches A Level. They are indefensible as a default across two years and four subjects. And a caution on the premium end: examiner status means nothing unless it is current and evidenced, and it never implies access to marking, boundaries or paper content.

sections.heading: If June goes wrong: pricing a November attempt
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit the June and November series. The February-March series exists but is offered to India only, and incorrect advice about it circulates widely enough in this market to be worth contradicting directly. So a disappointing June grade in mathematics means a November decision, taken in August with real dates to work from.

The published Pearson pattern gives the shape. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also issues provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the right habit is to open the live official timetable rather than rely on any restated date, including the ones here.

That leaves roughly eight to ten weeks between a June result and a November sitting, and those weeks have a clear best use. Mathematics resits are won on paper technique rather than on content, because a candidate who sat the paper in June has met the syllabus. Six to ten sessions on the failed papers, marked against the scheme, with working legibility and question-type recognition addressed directly, is a defensible AED 1,200 to 4,500 with an end date attached.

What is not defensible is converting a resit into a new rolling arrangement. The grade is decided in November; the arrangement should end there. And the resit decision itself should be weighed honestly against accepting the grade, because a C or a 5 that is sufficient for the intended post-16 route is a finished matter, and spending eight weeks and several thousand dirhams to improve a grade nobody will ask about is a poor use of both.

sections.heading: Why more hours is usually the wrong purchase
paragraphs: The default response to a weak maths report is to add hours, and it is usually wrong because it treats a diagnostic problem as a quantity problem. A student losing marks to rounding does not need more mathematics; they need a twenty-minute conversation and a term of habit. A student whose working is unreadable needs a rule and enforcement, not content. A student in the wrong tier needs an entry changed, and no number of hours substitutes for it.

There is a second reason, which is time. A Year 11 already carries school lessons, homework, coursework, the Arabic and Islamic Education lessons KHDA requires of every Dubai private school, and whatever activities survive. Adding three tutoring hours a week to that produces a tired student and worse papers. The hour that works is one protected hour with a clear target, not three unfocused ones.

The third reason is that the most valuable hours are not extra at all, they are better placed. The week a mock paper comes back marked is the highest-value tutoring hour in the entire course, because the student has just demonstrated exactly where the marks go. Families routinely cancel during mock weeks because the fortnight is busy, which is precisely backwards, and nobody ever charges less for it.

So the honest sequence is: establish the cause from marked work, buy the specific repair, review against the school's own data at six weeks, then extend or stop. Where a diagnosis predicted four sessions and ten have passed with no movement, the diagnosis was wrong. That is useful information and far cheaper to act on than another term of the same arrangement, and a provider who never surfaces it is not working in your interest.

sections.heading: Permits, premises and what you are entitled to ask
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit, and the rule is specific enough to quote. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced private tuition work permits, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students.

MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts has been published, so none is quoted here; a figure circulating informally could not be verified against any official source.

Two further things you are entitled to ask about. Whether the tutor is your child's own teacher, because a teacher cannot be paid to tutor students enrolled at their own school and the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. And whether any claimed accreditation exists: a tutoring operation with premises in Dubai needs a KHDA educational services permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry.

IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no premises in the UAE, and claims no approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson. We will also not supply syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, because those are copyright and reproducing them is infringement. What a tutor legitimately provides is the teaching that a mark scheme rewards, not the mark scheme.

process.title: Send two marked papers
process.description: Recent, with annotations. Rounding losses, illegible working, abandoned algebra, graph errors and incomplete descriptions are all visible within minutes, and each points to a different and much shorter piece of work than a year of weekly hours.

process.title: Buy the diagnosis before the hours
process.description: A two-session diagnostic at AED 150 to 300 an hour tells you whether the problem is tier, technique or content. It is the cheapest purchase in the subject and the one families skip, going straight to a rolling weekly commitment instead.

process.title: Take the free trial, then agree a target
process.description: The trial should end with a named cause and an estimate in hours, not a monthly figure. Write the target down, because that is what the six-week review is measured against rather than a general sense that things are going better.

process.title: Review at six weeks and act on it
process.description: Compare the school's own assessment data. If the estimate was four sessions and ten have passed with nothing moving, the diagnosis was wrong, and changing the approach is cheaper than continuing. Stop when the target is met rather than when the term ends.

whyPoints.title: Hours estimated before rates quoted
whyPoints.description: A tier diagnostic is two hours, a technique block is six to ten, a two-year arrangement is about seventy. Those are three different purchases with three different totals, and we publish all three rather than quoting a monthly figure and letting it run.

whyPoints.title: The tier treated as the main decision
whyPoints.description: Cambridge Core caps at grade C and Pearson Foundation at grade 5. No amount of tutoring lifts a ceiling, so we pressure-test the tier in Year 10 with evidence a head of department can act on, including when the answer is that the current tier is right.

whyPoints.title: The calculator split taken seriously
whyPoints.description: One Cambridge paper per tier is sat without a calculator, which is half the entry. Deliberate non-calculator practice from the first term prevents a gap that otherwise appears in mock results with months rather than years left to fix it.

whyPoints.title: The cheap substitution named out loud
whyPoints.description: A student who understands the content and will not practise needs supervision at AED 33 to 65 an hour, not diagnosis at AED 250. Saying so costs us revenue and is the correct advice, which is the only reason worth saying anything.

whyPoints.title: Online one-to-one, with working annotated live
whyPoints.description: Al Warqa lessons run one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own working screen-shared and marked up against a scheme. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service.

whyPoints.title: No copyright material, no accreditation claims, no grade promises
whyPoints.description: We do not supply past papers, mark schemes or grade boundaries, hold no board or regulator approval, and promise nothing about a grade. Each of those is something at least one page researched for this project does, and each is a liability.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE maths tutor in Al Warqa cost in total?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on how many hours the problem needs, which is why the hours should be established first. At the qualified band of AED 150 to 300 an hour, a two-session tier diagnostic is AED 300 to 600, a short technique block of six to ten sessions is AED 1,200 to 4,500 at specialist rates, and one weekly hour across Years 10 and 11 is roughly seventy hours, or AED 10,500 to 21,000. Most families buy the third when the first was the right purchase.

faqs.question: Can tutoring get my child above a grade C if they are entered for Core maths?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge 0580 Core candidates cannot be awarded above grade C regardless of how well they perform, and Pearson 4MA1 Foundation candidates cannot be awarded above grade 5. That ceiling is set by the entry, not by ability, so if a sixth-form place requires more the tier has to change before entries close. This is the one decision in IGCSE mathematics that tutoring genuinely cannot influence after the fact, which is why it should be addressed in Year 10.

faqs.question: Does my Al Warqa child sit a 0580 paper with no calculator allowed?
faqs.answer: Each Cambridge 0580 tier has two written papers and one of each pair is sat without a calculator. The consequence is that a candidate who has done all their practice with technology in hand is unprepared for half their entry, and the gap rarely shows in classwork because calculators are usually permitted there. It appears in mock results instead. Pearson 4MA1 differs: both papers are calculator-permitted, so the priority shifts to calculator speed rather than mental technique.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for Additional Mathematics 0606 support?
faqs.answer: Only when Extended Mathematics is already secure. Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics covers functions, calculus, series, trigonometry and vectors at a level overlapping early A Level, and it is excellent preparation for A Level or Higher Level IB mathematics. Buying support for 0606 while 0580 Extended is still shaky is the clearest misallocation in this subject: the foundation is where the grade comes from, and the additional qualification helps nobody if the main one disappoints.

faqs.question: My child understands maths but will not do the homework. What should we buy?
faqs.answer: Supervision, not diagnosis. The budget online tier at AED 33 to 65 an hour, where Tutopiya and EdFlik advertise, buys presence and question-answering, which is exactly what makes set work get completed. Paying AED 250 an hour for the same service is a common and avoidable expense in this market. If the completed homework does not move the marks after a term, that is new information and the purchase should change then rather than pre-emptively.

faqs.question: Where do Al Warqa students lose the most IGCSE maths marks?
faqs.answer: Five places. Working an examiner cannot follow, which forfeits method marks that were genuinely earned. Abandoned algebra, where a correct method is started and left half done. Graph errors, especially gradients counted in grid squares rather than read from axis values. Accuracy and rounding, which bleeds single marks across an entire paper invisibly. And incomplete descriptions, such as a rotation given without a centre. All five appear on two marked papers within minutes.

faqs.question: Should we start maths tutoring in Year 10 or wait for Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10 if the problem is fluency or tier, because both take months rather than weeks. Algebraic automaticity is built by short frequent practice, and a tier decision can only be influenced while the school can still act on it. Year 11 if the problem is paper technique, where a short block of past papers marked against the scheme in the eight to ten weeks before a series is one of the few places specialist rates genuinely earn themselves.

faqs.question: Is a group maths class at a Dubai centre good value for an Al Warqa family?
faqs.answer: For one job, yes. At roughly AED 80 to 180 per student per hour it covers a shared syllabus at a shared pace, which suits a student who needs the whole course rather than a specific repair. It is poor value for the problems that usually bring families to a tutor, because a centre timetable cannot spend forty minutes on one child's bearings diagrams while five others wait. Add the drive to Al Qusais or Mirdif twice a week to the real cost.

faqs.question: What does a November maths resit cost after a disappointing June?
faqs.answer: Between roughly AED 1,200 and AED 4,500 for six to ten specialist sessions, with an end date at the first paper. The timing works: June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026 and the November 2026 final Pearson timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, leaving eight to ten weeks. Resits are won on paper technique rather than content, because the candidate has already met the syllabus. Weigh it honestly against accepting a grade that is sufficient.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover maths for two children sitting different boards?
faqs.answer: Ask directly rather than assuming. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 differ in tiering, in the calculator split and in question phrasing, and a tutor who teaches one by default will waste the first few weeks with the other. Some tutors handle both comfortably. Online, two children can be taught at different hours on the same evening by two specialists with nobody waiting, which usually beats compromising on one tutor to save a journey that does not exist anyway.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a permit to teach maths online to a Dubai student?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tuition need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time via its app, website and e-services, and eligible applicants include school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no schedule of amounts published officially.

faqs.question: Can you give us past papers and mark schemes for 0580?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge and Pearson materials are copyright, and reproducing or distributing syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables is infringement. What a tutor can legitimately do is work with material the school has already issued, point you to the official source, and teach the technique a mark scheme rewards, which is the part that actually produces marks. Be cautious of any provider whose main offer is a library of other people's assessment material.

faqs.question: How many hours a week of maths tutoring is too many?
faqs.answer: More than two, for almost every IGCSE student. A Year 11 already carries school lessons, homework, coursework and the Arabic and Islamic Education lessons KHDA requires of every Dubai private school. Adding three tutoring hours produces a tired student and worse papers, not better ones. One protected hour with a named target outperforms three unfocused ones, and the genuinely valuable extra hour is the one in the week a mock paper comes back marked.

faqs.question: What should the first maths session actually produce?
faqs.answer: A named cause and an estimate in hours. Not a monthly figure, not enthusiasm, and not a reading list. By the end of a free trial you should know whether the marks are going on rounding, on legibility, on abandoned algebra, on graph technique or on the tier, and roughly how long the specific repair takes. Write that estimate down, because it is what the six-week review measures against. A tutor who cannot produce it has not read the marked work carefully enough.

Then the rate is a small decision rather than the only one you were given. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time with working annotated live.
